fields.title: 11～12个月：喂养的常识与方法
fields.subtitle: 喂养指南
fields.content:
11～12个月婴儿的喂养重点
合理补充蛋白质
蛋白质仍是这一时期的孩子需要重点补充的营养，其主要来源还是奶、蛋类、肉类。这些动物蛋白质是优质蛋白质，吸收率和利用率要比植物蛋白高。豆制品属于植物性蛋白质，虽然其中的蛋白质含量也很丰富，但主要是粗蛋白，婴儿的消化吸收能力差，吃多了粗蛋白会加重肾脏的负担。所以，豆制品不是不能给孩子吃，而是不要多吃，每天最好不要超过50克。
额外补充维生素
不爱吃蔬菜和水果的孩子可能会缺乏维生素。另外，食物在烹调加工过程中，维生素会大量流失，即使孩子不挑食，什么食物都吃，也有可能出现维生素不足。所以，额外补充维生素还是很有必要的。
这一时期，孩子每日需要补充维生素A约800国际单位；因为户外活动相对增加，阳光照射能够帮助孩子合成一些维生素D，所以维生素D制剂的补充量可以适当减少一些，每日200国际单位就可以了。
挑食孩子的营养补充
● 不爱吃奶的孩子，可以用蛋肉来补充蛋白质；相反，如果孩子不爱吃蛋肉，那就适当多给他吃些奶。
● 不爱吃蔬菜的孩子，应该多给他吃水果，来补充维生素的不足，或者在医生的指导下添加一些维生素制剂。
● 不爱吃粮食的孩子，除了多吃蔬菜水果外，还是要以奶为主，因为相比蛋类和肉类，奶能够提供更多的热量。
11～12个月婴儿的饮食要点
饭菜由辅食变为主食
随着孩子一天一天长大，奶已经满足不了他的生长发育需求，而是需要由食物来提供营养。这个月孩子的饮食结构要逐步向幼儿期过渡，一日三餐以饭菜为主，中间再加两顿点心。奶还是要喝，但不要放在正餐前后，以免影响进食。所选的食物应该包含更全面的营养，碳水化合物、脂肪和蛋白质是必不可少的，可以通过粮食、肉类、蛋类、鱼类、蔬菜和水果提供。
食物硬度比大人的饭菜稍软
这个月大多数婴儿都已经长出了上下中切牙，可以咬得动较硬的食物，但臼齿还没有长出来，不能把食物咀嚼得很细，因此饭菜要做得比大人的相对细软一些，如软饭、细面、饺子、烂菜、碎肉等等。不需要像以前一样把食物制成泥或糊，蔬菜只要切成细丝或薄片再煮烂即可，以便帮助孩子逐渐适应幼儿期的食物形态。
每餐食物量稍有增加
以前吃4～5餐的可以适当减少餐数，但每餐的进食量要略为增加，为大人食量的1/3～1/2，约半碗左右。如果以往一直以粥为主食，现在可尝试换成米饭，可在喂粥前先喂2～3匙软米饭，适应后即可完全换成米饭。奶每天喂2次，每次200毫升即可。
让孩子上桌同大人一起吃饭
正在断奶期或已经断掉母乳的这段时间，是建立孩子良好进餐规律的好机会，父母要给孩子在饭桌上留一个固定的位置，有规律地进食正餐也会对顺利断奶有帮助。而且经过几个月的辅食添加训练，孩子可以接受的食物品种已经很多了，对于大人吃的食物会有强烈的好奇心。虽然孩子这时候多半会将饭桌搞得比较狼狈，但这是让孩子体验和形成良好进食规律和习惯的一个重要途径。
适当加调味品调动孩子食欲
我们提倡婴儿期的饮食以清淡为主，在此之前给孩子做的食物也都是不加任何调味品的。不过适当的味觉刺激能够调动食欲，如果孩子不爱吃饭、食欲差（除疾病方面的原因），父母在给孩子做饭时可以稍微加点盐等调味品，让孩子尝试不一样的味道。
盐：每天不要超过2克，不必每顿都加盐，1～2顿加就可以。
糖：每天最多1/3小勺，只在需要添加一点味道时才使用，糖吃多了也容易影响孩子正餐的食欲，还容易患龋齿。
酱油：酱油里含盐量很高，要注意控制用量，每天1～2滴即可。如果饭菜的味道已经够了，加酱油只是为了让颜色更好看一些，那就不要加。
食用油：最好使用植物油，每天2～3滴。比如给孩子吃面条或馄饨时，在汤里滴一滴芝麻油。
11～12个月婴儿可添加的食物
主食类
主食不但能为孩子提供热量，还可以锻炼咀嚼和吞咽能力。包括各种谷物食品以及面食，如粥、米饭、面条、馄饨、小包子、馒头等。
婴儿能不能吃粗粮
对于成人来说，多吃粗粮有很多好处，可以缓解便秘、降血脂血糖、预防肥胖等等。但婴幼儿的消化系统发育不完善，消化能力比较差，而粗粮不容易消化，所以最好不要给婴儿多吃粗粮。如果要吃，也要粗粮细做，熬成烂粥或和白面混合做成发糕，让婴儿容易接受。
蔬菜水果类
各种当季的新鲜水果蔬菜都可以给孩子吃，但葱、蒜、姜、香菜、洋葱等味浓、刺激性比较大的蔬菜除外，一些容易引起过敏的水果，如芒果、菠萝也不要轻易给孩子尝试。蔬果可以不必弄得很碎了，很多水果都可以直接让孩子拿着吃。
肉蛋类
家禽和家畜肉：鸡肉、猪肉、牛肉均可，注意去掉皮和肥肉，牛肉纤维比较粗，要切得细碎一些。
水产品：鱼、虾等海产品都可以吃，但是要注意食用后的反应，过敏性体质的孩子在吃海鲜的时候尤其要谨慎。
动物血和肝脏：补铁防贫血的重要食材，可以将猪肝或猪血蒸熟压成泥给孩子吃。但如果孩子接受不了那种味道，也不要强迫。
蛋类：鸡蛋、鸭蛋、鹌鹑蛋，可用蒸、煮、炒、炖等各种方式做。...

fields.title: 11～12个月：环境与异常情况
fields.subtitle: 环境与护理
fields.content:
11～12个月婴儿的睡眠问题
由于个体间的差异，每个孩子都有自己的生物钟，睡眠规律也就不尽相同。孩子有充足的睡眠时间当然最好，但如果孩子生长发育正常，白天精神好，吃饭、玩耍都没有问题，即使睡不够建议的时间也是没有多大问题的。
晚上很晚都不睡觉
对待很晚都不睡觉的孩子，强迫或呵斥哄睡是不起作用的，甚至还有可能导致孩子产生睡眠障碍。父母应该采取一些方法来帮助孩子尽早入睡。
● 调整睡眠时间：白天不要让孩子睡太多，如果午觉睡得很久，或者傍晚又睡一觉，那势必造成孩子到了晚上该睡觉的时间仍然精力旺盛。这种情况下就要对孩子白天的睡眠时间进行适当的调整。午觉早睡一些早起一些，傍晚尽量不要再睡。
● 睡前不要让孩子太兴奋：睡前孩子的大脑活动很兴奋就不容易入睡，所以晚上不要过分逗乐孩子，尤其是爸爸，尽量不要和孩子玩得太疯。
● 哼摇篮曲、讲故事：父母可以将孩子搂在怀里，轻声地给孩子哼摇篮曲或讲故事，在轻柔的声音中孩子比较容易入睡。
● 营造良好的睡眠环境：把卧室的灯关闭或调暗，将一切能够吸引孩子注意力的东西收起来，如玩具、食物等。从而让孩子认识到夜幕降临、万籁俱寂就是该睡觉的时候了。
● 父母以身作则：孩子的很多行为都是模仿自父母的，看到父母不睡觉，自己也就不想睡觉了。因此，父母应该给孩子树立一个好榜样，每天晚上到了睡觉的时间就关闭电视，停止一切活动，和孩子一同入睡。
睡前不要让宝宝太兴奋，尽量不要和宝宝玩得太疯。
如何护理总是流鼻涕的婴儿
感冒时会流涕是我们都熟知的，但父母不要一看到孩子流鼻涕就认为孩子感冒了。引发流涕的原因是多种的，处理方法也应该有所不同。
有些流涕是正常生理现象
正常人每天会分泌数百毫升的鼻涕，只不过这些鼻涕都顺着鼻黏膜纤毛运动的方向流向鼻后孔了。一部分通过咽喉被吞下，一部分被咳出变成痰，还有一部分蒸发干结，这样一般也就没有鼻涕从鼻腔流出了。但婴幼儿的鼻腔黏膜血管比成人的要丰富，分泌物也较多，加上神经系统对鼻黏膜分泌及纤毛运动的调节功能尚未健全，而且小孩子又不会自己擤鼻涕，所以经常会流清鼻涕。这是一种正常的生理现象，不必担心。
不要随便给孩子吃药
如果没有确认是感冒病毒引起的流涕，父母不要随意给孩子吃感冒药。是药三分毒，能不吃就不吃。
异常的流涕情况
脓样黄绿色鼻涕 伤风感冒时起初是清水样鼻涕，后期会流黄色的鼻涕，这种情况下常提示有病毒感染，只要用药杀灭病毒，感冒好时也就不再流涕了。但如果孩子的鼻孔下长期挂着两行鼻涕，或流出黄绿色的脓鼻涕，那就是病态的表现了，可能患有副鼻窦炎。
白鼻涕 如果孩子经常流白鼻涕，可能是由于缺乏维生素A和维生素B导致的，及时补充这两种维生素可以使流鼻涕的情况得到改善。
鼻塞、鼻涕中有血丝 如果孩子流鼻涕的同时出现鼻塞、呼吸不畅、烦躁不安，甚至流出的鼻涕中带有血丝，则可能是有异物（如玩具小零件）附在鼻腔中。这时要立刻带孩子去医院检查，千万不要当作感冒、气管炎、肺炎等疾病来治疗，以免耽误最佳抢救时间，造成不可挽回的损失。
孩子流涕的护理
1．父母要经常用柔软的手绢或纸巾帮孩子擦拭流出的鼻涕。婴儿的皮肤比较娇嫩，反复擦拭可能会造成鼻头红肿或破损，为防止这种情况发生，每次擦完鼻涕后用湿毛巾捂一捂，然后再抹上护肤油，防止鼻部皮肤皴裂疼痛。
2．不方便擤鼻涕时可以用吸鼻器帮孩子把鼻涕吸出来。
3．不要轻易使用滴鼻剂，因为使鼻子通气的药物中一般都含有麻黄素，由于鼻腔和咽部是相通的，滴药时药剂很有可能流入咽喉，被孩子咽下。麻黄素被孩子身体吸收后，会产生一定的毒副作用。
为婴儿按摩的方法
按摩可以促进身体血液循环，使全身的肌肉得到锻炼，对孩子来说，是提高免疫力的一种很好的方法。另外，父母更是可以通过按摩向孩子表达爱意，是一种很好的亲子互动方式。如果从新生儿起父母就有给孩子按摩的习惯，那当然要一直坚持，如果没有，从现在开始也不晚。
按摩的时机与时间
吃完饭并休息好后或洗完澡后孩子的身心都比较平稳，没有什么不适，这时候进行按摩，孩子会很乐于接受。不要在孩子刚吃完饭（吃完饭30分钟之内）、发烧时或接种疫苗48小时内进行按摩。
每次按摩的时间不是越久就好，大约20分钟就可以了。孩子的皮肤和骨骼还比较柔嫩，所以要注意按摩力度不能太大。如果孩子不愿意接受，那就不要勉强。
把按摩当成一种游戏
这个月龄的孩子正是好动的时候，如果不是睡觉的时间，让他乖乖地躺几十分钟是非常困难的事情。但是，父母如果能把按摩变成一种游戏来和孩子玩，或者将按摩的过程和有趣的故事结合起来，相信孩子会非常乐意配合。而且这时候孩子已经能听懂许多话，交流起来也比较容易。
开始按摩前要准备些什么
● 将室温调到22℃以上，准备按摩油或乳液及铺在孩子身下的柔软毛巾。
● 摘掉戒指等首饰，剪去指甲，用温水洗净双手，涂上润肤油。
● 边给孩子脱衣服边说：“按摩游戏就要...

fields.title: 11～12个月：产后保养须知
fields.subtitle: 产后保养
fields.content:
重要的产后第一天
产后第一天这24小时，对新妈妈来说是经历严峻考验的一天，如何做好自我健康监测和护理，请关注下面的建议。
观察出血量：产后出血，是产妇第一天最需要注意的问题，因此，不管再疲乏、再虚弱，观察自己的出血量是新妈妈最重要的功课。目前，在我国导致孕产妇死亡的第一原因是产后出血，产妇在分娩后两小时内最容易发生产后出血，产后2小时出血400毫升，24小时内出血500毫升都可以判断为产后出血。
产妇出血过多：会导致休克、弥漫性血管内凝血甚至死亡。所以，分娩后仍需在产房内观察。此时，要特别注意子宫收缩乏力也会引起产后出血。
因此，在上厕所时，应注意把卫生护垫等收集起来，不要丢弃，如果出血量较多，或阴道排出组织都应及时告知医生。
多喝水：如果是顺产产妇，下了产床以后就要多喝水。因为在生产过程中，胎头下降会压迫膀胱、尿道，使得膀胱麻痹以及产后腹壁肌肉松弛而排不出尿。膀胱过度充盈，会影响子宫的收缩，也会导致产后出血。
此外，由于产程中失血，以及进食过少也会导致体液丢失，因此要注意多喝水补充体液。一般来说，在顺产后4～6个小时内就可以自己小便了，但由于外阴创伤，新妈妈会惧怕疼痛而不敢用力排尿，极易导致尿潴留。一旦发生了尿潴留或尿不彻底，则可能会让细菌侵入，引发尿路感染。如果在分娩6～8小时后甚至在月子中，仍然不能正常地排出尿液，并且膀胱还有饱胀的感觉，就可能已经患上尿潴留了。
辅助方法帮助排尿
听流水声：利用条件反射解除排尿抑制，使自己产生尿意，促使排尿。
热敷疗法：用温水冲洗外阴；也可以用开水熏下身，让水汽充分熏到会阴部，注意要保持身体不接触水，以免烫伤；或者在下腹正中放置水袋刺激膀胱收缩，促进膀胱肌肉的收缩，有利于排尿。
﻿因此，尽快排出第一次小便很重要。产后6～8小时是最易出现异常情况的阶段，如果怎么都尿不出，就得求助于医生了。
定时测量体温：产后发热是大事，不能等闲视之。新妈妈在产后一定要养成定时量体温的好习惯，如果发现体温超过38℃就要当心有问题。
在刚生过孩子的24小时内，由于过度疲劳，可能会发热到38℃，但以后体温应该恢复正常。如果发热，必须查清原因、适当处置。有个别新妈妈因为乳胀可能发烧，在奶汁排出后体温将会下降。如果奶汁排出后仍不退烧，就可能是身体某处有炎症。
产后发热的最常见原因是产褥感染，就是“产褥热”。引起产褥热的原因很多，包括产道感染，泌尿系统感染、乳房感染等。女性在产后体力要比平时差很多，又伴有流血、恶露和子宫口松弛，阴道本来有的细菌或外来细菌容易滋生，并漫延到生殖道或侧切伤口。这时的恶露有异味、腹部有压痛，如果治疗不及时，可能转为慢性盆腔炎而长期不愈。毒性大的细菌侵入，还可能有引起腹膜炎或败血症的危险。
因此，产后新妈妈要注意观察自己的体温，多喝水，注意摄入营养，如果高烧连续不退就得赶紧找医生了。
多吃蔬菜水果：产后第一天，应该吃一些稀、软但有丰富营养的食物，如肉、蛋、鱼和豆腐之类。汤水类食物像鸡汤、排骨汤，对催乳很有效。而富含膳食纤维的新鲜蔬菜和水果，不仅能增加维生素的摄入，对防止便秘也有帮助。
要荤素搭配、开胃口、多样化：贫血的产妇要多吃一些猪肝、鸭血和菠菜。有抽筋和关节痛的产妇更要继续服用钙片。为了保证泌乳的需要，晚上也可以再加一次半流质或点心之类的夜宵。
坐一坐，走一走：产后有很多新妈妈因为疲惫不堪，产后第一天基本上躺着度过，这样不好。
顺产产妇可以在产后6～8小时坐起来；剖宫产的产妇在手术后24小时可以坐起。要多坐、少躺，不能总躺在床上。躺在床上不仅不利于体力的恢复，还容易降低排尿的敏感度，有可能阻碍尿液的排出，引起尿潴留，并可能导致血栓形成。
根据体力适当活动
如果分娩顺利，产后可根据体力恢复情况下床，适当活动。产后24小时可以随意活动，避免长时间站立、久蹲或做重活，以防子宫脱垂。产后8周可逐渐恢复正常活动，并且适时尝试做一做较轻缓的体操，有助于形体恢复。
关注初乳：初乳不要浪费，一般来说，当宝宝脐带处理好后，就可以尝试给孩子喂奶。新妈妈第一天会分泌少量黏稠、略带黄色的乳汁，这就是初乳。初乳含有大量的抗体，能保护婴儿免受细菌的侵害，所以应尽可能地给宝宝哺喂初乳，以减少新生儿疾病的发生。
其次，哺乳的行为能刺激大脑，大脑会发出信号增加乳汁的分泌。因此，在产后第一天尽早地给孩子哺乳，能形成神经反射，增加乳汁的分泌。新妈妈也可多吃一些增加乳汁分泌的食物，如花生煲猪蹄、鱼汤等。
﻿新妈妈还应该随时关注自己的乳房温度和硬度。如果乳房摸上去有红肿热痛的硬块，并伴有发热感，同时体温升得较快，甚至到了39℃以上，则很有可能患上了乳腺炎。开始可行热敷，用中药和在医生指导下适当采用抗菌素。如已化脓，就可能要手术治疗了。
乳腺炎往往因为乳汁分泌不畅，在乳腺内郁积成块，再加上乳头有裂口，细菌侵入而引起祸患。所以，在产...

fields.title: 11～12个月：产褥期有哪些注意事项
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
产褥期，有如下事项应给予关注：
（1）产后10日内，应每天观察产妇的体温、脉搏、呼吸和血压。
（2）产后24小时内，应卧床休息。保证充分的睡眠时间。但尽量避免做重体力劳动，以免发生子宫脱垂。
（3）产后第一天的饮食可清淡一些，吃些易消化的食物，第二天以后可多吃高蛋白和汤汁食物，适当补充维生素和铁剂。
（4）产后尿量增多，应及时排小便，以免胀大的膀胱妨碍子宫收缩。产后2日内应排大便。如有便秘，可用开塞露、肥皂水灌肠等进行处理。
（5）每日可用温开水或消毒液冲洗阴部2～3次，保持会阴部清洁干燥。一般在产后4～5天拆除会阴缝线。
（6）产妇产后宫底高度逐日复原，产后10天后应在腹部摸不到子宫；剖宫产的产妇一般复原较慢，应适当使用宫缩剂；如果恶露出现臭秽气味或腐臭气味，应进行抗炎治疗。
什么叫产褥期
胎儿出生后，胎盘自母体排出，从这时开始，产妇进入了产后恢复阶段。这个阶段在生理变化上是一个很大的转折时期。因为在妊娠期间，母体的生殖器官和全身所发生的一系列变化，都要在产后约6～8周内逐步调整以至完全恢复，医学上就把这段时间叫做产褥期。

fields.title: 11～12个月：产后做好卫生保健
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
怀孕期间，准妈妈的生理状况会有极大的变化，不单是体重增加，血液、心脏、内分泌功能也会改变，乳房、子宫、骨盆等构造也有明显的变化。这些生理变化是怀胎十月逐渐累积的成果，所以生产以后自然也需要一段时间才会恢复，妈妈要做好产后的卫生保健。
恢复期间要注意：
（1）注意身体清洁。产后出汗多，要勤擦澡，维持皮肤正常的排泄功能，避免盆浴，沐浴后应尽快擦干水分、吹干头发；夏天要勤洗澡，保持皮肤干净，以免生痱子和疖子。
（2）注意会阴部卫生。产后子宫腔内胎盘剥离的伤口、子宫颈口的开放、阴道会阴的裂伤，为细菌侵入及繁殖创造了有利条件。因此，产后一定要注意会阴部清洁，每天要用温开水清洗2次，大便后也应擦洗。卫生纸及卫生垫要勤换。42天内不洗盆浴及不进行房事，以免发生月子病。
（3）活动和休息。正常产后24小时内应卧床休息，24小时后可根据情况起床活动，如洗漱、上厕所、喂奶等，这样做能减少大小便困难、促进子宫收缩、有利于子宫内瘀血的排出。此外，应保证每天10小时睡眠，以免影响乳汁分泌。
（4）保持大小便通畅。产后4小时应解小便，因为膀胱膨胀能影响子宫收缩及恶露排出，如膀胱胀得太久，小便会更困难。如果大便秘结，可多吃蔬菜，多下床活动，必要时在医生指导下服用一些药。
（5）居住环境。卧室要保持安静、清洁，温度适宜。空气新鲜。冬天要注意保温，不能吹冷风；夏日则要注意通风凉爽，衣着要适当，以防中暑。
（6）产后检查。产后满6周，必须回到接生的医院做产后检查，以便了解生殖器及身体恢复情况，如果发现异常，应及时处理，以免出现后遗症。

fields.title: 11～12个月：剖宫产妈妈的注意事项
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
剖宫产妈妈的产后恢复和自然产的妈妈有所不同。虽然随着手术技术的不断提高，剖宫产的伤口愈合越来越好，但是它毕竟是一个手术，产妇在身体恢复的坐月子期间，应必须十分注意术后伤口的恢复。
剖宫产的产妇，要特别注意以下几点：
（1）手术后产妇腹部的伤口会疼痛，但这种疼痛是可以忍受的，妈咪要做好一定的思想准备，对疼痛做些忍耐，少用止痛药物。如果疼痛难忍，就要请医生检查，是否腹壁有血肿。
（2）术后阴道会流血，其流血量不应超过月经量，过量者应报告医生，及时查找原因进行治疗，以免失血过多。
（3）在手术前后，医生会在产妇身上放置导尿管。导尿管一般在术后24～48小时且待膀胱肌肉恢复收缩排尿功能后拔掉，拔管后妈妈要尽量努力自行解小便，否则，再保留导尿管容易引起尿路感染。
另外，只要体力允许，在导尿管拔除后应尽早下床活动，并逐渐增加活动量，这样不仅可促进肠蠕动和子宫复归，还可避免术后肠黏连及血栓性静脉炎的形成。如感觉头晕、难受，应立即上床休息，谨防摔伤。
（4）腹部伤口通常在手术后7天拆线，拆线后咳嗽时要用手按压伤口两侧，防止震开伤口。
（5）手术后要特别注意卫生，除每日洗脸刷牙、饭前便后及哺乳前洗手外，还应保持伤口处的卫生。当然会阴部的卫生也不可忽视。
（6）手术后的饮食，可根据手术情况而定。术后第2天妈妈可以吃清淡的流质食物，如蛋汤、米汤，切忌进食牛奶、红糖水、豆浆、大量蔗糖等胀气食品；待排气后，则可进食半流质食物，如稀粥、汤面、馄饨等；稍后再恢复普通饮食。

fields.title: 11～12个月：产妇的膳食原则
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
多吃营养价值高的食物
孕妇分娩时，大量液体排出，如羊水、胎盘等，在生产过程中出汗较多，所以产后应多补充高热量的流质饮食，多喝汤水，以利促进身体恢复和促进乳汁的分泌。产妇一定要记住，产后所需营养并不比怀孕期间少。尤其要多吃含蛋白质、钙、铁比较丰富的食物，如牛肉、鸡蛋、牛奶、动物肝和肾，可以多吃豆类和豆制品，也可用猪骨头、猪蹄煮汤喝，因为其含钙较多。
增加餐次，少食多餐
新妈妈胃肠功能减弱，蠕动减慢，如果一次进食过多会增加胃肠负担，减弱胃肠道功能，过量的饮食还会让新妈妈体重增加，对产后恢复无益。
产妇每日餐次应比一般人多，以5～6次为宜。餐次增多有利于食物消化吸收，保证充足的营养。产后胃肠功能减弱，蠕动减慢，如一次进食过多过饱，反而增加胃肠负担，从而减弱胃肠功能。如采用多餐制则有利胃肠功能恢复，减轻胃肠负担。
食物干稀搭配
每餐食物应做干稀搭配。干者可保证营养的供给，稀者则可提供足够的水分。奶中含有大量水分，所以乳母哺乳需要大量补充水分，使乳汁便于分泌。产后失血伤津，也需要水分来促进母体的康复，还可防止产后便秘。食物中干稀搭配较之于单纯喝水及饮料来补充水分要好得多。因为食物的汤汁既有营养，又有开胃增进食欲的功能，而单纯饮水则反而冲淡胃液，降低食欲。可多喝营养丰富的下奶汤或粥，此外还可饮用果汁、牛奶等。
荤素搭配，避免偏食
在产后身体恢复及哺乳期间，食用产热高的肉类食物是必需的，但荤食过量不利于胃肠蠕动，影响消化。蛋白质及糖类的代谢必须有其他营养素的参与，过于偏食肉类食物反而会导致其他营养素摄入不足。
某些素食除含有肉食类食物不具有或少有的营养素外，一般含有大量纤维素，能促进胃肠蠕动，促进消化，防止便秘。
因此，广泛摄食各类食物，荤素搭配，既能保证营养均衡，促进食欲，又可预防疾病，且进食的品种越丰富，营养越平衡和全面。
清淡适宜
一般认为，月子里以饮食清（尽量不放调味料）淡（不放或少放食盐）为好，但此种观点并不正确。
从科学角度讲，月子里的饮食应清淡适宜，即调味料如葱、姜、大蒜、花椒、辣椒、酒等应少于一般人的量，食盐也以少放为宜，但并不是不放或过少。调味料除可增加食欲外，对产妇身体康复也是有利的。
注意调理脾胃
月子里应食用一些健脾开胃、促进消化、增进食欲的食物，如山药、山楂糕（片）、大枣、番茄等。山楂除开胃助消化外，还有促进子宫恢复等作用。

fields.title: 11～12个月：产后每日膳食营养素供给量
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content: 下表为我国营养学会推荐产褥期妇女每日膳食营养素的供给量。以轻体力劳动强度为例：

fields.title: 11～12个月：坐月子吃得越多越好吗
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
一般人都知道在“坐月子”期间应该加强营养，以恢复分娩时消耗的体力，并且要为宝宝提供高质量的乳汁，所以把好吃的东西统统拿出来，每顿都是猪蹄汤、鱼汤或大鱼大肉。其实，这个时期吃东西是很有学问的。坐月子期间食物并非吃得越多越好，应以补充充足的能量、高含量的蛋白质、适量的脂肪、丰富的无机盐、多样的维生素，以及充足的水分为原则。
能量是保证泌乳量的前提，热能不足将导致泌乳量减少40％～50％，食物应以奶制品、蛋类、肉类、豆制品、谷类、蔬菜为主，配合适量的油脂、糖、水果。食物应清淡、易于消化，烹调时应少用油炸油煎的方法，每餐应干稀搭配、荤素结合，少吃、不吃生冷或凉拌的食物，以免损伤脾胃，影响消化功能。产后虽不要忌口，但要注意不食辛辣之物，如辣椒、大蒜、酒、茴香等，以免引起便秘或痔疮发作。

fields.title: 11～12个月：剖宫产新妈妈饮食要注意
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
临床验证发现，剖宫产术后早进食利大于弊，无论术后胃肠蠕动的恢复还是乳汁的分泌都早于对照组，并且安全和顺利。
一方面进食本身的咀嚼运动可反射性引起胃肠蠕动，同时食物可直接刺激胃肠道，促进胃肠的运动功能增强，有利于产妇术后早排气。另一方面剖宫产术后早进食，有利于及时补充营养，不仅可促进产妇体力和精力能较快恢复，还可促进乳汁分泌，满足母乳喂养的需要。
因此，做剖宫手术的产妇，剖宫产术后6小时内，产妇应平卧、禁食。手术后约24小时胃肠功能恢复，应再给予术后流食1天，忌用牛奶、豆浆、大量蔗糖等胀气食品，情况好转后给予半流食1～2天，再转为普通膳食。个别产妇术后有排气较慢或身体不适，又无食欲者，可多吃一两天半流食，再给予普通饮食。

fields.title: 11～12个月：月子中的饮食禁忌
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
产后的饮食，中医古籍有种种禁忌：如“毋食冷硬物”、“毋食重浊、辛热、生冷”，“外薄五味、大冷、大热，谨节饮”……
产后的女性，体质较虚弱，中医认为这个阶段如果太多偏重味道过重的食物，容易增加母体自我调节与代谢的负担，以下这些食物，建议不宜多吃：
（1）忌食辛辣燥热之物
分娩中产妇大量失血、出汗，加之组织间液也较多地进入血循环，故机体阴津明显不足，而辛辣燥热食物均会伤津耗液，使产妇上火，口舌生疮，大便秘结或痔疮发作，而且会通过乳汁使婴儿内热加重。因此产后忌食韭菜、葱、大蒜、辣椒、胡椒、小茴香、酒、羊肉、狗肉、龙眼、荔枝、芒果、榴莲等。
（2）忌食不易消化及生冷、寒凉食物
产妇身体虚弱，运动量小，如吃硬食或油炸食物，容易造成消化不良。另外，产妇脾胃功能尚未完全恢复，过于寒冻的食物会损伤脾胃影响消化，且生冷之物易致瘀血滞留，可引起新妈妈腹痛、产后恶露不绝等。像冷饮品、西瓜、鸭梨、葡萄柚、柚子、橘子、山竹、莲藕、绿豆、白萝卜、西红柿、大白菜、苦瓜、黄瓜、丝瓜、冬瓜等都要注意少吃。
（3）忌食大麦及其制品
大麦及其制品，如大麦芽、麦乳精、麦芽糖等食物有回乳作用，所以产后仍在哺乳期的产妇应忌食。
（4）忌常饮茶
产妇在哺乳期间忌饮茶。因为茶内的咖啡因可通过乳汁进到婴儿腹中，引起婴儿肠痉挛。常饮茶的产妇哺育的宝宝经常无缘无故啼哭，就是这个原因。
（5）忌吃巧克力
产妇在产后需要给新生儿喂奶，如果过多食用巧克力，对哺乳婴儿的发育会产生不良的影响。这是因为巧克力所含的可可碱，会渗入母乳并在婴儿体内蓄积，能损伤神经系统和心脏，并使肌肉松弛，排尿量增加，结果会使婴儿消化不良，睡眠不稳，哭闹不停。

fields.title: 11～12个月：注意催乳饮食
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content: 乳汁的分泌量与乳母的营养有关。为使乳汁分泌充足，哺乳期的母亲不仅在“月子”里要重视营养，而且补充营养要贯穿在整个哺乳期。饮食应多样化，并多吃些奶类食物，不要忌口。经验证明，乳母在哺乳期经常进食鸡、鸭、鱼（鲫鱼）、肉、虾、猪蹄、排骨等熬煮的汤水，可以有效地起到促进乳汁分泌的作用。

fields.title: 11～12个月：产后运动的注意事项
fields.subtitle: 产后运动
fields.content:
由于受“坐月子”传统习惯的影响，许多人认为，产妇在月子里不应主动进行身体锻炼，而是应该卧床休息由他人照料生活，并尽量减少身体运动。其实，这种观念和做法有不科学的一面。
当然，产妇由于气血骤虚，确实需要充分的休息和充足的营养，但仅是注意健康和保养则显然不够，应在此基础上主动安排一些适当的身体运动，才能更好地促进产后恢复。产后整日卧床休息，会使产妇食欲减退、精神不振，并不利于子宫的恢复（复旧）和恶露的顺畅排出，易于导致日后子宫后位和腰酸不适。另外，如果不适量运动，产妇还常发生产后便秘，而经常便秘常导致腹压增大，由此使盆底组织松弛和子宫脱垂。
对正常经阴道分娩的产妇，一般经产后1～2天的充分卧床休息后，即可起床大小便和稍微坐、站、行。在产后2周左右，可做些轻便的家务和进行产褥保健操。产后40～50天，如体力恢复过程无异常，可恢复到如常人一样地进行日常活动。
产褥保健操应在得到医生、助产士的许可后，在他们指导下进行。要配合体力的恢复，从轻微的动作开始，渐渐地加大运动量。
做体操前应排尿、排便，在发烧时，饭后不要做，以不过度疲劳为限。要保持室内空气清新，保持愉快的心情。如果室内暖和，可少穿衣服。
需要注意的是，在整个产褥期间，不能过多地从事体力劳动，更不能经常挑、搬、抬、举重物，也不宜长时间站立或下蹲，以免引起盆底组织松弛和子宫脱垂。
何时开始做产褥保健体操
正常分娩的健康产妇，产后第二天可以下床活动，同时可开始做产褥操。体力衰弱、产程长、手术分娩的产妇，则应根据产妇的体质和恢复情况，安排做产褥操的时间及运动量。
产后发烧、大出血、严重心血管及肾脏疾病、会阴严重裂伤等产妇不适于做产褥操。如产妇在做操时出现明显心慌、气短、头晕现象，就要暂时停止锻炼，再慢慢地从轻微活动开始，逐渐增加到产妇能适应的程度，不要强求。
一般说来，产后运动分为2个阶段。
第一阶段：从产后3天到3个月，主要做一些轻松简单的动作。
运动项目：骨盆腔底部肌肉训练、腹部肌肉运动、腿部肌肉运动、胸部运动等。我们建议最好在床上做，从最简单的运动做起，根据自己的身体状况决定运动量的大小，以不累不痛为原则。如果是剖宫产，则需要推迟运动的时间，一般根据医生的指示，在伤口愈合良好之后再进行适量的运动。
第二阶段：从3个月到6个月，可开始增加运动量。
运动项目：最好进行全身肌肉力量的恢复训练，并加强腹部和骨盆腔底部肌肉锻炼，运动量还是根据个人体能状况而定。

fields.title: 11～12个月：产褥保健体操这样做
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
产褥体操具体做法可以按产后日期进行，如第一天适合做哪项，第二天适合做哪项，逐日推延。
第一体操
产妇第一体操，适用于产后第一天做。第一体操可以在分娩后8小时开始做。这个体操对于子宫恢复到正确的位置很有效。其方法如下：
（1）头离开枕头，俯卧，脸朝一侧。这个动作持续1分钟左右，习惯后可持续20分钟。早晚各做一次。
（2）如果按上述要求，却做得辛苦的话，可以在前胸抱住枕头垫着胸部，两膝向两侧张开，手交叉放在下巴下，这时会感觉舒服些。
第二体操
第二体操适合于产后第二天做。分娩24小时后可进行第二体操。第二体操主要是恢复因分娩而变松弛的局部肌肉，预防尿失禁或尿闭塞。其方法如下：
（1）首先，应完成第一体操。
（2）将身体翻过来，直直地仰卧，两手掌紧贴身体伸直，平静地呼吸；两手掌张开，手臂水平地伸开呈十字形状；用力呼吸，两手臂伸到头上，两手掌合并，身体呈一直线姿势；屏住气，然后呼气，手臂又恢复到水平状态。
（3）用腹肌做几次腹式呼吸。
（4）在阴道和肛门处用力，一收一放，做收缩动作。这个动作可以单独地做几次。
做上述动作之前都是以深呼吸为主的上体运动。
第三体操
第三体操在产后第五天以后做。这组体操动作主要是进行肌肉锻炼，算是运动量较大的动作。需要注意的是：如果做这个体操动作时，用手撑住木床来帮助腿的上举，那么效果就不太好了。在产后5～10天，应坚持做这个体操。其方法如下：
（1）先做第一、第二体操。
（2）仰卧，一只腿笔直地向上慢慢地运动到与身体成直角，然后慢慢放下，腿不能弯曲，反复几次；接着换另一只腿重复上面的动作，反复做几次。
（3）和上面的动作要领相同，这次两腿同时上举后放下。这个动作难度较大，开始做时，可以稍微离开床，慢慢练习举得更高。
第四体操
第四体操适合在产后第10天以后做。这组体操动作是为了矫正子宫的位置，通过上身的活动，增加肌肉的活力，是运动量较大的动作，产妇应根据自己身体状况来进行。其方法如下：
（1）先做第一、第二、第三体操。
（2）胸朝下，腰抬高，两膝距离30厘米宽左右，胸伏床上。
（3）在床上进行四肢爬行。
（4）仰卧，两手臂放在头顶伸直；手伸直，上身抬起，手接着伸向脚尖方向；抱住脚尖和脚踝不动，过一会儿，手向上举，回到开始的姿势；反复上述动作，多做几次。
第五体操
第五体操适宜在产后1个月以后做。其方法如下：
（1）立正姿势，上身向前并向下弯曲5次左右，腿不能弯曲。
（2）上半身躺在床上，膝弯曲，左右运动5次左右。
（3）立正姿势，提起脚后跟12次左右，脚尖着地。

fields.title: 11～12个月：剖宫产妈妈的运动
fields.subtitle: 日常护理
fields.content:
为避免伤口疼痛或不小心扯裂，剖宫产妇女产后的复原操，最初是以呼吸为主，等到伤口愈合之后，再进行较大动作的肢体伸展。
产后深呼吸运动
（1）仰躺床上，两手贴着大腿，将体内的气缓缓吐出。
（2）两手往体侧略张开平放，用力吸气。
（3）一面吸气，一面将手臂贴着床抬高，与肩膀呈一直线。
（4）两手继续上抬，至头顶合掌，暂时闭气。
（5）一面吐气，一面把手放在脸上方，做膜拜的姿势。
（6）两手慢慢往下滑，手掌互扣尽可能下压，同时吐气，吐完气之后，双手放开回复原姿势，反复做5次。
下半身伸展运动
（1）仰躺，双手手掌相扣，放在胸上。
（2）右脚不动，左膝弓起。
（3）将左腿尽可能伸直上抬，之后换右脚，重复做5次。
腹腰运动
（1）平躺床上，旁边辅助的人以左手扶住产妇的颈下方。
（2）辅助者将产妇的头抬起来，此时产妇暂时闭气，再缓缓吐气。
（3）辅助者用力扶起产妇的上半身，产妇在过程中保持吐气。
（4）产妇上半身完全坐直，吐气休息，接着再一面吸气，一面慢慢由坐姿回到原来的姿势，重复做5次。
骨盆运动
（1）仰躺，屈膝，脚掌贴于地面。一只手置于背部，同时感觉到轻微的空隙。
（2）深吸气，随后再慢慢吐气，同时将背部的肌肉平贴地板，压在手上。
（3）保持动作数4下，然后放松，重复数次，使肌肉的力量增强。
练习要点
要深呼吸，而其重点在于呼气。在吐气的时候，用双手或枕头护住伤口。维持膝盖的弯曲，同时试着在吐气的时候，做一个轻咳的动作，而不是做一个正常的咳嗽，否则会引起疼痛。
腿部运动
（1）坐在床上，脚趾向前伸展。将脚趾往上扳，然后再把脚趾往下推。此连续动作做大约20次，迅速移动，使血液循环加快。
（2）双脚同时往相同的方向移动，或一只脚往上，一只脚往下地运动。接着，张开双脚，同时做脚踝的环绕运动，首先要顺时针环绕，然后再逆时针环绕。
（3）压紧膝盖，贴着床面，然后再放松。
（4）一次弯曲一只脚，将脚跟在床上滑动，然后在换膝盖弯曲的时候，伸直另一只脚。

0～1岁婴儿带给父母的是甜蜜的烦恼：甜蜜者，宝宝带给父母的喜悦难以言表；烦恼者，宝宝尚不能开口说话，照顾宝宝时，各种问题会让父母不知所措，有一种爱很多，却无法给予的感觉。
本书针对新手爸妈这一迫切需要，结合婴儿不同月龄的发育特点，介绍了饮食喂养、日常护理、常见疾病防治、早教开发等内容，提供给父母们不知道的、想知道的、应该知道的婴儿护理知识。

fields.title: 野天鹅
fields.subtitle: 爱可以战胜一切困难
fields.subtitle_en: Love Can Overcome All Obstacles
fields.content:
在遥远的地方住着一个国王，国王有11个英俊的儿子，还有一个美貌的女儿，女儿名叫艾丽莎。他们与继母——新王后一起生活。新王后非常恶毒，她视这11个王子和艾丽莎为眼中钉，最后她把王子们变成了11只野天鹅，让他们在海的另一边的国家里生活。艾丽莎并不知道哥哥们已经变成了野天鹅，只是很想他们，就偷偷跑出王宫去找他们。
艾丽莎跑到森林里，遇到一位老太婆，老太婆告诉她曾看到11只野天鹅。艾丽莎认定那就是哥哥们。按照老太婆的指点，艾丽莎一路找到了海边。太阳快要落山的时候，海面上飞来了11只野天鹅。当太阳落下时，11只野天鹅变成了人，他们正是她的哥哥们。
哥哥们告诉艾丽莎，他们每天只要太阳升起就要变成野天鹅在天上飞，太阳落山时变成人再落到地面上，每年只能回来一次。
他们必须回去了，可是又不愿意离开艾丽莎，就花了整整一夜时间，用结实的芦苇编了一张又大又结实的网，把艾丽莎放在网上。他们还放上浆果和可以吮吸出汁液的青草，然后在太阳升起的时候，用嘴衔着网带着艾丽莎飞往他们住的国家。当太阳直射到艾丽莎的时候，有一只天鹅就飞到她的头上，用宽大的翅膀把阳光挡住。
艾丽莎做了一个梦：曾经在森林里遇到的老太婆告诉她，如果她用荨麻编织11件披甲给哥哥们披上，哥哥们身上的魔法就能解除。11件披甲需要一年时间完成，她必须亲自做每一件，并且不能说一句话，要不然就会威胁到哥哥们的性命。
艾丽莎来到哥哥们所住的山洞之后便开始采集荨麻。荨麻上的刺扎了她的手，就像被火烫一样疼。她的手还起了许多泡，但是艾丽莎不在乎，她一定要救哥哥们。哥哥们知道艾丽莎是为自己受苦，都很心疼，眼泪流到艾丽莎手上，她的手就不疼了。她加紧编织披甲，整夜整夜地工作。
一天，一群猎人来到洞里，其中有一个是国王。他喜欢上了艾丽莎，想把她带回宫中，娶她做王后。艾丽莎愁眉不展，但不说话，她一心只想把披甲编好。
不过，国王为了让她高兴，把她放在洞中的披甲和一些荨麻运到了宫中。于是她又能编织了。那些荨麻用完之后，她就每天晚上到教堂的墓地上去采集。尽管墓地上的吸血鬼让她很害怕，但她还是硬着头皮每天都去。她终于被大主教发现了。大主教看她每天晚上都到墓地去，以为她是巫婆，就报告给了国王。国王悄悄跟踪后也相信了，以为她跟墓地上那些吸血鬼是一样的。于是，国王下令，把她押进了地窖中。她仍然一句话都没有说。国王还命令扒下了她美丽的衣服，只把那些披甲和荨麻扔给她。这真让艾丽莎高兴，她整夜整夜地编织着披甲。
第二天艾丽莎要被处死了。艾丽莎不怕死，但很担心披甲编不完，于是更加努力地编织。刽子手把她押到囚车上。在押往刑场的路上她仍然不停地在编织。哥哥们飞来围在她的四周。
披甲还没有完全编好，可刽子手就要处死她了。艾丽莎赶忙把11件披甲扔向空中。穿上披甲的哥哥们马上变成了王子，只是最小的哥哥还有一只胳膊是天鹅的翅膀，因为那件披甲还没有最后完成。
艾丽莎终于可以开口说话了，她和王子们向国王讲述了事情的来龙去脉。国王感动了，他又让艾丽莎做了他的王后。
（选自《安徒生童话》）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Wild Swans

In a land far away, there lived a king who had eleven handsome sons and one beautiful daughter named Eliza. They lived together with their stepmother, the new queen. She was very cruel, and she hated the eleven princes and little Eliza so much that she turned the princes into eleven wild swans and sent them to live on the other side of the sea. Eliza did not know her brothers had been changed. She missed them terribly, so she quietly ran out of the palace to find them.

Eliza ran all the way to the forest, where she met an old woman. The old woman told her that she had seen eleven wild swans. Eliza knew they must be her brothers. Following the old woman's guidance, she traveled until she reached the seashore. Just as the sun was setting, eleven wild swans came flying over the water. When the sun dipped below the horizon, the swans transformed into men—her eleven brothers!

They told Eliza that every day, when the sun rises, they must fly through the sky as wild swans, and when the sun sets, they turn back into humans and land on the ground. They could only return home once a year.

They had to go back, but they did not want to leave Eliza. So they spent the whole night weaving a strong net from tough reeds. They placed Eliza gently inside and put berries and grass that could be squeezed for juice. When the sun rose, they carried the net in their beaks and flew with Eliza to the land where they lived. As the sun shone directly on Eliza, one of the swans would fly above her and spread his wide wings to shade her.

That night, Eliza dreamed. In the dream, the old woman from the forest told her that if she could knit eleven cloaks from stinging nettles and throw them over her brothers, the magic would be broken. It would take a whole year to make all eleven cloaks, and she must work on every one of them herself. She must not speak a single word, or else her brothers' lives would be in danger.

After arriving at the cave where her brothers lived, Eliza began to gather stinging nettles. The stings burned her hands like fire, and blisters formed all over them. But Eliza did not care. She was determined to save her brothers. Her brothers knew she was suffering for their sake, and their tears fell onto her hands. Wherever their tears touched, the pain went away. She worked harder, weaving the cloaks through the long nights.

One day, a group of hunters came to the cave, and among them was a king. He fell in love with Eliza and wanted to bring her back to his palace to marry her. Eliza looked worried, but she said nothing. All she cared about was finishing the cloaks.

Still, the king wanted to cheer her up. He had the unfinished cloaks and some of the nettles from the cave transported to the palace so she could keep weaving. When the nettles ran out, she went every night to the churchyard to gather more. Even though the ghosts there terrified her, she forced herself to go each time. Finally, the archbishop noticed her. Seeing her go to the graveyard every night, he thought she was a witch and told the king. The king secretly followed her and began to believe it too. He ordered that Eliza be thrown into the dungeon. Still, she did not say a word. The king also had her beautiful clothes taken away, giving her only the cloaks and nettles to continue her work. This made Eliza happy, and she wove through many sleepless nights.

The next day, Eliza was to be executed. She was not afraid of death, but she worried that the cloaks would not be finished, so she worked even faster. The executioner led her into a cart. Even on the way to the scaffold, she did not stop weaving. Her eleven brothers came flying and circled around her.

The cloaks were not yet quite complete when the executioner was ready. Quickly, Eliza threw all eleven cloaks into the air. As her brothers put them on, they turned back into princes. Only the youngest brother still had a swan's wing on one arm, because that last cloak was not quite finished.

At last, Eliza could speak. She and the princes told the king everything that had happened. The king was deeply moved, and he made Eliza his queen.

(From Hans Christian Andersen's Fairy Tales)
fields.tips: 即将为人母的准妈妈有时候会担心自己做不好一个妈妈，其实只要有爱心，像艾丽莎爱哥哥们一样，一切都不在话下。要相信自己会是一个好妈妈，不要整天杞人忧天地担心这担心那，否则会让胎宝宝不安的。
fields.tips_en: Sometimes, expecting mothers worry about whether they'll be good enough as a parent. But as long as there is love—just like Elisa loved her brothers—there is nothing you cannot face. Believe in yourself. Worrying endlessly won't help, and it may even unsettle your little one.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 青蛙王子
fields.subtitle: 帮助别人就是帮助自己
fields.subtitle_en: Helping Others Is Helping Yourself
fields.content:
在遥远的古代有一个国王，他有好几位公主，其中小公主最漂亮，也最善良，连太阳都喜欢她，看见她就向她洒下万道金光。
小公主喜欢到森林里的一口井边玩耍。这一天，天气非常凉爽，她又到井边来玩儿了，手里还拿着她最喜欢的小金球。她坐在井台上，手里拿着金球，抛上抛下，玩得正高兴时，突然，一只小鸟快速飞了过来，直奔小公主的脸而去。小公主急忙转头避开，一不小心，手里的金球掉到井里去了。
金球是小公主最喜欢的玩具，可是井那么深，该怎么办呢？小公主站在井台边难过地哭了起来。小公主哭呀哭呀，谁都安慰不了她。哭得正伤心时，一只青蛙跳出来说，他能帮助小公主到井底把金球捡上来。小公主很高兴地感谢青蛙，对青蛙承诺道：“你要是能帮我把小金球捡上来，我愿意给你任何报酬，我的衣服、我的珍宝，还有我的金冠，只要你要，都可以给你。”但是这些青蛙都不要，他说：“您的衣服、珍宝，还有金冠，我都不需要，我只想得到你的爱，就像你爱你的朋友一样。我捡到金球，你要亲吻我一下。”小公主一口答应了。青蛙一蹦就跳到井底去了，没一会儿金球真的被捡上来了。
小公主捡起金球，却犹豫着不肯亲吻青蛙，因为青蛙看上去滑溜溜的，一点儿都不可爱。但是青蛙恳求道：“求求您，只要您肯吻我，我身上的咒语就可以解除。”小公主想到自己能帮他解除咒语，就心软了。她弯腰捧起青蛙，真的亲吻了他。一眨眼的工夫，青蛙变成了一个王子，长得亲切又迷人，他身上的咒语被解除了。
青蛙爱上了善良的小公主。后来他们结婚，永远幸福地生活在一起了。
（选自《格林童话》）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Frog Prince**

Long, long ago, there was a king who had several daughters. The youngest princess was the most beautiful and the kindest, and even the sun loved her. Whenever he saw her, he would shine his golden rays down upon her.

The little princess loved to play by a well in the forest. One day, the weather was very cool, so she went to the well again, holding her favorite little golden ball. She sat by the edge of the well, tossing the golden ball up and down, having so much fun, when suddenly a little bird flew over quickly, heading straight for the princess's face. The little princess turned away in surprise, and oh no—her golden ball fell right into the deep well!

The golden ball was the princess's most treasured toy, and the well was so deep. What should she do? The little princess stood by the well and cried sadly. She cried and cried, and no one could comfort her. Just then, a frog hopped out and said he could help retrieve the golden ball from the bottom of the well. The princess was so happy and thanked the frog. She promised him, "If you can bring my little golden ball back, I will give you anything you want—my clothes, my treasures, and even my golden crown. Whatever you ask, it is yours." But the frog refused all of those things. He said, "I do not need your clothes, your treasures, or your golden crown. All I want is your love, just like the love you give your dear friends. When I bring back the golden ball, you must give me one little kiss." The princess gladly agreed. And with a single hop, the frog jumped into the well. Before long, he truly brought the golden ball back up.

The princess picked up her golden ball, but she hesitated and did not want to kiss the frog, for he looked slimy and not at all cute. But the frog gently begged, "Please, if you will only kiss me, the spell upon me will be broken." The princess thought about how she could help free him, and her heart softened. She bent down, held the frog gently in her hands, and gave him a sweet kiss. In the blink of an eye, the frog transformed into a prince—kind-looking and charming. The spell was broken!

The frog prince had fallen in love with the kind and gentle princess. They were married, and they lived happily ever after.

(Adapted from *Grimm's Fairy Tales*)
fields.tips: 孕妇常常是众人关注和帮助的对象，准妈妈得到帮助的时候，可以讲述给胎宝宝听。告诉他自己得到了怎样的帮助，这些帮助对自己有什么意义，希望胎宝宝将来也做一个乐于助人的孩子，毕竟帮助别人就是帮助自己。
fields.tips_en: Pregnant women are often the ones receiving care and support. When someone helps you, share the story with your baby. Tell them how you were helped, what it meant to you, and that you hope they, too, will grow up to be kind and generous. After all, helping others is a gift that returns to us.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 乌鸦喝水
fields.subtitle: 动脑筋战胜困难
fields.subtitle_en: Use Your Mind to Overcome Challenges
fields.content:
一只乌鸦口渴了，到处找水喝。它找了很久都没找到，越找越口渴。就在它渴得快要受不了的时候，突然看到沙砾堆上有一只玻璃瓶子，玻璃瓶子里有半瓶水呢。乌鸦很高兴，立刻一个俯冲来到瓶子边，一下子就把嘴伸到瓶口里了。可是瓶里的水太少了，乌鸦根本喝不到。乌鸦想把头也往里伸一伸，可是瓶口太小了，只容得下乌鸦的嘴进去。
怎么办呢，把瓶子推倒吧？瓶子里的水瞬间就会流出，渗入地下的，也喝不到。把瓶子砸烂吧？没有工具办不到。看着眼前的水喝不到嘴里，口渴的乌鸦急得团团转。转着转着，它看到了瓶子边上的小石子，哎，如果把小石子放到瓶子里，瓶子里的水不就会升高了吗？当小石子足够多的时候，瓶子里的水不就升到瓶口了吗？那样我就能喝到水了。乌鸦想到这里，立刻行动起来，一颗一颗地衔来小石子，放到瓶子里。眼看着瓶子里的水一点儿一点儿升高，乌鸦别提多高兴了。乌鸦越干越有劲儿。终于，当乌鸦把最后一颗小石子放入瓶中的时候，水就升到瓶口来了。乌鸦喝饱了水，终于解渴了。
（选自《伊索寓言》）
知识
lian
接
乌鸦是一种很聪明的鸟，在传说中，有“乌鸦反哺”的说法。据说乌鸦在母亲的哺育下长大后，当母亲年老体衰、不能觅食或者飞不动的时候，它的子女就四处去寻找食物，衔回来嘴对嘴地喂给母亲，回报母亲的养育之恩，并且从不感到厌烦，一直到老乌鸦临终，再也吃不下东西为止。
fields.content_en:
# The Crow and the Water Bottle

Once upon a time, a crow was very thirsty and looked everywhere for water. It searched for a long time but couldn't find any, and it became thirstier and thirstier. Just when the crow thought it couldn't bear the thirst anymore, it suddenly spotted a glass bottle on a pile of pebbles. Inside the bottle was half a bottle of water.

The crow was so happy and immediately swooped down to the bottle, stretching its beak right to the opening. But the water inside was too low, and the crow simply couldn't reach it. It tried pushing its head farther in, but the opening was too small — only its beak could fit through.

What should it do? If it tipped the bottle over, the water would spill out and sink into the ground, and it still wouldn't be able to drink. If it smashed the bottle, it had no tools to do that. Watching the water just out of reach, the thirsty crow spun around in circles, worried and restless. Then, as it paced back and forth, it noticed the little pebbles beside the bottle. Wait! It thought, what if I put the pebbles inside the bottle? Wouldn't the water level rise? When there were enough pebbles, wouldn't the water reach the top? Then I could finally drink!

The crow sprang into action right away, picking up one pebble at a time and dropping them into the bottle. Everyone could see the water rising little by little, and the crow was overjoyed. The more it worked, the more energy it had. Finally, when the crow dropped the very last pebble into the bottle, the water rose right to the top. The crow drank its fill and finally quenched its thirst.

*(Adapted from Aesop's Fables)*

Did you know? Crows are very clever birds. In folklore, there is a saying about crows showing gratitude to their parents. It is said that when a crow grows up after being raised by its mother, and her mother grows old, weak, can no longer find food, or can no longer fly, her young ones go out to find food and feed her directly from beak to beak. They never grow tired of caring for her, all the way until the old crow can no longer eat at all.
fields.tips: 准妈妈不妨找些益智游戏来，像九宫格、脑筋急转弯、猜谜等，孕期一定要多动动脑筋，想一想。准妈妈多动脑，胎宝宝脑筋也会灵活，并且有利于他养成爱动脑的习惯。
fields.tips_en: Why not find some fun brain games to enjoy during this special time? Try number puzzles, riddles, or clever word games. Keeping your mind active is wonderful for both you and your baby—a bright, thinking mom nurtures a bright, curious little one.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title_en: The Little Bear and the Red Shoes
fields.subtitle: 纯洁的友谊
fields.subtitle_en: A Pure and Gentle Friendship
fields.content:
咯噔，咯噔，什么声音这么清脆、这么好听。哟，原来是一个穿着红皮鞋的小姑娘在走路啊。她的鞋子好漂亮，红红的、亮亮的。小熊看见了，非常喜欢。
小熊一直跟在小姑娘后面跑，小姑娘并没发现它，只管咯噔、咯噔地走着。不一会儿，小姑娘走到了一个大水坑边上。她脱下鞋子，卷起裤管，去抓小虾。小熊轻轻跑过去，把红皮鞋套在脚上。哈哈，真好看啊！小熊舍不得脱下红皮鞋，自言自语地说：“小姑娘一定是不喜欢这鞋子了，要不，干吗把它扔在地上呢？她不要，我要。”小熊穿着红皮鞋，跑回家去了。
一天傍晚，小熊约大家一起去看表演。剧幕拉开了，台上有个小朋友在唱歌，歌声很动听。唱得真好呀！忽然，小熊愣住了，唱歌的小朋友正是那个穿红皮鞋的小姑娘。可这会儿，她的脚上没穿红皮鞋，穿的是一双很旧很旧的黑皮鞋。小熊看看自己脚上的红皮鞋，脸红了，比红皮鞋还要红。它脱下鞋子，跑上台，把它塞到小姑娘的手里就跑开了。
小姑娘又表演了跳舞，她跳啊跳啊，脚上的红皮鞋一晃一晃，闪着亮光，真是太漂亮了，太好看了！
回家的路上，小熊使劲地踩着地面，吧嗒、吧嗒地响着，就像穿着红皮鞋一样神气。
fields.content_en:
**Little Bear and the Red Shoes**

Click-clack, click-clack. What a nice, bright sound. Oh! It's a little girl walking in red shoes. Her shoes are so pretty — shiny and red. Little Bear saw them and loved them right away.

Little Bear trotted behind the little girl without her noticing. Before long, she came to a puddle, took off her shoes, rolled up her trousers, and went to catch little shrimp. Little Bear crept over and slipped the red shoes onto his paws. Wow, they looked wonderful! He didn't want to take them off. "She must not like these shoes," he said to himself. "Why else would she leave them there? She doesn't want them — but I do." And so Little Bear ran home wearing the red shoes.

One evening, everyone gathered to watch the show. The curtain rose, and there was a little one singing on stage — beautiful, clear notes. What a lovely song! Then Little Bear froze. The singer was the little girl who had worn the red shoes. But now her feet held no red shoes — only a pair of old, scuffed black ones. Little Bear looked down at the red shoes on his paws, and his face turned redder than the shoes themselves. He took them off, ran up to the stage, pressed them into her hands, and ran away.

Then the little girl danced. She danced and danced — the red shoes flashing and gleaming on her feet. So pretty, so beautiful!

On the way home, Little Bear stomped his paws on the ground as hard as he could — step-stomp, step-stomp — as proud and happy as if he were still wearing the red shoes himself.
fields.tips: 能有一双小小的红色皮鞋，是很多准妈妈童年时候的一个美丽梦想。在读这个故事的时候，准妈妈一定会想，肚子里的是女孩还是男孩呢？如果是女孩，就可以给她穿漂亮的红皮鞋了，看她跳舞，看她咯噔、咯噔地走路。如果是男孩，会不会和一个穿红皮鞋的小女孩做朋友呢。看看，宝宝的性别真是一件值得期待的美好事情啊。
fields.tips_en: Many mothers dreamed, as children, of owning a pair of little red shoes. While reading this story, you may wonder: will my baby be a girl or a boy? If a girl, you can dress her in pretty red shoes and watch her dance and patter along. If a boy, perhaps he'll make a sweet friend with a girl who wears red shoes. Isn't discovering your baby's little personality one of life's most beautiful expectations?
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小猫钓鱼
fields.subtitle: 做事应该专心致志
fields.subtitle_en: Focus Makes All the Difference
fields.content:
老猫和小猫一块儿在河边钓鱼。
一只蜻蜓飞来了，小猫看见了，放下钓鱼竿，就去捉蜻蜓。蜻蜓飞走了，小猫没捉着，空着手回到河边来。小猫一看，老猫钓着了一条大鱼。
一只蝴蝶飞来了，小猫看见了，放下钓鱼竿，又去捉蝴蝶。蝴蝶飞走了，小猫又没捉着，空着手回到河边来。小猫一看，老猫又钓着了一条大鱼。
小猫说：“真气人，我怎么连一条小鱼也钓不着？”
老猫看了看小猫，说：“钓鱼就钓鱼，不要这么三心二意的。一会儿捉蜻蜓，一会儿捉蝴蝶，怎么能钓着鱼呢？”
小猫听了老猫的话，就一心一意地钓鱼。
蜻蜓又飞来了，蝴蝶又飞来了，小猫就像没看见一样。不大一会儿，小猫也钓着了一条大鱼。
fields.content_en:
**The Little Cat Goes Fishing**

One day, an old cat and a little cat went fishing by the river together.

A dragonfly flew over. The little cat saw it, put down the fishing rod, and went to catch the dragonfly. But the dragonfly flew away, and the little cat caught nothing. It returned to the riverside with empty hands. When it looked over, the old cat had caught a big fish!

A butterfly flew over. The little cat saw it, put down the fishing rod again, and went to chase the butterfly. The butterfly flew away, and once more the little cat caught nothing. It came back empty-handed. The old cat had caught another big fish!

The little cat said, "I'm so upset! Why can't I catch even a small fish?"

The old cat looked at the little cat and said, "Just fish. Don't be so distracted. First chasing dragonflies, then chasing butterflies — how can you ever catch fish like that?"

The little cat listened to the old cat's words and fished with all its heart.

When a dragonfly flew by and a butterfly fluttered near, the little cat pretended not to see them at all. Soon enough, the little cat also caught a big fish.
fields.tips: 小猫三心二意的时候，一无所获，而它专心时，就钓到了大鱼。准妈妈做胎教也一样，如果很专心，在讲一个故事、听一首歌、欣赏一幅画时，将意念集中，想着胎宝宝，把胎教内容在脑海里形成画面，胎教效果会更好。
fields.tips_en: The little cat caught nothing when its attention wandered, but when it focused, it caught a big fish. The same is true for prenatal bonding: when you tell a story, listen to a song, or admire a painting, give your full attention. Picture your baby in your mind, pour your love into the moment, and your bond will blossom even more beautifully.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 三个好朋友
fields.subtitle: “齐心”还要“协力”
fields.subtitle_en: A United Heart Needs United Action
fields.content:
天鹅、虾和梭子鱼，它们三个是好朋友，经常互相帮忙。有一天，天鹅要送一辆车到城里去，虾和梭子鱼主动要求帮忙，天鹅很感激它们，接受了它们的好意。三个好朋友商定，在车子上绑上三根绳子，每人拉一根，三人之力肯定大于天鹅一人之力。于是它们在车上绑好了三根绳子。天鹅说：“我喊一二三，一起发力拉车。”梭子鱼和虾一起答应：“好！”于是每人拉起一根绳子做好了准备，只等天鹅喊“一二三”。
天鹅喊了：“一二三，开始！”它自己拉着一根绳子展翅向天空中飞去，虾只会往后蹦，所以拉了绳子向与天鹅相反的方向蹦去，梭子鱼却是拉住绳子蹦到池塘里使劲向水底游，它们拼尽全力，拉了好久，却发现车子根本没有动，更别提向城里前进了。而这时天鹅累得翅膀都要抬不起来了，虾憋得满脸通红，梭子鱼则全身发灰，没有半点儿力气了，所以只好先休息一下。
休息了一会儿，天也不早了，车子还是待在原地。于是三个好朋友互相打气，再试，试了好几次，然而结果还是一样，车子根本不动。没办法了，天鹅谢过两位好朋友，让它们先回家，以免因为自己的事耽误它们太多时间。两个朋友看自己也的确帮不了什么忙了，也就回家了。天鹅自己最后检查了一遍车子，觉得没有任何问题，就套上绳子又试了一下。哎，这次居然成功了，车子向着城里进发了。
天鹅边飞边想，终于想明白了，原来三个好朋友“齐心”了，却没有“协力”，三人合作并没有使力量增加，反而却互相抵消了。天鹅想：“下次碰到两个好朋友，一定要告诉它们这个道理。”
（选自《克雷洛夫寓言》 作者：克雷洛夫）
fields.content_en:
Title: Three Good Friends

A swan, a shrimp, and a pike were three good friends. They often helped each other. One day, the swan needed to take a cart to the city. The shrimp and the pike offered to help, and the swan gratefully accepted their kind offer.

The three friends decided to tie three ropes to the cart, one for each of them. They figured three pulling together would surely be stronger than just the swan alone. And so, they tied the ropes to the cart.

"Ready?" said the swan. "On the count of three, we pull together!"

The pike and the shrimp happily agreed, "Okay!" Each one grabbed their rope and got ready, waiting for the swan to call out the count.

"One… two… three, go!" called the swan. And off it flew into the sky, pulling its rope with all its might. But the shrimp could only hop backward, so it tugged the rope in the opposite direction from the swan. And the pike? It dragged its rope and plunged into the pond, swimming hard toward the bottom. They pulled and pulled with all their strength, but the cart simply would not move — not even an inch toward the city.

By then, the swan was so tired its wings could barely lift, the shrimp was bright red from straining, and the pike had gone pale and grey, completely spent. So they all decided to take a rest.

After a while, it was getting late, and the cart was still sitting right where it was. The three friends cheered each other on and tried again. And again. And again. But the result was always the same — the stubborn cart wouldn't budge.

At last, the swan thanked its two good friends and asked them to go home, so they wouldn't be kept up any longer because of its business. Seeing they truly couldn't help, the shrimp and the pike waved goodbye and headed home.

Left alone, the swan double-checked the cart. Everything seemed perfectly fine. It tied the rope again and gave it one more try. And this time — to its surprise — it actually worked! The cart began to roll toward the city.

Flying along, the swan finally understood. The three friends had been "united in heart," but they hadn't been "united in effort." Instead of combining their strength, they had cancelled each other out. The swan smiled to itself, thinking, "Next time, I'll make sure my two good friends understand this little lesson."

(From *Krylov's Fables* by Ivan Krylov)
fields.tips: 这个故事告诉我们，做事方法一定要得当，否则会适得其反，胎教也是如此。做胎教最忌做得太频繁，频繁做胎教会打扰宝宝的生长。一般每天做一两次，每次5～10分钟就足够了。
fields.tips_en: This story teaches us that the right approach matters—if we use the wrong method, we may end up working against our own goals. The same is true for prenatal education. The greatest mistake is doing it too frequently, as excessive stimulation can disturb your baby's growth. Once or twice a day, each session lasting just 5 to 10 minutes, is more than enough.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 等明天
fields.subtitle: 今天的事今天做
fields.subtitle_en: Today's Tasks Belong to Today
fields.content:
有一只小猴子住在一座美丽的树林里。这里有很多好玩儿的，它总也玩儿不够，开心得不行。只是一到下雨天，它就遭殃了。别人都有家，小松鼠有树洞，小刺猬有蘑菇似的大房子，只有小猴子无处可躲，总是被雨淋得像落汤鸡一样。终于，小猴子决定，要给自己盖一座大房子。房子要盖得高高的，还要装上大大的门窗，比其他任何小动物的房子都要美丽。它还决定，明天就动工。
第二天，小猴子想着盖房子，早早就起来了，又是搬木头，又是折芭蕉叶子，它在准备盖房子的材料。可是干了没一会儿，小猴子就感觉累了，便躺下休息。小猴子躺在树干上看着天空，心想：“天气这么好，还是先玩一会儿吧，房子等明天再盖。”这一天就在小猴子的玩耍中过去了。
又一个第二天来了，小猴子就没那么早起来了，它也不想去准备盖房子的材料，但不能什么都不做啊，它想那就先画个图样吧，涂涂改改终于画好了。小猴子拿着图样请小松鼠欣赏。小松鼠说：“这个房子好大、好漂亮呀！什么时候才能盖好呢？”小猴子说：“快，很快，明天就能盖好了。对了，我要请好朋友明天都来我的新房子里玩儿。现在就请去。”小猴子蹦蹦跳跳地走了。它请了大象，请了小白兔、小刺猬、青蛙、啄木鸟、长颈鹿等，就这样这一天又在小猴子请客当中过去了。
小猴子请好朋友来新房子玩儿的时间到了，好朋友们都来了，可是左瞧右看，不见新房子，而小猴子还在树上睡觉呢。大家都来叫小猴子，让它醒醒。可怎么叫它都不醒，小猴子正在做美梦呢。它梦到自己的新房子已经盖起来了，木头做的墙，芭蕉叶做的房顶，青草铺满地板，窗户明亮，很多朋友都来了，一起在房子里唱歌跳舞，好不开心。最后，小猴子是笑醒的。见小猴子醒来了，大家赶忙问它的新房子在哪里。但是小猴子没有马上回答，它还没有完全从好梦中清醒过来呢。发了一会儿呆，小猴子终于明白眼前的状况了，却说：“我的新房子明天才能盖好呢。你们明天再来吧。”小兔子不解地问：“今天不就是你昨天说的明天吗？怎么还要明天啊？”大象说：“明天还有明天呢，你就这样拖吧。”小松鼠则替它担心：“看下雨时，你往哪儿躲。”小猴子恼了，强词夺理说：“天气这么好，哪里会下雨？”可是很不凑巧，好好的天气突然就下起雨来了，大家各回各家，只有小猴子留在雨里，又被淋成了落汤鸡。
不知道这场雨有没有把小猴子浇醒，让它把这个“等明天”的毛病纠正一下，但愿它的好朋友都能等到那一天，到它的新房子里参观。
知识
lian
接
《等明天》这个故事最初是一部剪纸动画片的内容。剪纸动画片是我国特有的一种电影种类，借鉴了皮影戏和剪纸两种艺术形式。我国最早的一部剪纸动画片是《猪八戒吃西瓜》，拍摄于1985年，之后还有《葫芦兄弟》《人参王国》《济公斗蟋蟀》《山羊和狼》等多部。准妈妈不妨找来和胎宝宝一起看一看，一定别有一番感觉。
fields.content_en:
# Waiting for Tomorrow

Once upon a time, there was a little monkey who lived in a beautiful forest. There were so many fun things to play with, and he never got tired of them. He was so happy! But whenever it rained, he had a hard time. Everyone else had a home—the little squirrel had a tree hollow, and the little hedgehog had a big house like a mushroom. But the little monkey had nowhere to hide, and he always got soaked to the bone in the rain. Finally, the little monkey decided to build himself a big house. It would be tall, with big windows and doors, and more beautiful than any other animal's house. He also decided to start building the very next day.

The next day, the little monkey woke up early, thinking about building his house. He carried pieces of wood and folded banana leaves, getting all the materials ready. But after working for only a little while, he felt tired, so he lay down to rest. Lying on a tree trunk and looking at the sky, he thought, "The weather is so nice today. I should play a little first, and build the house tomorrow." So the day passed while the little monkey played.

Another "next day" came, and the little monkey didn't wake up quite so early. He didn't feel like preparing building materials either, but he couldn't do absolutely nothing. So he thought, "I'll just draw a picture of the house first." After drawing and erasing many times, he finally finished. The little monkey took his drawing to the little squirrel to admire. The little squirrel said, "This house is so big and so pretty! When will you finish building it?" The little monkey said, "Soon, very soon—it will be done tomorrow! Oh, by the way, I want to invite all my good friends to play in my new house tomorrow. Go ahead and invite them now." And off hopped the little monkey. He invited the elephant, the little white rabbit, the little hedgehog, the frog, the woodpecker, the giraffe, and many others. And so that day passed as well, while the little monkey was busy inviting everyone.

The time came for the little monkey to invite his good friends to his new house. All his friends arrived, but they looked here and there and couldn't find any new house. And the little monkey was still fast asleep in a tree! Everyone came to call to him, telling him to wake up. But no matter how they called, he wouldn't wake. The little monkey was having a sweet dream. In his dream, his new house was already built—walls made of wood, a roof made of banana leaves, a floor covered in green grass, bright windows, and lots of friends all came, singing and dancing together inside the house. It was so wonderful. In the end, the little monkey woke up laughing. When he finally woke, everyone quickly asked him where his new house was. But the little monkey didn't answer right away—he hadn't fully come out of his lovely dream yet. After dazing for a while, he finally realized what was going on, and said, "My new house won't be ready until tomorrow. Come back tomorrow, everyone." The little rabbit asked in confusion, "Isn't today the tomorrow you talked about yesterday? Why do you need another tomorrow?" The elephant said, "There's always another tomorrow. You just keep pushing it off." The little squirrel worried for him and said, "Just think about where you'll hide when it rains again." But the little monkey grew angry and made excuses, saying, "The weather is so nice—how could it possibly rain?" But as luck would have it, the fine weather suddenly turned and it began to rain! Everyone went back to their own homes, and the little monkey was left standing in the rain, getting soaked to the bone once again.

I wonder if this rain woke the little monkey up, so he can correct his habit of always "waiting for tomorrow." Let's hope his good friends get to enjoy that day someday, when they can visit his new house.

---

**About the Story**

This story, *Waiting for Tomorrow*, originally came from a traditional Chinese paper-cut animation. Paper-cut animation is a special kind of film made in China, inspired by both shadow puppetry and paper-cut art. China's first paper-cut animation was *Pigsy Eats a Watermelon*, made in 1985. Since then, many others have followed, such as *Calabash Brothers*, *Kingdom of Ginseng*, *Jigong Battles the Cricket*, and *The Goat and the Wolf*. A expecting mother might enjoy finding one of these charming films to share with her little one in her tummy—it would be a lovely experience for us both.
fields.tips: 准妈妈如果做了胎教计划，就要天天照着计划进行，不要只做计划不执行，永远等明天，那样胎教的效果永远出不来，像小猴子的房子似的永远见不着。
fields.tips_en: If you've made a prenatal education plan, please follow it every day. Don't create beautiful plans and then never carry them out, always waiting for tomorrow. Otherwise, the benefits of prenatal education will never come to light—just like the little monkey's house, it remains forever out of reach.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 狐狸和乌鸦
fields.subtitle: 不要轻信花言巧语
fields.subtitle_en: Do Not Be Fooled by Sweet Words
fields.content:
森林里有棵好大好大的树，树上住着一只乌鸦。树下有个洞，洞里住着一只狐狸。
一天，乌鸦叼来一块肉，站在树上休息，被狐狸看到了。狐狸垂涎欲滴，很想从乌鸦嘴里得到那块肉。由于乌鸦在树枝上嘴里叼着肉，所以狐狸没有办法得到。对肉垂涎三尺的狐狸不肯轻易放弃。它眼珠一转说：“亲爱的乌鸦，您好吗？”乌鸦没有回答。狐狸只好赔着笑脸又说：“亲爱的乌鸦，您的孩子好吗？”乌鸦看了狐狸一眼，还是没有回答。狐狸摇摇尾巴，第三次说话了：“亲爱的乌鸦，您的羽毛真漂亮，麻雀比起您来就差远了。您的嗓子真好，谁都爱听您唱歌，您就唱几句吧？”乌鸦听了非常得意。它想：“说我嗓子好，爱听我唱歌的只有你狐狸，我就给你唱一首吧。”于是乌鸦就高兴地唱了起来。可它刚一张嘴，肉就从嘴里掉了下去。狐狸叼起肉就钻到洞里去了，只留下乌鸦在那里“歌唱”。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Fox and the Crow

In the forest there stood a very, very big tree. A crow lived high up in that tree. And down below, there was a little hole in the ground, where a fox made his home.

One day, the crow brought a piece of meat and perched on a branch to rest. The fox saw it from below. His mouth watered, and he really, really wanted that piece of meat. But because the crow sat on a branch with the meat in her beak, the fox couldn't reach it. The fox didn't want to give up so easily. Then an idea came to him. He rolled his eyes and said, "Dear Crow, how are you today?" The crow said nothing. So the fox tried again with a smiling face, "Dear Crow, are your babies well?" The crow glanced at the fox but still didn't say a word. The fox wagged his tail and spoke a third time, "Dear Crow, your feathers are so beautiful! The sparrow is nothing compared to you. And your voice is wonderful — everyone loves to hear you sing. Just sing a little for me?" The crow felt so pleased. She thought, "Only this fox says he loves my singing. All right, I'll sing for him." So the crow happily began to sing. But the moment she opened her beak, the meat fell right out. The fox caught the meat and darted back into his hole, leaving the crow all alone, still singing.
fields.tips: 乌鸦不能理性认识自己，不能理性认识狐狸，让自己遭受了损失。准妈妈对待胎教，一定要有一个理性的态度，胎教的目的不是培养神童，而是让腹中的胎宝宝感受到更多的爱，在出生后性格更完美，心理更健康。
fields.tips_en: The crow suffered loss because she couldn't see herself and the fox clearly. As an expectant mother, please keep a rational attitude toward prenatal education. The purpose is not to raise a genius, but simply to let your baby feel more love while in the womb—so that after birth, your child may have a well-balanced personality and a healthier heart and mind.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 狮子和老鼠
fields.subtitle: 不小看别人，不妄自菲薄
fields.subtitle_en: Never Look Down on Others, Nor Doubt Yourself
fields.content:
在一片广袤的大草原上，住着一只狮子，也住着一只老鼠。一天，老鼠外出觅食，尽管已经十分小心了，可还是中了机关，被捕鼠器逮住了。小老鼠太害怕了，急得吱吱乱叫，一点儿办法都没有。恰好此时狮子经过，狮子不费吹灰之力就把小老鼠救了出来。小老鼠很感激，对狮子说：“谢谢你救了我，我一定会报答你的。”狮子感到很好笑，摸着老鼠的头笑着说：“好了，你那么小，能帮我什么啊？”但小老鼠仍然坚持说：“我一定能帮到你的。”说完就走了。
过了几天，狮子也中了机关，落入了猎人的捕兽网中，无论如何挣扎都无济于事。正当狮子绝望地停止挣扎的时候，听到狮子吼叫声的小老鼠赶来了。小老鼠安慰狮子说：“别着急，我来帮你了。”狮子沮丧地说：“你这么小，怎么帮我啊？”小老鼠二话不说，就用牙齿开始咬捕兽网，不一会儿还真咬开一个大口子，把狮子放了出来。狮子很高兴，握着老鼠的手说：“谢谢你，是你救了我。”紧接着，它又不好意思地说：“对不起，我不该小看你。”
（选自《伊索寓言》）
fields.content_en:
# The Lion and the Mouse

On a vast grassy plain, there lived a lion and a mouse. One day, the mouse was out looking for food. Even though she was being very careful, she stepped into a trap and got caught in a mousetrap. The little mouse was so scared that she squeaked and cried, not knowing what to do at all. Just then, the lion walked by. With no effort at all, the lion saved the little mouse. The mouse was very grateful and said to the lion, "Thank you for saving me. I will definitely repay you someday." The lion thought it was funny and, patting the mouse on the head, smiled and said, "Oh, you are so tiny. What could you ever do to help me?" But the little mouse still insisted, "I will be able to help you!" And with that, she ran off.

A few days later, the lion also fell into a trap set by hunters. He was caught in a big net and no matter how he struggled, he could not get free. Just as the lion was giving up and stopping his struggles in despair, the little mouse, who had heard the lion's loud roar, came running as fast as she could. She comforted the lion and said, "Don't worry! I'm here to help you!" The lion said sadly, "You are so small. How can you possibly help me?" But the little mouse didn't say another word. She simply began biting the net with her teeth. Before long, she had bitten a big hole right through it and freed the lion. The lion was overjoyed and took the mouse's paw and said, "Thank you. You saved me." Then he added shyly, "I'm sorry. I should never have looked down on you."
fields.tips: 准妈妈要像小老鼠一样自信，相信自己的胎教一定有益于宝宝，这样才能把胎教坚持下去。另外，不要像狮子小看老鼠那样，小看准爸爸的作用，准爸爸可是胎教的主力军啊。胎宝宝喜欢听准爸爸的声音，要让准爸爸积极参与到胎教中来。
fields.tips_en: Be confident like the little mouse and trust that your prenatal education will benefit your baby—that belief is what will keep you going. And please don't look down on the father-to-be, as the lion once looked down on the mouse. He is a key player in prenatal education! Babies love hearing their father's voice, so make sure he is actively involved.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 龟兔赛跑
fields.subtitle: 骄傲使人落后
fields.subtitle_en: Pride Leads to Falling Behind
fields.content:
兔子长着四条腿，乌龟也长着四条腿，兔子跑起来飞快，一溜烟儿就看不见了，可乌龟爬起来却很慢。兔子就常常嘲笑乌龟，有时候还刺激他说：“乌龟，咱们来比赛吧。说不定能激发你奔跑的潜能呢！”乌龟从来不理会兔子这些无聊的挑衅，自己该干什么还干什么。
但是，后来兔子编出了一个故事到处宣传，说它看到乌龟早上出门采花去，到了晚上看到乌龟在门口，以为乌龟采花回来了，没想到是刚爬到门口。这个故事在小动物们中间传来传去，沸沸扬扬，最后传到乌龟的耳朵里。乌龟终于生气了，它去找兔子。乌龟跟兔子说：“兔子，咱们来比赛，如果我赢了你，你就要跟我公开道歉、辟谣。”兔子不以为然地说：“比就比，我还能输给你？你爬得慢是大家都知道的。”
第二天早上，比赛从小河边开始了，终点是山脚下的一棵大树。燕子在起点发完起跑口令，就飞到大树那边了。那里有很多小动物，它们都是乌龟和兔子邀请来的，来见证比赛结果。
燕子的起跑口令一发完，兔子撒腿就跑，果真跑得非常快，一会儿就跑远了。兔子跑了一段回头一看，乌龟爬得真慢啊，才爬出一小段。兔子想：“乌龟爬得这么慢，我先睡一觉吧，睡一觉都能赢它。”兔子果然就在路边睡着了。乌龟也感觉很累，想休息一下，可是它知道自己爬得慢，只有坚持才有可能赢，就继续埋头向前爬去。当乌龟爬到兔子身边的时候，兔子还在睡觉呢。乌龟继续爬啊、爬啊，终点越来越近，一步、两步，马上就到终点了。这时兔子睡醒了，它想乌龟肯定还在后面呢，就朝后看去，可朝后一看没看到乌龟，就急忙向前看去，哎呀不得了，乌龟就快到终点了。兔子撒开腿赶紧追，可是再怎么追也无济于事了，乌龟还是首先到达了终点。
兔子不得已当着大伙的面向乌龟道了歉，并且承认采花的事是自己编出来的，是个谎言，让大家不要再提起了。
（选自《伊索寓言》）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Tortoise and the Hare

The rabbit has four legs, and the tortoise has four legs too. The rabbit can run very fast—one moment he is there and the next he is gone like a wisp of smoke. But the tortoise climbs along so slowly. The rabbit often laughed at the tortoise and sometimes even teased him, saying, "Tortoise, let's have a race! Maybe it will help you discover your hidden speed!" But the tortoise never paid any attention to the rabbit's silly provocation. He just went about his own business as usual.

Later, though, the rabbit made up a story and told it everywhere. He said that in the morning he saw the tortoise go out to pick flowers, and in the evening he saw the tortoise at the door and thought he had come back with flowers—but actually the tortoise had only just crawled to the door! The story spread all through the little animal community until it finally reached the tortoise's ears. The tortoise was truly angry at last. He went to find the rabbit and said, "Rabbit, let us have a race. If I win, you must apologize to everyone publicly and tell the truth about those flowers." The rabbit said carelessly, "Fine, let's race. How could I possibly lose to you? Everyone knows you crawl so slowly."

The next morning, the race began by the little river, and the finish line was a big tree at the foot of the hill. The swallow gave the starting signal at the starting point and then flew over to the big tree. Many little animals were already there—they had been invited by both the tortoise and the rabbit to witness the result of the race.

As soon as the swallow's signal rang out, the rabbit took off running. He really did run very fast and soon disappeared into the distance. After running a while, the rabbit looked back and saw how slowly the tortoise was crawling—he had only moved a tiny bit. The rabbit thought, "The tortoise crawls so slowly. I'll just take a nap first. Even a nap won't stop me from winning!" And indeed, the rabbit fell asleep right by the roadside. The tortoise also felt very tired and wanted to rest. But he knew he crawled slowly, and only by keeping going might he have a chance to win. So he continued to bow his head and crawl forward. When the tortoise finally reached the rabbit, the rabbit was still fast asleep. The tortoise kept on crawling and crawling. The finish line drew nearer and nearer—one step, two steps, almost there. At that moment, the rabbit woke up. He thought the tortoise must still be far behind, so he looked back. But he couldn't see the tortoise anywhere! He quickly looked forward—and oh no! The tortoise was almost at the finish line! The rabbit sprang to his feet and ran as fast as he could, but it was no use. The tortoise crossed the finish line first.

Reluctantly, the rabbit apologized to everyone in front of all the little animals and admitted that the story about picking flowers was made up—a lie—and asked everyone not to talk about it anymore.

(Based on Aesop's Fables)
fields.tips: 有好的胎教方法、胎教计划，还要坚持做下去，这需要一定的耐力。千万不能像兔子一样，空有好本事，因为无法坚持，最终没能成功。
fields.tips_en: Having good prenatal education methods and a thoughtful plan is wonderful, but the real key is to keep at it steadily—it takes patience and perseverance. Don't be like the hare, who had all the ability but could not stick with it, and in the end, failed to succeed.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 猴子捞月
fields.title_en: The Monkeys Fishing for the Moon
fields.subtitle: 美丽因为分享而更有价值
fields.subtitle_en: Beauty Becomes More Precious When Shared
fields.content:
已经很晚了，但月色很好，把大地照得一片光明，所以猴子们都没有睡觉，还在山上玩耍。突然一只猴子指着天空中的月亮跟大家说：“我们把月亮摘下来玩儿吧。”“好主意。”大家齐声叫好。可是月亮高高在上，猴子们根本没办法摘到，只好悻悻作罢，又去玩儿别的了。
正玩儿着，突然听到一只猴子高兴地大叫：“大家快来看，月亮掉到井里了。”猴子们围上来一看，可不是吗？圆圆的、明亮的月亮正在井里呢。
猴子们再一商量，决定下井去捞。于是一个拉着另一个的脚，最小的猴子在最下边，一伸手就碰到水中的月亮了。可是手刚碰到月亮，月亮就摇晃着不见了。手捞不到，小猴子想了个办法。让上面的猴子拿一只水瓢来，轻轻一舀，把月亮舀在了水瓢里，大家一个传一个，把水瓢传到了井上。猴子们可高兴了，围着水瓢里的月亮又唱又跳。
可是，有一只小猴子太贪心了，它趁别的猴子不注意，一下子就把水瓢拿走了，想把月亮据为己有。这下猴子们闹开了，你抢我夺，没几下一瓢水都泼在了地上，月亮没有了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Monkeys and the Moon

It was very late, but the moonlight was beautiful, lighting up the whole earth in silver brightness. So the monkeys didn't go to sleep—they were still playing on the mountain. Suddenly, one monkey pointed at the moon in the sky and said, "Let's pick the moon down and play with it!" "What a great idea!" they all cheered. But the moon was so high up, and the monkeys could never reach it. They sighed and gave up, going off to play something else.

Just then, one monkey shouted happily, "Come quickly! The moon has fallen into the well!" The monkeys gathered round and looked—couldn't it be? The round, bright moon was right there in the well.

After a little商量, the monkeys decided to go into the well and retrieve it. So one held onto another's feet, with the smallest monkey at the very bottom. She reached out and just touched the moon in the water! But the moment her hand made contact, the moon wobbled and disappeared. When bare hands wouldn't do it, the little monkey thought of another way. She asked the monkey above to bring a water ladle, and gently scooped the moon right into it. One by one, they passed the ladle up the chain until it reached the top. The monkeys were overjoyed, singing and dancing around the moon in the ladle.

But one little monkey was too greedy. While the others weren't looking, she snatched the ladle away, wanting the moon all to herself. Chaos broke out! The monkeys tugged and grabbed at each other, and before long, all the water splashed onto the ground—and the moon was gone.
fields.tips: 准妈妈在读故事的时候，脑海里一定会出现一群可爱的小猴子淘气、顽皮的样子。别忘了告诉胎宝宝，长大后一定要学会分享哦。因为心甘情愿的分享可以让自己获得给予的快乐，也可以收获更真诚的友情。此外，准妈妈还可以经常到公园等地方走走，赏赏花、看看水，这些属于公众的美丽同样也属于你。边走、边看、边给胎宝宝讲讲你看到了什么、闻到了什么、想到了什么，就像胎宝宝在跟你一起旅行一样。
fields.tips_en: As you read this story aloud, a picture of those lovely little monkeys being playful and mischievous will surely fill your mind. Don't forget to share with your baby that learning to share is one of life's greatest joys. Generous sharing brings the warmth of giving and the gift of true friendship. You might also enjoy strolling through the park often—admiring flowers, watching the water, and soaking in beauty that belongs to everyone, yet is yours to treasure too. As you walk and explore, talk to your baby about what you see, smell, and feel, as though you are on a wonderful journey together.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 七色花
fields.subtitle: 给予的快乐
fields.subtitle_en: The Joy of Giving
fields.content:
有一天，小姑娘珍妮到树林里玩儿，结果迷路了。她又着急又害怕，就哭了起来。这时，树林里走出一位老婆婆。老婆婆问珍妮怎么啦，珍妮告诉了老婆婆原因。老婆婆听完后慈祥地安慰珍妮说：“别哭，我这里有一朵七色花，能帮你做到任何事情。”然后她把七色花交给珍妮，告诉珍妮使用方法后就不见了。这朵花很漂亮，有七片花瓣，每片颜色都不一样，有红的、黄的、蓝的、绿的、青的、紫的和橙色的。珍妮撕下一片红色花瓣，对花瓣说：“飞呀，飞呀，小花瓣，请你送我回家去。”话刚说完，珍妮就已经回到家中了。
珍妮想这朵花这么好，就把它插到花瓶中，结果一不小心把花瓶打碎了。珍妮揪下一片黄色花瓣，对花瓣说：“飞呀，飞呀，小花瓣，请你让花瓶复原吧。”花瓶就复原了，像从来没打碎过一样。
珍妮拿着花瓣来到花园里，想和男孩子们爬山。但他们不要她，珍妮就生气地让蓝色花瓣把自己送到山顶上去。在山顶上风很大，而且还有厚厚的冰雪。珍妮撕下绿色花瓣，让它把自己送回了花园。在花园里，珍妮看见女孩子们在玩玩具，就撕下青色花瓣，让它把所有的玩具都给自己。玩具都来了，多得都快把珍妮埋起来了。珍妮赶紧撕下紫色花瓣，让它把玩具都送回去。现在，珍妮手中只剩下一片橙色的花瓣了。珍妮想：“我已经用掉六片花瓣了，可是一点儿快乐都没得到，这一片一定要好好用。”
珍妮拿着七色花来到大街上，看到一个小男孩坐在轮椅上，吃力地用双手摇着轮子往前走。她就撕下橙色花瓣说：“飞呀，飞呀，小花瓣，请你让坐轮椅的小男孩站起来。”小男孩马上就从轮椅上站起来了。
小男孩和珍妮一起跑到花园里玩儿。跑啊，跳啊，他们玩儿得非常开心。珍妮终于得到了快乐。
（作者：卡达耶夫/苏联）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Seven-Colored Flower

One day, a little girl named Jenny went to play in the woods and got lost. She was worried and scared, so she started to cry. Just then, an old grandmother walked out from the forest. Grandmother asked Jenny what was wrong, and Jenny told her what happened. After listening, Grandmother kindly comforted Jenny and said, "Don't cry. I have a seven-colored flower here that can help you do anything." Then she gave the flower to Jenny, told her how to use it, and disappeared. The flower was beautiful, with seven petals, each a different color—red, yellow, blue, green, cyan, purple, and orange. Jenny tore off a red petal and said to it, "Fly away, fly away, little petal, please take me home." And just as she finished speaking, Jenny was already back home.

Jenny thought the flower was wonderful, so she placed it in a vase. But by accident, she knocked the vase over and broke it. Jenny tore off a yellow petal and said, "Fly away, fly away, little petal, please make the vase whole again." And just like that, the vase was restored, as if it had never been broken at all.

Jenny took the flower petals to the garden and wanted to go climbing with the boys. But they wouldn't let her play, so Jenny got upset and tore off a blue petal, asking to be sent to the top of the mountain. At the mountaintop, the wind was very strong, and there was thick ice and snow. Jenny tore off a green petal and asked it to take her back to the garden. In the garden, Jenny saw some girls playing with toys, so she tore off a cyan petal and asked it to bring all the toys to her. The toys came flooding in, so many that they were almost burying Jenny! She quickly tore off a purple petal and asked it to send all the toys back. Now, only one orange petal remained in Jenny's hand. Jenny thought, "I've used six petals already and haven't found any happiness at all. I must use this last one wisely."

Jenny took the seven-colored flower to the street and saw a little boy in a wheelchair, struggling to push himself forward with his hands. She tore off the orange petal and said, "Fly away, fly away, little petal, please make the little boy in the wheelchair stand up." And the little boy stood up right away!

The little boy and Jenny ran together to the garden to play. They ran and jumped and had the most wonderful time. And Jenny finally found true happiness.
fields.tips: 珍妮实现的前六个愿望都没能让她得到快乐，只有最后一个愿望实现了，她才真正快乐起来。很多时候，给予比收获更能让人感受到快乐。准妈妈在生活中如果能做到多付出、不计较，你会发现，你获得的快乐也会越来越多。而准妈妈的快乐在潜移默化中会对胎宝宝产生良性的影响，这样的效果是非常好的。
fields.tips_en: 珍妮's first six wishes did not bring her true happiness. It was only when she used her final petal to selflessly help another that joy truly filled her heart. Often, giving brings more lasting happiness than receiving. When you live with an open and generous spirit, you will find happiness growing richer within you. And the happiness you carry quietly nurtures your baby in the most beautiful way, creating a gentle, positive bond even before birth.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小老鼠偷油喝
fields.title_en: The Little Mice and the Oil Jar
fields.subtitle: 自私害人害己
fields.subtitle_en: Selfishness Harms Everyone, Including Ourselves
fields.content:
小老鼠喜欢喝油。有一天三只小老鼠发现了一个油缸，可是里面的油太少了，谁都够不着。三只老鼠想了个好办法，就是一个咬着另一个的尾巴，把前面的一个倒吊着下去。等它喝饱了，就吊上来，换第二只去喝。这样每只老鼠就都能喝到油了。
办法有了，马上就干。第一只老鼠下去了。它边喝油边想：“油只有这么一点儿，幸亏我第一个下来，可以先喝个饱。”第二只老鼠看第一只老鼠喝个没完，着急地想：“它喝这么多，轮到我不就没有油了？不如把它放开，我也跳下去喝吧。”第二只老鼠这么打算的时候，第三只老鼠也在打算：“第一只喝了这么多，第二只再喝，它们两个喝完了，哪还有我的份？”于是第二只老鼠就把第一只老鼠的尾巴放开了，第三只老鼠也把第二只老鼠的尾巴放开了。三只老鼠一起喝油，终于都喝到了分量差不多相等的油，但是它们再也爬不上来了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Mice and the Oil Jar

Once upon a time, there were three little mice who loved to drink oil. One day, they found a big jar of oil, but the oil was so low that none of them could reach it.

The three mice thought of a wonderful plan. One mouse would hold onto the tail of the mouse above him, letting the one at the bottom hang upside down to drink. When he was full, they would pull him up, and the next mouse would take his turn. That way, every mouse would get a taste of the sweet oil.

They set to work right away. The first mouse went down. As he drank, he thought, "There's only a little oil left. I'm lucky I went down first — I can drink my fill!"

The second mouse watched the first one drinking and kept on drinking. He grew worried. "If he drinks all of it, what will be left for me? Perhaps I should let go and jump in myself."

At the same time, the third mouse was thinking, "The first one drank so much, and now the second one is drinking too. What will be left for me?"

And so, the second mouse let go of the first mouse's tail, and the third mouse let go of the second mouse's tail. All three mice tumbled into the jar, splashing into the oil. They drank together until their bellies were full, all drinking nearly the same amount. But oh no — they could never climb back out again.
fields.tips: 这三只小老鼠为了一己私利，纷纷做出对伙伴不利的事情。由于没能像计划好的那样去做，最后它们都陷在缸里出不来了，多得不偿失啊！准妈妈要教胎宝宝宽容的美德，切不可过于小肚鸡肠。对人对事大度一点儿，对人对己都有利。
fields.tips_en: Those three little mice acted only for their own gain, each thinking only of themselves—and in the end, they all found themselves trapped in the jar with no way out. Such a pity! Teach your baby the virtue of generosity and kindness. Being open-hearted and forgiving toward others—and toward yourself—is a gift that brings peace and joy to all. A generous spirit benefits everyone around you.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小蝌蚪找妈妈
fields.title_en: The Little Tadpoles Searching for Their Mother
fields.subtitle: 亲情是割不断的
fields.subtitle_en: The Bond of Love Can Never Be Broken
fields.content:
春天来了，青蛙妈妈醒来了。它把很多又黑又圆的卵产在水草上。
天气暖和了，又黑又圆的卵长大了，变成了一群尾巴长长、脑袋大大的小蝌蚪。
一天，鸭妈妈带着小鸭子来池塘游泳，小蝌蚪们看到了，不禁想为什么自己没有妈妈呢？它们你看看我，我看看你，谁都不知道。小蝌蚪们决定问问鸭妈妈。鸭妈妈告诉它们可以自己去找，它们的妈妈头顶上有两只大眼睛，还长着又大又宽的嘴巴。
小蝌蚪们谢过鸭妈妈，就去找自己的妈妈了。游着游着，它们看到一条大鱼。大鱼的头顶长着两只大眼睛，嘴巴又宽又大，这不就是妈妈吗？小蝌蚪们高兴了，追上去喊妈妈。可是大鱼说不是它们的妈妈，它们的妈妈有四条腿。
谢过大鱼，它们继续找妈妈，游着游着看到一只乌龟。乌龟长着四条腿，小蝌蚪们想这回是真的妈妈了，就追上去喊妈妈。可是乌龟告诉它们自己不是它们的妈妈，它们的妈妈肚皮是白的。
小蝌蚪们谢过乌龟，继续往前游去找妈妈。游着游着看到一只大白鹅，肚皮是白的。它们想这回可找到妈妈了，就追上去大声喊妈妈。大白鹅告诉它们自己不是它们的妈妈，它们的妈妈穿着绿衣服。
谢过大白鹅，小蝌蚪们又开始找妈妈。它们游啊游啊，游到池塘边，看见一只青蛙坐在荷叶上，穿着绿衣服。可小蝌蚪们闹了那么多笑话，不敢再贸然喊妈妈了。它们小心翼翼地问青蛙：“请问您认识我们的妈妈吗？它头顶上有两只大眼睛，嘴巴又宽又大……”青蛙“呱呱”地笑了，说：“傻孩子，我就是你们的妈妈！”小蝌蚪们疑惑了：“为什么我们跟您一点儿都不像呢？”青蛙告诉它们，等它们长大了就像了。
果然，过了几天，小蝌蚪们长出了两条前腿，又过了几天，长出了两条后腿，连皮肤都变成绿色的了，终于跟妈妈一样了。
fields.content_en:
# Little Tadpoles Look for Their Mama

Spring has come, and Mother Frog wakes up. She lays many tiny, black, round eggs on the water plants.

The weather grows warm, and those black, round eggs grow bigger, turning into a group of little tadpoles with long tails and big heads.

One day, Mother Duck takes her ducklings to swim in the pond. The little tadpoles see them and wonder why they don't have a mama of their own. They look at each other, but nobody knows. So the tadpoles decide to ask Mother Duck. Mother Duck tells them they can look for their mama themselves. She says their mama has two big eyes on top of her head and a wide, big mouth.

The little tadpoles thank Mother Duck and set off to find their mama. Swimming along, they see a big fish. The big fish has two large eyes on top of her head and a wide, big mouth. Could this be Mama? The tadpoles are so happy and swim after her, calling out "Mama! Mama!" But the fish says no, she isn't their mama. Their mama has four legs.

They thank the fish and keep looking. Swimming along, they see a turtle. The turtle has four legs, and the tadpoles think, "This time it must be our real mama!" They chase after and call out "Mama!" But the turtle tells them no, she isn't their mama. Their mama has a white belly.

The tadpoles thank the turtle and keep swimming forward. Along the way, they see a big white goose with a white belly. "This time we've found Mama!" they think, and they call out loudly, "Mama!" But the goose says no, she isn't their mama. Their mama wears green clothes.

The tadpoles thank the goose and start looking again. They swim and swim, until they reach the edge of the pond. There sits a frog on a lotus leaf, wearing green clothes. But after all the funny mix-ups, the tadpoles are too shy to call out "Mama" right away. They timidly ask the frog, "Excuse me, do you know our mama? She has two big eyes on top of her head, and a wide, big mouth..." The frog laughs and says, "You silly little ones, I am your mama!" The tadpoles are puzzled. "But why don't we look anything like you?" The frog tells them that when they grow up, they will look just like her.

Sure enough, after a few days, the little tadpoles grew two front legs. A few days later, they grew two back legs, and even their skin turned green. At last, they looked just like Mama.
fields.tips: 亲情是一条坚实的纽带，无论如何也割不断。宝宝跟妈妈的亲情从胎儿期就开始了。准妈妈要把胎宝宝当成一个家庭成员，经常跟他交流，这可为宝宝出生后和妈妈建立亲子关系打下基础。
fields.tips_en: Family love is a strong and unbreakable thread. The bond between you and your baby begins even before birth, from the very days you carry them close to your heart. Treat your baby as a beloved member of your family, talking and connecting with them each day. This loving communication lays the sweetest foundation for the beautiful mother-child bond that will flourish after they are born.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 运盐的驴子
fields.subtitle: 不要被已有的经验迷惑
fields.subtitle_en: Do Not Be Fooled by Past Experiences
fields.content:
从前有一位商人，他有一头驴，用来帮助自己运送货物。有一天，天气炎热，驴的背上驮了好几包盐，跟着商人到城里卖盐去。盐很重，驴子被压得都快走不动了，但是商人不停地催促，驴子只得卖命地埋头向前走。走到一条小河边的时候，驴子心想可以歇一歇了，可是商人并没有休息的意思，在驴子喝了几口水后就催促它过河了。驴子无奈，只得抬起软绵绵的四条腿迈进了河里，向河心走去。可它的腿实在是太无力了，双脚一软，“咕咚”一声四脚朝天跌在水里了，背上的盐袋也都泡在了水里。驴子拼命挣扎，费了好大一会儿工夫，才站起来。站在河心，驴子不停地喘着粗气，心里正埋怨商人心狠，但突然感觉身上轻松了不少，原来是盐在水里溶化了。驴子高兴极了，脚步也轻快了。
过了几天，商人又赶着驴子驮着盐去城里。驴子有了上次的经验，这次也如法炮制，走到河中间就假装摔倒躺一会儿，待盐溶化一些再起来，它得逞了。
但是下次再进城，驴子驮的不是盐而是棉花了。驴子走到河中间又故意摔倒了，可是这次驴子站起来，出乎意料的是背上的负担不但没减轻，却更重了。因为棉花吸满了水。这次可把驴子累惨了。
从此以后，驴子再也不敢这么做了。
（选自《伊索寓言》）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Donkey Who Carried Salt

Once upon a time, there was a merchant who had a donkey to help him carry goods. One day, the weather was hot, and the donkey's back was loaded with several sacks of salt as he followed the merchant to town to sell the salt. The salt was very heavy, and the poor donkey could barely walk. But the merchant kept urging him on, so the donkey could only plod forward with all his might.

When they reached a small river, the donkey thought he might finally get a rest. But the merchant had no intention of stopping. After the donkey took a few drinks from the river, the merchant told him to cross. With a heavy heart, the donkey lifted his tired, wobbly legs and stepped into the water, making his way toward the middle. His legs were too weak to hold him, and suddenly—"splash!"—he tumbled onto his back in the river, and all the salt sacks soaked in the water.

The donkey struggled hard and, after what felt like forever, managed to stand up again. Panting heavily in the middle of the river, he was starting to complain about how unkind his merchant was when he suddenly noticed something wonderful—he felt much lighter! It turned out the salt had dissolved in the water. The donkey was overjoyed, and his steps became light and happy.

A few days later, the merchant sent the donkey out again with more salt. Remembering his lucky experience, the donkey went through the same trick. Halfway across the river, he pretended to stumble and lie down for a while, letting the salt soften, and then got back up. And it worked perfectly!

But on the next trip to town, the donkey was carrying cotton instead of salt. When he reached the middle of the river, he deliberately fell down once again. This time, however, when he stood back up, something surprising happened. The load on his back did not get any lighter—it was even heavier than before! The cotton had soaked up all the water. The poor donkey was exhausted.

From that day on, the donkey never tried that trick again.

(Based on Aesop's Fables)
fields.tips: 驴子根据前两次的经验处理第三次的事情，结果吃了大亏。因为外在条件已经变了。准妈妈在怀孕的时候也难免会有过来人向你传授经验，要记得甄别看是否适合你。个体不同，同样的方法不一定仍适用。
fields.tips_en: The donkey relied on what had worked twice before, but this time the circumstances had changed—and he learned a costly lesson. In your own pregnancy, well-meaning friends and family may offer you advice based on their own experiences. Remember to gently consider whether each piece of advice truly suits you. Every mother and every baby are unique, and what worked for others may not be the right path for you. Trust your own heart and your own journey.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 两只小羊过桥
fields.title_en: Two Little Lambs Cross the Bridge
fields.subtitle: 不懂礼让，害人害己
fields.subtitle_en: Without Courtesy, Everyone Suffers
fields.content:
在广袤的大草原上，一条清澈的小河自东向西穿流而过。小河说宽不宽，但要涉水而过也不太安全，需要走一座小桥。
小河的南北两面各住着一只小羊，河南面的小羊全身都是白色，大家叫它小白羊；河北面的小羊全身都是黑色，大家叫它小黑羊。小白羊的姥姥住在河北，而小黑羊的爷爷则住在河南。它们每次去探望姥姥或者爷爷都要经过那座小桥。
这天，天气很好，小白羊和小黑羊不约而同想要到河对面去，小白羊要去看姥姥，小黑羊要去看爷爷。可不巧的是，它们同时到达了小桥，走到桥中间就相遇了。小桥很窄，它们无法擦肩而过。于是小白羊开口了：“你退回去，你退回去，让我先过去，我要去看姥姥。”但是小黑羊丝毫没有退让的意思，反而马上顶了回来：“你退回去，我还要去看我爷爷呢。”小白羊自然不肯退让，争辩道：“是我先上桥的，当然是应该让我先过。”小黑羊也不松口：“是你先上桥，怎么才走到这啊？是我先上桥的，让我先过。”两只小羊谁都不肯退让，就站在桥中间争吵不休。这时不断有别的小动物走过来要过桥，可是两只小羊站在中间，无路可走，劝谁都不听。没办法，它们都退回去从别的地方绕道过河了。两只小羊还是气鼓鼓地站在桥中间，争吵不休。
眼看着太阳越来越高，快到中午了，小白羊想着姥姥肯定已经准备好了鲜嫩的青草蛋糕等着自己呢，小黑羊也想着爷爷肯定给自己准备好了清香的青草点心，一想还真饿了，可是过又过不去，两只小羊都生起气来。小白羊高声叫着：“你再不让，我撞你了！”小黑羊也不示弱：“要撞就撞，谁不会撞，我怕你啊！”话音刚落，两只小羊小腿用力，蹄子把桥面蹬得噔噔响，向对方用力撞去。“咚”的一声，两只小羊的头撞在了一起。大概是它们都用力太猛了，而桥面又太窄，只见两只小羊同时从桥面掉下去，紧接着“扑通”“扑通”两声，它们都落水了。呵呵，这下它们都不用走桥了，只能涉水过河啦。
fields.content_en:
# Two Little Sheep Crossing the Bridge

On a vast green prairie, a clear little river flows from east to west. The river isn't very wide, but it isn't safe to wade across either—you have to use a little bridge.

On the north side of the river lives one little sheep, and on the south side lives another. The little sheep on the south side is all white, so everyone calls him Little White Sheep. The little sheep on the north side is all black, so everyone calls him Little Black Sheep. Little White Sheep's grandma lives on the north side, and Little Black Sheep's grandpa lives on the south side. Every time they go to visit their grandma or grandpa, they have to cross that little bridge.

One day, the weather was beautiful. Little White Sheep and Little Black Sheep both felt like going to the other side of the river. Little White Sheep wanted to visit his grandma, and Little Black Sheep wanted to visit his grandpa. Unfortunately, they arrived at the bridge at the same time and met right in the middle. The bridge is very narrow, and they couldn't squeeze past each other. So Little White Sheep spoke up: "Go back, go back! Let me pass first. I need to go visit my grandma." But Little Black Sheep had no intention of stepping aside. Instead, he quickly retorted: "You go back! I need to go visit my grandpa!" Little White Sheep refused to yield and argued, "I got on the bridge first, so of course I should go first." Little Black Sheep wouldn't give in either: "You got on first, but you walked so slowly! I got on first—let me pass!" Neither little sheep would back down, and they stood in the middle of the bridge arguing and arguing. Meanwhile, other little animals came along wanting to cross, but with the two sheep blocking the way, there was no path through. No one could persuade them. In the end, they both had to turn around and take a long detour to cross the river another way. The two little sheep stayed on the bridge, still puffing with anger and still arguing.

The sun climbed higher and higher until it was almost noon. Little White Sheep thought about how his grandma must have already prepared his favorite tender grass cake for him. Little Black Sheep thought about how his grandpa must have ready some fragrant grass treats for him too. They both began to feel quite hungry. But they still couldn't cross, and they both grew even more annoyed. Little White Sheep called out loudly, "If you don't move, I'm going to bump you!" Little Black Sheep didn't back down either: "Go ahead and bump me! Who doesn't know how to bump? I'm not afraid of you!" Before the words were even out, both little sheep dug in their little legs and pounded their hooves against the bridge—thud, thud, thud!—and charged at each other with all their might. *Bonk!* Their heads bumped together. They had pushed too hard, and the bridge was so narrow. In the next moment, both little sheep tumbled off the bridge together. Then came two quick *plop* sounds as they fell into the water. Well, now they didn't have to walk across the bridge at all—they got to cross by wading!
fields.tips: 怀孕期间，准妈妈要学会宽容、礼让，不要拥挤、争抢。这不但能直接保护胎宝宝的安全，还能让自己的心态保持轻松、愉快。好心情本身就是好胎教。
fields.tips_en: During pregnancy, mama should practice kindness and patience, avoiding pushing and crowding. This not only keeps your little one safe but also helps you stay calm and joyful. A happy heart is the very best prenatal bonding.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 3只小猪
fields.subtitle: 到底谁是好榜样
fields.subtitle_en: Who Is the True Role Model?
fields.content:
山脚下住着一位猪妈妈，它带着3只可爱的小猪过日子。猪妈妈每天都很辛苦地工作。小猪们一天天长大了，可是什么事都不做。猪妈妈决定让它们自己出去独立生活。
这天晚上，吃过晚饭后，猪妈妈把3只小猪叫到跟前，跟它们说：“你们已经长大了，到了该独立的时候，从明天起你们都开始盖房子吧，盖好房子就搬出去。”
小猪们都不愿意，跟妈妈一起生活多好啊，可是它们也不敢违背妈妈的意愿，第二天就都开始着手盖房子了。
老大最好吃懒做，它想用最快最简单的方法盖个房子，能住就行。它跑到田里，扛了一些稻草回来，在离猪妈妈的房子不远的地方找了一片空地，用稻草很快就搭成了一个简易的房子。老大很高兴，第二天就搬了进去。
老二和老三很惊奇，老大这么快就盖好房子了。于是他们跟着老大一起来参观，原来老大盖的只是一个稻草棚。回去的路上，老二对老三说：“老三，你看老大的房子太简陋了，我一定要盖一个最漂亮的房子。”
老二跑到山上砍了许多木头扛回来，用锯子先锯成木板、木条，用这些木条、木板盖起很漂亮的房子，而且还有明亮的窗户。老二得意极了，第二天也搬了进去。
老大和老三也来参观老二的房子。老大很羡慕老二的房子，但老三说自己要盖最结实的房子。什么样的房子最结实呢？猪妈妈告诉老三，砖头盖的房子最结实，就是盖起来比较慢，很费力。但老三不怕累，不怕麻烦。老三从此每天起早贪黑，搬回来许多砖头。砖头搬够了，又开始一块块砌成墙。老大、老二看着老三忙碌，都取笑他说：“只有傻瓜才这么干呢，能住就好了，你盖这么结实有什么用！”但老三仍然忙碌着。
过了几天，老三的房子终于盖好了。虽然因为手艺不精，房子不算漂亮，但是绝对结实。老三也搬了进去。
这样，三兄弟都各自过起了独立生活。
有一天，来了一只大野狼。老大远远地看见野狼，赶忙躲进了稻草棚里。野狼根本没把稻草棚看在眼里，猛吹一口气，稻草棚就倒了。
老大一看稻草棚倒了，撒腿就跑，慌慌张张地跑到老二的木板房里。老二连忙让老大进去避难，可是大野狼也没把老二的木板房放在眼里。它哼了一声，说道：“你们以为木板房就能把我难住了吗？”它不慌不忙走到房子跟前，一下一下向房门撞去，不消几下，只听“哗啦”一声，木头房子就被野狼撞倒了。
老大和老二赶紧跑到了老三的砖头房子里，弟兄3个一起躲起来。野狼来到老三的房子前，绕着房子走了一圈都没想到好办法。它只好故技重施，先大口对着房门吹气，房门纹丝未动，然后用力撞门。门倒是“哐”地响了一声，但野狼也撞得眼冒金星、头疼欲裂。野狼又去找了一把锤子，想把房子砸个洞出来。结果锤子砸在墙上反弹回来，反倒打中了野狼的鼻子，野狼被打得满脸是血。
野狼始终都没有办法攻克老三的砖头房子，只好悻悻地走了。
（作者：约瑟夫·雅各布斯/英国）
fields.content_en:
**Title: Three Little Pigs**

At the foot of a mountain lived a mother pig with her three little pigs. Mother pig worked hard every day. The little pigs grew bigger each day, but they never helped with anything. So mother pig decided they should go out and live on their own.

One evening after dinner, mother pig called her three little pigs over and said, "You have all grown up now. It is time to be independent. Starting tomorrow, you must each build your own house. When your house is ready, you can move out."

The little pigs did not want to leave home. Life with mother was so comfortable! But they dared not disobey her, so the next day they all began to build their houses.

The eldest pig loved to eat and do nothing. He wanted to finish quickly with the simplest method. He ran to a field, carried some straw back, found a piece of empty land near mother's house, and quickly built a simple little house from straw. The eldest was very happy and moved in the next day.

The second and third pigs were surprised. Their brother had finished so fast! They went to visit his house together and discovered it was only a straw shed. On the way home, the second pig said to the third, "Look at the eldest's house — it is so简陋 (simple)! I will build the most beautiful house."

The second pig ran to the mountain, cut many pieces of wood, and carried them back. He used a saw to cut the wood into planks and strips, then built a beautiful house with bright windows. The second pig was very proud and moved in the next day.

The eldest and third pigs came to see the second pig's house. The eldest was envious. But the third pig said he would build the strongest house. What kind of house is strongest? Mother pig told the third pig that brick houses are the strongest, though they take longer and more effort to build. But the third pig was not afraid of hard work or trouble. From that day on, he rose early and worked late, carrying back many bricks. Once enough bricks were gathered, he began laying them one by one into walls. The eldest and second pigs watched the third pig working busily and teased him, saying, "Only a fool would do this! It is enough to have a place to live. What good is such a strong house?" But the third pig kept working.

After a few days, the third pig's house was finally finished. Though not very beautiful because his skill was not perfect, it was certainly strong. The third pig moved in.

In this way, the three brothers all began living independently.

One day, a big wolf came. The eldest pig saw the wolf from far away and quickly hid in his straw shed. The wolf did not care about the straw house at all. With one mighty breath, the straw shed blew down.

Seeing his house collapsed, the eldest pig ran as fast as he could. He rushed in a panic to the second pig's wooden house. The second pig quickly let him in for shelter. But the big wolf did not fear the wooden house either. He sniffed and said, "Do you think a wooden house can stop me?" He walked calmly to the house and pushed against the door again and again. In just a few tries, there was a crash — the wooden house fell down.

The eldest and second pigs hurried to the third pig's brick house and hid together. The wolf came to the brick house and walked around it once, unable to find a way in. He tried his old trick again, blowing hard at the door, but the door did not move at all. Then he pushed against the door with all his might. The door made a loud bang, but the wolf ended up dizzy with a splitting headache. The wolf then searched for a hammer, hoping to break a hole in the house. But when the hammer struck the wall, it bounced back and hit the wolf right in the nose. The wolf was covered in blood.

The wolf could never overcome the third pig's brick house, so he left in anger.

*(Author: Joseph Jacobs / England)*
fields.tips: 不管做什么事情，都要有长远打算，否则就会有不好的后果。第一只小猪懒惰、凑合；第二只小猪追求华而不实的东西；只有第三只小猪勤劳肯干、聪明机智，也是它帮助自己的兄弟免受野狼袭击。准妈妈在讲故事的时候，一定要在脑海中呈现出画面，将画面传达给腹中的胎宝宝，相信哪种小猪是学习的好榜样，胎宝宝能感觉到哦。
fields.tips_en: No matter what we do, it is wise to think ahead, for lack of planning can lead to trouble. The first pig was lazy and careless; the second chased fancy but useless things; only the third pig was hardworking, clever, and brave enough to rescue his brothers from the big bad wolf. When you tell this story, paint vivid pictures in your mind and share them with your baby. Your little one can feel the wonderful example the third pig sets.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 渔夫和金鱼的故事
fields.title_en: The Fisherman and the Golden Fish
fields.subtitle: 知足才能常乐
fields.subtitle_en: Contentment Brings Lasting Joy
fields.content:
从前一个渔夫和他的老太婆住在大海边，渔夫每天撒网打鱼，老太婆纺纱织网，日子过得很清贫。他们只有一间破木棚房子和一只用了很久的破木盆。
一天渔夫到海边打鱼，他的运气不太好，连打了两网，一条鱼都没打到，只有一些水草，第三网也只是打到一条金鱼。不过，这条金鱼很奇怪，它居然会说话。它对渔夫说：“老爷爷，只要你放了我，作为报酬，我可以给你一切你想要的东西。”渔夫有点儿害怕，他打了这么多年鱼了，还没听说过有会说话的金鱼，就赶忙把金鱼放了。他还安慰金鱼说：“回大海里去吧，上帝保佑你，我不要你的报酬。”
回到家里，渔夫把这件怪事告诉了老太婆。没想到老太婆生气了。她指责渔夫说：“你真是个傻瓜，怎么能不要报酬呢？就是要只木盆也好啊！你看我们的木盆已经破得没样了。”渔夫看看木盆，的确破得不像样了。他觉得老太婆这样说也有道理。于是，渔夫走向大海，对着大海喊金鱼。金鱼游过来，问道：“老爷爷，你要什么呀？”老头告诉金鱼：“老太婆骂了我一顿，她想要只新木盆。”金鱼安慰渔夫说：“老爷爷，别难过，我答应你的要求，你回去吧。”渔夫回到家，发现老太婆面前果然摆着一只新木盆，渔夫很高兴。
可是，老太婆却发起火来。她怨渔夫只要了一只木盆，要求渔夫再去要一座木房子。渔夫想想老太婆想要一座木房子也不过分，毕竟家里的木棚已经破得快不能住人了，所以再次走向大海。金鱼答应了渔夫的要求，老太婆就有了一座漂亮的大木房子了。此外，还有一个院子和橡木门。渔夫想这回老太婆该满意了，不会再骂他了。
可是，老太婆并不满足，她的要求越来越多，越来越过分。她先是不想做渔婆子了，要做贵妇人，后来贵妇人也不想做了，要做女皇。渔夫觉得她有些过分了，但不能反驳，只要反驳，她不是骂就是打。渔夫没办法，只能每次都去求金鱼，金鱼都答应了他的要求，实现了老太婆的愿望。
可是，老太婆并不感谢渔夫，也不感谢金鱼，她对渔夫越来越不好。她是贵妇人的时候，派渔夫到马棚干活儿；她当了女皇，都不让渔夫靠近她，还让卫兵把渔夫赶走了，再要用到渔夫的时候，就派人把他抓回来。
这次，老太婆又把渔夫抓回来，告诉渔夫她要做海上的女霸王，还要金鱼亲自伺候她。老头不敢顶嘴，只能无奈地再次去求金鱼，但是这次金鱼没有安慰渔夫，也没有说任何别的话，只是尾巴一摆就游走了。渔夫站在海边等了很久，金鱼也没回来。渔夫不敢回去，但也不能不回去。不过当他走到家的时候，渔夫高兴了，因为他的家又恢复了原样，只有木棚房子和一只旧木盆。他的老太婆坐在破旧的门槛上，再也不是那个高高在上的女皇了，他们的日子终于恢复正常了。
（作者：普希金/俄国）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Fisherman and the Goldfish**

Once upon a time, a fisherman and his old wife lived by the sea. The fisherman cast his nets every day to catch fish, and the old wife spun thread and wove nets. They lived a poor but quiet life. All they had was a tiny wooden shack and a worn-out old basin that had seen many years of use.

One day, the fisherman went to the sea to fish. His luck was not kind to him that day. He cast his net twice and caught nothing at all — only seaweed. On the third cast, he caught just one little goldfish. But this goldfish was very strange. It could actually speak! It said to the fisherman, "Dear old man, if you only let me go, I will give you anything you desire as a reward." The fisherman was a little frightened. He had been fishing for so many years and had never heard of a talking goldfish before, so he quickly let the goldfish go. He also comforted the little fish and said, "Go back to the sea, may God bless you. I do not want your reward."

When he returned home, the fisherman told his wife about this curious event. To his surprise, the old wife became angry. She scolded the fisherman, saying, "You fool! How could you refuse a reward? Even a new wooden basin would have been enough! Look at our basin — it is broken beyond repair." The fisherman looked at the basin, and indeed, it was in terrible condition.
