农夫醒来后发现珠宝商已经走了，他也不在意，戒指被换了，也没发现。回到家以后，他把这个故事跟自己的妻子也说了一遍。妻子立刻说：“那让它给我们一头牛、一亩地吧。”但农夫说：“一头牛、一亩地，我们好好干一年就有了，没必要动用希望戒指，还是等我们真正有需要的时候再用它吧，毕竟它只能帮我们实现五个希望。”一年后，他们果真用劳动所得换来了一头牛、一亩地。农夫的妻子又想让希望戒指给他们两匹马。农夫依旧说劳动一年也可以得到两匹马，把希望留下吧。于是一年又一年，农夫始终都没有用希望戒指，但他们都努力工作，他们的日子也一年比一年富足，生活也一直很幸福。关键是他们一直都拥有希望。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Ring of Hope

Once upon a time, long, long ago, there was a farmer who went up the mountain every day to cut firewood. One day, something small and unexpected happened: he bumped his head against a tree, and a bird's nest fell down. The nest hit the ground, and two bird eggs rolled out. The eggs bounced twice and then cracked open. From one egg came a little hawk, and from the other egg rolled out a ring. The farmer was puzzled by the ring when the little hawk spoke up: "I am under a spell inside this egg. Now that you've rescued me, take this ring as a thank-you gift. It is a Ring of Hope, and it can grant you five wishes. To use it, simply put it on your finger, turn it around once, and say your wish out loud." With that, the little hawk flew away. The farmer wasn't sure what to believe, but he put the ring on and continued up the mountain to gather firewood.

After cutting two bundles of firewood, the farmer carried them down the mountain. He felt tired and thirsty, so he stopped at a small tea house by the road. A jeweler sitting nearby noticed his ring and thought it looked beautifully old-fashioned. He asked the farmer where he had gotten it, and the farmer told him everything. Greed sparked in the jeweler's heart. He invited the farmer to dinner and bought fine wine to share. The farmer got drunk, and the jeweler swapped the ring for his own and slipped away.

The jeweler walked to a lonely place, put the ring on his finger, turned it once, and shouted loudly, "Give me 100 gold coins!" The moment he finished speaking, 100 gold coins rained down from the sky with a loud clatter, all landing right on the jeweler and killing him instantly.

When the farmer woke up, he noticed the jeweler was gone and didn't think much of it, not even realizing his ring had been swapped. When he got home, he told his wife the whole story. His wife said right away, "Let's wish for a cow and an acre of land!" But the farmer replied, "A cow and an acre of land — we can earn those by working hard for a year. There's no need to use the Ring of Hope yet. Let's save it for when we truly need it, since it can only grant five wishes." And sure enough, a year later, they had earned a cow and an acre of land through their own hard work. Later, the farmer's wife wanted to wish for two horses. Again, the farmer said they could work for a year and earn two horses just fine. So they kept the ring safe. Year after year passed, and the farmer never used the Ring of Hope. But they kept working hard, and their life grew richer and more comfortable with each passing year. They were happy. Most importantly, they always had hope.
fields.tips: 每一位准妈妈都会对胎宝宝有无限的爱和美好的希望。在做胎教的时候，别忘了把对胎宝宝的美好希望传达给他。准妈妈可以每天在固定的时间做做冥想，把对胎宝宝的希望刻画在脑海中，他会朝着准妈妈希望的方向努力哦。
fields.tips_en: Every expectant mother holds boundless love and beautiful hopes for her baby. During your bonding time, don't forget to share those wonderful hopes with your little one. You can sit quietly each day at a set time and gently picture your hopes for your baby in your mind — your little one will naturally grow toward the direction of those loving wishes.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 老鼠嫁女儿
fields.subtitle: 糊涂的老鼠爸爸
fields.subtitle_en: The Confused Mouse Father
fields.content:
从前有个老鼠爸爸，它有一个女儿，它特别疼爱女儿，把女儿视如掌上明珠。转眼老鼠女儿长大了，到了该出嫁的年纪。老鼠爸爸心想：“我一定要让宝贝女儿嫁给世界上最厉害的人。”
老鼠爸爸开始寻思谁才是最厉害的人呢？抬头看到了太阳，它想太阳很厉害，天下人都需要太阳，太阳一出来，天下就都光明了，谁都怕太阳不出来，于是它去找太阳。可太阳说：“我不是最厉害的，乌云一出来就把我遮住了，我见了乌云也害怕。”既然太阳都怕乌云，想必乌云是最厉害的。老鼠爸爸又去找乌云，可乌云说它也不是最厉害的，它怕大风。老鼠爸爸又去找大风，可大风说它也不是最厉害的，它怕围墙。老鼠爸爸又去找围墙。围墙说它还怕老鼠呢。老鼠爸爸一想老鼠怕猫，那猫就是最厉害的了，那就把女儿嫁给猫吧。老鼠爸爸越想越得意，就跟猫提亲了。猫当然愿意，还说：“喜事宜早不宜晚，我等不及要见你的女儿呢。看您这么帅，您的女儿一定也很漂亮。今天晚上就可以成亲了。”老鼠爸爸听了心里很受用，不过因为舍不得女儿马上出嫁，就提出第二天再成亲，猫勉强答应了。第二天，老鼠爸爸敲锣打鼓把女儿嫁给了猫，一桩心事终于了了。老鼠爸爸很满意，觉得自己真是聪明无比。
过了一段时间，老鼠爸爸去探望出嫁的女儿。到了猫的家里，没有见到女儿。于是它问猫：“我女儿呢？怎么没在家呀？”猫说：“哦，我怕别人欺负它，就把它藏到我肚子里去了。”它还边说边挤眉弄眼，叽叽咕咕地笑呢。老鼠爸爸生气了，可是它敢怒不敢言。不过，猫并没打算放过它，“啊呜”一口把老鼠爸爸也放到自己的肚子里去了。
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Mouse Who Married Off Her Daughter**

Once upon a time, there was a mouse father who had a daughter. He loved her more than anything in the world and treasured her like a precious jewel. Before he knew it, his little daughter had grown up and it was time for her to get married. The mouse father thought to himself, "I must make sure my darling daughter marries the most powerful person in all the land."

The mouse father began to wonder who could be the most powerful. He looked up and saw the sun shining brightly. "The sun is very powerful!" he thought. "Everyone in the world needs the sun. When it shines, everything becomes bright and warm, and everyone depends on it." So he went to visit the sun. But the sun said, "I'm not the most powerful. When clouds come, they cover me up, and I'm afraid of them." Since even the sun fears the clouds, the mouse father decided the clouds must be the most powerful. He went to visit the clouds, but the clouds said, "I'm not the most powerful either. I'm afraid of the wind." So the mouse father went to visit the wind. The wind said, "I'm not the most powerful. I'm afraid of the wall." The mouse father went to visit the wall. The wall said, "I'm afraid of mice!"

The mouse father thought, "Mice are afraid of cats! That means the cat is the most powerful of all! I'll marry my daughter to the cat!" The more he thought about it, the prouder he became. So he went to the cat to ask for his daughter's hand in marriage. The cat was very pleased and said, "Weddings should happen soon rather than late! I can hardly wait to meet your daughter. You're such a handsome father—your daughter must be lovely too. How about we hold the wedding tonight?" The mouse father was flattered, but because he couldn't bear to part with his daughter right away, he suggested the next day instead. The cat agreed, though a little reluctantly. The next day, the mouse father beat drums and gongs and happily gave his daughter away. At last, his worry was over. He felt very proud of himself and thought how clever he was.

After some time had passed, the mouse father went to visit his daughter at the cat's house. But when he arrived, he couldn't find her anywhere. "Where is my daughter?" he asked the cat. "Why isn't she here?" The cat smiled and winked slyly. "Oh," he said, "I was worried someone might bully her, so I hid her inside my belly." And as he spoke, he chuckled to himself. The mouse father was angry, but he didn't dare say anything. But the cat wasn't done with him. "Ahhh!" went the cat, and with one big bite, he swallowed the mouse father too.
fields.tips: 老鼠爸爸执著于找个最厉害的女婿，结果犯了糊涂，将女儿交到了对它垂涎欲滴的猫手里，不但害了女儿，最后还害了自己。在讲这个故事的时候，准妈妈可能会对老鼠爸爸的糊涂行为感到好笑，但有些时候，准妈妈在做胎教的时候，也会犯老鼠爸爸那样的错误哦，比如寻求最快速、最高效的捷径，或者特别频繁地进行胎教而不管胎宝宝是不是在休息。这样的胎教方式都对胎宝宝有害无益，轻则起不到胎教效果，重则影响胎宝宝发育。准妈妈做胎教不能太频繁，每天1～2次，每次5～10分钟就好；也不能太高深，讲的内容应该浅显易懂。
fields.tips_en: The mouse father was so determined to find the most powerful son-in-law that he acted foolishly and handed his daughter over to a cat who was drooling for her meal. He not only harmed his own daughter but ended up harming himself as well. While listening to this story, you may chuckle at the mouse father's silly mistakes — but sometimes, dear mom, you might make similar errors during your bonding time. This can happen when you seek the fastest or most efficient shortcut, or when you practice bonding too frequently without considering whether your baby needs a rest. Such approaches can be more harmful than helpful — lightly, they won't bring the desired results; seriously, they may affect your baby's development. Keep your bonding sessions gentle and balanced: once or twice a day, five to ten minutes each time is just right. And keep the content simple and easy for your little one to absorb.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 森林里的快乐晚会
fields.title_en: The Joyful Gathering in the Forest
fields.subtitle: 快乐是最重要的
fields.subtitle_en: Happiness Is What Matters Most
fields.content:
森林里要举办一年一度的快乐晚会了！
大象说：“开快乐晚会就是要唱歌跳舞。唱歌跳舞是小动物的事，我可参加不了。这样吧，我去帮它们布置会场吧。”
大象把河边的草地打扫得干干净净，搭起舞台，挂上彩纸，还在四周种上了鲜花。忙完这一切后，大象感到很满意，也很疲劳，便打了一个哈欠，躺下来睡着了。
晚上月亮出来了。噢！快乐晚会要在今夜举行。小动物们穿着漂亮的服装，纷纷来到小河边。
呀！它们发现大象睡着了，身上脏脏的，也没有穿晚会服装。
小动物们急坏了，现在到哪儿去为大象找一件特别大的服装呢。
“我们为大象准备帽子吧。”小鸭们嘎嘎叫着，下河摘荷叶，把它戴在大象头上。
“我们为大象准备衣服。”小鸟们飞进森林，衔来一片片绿叶，把它贴在大象身上。
大伙忙完后，就齐声把大象叫醒了。
“大象，你穿得这么漂亮，一定准备了很精彩的节目吧？”小动物们调皮地问。
大象看看自己身上，果然穿戴得很漂亮。啊，一定是小动物们帮自己准备的。
“我不会演节目。”大象不安地说。
“没关系，和我们一起跳舞吧！”小动物们说，“只要你跳得开心，感到快乐就行，谁也不会笑话你的。”
大象真的和小动物们跳起来了。它扭着粗笨的身子，感到很别扭，可心里却很快乐。
fields.content_en:
# The Happy Party in the Forest

A happy party was going to be held in the forest once a year!

The elephant said, "A happy party is about singing and dancing. That's for the little animals—I can't join in. How about I help them set up the venue instead?"

The elephant cleaned the grassy area by the river until it was spotless, built a stage, hung colorful paper decorations, and planted flowers all around. After finishing everything, the elephant felt quite pleased but also very tired, gave a big yawn, and lay down to sleep.

That night, the moon came out. Oh! The happy party was going to be held tonight. The little animals, dressed in beautiful clothes, gathered one by one at the riverside.

Oops! They noticed the elephant was fast asleep, covered in dirt and wearing no party clothes at all.

The little animals were worried. Where could they find a specially large outfit for the elephant?

"Let's make a hat for the elephant!" cried the ducklings. They jumped into the river and picked lotus leaves to wear on the elephant's head.

"Let's make clothes for the elephant!" said the birds. They flew into the forest and brought back green leaves, sticking them onto the elephant's body.

After everyone finished, they called out together to wake the elephant up.

"Elephant, you're dressed so nicely—you must have prepared a wonderful performance, right?" the little animals asked playfully.

The elephant looked down at itself and saw it was indeed dressed beautifully. Ah, the little animals must have helped get it ready.

"I don't know how to put on a show," said the elephant nervously.

"That's all right—just dance with us!" the little animals said. "As long as you're having fun and feel happy, nobody will laugh at you."

And so the elephant really did dance with the little animals. It twisted its bulky body, feeling a bit awkward, but its heart was full of joy.
fields.tips: 胎教最重要的，不是让胎宝宝学到多少知识，而是让胎宝宝感受到准妈妈的快乐情绪。准妈妈可以唱歌、跳舞或者画画，只要能让自己快乐就行，不用担心自己是不是水平不够，就像小动物们说的那样，只要跳得开心，感到快乐，谁也不会笑话的。看大象最后多开心啊！
fields.tips_en: The most important part of prenatal education is not what knowledge the baby learns, but that the baby feels your joyful emotions. Whether you sing, dance, or paint, simply do what makes you happy. Don't worry about your skills—just like the little animals said, if you dance with joy and feel happy, no one will laugh at you. See how wonderfully happy the elephant is in the end!
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 鹅的魔法
fields.subtitle: 勇气是困难的天敌
fields.subtitle_en: Courage Is the Bane of All Difficulties
fields.content:
一个小男孩叫尼盖。这个暑假，他想找个牧童的活干，可找了很久都没找着，大家都嫌他太小了。
不过，有一天，有个陌生人来到尼盖家说要请他做牧童。妈妈不太放心他去，但是尼盖坚持要去，也就让他去了。
尼盖跟着陌生人来到了一户孤零零的农舍，想必这是陌生人的家了。但是他家里却并没有羊，只有七只鹅，原来是让尼盖来放鹅的，主人还交给他一条黑狗，让狗帮着放鹅。
尼盖开始放鹅了。第一天，他把鹅带到一片草地上，刚刚安定下来，天空中就飞来一只巨大的老鹰，抓起一只鹅飞走了。回到家，主人发现鹅少了一只，就推了他一把，叫他明天放鹅仔细点儿。第二天，尼盖带着鹅远离草地，避开老鹰，到了森林边。刚刚以为安全了，突然从森林里冲出一只狼，叼起一只鹅就跑远了。回到家，主人发现又少了一只鹅，就打了尼盖一巴掌。第三天，尼盖到路边放鹅，结果被一个吉卜赛女人抢走一只鹅，回到家主人打了他两个耳光。第四天，尼盖到池塘边放鹅，不知道黑狗为什么狂追一只鹅，结果鹅掉到池塘里淹死了。第五天，尼盖到菜园去放鹅，一只鹅误吞了一条小毒蛇，痛得满地打滚也死了。第六天，尼盖把鹅带到广场上去放，一只鹅突然被狂风卷起来，眨眼间就飞得不见踪影了。每丢一只鹅，主人对他的惩罚就更重一些，上次他已经被主人狂揍了一顿，被打发到地窖去睡了。如果主人知道又丢了一只鹅，一定会打死他的。尼盖不敢回去，也怕别人知道他一天丢一只鹅，笑话他，所以决定去找回那些鹅。他把狗和剩下的一只鹅赶进农舍，就出发了。
尼盖先到山里，去找老鹰。老鹰住在很高的山上，山上不断有石头滚下来，但尼盖不怕，终于爬到山上，逮住了一只小鹰。他把小鹰的脚捆住送到动物园里。动物园的负责人很佩服他，用100法郎买下小鹰，还请他吃了一顿饭。尼盖又出发到森林里去找狼。森林里荆棘密布，但尼盖坚持往里走。他看到抓鹅的狼了，拼尽全身力气和狼搏斗，最后把狼掐死了。他用皮带把狼拖到动物园里，负责人更佩服他了，又给了他100法郎买下了他的狼，并请他吃饭。尼盖休息好了，继续出发，他要去找剩余的鹅。他先去找吉卜赛女人，抢到了她的金耳环，卖掉后获得了100法郎。再到池塘底下找淹死的鹅，结果找到一枚镶着珍珠的白金戒指，白金戒指也卖了100法郎。他又到处找毒死鹅的蛇，看到毒蛇就打死，最后打死了很多。他把它们捆成一捆交给村长，村长奖励他100法郎。最后他想找飞走的那只鹅，恰好城里正举行跳伞比赛，尼盖急忙报名，这样他就能飞到天上了。飞到天上后，尼盖急着找鹅，所以第一个跳下飞机，第一个落地了，得到了100法郎奖金。
现在尼盖有了这么多的钱，他想足够赔主人的鹅了，于是回到主人的农舍去。可是却发现主人和鹅都不见了，尼盖就拿着钱回家了。
（作者：贝阿丽特·贝克/法国）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Goose's Magic**

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Niguai. That summer, he wanted to find work as a shepherd, but no one would hire him because he was too small.

But one day, a stranger came to Niguai's house and said he wanted to hire him as a shepherd. Mama wasn't sure it was safe, but Niguai insisted, so she let him go.

Niguai followed the stranger to a lonely farmhouse. It was probably the stranger's home. But there were no sheep there at all—only seven geese. It turned out the job was to guard the geese. The owner also gave him a black dog to help watch the flock.

Niguai started his goose-herding job. On the first day, he led the geese to a grassy meadow. They had barely settled down when a giant eagle swooped from the sky and snatched one goose away. When they returned home, the owner noticed a goose was missing and gave Niguai a push, telling him to be more careful tomorrow. On the second day, Niguai led the geese far from the meadow to avoid the eagle, all the way to the edge of the forest. Just when he thought they were safe, a wolf suddenly burst from the forest and carried off another goose. Back home, the owner发现 another goose was gone and slapped Niguai. On the third day, Niguai took the geese to the roadside, and a Gypsy woman stole one. When he returned, the owner spanked him twice. On the fourth day, Niguai went to the pond, and the black dog began chasing a goose furiously for no reason—the goose fell into the water and drowned. On the fifth day, Niguai let the geese roam in a vegetable garden, where one goose swallowed a tiny poisonous snake and writhed in pain until it died. On the sixth day, Niguai took the geese to the square, when a fierce wind suddenly swept one goose away and it vanished in the blink of an eye. Each time a goose was lost, the owner punished him more harshly. Last time he had been beaten badly and sent to sleep in the cellar. If the owner found out another goose was lost, he would surely kill him. Niguai didn't dare go back. He was also afraid others would hear he lost a goose every day and make fun of him, so he decided to go find the geese himself. He drove the dog and the last remaining goose into the farmhouse and set off.

Niguai went to the mountains first to find the eagle. The eagle lived high up on a mountain where rocks tumbled down constantly, but Niguai wasn't afraid. He climbed to the top and caught a young eagle. He tied its feet and took it to the zoo. The zookeeper was amazed by his bravery and bought the young eagle for a hundred francs, and even invited him to a meal. Then Niguai set out for the forest to find the wolf. The forest was full of thick thorns, but Niguai pressed on. He found the wolf that had taken his goose and fought it with all his might, finally strangling it to death. He dragged the wolf to the zoo with a belt. The zookeeper admired him even more and bought the wolf for another hundred francs, and treated him to another meal. After resting, Niguai continued on his quest. First he found the Gypsy woman, took her golden earring, and sold it for a hundred francs. Then he went to the bottom of the pond to find the drowned goose—and instead discovered a platinum ring set with a pearl. The ring sold for a hundred francs. He searched everywhere for the snake that had poisoned his goose, beating any poisonous snake he saw until he had killed many. He bundled them together and took them to the village headman, who rewarded him with a hundred francs. Finally, he thought about finding the goose that had flown away. It happened that a skydiving competition was being held in town. Niguai quickly signed up so he could fly into the sky. Once airborne, Niguai was so eager to find his goose that he jumped from the plane first and landed first, winning a hundred francs prize.

Now Niguai had so much money that he felt it would be enough to pay the owner back for his geese. So he returned to the farmhouse. But when he arrived, both the owner and the geese were gone! Niguai simply took his money and went home.

*(Author: Béatrice Bec / France)*
fields.tips: 勇气可以帮助一个人克服所有困难。准妈妈怀孕后，享受甜蜜孕期的同时，常常会想到分娩的痛苦，时时有恐惧情绪，这就需要准妈妈拿出勇气来克服这种情绪。准妈妈恐惧，胎宝宝也会不安，因此，他的生长发育会受影响。
fields.tips_en: Courage can help you overcome every challenge. During your pregnancy, while enjoying the sweet moments, you may also think about the pain of childbirth and feel fear from time to time. Finding courage to face these feelings is so important. When you feel fearful, your baby may feel uneasy too, which can affect growth and development. So take a deep breath, let courage fill your heart, and let love guide you forward.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 蒂丽玲河
fields.subtitle: 不要听信甜言蜜语
fields.subtitle_en: Don't Be Fooled by Sweet Words
fields.content:
蒂丽玲河非常美，浅浅的笑窝，明亮的眼睛，长长的墨绿色头发，它的身材苗条、修长，婀娜多姿，真美啊！没有人敢说蒂丽玲河不美，连太阳、月亮、风都赞美它。它不禁想：“我多美啊，谁才能配得上我呢？”
大海爱上了美丽的蒂丽玲河，可蒂丽玲河嫌大海的味道太苦了，也不愿意跟大海一起忍受狂风暴雨和炎炎的烈日，更不愿意帮助大海运送船只，还嫌大海说话的声音太大了，不愿意跟大海在一起。它想，像它这么美丽的河，只应该被呵护、被疼爱、收礼物，哪能去受苦呢。
这时，池塘向蒂丽玲河求婚了。池塘说它可以用涟漪温暖蒂丽玲河，可以把睡莲和天上的白云送给蒂丽玲河，还能让山林为蒂丽玲河唱歌，让鲜花为蒂丽玲河开放。蒂丽玲河很高兴，池塘是多么喜欢它呀，能为它做这么多事，比大海好多了。
蒂丽玲河接受了池塘的求爱，可是池塘不能像大海一样涌起大浪把蒂丽玲河接走，所以蒂丽玲河只能自己去找池塘。路上沙子太多了，蒂丽玲河的水珠一直在减少，它越来越瘦，到达池塘的时候，已经变成一条细细的小溪，不再美丽了。池塘不再爱它了，最后它只剩下了几滴眼泪。
（作者：贝阿丽特·贝克/法国）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The River Tililing**

The River Tililing was very beautiful, with a gentle little smile, bright eyes, and long dark green hair. She was slim and graceful, truly lovely! No one could say that River Tililing wasn't beautiful—even the sun, the moon, and the wind all praised her. She couldn't help thinking, "How beautiful I am! Who could ever be good enough for me?"

The sea fell in love with beautiful River Tililing, but she thought the sea tasted too salty. She didn't want to endure stormy winds and scorching sun together with the sea, nor did she want to help the sea carry boats. She even thought the sea's voice was too loud and didn't want to be with it. She thought, a river as beautiful as her should only be cherished and loved and given gifts—how could she go through hardships?

Then the pond proposed to River Tililing. The pond said it could warm River Tililing with gentle ripples, could give her water lilies and white clouds from the sky, and could ask the mountains and forests to sing for her and flowers to bloom for her. River Tililing was very happy. How much the pond liked her! It could do so many things for her—much better than the sea.

River Tililing accepted the pond's love, but the pond could not rise up in great waves to come and take her away like the sea could. So River Tililing had to travel to find the pond herself. Along the way, there was too much sand, and her water drops kept disappearing. She grew thinner and thinner, and by the time she reached the pond, she had become a tiny, narrow stream—no longer beautiful at all. The pond no longer loved her, and in the end, she was left with only a few tears.

*(Author: Béatrice Beke / France)*
fields.tips: 大海的请求没有得到蒂丽玲河的回应，池塘的谄媚却获得了蒂丽玲河的欢心。怀孕的准妈妈特别敏感，容易感情用事，常常会因为准爸爸不够体贴、暖心而懊恼。如果出现了这样的情绪，准妈妈一定要提醒自己，站在准爸爸的角度去理解他。准爸爸为了整个家在外面努力打拼，回到家也有累的时候，就像大海，因为包容，所以难免有些苦涩。准妈妈如果能体贴、理解准爸爸，想必准爸爸也会产生更多感激之情。而夫妻恩爱、和睦，也能让胎宝宝感受到来自准父母的更多爱意。
fields.tips_en: In the story, the sea's sincere request went unanswered, while the pond's flattery won the river's affection. Pregnant mothers are often especially sensitive and emotional, and may feel upset when their partner doesn't seem thoughtful enough. If such feelings arise, try to remember to see things from your partner's perspective. He works hard outside for your whole family, and even he feels tired at times. Like the sea, his love may sometimes taste a little bitter, but it is deep and enduring. When you show understanding and kindness toward your partner, he will likely feel even more grateful. And when parents love and care for each other, your baby can feel that warm love every day.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: “公主怨”鸟
fields.subtitle: 微笑着面对生活
fields.subtitle_en: Face Life with a Smile
fields.content:
从前，有一位公主特别厌世。有一天，她觉得自己实在受不了了，就从宫里逃出来。逃出宫后，她边走边哭，走得筋疲力尽后倒在一片地上。她躺在地上，哭诉人类的卑劣和世界的脆弱，眼泪都流干了。公主流出的眼泪最后汇成了一个湖泊，就是“公主泪”湖。
眼泪流干的公主继续向前走，悲哀和疲劳使她再次停下来。公主站着，绝望地对着天空哀号，直到嗓子沙哑，再也发不出声音。她的哀号声变成了一群野鸟，就是“公主怨”鸟。
嗓子沙哑的公主继续向前走。最后走得疲惫不堪的她跪了下来，公主痛苦地使劲儿揪扯自己的头发。揪下来的头发变成了一片森林，就是“公主发”森林。
“公主泪”湖很不友好，它讨厌一切接近它的事物。它的水是苦涩的，不能喝。它不愿意天鹅在湖里游泳，不愿意睡莲在湖面开花，不愿意浇灌岸边的芦苇，就连月亮照个影子，它都要泛起浊浪，使月影丑陋，把月亮弄得很伤心。对人类就更不友好了，总是把毒蛇和毒蚊子送给来湖边洗衣服的人，用水草缠住来湖里游泳的人。尽管如此，“公主泪”湖仍然很不快乐，最后干脆躲入地下，永远不想再看地上的一切。
“公主发”森林一点儿都不美丽，到处是密布的荆棘，人们根本无法进去，而且树叶严密，一点儿阳光都进不去。森林里的树木不让鸟儿在它们的身上筑巢，也不让藤缠在它们身上。当风吹过森林，森林发出一片怒骂，使风感觉伤心。但是尽管如此，“公主发”森林心头的悲伤还是不能消除，最后它也沉入地下了，永远都不想再到上面来。
“公主怨”鸟一点儿都不讨人喜欢，羽毛又黑又灰，叫声也很难听，根本不能像别的鸟儿一样唱出动听的歌。当太阳照耀着它们的时候，它们把头藏在羽毛下，叫声更加凄厉，让太阳很伤心。但是鸟儿们依然感觉愤怒，它们最终也沉入地下了，不愿再到地上来。
过了很多年，有一个老妇人走到了“公主泪”湖和“公主发”森林所在的这条路上来。她满脸皱纹，眼皮发红，一看就知道饱经风霜，但是她的眼睛却炯炯有神。
老妇人走累了，她坐下休息。忽然，她听见地底下“公主泪”湖的哭声。老妇人说：“快上来吧，我想喝你的水。”话音刚落，就看到一滴水出现在草地上，迅速地变成溪流、变成湖泊。老妇人喝了一口湖里的水，湖水立刻变得香甜，也不再混浊，而且波光粼粼，显得纯洁、晶莹……
老妇人继续走，走累了，就又坐下休息。这次她听到了“公主发”森林的呻吟声。老妇人就跟森林说：“森林呀，回到地面上来吧，给我一点儿阴凉。”刚说完，就看见地面隆起来了，树木一棵棵地从地下长出来，老妇人抚摸着树木，树木立刻长出嫩芽，抖掉了所有的悲伤，为人类带来树荫，给鸟儿提供筑巢的枝条……
老妇人继续走路，走累了，就坐在地上休息。她听到了地底下传来的“公主怨”鸟发出的叫声。老妇人说：“快回到光明里来吧，我非常想看见你们。”“公主怨”鸟也啄破土地，回到地面上来了。老妇人摸摸鸟儿的喉咙，鸟儿唱出了动听的歌。
原来这个老妇人就是当初厌世的公主。
（作者：贝阿丽特·贝克/法国）
fields.content_en:
# "The Princess's Lament" Bird

Once upon a time, there was a princess who grew very weary of the world. One day, she felt she could bear it no longer, so she ran away from the palace. After escaping, she walked along crying, until she was so exhausted that she collapsed onto the ground. There she lay, weeping and complaining about how cruel people were and how fragile the world had become, until her tears had all run dry. The tears shed by the princess eventually gathered together into a lake, known as "Princess Tear" Lake.

With her tears spent, the princess continued walking. Sorrow and fatigue made her stop once again. She stood there and cried out in despair toward the sky, until her voice grew hoarse and she could no longer make a sound. Her lament turned into a flock of wild birds, which became the "Princess's Lament" Birds.

With her voice now hoarse, the princess kept walking. At last, worn out beyond measure, she fell to her knees. The princess, in her pain, desperately pulled at her hair. The hair she pulled out turned into a vast forest, known as "Princess Hair" Forest.

"Princess Tear" Lake was quite unfriendly. It disliked everything that came near it. Its water was bitter and undrinkable. It would not let swans swim within its waters, would not allow water lilies to bloom on its surface, and would not nourish the reeds growing along its banks. Even when the moon cast its reflection upon it, the lake would churn up muddy waves, making the moon's image ugly and deeply saddening the moon itself. As for people, it was even less kind—it would send snakes and poisonous mosquitoes to those who came to wash clothes by the lake, and it would tangle the swimming waters with seaweed to trap anyone who tried to swim in it. And yet, "Princess Tear" Lake remained deeply unhappy. In the end, it simply retreated underground and never wished to see the world above again.

"Princess Hair" Forest was not beautiful at all. Everywhere there were dense, tangled thorns, and no person could ever enter. Its leaves were so thick and close that not a single ray of sunlight could reach the ground. The trees of the forest would not let birds build nests upon them, nor would they allow vines to climb around them. When the wind blew through the forest, the forest would roar its anger, making the wind feel deeply sad. But even so, the sorrow in the heart of "Princess Hair" Forest could never be eased, and in the end, it too sank beneath the earth and never wished to rise again.

"Princess's Lament" Birds were not lovely creatures at all. Their feathers were black and grey, and their calls were harsh and unpleasant. They could never sing beautiful songs like other birds. When the sun shone upon them, they would hide their heads beneath their feathers, and their cries would grow even more piercing and mournful, which made the sun very sad. But the birds still felt angry inside, and in the end, they too sank underground and never wanted to return to the world above.

Many years passed. Then, one day, an old woman walked along the road that led to "Princess Tear" Lake and "Princess Hair" Forest. Her face was lined with wrinkles, and her eyelids were red—anyone could tell she had weathered many hardships. But her eyes still shone brightly.

The old woman grew tired and sat down to rest. Suddenly, she heard a weeping sound coming from underground—the voice of "Princess Tear" Lake. The old woman said, "Please come up. I would like to drink your water." And no sooner had she spoken than a drop of water appeared upon the grass, quickly swelling into a stream, then into a lake. The old woman took a sip of the water, and instantly the lake became sweet and clear, no longer cloudy or murky, but sparkling with pure, gentle light…

The old woman continued on her way. When she grew tired again, she sat down to rest. This time, she heard a low groaning coming from underground—from "Princess Hair" Forest. The old woman said to the forest, "Dear forest, please come back to the surface and give me some shade." No sooner had she finished speaking than the ground began to rise, and trees slowly grew upward from below the earth. The old woman gently touched the trunks, and instantly, tender green buds sprouted. The forest shook off all its sorrow and became a shelter of shade for people, offering branches for birds to build their nests…

The old woman kept walking. When she grew tired, she sat upon the ground to rest once more. She heard a faint calling rising from underground—the voice of the "Princess's Lament" Birds. The old woman said, "Please come back into the light. I so dearly want to see you." And the birds broke through the soil and returned to the surface. The old woman gently stroked the birds' throats, and they began to sing the most beautiful songs.

It turned out that this old woman was the very princess who had once grown weary of the world.

(Author: Béatrice Beck / France)
fields.tips: 有些孕妇会患上产前忧郁症，准妈妈如果发现自己有悲伤、厌世、消极的情绪，要特别注意，必要时要求助于医生，要意识到这是一个问题，从而有动力积极调整。毕竟心理问题必须自己有改变的要求，才能最终彻底消除。
fields.tips_en: Some mothers experience sadness before their baby arrives. If you notice feelings of sorrow, weariness, or hopelessness, please pay special attention to them. It is okay to ask for help from your doctor when needed. Recognizing these feelings is the first step, and with that awareness, you can find the strength to gently lift your spirits. Remember, emotional healing grows strongest when you allow yourself the courage to seek change and care.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 一个出卖心的人
fields.title_en: The One Who Sold His Heart
fields.subtitle: 有真心才能获得快乐
fields.subtitle_en: Only a True Heart Can Find True Joy
fields.content:
彼得的父亲已经过世，他和妈妈一起住在一间小木屋里。彼得靠烧炭维持母子二人的生活。
有一天，彼得对烧炭的工作感觉厌倦了。他想起父亲曾经讲过一个小玻璃人的故事：谁能唱出《小玻璃人》的四句山歌，小玻璃人就会给他很多钱。彼得想：“如果真能得到小玻璃人的帮助，那么我就再也不用烧炭了。”可是他跟妈妈只记得前三句，最后一句怎么也想不起来了。
彼得想到森林里碰碰运气，看能不能碰到小玻璃人。他在山中唱那支山歌，唱到第三句后，听到还有一个人在轻轻唱歌，唱的正是第四句。彼得高兴极了，把四句山歌一起唱了出来。歌唱完时，小玻璃人出现了，他戴着花帽子，穿着黑外套、白裤子，还穿着红袜子，长着一张和善的脸，还留着一簇小胡子，样子非常可爱。小玻璃人果然答应了彼得的要求，给了彼得2000个金币。
彼得有钱了，买了一家玻璃厂，认真管理着玻璃厂的生产。他对周围的人也很慷慨，遇到乞丐的时候总是给他们一些钱。他对妈妈很好，吃的穿的都给妈妈准备好了，不用妈妈再劳作。周围谁有困难来求彼得，彼得总是会解囊相助。谁都知道彼得有一副好心肠。
开始的时候，彼得对玻璃厂很上心，天天亲自督促生产，但没多久就感觉厌倦了。他整天沉迷在舞厅里，天天跳舞。很快，彼得的钱花光了，而玻璃厂因为彼得经营不善也不得不被拍卖掉。彼得又变成了穷光蛋，还背负了一大笔债务。
彼得又来到森林里找小玻璃人，想让小玻璃人帮他。但他的态度实在太坏了，把自己现在的麻烦都怪罪到小玻璃人的头上，还揪着小玻璃人的衣领不停地骂。小玻璃人生气了，变成了一段烧红的玻璃从彼得手中逃走了。彼得后悔了，但是小玻璃人没有再回来。就在彼得不知该怎么办的时候，身边出现了一个“荷兰鬼”。“荷兰鬼”告诉彼得，他可以像小玻璃人一样施魔法，能帮助彼得，但是彼得必须把心卖给他。彼得急着想要钱，就答应把心卖给“荷兰鬼”。“荷兰鬼”给了彼得10万个金币，用魔法把彼得的心取走了。
现在彼得有的是钱，他整天坐着豪华的马车四处游览，去听音乐会，去跳舞，但是，彼得总感觉不到快乐和幸福。当他回到家，妈妈笑着出来迎接他，他都感觉不到快乐。他还成了一个放债人。钱生钱，钱源源不断地流进他的口袋，但他仍然不快乐。后来，他娶了森林里最漂亮的少女做妻子，可是妻子也没能带给他快乐。因为彼得已经没有心了，感觉不到快乐了。
彼得不快乐，也不让别人快乐，他不肯给妈妈一个铜板，让妈妈不得不以乞讨为生。他把借了钱还不上的人都立刻送进监狱，也不允许妻子给乞丐任何帮助。他的心没有了，他变得麻木不仁。
大家都希望彼得变回原来的样子，劝他找回真心。彼得也想找回真心，他去找小玻璃人，在小玻璃人的帮助下，跟“荷兰鬼”赎回了真心。他的妈妈和妻子原谅了他。他们快乐地生活在一起了。
（作者：威廉·豪夫/德国）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Man Who Sold His Heart

Peter's father had already passed away, and he lived with his mother in a small wooden cabin. Peter made charcoal to support them both.

One day, Peter grew tired of making charcoal. He remembered a story his father had once told him about a little glass man: anyone who could sing the four lines of a mountain song about the little glass man would be given a great deal of money by him. Peter thought, "If only I could get help from the little glass man, then I would never have to make charcoal again." But he and his mother only remembered the first three lines; no matter how hard they tried, they could not recall the last line.

Peter decided to go into the forest and see if he could find the little glass man. He sang the mountain song in the mountains, and after the third line, he heard someone else singing softly—the very fourth line. Peter was overjoyed and sang all four lines together. When the song was finished, the little glass man appeared. He wore a flowered hat, a black coat, white pants, and red socks. He had a kind face and a small tuft of a mustache, and he looked terribly cute. The little glass man indeed kept his promise and gave Peter two thousand gold coins.

Peter now had money. He bought a glass factory and managed its production carefully. He was also generous to those around him, always giving money to beggars when he met them. He treated his mother very well, making sure she had everything she needed to eat and wear so she never had to work again. Whoever had trouble and came to ask Peter for help always found him willing to lend a hand. Everyone knew Peter had a kind heart.

At first, Peter was very devoted to the glass factory and personally supervised production every day. But soon he grew tired of it again. He spent his days沉迷 in dance halls, dancing every day. Soon, Peter ran out of money, and the glass factory, mismanaged by him, had to be auctioned off. Peter was poor once more, and he was heavily in debt.

Peter went back into the forest to find the little glass man, hoping he would help him again. But his attitude was terrible. He blamed all of his troubles on the little glass man and grabbed him by the collar, scolding him endlessly. The little glass man became angry and turned into a piece of glowing red glass, escaping from Peter's hands. Peter was filled with regret, but the little glass man did not come back. Just as Peter did not know what to do, a "Dutch ghost" appeared beside him. The Dutch ghost told Peter that he, too, could perform magic and could help him, but Peter would have to sell him his heart. Desperate for money, Peter agreed to sell his heart to the Dutch ghost. The Dutch ghost gave Peter one hundred thousand gold coins and used magic to take Peter's heart away.

Now Peter had plenty of money. He rode around in a luxurious carriage all day, going to concerts and dancing. But Peter could never feel happy or content. When he returned home and his mother came out smiling to greet him, he still felt nothing. He even became a moneylender. Money brought more money, flowing into his pockets endlessly, but he remained unhappy. Later, he married the most beautiful girl in the forest, but she, too, could not bring him happiness. For Peter no longer had a heart and could no longer feel joy.

Peter was unhappy, and he did not let others be happy either. He refused to give his mother a single copper coin, forcing her to earn a living by begging. He sent anyone who could not repay their debt straight to prison and would not even let his wife give anything to beggars. His heart was gone, and he had become numb and cruel.

Everyone hoped Peter would return to his old self and urged him to find his heart again. Peter also longed to get his heart back. With the help of the little glass man, he redeemed his heart from the Dutch ghost. His mother and his wife forgave him, and they all lived happily together.

(Author: Wilhelm Hauff / Germany)
fields.tips: 真心不但是获得快乐的基础，也是与人快乐沟通所必需的。准妈妈和胎宝宝沟通也依靠一颗真心。准妈妈越真心地爱胎宝宝，宝宝将来对妈妈的接受度就越高。
fields.tips_en: A genuine heart is the foundation of happiness and the key to joyful connection with others. Your communication with your baby also rests on a sincere and loving heart. The more truly you love your baby, the more warmly your little one will receive you in the days ahead. Let your love be open, honest, and full of light.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 辛伯达航海历险记
fields.title_en: The Adventures of Sinbad the Sailor
fields.subtitle: 勇气加头脑，可以战胜一切困难
fields.subtitle_en: With courage and wisdom, all difficulties can be overcome
fields.content:
辛伯达住在巴格达，是一名脚夫，日子过得很贫穷。他不想再继续这样平淡地过日子了，就变卖了所有的家当，搭上了一条远洋的船，去旅行了。
海上航行很顺利，一天他到达了一个小岛。这个小岛非常美丽，有茂密的森林、潺潺的小溪，鲜花遍地开放，小鸟在无忧无虑地歌唱，是以前到过的任何一个地方都无法比拟的。辛伯达很喜欢，就一个人往岛内走去。走到一条小溪边，辛伯达坐了下来，吃着干粮，喝着泉水，看着小鸟，不知不觉躺在草地上睡着了。
辛伯达醒来了，这一觉睡得好舒服啊。他站起身慢慢向海边走去。当走到海边的时候，辛伯达傻眼了，船已经走了，只把他一个人留下了。这可怎么办呢？小岛虽然美丽，但是个荒岛，根本没有人烟。辛伯达无奈地在小岛上到处走，他希望可以找到土著的居民。在傍晚的时候，辛伯达果然看到远处有一个白色的大房子。只是房子是圆形的，像个大鸡蛋。可能是土著特有的房子吧，辛伯达心想。辛伯达走到房子前，绕着房子走了好几圈都没有找到门，连窗户也没有。正当他纳闷儿的时候，突然天变暗了，他以为是乌云遮住了太阳。他抬头一看，一只巨大的鹰正飞过来。辛伯达瞬间明白过来，这个大白房子并不是房子，其实是这只鹰的蛋。辛伯达急忙藏了起来，躲在树丛后面悄悄观察鹰。
鹰飞来后，就趴在蛋上睡着了。辛伯达看着鹰巨大的爪子，想到了一个离开这里的好办法。他解下了自己的缠头布，趁鹰熟睡的时候，用缠头布把自己紧紧绑在鹰的爪子上，这样鹰就可以把他带到别的地方去了。但愿能去个有人烟的地方。
第二天，太阳升起后，鹰就起飞了。鹰飞了好久，终于在一个山谷里降落下来。趁鹰休息的时候，辛伯达急忙把缠头布解开，从鹰的爪子上下来，心想终于离开那个小岛了。可是没多久，他就高兴不起来了，因为这里还不如小岛呢。这是一个荒凉的山谷，两边峭壁耸立，山谷里不但没有人，连泉水和野果都没有。
辛伯达着急地在山谷里往前走去，走着走着，他看到一大块新鲜的羊肉。他走过去翻开一看，底下的羊肉上沾满了耀眼的钻石。辛伯达想起来，以前听说过，在一些山谷里盛产钻石，可是人们无法下去采集，就把羊肉丢下去，羊肉上会沾满钻石。鹰看到羊肉就会飞过来把羊肉叼上平地。这时人们就用石头砸鹰，鹰就会丢下羊肉飞走，人们就可以把羊肉上的钻石捡起来了。眼前的这块羊肉肯定也是这个功能。想到这里，辛伯达又有了主意。他马上捡钻石，把衣袋和鞋子都装满了，然后把羊肉用缠头布捆在自己身上，最后伏在谷底，静静等待鹰的到来。果然过了一会儿，一只鹰就飞来了，鹰抓起羊肉就往上飞，当然还带着辛伯达。
当鹰带着羊肉和辛伯达降落在平地的时候，石头像雨点般地砸向鹰，鹰挥动翅膀逃走了。辛伯达把自己从羊肉上解下来，他终于得救了。
辛伯达很感谢这些采钻石的人，把自己的钻石给他们分了很多。他还留了一部分钻石作为继续航海的资本。
（选自《一千零一夜》）
fields.content_en:
Title: Sindbad’s Sea Adventures

Sindbad lived in Baghdad and worked as a porter. Life was very poor for him. He did not want to go on living such an ordinary life anymore, so he sold everything he had, boarded a big ship, and set off on a journey.

The sea voyage went smoothly, and one day he arrived at a small island. This little island was so beautiful, with thick forests, babbling streams, flowers blooming everywhere, and birds singing carefree songs. It was more wonderful than any place he had ever been before. Sindbad liked it very much, so he walked alone deeper into the island. When he reached a stream, he sat down, ate his dry food, drank the spring water, watched the little birds, and before long, fell asleep on the grass.

Sindbad woke up. That was such a comfortable nap. He got up and slowly walked toward the sea. But when he reached the shore, he was completely stunned. The ship had already sailed away, leaving him all alone. What was he to do? The island was beautiful, but it was deserted and there was no sign of anyone. Helplessly, Sindbad wandered all over the island, hoping to find some local people. In the evening, he finally saw a big white house in the distance. But the house was round, like a giant egg. Perhaps it was a special kind of house belonging to the natives, Sindbad thought. When he arrived at the house, he walked around it several times but could not find a door, nor a window. Just as he was puzzled, the sky suddenly grew dark, and he thought dark clouds had covered the sun. He looked up and saw a giant eagle flying toward him. Sindbad suddenly understood. That big white “house” was not a house at all—it was the eagle’s egg! Hurriedly, he hid behind a bush and quietly watched the eagle.

After the eagle landed, it lay down on the egg and fell asleep. Sindbad looked at the eagle’s huge claws and came up with a great idea for getting away. He untied his headcloth and, while the eagle was sound asleep, tied himself tightly to its claw, so that the eagle would carry him to some other place. Hopefully, it would be somewhere with people.

The next day, after the sun rose, the eagle took off. The eagle flew for a long time and finally landed in a valley. While the eagle was resting, Sindbad quickly untied himself and climbed down from its claw, thinking that at last he was away from that little island. But soon he was no longer happy, because this place was even worse than the island. It was a barren valley with steep cliffs on both sides. There were not only no people, but no spring water or wild fruit either.

Sindbad walked anxiously through the valley. As he went on, he saw a large piece of fresh mutton. He walked over and turned it over, only to find that the meat underneath was covered with dazzling diamonds. Sindbad remembered having heard before that some valleys were rich in diamonds, but people could not go down to collect them. So they would throw pieces of mutton into the valley, and the diamonds would stick to the meat. When the eagle saw the mutton, it would fly down and carry it to the flat ground. Then people would throw rocks at the eagle, which would drop the meat and fly away, allowing the people to pick up the diamonds. This mutton in front of him must have the same purpose. Thinking this, Sindbad had another idea. He immediately started gathering diamonds, filling his pockets and shoes to the brim. Then he tied the mutton around himself with his headcloth and lay quietly at the bottom of the valley, waiting for the eagle to come. Sure enough, after a while, an eagle flew down, picked up the mutton, and flew upward—with Sindbad along.

When the eagle landed on the flat ground with the mutton and Sindbad, stones rained down upon it. The eagle flapped its wings and fled. Sindbad untied himself from the mutton. At last, he had been saved.

Sindbad was very grateful to those diamond miners and shared many of his diamonds with them. He also kept a portion of the diamonds to fund his further voyages.

(Adapted from One Thousand and One Nights)
fields.tips: 准妈妈虽然不适合冒险，但是可以去旅游。在怀孕5～6个月的时候，胎宝宝已经稳定，自己身体还较轻便的时候最好。孕期旅行会成为一生中最美好的一段回忆，同时可以给胎宝宝做很多胎教，像美学胎教、运动胎教和情绪胎教等。
fields.tips_en: While adventure may not be suitable for expectant mothers, traveling is a wonderful idea. The best time is around the fifth or sixth month of pregnancy, when the baby has settled and you still feel light and agile. A孕期 journey can become one of the most beautiful memories of your life, while also offering wonderful opportunities for prenatal bonding—through aesthetic stimulation, gentle movement, and nurturing a calm, joyful mood.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 水晶姑娘
fields.subtitle: 诚实像水晶一般美好
fields.subtitle_en: Honesty is as beautiful as crystal
fields.content:
水晶姑娘是个透明美丽的玻璃人，不但漂亮，嗓音也特别好听。大家都喜欢听她唱歌。
爸爸妈妈自然很喜欢她，但总担心她会碎掉，于是妈妈就经常给她系上一条蝴蝶结，在上面绣上“易碎”两个字，预防别人不小心伤到她。
人们喜欢水晶姑娘还有一个原因，就是水晶姑娘非常诚实，从来不说谎话，只会说真话。
这天是水晶姑娘的生日，爸爸给了她一百块钱，让她去玩儿。可是，刚离开家不久，水晶姑娘就发现她的钱丢了。水晶姑娘找啊找啊，怎么也找不到。她的水晶心叮当叮当地响起来，她的眼睛里也满是晶莹的泪水。
天晚了，水晶姑娘不得不回家去。回到家，爸爸问她：“今天玩得好吗？”水晶姑娘点点头，这时她听到身体里“咔嚓”响了一声。水晶姑娘走进屋里躺下，这时妈妈来看她，问她：“你玩得好吗？”水晶姑娘刚说“好”，她的身体就突然炸裂了，发出了可怕的声音。水晶姑娘碎成了一千块碎片。
妈妈找到接骨医生把一千块碎片接好了，可是水晶姑娘再也不能动了，她变成了一尊雕像。
（作者：贝阿丽特·贝克/法国）
fields.content_en:
**The Crystal Girl**

The Crystal Girl was a beautiful glass figure, clear and shining. She was not only lovely to look at, but her voice was wonderfully sweet, too. Everyone loved to hear her sing.

Her mommy and daddy naturally adored her, but they always worried she might break. So her mommy often tied a pretty bow around her neck, embroidered with the words “Fragile,” to remind others to be careful near her.

People also loved the Crystal Girl because she was very honest. She never told a lie and only ever spoke the truth.

One day was the Crystal Girl’s birthday, and her daddy gave her a hundred coins to go play with. But hardly had she left home when she discovered her coins were missing. She searched and searched, but just could not find them. Her crystal heart began to chime with a tinkling sadness, and her eyes filled with glistening tears.

It was getting late, and the Crystal Girl had to go home. When she arrived, her daddy asked her, “Did you have fun today?” The Crystal Girl nodded. Then she heard a small *crack* inside her body. She went into her room and lay down. Her mommy came to see her and asked, “Did you have fun today?” The Crystal Girl just said, “Yes”—and suddenly her body shattered with a terrible sound. She broke into one thousand tiny pieces.

Her mommy found a bone-setting doctor who carefully pieced the thousand fragments back together. But the Crystal Girl could no longer move. She became a statue.

(Author: Béatrice Beck / France)
fields.tips: 水晶姑娘只要说假话就会碎裂。准妈妈读这个故事的时候，可以给胎宝宝描述一下水晶的样子，告诉胎宝宝水晶的特性，并说明透明、晶莹这些词与诚实的关系。
fields.tips_en: In this tale, the Crystal Maiden shatters whenever she tells a lie. As you read this story to your baby, describe the lovely sparkle and clarity of crystal, and gently explain how words like transparent and clear connect to the precious quality of honesty.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 教士和鼬鼠
fields.subtitle: 遇事不慎重，必然要懊悔
fields.subtitle_en: Carelessness in action leads to regret
fields.content:
从前有个教士，妻子怀孕了，他非常高兴，禁不住憧憬起未来的日子来。教士对妻子说：“希望是个男孩，我要为他取个好名字，给他聘请大学者当教师，让他成才。将来还要娶个和你一样美貌和富有的妻子……”妻子打断了他说：“这些都是将来的事了，现在说没有任何意义。”她说着莞尔一笑：“我看你现在的样子跟那个满头流蜜的教士很像呢。”“满头流蜜的教士？”教士一听很感兴趣，问：“那是怎么回事？”妻子就给他讲了这个故事。
“有一个教士，有个商人每天都送给他一些蜂蜜，除了吃，还能剩下一些。他就把这些剩下的蜂蜜放在罐子里，挂在房梁上。时间久了，竟然存了满满一罐子。
“有一天，教士手里拿着手杖，靠在床上，看着房梁上的蜂蜜。他突然想到：‘现在蜂蜜价格很高，如果我把这一罐蜂蜜卖了，可以卖一磅钱呢。这样，我用这一磅钱可以买10只羊；羊长大了，每五个月就可以生一胎，10只羊最少可以再生10只。这样大羊生小羊，小羊长大以后再生小羊，过不了多久，我就有一群羊了。然后我把羊卖了，买些田地和牛，种庄稼，再过几年，我就能请用人，盖大房子，娶个美丽的妻子，生个漂亮的孩子，给他取个好名字，请大学者给他做教师。然后再给他娶个美丽的妻子。’教士越想越高兴，忍不住站起来手舞足蹈。谁知手里的手杖‘咣’的一声就打在了房梁上的蜜罐上。蜜罐破了，蜂蜜流了教士一头。教士的羊、牛、田地、美丽妻子、漂亮孩子统统都没有了。”
教士听完故事，嘿嘿笑了。他说：“还真是的，将来的事还是不要瞎妄想的好。”
后来，妻子果然生下了一个可爱的男孩。夫妻两个自然都很高兴。有一天，妻子要沐浴，就把孩子交给教士照顾，自己进沐浴室去了。恰巧这时，国王要召见教士，教士没有人可以托付照顾孩子，就把孩子交给自己从小养的一只鼬鼠。教士走后不久，突然从墙洞里爬出一条蛇。鼬鼠勇敢地冲上前和蛇搏斗，终于把蛇咬死了。鼬鼠为确保安全，还把蛇咬成了几节。
教士觐见国王后马上赶回家里，鼬鼠急忙跑去迎接，想让教士知道自己干了多么了不起的事。结果教士看见鼬鼠嘴上的血，以为鼬鼠咬死了孩子。本来，教士很爱鼬鼠，像爱自己的儿女一样，可现在满腔愤怒，举起手杖一下就把鼬鼠打死了。
教士急忙跑到卧室去看孩子，却看到孩子好端端地躺在床上，旁边还摆着几节蛇，他这才知道自己错怪了鼬鼠。教士后悔得捶胸顿足。他跟妻子说：“我恩将仇报。鼬鼠保护了我们的孩子，我却打死了鼬鼠。”接着又说：“早知道，我宁可不要这个孩子，那我就不会做这种亏心事了。”可是他再怎么后悔也已经无济于事了。
妻子则说：“这跟有没有这个孩子没有关系，完全是你自己的问题。”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Priest and the Weasel

Once upon a time, there was a priest whose wife was pregnant. He was overjoyed and couldn't help but daydream about the future. He told his wife, "I hope it's a boy. I'll give him a fine name and hire a great scholar as his teacher, so he'll grow up to be accomplished. And when he grows up, he can marry a wife who is as beautiful and wealthy as you…" His wife gently interrupted him, "That's all for the future. There's no point talking about it now." She smiled softly and said, "You know, you sound just like that priest whose head was covered in honey."

"The priest covered in honey?" The priest was quite interested. "What happened there?" So his wife told him the story.

"There was a priest who had a merchant who brought him some honey every day. Besides eating it, he always had some left over. He kept putting the extra honey into a jar and hanging it from the beam of his house. Before long, the jar was completely full.

"One day, the priest was leaning on his bed with a staff in his hand, gazing up at the jar of honey on the beam. Suddenly he thought, 'Honey is very expensive now. If I sell this jar, I can get a pound of money. With that pound, I can buy ten sheep. When the sheep grow up, they can have a lamb every five months, so my ten sheep could have at least ten more. Soon, big sheep will have little sheep, and little sheep will grow up and have their own. Before I know it, I'll have a whole flock! Then I can sell the sheep, buy some land and cows, farm the land, and in a few years I'll be able to hire servants, build a big house, and marry a beautiful wife and have a lovely child. I'll give him a fine name and hire a great scholar to be his teacher. And when he grows up, I'll find him a beautiful wife too.' The priest grew happier and happier with each thought, until he couldn't help himself — he stood up and danced with joy. But when he moved, his staff went 'clang!' and struck the honey jar on the beam. The jar broke, and honey poured all over the priest's head. His sheep, his cows, his land, his beautiful wife, and his lovely child — all of it vanished."

The priest listened and chuckled. "Well," he said, "you're right. It's no good dreaming about things that haven't happened yet."

Later, his wife indeed gave birth to a lovely baby boy, and both parents were delighted. One day, his wife wanted to take a bath, so she handed the baby to the priest to watch while she went into the bathing room. Just then, the king sent for the priest. Having no one else to leave the child with, he placed the baby beside his weasel, whom he had raised since it was small.

Soon after the priest left, a snake crept through a hole in the wall. The weasel bravely rushed forward and fought the snake, eventually biting it to death. To make sure it was truly safe, the weasel bit the snake into several pieces.

After audience with the king, the priest hurried home. The weasel ran eagerly to greet him, wanting to show what a wonderful thing it had done. But when the priest saw the blood on the weasel's mouth, he thought the weasel had killed his child. The priest loved the weasel dearly, as if it were his own child — yet in a burst of anger, he raised his staff and struck the weasel dead.

He rushed into the bedroom to check on the baby, only to find the child lying safe and sound in his crib, with the pieces of snake beside him. He realized he had wronged the weasel. He beat his chest and wailed in regret. He told his wife, "I repaid kindness with cruelty. The weasel protected our child, and I killed it." He added, "If I had known, I would rather not have had this child at all — then I wouldn't have done such a guilty thing." But no amount of regret could bring the weasel back to life.

His wife said, "This has nothing to do with whether we had the child or not. This is your own doing."
fields.tips:
童话故事有很多都有讽刺意味，比如《豌豆上的公主》《小农民》《夜莺》《皇帝的新装》等。这篇故事里的教士就是一个被讽刺的对象，浅薄、虚荣、不负责任等都是他的特点。
教士遇事不慎重让他办了错事。对孕期的准妈妈来说，遇事慎重做决定是基本要求。准妈妈无论做什么事情都要先为胎宝宝考虑，想一下后果，避免作出事后后悔的事情。
fields.tips_en: Many fairy tales carry a gentle satire. Stories like The Princess on the Pea, The Little Farmer, The Nightingale, and The Emperor's New Clothes all whisper playful lessons. In this tale, the priest is the one being gently teased—his shallowness, vanity, and irresponsibility shine through. Acting without careful thought led him astray. For you, dear mother, taking a thoughtful pause before making decisions during pregnancy is so important. Always keep your baby in your heart, consider the consequences, and choose wisdom over haste.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 太阳、月亮和风
fields.title_en: The Sun, the Moon, and the Wind
fields.subtitle: 有关自然现象的美丽传说
fields.subtitle_en: A beautiful legend about the wonders of nature
fields.content:
太阳、月亮和风在古时候是三兄弟，星辰是它们的妈妈。有一天，雷神和电神请它们吃饭，但是它们的母亲因为要上班，必须在天上发光发亮，所以没办法去。母亲就叮嘱三兄弟，让它们吃完后给自己也带一点儿回来。
太阳和风都很贪吃，低着头只管吃，根本没有想到正在工作的母亲。而月亮却总是记着母亲，每吃一道菜，都挑出一点儿，装到随身携带的袋子里，准备带回去给母亲吃。
太阳、月亮和风吃完饭后一起回家去。到家了，母亲问它们：“你们吃得好吗？有没有带什么回来给我吃？”太阳回答说：“对不起母亲，我吃得非常爽快，但把您忘了，我没有给您带什么。”风理直气壮地说：“东西太少了，我自己都不够吃呢，所以也没有给您带。”只有月亮很温柔地对妈妈说：“有，有，母亲，我带了一包好东西给您呢。”说着，解开衣服把袋子取出来，把食物都给母亲吃了。
母亲对月亮的行为感到很欣慰。它对月亮说：“你在快乐当中，也没有忘记母亲，我要奖赏你。从今天起，你的光芒会非常温和、清凉、洁白，你的外形也会光亮、好看，让大家都喜欢你。”
母亲转过脸对太阳说道：“你在快乐当中忘了母亲，我现在要罚你。从今以后，你每年都有一段时间发大热，炙烤着人们，使人们都不喜欢你。看到你在天上，就一定要用东西遮盖着头，避免你的光线照到他。”
接着，母亲又转过来对风说：“你在快乐当中忘了母亲，我也要罚你。从今天起，你会不定时地用力吹，把沙粒、尘土都吹起来，让人们都讨厌你。”
太阳、月亮和风就变成了现在的样子。太阳暴晒的时候人人讨厌，刮大风的时候人人讨厌。只有月亮一直那么柔和、安详，始终受到所有人的喜欢。
fields.content_en:
**The Sun, the Moon, and the Wind**

A long, long time ago, the Sun, the Moon, and the Wind were three brothers. Their mother was the Stars, who shone brightly overhead.

One day, the Thunder God and the Lightning God invited them to a meal. But their mother had to work that day — she had to stay in the sky and keep shining — so she could not come. Before they left, she asked her three sons to save a little bit of food for her on their way back.

The Sun and the Wind were very greedy. They bowed their heads and ate and ate, thinking only of themselves. They did not think of their mother working up in the sky. But the Moon was different. Every time a dish was served, the Moon would pick out a small piece and put it gently into the little bag he always carried, saving it all for his mother.

When they finished eating, the three brothers traveled home together. When they arrived, their mother asked, "Did you enjoy your meal? Did you bring anything back for me?"

The Sun answered, "I am sorry, Mother. I ate very happily, but I forgot about you. I did not bring you anything."

The Wind stood tall and said, "I did not bring enough for you. There was not much, and I needed it all myself."

But the Moon spoke softly and said, "Yes, yes, Mother! I brought you something very special." He untied his clothes, took out his little bag, and gave all the food he had saved to his mother. She ate every bit.

Their mother was so happy to see how thoughtful the Moon had been. She said to him, "You remembered me even while you were having fun. I want to bless you. From this day on, your light will be gentle and cool and white. Your face will shine beautifully, and everyone will love looking at you."

Then she turned to the Sun and said, "You forgot your mother in your joy. So I must give you a lesson. From now on, you will have times when you grow very hot and shine too strongly. People will cover their heads to hide from your harsh rays."

She turned to the Wind and said, "You also forgot your mother. So you will blow suddenly and wildly at times, stirring up sand and dust, and people will not always like you."

And that is why the Sun, the Moon, and the Wind are the way they are today. When the Sun is too hot, people wish for shade. When the Wind blows too hard, people wish for calm. But the Moon has always been gentle and peaceful, and everyone loves to look up and see her shining softly in the night sky.
fields.tips: 这个故事对太阳、月亮和风的自然现象展开了奇妙的想象。准妈妈可以给胎宝宝讲讲太阳暴晒、大风刮起来以及明月当空的情形和给人的感觉，让胎宝宝认识这些自然现象。也别忘了告诉胎宝宝，以后要做一个孝顺母亲的好孩子哦。
fields.tips_en: This story paints a wonderfully imaginative picture of the sun, the moon, and the wind. Share with your baby the warmth of the sun's embrace, the mighty rush of the wind, and the soft glow of the moonlit sky—help your little one begin to understand the beauty of the natural world. And don't forget to whisper that one day, they too will grow up to be a loving and filial child.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 狼来了
fields.subtitle: 撒谎会失去人们的信任
fields.subtitle_en: Telling lies will make people stop trusting you
fields.content:
从前，有个孩子每天都要赶着羊到山上去放。山下有很多农田，农夫们都在那里忙碌。
有一天，放羊娃躺在草坡上，觉得实在无聊，就想逗逗山下的农夫。他站起来，冲着山下大喊：“狼来了，狼来了，快救救我啊！”农夫们一听，急忙拿着锄头和镰刀往山上跑，边跑还边喊：“别怕，别怕，我们来帮你把狼打跑。”待农夫们气喘吁吁地跑到山上，连狼的影子也没看到。看着农夫们着急的样子，放羊娃哈哈大笑，说：“你们上当了，我是逗你们玩儿的。”农夫们摇摇头说他太顽皮了，就转身都下山继续忙去了。
第二天，放羊娃故技重施，又把农夫们骗了一次，农夫们生气地走了。
过了几天，真的有一只狼冲着放羊娃的羊群过来了。放羊娃着急地大喊：“狼来了，狼来了，救命啊！”可是没有人理他。他急得继续喊：“狼真的来了，我没有骗你们！”但还是没有人来。结果，放羊娃的羊被狼咬死了好几只。
（选自《伊索寓言》）
知识
lian
接
在童话故事中，狼的形象总是和凶残、贪婪等挂钩。其实，狼本身并无所谓狡猾或贪婪之本性，只是因为狼在狩猎时的习性以及智慧让人感觉如此。而狼的智慧和勇猛，也让蒙古等民族把它视为图腾。准妈妈有兴趣的话可以阅读畅销书《狼图腾》。这部作品在2015年由中法合拍了同名电影，也非常精彩。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who took his sheep up to the hill every day to graze. Below the hill were many green fields, where farmers were busy working.

One day, the boy lay down on the grassy slope and felt quite bored. So he decided to play a little trick on the farmers down below. He stood up and called out loudly, "Wolf! Wolf! Come quick, please help me!" Hearing this, the farmers hurriedly picked up their hoes and sickles and ran up the hill. They shouted, "Don't be afraid! Don't be afraid! We're coming to chase the wolf away!" But when they arrived, out of breath, they couldn't find a single trace of a wolf. Seeing how worried everyone looked, the boy burst out laughing. "You've been fooled!" he said. "I was just playing with you!" The farmers shook their heads, saying he was too naughty, and then they turned around and went back down the hill to continue their work.

The next day, the boy played the same trick again, fooling the farmers a second time. This time, the farmers left in anger.

A few days later, a real wolf did come toward the boy's flock. The boy called out in fear, "Wolf! Wolf! Help me!" But no one came. He cried out again, "It's really a wolf! I'm not lying to you!" Still, no one came. In the end, the wolf hurt and killed several of the sheep.
(Adapted from Aesop's Fables)

Now here's a little something special for you, Mommy.

In fairy tales, wolves are often shown as fierce and greedy creatures. But actually, wolves aren't naturally cunning or greedy. It's just that their way of hunting and their cleverness make people think that way. In fact, wolves are wise and brave animals, and the Mongolian people, among others, have even regarded them as a sacred symbol. If you feel curious, Mommy, you might enjoy reading the bestselling book *Wolf Totem*. In 2015, China and France made a beautiful movie based on it, and it's truly wonderful to watch.
fields.tips: 《狼来了》的故事短小精悍，孩子很喜欢听，也能很快让孩子明白不能撒谎的道理。准妈妈可以和准爸爸一起念这个故事，让准爸爸进行一下角色扮演，这样会更生动，胎教效果也会更好。
fields.tips_en: This short and lively tale is a favorite among children and gently teaches them the importance of truthfulness. Reading it together with your partner can make it even more special—invite the expectant father to act out the parts! A lively storytelling session like this brings the story to life and makes the prenatal bonding even more meaningful.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 美女与野兽
fields.subtitle: 真爱改变性情
fields.subtitle_en: True Love Changes Hearts
fields.content:
从前有个王子，他很自私。在一个寒冷的冬夜里，有个老婆婆请求允许她在王子的城堡里避避寒，但王子无论如何都不肯答应。老婆婆就把他变成了一头丑陋的野兽，把他的仆人变成了各种器皿。原来老婆婆是个女巫。女巫走的时候留了一支玫瑰给王子，告诉他玫瑰花会盛开到王子21岁的时候。如果在玫瑰花凋谢之前，他能学会爱别人，也得到别人的爱，魔法就能破除，他就能恢复人形。如果不能，那么他将永远不能恢复人形。
几年后，在城堡附近的一个村子里，姑娘贝儿长大了。这天贝儿的爸爸莫维斯让一匹叫费立的马驾着车，拉着他的新发明去参加展览会。但是在夜里，他们进入了一个森林里后就迷路了，还受到了一群野狼的攻击。情急之下，费立拉着车拼命奔跑，最后逃进了王子的城堡。
在这个城堡里，所有的器皿都会说话。沙发请莫维斯坐下休息，茶壶请他喝茶。然而这里还有一只野兽，野兽怒气冲冲地下令把他关进牢房。
费立跑回家，把贝儿带到了城堡。器皿们看到贝儿都很兴奋，她如此美丽，看上去也很善良。如果王子能和贝儿相爱，那么魔法就会破除，他们就能恢复人形了。
在城堡里，贝儿答应野兽让自己做他的犯人，把爸爸救了出去。这样贝儿就在城堡里住了下来，她得到了所有家具和器皿的爱护。
有一天，贝儿好奇地走进野兽的房间，结果被野兽发现了。野兽曾告诉贝儿不准她进这个房间，所以野兽发火了。贝儿吓坏了，冲出了城堡。刚出城堡，森林里的狼群就开始攻击她，但是野兽出现了。他把狼群打退，自己也受伤了。
此后，贝儿照顾着受伤的野兽，还常常念书给他听，并教导他用餐的礼仪，教他跳舞。他们的感情越来越深厚。
野兽有一面魔镜，能看到外面的世界。贝儿用魔镜看到了爸爸正在找她，就想去找爸爸。野兽尽管舍不得贝儿走，但还是让她走了，并且给她带上了魔镜，请求她能常常看看自己。
贝儿和爸爸回到家后，村里的一个青年加斯顿来了。他一直想让贝儿嫁给他，但是贝儿拒绝了。这次他带着很多村民一起来了，并威胁贝儿说：“你爸爸一直在村子里说什么野兽的浑话，如果你不嫁给我，我就跟大家说他疯了，把他关起来。”
贝儿拿出魔镜，让大家从魔镜里看到了野兽，证明了莫维斯说的是真话。但加斯顿鼓动村民跟他一起去打死野兽，还把贝儿和爸爸关了起来。
小茶杯在贝儿离开城堡的时候偷偷跳进了她的衣袋，所以现在它跟贝儿在一起。它看到贝儿和她爸爸被关起来，就用莫维斯发明的机器把他们救了出来。然后他们一起回城堡去帮助野兽。
贝儿到达城堡时，野兽已经制伏了加斯顿，准备杀死他。但当野兽看到贝儿时，一下子就心软了，并松开了加斯顿。凶狠的加斯顿趁机一刀刺中了野兽的背。
贝儿抱住野兽深情地说：“你不要死，我爱你！”贝儿的话音刚落，魔法解除了！野兽变回王子，所有的器皿也都恢复了人形。
（作者：博蒙夫人/法国）
fields.content_en:
Title: Beauty and the Beast

Once upon a time there was a prince who was very selfish. On a cold winter night, an old crone asked to take shelter in the prince's castle, but he refused again and again. So she turned him into a hideous beast and his servants into various objects. The old woman was actually a witch. Before she left, she gave the prince a rose and told him it would bloom until his twenty-first birthday. If he could learn to love someone and be loved in return before the rose wilted, the magic would break and he would become human once more. But if he couldn't, he would remain a beast forever.

Years later, in a village near the castle, a girl named Belle grew up. One day, Belle's father Maurice hitched a horse named Philippe to the cart and set off for an exhibition with his latest invention. But at night they got lost after entering a forest and were attacked by a pack of wild wolves. In desperation, Philippe pulled the cart and ran as fast as he could, finally escaping into the prince's castle.

In the castle, all the objects could talk. The sofa invited Maurice to sit and rest, and the teapot offered him tea. But then there was the beast, who angrily ordered that Maurice be thrown into the prison cell.

Philippe ran home and brought Belle to the castle. The objects were excited to see Belle — she was so beautiful and seemed so kind. If the prince could fall in love with Belle, then the magic would break and they would all be restored to their human forms.

Inside the castle, Belle agreed to become the beast's prisoner in exchange for setting her father free. So Belle stayed in the castle, and all the furniture and objects cared for her warmly.

One day, Belle curiously wandered into the beast's private room, and the beast discovered her. He had warned her not to enter that room, so he flew into a rage. Belle was terrified and ran out of the castle. But as soon as she stepped outside, the wolves from the forest began to attack her. Then the beast appeared. He drove the wolves away, but he himself was wounded in the battle.

After that, Belle cared for the injured beast. She often read books to him and taught him table manners and how to dance. Their bond grew deeper and deeper.

The beast had a magic mirror that could show the outside world. Using it, Belle saw her father searching for her, so she asked to go find him. Though the beast did not want to let her leave, he did, and he gave her the magic mirror, asking only that she look into it often and think of him.

When Belle and her father returned home, a man from the village named Gaston came to visit. He had long wanted Belle to marry him, but she had always refused. This time, he arrived with a group of villagers and threatened her: "Your father has been going around the village talking nonsense about a beast. If you don't marry me, I'll tell everyone he's mad and have him locked away."

Belle took out the magic mirror so everyone could see the beast inside, proving that Maurice had told the truth all along. But Gaston stirred up the villagers, convincing them to go and kill the beast, and locked Belle and her father in a room.

A little teacup had secretly jumped into Belle's pocket when she left the castle, so he was still with her. Seeing Belle and her father locked up, he used Maurice's invention to rescue them. Then together they rushed back to the castle to help the beast.

When Belle arrived at the castle, the beast had already overpowered Gaston and was about to kill him. But when the beast saw Belle, his heart softened instantly, and he released Gaston. Cruel Gaston took the chance and stabbed the beast in the back.

Belle held the beast close and said deeply, "Please don't die. I love you!" The moment those words left her lips, the magic was broken! The beast transformed back into the prince, and all the objects returned to their human forms.

(author: Madame de Beaumont / France)
fields.tips: 真爱能让凶残的人变温柔，但一定要宣之于口，说出来才能让对方更真切地感受到，准妈妈要不吝表达，多跟胎宝宝说你爱他，也多跟准爸爸说你爱他，这样日子会更温馨。
fields.tips_en: True love can soften even the wildest heart. But love must be spoken aloud — it is only when words are shared that they truly reach the one we care for. Dear mama-to-be, do not hold back your loving words: tell your little one often how much you love them, and share those same sweet words with your partner as well. Doing so will make every day together feel warmer and more tender.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 完全是真的
fields.subtitle: 传闻就是这样成真的
fields.subtitle_en: How Rumors Come to Life
fields.content:
天黑了，农场里所有的母鸡都回到鸡窝，栖息到了栖木上。有一只白色的母鸡，总是喜欢在睡觉前梳理一下自己的羽毛，今天也一样，不过梳理的时候，有一片羽毛掉了下来。它感觉有点儿可惜：“才啄了两下，就掉了一片羽毛。”不过很快它就快乐地打趣道：“不过羽毛掉了一片，我更漂亮了。”它是一只爱逗趣的鸡，说完就闭上眼睛睡着了。
这话让栖息在上面栖木上的一只鸡听到了，它嘀咕道：“为了要好看，就啄掉自己的羽毛，我要是公鸡才看不起你呢。”
住在鸡窝上面的猫头鹰和它的丈夫听到了。猫头鹰女士不满地对丈夫说：“听听，这还像话吗，为了让公鸡看个仔细，居然把自己的羽毛都啄掉了。我要告诉对面的猫头鹰去。”猫头鹰女士飞走了。
两只猫头鹰的对话被下面鸽子窝里的鸽子听到了。它们叽叽喳喳议论起来：“听到了吗，为了讨好公鸡，一只母鸡把自己的羽毛都啄掉了。它一定会被冻死的。”鸽子们纷纷去告诉下边鸡窝里的鸡，说邻居家有一只还是两只母鸡为了引起公鸡的注意，而把自己的羽毛都啄掉了，然后发起高烧，它们都死了。
听到这个消息的公鸡大声叫醒鸡窝里的鸡，大叫着：“三只母鸡因为争夺一只公鸡大打出手，现在都死去了。”公鸡叫，母鸡啼，连蝙蝠都参与进来了，它们都认为应该让大家都知道这件事。于是这件事一传十，十传百，越传越远。最后这个故事变成了这样：“五只母鸡把羽毛啄掉，为了比比谁因为失恋变得更消瘦，最后起了争执，互相啄得流血，都死掉了。它们的主人因此受了很大的损失。”
啄掉一根白羽毛的母鸡也听说这件事了。它一点儿也没想到这件事的原型正是自己掉了一根羽毛的事。所以它说：“我瞧不起这些母鸡，真丢人。应该把这件事在报纸上报道出来，让全国都知道。”
（选自《安徒生童话》）
知识
lian
接
这篇童话故事是《安徒生童话》的一篇。一只鸡掉了一片羽毛，最后变成了五只鸡死了，还要在报纸上公布出来，这可能是当时新闻舆论的普遍现象。安徒生的很多童话都有讽刺意味，比如《幸福的家庭》《衬衫的领子》《园丁和主人》等。对中国人来说可能最熟悉的讽刺童话是《皇帝的新装》。当然，安徒生更多的作品是温馨的、美好的和给人带来快乐的，比如《拇指姑娘》《小意达的花儿》《顽皮的孩子》等。安徒生一生共写了168篇童话，被译成150多种语言。他的名作《丑小鸭》被认为是他的自传。他的童话不仅适合儿童阅读，而且也适合年轻人品味，老年人回味。
其实，安徒生不仅写童话，他还写过很多诗、剧以及小说，是诗人、剧作家以及小说家。他多才多艺，甚至能剪出栩栩如生的剪纸。在纪念他的博物馆，悬挂在大门上的就是他创作的人头剪纸。但童话是安徒生创作中最为光彩夺目的皇冠。是他首先让童话从粗糙的民间故事发展成为优美的、感情丰富的儿童文学。
fields.content_en:
Title: Totally True

When night fell, all the hens on the farm returned to the coop and settled onto their perches. One white hen always liked to preen her feathers before bed, just as she did today. But while she was at it, a single feather fell out. She felt a little sad. "I barely pecked twice, and a feather already fell," she thought. But soon she chuckled happily to herself, "But losing a feather only makes me even prettier." She was a cheerful bird, and with that, she closed her eyes and fell fast asleep.

A hen on the same perch overheard her and muttered, "You'd have to be a rooster not to look down on you—plucking out your own feathers just to look pretty."

An owl and her mate, living above the coop, heard everything too. Mrs. Owl turned to her husband with a frown. "Did you hear that? Is that proper behavior? She actually plucked all her feathers out just to impress the rooster. I'm going to tell the owls across the way." And she flew off.

The conversation between the two owls was overheard by the pigeons in the dovecote below. They began chattering excitedly. "Did you hear? To please a rooster, a hen plucked out all her feathers. She'll surely freeze to death." The pigeons spread the word to the hens in the coop below, saying that one or perhaps two hens had plucked out their feathers to catch a rooster's attention, caught a terrible fever, and had both died.

Hearing this news, a rooster loudly woke the hens in the coop and crowed, "Three hens fought over one rooster, and now they're all dead!" The rooster crowed, the hens clucked, and even the bats joined in—all believing everyone should know about this. So the tale spread, one person to ten, ten to a hundred, traveling farther and farther. In the end, the story had become: "Five hens plucked out their feathers to see who grew thinner and sadder after a broken romance. They ended up quarreling, pecking each other until they bled, and all of them died. Their owner suffered great losses as a result."

The white hen who had lost just one feather also heard about this. She had no idea that the original event was nothing more than her losing a single feather. So she said, "I look down on those hens. How shameful. This ought to be reported in the newspaper so the whole country knows."

(From *Andersen's Fairy Tales*)

**About the Author**

This fairy tale comes from *Andersen's Fairy Tales*. A chicken loses one feather, and it grows into a story about five dead chickens, with a demand to publish it in the newspaper. This may reflect the nature of news and public opinion in Andersen's time. Many of Andersen's fairy tales carry a satirical edge, such as *The Happy Family*, *The Shirt's Collar*, and *The Gardener and the Master*. For Chinese readers, the most familiar satirical tale is likely *The Emperor's New Clothes*. Of course, Andersen wrote many more stories that are warm, beautiful, and joyful—such as *The Little Mermaid*, *Little Ida's Flowers*, and *The Naughty Boy*. Andersen wrote a total of 168 fairy tales in his lifetime, translated into over 150 languages. His famous work *The Ugly Duckling* is considered his autobiography. His fairy tales are suitable not only for children but also for young people to savor and older readers to reflect upon.

In fact, Andersen wrote far more than fairy tales. He also wrote many poems, plays, and novels, making him a poet, playwright, and novelist all at once. He was gifted in many areas—even剪纸creating lifelike paper-cuttings. Hanging above the entrance of the museum dedicated to him is a paper-cutting of a human head, crafted by his own hand. But fairy tales remain the most brilliant crown of his creative achievements. It was he who elevated fairy tales from rough folk stories into beautiful, emotionally rich children's literature.
fields.tips: 传闻几经易口，常常会变得面目全非。特别是在网络普及之后，很多事情都以讹传讹。准妈妈要学会判断真伪，比如很多人都在说电磁辐射会影响胎儿发育，不过目前仍只是传闻，还未被证明，所以准妈妈不必为此整天忧心忡忡。压抑的情绪可能比电磁辐射更容易对胎儿有不利影响。
fields.tips_en: Rumors have a way of changing as they pass from person to person, often becoming quite different from the truth — especially in the age of the internet. As an expectant mother, it is important to learn to tell fact from fiction. For instance, many people say that electromagnetic radiation affects a baby's development, but so far this remains just a rumor, nothing confirmed. So please do not spend your days worrying about it. Remember, a heavy heart may harm your little one more than any unproven fear ever could.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 癞蛤蟆与钻石
fields.subtitle: 体会语言的魔力
fields.subtitle_en: Discovering the Magic of Words
fields.content:
以前有户人家有两个女儿，大女儿脾气很坏，小女儿性格柔顺。
母亲认为大女儿像自己，所以喜欢大女儿，家务活大部分都让小女儿干。在所有家务活里有一项是每天到林中打泉水。这天，小女儿刚到泉水边，就有一位可怜的老妇人来向她讨水喝。小女儿对老妇人说：“没问题，老奶奶，我马上打水给你喝。”她很快就打了一桶水，还双手帮忙捧着水勺，好让老奶奶喝起水来更容易些。
喝完水后，老奶奶说：“孩子，你心肠真好，我要送你一件礼物。以后你每说出一个字，嘴里就要么开出一朵花或者掉下一件珠宝。”说完她就不见了。原来这个老奶奶是仙女变的。
小女儿回到家后，母亲责骂她打水花了这么长时间。小女儿赶忙分辩说自己没有偷懒。她边说话，嘴里边往外掉东西，总共掉出了两朵玫瑰、两颗珍珠和两颗钻石。
母亲很惊奇，就问是怎么回事。小女儿把在泉水边发生的事原原本本告诉了母亲。
母亲心想这样好的事让大女儿碰上才好，就打发大女儿去打水，并叮嘱她有穷苦的老女人跟她讨水喝就给她喝。母亲还特意给她带上了家里最好的银水勺。
大女儿不愿意去，认为妹妹的珠宝自己可以都据为己有，但是母亲并不答应。大女儿一路上都咕咕哝哝地抱怨，到了泉水边也没有好心情。这时有个漂亮的年轻女人走过来跟她讨水喝。大女儿哪有心思给她水喝，就没好气地对她说：“你喝水自己不会打吗？你以为我带着银水勺就是给你打水喝的？”漂亮女人说：“你心肠真坏，一点儿礼貌也没有，我要给你一件礼物，以后你每说一句话，嘴里就会蹦出蛇和癞蛤蟆。”说完她就不见了。原来这个女人就是小女儿上次遇到的老妇人。
大女儿回到家里，母亲急忙问她有没有碰到仙女。大女儿一开口答话，嘴里就蹦出了蛇和癞蛤蟆。母亲问她做了什么，她急着想解释，结果只要一说话就蹦出蛇和癞蛤蟆。
如果大女儿不能悔改，得到仙女的原谅，以后恐怕就永远这样了。
（作者：夏尔·佩罗/法国）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Toad and the Diamond

Once upon a time, there was a family with two daughters. The older sister had a fiery temper, while the younger one was gentle and sweet.

The mother thought the older daughter was just like her, so she favored her. Most of the housework fell to the little girl. Among all the chores, one had to be done every day—going into the forest to fetch spring water. One day, when the little girl had just arrived at the spring, a poor old woman came and asked for a drink. The little girl replied kindly, "Of course, dear grandmother, I'll get you some water right away." She quickly drew a bucket full and even held the water ladle with both hands so it would be easier for the old woman to drink.

After finishing her water, the old woman said, "Child, you have such a kind heart. I want to give you a gift. From now on, every word that comes out of your mouth will either bloom into a flower or fall as a precious jewel." Then she vanished. It turned out she was a fairy in disguise.

When the little girl returned home, her mother scolded her for taking so long to fetch the water. Hurrying to explain that she hadn't been lazy, she opened her mouth—and out tumbled two roses, two pearls, and two diamonds.

The mother was amazed and asked what had happened. The little girl told her everything that had occurred at the spring, from beginning to end.

The mother thought to herself, "It would be wonderful if my older daughter had run into such luck." So she sent the older daughter to fetch water instead, telling her to give water to any poor old woman who might ask. She also made sure the older daughter took the family's best silver ladle along.

The older daughter didn't want to go. She thought her sister's jewels should all belong to her, but Mother wouldn't agree. On her way, the older daughter grumbled and complained, arriving at the spring in a terrible mood. Just then, a beautiful young woman approached and asked for a drink. The older daughter had no mind to help and snapped, "Can't you draw your own water? Did you think I brought this silver ladle for you to drink from?" The beautiful woman replied, "You have a cruel heart and no manners at all. I will give you a gift: from now on, every word you speak will bring forth snakes and toads from your mouth." Then she too disappeared. It turned out she was the same old woman the younger sister had met before.

When the older daughter returned home, her mother quickly asked if she had met a fairy. The moment she opened her mouth to answer, snakes and toads tumbled out. When her mother asked what she had done, the older daughter tried desperately to explain—but every time she spoke, more snakes and toads came flying out.

Unless the older daughter repents and receives the fairy's forgiveness, she fears she will be like this forever.

(Author: Charles Perrault / France)
fields.tips: 美的语言像玫瑰和珠宝，丑的语言像蛇和癞蛤蟆，可见语言的魔力之大。准妈妈的胎教语言要尽量准确、优美，日常注意不要说粗话。
fields.tips_en: Beautiful words are like roses and jewels; ugly words are like snakes and toads. How powerful language truly is! As you nurture your baby through prenatal bonding, let your words be gentle, kind, and full of beauty. Be mindful in everyday conversation, and let your speech always reflect the warmth in your heart.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 金色的小星星
fields.subtitle: 心灵美才耀眼
fields.subtitle_en: Beauty From Within Truly Shines
fields.content:
有三颗同月、同日、同时生的小星星，它们一颗是蓝的，一颗是红的，第三颗似乎没有什么颜色，只有一点儿微弱得可怜的光。
当太阳落山时，三颗小星星就各自在出生的地方放射着光芒。但是，每天天黑以前，它们必须从天河里打来第二天做早饭用的水，不然万一夜里下雨，会把干净的水弄浑，那就不好做饭了。
一天傍晚，三颗小星星各自拎着一只小水桶去打水。它们并排站在天河边上，眺望着美丽的晚霞和映在水里的彩云，之后小心翼翼地用桶打满了水。红艳艳的晚霞也映在了水桶里。
“啊，真美！”
“真的！好像云彩燃烧起来啦。”
三颗小星星一边说话，一边离开河边，不时瞅瞅自己的水桶。快到家了，晚霞的余晖、美丽的云彩，都从水桶中消失了。不过，随着夜幕降临，桶中的水面上又发出光彩，这是星星们各自的身影。
“瞧，我的脸多像一块蓝宝石呀！”
“看，我和红宝石一模一样。”
这两颗星星肩并着肩，兴高采烈地边说边走。第三颗小星星默默地跟在它们身后，它的小桶里好像没有什么光亮，只映着一张冰冷的脸。
不一会儿，它们来到三岔路口。这儿有一棵老树，它们发现树根下有一个小东西在蠕动。三颗星星停下了……
“啊！原来是喜鹊。”
“它怎么了？”
红星和蓝星把水桶抱在胸前，伸长了脖子观望。喜鹊躺在地上，两个爪子弯曲，两眼紧闭。仔细一瞧，原来它浑身沾满了污泥，翅膀耷拉在地上，两条腿不住地哆嗦。
“怪可怜的！”
“可咱们有什么办法呢？”
红星和蓝星这样说。第三颗小星星站在旁边，默默地望着喜鹊说：“我给你洗一洗吧。”
“这不是明天做早饭用的水吗？”红星说。
第三颗小星星走近喜鹊，放下水桶，一捧一捧地把水浇在喜鹊的身上。这时天色渐渐黑了，星光更加明亮，红星和蓝星想早点儿回去，放出比其他星星更加耀眼的光芒。
“咱们先走吧。”蓝星说着便和红星一起走了。留下了那颗只有微弱光亮的小星星。
喜鹊渐渐地恢复了元气，它挺了挺身子，一下就睁开了眼睛。这时从喜鹊的眼睛里闪射出金色的光芒，那金色的光芒越来越强烈，令人目眩。接着喜鹊抖动了一下翅膀，意味深长地叫了一声，一下子飞了起来。
“再见，小喜鹊！小心点儿飞呀！”小星星亲切地叮嘱着。
天已经全黑了，可小星星还得再到天河去打水。它拎着空桶急急忙忙地向天河走去。四下静悄悄的，小星星摸着黑，打满一桶水，又急急忙忙地往回赶。它走着、走着，突然发现小水桶里闪烁着一颗非常好看的金色的星星。
“啊！这？”
小星星停住脚步，仰望天空，寻找着这颗金色的星星，却找不到。原来这颗星星就是它自己。小星星的光芒并不是从它脸上或身上放射出来的，而是从它善良的心中放射出来的。
（作者：滨田广介/日本）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Golden Star

There were three little stars, born in the same month, on the same day, and at the same time. One was blue, one was red, and the third seemed to have no color at all—only a tiny, trembling bit of light.

When the sun set, the three little stars began to shine from where they were born. But every day before it grew dark, they had to fetch water from the Milky River for tomorrow’s breakfast. If they didn’t, the rain might cloud the clean water, and that would make cooking very difficult.

One evening, each star carried a small bucket to draw water. They stood side by side on the bank of the Milky River, gazing at the beautiful sunset clouds and their reflections dancing in the water. Then they carefully filled their buckets. The fiery red of the sunset was captured inside each one.

“Oh, how beautiful!”
“Really! It looks like the clouds are on fire.”

The three stars spoke as they walked away from the river, often glancing down at their buckets. By the time they were nearly home, the glow of the sunset and the lovely clouds had vanished from the water. But as night fell, the surface of the water in each bucket began to shine—reflecting each star’s own face.

“Look, my face shines like a sapphire!”
“See, mine is just like a ruby.”

These two stars walked side by side, chatting joyfully. The third little star followed quietly behind, and its bucket held no brightness at all—only the reflection of a pale, cold face.

Soon they came to a fork in the path. There stood an old tree, and at its roots they spotted something small squirming. The three stars stopped…

“Oh! It’s a magpie.”
“What’s wrong with it?”

The Red Star and the Blue Star hugged their buckets close and craned their necks to look. The magpie lay on the ground, its two claws curled, its eyes tightly shut. Upon closer looking, they saw it was covered in mud, its wings drooping to the earth, and its legs shaking uncontrollably.

“How pitiful!”
“But what can we do?”

Said the Red Star and the Blue Star. The third little star stood nearby and silently looked at the magpie. “Let me wash you,” it said.

“Isn’t that the water you need for tomorrow’s breakfast?” asked the Red Star.

The third little star walked closer to the magpie, set down its bucket, and gently poured water over it, scoop by scoop. By then the sky had grown dark, and the starlight grew brighter. The Red Star and the Blue Star wanted to hurry home so they could shine even more brilliantly than all the other stars.

“Let’s go on ahead,” said the Blue Star, and together they left, leaving behind the little star with only its faint glow.

Slowly, the magpie began to recover. It straightened its body and suddenly opened its eyes. At that moment, a golden light shone from the magpie’s eyes, growing stronger and brighter, dazzling to behold. Then the magpie fluttered its wings once, gave a meaningful cry, and soared into the sky.

“Goodbye, little magpie! Fly carefully!” the little star called warmly after it.

It was now completely dark, but the little star still had to fetch more water from the Milky River. Carrying its empty bucket, it hurried along. Everything was quiet. The little star felt its way in the dark, filled its bucket, and hurried back. As it walked, it noticed something sparkling inside its small bucket—a most beautiful golden star.

“Oh… what is this?”

The little star stopped and looked up at the sky, searching for the golden star—but it couldn’t find it anywhere. In truth, that star was the little star itself. Its light was not shining from its face or its body, but from the kindness inside its heart.

(Author: Kosuke Hamada / Japan)
fields.tips: 俗语说相由心生，小星星金子般的心让它的外表也璀璨生辉。胎宝宝虽然还在腹中，但他也一样能感应到准爸爸和准妈妈的情感。所以准爸爸在日常生活中一定要为胎宝宝做表率，把真、善、美的情操传递给胎宝宝。
fields.tips_en: There is an old saying: the face reflects the heart. The little star's golden heart made its outer glow shine all the brighter. Even while still in the womb, your baby can sense the love and emotions shared between you and your partner. So, dear father-to-be, be a shining example every day — let your kindness, your goodness, and your love pass gently down to your little one.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 白蝴蝶
fields.subtitle: 爱是永久的追随与陪伴
fields.subtitle_en: Love Is a Lasting Journey Together
fields.content:
在街道的拐角处，一个老爷爷在卖气球。有红的、蓝的、绿的、黄的……它们脸贴着脸，随着风自由地飘动，别提多高兴啦。
有一只白色的蝴蝶，每天都飞到这里来，跟气球们一起玩儿。这束气球里有个很小的红气球，白蝴蝶跟它最好啦！
有一天，一个背着娃娃的阿姨过来了，阿姨用一分钱买走了那个小红气球。在走的时候，小红气球说：“再见啦，蝴蝶！”可是，白蝴蝶说：“不，我们是朋友，我要跟你走！”
白蝴蝶扇动着翅膀，跟在红气球的后边。那个背娃娃的阿姨穿过一条林荫道，朝着公园走去。红气球被一根细线牵着，跟在她背后。在红气球的后边，又跟着白蝴蝶。
阿姨在公园的长椅子上坐下来，唱起哄娃娃睡觉的催眠曲：
噢——噢——乖宝宝睡觉喽——
还没等小娃娃睡呢，阿姨自己倒先“呼呼”地睡着了。白蝴蝶不放心地问红气球：“这以后，你要到什么地方去呢？”红气球说：“这个，我也不知道。”
这时候，阿姨不知不觉地松开了手，细线滑了出去，红气球开始飘向天空。白蝴蝶也跟着红气球，向天空飞去。
“我不知道会飞到哪里去，蝴蝶，你快回家去吧……”红气球焦急地说。“不，你去哪儿我就去哪儿！”白蝴蝶说。
红气球越飞越高，白蝴蝶也越飞越高。往下看去，城市变小了，房子跟玩具积木似的。“好蝴蝶，我还不知道会飞到哪儿去呢，别再跟着我了！”红气球恳求道。
可是，白蝴蝶还是扇动着翅膀，跟着它走。不一会儿，红气球和白蝴蝶就都飞到很高很远的蓝天上去了，一点儿也看不见了。
（作者：新美南吉/日本）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The White Butterfly**

At the corner of the street, an old grandfather was selling balloons. There were red ones, blue ones, green ones, yellow ones…they pressed their faces together and floated freely in the wind. They looked so happy!

A white butterfly came flying here every day to play with the balloons. Inside that bunch of balloons was a tiny red balloon, and the white butterfly was best friends with it!

One day, an aunt carrying a baby on her back came over, and she bought that little red balloon for one penny. As she was walking away, the red balloon said, "Goodbye, butterfly!" But the white butterfly said, "No, we are friends. I'm going with you!"

The white butterfly fluttered its wings and followed behind the red balloon. The aunt carrying the baby walked through a tree-lined path and headed toward the park. The red balloon was tied with a thin string and trailed behind her, and behind the red balloon followed the white butterfly.

The aunt sat down on a bench in the park and sang a lullaby to help the baby fall asleep:

Ohh—ohh—sleepy little baby, time to sleep now—

Before the baby had even fallen asleep, the aunt herself began snoring. The white butterfly asked the red balloon worriedly, "Where will you go from here?" The red balloon said, "I don't know either."

At that moment, the aunt unknowingly let go of her hand, the thin string slipped away, and the red balloon began to float up into the sky. The white butterfly followed the red balloon and flew up into the sky as well.

"I don't know where I'll end up, butterfly. You should go home…"said the red balloon anxiously. "No, wherever you go, I will go too!" said the white butterfly.

The red balloon flew higher and higher, and so did the white butterfly. Looking down, the city grew smaller, and the houses looked like toy blocks. "Good butterfly, I don't even know where I'm going! Please stop following me!" pleaded the red balloon.

But the white butterfly kept fluttering its wings and followed along. Before long, both the red balloon and the white butterfly had flown up into the high, far blue sky, and they could no longer be seen.

(By Namboku Shimeta / Japan)
fields.tips: 在怀孕过程中，因为生理和心理的一些变化，准妈妈更需要准爸爸的陪伴。在准妈妈情绪起伏大的时候，准爸爸要多一点儿爱与耐心，多迁就、多包容、多付出、多想想法子，帮助准妈妈甩掉坏情绪，争取快快乐乐地度过每一天！
fields.tips_en: During pregnancy, as the body and heart go through many changes, a mother-to-be needs her partner's companionship more than ever. When her emotions rise and fall, dear father-to-be, offer a little more love, a little more patience — be understanding, be forgiving, give generously, and find little ways to help her smile away the shadows. With your warmth beside her, every day can be filled with joy.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 不肯借钱的林肯
fields.title_en: Lincoln Who Would Not Borrow Money
fields.subtitle: 生活需要用自己的劳动来创造
fields.subtitle_en: Life Is Built Through Our Own Hands
fields.content:
美国总统亚伯拉罕·林肯有一个弟弟，是他继母的儿子。有一次，他来信向当了总统的哥哥林肯借钱，没想到林肯写信这样回复了他。
亲爱的詹斯顿：
你向我借80块钱，我觉得最好不要借给你。因为你现在的问题是有浪费时间的恶习。改掉它，对你，还有你的孩子们来说都很重要。
我建议你去工作，只要你挣到一块钱，我就再给你一块钱。这样你的劳动可以获得双倍的酬金。当然，我并不是说让你到很远的地方去做苦工，你只需要在离家近的地方找个最挣钱的工作。
如果你愿意的话，很快就能还清债务。更重要的是你会养成不再欠债的好习惯。但如果我现在帮你还了债，明年你又会负债累累。
你说你愿意把田产抵押给我，这太不明智了。假如你有田地都无法生存，将来没有了田地又该怎么办呢？相信我，如果你肯采纳我的建议，你会发现，这比8个80块钱还值！
挚爱你的哥哥：亚伯拉罕·林肯
fields.content_en:
# Lincoln Who Wouldn't Lend Money

President Abraham Lincoln of the United States had a younger brother, the son of his stepmother. One day, his brother wrote to him asking to borrow money. To his surprise, Lincoln replied with a letter like this:

Dear Jamison,

You asked to borrow eighty dollars from me, and I think it would be better not to lend it to you. Because right now you have a habit of wasting your time. Giving up that habit is very important—for you and for your children, too.
