I suggest you go find work. For every dollar you earn, I will give you another dollar. In this way, your hard work will be rewarded twice over. Of course, I'm not saying you should travel far away to do difficult labor. You only need to find the best-paying job close to home.

If you are willing to try, you can pay back your debt very soon. Even more importantly, you will develop a good habit of never falling into debt again. But if I simply pay off your debt for you now, next year you will be in debt all over again.

You said you would mortgage your land to me, but that is not wise at all. If you cannot survive with your land, then what will you do when you no longer have it? Trust me—when you follow my advice, you will find it is worth far more than eight times eighty dollars!

With all my love, your brother,
Abraham Lincoln
fields.tips: 我们想要的任何东西，都可以通过自己的劳动去换取。享受这个过程，人生才变得更加美妙。爸爸妈妈应该让孩子明白：无论怎样，生活还是要靠自己努力。
fields.tips_en: Anything we desire can be earned through our own hard work. Enjoy the journey — it is what makes life truly beautiful. Parents should help their children understand: no matter what, life must be built by one's own effort.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 一件衬衫
fields.subtitle: 快乐是一种心境
fields.subtitle_en: Happiness Is a State of Mind
fields.content:
在一个遥远的国家里，国王正病得厉害。所有的御医都来瞧过了。虽然大家都尽了最大的努力，可国王的病情丝毫不见好转，反而一天天恶化了。
后来，宫里只得从国外请来了一位著名的医生。这位外国医生看了一下国王的病，严肃地说：“陛下，只有一样东西能够救你！”
国王问：“什么东西？只要你能救活我，无论你要什么，我都能给你。”
医生说：“不！我是说，你只要穿着一件快乐的人的衬衫睡上一夜，你的身体就会康复的。”
于是，国王派了两个大臣去找快乐的人，并让大臣把他的衬衫带回来。
两个大臣首先找到了城里最富裕的人，问他：“你是不是一个快乐的人？”
最富裕的人说：“快乐？我难以预料明天我的船会不会遭难，我每天还要防着小偷跑到我的家里来。哎！有一箩筐的烦恼事儿，一个人怎么会快乐呢？”
后来，两个大臣又找到了权力只在国王之下的宰相。他们问：“你是个快乐的人吗？”
宰相说：“别傻了！外国有人要侵略我们，奸佞企图夺走我的大权，奴仆们希望增加收入，有钱的人又想少缴些税。你们说，宰相会是一个快乐的人吗？”
两个大臣走遍了整个国家，始终找不到一个快乐的人。他们又疲劳又悲伤，只得准备回宫了。这时，他们看到一个乞丐坐在路旁。他生了一堆火，正在用一个长柄平锅煎香肠、煮饭吃，还在得意地唱着歌呢！
两个大臣对望着：“他就是我们要找的人！”于是上前攀谈：“看上去，你很快乐！”
乞丐回答：“当然，我很快乐！”
两个大臣高兴极了，连忙异口同声地说：“朋友，我们想出高价借用你的衬衫！”
乞丐一阵大笑，说：“对不起，先生们！我可是一件衬衫也没有啊！”
（选自《英国寓言故事》）
fields.content_en:
# A Shirt

Once upon a time, in a faraway land, the king was very sick. All his royal doctors came to see him. Everyone did their very best, but the king's illness did not get better at all. In fact, he became sicker every day.

In the end, the palace had to invite a famous doctor from another country. The foreign doctor looked at the king's illness and said gravely, "Your Majesty, only one thing can save you!"

The king asked, "What is it? As long as you can heal me, I will give you anything you want."

The doctor said, "No! I mean, you must sleep wearing the shirt of a happy person, and your body will be healed."

So the king sent two ministers to find a happy person and asked them to bring back that person's shirt.

The two ministers first found the richest man in the city and asked, "Are you a happy person?"

The richest man said, "Happy? I can never be sure my ships won't be lost at sea tomorrow, and every day I have to worry about thieves sneaking into my home. Oh! I have a basket full of troubles. How can a person be happy like that?"

Then the two ministers went to the prime minister, whose power was only less than the king's. They asked, "Are you a happy person?"

The prime minister said, "Don't be silly! Foreign countries want to invade us, dishonest people are trying to take away my power, servants want higher wages, and rich people want to pay less tax. Do you think a prime minister can be happy?"

The two ministers searched all across the country but could not find a single happy person. They were tired and sad, and they prepared to return to the palace. At that moment, they saw a beggar sitting by the road. He had built a fire and was cooking sausages and rice in a long-handled pan, singing proudly as he ate!

The two ministers looked at each other and said, "He must be the happy person we're looking for!" So they went up and began to talk. "You look like a very happy person!"

The beggar replied, "Of course I am happy!"

The two ministers were overjoyed and said together, "Friend, we would like to borrow your shirt at a high price!"

The beggar laughed loudly and said, "Sorry, gentlemen! I don't have a single shirt!"

(Adapted from *British Fable Stories*)
fields.tips: 看来，国王的病是心病啊。如果他能看到一无所有的乞丐的快乐，他的病会不医自好的。简单的生活更加乐趣无穷。
fields.tips_en: It seems the king's illness was of the heart. If he could see the joy of a beggar who owns nothing, his sickness might heal all on its own. A simple life is full of endless little joys.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 爬上树的孩子
fields.title_en: The Child Who Climbed the Tree
fields.subtitle: 孩子对父母的爱是天然的需求
fields.subtitle_en: A Child's Love for Their Parents Is a Natural Need
fields.content:
少年辰吉没见过自己的妈妈，他在奶奶的抚养下长大，他很羡慕别的小朋友有父母。
“奶奶，我妈妈怎么啦？”辰吉这样问奶奶。奶奶用满是皱纹的手抚摸着辰吉的头说：“你妈妈在天上呢，已经变成星星了。她每天都往下看，看着你平安长大，希望你成为一个好孩子。”
辰吉相信奶奶的话，他每天晚上都到外边仰望夜空中闪烁的星星，使劲儿在星群里寻找妈妈。夜空里的星星可真多啊，有闪着白光的大星星，有一动不动射着红光的星星，还有像萤火虫一样的小星星……
终于，辰吉认定一颗柔和的、不太大、不太亮的红星星是自己的妈妈。这颗星星好像两眼饱含着泪水，向他诉说什么一样。
在辰吉满12岁那年，他不得不离开奶奶，到五六里地外的村子去做工。这家的主人是一个非常严厉的人。辰吉听他使唤，给他挑水，干许多许多的活儿，简直没有一点儿休息的时间。辰吉想起和蔼慈祥的奶奶来，想着想着，眼圈就红了。他也更加感激她老人家。
每天晚饭后，辰吉像往常一样到外边看星星。在这儿也可以看见那颗红星星。辰吉想：“妈妈正跟着自己呢，她每天都看着自己！”
季节已是夏末秋初，但天气依旧很炎热。村里的孩子们都爱到村头的庙里玩，他们捉迷藏，做各种游戏。这里有一棵很大的杉树，孩子们玩累了就在树下休息。
“这棵树一直连着天呢！”一个孩子抬头望着杉树说。
“傻瓜，天比这棵树高出不止10里、100里，还要高得多呢！”另一个孩子说。
“胡说！星星不就挂在树尖上吗？”说树连着天的孩子说。
一个孩子插嘴说：“听说有的星星上边是住着人的！”
辰吉想起奶奶曾经说过，人死了以后，都要升天，变成星星。辰吉觉得今天的天空很低，好像就在树顶上似的。“说不定妈妈下来了呢！”辰吉想。
两个孩子还在继续争吵着。“不用吵啦，谁上树看看不就一清二楚了吗？”大孩子说。
但是，没有一个人敢上去，只有辰吉说“我上”。跟别的孩子不同，他一点儿也不害怕，说完就开始爬树了。辰吉越爬越高，四周完全黑下来了。星星在杉树顶上闪烁着，把夜空映照得非常美丽，很快辰吉就消失在黑暗的树枝丛中了。
“爬了这么久，大概已经到高高的树顶了吧？”孩子们在底下议论着。
“喂，辰吉！”孩子们在树下嚷开了。
可是，不知辰吉怎么了，没有回音，也没有下来。孩子们觉得很奇怪，在树底下往上看呀看的。夜深了，辰吉还是没有下来。孩子们有些害怕，不知谁说了一声：“到明天就知道怎么回事啦！”孩子们一听，就回家睡觉去了。
天亮以后，很多人集中在杉树下，一个大人爬上树去，结果只发现辰吉的衣服挂在树枝上，却没见到人影。
人们惊讶万分，但谁也不知道究竟是怎么回事。有人说辰吉变成了鸟，有人说辰吉变成了猫头鹰，已经飞离了这棵树，到天上去了。
（作者：小川未明/日本）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Boy Who Climbed the Tree

Young Chenji had never met his mother. He grew up raised by his grandmother, and he often felt envious of other children who had parents.
"Grandma, what happened to my mom?" Chenji asked her one day. Grandma stroked his head with her wrinkled hands and said, "Your mother is in the sky. She has become a star. Every day she looks down and watches you grow up safely, hoping you become a good child."
Chenji believed what his grandmother said. Every night, he went outside to gaze at the twinkling stars in the night sky, searching hard among them for his mother. There were so many stars in the night sky—big ones glowing white, ones that stayed perfectly still shining red, and tiny ones like fireflies...
At last, Chenji decided that a gentle, neither too large nor too bright red star was his mother. That star seemed to have tears in its eyes, as if whispering something to him.
On the twelfth birthday of Chenji, he had to leave his grandmother and go work in a village five or six li away. The master of that house was a very strict person. Chenji obeyed his every order, carrying water for him and doing many, many tasks, with hardly any time to rest. Thinking of his kind and loving grandmother, his eyes would grow red. He also felt even more grateful to her.
Every night after dinner, Chenji went outside to watch the stars, just as he always did. From here, he could also see that red star. Chenji thought, "Mom is following me. She watches over me every day!"
The season had reached late summer and early autumn, yet the weather remained hot. The village children loved to play near the temple at the edge of the village. They played hide-and-seek and many other games. There was a large fir tree there, and the children rested under it when they grew tired from playing.
"That tree reaches all the way to the sky!" said one child, looking up at the fir tree.
"Foolishness. The sky is far higher than this tree—more than ten li, more than a hundred li, even higher!" said another child.
"Nonsense! Don't the stars hang right on the tips of the tree?" replied the child who said the tree connected to the sky.
Another child chimed in, "I heard there are people living on some stars!"
Chenji remembered what his grandmother had once said—that after people die, they go up to the heavens and become stars. The sky tonight seemed very low, as if it rested right on top of the tree. "Maybe Mom has come down!" Chenji thought.
The two children continued to argue. "There's no need to argue," said the older child. "Whoever climbs the tree will know right away, won't they?"
But no one dared to climb up. Only Chenji said, "I'll go." Unlike the other children, he was not afraid at all. After saying this, he began to climb. Chenji climbed higher and higher, and all around him, darkness settled in. The stars twinkled atop the fir tree, illuminating the night sky beautifully. Before long, Chenji disappeared among the dark branches.
"He's been climbing for so long. He must have reached the very top by now, right?" the children whispered below.
"Hey, Chenji!" the children called from under the tree.
But something had happened to Chenji. There was no reply, and he did not come down. The children grew puzzled and looked up at the tree again and again. Night deepened, yet Chenji still had not come down. Feeling a little scared, someone said, "We'll find out tomorrow!" Hearing this, the children went home to sleep.
After dawn, many people gathered under the fir tree. An adult climbed up and discovered only Chenji's clothes hanging on a branch—there was no sign of him anywhere.
Everyone was greatly astonished, but no one knew what had truly happened. Some said Chenji had turned into a bird. Others said he had become an owl and had already flown away from the tree, up into the sky.
(Author: Ogawa Minako / Japan)
fields.tips: 辰吉到底去哪里了呢，可能他真的像人们说的一样，变成鸟儿找妈妈去了吧。孩子对父母的爱是一种天然的需求，无论如何，爸爸妈妈都要在百忙之中抽点儿时间与孩子相处，这将极大地保护孩子的心灵。
fields.tips_en: Where did Chenji go? Perhaps he truly became a little bird, flying off to find his mommy. A child's love for their parents is a deep, natural need. No matter how busy life gets, parents should always make time to be with their children — it nurtures and protects their precious hearts.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 金铃铛
fields.subtitle: 要学会抑制好奇心
fields.subtitle_en: Learning to Restrain Curiosity
fields.content:
白皙的皮肤、金黄的头发，模样漂亮，又风趣十足，年纪不大却千般乖巧，这就是罗莎小姐。啊，忘记说明了，小罗莎还有一个十分明显的缺点，就是她的好奇心太强了！
这个小罗莎常常是一整天一整天地窥探别人的秘密，不论是什么事，好的或是坏的，都要偷听，接着又添油加醋，向邻居，甚至向不太熟悉的人四处传播。
为此，罗莎受到了人们的指责，她自己也遭到惩罚，失去了平日的快乐。
罗莎的母亲自言自语：“我要想个办法，用个计谋，让女儿改掉她的坏毛病。”
聪明的母亲立刻采取行动。很快一位家庭医生来访，这一切都好像偶然发生似的。母亲和医生走进房间，顺手关上门，又从里面把门锁好。看样子，要商量一件特别重大的事情。
小罗莎立刻警觉起来，脱掉鞋子，爬上楼梯，脚步轻轻，活像一个作案的小偷。她爬到门口偷听，好奇心使她趴在地上，嘴已啃着地啦。
罗莎听到母亲说：“讲道理，软的硬的办法都用过了，可是对我的孩子全不管用。如果是别的小毛病，我还可以忍受，可是这个毛病太使我丢脸啦，谁愿意和一个小特务生活在一起！”
“好了，好了，夫人，”医生说，“这种不幸的人，我们十分同情。他们生下来就好奇，因为他们脸部组织有缺陷。”
“别胡说！什么脸部组织？”
“我指的是鼻子，鼻子轻的人天生极端好奇，我有治这种病的良药。照我说的去做，最固执的人，也会忘记偷听和乱传闲话的。”
“您说的管用吗？”
“最管用不过了，她会变成十分时髦的小姐。”
“什么时髦？”
“鼻子上戴上首饰。我就去马德里，让银匠精心制作两个纯金的小铃铛，还要加上一个小球，增加点儿分量。鼻子上穿个洞，这手术很快就能做完。用漂亮的金铃铛打扮自己，她可以和历史上的美女阿维塞娜比美啦！”
“快，给我女儿做铃铛。”
罗莎悄悄地跑了。她心里害怕极了：“医生真残酷！他要用铁针在我鼻子上穿洞！给我挂上铃铛！鼻子穿孔会挖心似的痛。我鼻子挂着两个铃铛算是什么角色呀？谁还喜欢我呀？这样稀奇古怪，这种可怕的时髦，谁能感到舒服？什么鬼时髦！这等于给自己挂一个牌子，上面写着：我是坏人！上帝啊，这要轰动全城，人人都会笑话我的。要防止这种侮辱性的事件发生！我要说，我的鼻子沉了，而且，要改正错误。”
事实上，她真改正了错误。小鼻子还十分完整，直到今天也非常健康。妈妈十分满意地对她说：“不知为什么，我们罗莎的鼻子，过去像羽毛那么轻，现在变得像铅那么重，已经不偷听，也不传闲话了。那么，就取消穿鼻手术吧。不过，万一老病复发，我们还是要挂上金铃铛。”
（作者：阿特塞布斯切/西班牙）
fields.content_en:
**Title: Little Golden Bells**

Pretty with fair skin and golden hair, clever and funny, sweet in a hundred little ways though still so young—this was Miss Rosa. Oh, I almost forgot to mention, little Rosa had one quite obvious flaw: she was far too curious!

This little Rosa would spend day after day spying on people's secrets, no matter what they were—good or bad—she'd eavesdrop and then go adding color to the story as she told her neighbors, and even people she hardly knew.

Because of this, Rosa was scolded by everyone, and she herself was punished, losing her usual happiness.

Rosa's mother talked to herself: "I must think of a plan, a little trick, to help my daughter give up her bad habit."

The clever mother acted at once. Soon a family doctor came to visit, and everything seemed to happen quite by accident. Mother and the doctor walked into a room and quietly closed the door, locking it from the inside. It looked as though they needed to discuss something very important.

Little Rosa immediately grew alert. She took off her shoes, climbed up the stairs on tiptoe, very softly, just like a little sneaky thief. She crept to the door to listen, and curiosity made her lie flat on the floor with her mouth nearly touching the ground.

Rosa heard her mother say, "I've tried reasoning, and I've tried both soft and hard methods, but nothing works on my child. If it were some small bad habit, I could tolerate it, but this one embarrasses me so much! Who would want to live with a little spy!"

"Now, now, madam," said the doctor, "we feel great sympathy for people like this. They are born curious because of a defect in their facial structure."

"Nonsense! What facial structure?"

"I mean the nose. People with light noses are born extremely curious. I have a wonderful medicine to cure this illness. Follow my advice, and even the most stubborn person will forget eavesdropping and gossiping."

"Will what you say really work?"

"It will work wonderfully. She will become the most fashionable young lady."

"What kind of fashion?"

"Jewelry on the nose. I will go to Madrid and have a silversmith carefully make two little pure-gold bells, with a small ball attached to add a bit of weight. A tiny hole in the nose, and the operation will be done very quickly. Decorating herself with beautiful golden bells, she could rival the lovely Avicenna of history!"

"Quickly, make the bells for my daughter."

Rosa quietly slipped away. She was terribly afraid: "The doctor is so cruel! He wants to pierce a hole in my nose with an iron needle! Hang bells on it! Piercing a nose would hurt as if my heart were being torn out. What kind of creature would I be with two bells hanging from my nose? Who would still like me? So strange and bizarre—this awful fashion, who could feel comfortable? What nonsense! This is like putting up a sign that says: I am a bad person! Oh dear, this will cause a sensation all over town, and everyone will laugh at me. I must prevent this insulting thing from happening! I must say that my nose has become heavy, and I must correct my mistake."

In fact, she truly corrected her mistake. Her little nose remained perfectly intact, and to this day it stays very healthy. Mother said to her very happily, "I don't know why, but Rosa's nose, which used to be as light as a feather, has become as heavy as lead. She no longer eavesdrops or spreads gossip. Then let's cancel the nose-piercing operation. But just in case the old habit returns, we will still hang the golden bells."

(Author: Atzebusche / Spain)
fields.tips: 从小姑娘罗莎的故事我们可以看到，好奇心如果滥用的话，就会有窥探别人秘密的行为。稍微不克制自己，就会让自己变成散播小道消息的讨厌鬼啦。学会适当克制自己，这样才不会作出愚蠢的事情来。
fields.tips_en: From little Rosa's story, we learn that unchecked curiosity can lead us to pry into secrets that do not belong to us. Without a little self-restraint, we risk becoming the sort of person who spreads gossip — and no one enjoys that! Learning to hold ourselves back at the right moment keeps us from doing foolish things.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 冯·卡门与飞机
fields.subtitle: 不要盲从权威
fields.subtitle_en: Do Not Follow Authority Blindly
fields.content:
冯·卡门是匈牙利的犹太人，是20世纪最伟大的航天工程学家。他6岁时的一天晚上，大哥不经意地问他：“15×15是多少？”冯·卡门边玩边答“225。”二哥接着问：“924×826是多少？”冯·卡门头也没抬一下就说“763224。”
全家人都发出了惊叹声，但冯·卡门的父亲莫里斯·卡门教授却不以为然地说：“你们是串通好了在演戏吧？小宝贝，难道你还能心算出来18876×18876是多少吗？”冯·卡门只思索了一会儿就说出了正确答案“356303376”。大家欢呼着把冯·卡门抱了起来。
莫里斯·卡门教授决心将儿子培养成才。他找来许多名家的作品让冯·卡门研读。从此，冯·卡门在父亲规划好的道路上走得一帆风顺，1902年获得硕士学位，1908年获得博士学位。
1908年的一天，冯·卡门亲眼目睹了法国航空先驱法尔芒又一次打破纪录的飞行。飞行结束后，冯·卡门从人群中挤过去，与法尔芒之间有过一段精彩的对话。
冯·卡门问法尔芒：“我是研究科学的，有一位伟大的科学家，用他的定律证明了比空气重的东西是绝对飞不起来的。你能解释一下，飞机为什么会飞起来吗？”
法尔芒幽默地回答：“是那个研究苹果落地的人吗？幸好我没有读过他的书。不然，今天就不会得到这次飞行的奖金了。我以前只是个卡车司机，现在又成了飞行员。至于飞机为什么会飞起来，不关我的事。您作为教授，应该研究它。祝您成功，再见。”
法尔芒的话令冯·卡门大吃了一惊。他决心研究清楚飞机为什么能上天的道理。正是这次谈话把冯·卡门引上了毕生从事航空航天研究的道路。他对航空航天技术的发展有过很多重要的预见，后来都成为现实，例如超声速飞行、远程导弹、全天候飞行、卫星……
fields.content_en:
Title: Von Karman and the Airplane

Von Karman was a Hungarian Jew, and one of the greatest aerospace engineers of the 20th century. One evening when he was six years old, his big brother casually asked him, "What is 15 times 15?" Von Karman, while still playing, answered, "225." Then his second brother followed up, "What about 924 times 826?" Von Karman didn't even look up and said, "763224."

The whole family gasped in amazement, but Von Karman's father, Professor Maurice Karman, wasn't impressed. He said, "You two planned this as a show, didn't you? Little one, can you also figure out in your head what 18876 times 18876 is?" Von Karman thought for just a moment and gave the correct answer: "356303376." Everyone cheered and lifted him up in their arms.

Professor Maurice Karman was determined to raise his son to be someone great. He found many works by famous authors for Von Karman to study. From then on, Von Karman walked smoothly along the path his father had planned for him. He earned his master's degree in 1902 and his doctoral degree in 1908.

One day in 1908, Von Karman watched with his own eyes as the French aviation pioneer Farman broke another record in the sky. After the flight, Von Karman pushed through the crowd and had a wonderful conversation with Farman.

Von Karman asked Farman, "I study science. There is a great scientist who proved with his law that nothing heavier than air can ever fly. Can you explain to me why an airplane can fly?"

Farman answered with a smile, "You mean the man who studied apples falling from trees? Good thing I never read his books. Otherwise, I wouldn't have won the prize for this flight today. I used to be just a truck driver, and now I'm a pilot. As for why airplanes fly, that's not my concern. You're the professor—you should figure it out. Good luck, goodbye!"

Farman's words surprised Von Karman greatly. He made up his mind to understand clearly why airplanes can fly. That very conversation led Von Karman onto the path of spending his whole life researching aerospace. He made many important predictions about the development of aerospace technology, and later, all of them came true—for example, supersonic flight, long-range missiles, all-weather flying, and satellites.
fields.tips: 一位卡车司机影响了冯·卡门的一生。他让冯·卡门明白了一个真理：权威也不能盲目相信，自己的路要靠自己走。是啊，保护孩子的创造性，这也是父母需要努力的方向。
fields.tips_en: A truck driver changed the course of von Kármán's life. He taught him a vital truth: even authority should not be followed without question — we must carve our own path. Likewise, nurturing a child's creativity is something every parent can strive to do.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 逃到天亮
fields.subtitle: 盲从害人害己
fields.subtitle_en: Blindly Following Hurts You and Others
fields.content:
从前有个戏班子，有一次戏子们带着行头要到很远的地方去演戏。
这一天夜里，因为赶不到镇上去投宿，他们只好在一座山上过夜。听人说，这座山里一直住着吃人的恶魔。
这一天天气不好，山上又有风，冷极了。所以他们就烧起火来，大家围着火睡觉。其中一个戏子生了寒热病，他太冷了，就随手拿了一件戏衣穿上，坐着烤火。那件戏衣恰恰是戏台上恶魔穿的。
过了一会儿，其中一个戏子醒过来了，一看火边坐着一个吃人的恶魔，吓得马上就逃。这么一来，惊动了大家，大家也都起来跟着跑。
那个穿戏衣的人看见大家都在逃，他也拼命跟着逃。可怜那些逃在前头的人，一看后面有“恶魔”追来，吓得加快了速度，不管荆棘和石块，都没命地飞跃过去，弄得伤痕累累，身心疲倦。
一直到天亮，大家才知道那不是恶魔，是自己的伙伴啊！
（选自《西班牙寓言故事》）
fields.content_en:
**Title: Running Until Daylight**

Once upon a time, there was a traveling group of actors who packed up their costumes and props and set off to perform far away.

That night, because they couldn't make it to town before dark, they had no choice but to spend the night on a mountain. They say a man-eating demon lives in that mountain.

It was a bad night — the wind blew hard on the mountain, and it was freezing cold. So they built a fire and slept together around its warmth. One of the actors had a fever and was shivering badly, so he picked up a costume that was lying nearby and threw it on, sitting close to the fire. That costume happened to be the one worn by the demon character in their play.

After a while, one of the actors woke up, looked over at the fire, and saw what appeared to be a man-eating demon. He was so frightened that he took off running. The commotion woke everyone else, and soon they were all scrambling away in terror.

The actor wearing the costume saw everyone running and started running too. Poor ones ahead saw the "demon" chasing them and ran even faster, not caring about thorns or sharp rocks, and ended up bruised and exhausted.

They didn't realize it wasn't a demon at all — it was just their own friend — until daylight came.

(Adapted from *Spanish Fables*)
fields.tips: 这个故事中的戏子因为盲从第一个被吓坏了的戏子，结果让自己奔跑一晚，弄得身心疲倦。盲从是人的劣根性。准爸爸在给胎宝宝读这个故事的时候，可以跟准妈妈讨论一下，自己在生活中是不是也有过盲从别人，最后做了错事的时候呢？可以总结一下经验与教训哦。
fields.tips_en: In this story, a stage actor ends up exhausting himself by blindly following the first actor who panics and runs away. Blind conformity is a common human weakness. While reading this to your baby, you and the mother-to-be might reflect on moments when following the crowd led you astray, and share what you've learned.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 一本不说话的书
fields.subtitle: 生命的每一天都很奇特
fields.subtitle_en: Every Day of Life Is Wondrous
fields.content:
在乡间公路旁的树林里，有一个孤独的农庄，沿着公路可以一直走进这户农家的院子里去。这天，院子里的凉亭下停着一口敞着的棺材，上午就要下葬了。
死者的头底下垫着一大本厚书。这本书的每一页上都夹着一朵凋谢了的花或树叶。这是一本完整的植物标本，是在许多不同的地方搜集得来的。标本要陪着它的主人葬掉，这是主人的遗嘱，每朵花都记载着他生命中的一个故事。
“死者是谁呢？”有人问。
回答是：“他是乌卜萨拉（瑞典的一个古老大学，常常有些学生到老还没有毕业）的一个老学生。”
据说他曾经是一个活泼的年轻人，懂得古代文学，会唱歌，甚至还会写诗。但是，后来他遭遇到事故，之后他就把他的思想和生命沉浸在烧酒里，再后来，他就搬到乡下来了。
在乡下的日子里，只要坏情绪不来袭击他的时候，他都纯洁得像一个孩子，非常活泼地在森林里跑来跑去。不过只要人们把他喊回家来，他看到这本装满了植物的花和叶的书，就能坐一整天，一会儿看看这种花，一会儿看看那种花。有时他的眼泪就顺着脸庞滚下来，一段段往事又浮现在眼前。
假如，当我们年老的时候把年轻时代的信件拿出来读读，那将会有一种多么奇特的感觉啊！整个一生和这生命中的希望和哀愁都会浮现出来。
我们在年轻时来往很亲密的一些人，该有多少已经逝去了啊！也有多少中断了联系，杳无音信。那时我们以为永远会跟他们亲密地生活在一起，会跟他们一起共甘苦。
这书里面有一片枯萎了的栎树叶子。它使这本书的主人记起一个老朋友、老同学。他在一个绿树林里把这片叶子插在学生帽上，从那时起他们结为好朋友。现在他住在什么地方呢？这片叶子被保存了下来，但是朋友已无音信！
这儿有一棵异国的、在温室里培养出来的植物。对于北国的花园来说，它是太娇嫩了。它的叶子似乎还保留着它的香气。这是一位贵族小姐在自己花园里把它摘下来送给他的。
这儿有一朵睡莲。它是他亲手摘下来的，并且用他的咸的眼泪把它润湿过——这朵在河塘里生长的睡莲。
这儿有一根荨麻——它的叶子说明什么呢？当他把它采下来并保存下来的时候，他心中在想些什么呢？
这儿有一朵幽居在森林里的铃兰花；这儿有一朵从酒店的花盆里摘下来的金银花；这儿有一个尖尖的三叶草！
开满了花的紫丁香在死者的头上轻轻垂下它新鲜的、芬芳的花瓣。燕子又飞过去了。“唧唧！唧唧！”
这时人们拿着钉子和锤子走来了。棺材盖在死者身上盖上了，他的头枕在这本不说话的书上。
（作者：安徒生/丹麦）
fields.content_en:
Title: A Book That Does Not Speak

In a forest alongside a country road, there stood a lonely farmhouse, and you could walk from the road right into its courtyard. One morning, beneath a pavilion in the yard, lay an open coffin, for the burial would take place that very day.

Beneath the head of the dead lay a large, thick book. On every page were pressed flowers and leaves that had withered long ago. It was a complete collection of plant specimens, gathered from many different places. The specimens were to be buried with their owner, as he had requested in his will, for each flower told the story of a moment in his life.

"Who was this man?" someone asked.

The answer was: "He was an old student from Uppsala (an ancient university in Sweden, where sometimes students remain students until they grow old)."

He was said to have once been a lively young man who knew ancient literature, could sing, and even wrote poetry. But later, he went through a hard time, and after that he drowned his thoughts and his life in spirits. Still later, he moved to the countryside.

In those days in the countryside, whenever his sorrows did not overcome him, he was as pure as a child, running and playing happily through the forest. But whenever he was called home and saw this book, filled with flowers and leaves, he could sit all day long, now looking at one flower, now at another. Sometimes tears would roll down his face, and memories of days gone by would rise before his eyes again.

Oh, how strange it must feel when we are old and take out letters written in our youth and read them once more! The whole of life, with all its hopes and sorrows, will come floating before us.

How many of those dear friends we were once so close to in our younger days have already passed away! How many have lost all touch and given no news? At that time we thought we would always live closely with them, sharing in all their joys and trials.

Inside this book there is a withered oak leaf. It reminds the owner of an old friend and fellow student. In a green forest, that friend tucked this leaf into his student's cap, and from that day on they became close friends. But now, where in the world can he be? The leaf has been preserved, but there is no news of the friend!

Here is an exotic plant, grown in a warm greenhouse. It is too delicate for a garden in the north. Its leaves seem to still retain their fragrance. It was picked in the garden of a noble lady and given to him as a gift.

Here is a water lily. He picked it himself and moistened it with his salty tears—that water lily which grew in the river pond.

Here is a stalk of nettle. What do its leaves tell us? What was he thinking when he gathered and kept it?

Here is a lily of the valley, living quietly in the forest; here is a honeysuckle picked from a flowerpot at the inn; and here is a sharp little clover leaf!

Flowering lilac hangs its fresh and fragrant petals gently above the head of the dead. The swallows have flown by. "Tweet! Tweet!"

Then people came with nails and a hammer. The coffin lid was laid upon the dead man, his head resting on that book that does not speak.

(Author: Hans Christian Andersen / Denmark)
fields.tips: 这是一首散文诗一般的故事，语言亲切质朴，说的是一本“不说话的书”。实际上这本书说了许多话，它告诉我们一位“老学生”的一生。是啊，假如我们把年轻时代的信拿出来读读，会有一种多么奇特的感觉啊！坚持写日记是一件非常好的事情。准爸爸的日记，在宝宝出生、长大后仍然可以一直继续下去。
fields.tips_en: Written like a gentle prose poem, this story tells of a "silent book" that actually speaks volumes — recounting the life of an "old student." Imagine re-reading letters from your youth; how magical would that feel! Keeping a diary is a beautiful practice, and your own journal can continue well after your baby is born and grows.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 远方传来的雷声
fields.subtitle: 来自远方的情意
fields.subtitle_en: Warmth from Far Away
fields.content:
大雨过后，田里的种子都露出可爱的芽来了。黄瓜种子也发芽了，渐渐长出了像细线一样的藤，攀缠着妈妈搭的架子往上爬。不知不觉地就开出黄色的小花，花谢了，就长出了青青的、细长的黄瓜。
每年夏天，二郎都要这样看着黄瓜长大。在长出果实的时候二郎最快活了。“妈妈，黄瓜已经长这么大了！”每天，二郎从外面回家，照例要比画给妈妈看。
有一天，妈妈对二郎说：“二郎呀，去把最大的黄瓜摘下来吧。小心一些，不要伤了藤。”
二郎立刻跳跃着奔到田里去。他看到那根大的黄瓜悬挂在那里，一下子回忆起黄瓜长大的情景。他有点儿舍不得，但最后还是摘下了黄瓜。
“你总是去钓鱼啊，游泳呀，就把这个黄瓜送给水神吧。”妈妈说。
“水神还吃黄瓜吗？”
“黄瓜能顺水向遥远的海的方向漂去，水神会了解你的情意的……”
二郎似懂非懂。他把自己的名字写在这根黄瓜上，描了又描，然后把它从自己和伙伴们经常去玩的桥头投到河里去了。黄瓜一浮一沉地向着下游的方向漂去。
傍晚晴朗的天空上，灰色的云慢慢地聚集起来，远方传来了雷声。这一天，二郎总是没有边际地想着黄瓜的去向。可晚上他一钻进被窝，立刻就睡着了。
这时候，黄瓜在水里漂呀、漂呀，夜里经过了森林、原野和几个村落，在天亮时到了很远的地方。这天下午，一个衣衫褴褛的小乞丐在低低的小桥上发现了它。黄瓜上的字已经完全被水冲掉了，可是小乞丐也知道这根黄瓜是从很远很远的地方漂来的。因为这一带风还很寒冷，黄瓜的秧还很小呢。
小乞丐拿着黄瓜，高兴地跑去给妈妈和妹妹看。突然，孩子在路上站住，侧着耳朵听着，山那边传来隐约的雷声。在北方，夏天也来到了。
（作者：小川未明/日本）
fields.content_en:
# Thunder from Afar

After the heavy rain, seeds in the fields all poked out their cute little sprouts. The cucumber seeds had sprouted too, and slowly grew vines as thin as thread, winding upward along the trellis Mama had built. Before long, they opened tiny yellow flowers, and when the flowers faded, tender green cucumbers began to grow — long and slender.

Every summer, Ji'anger watched his cucumbers grow this way. He was happiest when the fruit began to form. "Mama, look how big the cucumber has gotten!" Every day, when he came home, he would show it to Mama, just as he always did.

One day, Mama said to Ji'anger, "Ji'anger, go pick the biggest cucumber. Be careful not to hurt the vine."

Ji'anger immediately hopped and ran to the field. He saw that big cucumber hanging there, and suddenly remembered all the days he had watched it grow. He felt a little reluctant to pick it, but in the end, he gently plucked the cucumber.

"You're always off fishing and swimming," said Mama. "Why don't you give this cucumber to the Water God?"

"Does the Water God eat cucumbers too?"

"The cucumber will float along the water all the way to the distant sea," said Mama. "The Water God will understand what's in your heart…"

Ji'anger didn't fully understand, but he wrote his name on the cucumber, traced it over and over, and then tossed it from the stone bridge where he and his friends loved to play, into the river. The cucumber bobbed up and down as it drifted downstream.

That evening, the clear sky grew cloudy as gray clouds gathered slowly, and thunder rumbled in the distance. All day long, Ji'anger's thoughts wandered far away, wondering where the cucumber was going. But the moment he snuggled under his covers that night, he fell fast asleep.

Meanwhile, the cucumber floated and floated through the water. It drifted through forests and meadows and several villages overnight, and by dawn it had reached a place very far away. That afternoon, a small beggar boy, dressed in tattered clothes, noticed it on a low little bridge. The words on the cucumber had been completely washed away by the water, but the little boy knew this cucumber had floated from very, very far away — for the wind in these parts was still cold, and cucumber vines were still tiny.

The little boy held the cucumber and happily ran to show it to his mama and his little sister. Suddenly, the child stopped on the road and tilted his ear, listening. Faint thunder came from beyond the mountains. Summer, too, had come to the north.

*(Author: Yunmi Ogawa / Japan)*
fields.tips: 二郎顺流漂走一根新鲜、漂亮的黄瓜。这小小的举动却给小乞丐带来了温暖，而且也带来了夏天到来的信息。夏天雷雨比较多，准爸爸在雷雨前应提早关好门窗，给准妈妈温暖的关怀。
fields.tips_en: Er Lang floats a fresh, lovely cucumber downstream. Such a small act brings warmth to a little beggar child and signals the arrival of summer. Summer storms are frequent, so be sure to close the windows and doors early, and shower the mother-to-be with your tender care.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 数数的猪
fields.subtitle: 别忘记了自己
fields.subtitle_en: Don't Forget Yourself
fields.content:
在一条小溪边，一只老猪正准备带着自己的一群小猪走过溪水。
老猪对小猪们说：“我们一共12只，到对岸之后，要记得数数对不对。”它吩咐完毕，就和小猪们一同渡水过去了。
不一会儿就到了对岸，小猪们抖落着身上的水，老猪则开始清点猪群，看有没有遗失。
但是，它数来数去，都只有11只，这是怎么回事啊？忽然，它惊叫道：“肯定有一只在渡河时被水冲走了。”
小猪们一听，立刻伤心地大哭起来。
一个聪明人见到这种情形，不禁“扑哧”一声笑了。他对这头老猪说道：“你数了几次，都忘记了你自己。世界上第一件要注意的事就是自己。你为什么竟忘了你自己呢！”
（作者：泰戈尔/印度）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Counting Pig

By a little stream, an old pig was about to lead her group of piglets across the water.

The old pig said to her babies, "We are twelve in all. When we reach the other side, remember to count, okay?" And with that, she crossed over together with her piglets.

Soon they reached the other side. The piglets shook the water off their bodies, and the old pig began to count her herd, making sure no one was missing.

But no matter how many times she counted, there were only eleven. What was going on? Suddenly, she cried out in alarm, "One must have been swept away by the river while crossing!"

Hearing this, the piglets immediately burst into sad tears.

A clever person who saw this couldn't help but chuckle. He said to the old pig, "You counted and counted, but you forgot yourself. The first thing to remember is always yourself. How could you have forgotten that you are a pig too!"

(Author: Rabindranath Tagore / India)
fields.tips: 是啊，我们首先要把自己安顿好，忠于自己的内心，这样才不至于出现自责、不安、焦虑的感觉。在给胎宝宝读胎教故事的过程中，准爸爸也应当忠于自己的内心。如果你不赞同故事的观点，那么，就按照自己的想法来说给他听吧。
fields.tips_en: We must first settle ourselves and stay true to our hearts, so we need not fall into guilt, unease, or anxiety. As you read these stories to your baby, dear father, be faithful to your own inner voice. If you don't agree with something in the tale, share your own thoughts aloud — your baby will feel the sincerity.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 鸟
fields.subtitle: 感受幻想的魔力
fields.subtitle_en: Feeling the Magic of Imagination
fields.content:
从前在一个城镇里住着一位耳科医生。由于他的医术很好，来就医的人络绎不绝。
一天黄昏，来了一个少女，她捂着一只耳朵，脸色苍白，喘着粗气。“你怎么啦？”医生一边洗手一边问。
少女指着自己的右耳，叫道：“耳朵里进了不得了的东西，请快给我取出来吧！”
于是医生从柜子里拿出纱布和镊子，悠闲地坐在椅子上，问道：“是什么进去啦？”
“是秘密，秘密钻进我耳朵里去了。希望您能赶快把它取出来，否则等太阳西下的时候就完了。”
医生直眨眼睛。这样的病人，还是头一回遇见。“那，你到底听了什么样的秘密？”他和蔼地问。
少女小声说：“我听说我最喜欢的人，其实是只鸟，是被施了魔法的海鸥。”
“唔。”医生露出惊奇的神色，点点头，然后鼓励少女讲得更详细一点儿。于是少女讲了这样的事：
“我和他是在海边认识的。后来我才知道，他是渔女的儿子。我惊讶极了。渔女的年纪很大了，眼睛凹陷，很模糊。我们总是害怕她的眼睛——那双像奇异的沉淀物，仿佛在海底活了200年的鱼的眼睛！
“时间一天天过去，我们既快乐又觉得恐惧，想逃离这里，到更宽广的地方去无拘无束地生活。但是他害怕会魔法的妈妈，最后我们还是决定傍晚坐着小船偷偷逃走。
“到了约定的时间，我一溜烟儿朝小船跑去。那种期盼与甜蜜感围绕着我。然而等我到船上时，看到的却是渔女。她把他锁在小房子里了。她冷笑着告诉我一个秘密：我心爱的人是一只海鸥，很早以前受了伤，被渔女救了。她把他当做自己的孩子一样疼爱，想让他一直待在自己身边。没想到有一天，从海里来了一只雌海鸥。他们相爱了，想飞到海上去。渔女对雌海鸥恨得要命，于是她把两粒施了魔法的红色海藻果实给家里的海鸥吃了。结果，只吃了一粒，海鸥就变成了男孩子。她高兴得不得了，甚至没有觉察到剩下的一粒丢在什么地方了。”
渔女恶毒地告诉我这个秘密，是因为一旦有人知道了，魔法就会解除，他就会重新变回海鸥了。除非我能忘掉或者从耳朵里取出这个秘密。
“原来是这样，”耳科医生点点头，“那么，给你看一下吧。”
呀，太奇怪了，医生看到少女的耳朵深处有一个恰如小人国的风景：深蓝色的大海，金色的沙滩，还有一朵盛开的闪光的白色的辛夷花——不，那不是花，那是一只海鸥！“这就是秘密吧！”医生高兴起来，想把那只鸟取出来。
可是，时间一点儿一点儿地过去了，医生用再长的镊子都够不着！突然，少女站起身来，悲伤地说：“太阳下沉了，我心爱的人已经变成鸟了！”
医生垂下头，他觉得非常过意不去。少女默默地回去了。这时，医生看见少女坐过的那把椅子上有些羽毛样的东西。他拿起来端详，啊，是海鸥的羽毛！
医生吃了一惊。他赶紧追了出去，一个劲儿地跑。那孩子不知道，她自己也是海鸥。不知什么时候，她吃了渔女丢下的红果实，变成了女孩。可是她一点儿也不知道。
医生不停地追赶着少女，他想要在少女的耳朵里，装进另一个美丽的秘密。
（作者：安房直子/日本）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Bird**

Once upon a time, in a little town, there lived an ear doctor. Because he was so good at his work, people came to him from far and wide.

One evening, a young girl came, covering one ear, her face pale and her breath quick. "What's wrong?" asked the doctor, washing his hands.

The girl pointed to her right ear and cried out, "Something terrible has gone in! Please take it out soon!"

So the doctor took out some gauze and tweezers from his cabinet, sat down comfortably in his chair, and asked, "What went in?"

"A secret, a secret crawled into my ear. Please take it out quickly, or it will be too late when the sun sets," she said.

The doctor blinked. He had never seen a patient like this before. "Well, what kind of secret did you hear?" he asked gently.

The girl whispered, "I heard that the person I love the most is actually a bird—a seagull under a spell."

"Oh," the doctor's eyes widened with wonder. He nodded and encouraged her to tell him more. So the girl told her story:

"I met him by the sea. Later, I found out that he was the son of a fisherwoman. I was so surprised. The fisherwoman was very old, with deep, clouded eyes. We were always afraid of those eyes—eyes like strange sediment, as if they had lived at the bottom of the sea for two hundred years!

"Day after day passed, we were happy yet afraid, wanting to escape here and live freely somewhere much wider. But he was afraid of his magical mother, and so we decided to sneak away in the evening on a small boat.

"When the appointed time came, I ran as fast as I could toward the little boat. That feeling of hope and sweetness surrounded me. But when I arrived, who did I see? The fisherwoman. She had locked him inside a small room. With a cold smile, she told me a secret: the one I love is a seagull. Long ago, he was hurt, and the fisherwoman saved him. She doted on him as if he were her own child, wanting him to stay by her side forever. One day, unexpectedly, a female seagull came from the sea. They fell in love and wanted to fly out to the ocean together. The fisherwoman hated the female seagull so much that she gave two red seaweed berries, enchanted with magic, to the seagull at home. The seagull ate only one berry and turned into a boy. The fisherwoman was overjoyed and never even noticed where she had dropped the other berry."

The fisherwoman told me this secret cruelly, because once someone knows it, the magic will be broken and he will turn back into a seagull. Unless I can forget it or take the secret out of my ear.

"I see," said the ear doctor, nodding. "Let me have a look."

Oh, how strange! The doctor saw deep inside the girl's ear a scene just like a miniature world: a deep blue sea, a golden beach, and a bright, shining white magnolia flower—no, that wasn't a flower, it was a seagull! "This must be the secret!" The doctor was delighted and tried to take the little bird out.

But as time slipped away little by little, no matter how long the tweezers he used, he couldn't reach it! Suddenly, the girl stood up and said sadly, "The sun has set. The one I love has already turned into a bird!"

The doctor bowed his head, feeling very sorry. The girl quietly went back. Then, the doctor noticed something feather-like on the chair where the girl had been sitting. He picked it up and looked closely. Ah, it was a seagull feather!

The doctor was startled. He ran out quickly, chasing after her with all his might. The girl didn't know it herself—she too was a seagull. Somewhere along the way, she had eaten the red berry the fisherwoman had dropped and turned into a girl. But she had no idea.

The doctor kept running after the girl, hoping to put another beautiful secret into her ear.

(Author: Nanao Se / Japan)
fields.tips: 医生能否追上少女，告诉她这个美丽的秘密呢？这仿佛是一个不可思议的梦一样。拿起久违的画笔吧，把这两只幻想世界里的鸟儿画出来，讲给准妈妈和胎宝宝听，他们一定会喜欢这个感觉的。
fields.tips_en: Will the doctor catch up with the young girl and whisper this beautiful secret? It feels almost like a wondrous dream. Pick up a long-forgotten brush and draw the two birds from this imaginative world — tell the story to the mother-to-be and your little one. They will treasure the magic of it.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小马阿索加
fields.subtitle: 总是帮倒忙的小可爱
fields.subtitle_en: You little chaos-maker, always trying to help but making things worse 🥰
fields.content:
阿索加是一匹小马，它总是学不会帮助别人。它妈妈十分生气，对它说：“今天，我要你去椰子林走一趟，要是你帮助了别人，就回来告诉我，我才给你午饭吃。”
阿索加哭着说：“我只是一匹小马。”可是妈妈说：“就是一匹小马也要去帮助别人，你不能总是想着自己。”看到妈妈这样生气，阿索加赶紧跑开了。它现在要找到一个能让它帮助的动物，然后才能快点回来吃午饭。
阿索加看见一只漂亮的蝴蝶停在一朵荷花上。“我敢肯定那只蝴蝶飞不起来了，所以它坐在那朵荷花上，我来帮帮它。”它走到荷花跟前，但是蝴蝶看见它来了，就立刻飞走了。
荷花责备它说：“你这只傻小马，蝴蝶正在喝甜蜜的甘露，你把它吓跑了。别在这里待着了，如果你站在这儿，会把所有在我身上停留的昆虫都吓跑的，快走吧！”
荷花气得脸都红了，可怜的小马赶快跑开了。小马心想：“我只是想帮它一下呀。”
当阿索加往前一路小跑的时候，它看见老牛米拉在一棵大树下睡着了。因为老牛太累了，身子在不停地摇晃，还直打哆嗦。阿索加想：“米拉一定病了，我该给它淋点水。它的眼睛紧闭着，一定病得很重。”它打来一桶水浇在米拉身上。
米拉跳了起来。它看见阿索加和水桶，就说：“你这匹笨马。我工作了一上午，把椰子运到一所大房子里，我累坏了，你却给我浇了一身水。你这笨马，快走开！”
阿索加见老牛生气，很害怕，赶紧跑掉了。阿索加又累又饿，都快天黑了，它还没帮助过任何动物。它站在一个小池塘旁喝水，看见大鱼跳出水面，喘了口气，然后又沉了下去。阿索加很高兴，它肯定大鱼需要帮助，大鱼想要跳出池塘。
阿索加弯下身，把鱼捞出池塘，放在草地上。大鱼一边挣扎，一边有气无力地说：“快把我放回池塘去，你这笨马，我需要水来呼吸。”
阿索加看着大鱼，不明白它为什么要使劲蹦跶。“你在草地上会很幸福的，我帮助了你，可以回家吃午饭了。”它喊道。
附近的鸭子穆林听见声音就跑过来看。可怜的大鱼还在扑腾着，想要回到池塘里去。老灰鸭赶紧把它推进池塘里。它责备阿索加说：“你这匹笨小马，这样会害死鱼的。”
可怜的阿索加坐下来哭了。老灰鸭问：“你为什么哭呀？”
小马回答说：“妈妈说我必须帮助过一个人才能回家。天都快黑了，我还没有帮助过任何人，我很饿了。”说完就大声地哭起来。
“来，”灰鸭说，“我带你回家去。”它把小马带回了家。马妈妈正在路上望着，它跑出来迎接阿索加。“我真担心呀！你哭什么呀？”
“我没有帮助任何人。当我想帮助别人的时候，它们都说我是一匹笨马。现在我又饿又累。”
老灰鸭说：“首先帮助你家里的人，你就能帮助其他人了。那时候你就是一匹好小马了。”阿索加紧紧依偎在妈妈的身旁说：“我会的，谢谢你啦，穆林。”
（选自《斯里兰卡寓言故事》）
fields.content_en:
**Title: Little Horse Asoka**

Asoka was a little horse who never seemed to learn how to help others. His mama was very upset and told him, "Today, I want you to go to the coconut grove. If you help someone along the way, come back and tell me, and then I will give you your lunch."

Asoka cried, "But I'm just a little horse!" But his mama said, "Even a little horse can help others. You cannot always think only of yourself." Seeing how angry Mama was, Asoka hurried off. He needed to find an animal he could help, so he could come back quickly and eat lunch.

Asoka saw a beautiful butterfly resting on a lotus flower. "I'm sure that butterfly can't fly anymore," he thought. "That's why it's sitting on the lotus. Let me help it!" He walked over to the lotus, but the butterfly saw him coming and immediately flew away.

The lotus scolded him, saying, "You silly little horse! The butterfly was drinking sweet nectar, and you scared it away. Don't stay here! If you stand around, you'll scare all the insects that visit me. Go away now!"

The lotus was so upset it turned red. The poor little horse ran away quickly, thinking to himself, "I was only trying to help!"

As Asoka trotted along, he saw old ox Mila asleep under a big tree. Poor old Mila was so tired that his body kept rocking and shaking. Asoka thought, "Mila must be sick. I should pour some water on him. His eyes are tightly shut—he must be very ill indeed." So he fetched a bucket of water and poured it all over Mila.

Mila jumped up. Seeing Asoka and the bucket, he said, "You foolish horse! I worked all morning, carrying coconuts to a big house. I'm exhausted, and you pour water on me! You foolish horse, go away!"

Asoka was very frightened by the old ox's anger and quickly ran off. He was tired and hungry, and soon it was nearly dark, yet he still hadn't helped any animal. He stood beside a small pond drinking water when he saw a big fish jump out of the water, catch its breath, and sink back down. Asoka was very happy. He was sure the big fish needed help—the fish wanted to jump out of the pond!

Asoka bent down, pulled the fish out of the pond, and placed it on the grass. The fish struggled and said weakly, "Put me back in the pond at once, you silly horse. I need water to breathe."

Asoka looked at the fish, confused by all its wriggling. "You'll be so happy on the grass," he called out. "I helped you, and now I can go home for lunch!"

Nearby, a duck named Mullin heard the noise and came running over. The poor big fish was still flopping about, trying to get back to the pond. Old Gray Duck quickly pushed it back into the water. She scolded Asoka, saying, "You silly little horse, you could have killed that fish!"

Poor Asoka sat down and began to cry. Old Gray Duck asked, "Why are you crying?"

The little horse answered, "Mama said I must help someone before I can go home. It's nearly dark, and I haven't helped anyone yet. I'm so hungry." And he began to cry loudly.

"Come," said Gray Duck, "I'll take you home." She led the little horse back home. Mama Horse was waiting along the path and ran out to meet him. "I was so worried! What are you crying for?"

"I didn't help anyone," said Asoka. "Whenever I tried to help, they all called me a silly horse. Now I'm hungry and tired."

Old Gray Duck said, "First, learn to help the people in your own home. Then you'll be able to help others. That's when you'll be a good little horse." Asoka snuggled close to his mama and said, "I will. Thank you, Mullin."

(Adapted from *Sri Lankan Fables*)
fields.tips: 小马阿索加就像一个可爱、善良的孩子，一心想要帮助大人做点啥，却总是帮倒忙。准爸爸在给胎宝宝讲这个故事的时候可要记得，将来宝宝出生后，也会像小马阿索加一样，喜欢去帮助爸爸妈妈做一些事情，但是却总也做不好。这时候，爸爸妈妈一定要耐心鼓励和引导，千万不能责备他是一个笨小孩哦。
fields.tips_en: Little pony Asoga is like a sweet, kind-hearted child who really wants to help grown-ups, but always seems to make things worse. When an expectant dad shares this story with his baby, he should remember that after birth, the baby will also want to help mom and dad like little Asoga does—even if they don't quite get it right yet. In those moments, parents must be patient, offering encouragement and gentle guidance. Please never scold your little one for being clumsy!
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: “需要”
fields.subtitle: 解决问题的动力
fields.subtitle_en: The drive to find solutions
fields.content:
从前有一个樵夫，他有两个儿子，他每天都轮流带一个儿子到森林里去打柴。
后来，这两个儿子都长大了，樵夫就对他们说：“孩子们，以后你们就自己到森林里去打柴吧，我就留在家里了。”
两个儿子说：“爸爸，要是大车坏了，由谁来修呀？”
“孩子们，如果大车坏了，或者还碰到了别的什么困难，你们都不用怕，‘需要’会帮助你们的！”樵夫告诉儿子们。
弟兄两个高高兴兴地进了森林。他们手脚很快，这一天他们打了很多柴。他们把柴捆好，装上车，赶着大车就往回走了。可是不巧，车子在半路上坏了，于是弟兄两个一起喊了起来：“‘需要’呀，你快来帮我们修车吧！”
他们喊了一遍又一遍，嗓子都干了，天也快要黑了，可是“需要”还是没有来。弟弟满肚子不高兴：“这个该死的‘需要’就是不来。哥哥，我们还是自己动手修吧！”哥哥说：“大概是‘需要’离我们太远了，没有听见我们的话，让我们用最大的力气再喊一阵！”
他们又喊了许多遍，直到把嗓子喊哑了，“需要”还是没有来。等得没有指望了，弟兄两个只好自己动手。两个人齐心协力，车很快就修好了。
回到家里，弟兄两个一起抱怨起来：“哎呀，我的爸爸，我们刚走到半路上，车就坏了。我们一直喊那个该死的‘需要’，把嗓子都喊哑了，它都不来。我们拿起斧头和凿子，自己把大车修好了。”
父亲听了高兴地说：“我的孩子们，这就是‘需要’呀！它就在你们身边，而你们还喊它呢！没有人帮助你们，你们自己不是也把事情办好了吗？”
fields.content_en:
Title: "Need"

Once upon a time, there was a woodcutter who had two sons. Every day, he took one son with him to the forest to gather firewood.

Later, the two sons grew up, and the woodcutter said to them, "My dear children, from now on, you can go into the forest yourselves to gather firewood. I will stay home."

The two sons said, "Father, who will fix the cart if it breaks?"

The father told his sons, "Children, if the cart breaks or if anything else goes wrong, don't be afraid. 'Need' will help you!"

The two brothers happily walked into the forest. They worked quickly, and that day they gathered a lot of firewood. They tied it up, loaded it onto the cart, and set off on their way home. Unfortunately, the cart broke down halfway there. So the two brothers called out together, "Oh 'Need,' please come and help us fix the cart!"

They called and called again and again until their voices grew hoarse, and soon it would be dark. Still, "Need" did not come. The younger brother was quite unhappy. "This silly 'Need' just won't show up. Brother, let's fix it ourselves!" The older brother said, "Perhaps 'Need' is too far away to hear us. Let's call out one more time with all our might!"

They called many more times until their voices were completely gone, but "Need" still did not come. With no hope left, the two brothers had no choice but to fix it themselves. Working together, they soon had the cart mended.

When they returned home, the two brothers complained together, "Oh, Father, our cart broke down just halfway. We kept calling out to that 'Need' until our voices were hoarse, but it never came. In the end, we picked up our axes and chisels and fixed the cart ourselves."

The father listened and said happily, "My children, that is exactly what 'Need' is! It was right beside you the whole time, and yet you kept calling for it! No one came to help, didn't you manage to get the job done on your own?"
fields.tips: “‘需要’会帮助你们的”，这真是一句智慧的话。是啊，我们的需要会帮助自己成长起来，渐渐地我们就能从容面对任何困难了。生活才是我们真正的老师啊。胎宝宝的需要，准妈妈的需要，自己的需要，这些都会是准爸爸努力生活的动力。
fields.tips_en: "'Need' will guide you,"—what truly wise words. Indeed, our needs become the very thing that helps us grow, and over time we learn to face whatever comes our way with calm confidence. Life is our truest teacher, after all. Your little one's needs, your partner's needs, even your own—they're all what will light a fire under dad-to-be to keep moving forward, giving his very best each day.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 臣子的“好”办法
fields.subtitle: 目光短浅害人害己
fields.subtitle_en: Short-Sighted Thinking Hurts Everyone
fields.content:
从前有一个贪婪的国王，有一天他听说有一个仙人来到他的国境。这个仙人可了不起啦，他的眼睛能够看见埋在地下的一切宝藏。
国王心里不知有多快乐，便和臣子们商议说：“我们要想一个办法，叫这个仙人总住在我们这里，不让他到别的国家去，那么我就能够得到藏在地下的所有财宝，我将比任何国王都富有了。”
有一个臣子眼珠转了转，马上说道：“臣有一个好法子！”
国王一听，高兴极了：“爱卿有什么好法子啊？”
可那个臣子却不肯说出是怎样的好法子。他立即跑到仙人那里去，把仙人的一双眼睛挖了出来，拿回来呈给国王说：“臣已经留下仙人的眼睛了，现在他就是到别的地方去也不要紧了。”
不用说，这个仙人被挖了眼睛就成了一个瞎子了。别人得不到，国王自然也得不到地下的财宝。（选自《印度寓言故事》）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Minister's "Good" Idea

Once upon a time, there was a greedy king. One day, he heard that a magical sage had come to his kingdom. This sage was truly amazing—his eyes could see all the treasures hidden underground.

The king was overjoyed and said to his ministers, "We must find a way to make this sage stay in our kingdom forever, so he can never go to another country. Then I will be able to find all the treasures underground, and I will be the richest king of all."

One minister twirled his eyes and quickly said, "I have a wonderful idea!"

The king was thrilled. "What is your idea, dear minister?"

But the minister would not say what his idea was. Instead, he ran straight to the sage, dug out his two eyes, and brought them back to the king. "I have left the sage's eyes here," he said. "Now it does not matter if he travels to other places."

As you can imagine, the sage was now blind. No one else could find the treasures underground—and neither could the king.
fields.tips: 这个愚蠢的臣子真是舍本逐末啊。其实，仔细想一想，做胎教也是一样的道理。不能光想着做胎教，而忘记了最重要的是让胎儿快乐地成长。如果扰乱他的睡眠就得不偿失啦。
fields.tips_en: That foolish minister truly put the cart before the horse! And you know what? Prenatal education works the same way. We shouldn't obsess so much over formal exercises that we forget the most important thing: helping our baby grow happy and content. If we're disturbing little one's sweet sleep, then we've missed the whole point altogether.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 给小鸭子让路
fields.title_en: Make way for the little duckling. 🦆💛
fields.subtitle: 来自城市的温情
fields.subtitle_en: The warmth of the city
fields.content:
鸭先生和鸭太太为找一个孵小鸭的好地方，已经飞很久了。它们飞到波士顿城时，就再也飞不动了。
在波士顿，它们一开始觉得公园是落脚的好地方：那里有池塘，池塘里有小岛……可是那里车辆来来往往，太不安全啦。
于是，它们飞到山那边的广场。广场倒是还行，可就是没有游泳的地方。不一会儿，它们飞到了一条河的上空，下面出现了一个小岛。“这儿好，”鸭先生说，“这儿安静，离广场也只一小段路。”“好的，就在这儿吧！”鸭太太绕着小岛飞了一圈说。
它们在矮树林里找了个又挨水又背风的地方安下了家。不久，鸭太太下了8个蛋，并开始孵蛋。它耐心地在8个蛋上趴了许多天，终于小鸭子孵出来了。最先出来的是杰克，接着是卡克、拉克、马克、奈克、威克、帕克和夸克。
一天，鸭先生决定到河对岸的公园去看看，它觉得公园一定会比这里更好。出发前，它对鸭太太说：“过一个星期，我在公园等你们，你可要照顾好孩子们！”
“你放心去吧，”鸭太太说，“我会把孩子一个不少地带到你那儿去的。”
鸭先生走后，鸭太太开始教小鸭子游水、扎猛子，还训练它们走路排成一条直线，同自行车和各种有轮子的东西保持安全的距离。
鸭太太觉得把孩子们训练得差不多了，于是，一天早上它说：“孩子们，跟我走！”
8只小鸭子，像平常妈妈教它们的样子，排成长长的一排。鸭太太率先跳进河里，小鸭子们纷纷跟着妈妈下水，游到对岸去。
到了对岸以后，它们摇摇摆摆来到公路上。鸭太太走在前面，领着孩子们快步穿过十字路口。公路上飞驰的汽车“嘀——嘀”给小鸭子让路，叫个不停。鸭太太带领孩子，大喉咙小喉咙一齐“嘎——嘎——嘎”，对着汽车也叫个不停。
嘀——嘀——嘀，嘀——嘀——嘀！
嘎——嘎——嘎，嘎——嘎——嘎！
吵闹声把警察米歇尔给引了过来，他边跑边吹警哨。他站在路中间，举起一只手，让行人和汽车全停下来，接着用另一只手招呼鸭妈妈带着孩子们穿过公路。之后，米歇尔赶回警亭，给总部挂电话：“有一帮鸭子，大大小小9只，正往大街走去！”
总部的警察一下子弄糊涂了，直问：“一帮什么？”“一帮鸭子！”米歇尔大声说，“赶快派警车来，要快！”
不一会儿，鸭太太一家9口已经来到一家书店，再拐弯就上大街了。街上行人们一个个都看呆了。一位老太太喃喃地说：“这可是一辈子没见过的！”一个扫街的男人说：“噢，排得真整齐！”鸭太太听到这些赞扬，感到非常自豪，高高地抬起头，走起路来更加摇摆了。
另一条大街的拐角处已经停着一辆警车和4名警察，警察举手拦住了行人和车辆，让鸭太太带着小鸭子们顺利通过十字路口，再从那里进到公园里去。
它们走进公园大门以后，又全部转过身子，围成一个半圆，向警察表示感谢。警察们笑了，挥手向鸭子一家告别：“再见！”
鸭先生早已在公园里迎接它们了。
（作者：罗伯特·麦克洛斯基/美国）
fields.content_en:
# Let the Ducks Cross

Mr. Duck and Mrs. Duck had been flying for a very long time, looking for a wonderful place to raise their ducklings. By the time they reached the city of Boston, they were too tired to fly any further.

At first, they thought the park would be a lovely place to settle: it had a pond, and a little island in the pond… But the cars were zooming by all the time, and it was far too dangerous.

So they flew over to the square on the other side of the hill. The square was okay, but there was nowhere for the ducks to swim. Soon, they found themselves flying over a river, and below them appeared a little island. "This is perfect," said Mr. Duck. "It's quiet, and only a short walk from the square." "Let's stay here!" said Mrs. Duck, circling the island once.

They found a cozy little spot in the bushy trees, right by the water and sheltered from the wind, and made their home. Soon, Mrs. Duck laid eight eggs and began to sit on them. She stayed patiently on those eight eggs for many, many days, and at last, out popped the ducklings. The first to hatch was Jack, then Clek, Lek, Mek, Nek, Weck, Pack, and Quack.

One day, Mr. Duck decided to swim across the river to visit the park on the other side. He felt it would surely be a nicer place than where they were. Before setting off, he told Mrs. Duck, "Wait for me a week in the park, and please look after our babies well!"

"Don't worry about a thing," said Mrs. Duck. "I'll bring them all, not one missing."

After Mr. Duck left, Mrs. Duck began teaching the ducklings how to swim and dive, and she practiced walking with them in a neat single file line, keeping a safe distance from bicycles and anything with wheels.

Mrs. Duck felt her little ones were ready, so one morning she said, "Children, follow me!"

The eight ducklings, just as Mommy had taught them, formed a long, wiggly line. Mrs. Duck led the way into the river, and the ducklings jumped in behind her, swimming across to the other side.

On the other side, they waddled right onto the road. Mrs. Duck walked bravely in front, leading her little ones quickly across the crosswalk. Cars zooming by went "Beep—beep" to let the ducklings pass, honking all the while. Mrs. Duck led her children, big voices and little voices together, "Quack—quack—quack," honking right back at the cars!

Beep—beep—beep, beep—beep—beep!
Quack—quack—quack, quack—quack—quack!

The noisy commotion drew Officer Michel over. He ran, blowing his whistle the whole way. Standing in the middle of the road, he raised one hand to stop all pedestrians and cars, then used his other hand to wave Mrs. Duck across with her babies. After seeing them safely through, Michel hurried back to the police booth and phoned headquarters: "We've got a flock of ducks—nine altogether, big and small—walking down Main Street!"

The officers at headquarters were completely puzzled and kept asking, "A flock of what?" "A flock of ducks!" Michel called out. "Send a police car quickly, hurry!"

Soon, the nine ducks had reached a bookstore and were turning onto the main street. The people walking along the street all stood and stared in wonder. An old lady murmured, "I've never seen anything like this in all my days!" A street sweeper said, "Oh, look how neatly they're walking!" Hearing these kind words, Mrs. Duck felt very proud. She lifted her head high and waddled even more proudly.

At the corner of another street, a police car and four officers were already waiting. They raised their hands to stop pedestrians and traffic, letting Mrs. Duck and her ducklings cross the intersection safely, and then pass into the park.

After entering the park gate, the whole family turned around, formed a half-circle, and thanked the officers. The officers smiled and waved goodbye to the duck family. "Goodbye!"

Mr. Duck was already there in the park, waiting to welcome them.
(Author: Robert McCloskey / USA)
fields.tips: 在钢筋水泥的城市，给小鸭子让路就像是浪漫的童话故事，温情满满。故事中的鸭爸爸鸭妈妈努力地给孩子找一个好的生活环境，努力地训练孩子的生存技能，跟人类多么类似。从决定要宝宝的那一刻开始，准爸爸准妈妈也在为孩子的到来尽量创造更合适的环境。准爸爸准妈妈需要记得的是，孩子不仅需要精致的玩具，更需要到大自然中去，听鸟叫声，他喜欢置身于绿树花海中的感觉。
fields.tips_en:
这段文字写得真好，小鸭子在城市里穿行，画面感特别强。

鸭父母的执着和人类准爸妈如出一辙——从决定要孩子的那一刻，就开始琢磨怎么给TA最好的世界。但文章最戳人的是后半句：**孩子需要的不是精致的玩具，而是鸟叫声、绿树花海。**

现在大城市里，钢筋水泥越盖越高，自然离孩子越来越远。周末带孩子去公园，他蹲在地上看蚂蚁的时间比看iPad还长——那种专注和快乐，是任何昂贵玩具都给不了的。

也许真正的"好环境"，不是学区房和兴趣班，而是能让孩子在泥土里打滚、在草地上奔跑的机会。

---

你是想分享这段感悟，还是有别的想法？比如想让我帮忙润色成更完整的小品文，或者延伸一些亲子自然的建议？
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 娃娃太婆
fields.subtitle: 回到生命之初
fields.subtitle_en: Return to the beginning of life.
fields.content:
从前，有两个老人家，他们过着很平静的生活。老头子每天上山去打柴，老太婆就在家里操持家务。
有一天，老头子到森林里去打柴了，一直到晚上很晚都还没有回来。老太婆等啊等，等了整整一夜，老头子都没有回来。“不会是出什么事了吧？”老太婆有点儿担心了。
第二天一大早，老太婆正在门口张望，忽然一个青年背着一捆柴火到了她家，径直朝着门口走来。老太婆仔细一看：这不就是她家的老头子吗？他怎么长得和20岁的时候一模一样啊！
“你这是怎么啦？”老太婆惊奇地问他。
“你说多神奇啊，”老头子于是给老太婆讲了他经历的事情，“昨天，我正在山里打柴，忽然间刮起了一阵大风。我抬头一看，一只从来没有见过的美丽的小鸟飞过来，在我的头上转了几圈就又飞走了。我跟着鸟儿往前走，它把我带到了一个奇异的山谷，那里漫山遍野开满了鲜花，到处都飘着花的香味，风景真是美极了！”
老头子又陶醉地说：“在离山谷不远的地方有一条小河，河里的泉水比任何一条河里的水都清澈。我渴了，就去舀河里的水喝。没想到，一喝这种水，我就突然感到浑身增添了力量。等我喝够了，就像喝醉了酒一样，在山泉旁边睡着了，醒来时已经是深夜了。我一个人感到害怕，就急忙往回赶，一路小跑着回来。”
“啊，这么说来，是泉水让你变年轻了。我也要找到这眼泉水，我也要变年轻点儿！”
“好吧，你去找吧！”老头子高高兴兴地给她指了路。
可是第二天，老太婆并没有回家。又过了几天，她还是没有回家。老头子心想：老婆子这一觉睡得可够久的啊。于是老头子又等了些天，可她仍是没有回来，老头子不得不去找她。
他到了一片林中空地，一看，周围空荡荡的，一个人也没有。他心里越来越不安了。他心想：“会不会是什么野兽把她吃掉了呢？”
他又到泉水边上走了一趟，还是没有找到老太婆的踪迹。他灰心了，刚要往回走，忽然听到一个小孩的哭声。
“谁会把小孩带到这个荒凉的地方呢？”他想着想着，便朝哭声传来的方向走去。
在一片茂密的草丛里，他发现了一个白色的东西，走近一看，原来是他家老太婆的一件衣服。衣服里面裹着一个哇哇大哭的孩子。
“糟糕！我的老伴变成个小娃娃了！”老头子急得不知怎么是好。
娃娃朝他点点头，哭得更凶了。
“可怜哪可怜，这就是你啊，我的老伴！”老头子对她说，“你太贪婪，青春的泉水喝得大多了，已经变成一个吃奶的娃娃了。现在可叫我怎么办呢？”
老头子没有别的办法，只好把他的娃娃老太婆捧在手上带回家。
从此以后，老头子每天都要抱着他的娃娃老太婆，挨家挨户地去求人家给她喂奶。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Granny in Baby Form**

Once upon a time, there was an old couple who lived a quiet and peaceful life. The old man went up the mountain every day to gather firewood, while the old woman stayed home and took care of the house.

One day, the old man went into the forest to collect firewood, but he didn't come back until very late at night. The old woman waited and waited, all through the long night, but he never returned. "Could something have happened to him?" she worried.

Early the next morning, just as she was standing at the door looking out, suddenly a young man carrying a bundle of firewood arrived at her house and walked straight toward her. She looked closely — wouldn't you know, it was her old man! But he looked exactly as he had when he was twenty years old!

"What on earth happened to you?" she asked in surprise.

"Isn't it wonderful?" the old man told her about his adventure. "Yesterday, while I was cutting wood in the mountains, a strong wind suddenly blew up. I looked up and saw a beautiful bird I had never seen before flying over my head, circling a few times, and then flying away. I followed the bird, and it led me to a magical valley where flowers bloomed everywhere, filling the air with the sweetest fragrance. It was the most beautiful scenery!"

The old man continued, still lost in the memory: "Near the valley there was a small river, and the water in it was clearer than any river water I had ever seen. I was thirsty, so I scooped some up and drank it. To my surprise, as soon as I drank it, I felt a sudden wave of strength run through my whole body. When I had had enough, I felt as sleepy as if I had been drinking wine, and I fell asleep beside the spring. When I woke up, it was already late at night. Feeling scared all alone, I hurried back, running all the way."

"Ah, so the spring water made you young again! I want to find that spring too, and become a little younger myself!"

"Alright, go find it then!" the old man cheerfully showed her the way.

But the next day, the old woman did not come home. Days passed, and she still hadn't returned. The old man thought, "My goodness, my wife has been sleeping a very long time." So he waited a few more days, but she still didn't come back. He had no choice but to go looking for her.

He came to a clearing in the forest and looked around — it was empty, with no one in sight. His heart grew more and more uneasy. "Could some wild animal have eaten her?" he feared.

He went to the side of the spring once more, but still couldn't find any sign of his wife. Just as he was about to give up and head back, he suddenly heard a baby crying.

"Who would bring a baby to such a deserted place?" he wondered, then followed the sound.

In a thick patch of grass, he spotted something white. Walking closer, he realized it was his wife's dress. Wrapped inside was a baby, crying loudly.

"Oh dear! My wife has turned into a little baby!" the old man cried, not knowing what to do.

The baby nodded at him and cried even louder.

"Poor thing, poor thing, that's you, my beloved wife!" he said. "You were so greedy — you drank too much of the youthful spring water, and now you've become a baby who needs to drink milk. What am I going to do now?"

Having no other choice, the old man gently held his baby wife in his hands and carried her home.

From that day on, the old man held his baby wife in his arms every day, going from house to house, asking people to help feed her.
fields.tips: 如果真有青春泉，准爸爸是不是也想回到无忧无虑的孩童时代呢？腹中的胎宝宝就是准爸爸准妈妈生命的延续。从他出生的那一刻开始，爸爸妈妈就要像故事中的老头子一样，捧着他、喂养他、呵护他，肩负起培育他成长的职责了。
fields.tips_en: If the Fountain of Youth were real, do you think an expectant dad would also long to return carefree to his childhood? The little one growing in the womb is a continuation of both parents' lives. From the moment he's born, mom and dad will be just like that old man in the story—holding him, feeding him, caring for him, and shouldering the beautiful responsibility of nurturing him into the wonderful person he's meant to become.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小猫和小鲫鱼
fields.title_en: The Kitten and the Little Fish
fields.subtitle: 温馨、动人的动物对话
fields.subtitle_en: A Warm and Touching Animal Conversation
fields.content:
有一只白色的小猫向水田信步走去，它走上了窄窄的田埂。水田中有一条小鲫鱼看到了白色的小猫，它问道：“你是谁呀？”
“我是小猫。”小猫回答说。它那圆圆的眼睛滴溜溜地看着小鲫鱼，这还是第一次有小鲫鱼跟它说话呢，它不禁想多和小鲫鱼聊一会儿。
这时水田里鲫鱼妈妈说话了：“孩子啊，你可不要跟小猫讲话呀，一声不响地快躲开吧，千万别吵嚷！”
“你不知道，猫抓走了我们许多伙伴。万一被那家伙抓住，我们可就完了。”妈妈着急地跟小鲫鱼说。
小鲫鱼觉得小猫还挺友善的，于是它在水中悄悄地问小猫：“听说你会抓我，对吗？”
“不，不，我不抓。可爱的小鲫鱼，我不抓你。”小猫可没想要抓小鲫鱼，它忙这样说着，然后就走开了。
小猫在附近随意散了一会儿步就回家了。走廊上，猫爸爸在睡觉。
“水田里有一条小鲫鱼，爸爸。”
“在水田的什么地方？”猫爸爸关切地问。
“在那边一个浅浅的水坑里。”
“那么，你抓住它了吗？”
“没有抓。”
“为什么不抓呢？只要伸出前爪就抓住了嘛！抓住了，吃起来可香呢。”
小猫摇摇头：“还是不吃吧！那么一个小小的、怪可爱的孩子。”
小猫的脖子上挂着一个小铃铛，它就叫小铃铛。“是呀，是呀！小猫真是个善良的孩子。”小铃铛这样说着，丁零，丁零，发出温柔、悦耳的声音。猫爸爸明白小猫的意思了，它亲切地摸了摸孩子的小脑袋。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Cat and the Tiny Carp

A little white cat walked at a leisurely pace toward the rice paddy, stepping onto the narrow earthen ridge. Inside the water, a tiny carp saw the white cat and asked, "Who are you?"

"I'm a little cat," replied the cat. Its round eyes blinked curiously at the carp. This was the first time a carp had ever spoken to it, and it found itself wanting to chat a little longer.

Just then, the carp's mother spoke up from the paddy: "My dear child, you must not talk to the cat. Stay quiet and swim away quickly. Please do not make a sound!"

"You don't know," the mother said anxiously, "cats have caught many of our friends. If that creature catches us, we are done for."

The little carp thought the cat seemed rather friendly, so it whispered from the water, "I heard you catch fish. Is that true?"

"No, no, I don't catch. Dear little carp, I won't catch you." The cat never had any intention of catching the carp. It hurried to say this, and then wandered off.

The cat took a little stroll nearby before heading home. On the veranda, the father cat was asleep.

"There's a little carp in the rice paddy, Daddy," said the cat.

"Oh? Where in the paddy?" asked Father Cat gently.

"In a shallow puddle over there."

"And did you catch it?"

"No, I didn't."

"Why not? All you'd have to do is reach out with your paw! It would be so delicious to eat."

The little cat shook its head. "I'd rather not. It's such a tiny, darling little thing."

A small bell hung around the cat's neck, and that was why it was called Little Bell. "That's right, that's right! You're such a kind-hearted kitten," chimed Little Bell, tinkling softly with a warm, pleasing sound. Father Cat understood his child's meaning, and he lovingly stroked the top of the little one's head.
fields.tips: 这是一只懵懂的可爱小猫和一条懵懂的可爱小鲫鱼之间的故事。充满童真与童趣的对话，读着让人的心境也不由变得温柔起来。准爸爸可以和准妈妈分别饰演其中一个角色，把故事生动地讲给胎宝宝听，增强胎教效果。
fields.tips_en: This is a sweet story between an innocent little kitten and an innocent little fish. Their childlike and playful conversation gently warms the heart. The expectant father can take turns playing each role, bringing the story to life for the baby-to-be and enhancing the bonding experience.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 乌龟和它的儿子
fields.subtitle: 智慧应该分享
fields.subtitle_en: Wisdom Grows When Shared
fields.content:
从前，有一只乌龟像集邮一样收集“智慧”，然后把“智慧”放在一个大沙罐里。终于它的沙罐装满了。
乌龟相信，世界上所有的智慧都属于它了，可是它害怕自己的沙罐被别人偷了去。突然，它有了主意：“对，把沙罐藏在高高的树枝中，就没有人能找到了。”
于是，乌龟用两臂提着沙罐爬树，爬不上，左臂提，还是爬不上，右臂提，仍然爬不上。这时，它的儿子小乌龟突然喊道：“爸爸，你为什么不把罐子背在背上再爬树呢？”
乌龟笑着对儿子说：“嗨！小家伙，你懂的比你老子还多吗？”但是，它试着把沙罐背在背上。真奇怪，它很轻易就爬上去了。
乌龟坐在树枝上，抱着大沙罐。它感觉很悲伤：“我以为我拥有了所有的智慧，可这个小孩却具有我所没有的智慧。”想了一阵，它便从树上把小罐推下去。沙罐摔破了，“智慧”便又全部播撒到大地上了。
（作者：莱雷托·图德/英国）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Turtle and Its Son

Once upon a time, there was a turtle who collected "wisdom" just like someone collects stamps, keeping it all in a big jar made of sand-colored clay. At last, the jar was completely full.

The turtle believed that all the wisdom in the world belonged to it now, but it was afraid someone might steal the jar. Then suddenly it had an idea: "Yes! If I hide the jar high up in the branches of a tall tree, no one will ever find it."

So the turtle tried climbing the tree with the jar held up in its arms, but it couldn't climb. Then it tried with just its left arm, but still couldn't climb. Then it tried with its right arm, but again, no luck. Just then, its baby son, a little turtle, called out, "Papa, why don't you just carry the jar on your back and then climb up?"

The turtle smiled and said to his son, "Oh! Little one, do you think you know more than your old father?" But he tried carrying the jar on his back. Truly wonderful — he climbed up very easily.

The turtle sat on the tree branch, holding the big jar close. He felt very sad. "I thought I had all the wisdom in the whole wide world," he said to himself, "but this little child has some wisdom I do not have." He thought about it for a little while, and then he pushed the jar off the branch. The jar broke, and the "wisdom" was scattered all over the ground once again.
fields.tips: 乌龟虽然认识到智慧比黄金更宝贵，可是它却不知道，智慧并不是收一点儿就多一点儿，而是越散播越多的，分享才是获得好办法的途径。
fields.tips_en: Though the turtle knows wisdom is more precious than gold, it has yet to learn that wisdom is not hoarded but multiplied when shared. Sharing is truly the best way to grow it.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 四个好朋友
fields.subtitle: 互帮互助的感人友情
fields.subtitle_en: The Heartwarming Bond of Mutual Help
fields.content:
乌龟、乌鸦、老鼠和鹿是好朋友。一天，到了约定的散步时间，鹿却迟迟没有来。乌龟、乌鸦和老鼠不禁为它担心起来，怕它遭到什么不幸。
于是，乌龟和老鼠就对乌鸦说：“亲爱的，我们俩走得太慢了，没法儿去寻找我们亲爱的朋友。还是你去吧！你无论如何也得辛苦一趟，看看鹿究竟发生了什么事，快去快回！”
乌鸦听了，就飞了出去。没飞多远，它就在一个小水池子旁边看到了鹿。原来鹿落到一个拴在大树上的套索里去了。这时它正在绝望地挣扎着，试图脱开身来。
乌鸦立刻向鹿叫道：“亲爱的！别害怕！只要你的朋友在，你就会摆脱困境。我这就把老鼠带来，让它把捆住你的套索咬断！”说完乌鸦就飞了回去。
不久，乌鸦用嘴叼着老鼠飞来了。乌龟呢，由于太牵挂朋友的安危了，竟然也拼命地赶来了。老鼠大吃一惊：“亲爱的乌龟呀，你干的这事可不妙呀！因为你不能够逃开猎人的毒手。你和我们并不一样呀！当我咬断套索后，乌鸦可以飞上树，我可以溜到一个洞里。可要是你被发现了，怎么办呢？”乌龟说：“别管那么多了！咱们还是赶快救鹿吧！”
这时，猎人拿着弓来了。老鼠赶在猎人到达之前，把那根套索咬断了。然后它就溜到洞里去了；乌鸦呢，飞上了天空；乌龟也想赶快跑掉，但它跑不快，只能慢慢地爬。
当猎人看见拴鹿的绳索已被咬断时，心中十分纳闷儿。他以为有神在帮助鹿，变得十分沮丧。这时，他看见了乌龟，便立刻迁怒于它。他用小刀割了一些草，拧成一条结实的绳子。然后他把乌龟的脚拉出来捆好，把绳子挂在弓的尖上，走了。
老鼠见乌龟被猎人带走了，又焦急又难过。它伤心地说：“真倒霉呀！失去了朋友，我也活不下去了！”这时，乌鸦和鹿也大声叫喊着跑了出来。它们也看到了刚才发生的事，于是一起商量对策。
最后老鼠想出了一个好主意。它说：“只要我们还能看见乌龟，就有可能救出它来。鹿呀，你快跑过去，跑到那个猎人的眼前，在靠近水的地方倒下去装死；乌鸦呀，你把你的两只脚放在鹿的天灵盖上，装出要挖它的眼睛的样子。那个倒霉的猎人一定会想：‘这只鹿死了。’他是个贪得无厌的人。他会把乌龟扔到地上朝鹿那里跑。我呢，等那家伙一跑走，只用一会儿工夫，就能把捆乌龟的草绳咬断，把它放开。让它爬到附近的水里去。然后我就躲到草丛里去。当猎人走近鹿的时候，鹿就立刻逃走。”
于是，它们就这样做了。猎人看到鹿果然心花怒放，他把乌龟往地上一丢，就挥舞着棍子跑了过去。当他就要靠近时，鹿以最快的速度跳起身，跑到树丛里面去了；乌鸦也飞上了树；乌龟得救后立刻钻到水里去了；而老鼠也窜到草丛里了。
猎人一无所获地回家了。四个善良的朋友又跑到了一起，它们相亲相爱、愉快地生活着。
（选自《五卷书》古印度故事集）
fields.content_en:
# Four Good Friends

Turtle, Crow, Mouse, and Deer were good friends. One day, when it was time for their walk, Deer did not arrive. Turtle, Crow, and Mouse grew worried about him, fearing some harm might have come to him.

So Turtle and Mouse said to Crow, "Dear friend, we are both too slow to go looking for our dear friend. You must go! Please make the journey and see what has happened to Deer. Come back quickly!"

Crow flew out right away. Before long, he spotted Deer beside a small pond. Deer had fallen into a noose tied around a big tree, and was desperately struggling to free himself.

Crow called out to Deer at once, "Don't be afraid, dear friend! As long as your friends are here, you will find a way out. I will bring Mouse, and he will bite through the rope binding you!" Then Crow flew back.

Soon, Crow returned with Mouse in his beak. Turtle, too worried about his friend's safety, had also hurried to come along. Mouse was startled. "Dear Turtle, this is not a good plan," he said. "You cannot escape a hunter's grasp like we can. When I bite through the rope, Crow can fly up into the tree, and I can slip into a hole. But if you are discovered, what will happen?" Turtle replied, "Never mind that! Let us save Deer quickly!"

Just then, the hunter arrived with his bow. Before the hunter could reach them, Mouse gnawed through the rope. He slipped into his hole, Crow took to the sky, and Turtle tried to scramble away, but he was too slow and could only crawl.

When the hunter saw that the rope holding Deer had been bitten through, he was very puzzled. He thought a god must be helping Deer, and he grew deeply discouraged. Then he spotted Turtle and immediately turned his anger on him. He cut some grass and twisted it into a strong rope. He pulled Turtle's legs together and tied them, hung the rope on the tip of his bow, and walked away.

Mouse saw Turtle being carried off by the hunter and felt both anxious and sorrowful. "How unlucky we are," he said sadly. "Without our friend, I cannot bear to live!" At that moment, Crow and Deer came rushing out, crying loudly. They had seen everything that happened, so they gathered together to think of a plan.

Finally, Mouse came up with a clever idea. He said, "As long as we can still see Turtle, there is hope of saving him. Deer, run ahead and fall down near the water as if you were dead. Crow, place your feet on Deer's head and pretend to peck at his eyes. That unfortunate hunter will certainly think, 'This deer is dead.' And he is a greedy man. He will drop Turtle on the ground and run toward Deer. When he runs off, I will quickly bite through the grass rope binding Turtle and set him free. Then Turtle can crawl into the nearby water, and I will hide in the grass. When the hunter draws near to Deer, Deer will jump up at once and flee into the bushes."

And so they did exactly as Mouse planned. The hunter was overjoyed to see the deer and, throwing Turtle to the ground, ran toward it with his stick waving. Just as he was about to reach it, Deer sprang up at top speed and dashed into the thickets; Crow flew up into a tree; Turtle, now rescued, slipped into the water; and Mouse darted into the grass.

The hunter returned home empty-handed. The four kind friends were reunited once more, and they lived together happily, caring for one another.

(Adapted from the Panchatantra, an ancient Indian story collection)
fields.tips: 每个人生活在这个世界上都会有亲密的朋友，亲密的朋友比任何财富都更重要。准爸爸给胎宝宝讲故事的时候，也可以给他讲讲自己的朋友们，以及朋友们之间发生的有趣的、感人的故事。相信胎宝宝一定非常愿意听。
fields.tips_en: Everyone needs close friends in this world, and true friendship is more valuable than any wealth. While telling stories to the baby-to-be, the expectant father can also share tales of his own dear friends and the wonderful moments they've shared together. The little one will surely love listening.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 神杧果
fields.subtitle: 生命如此奇妙
fields.subtitle_en: How Miraculous Life Is
fields.content:
很久很久以前，有一个神奇的杧果，它长在一棵高大的杧果树上。它可不像我们现在的杧果，噢，真的一点儿也不像。这家伙能思考，还会说话呢。
神杧果每天都坐在杧果树顶上。从高高的树顶上，神杧果能看到周围的许多事物。它能看见江边的村庄、远处的群山，还有村庄那边的大海。
就这样过了很久，渐渐地，神杧果感到有些无聊了。神杧果想：“我真希望能从树上下来，像别人那样到处走走，好好看看周围的村庄，去爬爬那里的山，要是还能在大海边的沙滩上走走，那该多好啊。”但是，可怜的神杧果离不开杧果树。
有一天，刮起了好大好大的风，把杧果树吹得晃来晃去。风实在太大啦，神杧果觉得自己都拉不住杧果树了。终于，神杧果从树上掉了下来。
神杧果没有受伤，因为它落在了软软的草地上。在那儿躺了一会儿，神杧果突然明白了：“啊，我终于离开了树，我可以去周游世界了。”于是，神杧果欢快地在地上滚了起来。它从小山上滚下来，朝村庄滚去。
在村外，神杧果遇到了一头猪。猪说：“喂！站住！我要吃你！”神杧果听了就笑起来，它还唱起了一首短歌：
“我是一个神杧果，谁也不能抓住我。
现在我要去赶路，看看世界多快活。”
神杧果越滚越快，猪在后面拼命追赶。
在村边，一个小男孩看见了神杧果。小男孩喊道：“喂！站住！我要吃你！”神杧果又笑着唱起了那首短歌：
“我是一个神杧果，谁也不能抓住我。
现在我要去赶路，看看世界多快活。”
神杧果越滚越快，猪和小男孩在后面拼命追赶。
他们穿过村庄，许多人都在那儿干活。两个女人看见了神杧果。她们说：“喂！站住！我们要吃你！”神杧果还是笑着唱起了那首短歌：
“我是一个神杧果，谁也不能抓住我。
现在我要去赶路，看看世界多快活。”
神杧果越滚越快，猪、小男孩和两个女人一起拼命追赶。
突然，一个饥饿的猎人看见了神杧果，喊道：“喂！站住！我要吃你！”神杧果又笑着唱起了那首短歌：
“我是一个神杧果，谁也不能抓住我。
现在我要去赶路，看看世界多快活。”
神杧果越滚越快，猪、小男孩、两个女人，还有饥饿的猎人一起在后面追赶。
他们跑啊，跑啊，直到他们找不到神杧果了。因为神杧果开始感到有些累了，它想找个地方好好休息一下，于是滚到了一丛深草里藏了起来。狗、小男孩、两个女人和饥饿的猎人没有找到它，就都回家去了。
这时候，神杧果觉得非常非常累，一会儿就睡着了。它一下子睡了好多好多天。它醒来的时候，太阳正晒着它，暖洋洋的，舒服极了。神杧果想：“这地方不错，在这待一会儿吧。”
许多天许多天过去了。有一天，一些很小、绿绿的嫩芽从神杧果身上长了出来。你知道是怎么回事吗？对了，神杧果长成树了。
（作者：雷·奥发里尔/巴布亚新几内亚）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Magic Mango

Long, long ago, there was a special mango growing on a tall mango tree. It was nothing like the mangoes we know today—not at all. This mango could think, and it could talk too.

Every day, the special mango sat perched at the top of the tree. From high up there, it could see many things around it. It could see the villages by the river, the faraway mountains, and the sea beyond the villages.

After a long, long time, the special mango began to feel a little bored. It thought, "I really wish I could come down from the tree and walk around like everyone else, see the villages, climb the mountains, and maybe even walk on the sandy beach by the sea." But poor special mango simply could not leave the tree.

One day, a very big wind blew, shaking the mango tree back and forth. The wind was so strong that the special mango felt it could barely hold on. At last, it let go and fell from the tree.

It wasn't hurt, because it landed on soft, green grass. After lying there for a little while, the special mango suddenly realized, "Ah! I'm finally off the tree! I can go see the whole wide world!" So it began to roll happily along the ground. It rolled down a little hill and headed toward the village.

Near the village, it met a pig. The pig said, "Hey! Stop right there! I'm going to eat you!" The special mango just laughed and sang a little song:

"I'm a magic mango, no one can catch me.
Now I'm on my way, happy as can be."

The special mango rolled faster and faster, and the pig chased after it as fast as it could.

At the edge of the village, a little boy spotted the mango and called out, "Hey! Stop! I'm going to eat you!" The special mango laughed again and sang the same little song:

"I'm a magic mango, no one can catch me.
Now I'm on my way, happy as can be."

It rolled faster and faster, and both the pig and the little boy chased after it.

They passed through the village, where many people were busy working. Two women saw the special mango and said, "Hey! Stop! We're going to eat you!" Still smiling, the special mango sang its little song:

"I'm a magic mango, no one can catch me.
Now I'm on my way, happy as can be."

It rolled faster and faster, and the pig, the little boy, and the two women all chased after it together.

Suddenly, a hungry hunter spotted the special mango and shouted, "Hey! Stop! I'm going to eat you!" The special mango laughed and sang once more:

"I'm a magic mango, no one can catch me.
Now I'm on my way, happy as can be."

It rolled faster and faster, with the pig, the little boy, the two women, and the hungry hunter all chasing behind.

They ran and ran until they could no longer find the special mango. It was starting to feel tired and wanted to find a nice place to rest, so it rolled into a patch of tall, thick grass and hid. The dog, the little boy, the two women, and the hungry hunter couldn't find it, so they all went home.

The special mango felt very, very sleepy and fell asleep almost right away. It slept for many, many days. When it finally woke up, the sun was shining warmly on it, and it felt so comfortable. The special mango thought, "This is a lovely place. I'll stay here a while."

Many days went by. Then one day, some tiny green sprouts began to grow out of the special mango. Do you know what happened? That's right—the special mango had grown into a tree!

(Author: Ray O'Farrell / Papua New Guinea)
fields.tips: 生命是非常神奇的存在，每一个生命的诞生与成长都是大自然最杰出的作品，它是幸运的，也是唯一的。准爸爸如果用心感受妻子怀孕的辛苦，一定会被妻子感动，为她感到自豪的。
fields.tips_en: Life is a truly wondrous gift. Every new life born and growing is nature's greatest masterpiece—both precious and one of a kind. When the expectant father truly feels the journey of his wife's pregnancy, he will be deeply moved and filled with pride for her.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 3年与3天
fields.subtitle: 用心做事更有成效
fields.subtitle_en: Doing Things with Heart Yields Better Results
fields.content:
米芾是我国北宋时期的大书法家、画家。不过，他小时候在私塾学写字时，学了3年，也没学好。
一天，听说一位写得一手好字的秀才路过这里，米芾就跑去求教。秀才翻看了他写的一沓纸，若有所悟。他对米芾说：“想跟我学写字有个条件，得买我的纸。不过，贵点儿，五两纹银一张。”
米芾一听吓了一跳，心想，哪有这么贵的纸？秀才见他犹豫就说：“嫌贵就算了，我还急着赶路呢！”米芾求学心切，一咬牙借来5两银子交给秀才。秀才递给他一张纸说：“回去好好写吧，3天后拿给我看。”
回到家，米芾捧着那张纸左看右看，不敢轻易使用。于是他翻开字帖，用没蘸墨汁的笔在书案上画来画去，把字一个一个印在心里。他这样横琢磨竖琢磨，竟入了迷。
3天后，秀才来了。他见米芾坐在那里，手握着笔，望着字帖出神，纸上却滴墨未沾，便故作惊讶地问：“怎么还没写？”
米芾一惊，如梦方醒，才想起3天期限已到。他喃喃地说道：“我，我怕弄废了纸。”秀才哈哈大笑，用扇子指着纸说：“好了，琢磨了3天，写个字给我看看吧！”
米芾提笔写了一个“永”字。秀才拿过来一看，这个字写得遒劲有力，大有长进。他便故意问道：“为什么3年学不成，3天却能突飞猛进呢？”
米芾想了想说：“因为纸贵，我不敢像以前那样信笔写来，而是先用心把字琢磨透了……”
“对！”秀才打断他的话说：“学字不只是动笔，还要动心；不但要观其形，更要悟其神。心领神会，才能写好。现在你已经懂得写字的窍门了，我该走啦。”说着，挥笔在“永”字后面添了7个字：“（永）志不忘，纹银五两。”又从怀里掏出那5两纹银还给米芾，头也不回地上路了。
fields.content_en:
Title: Three Years and Three Days

Mi Fu was a great calligrapher and painter during China's Northern Song Dynasty. But when he was little and learning to write at his schoolhouse, he studied for three whole years and still couldn't write well.

One day, he heard that a learned scholar known for his beautiful writing was passing through town. Mi Fu ran to ask for help. The scholar looked through a stack of Mi Fu's papers and seemed to understand something. He told Mi Fu, "I will teach you, but there is one condition—you must buy my paper. It costs five taels of silver for just one sheet."

Mi Fu was shocked. Such expensive paper? Seeing him hesitate, the scholar said, "If it's too dear, that's alright. I'm in a hurry to travel." Desperate to learn, Mi Fu borrowed the five taels and handed them over. The scholar gave him a single sheet and said, "Go home and practice. Bring it to me in three days."

When Mi Fu got home, he held the paper in his hands and looked at it carefully, afraid to use it so soon. So he opened his copybook and practiced moving his brush—without ink—over his desk, pressing each character into his heart and mind. He thought and pondered, over and over, until he became completely absorbed.

Three days later, the scholar arrived. He saw Mi Fu sitting there, brush in hand, gazing longingly at his copybook—the paper on the table still completely untouched by ink. Pretending to be surprised, he asked, "Why haven't you written yet?"

Mi Fu started awake, as if emerging from a dream. Only then did he remember that the three days had passed. He murmured, "I… I was afraid of ruining the paper." The scholar laughed aloud and pointed at the paper with his fan. "Very well! You've thought about it for three days—now write something for me!"

Mi Fu picked up his brush and wrote the character "yong"—forever. The scholar examined it and saw that the strokes were strong and confident. There had been wonderful improvement. He asked on purpose, "Why couldn't you learn in three years, yet in three days you improved so much?"

Mi Fu thought for a moment and said, "Because the paper was so expensive, I didn't dare write carelessly as I used to. Instead, I first used my heart to understand each character deeply…"

"Exactly!" the scholar interrupted him. "Learning calligraphy is not just about moving your hand—it's about moving your heart. You must not only see the shape of the characters but also understand their spirit. Only when your heart grasps it can you write beautifully. Now you have discovered the secret of writing, and I must go." Saying this, he picked up his brush and added seven small characters after the "yong": "Remember this forever—it cost five taels of silver." Then he took the five taels out of his pocket and returned them to Mi Fu, turned around, and walked away without looking back.
fields.tips: 对于那些来之不易的东西，我们往往会更加上心。其实这并不是问题的本质，而是我们没有要求自己去用心。讲胎教故事也是如此，敷衍的态度自然不会获得好的效果。
fields.tips_en: We tend to care more for things that are hard-won. Yet the real key is not what we have, but whether we choose to give our whole heart to it. The same is true of prenatal storytelling—reading with genuine care and attention will always bring richer rewards.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 钓蝴蝶
fields.subtitle: 花若盛开，蝴蝶自来
fields.subtitle_en: When Flowers Bloom, Butterflies Come Naturally
fields.content:
小兔子去找小熊玩儿，只见小熊在田野里摘花籽，便问：“你在干什么呢？”“我要钓蝴蝶，我正在做准备呢！”小熊一边摘一边说。“什么，钓蝴蝶？”小兔子以为小熊开玩笑呢，就没在意。
不久，小兔子见小熊在家门前挖了很多坑，便问：“你在忙什么呢？”“我要钓蝴蝶！明年春天，我要钓很多很多蝴蝶。”小熊说。“蝴蝶怎么能钓到，吹牛吧！”小兔子一摇头走了。
春天来了，这天小熊来找小兔子：“快去我家吧，我钓了好多好多蝴蝶！”小兔子忙赶去看。啊，小熊家像个大花园，真的有很多蝴蝶。
“啊，原来你是这样钓蝴蝶的呀？知道蝴蝶喜欢花，就用花来钓蝴蝶。啧啧！太聪明了！”小兔子高兴地学着蝴蝶的样子，挥动着两条前腿，在花丛中跑来跑去。
后来，小兔子也收集了很多花籽，它自己也想钓蝴蝶了。想象着家门前也有成群的蝴蝶飞舞，那该多美啊！小兔子高兴地笑了。
fields.content_en:
Title: Catching Butterflies

Little Rabbit came looking for Little Bear to play, and found him picking flower seeds in the field. "What are you doing?" asked Little Rabbit. "I'm catching butterflies! I'm getting ready!" said Little Bear, still picking away. "What, catching butterflies?" Little Rabbit thought Little Bear was joking and paid it no mind.

Soon, Little Rabbit noticed Little Bear had dug many small holes near his house and asked, "What are you busy with?" "I'm catching butterflies! Next spring, I'm going to catch lots and lots of butterflies," said Little Bear. "How can you catch butterflies? You're just boasting!" Little Rabbit shook his head and walked away.

Spring came. One day, Little Bear came to find Little Rabbit: "Come to my house quickly! I caught so many butterflies!" Little Rabbit hurried over to see. Oh, Little Bear's house looked like a big garden, and there really were butterflies everywhere.

"Oh, so this is how you catch butterflies! You know butterflies love flowers, so you use flowers to catch them. Wow! So clever!" Little Rabbit happily flapped his front paws like a butterfly and ran around in the flowers.

After that, Little Rabbit also collected many flower seeds. He wanted to catch butterflies all by himself too. Imagining clouds of butterflies fluttering in front of his house… how beautiful that would be! Little Rabbit smiled happily.
fields.tips: 花朵盛开不仅会吸引蝴蝶飞来，还能让人心情格外好。如果家里养了花，准爸爸可别忘了给它们浇水施肥啊，将美丽绽放给妻子看。
