白蛇见许仙逛庙会一直没回来，听说被法海关了起来，就带着小青来到金山寺找许仙。法海身披袈裟，一手举着青龙杖，一手捧着金钵出来，要收服白蛇。白蛇、青蛇和法海大战起来。三人大战僵持不下，白蛇就施法引来滔滔江水要淹金山寺。但法海用袈裟把金山寺罩了起来。水高一寸，寺高一寸，水高一尺，寺高一尺，水始终淹不到寺庙。白蛇无奈只好退去，带着小青回到了杭州。
许仙看到了妻子施法，知道法海所言不虚，妻子真的是妖精。但妻子对自己情深义重，即使是妖精，自己也要跟她在一起，所以找了个机会逃了出来，一直追到了杭州。许仙和白蛇两个人终于在断桥又相会了。他们继续过日子，更加恩爱了。
但是，法海紧追不舍，又追到了杭州。无论许仙怎么恳求，他都不肯放过白蛇。趁白蛇不小心，法海用金钵把她罩住，压到了雷峰塔下。白素贞和许仙最终还是被拆散了，但他们坚贞的爱情一直被传诵至今。
不过，后来法海也没有好下场。在白蛇被压到雷峰塔后，小青回到峨眉山刻苦修炼，最后打败了法海。法海请求如来佛祖救他，但因为法海的金钵是从如来佛祖那里偷的，所以如来佛祖不肯救他。法海不得不化作一个小和尚躲在了螃蟹的壳里，逃过小青的追杀。
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Legend of the White Snake**

Long ago, during the Song Dynasty, in a cave on Mount Emei, two snakes practiced their cultivation and became human. One was a white snake and the other was a green snake. The white snake was named Bai Suzhen, and the green snake was named Xiao Qing. She was Bai Suzhen's loyal servant and dear companion.

When Bai Suzhen was young, a kind child had once saved her life. She never forgot that kindness and wanted to repay him. Now that she had become human, her very first wish was to find that same child. Of course, the child had lived through many lifetimes and no longer looked like he used to.

Bai Suzhen and Xiao Qing traveled through the human world for a very long time, and at last they found him. This man's name was Xu Xian, and he was living in Hangzhou. Bai Suzhen found gentle ways to meet him. One day, when she saw Xu Xian about to cross a river, Xiao Qing used her magic to make a light rain fall. They approached him and asked if they could share his boat. Xu Xian had a kind heart and happily agreed. When they stepped off the boat, he even lent them his umbrella to stay dry. Later, Bai Suzhen returned the umbrella and thanked him. Little by little, they grew close. In the end, with Xiao Qing as their matchmaker, they were married and became husband and wife.

After their wedding, Xu Xian took his wife back to their hometown of Zhenjiang, where they opened a small medicine shop. Their days were peaceful and happy. But soon, a monk named Fahai came to Jinshan Temple. When he visited the shop, he told Xu Xian that a strange aura surrounded him — he must have been bewitched by a demon. Xu Xian thought hard. He couldn't think of any stranger he had met besides his wife and Xiao Qing. But his wife was so caring and gentle, nothing like someone who would harm him. So he smiled and kindly sent Fahai on his way.

But Fahai kept coming back, urging Xu Xian to chase away the demon. Each time, Xu Xian simply smiled and waved it aside. Then one day, Fahai arrived again and told Xu Xian about the temple festival on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. He invited Xu Xian to come to Jinshan Temple to light incense and pray to the Buddha, so that he might be protected from trouble.

Xu Xian thought, "Even if there is no benefit, there can be no harm." So on that day, he went to Jinshan Temple. But Fahai had another plan. He tried very hard to persuade Xu Xian to become a monk. Xu Xian, however, said he had a wife and that even if Bai Suzhen truly were a white snake, he would never leave her. He refused Fahai's request. In anger, Fahai locked Xu Xian inside the temple and would not let him go home.

When the white snake waited and waited for Xu Xian to return from the festival and heard that Fahai had imprisoned him, she rushed to Jinshan Temple with Xiao Qing to find him. Fahai came out wearing his robe, holding a dragon staff in one hand and a golden bowl in the other, ready to capture the white snake. A great battle erupted between the two snakes and Fahai. They fought until neither could gain the upper hand. Then Bai Suzhen used her magic to call upon the mighty river, hoping to flood Jinshan Temple. But Fahai spread his robe over the temple, shielding it from the rising waters. The water rose an inch and the temple rose an inch. The water rose a foot and the temple rose a foot. Still, the waters could not reach the temple. With no other choice, Bai Suzhen retreated and returned to Hangzhou with Xiao Qing.

Xu Xian had seen his wife use her magic and understood that Fahai had spoken the truth — his wife truly was a spirit. But she had loved him so deeply and faithfully, and no matter what she was, he wanted to stay with her. So he found a chance to escape and ran all the way back to Hangzhou. At last, Xu Xian and the white snake met once again upon the Broken Bridge. Their love only grew deeper, and they lived together happily ever after.

But Fahai would not give up. He pursued them all the way to Hangzhou. No matter how much Xu Xian begged, Fahai would not spare the white snake. When Bai Suzhen was caught off her guard, Fahai threw his golden bowl over her and trapped her beneath the Leifeng Pagoda. Though Bai Suzhen and Xu Xian were forever separated, their faithful love has been cherished and remembered to this day.

In the end, Fahai himself did not escape unhappy fate. After the white snake was imprisoned under the pagoda, Xiao Qing returned to Mount Emei and trained hard. Eventually, she grew strong enough to defeat Fahai. He pleaded with the Buddha for help, but the Buddha would not save him, because Fahai's golden bowl had been stolen from the Buddha in the first place. So Fahai was forced to shrink himself into the shape of a little monk and hide inside a crab's shell, escaping Xiao Qing's pursuit.
fields.tips: 《白蛇传》的故事深得大众的喜爱。很多准妈妈对这个故事也非常熟悉，特别是“70后”“80后”的准妈妈，很可能是看着《新白娘子传奇》长大的，对这个故事的感情自然不同一般。故事中，许仙对白蛇有爱情，但更难得的是他知道白蛇不是同类而仍然爱她。这种包容，准妈妈要学习。可能准爸爸很多地方都不能如自己的意，但要多看好的方面，尽量包容他的缺点，这样自己才会开心。
fields.tips_en: The tale of the White Snake is cherished by many, and especially close to the hearts of mothers born in the 70s and 80s—many of you grew up watching 'The New Legend of Madame White Snake.' What makes this story so touching is that Xu Xian loves the white snake not despite knowing she is different, but with full acceptance of who she is. That kind of包容 (open-hearted acceptance) is a beautiful lesson for pregnancy. Your husband may not always meet your expectations, but focusing on his good qualities and embracing his imperfections will help you stay happy and at peace.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 田螺姑娘
fields.title_en: The Girl from the River Snail
fields.subtitle: 善有善报
fields.subtitle_en: Kindness Is Rewarded
fields.content:
传说在晋朝时，有个孤儿名叫谢端，他很小的时候父母就去世了，是靠着好心的邻居接济才长大的。长大后的谢端忠厚老实，勤劳节俭，善良且乐于助人，不管是村里人还是路过的人，很多都曾得到过他的帮助。人们都很喜欢他。
这一年，谢端有18岁了，该娶妻了，但邻居们帮他说了几次媒都没有成功。毕竟谢端太穷了，只是在山脚下有一间草棚房子，家中一贫如洗。没有人愿意让自己的姑娘跟着他受苦。
谢端也知道自己条件差，所以说媒不成，也无怨恨，只是更加勤劳、认真地耕作。他相信凭着自己的劳动一定能过上好日子。
谢端喜欢一切小动物，喜爱一切漂亮的植物。这天他在田里劳动的时候看到一个很大的田螺，非常喜欢，就把它捡起来带回家中，放到水缸里养了起来。此后，谢端每天出门前、回家后都跟大田螺打个招呼，还时不时给它换水，精心照顾。
一天，谢端忙了一天，收工准备回家，边走边想回家吃点什么呢。可当他到家里发现屋子里的桌子上已经摆好了饭菜，还有汤，正冒着热气呢。虽不丰盛，但比谢端自己做的好多了。谢端很奇怪，但也看得出这就是给自己准备的，就坐下来吃掉了。
此后，每天收工回家，谢端都能吃到现成的饭菜。时间久了，谢端开始感到不安，也很想弄明白到底是怎么回事。一天，还没到收工时间，谢端就收拾农具悄悄回家了。他悄悄靠近房子，把头伸到窗户边向里张望，真真切切看到一个年轻姑娘正在灶间做饭。谢端一步冲进了屋子，问姑娘是谁，为什么在这里给他做饭。姑娘吓了一跳，忙向水缸走去。谢端以为她要跑，急忙挡在她前面。姑娘看躲不过去了，就索性继续做饭去了。
饭做好，端上桌了，姑娘这才跟谢端说话。她告诉谢端，她本是天上神仙，叫水素女，住在田螺壳里。这次下凡是受天帝派遣，来帮助善良的人的。谁捡到田螺壳并好好对待，就会帮助谁。谢端捡到了田螺壳，还这么精心照顾，所以水素女就出来帮助他了。水素女还说，她会专门给谢端烧火煮饭，料理家务，并且帮他在10年内变得富裕起来，成家立业，娶妻生子。之后，她的任务就完成了，就可以回到天庭复命了。
谢端一听非常激动，一个劲儿地感谢水素女，感谢天帝。但是水素女一点儿都不高兴。她说天机已经被谢端识破，就不能再留在人间了，必须回到天庭去。
谢端后悔不迭，但也无济于事了。水素女从水缸里捞出田螺壳交给谢端说，这个田螺壳可以用来储存粮食，里面的米永远用不完。她还叮嘱谢端以后要干好农活，多打鱼，多砍柴，保证他的日子会一天天好起来的。说完，水素女就飘然走远了。
谢端遵照水素女的嘱咐，认真干农活，多打鱼，多砍柴，日子真的一天比一天红火起来。还不到10年，他就娶了妻子。再后来，谢端去读书了，再后来就中举当上了县令。
谢端为了感谢水素女，给她建了庙，就是今天的素女祠。
fields.content_en:
# The Girl in the Snail Shell

Long ago, during the Jin Dynasty, there was an orphan boy named Xie Duan. His parents passed away when he was very young, and kind neighbors took him in and helped raise him. As he grew up, Xie Duan became a honest, hardworking, and gentle young man. He was always happy to help others, and both the villagers and travelers who passed through received his kindness. Everyone loved him.

By this year, Xie Duan was eighteen years old and it was time for him to get married. But although the neighbors tried to set him up on several matchmake efforts, nothing worked out. You see, Xie Duan was very poor. He only had a small straw hut at the foot of the mountain, and his home was nearly empty. No one wanted their daughter to suffer alongside him.

Xie Duan knew his situation was difficult, so he did not resent the failed matches. Instead, he simply worked harder and tended his fields with even more care. He believed that with enough honest effort, he would surely live a good life someday.

Xie Duan loved all little animals and beautiful plants. One day, while working in the field, he spotted a very large snail and fell in love with it at first sight. He picked it up gently and brought it home, placing it in a water jar to keep. After that, every morning before leaving and every evening after returning, Xie Duan would greet his big snail. He changed its water often and cared for it with great tenderness.

One day, after a long day of work, Xie Duan was on his way home, wondering what he might eat for dinner. But when he arrived, he was surprised to find a table already set with delicious food and steaming soup. It was not a grand feast, but it was far better than anything he could have made himself. Xie Duan was puzzled, but he could tell it had been made just for him, so he sat down and enjoyed the meal.

From then on, every evening after work, Xie Duan came home to warm, ready-made food. After some time, he began to feel uneasy and very curious about what was really going on. So one day, before his work was finished, Xie Duan packed his tools and quietly walked home early. He crept close to the house and peeked through the window—and there, clearly, he saw a young woman cooking in the kitchen. Xie Duan rushed into the room and asked who she was and why she was cooking for him. The girl was startled and hurried toward the water jar. Xie Duan thought she might try to run, so he quickly stood in her way. Seeing that she could not hide anymore, the girl simply went back to finishing the meal.

Once the food was ready and placed on the table, the girl finally spoke to Xie Duan. She told him that she was originally a heavenly spirit named Shuissu, who lived inside the snail shell. She had come down to the mortal world by order of the Heavenly Emperor to help those who were kind. Whoever found and cared for her snail shell would receive her help. Xie Duan had found her shell and treated it with such love, so Shuissu had come out to assist him. She said she would cook and manage his household, and help him grow wealthy within ten years, so that he could marry, start a family, and have children. After that, her task would be complete, and she could return to heaven.

Xie Duan was overjoyed and thanked Shuissu again and again, praising both her and the Heavenly Emperor. But Shuissu did not look happy at all. She said that because Xie Duan had discovered her secret, she could no longer stay in the human world and must return to heaven right away.

Xie Duan deeply regretted it, but there was nothing he could do. Shuissu reached into the water jar, took out the snail shell, and gave it to Xie Duan. She told him that this shell could store grain, and the rice inside would never run out. She also urged him to keep working hard on his farm, catch more fish, and gather more firewood, assuring him that his life would improve day by day. With that, Shuissu floated gracefully away into the distance.

Xie Duan followed Shuissu's advice. He worked diligently in the fields, fished often, and collected plenty of firewood. And truly, his days became brighter and better one after another. Before ten years had passed, he had married a wife. Later, Xie Duan went on to study, and eventually he passed the examinations and became a county magistrate.

To honor and thank Shuissu, Xie Duan built a temple for her—the very same Su Nü Shrine that can still be seen today.
fields.tips: 《田螺姑娘》是一个美丽的神话故事，勤劳的穷苦青年谢端因为善良得到了田螺姑娘水素女的帮助。在田螺姑娘的帮扶下，谢端慢慢将日子过得红火起来。其实作为家庭一分子的准妈妈，也像是那个为家人默默付出辛劳的田螺姑娘一样，准爸爸一定要用善良和加倍的好来回报她哦。
fields.tips_en: The Legend of the River Snail is a beautiful fairy tale. A kind-hearted but hardworking young man named Xie Duan is blessed with the help of Shuini, the snail maiden. Under her gentle care, his life gradually blossoms into warmth and prosperity. In much the same way, a pregnant mother quietly gives so much to her family, much like the devoted snail maiden. So, dear dad-to-be, be sure to return her love and kindness with all the warmth you can offer.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 鸿雁传书
fields.subtitle: 坚贞之鸟的由来
fields.subtitle_en: The Origin of a Symbol of Devotion
fields.content:
汉武帝时汉朝大臣苏武出使匈奴。匈奴单于很欣赏苏武的才能，想迫使苏武投降匈奴。可是苏武严词拒绝：“要我投降，除非海枯石烂，日从西升。”说完他便举刀自刎，幸亏被救下来了。
可是单于并没有放苏武回去，而是把他扣了下来，还把他流放到荒无人烟的北海（今贝加尔湖）去牧羊。单于对他说什么时候公羊生了小羊，就放他归汉。
就这样，苏武在那里一个人放羊放了19年。这中间汉朝换了新皇帝，匈奴也换了新单于。汉匈议和，汉朝与匈奴和亲。出使匈奴的汉朝使者问起苏武的事，单于谎称苏武已经死去。使者信以为真，就没有再提。
当汉皇再次派使者到匈奴时，当年与苏武同去也被扣留的副使设法买通了禁卒，秘密会见了汉使。副使把苏武还活着、正在北海牧羊的消息告诉了他，并想出一计。副使让汉使对单于说：“汉朝天子在上林苑打猎时，射到一只大雁。大雁腿上系着一封苏武的亲笔信，说他在北海牧羊。你怎么说他死了呢？”
果然，单于听后大为震惊，他无法再抵赖，只能向汉使道歉，把苏武放了回去。
这就是苏武牧羊的故事。随着故事的流传，鸿雁传书也广为人知，大雁逐渐演化为传信的象征了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Wild Goose's Message

A long, long time ago, during the time of Emperor Wu of Han, a loyal minister named Su Wu traveled to the land of the Xiongnu as their guest. The Xiongnu ruler admired Su Wu very much and wanted him to stay. But Su Wu kindly but firmly refused. He said that he would only consider staying if the seas ran dry and the sun rose in the west. He tried to protect his honor with his own sword, but luckily he was saved.

The ruler did not let Su Wu go home. Instead, he sent him far away to a cold, empty place called Beihai — where today's great lake is — to tend sheep all alone. He told Su Wu that he could return home only when a male sheep gave birth to a lamb.

So Su Wu stayed there, tending sheep by himself, for nineteen long years. During that time, a new emperor came to rule in Han, and a new ruler came to lead the Xiongnu. The two lands made peace with each other, and messengers from Han visited the Xiongnu and asked about Su Wu. The Xiongnu ruler said that Su Wu had already passed away, and the messenger believed him.

When the Han emperor sent another messenger later, an old friend of Su Wu's — who had also been kept there many years before — made a clever plan. He asked a guard to help him meet the messenger in secret. His friend told him that Su Wu was still alive, out in the cold pasture by Beihai, watching over his flock. Then he thought of a wonderful idea.

He asked the messenger to tell the Xiongnu ruler: "Our emperor was hunting in a beautiful garden when he shot a great wild goose. Tied to the goose's leg was a letter written in Su Wu's own hand. It said that Su Wu is alive and still herding sheep at Beihai. How can you say he is gone?"

And it worked! The Xiongnu ruler was greatly surprised. He could no longer hide the truth. He apologized to the messenger and finally let Su Wu go home.

And that is the story of Su Wu and his faithful flock of sheep. Over the years, people began to call wild geese "messenger birds," for they carry news and love from one heart to another.
fields.tips: 准爸爸准妈妈在谈恋爱的时候有没有书信往来呢？还记得那时候的小悸动、小甜蜜吗？其实很多时候，把想说的话写成字比用嘴说出来更能打动人。所以在孕期准爸爸准妈妈不妨一起写写日记，把想对胎宝宝说的话都写下来。这种交流方式会让你们更真切地明白自己对胎宝宝的感情。
fields.tips_en: Did you and your darling exchange letters when you were dating? Do you remember those sweet butterflies and little moments of joy? Sometimes putting our feelings into words on paper touches the heart more deeply than spoken words ever could. During this pregnancy journey, why not try writing a diary together? Jot down all the loving words you wish to share with your little one. This beautiful practice will help you both feel even closer to the baby growing within you.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 刘秀气桑树
fields.title_en: Liu Xiu and the Mulberry Tree
fields.subtitle: 生气有损健康
fields.subtitle_en: Anger Takes a Toll on Your Health
fields.content:
桑树的躯干上都有一条裂缝，被人们称作“气破肚”。为什么气破了，被谁气破的，据说这与汉武帝刘秀有关。
刘秀是东汉的第一个皇帝。在西汉末年，王莽篡位后，他逃出了京城，好不容易躲过王莽的追兵，一路风餐露宿，来到了一片树林里。
进了树林，刘秀饿得走不动了，就一下倒在一株桑树下，稍作休息。此时正是桑葚成熟的季节，只要有风吹过，成熟的桑葚就不断往下掉。有几颗桑葚掉落在了刘秀的嘴里。刘秀下意识地咀嚼了几下，发现这种东西酸甜可口，非常好吃。正在饥渴难耐之时的刘秀立即来了精神，把掉落在树下的桑葚都捡了起来，饱餐一顿。吃过桑葚之后，刘秀对着桑树许下诺言，如果自己将来能中兴汉室，一定给桑树封赏。
几年后，刘秀果然打败王莽，复兴了汉朝。刘秀登基后，念念不忘曾经对他算得上有救命之恩的桑树和自己对桑树许下的诺言，便带领大臣来到了那片树林，打算给桑树封赏。
刘秀和大臣来树林的时候正是冬季。到了之后，发现满林的树叶都落光了，而当年桑树旁边还有一株椿树，也没有树叶了，跟桑树看上去差不多。刘秀分不清了，以为当年是椿树救了自己，就把椿树封为树中之王。此后，椿树都比别的树长得快、长得高。人们不管做什么，也都喜欢用一点儿椿树木，意思是用王木镇邪。
桑树看到没有任何功劳的椿树被封为王，而自己什么也没有，刘秀食言，气得树干开裂，成了“气破肚”。桑树旁边还有一株柳树，柳树把一切都看在眼里，很替桑树抱不平，结果把腰气扭了，成了后来的“扭扭腰”。
fields.content_en:
Title: Liu Xiu and the Mulberry Tree

All mulberry trees have a crack running down their trunks, which people call an "angry belly." But who got them so angry? They say it has something to do with Emperor Liu Xiu of the Han Dynasty.

Liu Xiu was the first emperor of the Eastern Han Dynasty. After a man named Wang Mang seized the throne at the end of the Western Han, Liu Xiu fled the capital. He barely escaped Wang Mang's soldiers and traveled for many days and nights, finally arriving at a forest.

Inside the forest, Liu Xiu was so hungry he could hardly walk. He collapsed beneath a mulberry tree to rest. It happened to be the season when mulberries ripen, and every time the wind blew, ripe mulberries fell from the branches. A few landed right in Liu Xiu's mouth. He chewed them by instinct and found them sweet and sour — delicious! Though still very hungry and thirsty, Liu Xiu immediately felt refreshed. He gathered all the mulberries beneath the tree and ate his fill. After the meal, he made a promise to the mulberry tree: if he ever restored the Han Dynasty, he would reward this tree.

A few years later, Liu Xiu did indeed defeat Wang Mang and restore the Han Dynasty. After becoming emperor, he never forgot the mulberry tree that had once saved his life and his promise to it. So he led his ministers to that very forest to honor the tree.

But by winter, all the leaves had fallen. Beside the mulberry tree stood an ailanthus tree, which also had no leaves and looked much like the mulberry. Liu Xiu couldn't tell them apart. He believed the ailanthus tree was the one that had saved him and crowned it the king of all trees. From then on, ailanthus trees grew faster and taller than any others. People came to favor using ailanthus wood for many things, believing it could ward off evil, since it was the wood of a king.

When the mulberry tree saw the ailanthus — a tree with no功劳 — receive such honor while it received nothing, and when Liu Xiu broke his promise, it grew so angry that its trunk cracked open, becoming the "angry belly" we see today. Beside the mulberry tree stood a willow tree, which watched everything unfold and felt so sorry for its neighbor that it grieved so deeply its trunk twisted, becoming what we now call a "crooked waist."
fields.tips: 树生气会“气破肚”，人生气对健康也不利。准妈妈更不应该生气。准妈妈生气对胎宝宝的稳定影响很大。而且经常生气的准妈妈，胎宝宝出生后性格敏感、多疑、暴躁，很难带。所以准妈妈遇事要冷静，多做深呼吸，千万不可动不动就生气。
fields.tips_en: They say a tree can split open when it’s filled with anger — and the same is true for us. When a mother-to-be is angry, it can affect the peace and well-being of her precious baby. Babies born to mothers who are often upset may grow up sensitive, anxious, or easily startled, making parenting all the more challenging. So dear mom, take a deep breath, stay calm, and let go of worries. Your gentle peace is the greatest gift to your little one.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 孔子学琴
fields.subtitle: 学而不厌，精益求精
fields.subtitle_en: Never Stop Learning, Always Strive for Excellence
fields.content:
孔子年轻的时候，曾向鲁国一位有名的乐师襄子学习弹琴。当时，孔子一首曲子已经弹了10天，还在不断练习，没有学习新的曲子。师襄子就对孔子说：“可以学习新内容了。”但孔子说：“我虽然已经熟悉了这首曲子，但还没有掌握弹奏技巧。”于是继续弹这首曲子。过了一段时间，师襄子又说：“你已经掌握了弹奏的技巧了，可以学习新曲子了。”孔子又说：“我还没有领会这首曲子的意境。”他仍然弹奏这首曲子。又过了一段时间，师襄子说：“你已经领会了曲子的意境，可以学习新内容了。”孔子仍然不肯，说：“我还不了解作者的为人。”又过了一段时间，师襄子发现孔子有时低头沉思，神情庄重肃穆，有时抬头仰望，好像很高兴的样子，似乎对这首曲子已经有了新的领悟。果然，有一天孔子对师襄子说：“我已经了解这首曲子的作者了。此人皮肤深黑，体形修长，目光高远，像个统治四方诸侯的王。不是文王还能是谁呢？”
师襄子立刻从席子上站起来，对着孔子拜了两拜，说：“你真是圣人呢，据说这首曲子就是《文王操》。”
fields.content_en:
**Confucius Learns to Play the Zither**

Long ago, when Confucius was young, he went to learn how to play the zither from a famous musician named Xiangzi in the state of Lu. Confucius practiced the same song for ten days and still did not ask to learn a new one. Xiangzi said, "You may learn a new song now." But Confucius replied gently, "I know the melody by heart, but I have not yet mastered the art of playing it." So he continued practicing the same song. After some time, Xiangzi said again, "You have mastered the technique now. You can learn something new." But Confucius said, "I still do not feel the meaning behind this song." And he kept on playing. Once more, Xiangzi told him, "You understand the mood of the piece. You may move on." Confucius still shook his head and said softly, "I do not yet know the person who wrote it."

Still more time passed. Xiangzi noticed that sometimes Confucius sat with his head bowed, deep in thought, looking solemn and peaceful. Other times he lifted his eyes and smiled, as if touched by something beautiful. Xiangzi realized that Confucius was discovering something new in the music. At last, Confucius looked up and said, "I now know who wrote this song. He was a tall man with dark skin and far-reaching eyes. He carried himself like a king who ruled over all the lords. Could it be anyone other than King Wen?"

Xiangzi rose quickly from his seat, bowed twice before Confucius, and said with awe, "You truly are a great teacher. I did not even know this song was called *The Song of King Wen*."
fields.tips: 孔子能如此学而不厌，精益求精，是因为他足够投入。准妈妈做胎教也需要有这样的精神。一定要将自己的心思投入进去，不要潦草敷衍，这样才能真正刺激到胎宝宝。
fields.tips_en: Confucius mastered the qin through wholehearted devotion and an unyielding pursuit of perfection. Dear mom-to-be, your prenatal bonding works in much the same way. Pour your heart into every moment of connection with your baby — don’t rush through it or treat it as a task. When you truly engage, your baby feels it, and that is where real magic begins.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 义虎
fields.subtitle: 有信义就会被人尊重
fields.subtitle_en: Honor and Trust Earn Respect
fields.content:
唐朝贞元年间，申州有许多猛虎，猛虎伤人的事时有发生，闹得民不聊生。为了消除虎患，太守王徴发文高价悬赏善于捕虎的人。丁岩是个年老的差役，善于布设陷阱，就被入选专管捕虎之事。
丁岩领命以后，没过几天，他布设的陷阱就捕到一只猛虎。落在陷阱里的老虎暴跳如雷，吼声震耳，人们纷纷围观。丁岩自然喜形于色。可是乐极生悲，正当他眉飞色舞地嘲笑、挑逗老虎时，一个立足不稳，他就掉到了陷阱里，和老虎“同处一室”了。众人一下子惊慌起来，这下丁岩哪还能留得命在？可过了一会儿却发现，老虎并没有攻击丁岩。丁岩和老虎面面相对端坐着，一人一虎，谁也不动。
人们赶紧找来了辘轳和井绳，打算把丁岩拉上来。井绳放下去了，丁岩把井绳捆在自己腰间，拉动了一下绳子示意上面的人可以动手了。两个有力的壮汉就一起绞动辘轳，把丁岩拉了起来。可丁岩刚刚离地两三尺，辘轳就绞不动了。原来是老虎把绳子拉住了，不让丁岩离开陷阱。众人又尝试了几次，次次如此，都是丁岩刚离地，老虎就抓住了绳子。
人们无计可施，僵持了一会儿。丁岩仔细观察老虎，发现它神态祥和，没有要伤害自己的意思，就跟它说起了话。丁岩跟老虎说如果能让他上去，他一定请求太守放了它。他还要求老虎答应他被放之后，要领着其他老虎躲到深山里去，不再来伤害人类。
也不知道虎听懂没有，丁岩决定再尝试一下，就示意上面的人再拉他。这次老虎居然真的没有再拉住绳子，让丁岩顺利出了陷阱。
丁岩出了陷阱，跟太守讲了前因后果，请求他把老虎放了。太守答应了。人们把土顺着陷阱的边倒下去，陷阱越来越浅。当陷阱只剩下一丈来深的时候，虎一跃就跳了出来，兴奋地转了一大圈跑了。没到10天，申州就再也看不到老虎了，想必是那只义虎把它们都带入深山了。
fields.content_en:
**The Righteous Tiger**

Long ago in the Tang Dynasty, the city of Shenzhou was home to many fierce tigers. These tigers would sometimes hurt people, and the villagers lived in fear. To solve this problem, the governor issued a reward for anyone brave enough to catch tigers. Ding Yan was an elderly man who was very skilled at setting traps, so he was chosen to take care of this important task.

After Ding Yan set his traps, just a few days later, one of them caught a magnificent tiger. The trapped tiger roared with fury, its mighty sound shaking the ground. People gathered around to watch. Ding Yan couldn't hide his joy. But as he stood close to the trap, laughing and teasing the tiger, his footing gave way and he tumbled down into the trap with it. Everyone panicked! They thought poor Ding Yan was surely done for. But then something surprising happened—the tiger did not attack him at all. Instead, the man and the tiger sat facing each other inside the trap, both perfectly still.

Soon, people brought down a bucket on a rope lowered on a long rope to pull him out. Ding Yan tied the rope around his waist and gave it a gentle tug to signal the men above that they could begin pulling. Two strong men worked together to crank the wheel, slowly lifting Ding Yan up. But just as he lifted a few feet above the ground, the rope stopped moving. The tiger had caught the rope in its paws and was holding it tight, refusing to let Ding Yan leave the trap. The villagers tried several more times, but each time, the same thing happened—the moment Ding Yan rose from the bottom, the tiger held onto the rope.

With no other choice, the people waited. Ding Yan looked carefully at the tiger and noticed something wonderful. Its eyes were soft and calm, full of kindness rather than anger. It wasn't thinking about hurting him at all. So Ding Yan spoke gently to the tiger. He promised that if the tiger would let him go, he would beg the governor to set it free. And he asked the tiger to promise that, once released, it would lead all the other tigers deep into the mountains far away, where they would never again trouble the people. Whether the tiger understood every word or not, Ding Yan decided to try again. He signaled the men above to pull once more. This time, the tiger let go of the rope. Ding Yan climbed out of the trap safely and happily.

Ding Yan rushed to tell the governor everything that had happened and asked him kindly to release the tiger. The governor agreed. The villagers began filling in the trap with earth until it was shallow enough for the tiger to leap out. When the trap was only about three feet deep, the tiger sprang forward with a mighty bound and bounded gracefully out of the pit. It circled around once, proud and free, and then trotted away into the forest. Within ten days, not a single tiger was seen in Shenzhou anymore. People say that tiger led them all to safety in the deep, peaceful mountains—true to its promise.
fields.tips: 在许多故事中，老虎都被塑造成吃人的形象，而这个故事里老虎却是想和人类和谐相处的。当它落入陷阱后并没有伤害捕虎人，而是与捕虎人和谈。最终老虎在深山里过上了快乐的日子，而附近的居民也安居乐业。准妈妈不妨多看看自然与动物的纪录片，让胎宝宝感受到大自然的美丽、丰富、神奇以及和谐。
fields.tips_en: In many tales, tigers are feared as fierce predators. But in this story, the tiger longs only for harmony with humanity. After falling into a trap, it chooses peace over anger and lives happily in the deep mountains, while nearby villagers thrive in quiet contentment. During your pregnancy, consider watching nature and wildlife documentaries together — let your baby soak in the beauty, wonder, and harmony of the natural world.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 诸葛亮出师
fields.title_en: Zhuge Liang Sets Out on His Mission
fields.subtitle: 足智多谋已显现
fields.subtitle_en: Wisdom Shines Bright
fields.content:
诸葛亮是中国文化中忠臣与智者的代表人物，他神机妙算的本领，最为人乐道。他帮助刘备打江山用兵如神的故事，后人十分敬佩，争相传颂。其实诸葛亮年轻时，他的聪明机智就已经显露出来。从他出师，也就是毕业的事上就能看出一二。
诸葛亮当时师从司马徽在深山中学习。司马徽是襄阳的著名隐士，后来历史很多名人都曾师从司马徽，除了诸葛亮，还有庞统、徐庶等。
诸葛亮跟司马徽学习多年以后，司马徽给他们师兄弟几个出了一道题，就是3天之后午时，谁能得到师父的准许走出院子的大门，谁就出师毕业了。
3天之后，诸葛亮的师兄弟们想出了各种各样的借口，比如家中老人病逝、家中着火等，请师父允许回家看看。但师父都无一例外回答他们3天以后再说吧。师兄弟们只得继续留下来学习，大家都在等着看诸葛亮怎么说。平时他是最机智的。
轮到诸葛亮了。没想到诸葛亮破口大骂：“你这个老匹夫，跟你学了这么多年，什么本事都没有教给我们，现在你还出这样的破题为难我们。这跟出师有什么关系？我跟你这样的师父有什么用？我要另找师父了。”
师兄弟们看到诸葛亮这个样子，都瞪大了眼睛。平素里，诸葛亮是最尊敬师父的，师父也最喜欢他。现在他这样说，可不把老师气坏了吗？
果然，老师非常生气，气恼了半天，憋出几句话：“罢罢罢，算老夫看走了眼，竟收了你这样的徒弟。你要走就走吧！”
老师话音刚落，诸葛亮二话不说，气呼呼地就走出了院门。不过刚出院门，他就转过身来跪倒在地了，只听他朗声说道：“师父，我这是为了完成老师的题目啊。现在题目完成了，请老师降罪。”老师听完一愣，随即恍然大悟。老师自然没有责怪诸葛亮，诸葛亮就顺利出师了。
fields.content_en:
Title: Zhuge Liang Graduates

Zhuge Liang is a famous figure from Chinese culture, known as a loyal minister and a wise man. Everyone loves telling stories about his clever plans and brilliant mind. People have always admired how he helped his leader Liu Bei with his amazing strategies, and they happily share these tales from generation to generation. But the truth is, even when Zhuge Liang was young, his smartness was already shining through. You can see this even in the story of when he graduated from his studies.

At that time, Zhuge Liang studied deep in the mountains under a teacher named Sima Hui. Sima Hui was a well-known wise hermit in Xiangyang. Many famous people throughout history studied under him, including Zhuge Liang, as well as Pang Tong and Xu Shu.

After teaching Zhuge Liang and his fellow students for many years, Sima Hui gave them a little challenge. He told them that whoever could get permission to walk out of the courtyard gate by noon three days later would graduate.

Three days later, Zhuge Liang's classmates came up with all sorts of excuses. Some said an elderly family member had fallen ill. Others said their homes had caught fire. They all asked their teacher if they could go home to check. But one by one, the teacher simply replied, "Let's talk about it in three more days." So the classmates had to stay and keep studying. They were all waiting to see what Zhuge Liang would do, since he was always the cleverest among them.

When it was Zhuge Liang's turn, something unexpected happened. To everyone's surprise, he began scolding loudly: "You old grump! I've studied with you for so many years, and you haven't taught us anything at all! And now you set such a silly challenge to make our lives hard. What does this have to do with graduating? What good is a teacher like you? I'll find another teacher!"

His classmates' eyes widened in shock. Zhuge Liang was always the most respectful student toward his teacher, and the teacher loved him the most. Now he was saying such things—wouldn't this make the teacher terribly angry?

And indeed, the teacher was very upset. After fuming for a while, he managed to say, "Fine, fine, fine! I must have seen wrong when I took you on as a student. If you want to leave, then leave!"

No sooner had the teacher finished speaking than Zhuge Liang turned on his heel and strode out of the courtyard gate in a huff. But the moment he stepped outside, he turned around and knelt down on the ground. In a clear, bright voice, he said, "Teacher, I did all of that to finish your challenge. The challenge is now complete. Please punish me." The teacher paused for a moment, and then suddenly understood everything. Of course, the teacher did not blame Zhuge Liang at all. And so, Zhuge Liang graduated with ease.
fields.tips: 有关诸葛亮的传说非常多，因为智慧的魅力总是足够吸引人的。准妈妈在读这个故事的时候，不妨跟准爸爸一起回忆回忆自己的毕业场景，翻翻毕业论文，跟胎宝宝讲讲读书主要干什么，说说什么是毕业、什么是出师，祝愿他将来学习成绩好。
fields.tips_en: There are many legendary tales about Zhuge Liang, for the charm of wisdom always captivates the heart. When reading this story, dear mom and dad, why not reminisce together about your own graduation day? Look through your thesis and share with your baby the joys of learning—what it means to graduate, to master a craft. May your little one grow up to be a bright and eager student.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 包公审石头
fields.title_en: Judge Bao and the Stubborn Stone
fields.subtitle: “曲线”解决问题
fields.subtitle_en: Finding an Indirect Path to Solutions
fields.content:
包拯是北宋时期的清官，审案子公正严明，人们都敬重他，视他为青天大老爷，都称他为“包公”。因为他长得黑，又叫他“包老黑”“黑包公”。包公审案特别有智慧，有时候完全不按常理出牌，很复杂的案子都能举重若轻地解决掉。
有一天，包公带着人马从一条路上走过，看到路边有个小孩坐在一块石头上哭。他觉得奇怪，就叫人停下轿子。包公下了轿子走到小孩跟前，问小孩怎么了。小孩看来人长得黑乎乎的，感觉有点儿害怕，一个劲儿往后退。包公就笑着对他说自己是包拯，叫他别害怕，有什么问题自己可以帮他解决。小孩一听是大名鼎鼎的包公，就不害怕了。他告诉包拯：“我今天上午卖油条，好不容易卖了些钱，可以给我母亲买药了。母亲生病了，还等着药呢。可是我走得太累了，就坐在这块石头上歇了一歇，谁知道竟然睡着了。醒来一看，我的钱都不见了。”包公一听就知道这钱肯定是被人偷去了，就问小孩总共有多少钱。小孩说：“正好100枚，我仔仔细细数过了。”包公想了想对小孩说：“我知道了，肯定是这块石头把你的钱偷去了。我给你审审它，让它把钱还给你。”路过的人一听包公要审石头，觉得很奇怪，都围过来看。
包公看围的人越来越多了，就开始审石头了。他问石头：“石头，是不是你偷了小孩的铜钱？”石头当然不说话。包公又问：“石头，快说话，是不是你偷了小孩的铜钱？”石头当然还是一声不响。包公生气了：“石头，我看不打你，你不会招了。来人，给我打它20大板。”手下人听包公这么一说，还真的举起棍子，噼里啪啦地打起来了。一边打还一边问：“你说不说？你说不说？”周围看热闹的人忍不住哄笑起来，大家肆无忌惮开始议论了：“都说包公聪明，可见耳听为虚，实际上是个糊涂蛋。”人们的议论被包公听到了。包公非常恼火，对围观的人说：“我在审案，你们却在笑话我。以下犯上，每人罚一个铜钱，都丢到那个盆子里去。”说完，包公就叫手下人拿一个盆子装满了水，放到石头上。人们看包公发火了，不敢违抗，只得排着队一个一个地过来，每个人往水盆里投一枚铜钱。“扑通”“扑通”，盆子里已经有很多铜钱了。只听“扑通”又一声，一枚铜钱落入了盆子里。没想到包公大喝一声：“把他拿下！”刚投入那枚铜钱的人就被包公手下抓住了。人们都不明白是怎么回事。包公解释说：“他的钱进入水盆里，有一层油花漂起来，所以就是小孩卖油条的钱。”小偷早就做贼心虚，当场愣住了。他不得不把钱都还给了小孩。
大家都心服了，说包公是真的聪明，连审石头都能破案子。
知识
lian
接
民间关于包拯的传说很多。一个就是包拯母亲早逝，他是由嫂子带大的，所以他尊称他的嫂子为“嫂娘”。其实，包拯的父母一直活到包拯30多岁的时候。包拯为了照顾二老，曾经向皇帝请旨在离家较近的地方做官，后来又干脆辞官专门在家照顾父母10余年。父母离世大约5年以后他才又开始到开封府任职。
fields.content_en:
Title: Judge Bao Tries a Stone

Bao Zheng was a fair and honest judge during the Song Dynasty. People respected him deeply and called him "Lord Bao" or "Judge Bao." Because his skin was dark, some also playfully called him "Black Judge Bao." He was famous for solving tricky cases with great wisdom, often in ways no one expected.

One day, Judge Bao and his guards were walking along a road when he noticed a little boy sitting on a stone by the roadside, crying. Feeling curious, he told his guards to stop. Judge Bao stepped down from his sedan chair and walked over to the boy. He asked the child what was wrong. The boy saw a tall man with a dark face and felt a little frightened, so he kept backing away. Judge Bao smiled gently and told the boy that he was Bao Zheng, and that he had nothing to fear—he would help him solve whatever problem he had. When the boy heard it was the famous Judge Bao, he felt brave again.

He told Judge Bao: "This morning I sold fried dough sticks and managed to earn some money so I could buy medicine for my mother. She is sick and is waiting for the medicine. But I was so tired from walking that I sat on this stone to rest, and before I knew it, I fell asleep. When I woke up, my money was gone." Judge Bao immediately understood that the money must have been stolen. He asked the boy how much money he had lost. The boy replied, "Exactly one hundred coins. I counted them very carefully."

Judge Bao thought for a moment and then said to the boy, "I understand. This stone must have stolen your money. Let me hold a trial for it and make it give your money back." When the people passing by heard that Judge Bao was going to try a stone, they were all puzzled and gathered around to watch.

Judge Bao noticed more and more people had come to see, so he began the trial. He asked the stone, "Stone, did you steal the boy's copper coins?" Of course, the stone said nothing. Judge Bao asked again, "Stone, speak up! Did you steal the boy's coins?" Still, the stone remained silent. Judge Bao grew angry. "Stone, I see that unless I beat you, you won't confess. Men, give it twenty blows with a staff!" His guards, hearing this, actually picked up sticks and started hitting the stone—whack, whack, whack! As they hit, they also asked, "Will you confess? Will you confess?" The crowd burst out laughing, and people began chatting freely: "They say Judge Bao is clever, but I guess seeing is believing—and he seems quite foolish after all." Judge Bao heard their words and was quite displeased. He told the onlookers, "I am holding a trial here, yet you are all laughing at me. Such disrespect deserves a fine. Each of you must toss one copper coin into that bowl."

Then Judge Bao ordered his men to bring a basin filled with water and place it on the stone. Seeing that the judge was angry, no one dared to disobey. So the crowd formed a line and came forward one by one, each dropping a coin into the water. Plink, plink—many coins had already settled at the bottom of the basin. Suddenly, another plink echoed as a coin splashed into the water. To everyone's surprise, Judge Bao shouted loudly, "Seize him!" The man who had just thrown his coin in was immediately grabbed by the guards. Everyone was confused.

Judge Bao explained, "When his coin entered the water, an oily film floated to the surface. That oil came from selling fried dough sticks—which means it was the boy's money." The thief had been guilty all along and stood frozen on the spot. He had no choice but to return all the money to the boy.

Everyone was deeply impressed and said that Judge Bao truly was wise—even to the point of trying a stone to solve a case.

Knowledge

There are many folk tales about Bao Zheng. One says that his mother passed away when he was young, and he was raised by his sister-in-law, so he respectfully called her "Aunt Mother." In truth, however, Bao Zheng's parents lived until he was in his thirties. He once asked the emperor for permission to serve as an official closer to home so he could care for them, and later he even resigned from his post to stay home and look after his parents for over ten years. It was only about five years after his parents passed away that he returned to serve in the Kaifeng magistrate's office.
fields.tips: 解决问题的方法往往不止一个，直接面对只是其中之一。准妈妈无论是在工作中还是生活上与人发生矛盾的时候，思路要多转几个弯，尽量避免直接起冲突，不要让自己生气。
fields.tips_en: There is often more than one way to solve a problem—direct confrontation is only one of them. Whether at work or in daily life, dear mom, try to take a few extra turns in your thinking when conflicts arise. Avoid direct clashes as much as possible, and protect your peace of mind.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 田忌赛马
fields.subtitle: 如何化劣势为优势
fields.subtitle_en: How to Turn Disadvantages into Strengths
fields.content:
田忌是战国时期齐国的大将，喜欢赛马。这天他又和齐威王约定赛马了。他的好朋友孙膑也在旁观战。田忌用自己的上等马对齐威王的上等马，中等马对齐威王的中等马，下等马对齐威王的下等马。结果都输了。
输了的田忌垂头丧气，打算回家了。孙膑却拉住他说：“你的马比齐威王的马也差不到哪里去，再跟他比，你也未必全输。”田忌一向器重孙膑，知道他足智多谋，于是听从了他的话，再次向齐威王挑战。
齐威王心想你那三匹马是什么货色都已经很明显了，再比还是一样输。他就轻蔑地对田忌说：“悉听尊便，要比就比吧。”两人各下了赌注。
比赛开始了，孙膑让田忌用他的下等马对齐威王的上等马，当然输了。田忌还嘀咕孙膑出的是什么馊主意，还不是一样输，输得比前次还惨，明显落后更多。不过，第二场用田忌的上等马对齐威王的中等马，田忌赢了；第三场用田忌的中等马对齐威王的下等马，又赢一场。田忌以三比二的比分赢了齐威王。
fields.content_en:
# Tian Ji's Horse Race

Tian Ji was a great general from the State of Qi during the Warring States period, and he loved horse racing. One day he made plans to race against King Wei of Qi again. His good friend Sun Bin came along to watch. Tian Ji matched his best horse against the king's best horse, his middle horse against the king's middle horse, and his lowest horse against the king's lowest horse. And he lost every time.

Tian Ji was very sad after losing and started to go home. But Sun Bin stopped him and said, "Your horses are not much worse than the king's. If you race again, you might not lose everything." Tian Ji always respected Sun Bin and knew he was very clever, so he listened and challenged the king to another race.

King Wei thought, "His three horses are nothing special. I'll win again just like last time." So he said proudly to Tian Ji, "Go ahead and race. Let's see what happens." They both placed their bets.

The race began. Sun Bin told Tian Ji to use his lowest horse against the king's best horse first, and naturally Tian Ji lost that one. Tian Ji even wondered what silly idea Sun Bin had come up with. It was the same result — he lost, and this time he fell further behind than before. But in the second race, Tian Ji used his best horse against the king's middle horse, and he won! In the third race, Tian Ji used his middle horse against the king's lowest horse, and he won again. Tian Ji beat King Wei three to two.
fields.tips: 孙膑让田忌赛马取得胜利的关键就是给马重新做了一下排列组合。已经习惯成自然的生活程序，准妈妈不妨也重新做做排列组合，将事情分为紧急重要、紧急不重要、重要不紧急、不重要也不紧急等，然后有取舍地去做，自己会轻松不少。
fields.tips_en: The key to Tian Ji's victory lay in simply rearranging the order of his horses. Expectant mothers can do the same with the routines of daily life—reorganize and regroup your tasks by sorting them into urgent and important, urgent but not important, important but not urgent, and neither urgent nor important. Making thoughtful choices about what to do first will bring you considerable relief.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 郑板桥吟诗赶小偷
fields.title_en: Zheng Banqiao Chases Away a Thief with Poetry
fields.subtitle: 中国诗词的独特魅力
fields.subtitle_en: The Unique Charm of Chinese Poetry
fields.content: 郑板桥是清代著名的画家。他不仅画画得好，还擅长作文联对。一天晚上，已经很晚了，外面风大雨大，郑板桥躺在床上，辗转不能入睡，凝神构思一幅画。突然，他听到有人蹑手蹑脚地进来了，想必是小偷。这时的郑板桥已经年老，想着自己惊动了小偷，也难以应付。如果任小偷偷盗，也实在不甘心。略加思索，郑板桥想出一计。他翻了个身，低声吟起诗来。诗的第一、第二句是：“细雨蒙蒙夜深沉，梁上君子进我门。”小偷一听，吓了一跳。正当他愣在那儿犹豫的时候，郑板桥又吟出了第三、第四句：“腹内诗书藏万卷，屋中金银无半文。”小偷一听不生气，反而乐了，就打算离开。刚要抬腿，听到郑板桥又吟出一句：“出门休惊黄毛犬。”小偷一听这家还有狗呢，那就翻墙出去吧。他正欲翻墙，没想到郑板桥又说了这么一句：“越墙莫损兰花盆。”小偷低头一看，果然墙角有一盆兰花，于是急忙避开了。小偷翻墙而出，正想着这个人挺有趣，墙里居然还有两句诗送出来：“天寒不及穿衣送，趁着月色赶豪门。”小偷哭笑不得，只得转身离去。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Zheng Banqiao Recites a Poem to Drive Away a Thief**

Zheng Banqiao was a famous painter during the Qing Dynasty. He was not only great at painting but also very good at writing poems and couplets. One night, very late, when the wind was howling and the rain was pouring outside, Zheng Banqiao lay in bed, turning over and over, unable to sleep. He was deep in thought, imagining a painting. Suddenly, he heard someone creeping inside. It must be a thief.

At this time, Zheng Banqiao was already quite old. He worried that if he startled the thief, he might not be able to handle it himself. But if he just let the thief steal away, he would feel very unwilling. After a little thinking, Zheng Banqiao came up with an idea. He turned over and softly began to recite a poem. The first two lines went like this: "Through the misty rain, the deep night falls; / A gentleman upon the beam enters my halls." When the thief heard this, he was quite startled.

Just as he stood there, hesitating, Zheng Banqiao recited the next two lines: "Ten thousand books of poetry dwell within my heart; / Yet not a single coin of gold or silver in my home can be found." The thief, hearing this, was no longer angry but instead felt rather amused. He decided to leave. But just as he was about to step forward, he heard Zheng Banqiao call out another line: "As you go out, take care not to startle the little fluffy dog." The thief was surprised to learn there was a dog in the house, so he decided to climb over the wall instead.

Just as he was about to scale the wall, Zheng Banqiao spoke once more: "When climbing over, please do not knock down the orchid pot." The thief looked down and indeed spotted an orchid plant by the wall. He hurriedly stepped aside to avoid it.

After climbing over the wall, the thief was thinking how interesting this person was. Just then, two more lines of poetry floated out from inside the house: "The night is cold, and I cannot dress to see you off; / So I chase you along, by moonlight, to the wealthy gates." The thief could only laugh and shake his head, then turned and walked away into the night.
fields.tips: 中国古代诗词的语言魅力是公认的。准妈妈可以在闲暇时候找些唐诗、宋词来读。这些诗词节奏鲜明，韵律优美，既是很好的语言胎教，也有一定的音乐性，可培养胎宝宝的感受力。
fields.tips_en: The linguistic beauty of ancient Chinese poetry is universally admired. In your leisure moments, dear mom, consider reading some Tang Dynasty poems and Song Dynasty ci. Their clear rhythm and melodic grace make them wonderful language-based prenatal education—and their musicality helps nurture your little one's sensitivity and appreciation.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 王羲之教子
fields.subtitle: 成功无捷径
fields.subtitle_en: There Are No Shortcuts to Success
fields.content:
晋代书法家王献之的字是跟父亲王羲之学的。不过学字并不是那么容易，王献之开始学的时候也特别想知道父亲练成一手好书法的秘诀。
当王献之跟父亲请教书法秘诀的时候，王羲之指着院子里的18口大水缸说：“秘诀就在水缸里，等你把这些水缸里的水都写完就知道了。”
王献之觉得父亲是故弄玄虚，连亲生儿子都不肯教一下。王献之心里不服，下定决心练基本功，一定要超过父亲。他天天模仿父亲的字体，练习“横、竖、点、撇、捺”几个笔画，足足练习了两年。他用心写好后拿给父亲看，心想这下肯定能让父亲大吃一惊。王羲之看了看儿子拿来的字，不置一词，只是笑了笑。站在旁边的母亲倒是说：“进步不小，很有点铁划的劲儿了。”
接下来，王献之专门练习“钩”，各种各样的钩。他连续又练习两年之后，写了一个最得意的钩，递到父亲面前。父亲还是像上次一样，笑了笑，没说一句话。王献之只得再拿给母亲看。母亲又表扬了他：“嗯，不错，有点银钩的意思了。”
这样，王献之就开始练习写完整的字了。他足足练习了4年之后，写了一个“大”字，左看右看，觉得很不错，再次拿给父亲看。父亲这次仍然是笑而不语，不过拿起笔在他的“大”字下加了一个点儿，变成了“太”。王献之不明白是什么意思，把字拿给母亲。母亲看了一眼，叹了一口气说：“你练字总共加起来已经有3000天了吧，只有下面的这一点儿达到了你父亲的水平。”王献之一听，才知道写字真不是能浑水摸鱼的，彻底服了。此后，王献之练字不但更加勤快了，而且更加用心了。
这天，王献之正在练字，父亲走过来他都没有发觉。父亲悄悄站着看了一会儿，突然伸出手猛地拔他手中正握着的毛笔，结果王献之握在手中的笔一动不动。王羲之放心了，终于表扬了儿子：“这小子将来定能成大器。”果然，王献之后来也成了大书法家。他与父亲齐名，被合称“二王”。
fields.content_en:
Title: Wang Xizhi Teaches His Son

During the Jin Dynasty, the calligrapher Wang Xianzhi learned his craft from his father, Wang Xizhi. But learning to write well was not easy, and young Wang Xianzhi was very curious about the secret to his father's beautiful handwriting.

When Wang Xianzhi asked his father for the secret, Wang Xizhi pointed to eighteen large water jars in the courtyard and said, "The secret is inside those jars. When you have written them all dry, you will know."

Wang Xianzhi thought his father was being mysterious and refusing to teach his own son. Feeling a bit unwilling, he made up his mind to practice his basics hard and one day surpass his father. Every day, he copied his father's style and practiced the strokes—"horizontal, vertical, dot, sweep, and press"—for two full years. When he felt he had written well, he showed them to his father, thinking his father would surely be amazed. Wang Xizhi glanced at his son's work, said nothing, and just smiled. But the mother standing by said, "You have made great progress. There is real strength in your strokes now."

Then Wang Xianzhi focused on practicing hooks of all kinds. After two more years of continuous practice, he wrote what he was most proud of—a beautiful hook—and held it up for his father. Again, his father merely smiled and said nothing. Wang Xianzhi could only show it to his mother. She praised him, "Mm, quite good. You are starting to sound like silver hooks."

So Wang Xianzhi began practicing whole characters. Four more years went by. Finally, he wrote the character for "big," looked at it from left to right, and felt it was wonderful. He brought it to his father once more. This time, his father still smiled without speaking, but picked up a brush and added a small dot beneath the character, turning it into "too big." Wang Xianzhi did not understand, so he took the character to his mother. She looked at it and sighed, saying, "You have been practicing for three thousand days in total, and only that little dot here matches your father's level." Wang Xianzhi finally understood that one cannot cut corners when learning calligraphy, and he fully accepted it. From then on, he practiced with even greater diligence and care.

One day, while Wang Xianzhi was practicing, his father walked up behind him without him noticing. His father stood quietly for a while, then suddenly reached out and tried to pull the brush from his hand. But the brush did not move at all. Wang Xizhi was relieved. At last, he praised his son, "This boy will surely achieve great things someday." And indeed, Wang Xianzhi later became a great calligrapher himself. He was famous alongside his father, and together they are known as the "Two Wangs."
fields.tips: 王羲之教子采用的是一种以身作则的方法。准妈妈做胎教最好也这样，想让孩子将来成为怎样的人，自己从现在起也努力做个那样的人。
fields.tips_en: Wang Xizhi guided his children by leading through example. Dear mom, practicing prenatal education works best this way too: if you wish your child to grow into a certain kind of person, begin becoming that very person today.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 昭君出塞
fields.title_en: Zhaojun Marries Beyond the Great Wall
fields.subtitle: 女人的气度
fields.subtitle_en: A Woman's Grace and Courage
fields.content:
汉元帝时，匈奴的一支同西汉结盟。其首领呼韩邪单于三次进长安朝拜，并向汉元帝提出要娶一个汉王朝的公主，增强双方的联系。
汉朝当时正势盛，跟匈奴结亲只需要随便选个人封为公主嫁过去就可以了，自然不会让真的公主嫁过去。于是就派人到后宫里选愿意到匈奴和亲的人。后宫里宫女很多，但没有人愿意远嫁到匈奴去。负责选人的大臣着急无奈之时，有一个宫女倒站出来，说愿意去。她就是王昭君。负责的大臣非常高兴，即刻上报汉元帝。没多久王昭君就和呼韩邪单于在长安成了亲。
王昭君顶着公主的头衔嫁给呼韩邪单于，临走的时候要向汉元帝告别。告别时汉元帝看见王昭君，立刻后悔了。因为王昭君非常美丽，比他众多后宫宠妃有过之而无不及。汉元帝很舍不得把王昭君给呼韩邪单于，但现在为时已晚，只能眼睁睁看着她走了。
汉元帝回宫后非常懊恼，就命人把王昭君的画像拿来看。一看之下，发现画像上的人远不及王昭君本人十之一二，非常生气。就把画像师招来讯问。这才知道原来是画像师画像要收贿赂，有贿赂就画得美，王昭君没有给画像师贿赂就被画丑了。
王昭君辞别了汉元帝就跟着呼韩邪单于出发去匈奴了。王昭君去匈奴后，主动地适应匈奴的生活，并且把汉朝的文化传给了匈奴。她还鼓励匈奴和汉朝进行双边贸易，促进了匈奴的经济发展。她最终受到了匈奴人的爱戴。
和亲，远走番邦，生活环境、生活习惯都跟自己曾经的生活不一样，甚至有天壤之别，这对王昭君来说困难非常多，考验非常大，可以说很不幸。但是王昭君一个人的不幸成就了两个国家长时间的和平相处，又是大幸。王昭君和亲后，汉朝和匈奴和睦相处了60年，因此王昭君成了历史上备受称颂的人物。
王昭君死后，葬在大青山下，在现今的内蒙古呼和浩特郊区。匈奴人把昭君奉为神明，昭君墓也被称为“青冢”。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Zhaojun Leaves the Frontier**

During the time of Emperor Yuan of Han, one group of the Xiongnu people made an agreement with the Han dynasty. Their leader, Chanyu Huhuanye, visited the capital city of Chang'an three times to show respect, and he asked the emperor for a princess to marry, so the two sides would stay close and friendly.

At that time, the Han dynasty was strong and powerful. Marrying a princess to the Xiongnu was something they could arrange easily, so the emperor did not need to send a real princess. Instead, they looked inside the palace for a kind woman who would be willing to go. Many palace ladies lived in the palace, but none wanted to travel so far away. Just as the officials choosing the lady felt worried and helpless, one brave palace girl stepped forward and said she would go. Her name was Wang Zhaojun. The official in charge was very happy and quickly told the emperor. Soon after, Zhaojun married Chanyu Huhuanye in Chang'an.

Zhaojun traveled to the Xiongnu land wearing the title of a princess, and before she left, she had to say goodbye to Emperor Yuan. When the emperor saw her face during that final meeting, he immediately felt great sadness. Zhaojun was so beautiful, more beautiful even than all the other ladies in his palace. He did not want to let her go, but it was already too late, and he could only watch her leave.

When the emperor returned to his palace, he was full of regret. He asked someone to bring Zhaojun's painted portrait to look at it. When he saw it, he was very angry because the woman in the picture looked nothing like the real Zhaojun. He called the painter to question him and found out that the painter had taken money from some women to make them look beautiful in his paintings, but since Zhaojun did not give him money, he had painted her poorly.

Zhaojun said goodbye to Emperor Yuan and traveled with Chanyu Huhuanye to the Xiongnu lands. Once she arrived, Zhaojun warmly embraced their way of life. She also shared the culture and wisdom of Han with the Xiongnu people. She encouraged trade between the two groups, which helped the Xiongnu grow and prosper. In time, the Xiongnu people came to love and respect her deeply.

Leaving behind everything she knew to live in a faraway land was very hard for Zhaojun. The changes were huge, and the challenges were great. In many ways, her life was not easy. But because of her bravery and kindness, two great nations enjoyed peace together for a very long time. After Zhaojun married into the Xiongnu, the Han and the Xiongnu lived as friends for sixty years. Because of this, history remembers Zhaojun as a wonderful and beloved person.

After Zhaojun passed away, she was buried at the foot of Daqing Mountain, in what is now the suburbs of Hohhot in Inner Mongolia. The Xiongnu people honored her as a gentle spirit, and her resting place became known as the "Green Tomb," where her memory lives on like a quiet, enduring flower.
fields.tips: 女人在很多方面都是不输给男人的，就像王昭君的胆识和气度。她作出的贡献，超出很多男人。准妈妈可以学习，至少要有信心承受孕产中的一切痛苦，别给家人添太多的负担。
fields.tips_en: Women can stand shoulder to shoulder with men in so many ways, just as Wang Zhaojun showed remarkable courage and dignity. Her contributions surpassed those of many men. As an expectant mother, you can draw inspiration from her—above all, have confidence that you can face all the challenges of pregnancy and childbirth with grace, and spare your family unnecessary worry.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 李白与汪伦
fields.subtitle: 流传千古的友情佳话
fields.subtitle_en: A Friendship That Endures Through the Ages
fields.content:
李白是唐代著名的诗人，他不但诗写得好，性格也豪放不羁，当时就已经非常有名了。很多人都想结交他，领略一下他的风采。
这一年李白游历到了当时的泾州，就是今天的安徽省泾县。当地有一个人叫汪伦，特别仰慕李白的盛名，很想邀他来自己家做客，但又担心李白不答应。他左思右想之后，给李白写了一封信：“先生好游乎？此地有十里桃花；先生好饮乎？此地有万家酒店。”
李白果然被打动了，接到信后没几天就来到了汪伦家里。他发现这里是个小地方，哪里有什么十里桃花、万家酒店呢？不过汪伦很快就解释说：“我所说的十里桃花是说这里有个桃花潭，万家酒店是个姓万的人开的酒馆。”李白一听，知道汪伦骗了自己，但有感于汪伦的真情实意，也没有生气。于是他很愉快地在汪伦家里住了几天。
几天后，李白要走了，汪伦来送行。李白就即兴写了那首著名的《赠汪伦》：
李白乘舟将欲行，
忽闻岸上踏歌声。
桃花潭水深千尺，
不及汪伦送我情。
诗送给了汪伦，也留下了一段佳话。
知识
lian
接
桃花潭位于安徽省泾县，因李白写给汪伦的赠别诗而名扬天下。这里四季景色宜人，是值得观光的好去处。
fields.content_en:
# Li Bai and Wang Lun

Li Bai was a famous poet from the Tang Dynasty. Not only did he write wonderful poems, but he also had a free and carefree spirit. He was already very well-known back then. Many people wanted to meet him and see for themselves what he was like.

One year, Li Bai traveled to Jingzhou, which is today's Jing County in Anhui Province. There lived a man named Wang Lun, who admired Li Bai greatly and really wanted to invite him to visit, but he was worried Li Bai might say no. After thinking hard about it, Wang Lun wrote a letter to Li Bai: "Do you enjoy traveling, sir? Here there are ten miles of peach blossoms. Do you enjoy drinking, sir? Here there are ten thousand wine shops."

Li Bai was indeed touched. A few days after receiving the letter, he arrived at Wang Lun's home. But he discovered this was just a small place — where were the ten miles of peach blossoms and the ten thousand wine shops? Fortunately, Wang Lun quickly explained: "When I said ten miles of peach blossoms, I meant there is a Peach Blossom Pool here. When I said ten thousand wine shops, I meant a man surnamed Wan runs a little tavern." Li Bai understood that Wang Lun had tricked him, but he was so moved by Wang Lun's sincere friendship that he wasn't angry at all. So he happily stayed at Wang Lun's home for a few days.

A few days later, it was time for Li Bai to leave. Wang Lun came to see him off. Li Bai wrote on the spot his famous poem "To Wang Lun":

Li Bai boards his boat, ready to go,
When suddenly he hears singing from the shore.
The Peach Blossom Pool is a thousand feet deep,
But not as deep as Wang Lun's love for me.

He gave the poem to Wang Lun, and together they left behind a beautiful story of friendship.

**Fun Fact:**
Peach Blossom Pool is located in Jing County, Anhui Province. It became famous all over the world because of Li Bai's farewell poem to Wang Lun. Its scenery is lovely in every season, making it a wonderful place to visit.
fields.tips: 准妈妈如果有机会，建议多跟各种身份的人打交道、交朋友。不同的朋友带给你不同的人生体验、思维方式。肚子里的胎宝宝也会有更丰富的体验。
fields.tips_en: If you can, dear expectant mother, take the opportunity to meet and befriend people from all walks of life. Different friends will bring you different life experiences and ways of thinking—and your little one growing inside you will benefit from this rich tapestry of encounters too.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 鲁班造伞
fields.subtitle: 伟大的发明来自善于观察的眼睛
fields.subtitle_en: Great Inventions Come from observant Eyes
fields.content:
鲁班是我国古代春秋战国时期的一个大发明家。据说我们现在所用的伞就是出自他手。
鲁班善于观察、发现。很多发明都是他受自然现象的启发而发明、制作出来的，伞也不例外。据说，这天天气特别热，鲁班正一边干活，一边擦汗，偶尔还看看不远处荷塘边一群玩耍的孩子。过了一会儿，这群孩子过来了。他们每人手里都举着一张荷叶，罩在头上。
鲁班心里一动。当孩子们过来的时候，他就跟他们要了一张，仔细观察。鲁班早就想做个东西能够遮挡太阳和雨水。荷叶不就可以做个参考吗？他手里拿着荷叶就琢磨开了。
鲁班越想越觉得可行，就赶紧跑回家，找了一根竹子，分出许多细竹条，照着荷叶上脉络的样子，扎了个架子。然后，他找来一块羊皮，剪成圆圆的形状，绷在竹架子上。绷好后，他就举着出了屋子往院门口走去。他边走边兴奋地叫喊：“太好了，太好了！”
妻子听到他在院子里喊，知道肯定是又有什么新鲜玩意儿了。她急忙跑出来看，看到鲁班举着个圆形的东西正站在院子中央左顾右盼呢。看到妻子出来，鲁班赶紧报告：“你看这东西既能遮雨又能挡太阳，而且轻轻巧巧，一点儿都不妨事。你说好不好？”
妻子一看，果然是。不过她想了想问道：“雨停了，太阳下山了，拿着这么个东西就有点儿不方便了。能不能把它折起来呢？那样就好带多了。”
鲁班听了觉得这个主意的确不错，就跟妻子一起琢磨，动手改造这个东西。改好后，这个东西就用时能打开，不用时能折起，又方便又实用了。他们给这个东西起名为“伞”。它就是我们今天用的伞的雏形。
知识
lian
接
鲁班发明的东西非常多，涵盖机械、土木和手工工艺各方面。据说现在木工所用的曲尺、墨斗、刨子、凿子等都是鲁班的发明，还有磨、碾、锁也都是。他还发明过一些作战的工具，比如攻城用的云梯。
fields.content_en:
Title: Lu Ban and the Umbrella

Lu Ban was a great inventor from ancient China, during the Spring and Autumn and Warring States period. It is said that the umbrella we use today came from his hands.

Lu Ban was very good at watching and noticing things around him. Many of his inventions were inspired by nature, and the umbrella was no exception. One day, it was especially hot. Lu Ban was working and wiping sweat from his face when he happened to glance at a group of children playing near a lotus pond. After a little while, the children came over. Each of them was holding a large lotus leaf above their head like a little green hat.

Something clicked in Lu Ban's mind. As the children approached, he asked them for one of the lotus leaves and studied it carefully. He had long wanted to make something that could shield people from both the sun and the rain. Could a lotus leaf be the answer? Holding the leaf in his hand, he began to think deeply.

The more he thought about it, the more he felt it could work. He hurried home, found a piece of bamboo, and split it into many thin strips. Following the pattern of veins on the lotus leaf, he built a frame. Then he found a piece of sheepskin, cut it into a round shape, and stretched it over the bamboo frame. When he finished, he held it up and walked out of the house toward the gate, exclaiming excitedly, "Wonderful! Wonderful!"

His wife heard him calling in the yard and knew he must have come up with something new again. She hurried outside to see what it was. There stood Lu Ban in the middle of the yard, holding a round object and looking around proudly. When he saw her, he quickly showed it off. "Look! This can keep out both rain and sunshine, and it's so light and easy to carry. Don't you think it's wonderful?"

His wife looked and agreed. But then she thought for a moment and asked, "When the rain stops and the sun sets, it will be a bit troublesome to carry this big thing around all the time. Could we make it fold up? That would be much easier to bring along."

Lu Ban thought her idea was excellent. Together, he and his wife studied the design and set to work improving it. After they were done, the object could be opened when needed and folded up when it wasn't. It was convenient and practical. They named it "umbrella." And that was the very first umbrella!

Little Fact

Lu Ban invented many things, covering machinery, construction, and handicrafts. It is said that tools carpenters still use today—like the try square, ink marker, plane, and chisel—all came from his mind. He also invented the mill, the roller, and the lock. Additionally, he created tools for warfare, such as the siege ladder used for climbing city walls.
fields.tips: 准妈妈外出游玩，不要走马观花，对植物、动物观察要细致些，并把自己仔细的观察结果讲给胎宝宝听，让他将来也做一个细心的孩子。
fields.tips_en: When you go out to enjoy nature, don't rush through the sights. Take time to observe plants and animals carefully, and share your little discoveries with your baby-to-be. In doing so, you'll help nurture a thoughtful and attentive spirit within them.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 司马光砸缸
fields.subtitle: 与众不同才能脱颖而出
fields.subtitle_en: Standing Out by Thinking Differently
fields.content:
司马光是宋代著名的政治家、史学家、文学家。伟大的《资治通鉴》就是由他主持编纂的。他从小就显示出与别的孩子不一样的沉着冷静，遇到事情一点儿都不慌乱，总是一副小大人的模样。有一次，司马光和一群小伙伴在后院玩耍。孩子们爬高下低，追逐打闹，喧闹叫嚷，没一刻停歇。有一个最小的孩子特别顽皮，搬了个凳子爬到了水缸沿上去泼水玩，他把水扬洒在附近的小伙伴身上。
小伙伴们哪里容他随意泼，转身就往缸边冲来。缸沿上的孩子兴奋起来了，加紧泼水。他正高兴着呢，哪知一不小心，身体失去了平衡，“扑通”一声就掉到水缸里了。
缸非常大，非常深。小孩掉在缸里眼看就快没顶了。别的孩子一见，吓得又哭又喊，急忙跑到前院去向大人求救。
司马光却没有跑。他急中生智，跑到边上抱了一块大石头，用尽全身力气砸向大水缸。只听“砰”的一声，水缸破了一个大洞，缸里的水从洞里“哗哗”地流出来，缸里的小孩得救了。
司马光砸缸救人的故事使小小的司马光出了名。东京和洛阳有人把这件事画成了画，使这件事更加广泛地流传开来。这个故事一直流传至今。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Sima Guang Smashes the Vat**

Sima Guang was a famous politician, historian, and writer during the Song Dynasty. He helped write the great book *Zizhi Tongjian*. From a young age, he was calm and steady, unlike other children. When things happened, he never panicked. He always seemed like a little grown-up.

One day, Sima Guang and a group of friends were playing in the backyard. The children climbed up and down, chased each other, and made noise without stopping for a moment. The smallest child was very mischievous. He climbed onto the edge of a water vat with a stool and started splashing water around. He playfully threw water on his friends nearby.

The other children didn't let him splash freely. They turned and rushed toward the vat. The child on the edge got excited and splashed even more. Just when he was having so much fun, he lost his balance and—splash!—he fell right into the big water vat.

The vat was very large and very deep. The little boy was almost completely underwater. The other children were terrified. They cried and shouted and ran to the front yard to ask the adults for help.

But Sima Guang did not run away. Thinking quickly, he grabbed a large stone and smashed it against the vat with all his strength. There was a loud crash! The vat cracked open, and water gushed out. The little boy was saved!

The story of Sima Guang saving his friend made him well known even as a child. People in Dongjing and Luoyang painted pictures of this event, and the story spread far and wide. And this story has been told to children ever since.
fields.tips: 准妈妈可以准备个杯子和一截粉笔头，模仿大水缸和孩子，边做游戏，边说边想有几种能救出孩子的方法。
fields.tips_en: Try this little game with your bump: grab a cup and a piece of chalk. Imagine the cup is the big water vat and the chalk is the child inside. Together, think of all the different ways you could rescue the little one. It's a sweet way to spark creativity and problem-solving—for both of you!
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 孔融让梨
fields.title_en: Kong Rong Gives Up the Bigger Pear
fields.subtitle: 体会孝悌的意义
fields.subtitle_en: Discovering the Meaning of Filial Piety and Brotherhood
fields.content:
孔融是东汉的大文学家。他小时虽然聪明，但是却特别顽劣。他经常让祖父跪地给他当驴骑，手拿树枝，吆吆喝喝。父亲看见他这样，非常讨厌他。
母亲看见孔融如此顽劣，非常忧心。她想不能再由孔融顽劣下去了，就让他禁足，让他天天待在家中，由自己日夜教诲。渐渐地，孔融变得安静、有礼了，待人处世也守规矩了。
到孔融7岁的时候，某一天是祖父的60大寿，宾客盈门。桌子上有一盘酥梨，母亲想考验一下孔融，就让孔融把梨给大家分一下。孔融到盘子里拿了一个最大的梨。父亲还以为他是要自己吃，正要呵斥。没想到孔融径直走向祖父，双手捧给了祖父。父亲不禁动容。孔融接下来按照长幼次序之分，把梨分给了每个人。最后留下一个最小的，是孔融留给自己的。
父亲深以为怪，问孔融道：“你给别人的都是大梨，把最小的留给自己，这是为什么呀？”孔融从容地答道：“树有高有低，人有老有小。敬老尊老，是为人处世基本的准则。老人和长辈都应该得到大梨。”
父亲非常高兴，从此更喜爱孔融了。
fields.content_en:
**Kong Rong Gives Away the Pear**

Kong Rong was a great writer in the Eastern Han Dynasty. When he was little, he was clever, but he was also quite wild. He would often make his grandfather kneel on the ground and pretend to be a pony for him to ride, holding a branch like a whip and making loud noises. His father did not like this at all.

His mother worried about his bad behavior. She decided she could not let him go on like this, so she kept him at home and taught him day and night. Slowly, Kong Rong became calmer and more polite, learning to treat others with kindness and respect.

When Kong Rong was seven, it was his grandfather's sixtieth birthday, and the house was full of guests. On the table sat a plate of sweet pears. His mother wanted to test him, so she asked Kong Rong to share them. Kong Rong reached into the plate and picked up the largest pear. His father thought he was keeping it for himself and was about to scold him. But instead, Kong Rong walked straight to his grandfather and offered the pear with both hands. His father was deeply moved. Then, Kong Rong shared the rest of the pears by age, giving the biggest to the eldest and the smallest to himself.

His father was puzzled and asked, "You gave everyone else the big pears and kept the smallest for yourself. Why is that?" Kong Rong answered softly, "Trees grow at different heights, and people are young and old. We must honor and care for our elders. That is the most important way to be a good person. Grandfather and the older ones deserve the bigger pears."

His father was overjoyed and loved him even more from that day on.
fields.tips: 孔融让梨的故事虽然打动了一代又一代人，但放在今天这个物质并不匮乏的时代，人们慢慢觉得不足为奇了。准妈妈在讲这个故事的时候，不妨再讲一讲故事发生的时代背景。宝宝的品行如何，父母的教导是关键。准爸爸准妈妈在日常的一举一动中也要尊老爱幼，给胎宝宝树立良好的榜样。
fields.tips_en: The story of Kong Rong sharing pears has touched generations of hearts. But in today's world, where plenty is everywhere, it may not seem quite as remarkable. When you share this tale with your baby-to-be, consider also telling the story of the times in which it happened. Your little one's character will be shaped greatly by what they see and hear from you. Let your daily actions—treating elders with respect and caring for the young—be the gentlest, most powerful lesson of all.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 木兰从军
fields.subtitle: 巾帼不让须眉
fields.subtitle_en: A Heroine Without Equal
fields.content:
木兰的故事耳熟能详。有说她是隋代人，有说是唐代人，也有说是北魏人。北魏人的说法被更多人接受。她的姓氏也众说纷纭，有说姓花，有说姓朱，还有说木兰就是她的姓。姓花的说法接受度比较高。至于籍贯的说法也有很多，以河南商丘更为可信。不管如何，她都是古代女英雄的代表。
木兰的父亲是一位后备役军官，木兰从小就跟着父亲骑马射箭，练得一身好武艺。她长大后除了料理家务就是练武。
有一天，衙门贴出告示，要征兵去北方打仗。木兰看到告示后就开始犯愁：父亲已经年老，不适合再去征战，而且北方气候寒冷，父亲也适应不了。而自己没有哥哥，弟弟还小，怎么办呢？想来想去，只有一个办法就是自己代父从军。父母一听木兰要代父从军，觉得不妥。但是木兰说她会女扮男装，一定照顾好自己，不让别人发现。尽管父母舍不得木兰，但也实在没有别的办法，加上知道木兰武功不错，就同意她去了。
木兰立刻去置办装备，买马备鞍，没几天就跟着大部队出发了。在军队里，木兰处处小心，晚上都是和衣而睡。从来也没人怀疑过她的身份。木兰打仗非常勇敢，总是冲杀在前。几年下来，她屡建奇功，还当上了军官。同伴们都对她十分爱戴。
战争结束了，皇帝召见所有有功的将士，论功行赏。木兰当然也在其中。不过木兰拒绝了所有的封赏，她只希望得到一匹快马，赶紧回家和父母团圆。皇帝看其孝心可嘉，自然满口答应，还派了很多她的同伴护送她回去。
听说木兰要回家了，父母、姐姐、弟弟都非常高兴，早早地就等在城门外迎接她了。他们还杀了鸡、宰了羊。木兰跟着父母一起回到家。她进了自己屋里，立刻脱掉战袍，换上女装，梳好头发，化好妆，然后出来与护送她回家的同伴们相见。同伴们看着眼前的木兰一身女儿家的装扮，都惊呆了，想不到同吃同住同上战场拼杀的木兰居然是女儿身，对她更加佩服了。
木兰代父从军的故事很快流传开来，传的时间久了，后来形成了一首《木兰辞》：
唧唧复唧唧，木兰当户织。不闻机杼声，惟闻女叹息。问女何所思，问女何所忆。女亦无所思，女亦无所忆。昨夜见军帖，可汗大点兵。军书十二卷，卷卷有爷名。阿爷无大儿，木兰无长兄，愿为市鞍马，从此替爷征。
东市买骏马，西市买鞍鞯，南市买辔头，北市买长鞭。旦辞爷娘去，暮宿黄河边。不闻爷娘唤女声，但闻黄河流水鸣溅溅。旦辞黄河去，暮至黑山头。不闻爷娘唤女声，但闻燕山胡骑鸣啾啾。
万里赴戎机，关山度若飞。朔气传金柝，寒光照铁衣。将军百战死，壮士十年归。归来见天子，天子坐明堂。策勋十二转，赏赐百千强。可汗问所欲，木兰不用尚书郎，愿驰千里足，送儿还故乡。
爷娘闻女来，出郭相扶将；阿姊闻妹来，当户理红妆；小弟闻姊来，磨刀霍霍向猪羊。开我东阁门，坐我西阁床。脱我战时袍，著我旧时裳。当窗理云鬓，对镜帖花黄。出门看火伴，火伴皆惊忙。同行十二年，不知木兰是女郎！
雄兔脚扑朔，雌兔眼迷离。双兔傍地走，安能辨我是雄雌？
fields.content_en:
**Mulan Joins the Army**

The story of Mulan is well-known. Some say she lived during the Sui Dynasty, others say the Tang Dynasty, and still others say the Northern Wei Dynasty. Most people accept that she was from the Northern Wei period. There are also many theories about her surname—some say it was Hua, others say Zhu, and some believe Mulan was actually her family name. The theory that her surname was Hua is the most widely accepted. As for where she was born, there are many claims, but most historians find it most believable that she was from Shangqiu in Henan Province. Regardless of which story you prefer, she remains one of the great female heroes of ancient China.

Mulan's father was a reserve military officer, and from a young age Mulan learned to ride horses and shoot arrows by following him around. She grew up skilled in martial arts. After growing older, she spent her days managing the household and practicing her fighting skills.

One day, an official notice was posted at the government office: the army needed to conscript soldiers to fight in the north. When Mulan saw the notice, she began to worry deeply. Her father was already old and not suited for another campaign. The northern climate was harsh and cold—her father would never be able to endure it. She had no older brother, and her younger brother was still a child. What was she to do? After much thought, there was only one solution: she would take her father's place and join the army herself.

When her parents heard that Mulan wanted to go in her father's place, they felt it was wrong. But Mulan promised she would dress as a man, take good care of herself, and never let anyone discover her secret. Though her parents hated the idea of letting her go, they had no other choice. Knowing that Mulan was quite skilled in martial arts, they finally agreed.

Mulan went straight to buy her equipment. She purchased a horse, a saddle, and all the gear she needed. Within just a few days, she joined the main army and set off. In the camp, Mulan was very careful. She slept fully dressed, even at night, so she could wake quickly if needed. No one ever suspected her true identity. Mulan fought bravely in battle, always leading the charge. Over the years, she earned many medals of honor and was promoted to officer. Her fellow soldiers came to love and respect her deeply.

When the war finally ended, the emperor summoned all the soldiers who had shown bravery, to reward them according to their deeds. Mulan was among them. But when it came time to choose her reward, Mulan refused everything. She asked only for a fast horse so she could return home quickly and reunite with her parents. Seeing how devoted and filial she was, the emperor readily agreed. He also assigned many of her comrades to escort her on her journey home.

When word spread that Mulan was returning, her parents, older sister, and younger brother were overjoyed. They waited early at the city gate to welcome her. They killed chickens and slaughtered sheep to prepare a feast. When Mulan arrived with her parents, she went to her room, took off her battle armor, put on her women's clothes, combed her hair, applied her makeup, and then came out to meet the companions who had escorted her home. When her comrades saw Mulan dressed as a woman before their eyes, they were utterly stunned. They could not believe that the same Mulan who had eaten, slept, and fought beside them was actually a woman. They admired her even more.

Very soon, the story of Mulan joining the army in her father's place spread far and wide. Over time, it was turned into a famous poem called "The Ballad of Mulan":

*Click, click goes the loom, Mulan weaves at her door.*
*I hear not the sound of the shuttle, but only her sighs and her sorrow.*
*I ask you, what troubles your mind? I ask you, what weighs on your heart?*
*Nothing troubles my mind, nothing weighs on my heart.*
*Yesterday I saw the military roll, the Khan is drafting soldiers by millions.*
*Twelve volumes of papers, each bearing my father's name.*
*My father has no grown son, I have no elder brother.*
*I wish to buy a saddle and horse, and take my father's place in war.*

*I bought a fine steed in the eastern market,*
*A saddle in the western market,*
*A bridle in the southern market,*
*A long whip in the northern market.*
*At dawn I left my parents and set out,*
*At dusk I made camp beside the Yellow River.*
*I heard not my parents calling for their daughter,*
*But only the rushing waters of the Yellow River, splashing and churning.*
*At dawn I left the Yellow River and rode on,*
*At dusk I reached the Black Mountain.*
*I heard not my parents calling for their daughter,*
*But only the neighing of barbarian horses on Mount Yan.*

*For ten thousand miles I hurried to the battlefield,*
*Passing over mountain passes as though I could fly.*
*The cold north wind carried the sound of the sentry's clapper,*
*The cold light shone on my iron armor.*
*Generals died in a hundred battles,*
*But the brave soldier returned after ten long years.*

*Returning, I appeared before the Son of Heaven,*
*Who sat in his bright hall.*
*My merits were recorded twelve times over,*
*And I was gifted hundreds of thousands of silks and gold.*
*The Khan asked what I desired,*
*But Mulan declined the post of Secretary,*
*Wishing only for a swift horse,*
*To carry me back to my homeland.*

*My parents, hearing their daughter came, Supported each other as they left the outer gate;*
*My elder sister, hearing her sister came, Readied her rouge before the window;*
*My younger brother, hearing his sister came, Sharpened his knife, hiss-hiss, toward the pigs and sheep.*

*I opened the door of my eastern chamber,*
*Sat upon the bed in my western room.*
*I took off my war robe,*
*Put on my old garments.*
*Before the window I combed my cloud-like hair,*
*Before the mirror I pasted my flower-yellow ornament.*
*I went out to see my comrades,*
*But they were all astounded.*
*We marched and camped together for twelve years,*
*Yet never knew Mulan was a woman!*

*A male rabbit's feet kick and scramble,*
*A female rabbit's eyes grow misty and soft.*
*When two rabbits run side by side along the ground,*
*How can you tell which is male and which is female?*
fields.tips: 很多准妈妈肯定还记得当年坐在课堂里摇头晃脑念着“唧唧复唧唧，木兰当户织”的情景。一转眼，当年的少女已经将要为人母了。但当年的那些美好记忆，肯定难以忘怀。在读这个故事时，不妨给胎宝宝讲一下你的中学时光吧，相信胎宝宝很愿意倾听。
fields.tips_en: Many expectant mothers will surely remember sitting in the classroom back in their school days, swaying rhythmically as they recited the famous lines, 'Buzz, buzz again goes the loom — Mulan weaves at her door.' In the blink of an eye, that young girl has grown into a mother-to-be. But those beautiful memories will always remain close to your heart. As you share this story with your little one, why not tell your baby about your school days? I'm sure your little listener would love to hear every word.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 完璧归赵
fields.title_en: Returning the Jade Intact to Zhao
fields.subtitle: 面对强权不屈服
fields.subtitle_en: Standing Tall Against Adversity
fields.content:
战国时期，赵王得到一块名贵的宝玉——和氏璧，被秦王知道了。秦王就派使者来对赵王说，秦国愿意用15座城池换和氏璧。赵王猜想秦王不会真的拿15座城池来交换的，很可能就是个骗局。但当时秦国势大，赵王又不敢不答应，害怕招来战争，因为赵国根本不是秦国的对手。赵王自己委决不下，跟大臣们商量也没有什么好办法。
蔺相如知道了这件事，就自告奋勇对赵王说自己可以把和氏璧送到秦国。他到时看秦王是否有诚意，有诚意就交换，没诚意一定把和氏璧完整地带回来。赵王知道蔺相如的能力，就同意了。
蔺相如来到秦国，在秦王的王宫里把和氏璧交给秦王。秦王将和氏璧拿在手里，左看右看，简直是爱不释手。他自己看完后传给大臣们看。大臣们看完后又拿到后宫给妃嫔们看。很久也没有再传回来。
蔺相如站在旁边，秦王几乎忘了他的存在，更不提交换15座城池的事，蔺相如看出用15座城池来换只是个幌子，秦王就是想把和氏璧骗到手里。可是现在和氏璧在秦王手里，必须先拿回来才有谈判的筹码。于是蔺相如走上前一步，谦恭地对秦王说道：“大王，这块和氏璧看着挺好，其实是有瑕疵的。让我指给大王看。”秦王一听信以为真，立刻叫人把和氏璧从后宫里拿出来交给蔺相如，让他指给自己看。
蔺相如拿到和氏璧后，不但没有上前，反而后退了几步，身体靠在了一根柱子上。秦王正纳闷呢，只听蔺相如正色说道：“当初大王说要拿15座城池交换和氏璧，赵国上上下下都不相信。但我想秦国是大国，老百姓还讲信义呢，秦王不会连老百姓都不如。是我说服了赵王，这样赵王才让我把和氏璧带来了。现在我看大王把和氏璧传来传去，连后宫都看过了，却只字不提交换城池的事。看来赵国臣民的担心是对的。我们不必交换了。大王如果要逼我，那我情愿把自己的脑袋与和氏璧一起撞碎在这根柱子上！”说着，蔺相如就举起和氏璧，面对着柱子要撞过去。
秦王一看这架势慌了，生怕宝玉真的被撞碎。他连忙保证说自己说的话一定算数，还叫人立刻拿来了地图，指出15个城池给蔺相如看。他假惺惺地说这就是要交换的城池。
蔺相如可不相信秦王的话，使起了缓兵之计。他对秦王说赵王送这块和氏璧来秦国的时候，斋戒了5天，举行了隆重的赠送仪式。那么秦王接受这块和氏璧也应该斋戒5天，然后举行隆重的受宝仪式才行。
秦王自然不想听蔺相如的，但和氏璧在蔺相如手上，看蔺相如态度又十分坚决，没办法也只得答应。然后把蔺相如安排到驿馆去休息。
蔺相如一到驿馆，就叫一个手下乔装打扮把和氏璧带出驿馆，让他从小道逃回赵国。
秦王斋戒完了，召见蔺相如，要他把和氏璧献出。蔺相如很淡然地说自己已经把和氏璧送回赵国了。如果秦王想要和氏璧，先把交换的城池划过去，和氏璧就会送回来。
秦王自知理亏，想攻打赵国或挟持蔺相如，但都没有合适的理由，而且现在已经弄得人尽皆知，只能把蔺相如放了。
fields.content_en:
# Peaceful Return of the Jade

A long, long time ago, in the beautiful land of Zhao, the King had a precious treasure — a glowing jade stone called the He Shi Bi. When the King of Qin heard about it, he sent a messenger to say, "We would like to trade fifteen of our finest cities for your wonderful jade."

The King of Zhao worried deeply. He knew the King of Qin was powerful, but he also suspected this might just be a trick. He had no choice but to agree, because he did not want a war. He sat with his wise ministers, trying to find a solution.

That is when a brave man named Lin Xiangru stepped forward. "Let me go," he said gently but firmly to the king. "I will take the jade to the King of Qin. If he is truly sincere, we will trade. If not, I will bring it safely back to you." The king trusted Lin Xiangru and nodded warmly.

When Lin Xiangru arrived in Qin, he was welcomed into the great palace. He handed the beautiful jade to the King of Qin, who held it close, admiring its smooth glow, turning it over and over. He passed it to his courtiers, who passed it to the ladies of the palace. Soon the jade was gone, and no one mentioned the promise of fifteen cities.

Lin Xiangru stood quietly, watching. He knew the trade was only a clever trick. But his jade was in the king's hands, so he had to act wisely. Stepping forward with gentle respect, he said, "Your Majesty, this jade is lovely, but I notice a tiny flaw in it. Let me show it to you."

The king, eager to see the flaw, called for the jade to be brought back. As soon as Lin Xiangru held it once more, he stepped back slowly and leaned against a sturdy pillar.

"Your Majesty," he said with a calm and steady voice, "when you promised fifteen cities, no one in Zhao believed you. But I thought, surely a great king keeps his word. I persuaded my king to trust you, and now I see the jade passed around for everyone to admire — yet not a single word about cities. Our fears were right. Let us end this trade. If you force me, I would rather smash my head and this precious jade together against this pillar!"

And he raised the shining jade high, ready to strike.

The king panicked! He could not bear the thought of such beauty being broken. Quickly he promised, "I will keep my word! Look, here is a map!" He called for a map and pointed to fifteen cities on it, pretending they were meant for the trade.

But Lin Xiangru was clever. "Your Majesty," he said softly, "when our king sent the jade, he fasted and prepared himself for five long days. It would only be right if you also prepared your heart for five days before receiving such a precious gift."

The king had no choice. He agreed, and Lin Xiangru was given a peaceful place to rest at the guest house.

That very night, Lin Xiangru asked one of his faithful friends to dress simply and slip away through the hidden paths, carrying the beautiful jade back to Zhao.

When the five days passed and the king called for Lin Xiangru, the brave man stood calmly before him. "Your Majesty," he said gently, "the jade is already safe back in our home country. If you wish to receive it again, please send the cities first, and we will gladly bring it back."

The king knew he had been outwitted. There was no good reason to attack or to keep the kind man. And everyone now knew what had happened. So with a soft sigh, he let Lin Xiangru go, and our brave hero returned safely home.
fields.tips: 生活中，我们经常用到“完璧归赵”这个成语。这个故事本指蔺相如将和氏璧完好地自秦国送回赵国邯郸，后来比喻把原物完好无损地归还本人。随着孕期增长，准妈妈对分娩的恐惧会有所增加，可以借鉴蔺相如这种能豁出去的勇气。不妨想想，怀孕、生育本是平常且自然的事情，抱着爱咋地咋地的心态，恐惧就会少一些。
fields.tips_en: We often use the idiom 'returning the jade intact to Zhao' in everyday life. The story tells of Lin Xiangru's courage in bringing the precious Hebi jade safely back from the powerful state of Qin to his homeland, Zhao. As your pregnancy grows, it's natural to feel a bit more fearful about delivery. Drawing inspiration from Lin Xiangru's fearless bravery can help. Remember — pregnancy and childbirth are wonderfully natural parts of life. Embracing an easygoing attitude can ease those worries and fill your heart with calm confidence.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 诚实的晏殊
fields.subtitle: 好的人品最为人乐道
fields.subtitle_en: A Good Character Is a Treasure
fields.content:
晏殊是北宋著名的文学家，他不但词写得好，而且善于举荐人才。欧阳修和范仲淹皆出其门下。不过，晏殊最为人乐道的是他的诚实。
晏殊在14岁时被推荐给朝廷。恰逢朝廷举办科考，宋真宗就让晏殊也一同考试。晏殊拿到试题后，即刻跟皇帝禀报说自己10天前做过这样的题目，要求换一个。这样的诚实很少见，皇帝非常喜欢。自然，晏殊的才华也是不可小觑的，14岁的他做起试题来从容不迫，很快就写完了。
后来，晏殊入朝当了官，依然很诚实。当时朝臣士大夫们都喜欢游乐宴会，但晏殊因为家里比较穷，从不参加这些聚会，总是在家里和兄弟们读书学习。宋真宗要给太子选一个老师，就选中了晏殊。大臣们不理解，都问为什么选晏殊。皇帝说是因为晏殊从不参加这些游乐宴会，他是个谨慎、忠厚之人，所以选晏殊。没想到晏殊上任后，却对皇上直言说自己其实也喜欢聚会游乐，只是因为家里穷才不去，并非自己多么高尚。这样一来，宋真宗更喜欢他了，一直委以重任。到了宋仁宗登基后，晏殊最后做了宰相。
fields.content_en:
Title: Honest Yan Shu

Yan Shu was a famous writer during the Northern Song Dynasty. He wrote beautiful poems and was also very good at recommending talented people. Both Ouyang Xiu and Fan Zhongyan learned from him. But what people liked to talk about most was his honesty.

When Yan Shu was only fourteen years old, he was recommended to the court. Right then, the emperor was holding an exam, and Emperor Zhenzong invited young Yan Shu to take it too. As soon as Yan Shu received the test questions, he told the emperor something very special — he said he had practiced those exact questions ten days ago and asked if he could have different ones. Such honesty was very rare, and the emperor loved it. Of course, Yan Shu was also very clever. At just fourteen, he worked calmly and finished his test quickly.

Later, Yan Shu became an official in the court, and he stayed honest throughout his life. Back then, most officials loved going to parties and feasts. But because Yan Shu's family was not rich, he never went. Instead, he stayed home and studied with his brothers. When Emperor Zhenzong needed to pick a teacher for the crown prince, he chose Yan Shu. The other ministers were confused and asked why. The emperor explained that Yan Shu never went to那些 parties and feasts — he was careful and kindhearted, so he was the perfect choice. But when Yan Shu started his new job, he spoke truthfully to the emperor and said he actually did enjoy parties and fun times. It was only because his family did not have enough money that he stayed home. He was not as perfect as everyone thought. Hearing this, the emperor liked him even more and trusted him with important work. Years later, when Emperor Renzong became emperor, Yan Shu grew up to be the prime minister — the most important minister in all the land.
fields.tips: 想要腹中的胎宝宝成长为一个具有诚实好人品的人，准妈妈在生活中要以身作则，不仅对人要诚实，对自己也要诚实。准妈妈在生活中如果面临问题，一定要积极面对，跟周围的人交流，获得精神支持，不要强撑着说自己没事，以免酿成大问题。
fields.tips_en: If you wish for your little one to grow into an honest and kind-hearted soul, the journey begins with you, dear mama. Lead by example — be truthful with others and true to yourself. When challenges arise, don't carry them alone. Open up to those around you and let their support brighten your days.
