Never pretend everything is fine when it isn't; asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness. Your baby is already learning from your gentle, honest heart.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 少年难乾隆
fields.title_en: The Clever Youth Who Challenged the Emperor
fields.subtitle: 太熟悉反而容易忽视
fields.subtitle_en: Familiar Eyes Sometimes Miss What Matters
fields.content:
乾隆皇帝曾多次下江南，有一次来到无锡。这一天，他穿着便服，独自走进一条小巷子。走着走着，他发现一堵墙上写着“此路不通”四个字，字的下面站着一个孩子，呆呆地看着这四个字。四个字有什么好看的，这么入神。乾隆觉得很奇怪，就问孩子：“墙上的字你都认识吗？”孩子听到询问，恭恭敬敬地回答道：“老伯，我认识后面三个字是‘路不通’，第一个字不认识。老伯认识吗？”乾隆听了觉得好笑，这么常用的一个字反倒不认识，就问孩子：“你读了几年书？都读过什么书啊？”孩子回答道：“我跟着祖父认字，祖父教我读完了《论语》，里面没有这个字。”乾隆更觉得奇怪了，《论语》里怎么会没有这个字呢。就对孩子说：“你大概是忘记了。《论语》我也读过。这个字起码有几百个。”孩子一听，急了：“这位老伯，《论语》里确实没有这个字。你说有，你倒说说在哪一句里有？”乾隆想了想，一时真没想出来，就讪讪地走开了。
乾隆回到京城，对被一个孩子难住这件事一直耿耿于怀。有一天上朝，看着下面文武百官，突然又想了起来。于是他就问群臣是否都读过《论语》。群臣都回答读过。乾隆就问《论语》里有多少个“此”字。大臣们议论起来，有的说有几百个，有的说上千个，没有定论。最后乾隆就命令把《论语》拿上来，大家数一数。《论语》拿上来了，大家一行一行、一页一页找，最后竟一个都没有找出来。原来《论语》里所有需要用“此”字的地方，都是用“斯”表示的。这下乾隆终于相信了，无锡那个小孩原来说的是真的。最熟悉的东西反而并不了解。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Young Boy Who Outsmarted Qianlong

Emperor Qianlong visited the south of China many times. One day he came to Wuxi. Dressed in simple clothes, he walked alone down a narrow lane. Walking along, he noticed four characters written on a wall: "This road does not lead anywhere." Standing beneath the characters was a small child, staring at them with wide eyes. What was there to stare at so intently? Qianlong found it strange and asked the child, "Do you know all the characters on the wall?" The child answered politely, "Sir, I know the last three — 'road does not lead anywhere.' But I don't know the first one. Do you know it, sir?" Qianlong chuckled. A word so common and yet the child didn't know it. "How many years have you studied?" he asked. "What books have you read?" The child replied, "I learned from my grandfather. He taught me through the Analects, but that character isn't in it." Qianlong was even more puzzled now. How could such a common character be missing from the Analects? "You must have forgotten," he said. "I've read the Analects too. That character appears at least a hundred times." The child grew anxious. "Sir, it truly isn't in the Analects. If you say it is, then tell me where exactly!" Qianlong thought hard but couldn't recall a single place. Embarrassed, he walked away.

Back in the capital, Qianlong couldn't shake the feeling of being bested by a child. One morning during court, as he looked down at his civil and military officials, the memory struck him again. He asked all his ministers whether they had read the Analects. They all replied yes. Then he asked how many times the character "ci" appeared in the Analects. The ministers began to discuss it. Some said a hundred, others said a thousand — no one could agree. Finally, Qianlong ordered that a copy of the Analects be brought forward so they could count together. When the book arrived, everyone searched line by line and page by page. And not a single one could they find. It turned out that whenever the Analects needed the character "ci," it used "si" instead. That's when Qianlong finally understood. The little boy in Wuxi had been telling the truth all along. Sometimes the things we think we know best are the very things we understand the least.
fields.tips: 越熟悉越容易忽视，在家庭生活中也是如此，亲人之间因为太过熟悉彼此了，对他们的需求就不太在乎了，往往不能用心去对待。建议准妈妈和准爸爸一起检讨检讨，什么时候曾经感觉到自己对对方忽视了，下决心去改。这样家庭气氛会更融洽，对胎宝宝好处多多。
fields.tips_en: The closer we are to someone, the easier it is to overlook their needs — even the ones we hold dearest. In family life, this happens all too often. Dear mama and papa-to-be, why not take a tender moment together to reflect on times when you may have taken each other for granted? A simple promise to pay closer attention and cherish one another can fill your home with warmth and love. And what a beautiful, loving world you'll be creating for your little one!
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 杞人忧天
fields.title_en: The Man Who Worried About the Sky
fields.subtitle: 要避免不必要的担心
fields.subtitle_en: Let Go of Unnecessary Fears
fields.content:
古代杞国有个人本来好好的，突然有一天不知道怎么了，开始担心天会塌、地会陷，到时候自己就没地方待了。他愁得睡不着、吃不下，惶惶不可终日。
不过，幸好，这个人的朋友担心他这样过度焦虑会受不了，就过来劝解他。告诉他说：“天是积聚的气体，是漂浮着的，根本不会塌下来的。”
杞国人不相信，他说，如果天是气体，那星星、月亮、太阳怎么能挂在天上呢？朋友又解释说：“星星、月亮、太阳也是气体，只不过是会发光而已，即使掉下来也不会有多大危害。”
杞国人还是不放心，又问地陷了怎么办。朋友解释说地是由土堆积而成，所有的地方都实实在在地填满了土，没有一处是空的。人整天都在地上走都没事，所以根本不用担心地陷落。
这样一来，这个杞国人终于放心了，不再整天焦虑不安了。他的朋友也安心了。
fields.content_en:
# The Man Who Worried Too Much

Once upon a time, in the old land of Qi, there was a kind man who was living a perfectly happy life. But one day, without any reason at all, he began to worry that the sky might fall down and the ground might open up, leaving him with nowhere to go. He worried so much that he couldn't sleep or eat, and he was afraid all day long.

But luckily, his friend grew worried about him. He thought, "My friend is worrying too much — he can't keep this up!" So he came over to gently talk to him. He said, "The sky is just made of soft, floating gas. It will never, ever fall down."

The man from Qi wasn't convinced. He asked, "But if the sky is just gas, how can the stars, the moon, and the sun hang up there?" His friend explained gently, "The stars, the moon, and the sun are also made of gas. They just glow and shine. And even if they did fall, they wouldn't hurt us at all."

Still feeling uneasy, the man from Qi asked about the ground below. His friend smiled and said, "The earth is made of soil and earth packed tightly together. Everywhere you look, the ground is solid and full — there aren't any empty spaces underneath. You walk on it every single day and you're perfectly safe. So there is no need to worry about the ground giving way."

At last, the man from Qi felt at peace. The heavy worry lifted from his heart, and he was able to rest easy once again. And his friend was relieved, too.
fields.tips: 杞人忧天，主要是对天和地的实质不了解，所以产生了不必要的担心。每个准妈妈怀孕期间总会有杞人忧天的一面，担心的问题奇奇怪怪、林林总总。这主要是因为不了解、不懂而造成的。如果你有恐惧、忧虑，可以多查查资料或者询问一下过来人。相信了解后，恐惧就自然消除了。
fields.tips_en: The tale of the man from Qi who worried endlessly about the sky falling teaches us a gentle lesson: much of our anxiety comes from simply not knowing enough. Every expectant mother experiences moments of worry — strange, endless questions filling her mind. The wonderful thing is that knowledge is a powerful comfort. Don't hesitate to look things up or chat with mothers who have walked this beautiful path before you. Understanding brings peace, and a peaceful mama makes a happy baby.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 沉鱼落雁，闭月羞花
fields.title_en: Beauty That Makes Fish Sink and Birds Fall — The Quintessence of Language
fields.subtitle: 品味语言之极致形容
fields.subtitle_en: Savoring the Finest Descriptions
fields.content:
沉鱼、落雁、闭月、羞花是四个形容词，形容美女之美，连动物、植物和月亮都能感知。沉鱼说的是西施，落雁说的是昭君，闭月说的是貂蝉，羞花说的是杨贵妃。
西施是春秋时期越国的美女，她天生丽质，小时候常常到河边浣纱。每次西施来到溪边，溪水里的鱼就看不到了。因为它们看到西施的美貌以后，就都出神地看着她，忘记摇尾巴游水了，渐渐地就沉到水底下去了。
昭君是汉朝的美女，被封为公主后到匈奴和亲。传说昭君在去匈奴的路上，一路上都弹奏着一把琵琶。声调苍凉悲怆，闻者动容。这天，她来到匈奴和汉朝的边境时，一队大雁听到了琵琶声，低头一看，看到了王昭君。就这一眼，王昭君的美貌让大雁彻底折服。大雁忘记扇动翅膀了，一头栽了下来。
貂蝉是东汉时的人物，在《三国演义》里被描述成王允的义女。一天晚上，貂蝉在花园里设下香案祭拜月亮，祈祷上天保佑王允。正在貂蝉下拜之时，一片白云轻轻飘过，将皎洁的月亮遮住了。这个情景被王允看到了，于是他到处吹嘘说自己女儿漂亮，连月亮看到她的美貌都要躲起来。貂蝉“闭月”的说法就传开了。
杨贵妃是唐玄宗的宠妃，华清池是唐玄宗的行宫。唐玄宗经常带杨贵妃到华清池泡温泉。有一次，杨贵妃泡完温泉，披上衣服走出水池。池边摆着一盆鲜花，杨贵妃就看了一眼，摸了一摸，没想到花儿立刻收起花瓣，低垂了下去，绿叶也卷了起来。周围伺候的人就说这是花儿看到出浴的杨贵妃实在太美了，自觉惭愧，所以低下了头。因此，杨贵妃就有了“羞花”的美名。
知识
lian
接
沉鱼、落雁、闭月、羞花四个词简简单单就把四位美女的美形容到了极致，语言就有这样的妙处。这里的动词都是使动用法，在现代汉语里就是使鱼沉、使雁落、使月闭、使花羞。
fields.content_en:
# The Fish Sank, the Geese Fell, the Moon Hid, the Flowers Were Shy

The Fish Sank, the Geese Fell, the Moon Hid, and the Flowers Were Shy are four expressions used to describe the beauty of a wonderful woman—so beautiful that even animals, plants, and the moon can feel her charm. "The Fish Sank" tells the story of Xi Shi. "The Geese Fell" tells the story of Zhao Jun. "The Moon Hid" tells the story of Diao Chan. "The Flowers Were Shy" tells the story of Yang Guifei.

Xi Shi was a beautiful woman from the state of Yue during the Spring and Autumn period. She was naturally lovely, and when she was little, she often went to the river to wash silk. Every time Xi Shi came to the stream, the fish in the water would disappear. When they saw how beautiful she was, they stared at her in a daze, forgetting to wag their tails and swim. Slowly, they sank to the bottom of the water.

Zhao Jun was a beautiful woman from the Han dynasty. After she was given the title of princess, she traveled to the Xiongnu lands to form an alliance through marriage. It is said that on her journey, Zhao Jun played her pipa all the way along the road. The music was deep and moving, and everyone who heard it was touched. One day, when she reached the border between the Xiongnu and the Han dynasty, a flock of wild geese heard the sound of her pipa. They looked down and saw Wang Zhao Jun. Just that one glance was enough—the geese were completely captivated by her beauty. They forgot to flap their wings and fell right out of the sky.

Diao Chan was a person from the Eastern Han dynasty and is described in *Romance of the Three Kingdoms* as the adopted daughter of Wang Yun. One night, Diao Chan set up an incense altar in the garden to pray to the moon, asking heaven to protect Wang Yun. Just as she was bowing down, a soft white cloud drifted by and covered the bright moon. Wang Yun saw this scene, so he went around boasting that his daughter was so beautiful that even the moon hid itself when it saw her. And so, the story of Diao Chan and "the Moon Hiding" spread far and wide.

Yang Guifei was the beloved concubine of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang. Huaqing Pool was the emperor's retreat, and he often brought Yang Guifei there to soak in the hot springs. One day, after finishing her bath, Yang Guifei wrapped herself in a robe and stepped out of the pool. Beside the pool sat a pot of beautiful flowers. Yang Guifei glanced at them and gently touched them, but no sooner had she done so than the flowers immediately closed their petals and drooped down, and even their green leaves curled up. The servants standing nearby said that the flowers were so overwhelmed by the beauty of Yang Guifei rising from the water that they felt ashamed and hung their heads in shame. And so, Yang Guifei earned the wonderful name of "the Flowers Were Shy."

**Knowledge Corner**

The four phrases—The Fish Sank, the Geese Fell, the Moon Hid, and the Flowers Were Shy—simply and perfectly capture the beauty of these four wonderful women. This is the magic of language. In these expressions, the verbs are used in a special way that makes the fish sink, the geese fall, the moon hide, and the flowers feel shy.
fields.tips: 准妈妈现在看书不求量，完全可以慢一点儿，仔细体会每一个字、词的精妙之处，琢磨下词与词之间有什么细微差别等，给胎宝宝一些词汇方面的刺激。
fields.tips_en: Now is not the time to rush through books — take your time, quietly relishing every word and phrase. Notice the subtle differences between similar expressions and share those refined sounds with your baby, gently stimulating their developing mind.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 铁杵磨针
fields.title_en: Grinding an Iron Rod into a Needle
fields.subtitle: 坚持终有突破
fields.subtitle_en: Perseverance Leads to Breakthroughs
fields.content:
据说大诗人李白小时候并不喜欢读书，觉得学习每天都是一个样子，没意思，所以就经常逃学，到处去闲逛。
这一天，李白又逃学了。他跑到城外去玩，上树掏掏鸟窝，下河摸摸鱼。他觉得这可比读书痛快多了。
李白边走边玩，来到山下小河边，见到一个满头白发的老婆婆，正在石头上磨一根棍子般的铁杵。李白觉得很奇怪，反正没事，他就过去跟老婆婆攀谈。李白问老婆婆：“老婆婆，你磨这个铁棍干什么呢？”老婆婆回答道：“我要把这个铁棍磨成一根绣花针。”李白很惊讶。他不敢相信，就问：“是缝衣服的绣花针吗？”老婆婆点点头。李白觉得这根本是不可能成功的。但是老婆婆说滴水能够穿石，愚公能够移山，铁杵磨成针那自然也是可行的。李白又想到老婆婆年纪这么大了，即使铁棍真的可以磨成针，但老婆婆恐怕也等不到那一天了。但是老婆婆说她会多用些功夫的，争取在有生之年磨成针，即使没成功也不遗憾了。
李白听了深受震动。他回去之后，再没有逃过学，学习特别用功，终于成了誉满古今的诗仙。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Iron Pestle Becomes a Needle

It is said that when the great poet Li Bai was a little boy, he did not enjoy studying. He felt that learning was always the same every day and rather boring, so he often skipped school and went wandering instead.

One day, Li Bai skipped school again. He ran outside the city to play, climbing trees to peek into bird nests and wading into the river to摸 fish. He thought this was much more fun than studying.

Walking and playing along the way, Li Bai came to a small river at the foot of a hill. There he saw an old grandmother with white hair, grinding an iron pestle on a stone. Li Bai found this very strange. Since he had nothing else to do, he walked over and struck up a conversation with her. "Grandmother," he asked, "what are you grinding that iron rod for?" She replied, "I am going to grind this iron rod into an embroidery needle." Li Bai was very surprised. He could hardly believe it and asked, "A needle for sewing clothes?" The grandmother nodded. Li Bai thought it was simply impossible. But the grandmother said that dripping water can wear through stone, and that the foolish old man in the story had moved mountains. So of course, grinding an iron pestle into a needle was possible too. Li Bai then thought that the grandmother was so old that even if the iron rod could really be ground into a needle, she probably would not live to see the day. But she said she would work harder and do her best to finish it in her lifetime, and even if she didn't succeed, she would have no regrets.

Li Bai was deeply moved by what he heard. When he went back, he never skipped school again. He studied very hard and eventually became known as the immortal poet throughout all of history.
fields.tips: 铁杵磨针、愚公移山等故事并不是说让我们在做一件事情的时候认死理儿，而是告诉我们一个道理：任何事情只要你坚持不懈去做，总是会有突破的。但是并不是说每一件事情只要坚持就会成功。准妈妈可以对胎宝宝说一下把铁杵磨成针的可行性等，锻炼自己多角度思考问题的能力。
fields.tips_en: The tales of grinding an iron rod into a needle and the old man moving mountains teach us that perseverance can lead to breakthroughs in anything we undertake. Of course, not everything succeeds no matter how long we try — but persistence opens doors. You might share with your baby why turning a rod into a needle, though difficult, is a beautiful metaphor for love and dedication.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 画蛇添足
fields.title_en: Drawing a Snake and Adding Feet
fields.subtitle: 聪明反被聪明误
fields.subtitle_en: A Cleverness That Backfires
fields.content:
楚国有一个大人物在家中祭祀，很多门客都主动过来帮忙。祭祀完毕后，这个大人物就把一壶祭祀用的酒赏给门客们喝。门客太多，大家商量说：“几个人喝这壶酒，谁也喝不好，一个人喝就比较好，还能有所剩余。不如就一个人喝。”接下来的问题是这壶酒该给谁喝呢？大家又商量：“我们每人在地上画一条蛇，谁先画好，谁就喝这壶酒。”
接下来，大家开始聚精会神地用木棍在地上画蛇。有个人画技一直都是比较出众的，画得又快又好。他心想这壶酒肯定是自己的了。果然他很快就画好了蛇。他把酒壶拿了起来，面带笑容地看着众位还在画蛇的人。他想：“他们都还没有画完，不如我给蛇再加上4只脚吧。”想到这，他就一手拿酒壶，一手拿着木棍给蛇画脚。他还没有画完脚，另一个人已经把蛇画完了。刚画完的人笑嘻嘻地把他手上的酒夺过去，端起来喝了一口，说：“蛇本来没有脚，你怎么能给它画脚呢？”
给蛇画脚，本想更完善，却弄巧成拙，蛇不像蛇，而那壶酒也最终失掉了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Man Who Drew Feet on a Snake

Once upon a time, in the state of Chu, a distinguished man held a ceremony at his home. Many guests came to help. When the ceremony was over, he gave a pot of special wine to share among them.

But there were so many people, they said, "If we all try to drink from one pot, no one gets a proper sip. But if one person drinks it alone, they'll enjoy it more—and there might even be some left over. Let's just let one person have it." Then they wondered, "Who should get the wine?" So they agreed: "Let each of us draw a snake on the ground with a stick. Whoever finishes first gets to drink!"

They all bent down and began drawing carefully with their sticks. One man was much better at drawing than the rest, and he worked quickly and neatly. He thought, "This pot of wine is surely mine!" And soon, he had finished his snake. He picked up the pot and smiled at everyone else, who were still hard at work. Then he thought, "They haven't finished yet. I could add four feet to my snake—it will make it even better!" So, holding the wine pot in one hand, he used his stick to draw legs on the snake.

But before he could finish, another man had already completed his snake. He snatched the pot away, took a drink, and said with a smile, "Snakes don't have feet. How could you add feet to a snake?"

In the end, the man had tried to make things better, but instead made a mess of it. His snake no longer looked like a snake, and he lost the wine altogether.
fields.tips: 准妈妈可以给胎宝宝看看蛇的图片，讲讲蛇的生活习性和行动的特点，告诉胎宝宝画蛇添足为什么不对。准妈妈还可以画画蛇，给胎宝宝更强的刺激。
fields.tips_en: Show your baby a picture of a snake and tell them about its graceful movements and natural habits. Explain why adding feet to a snake only makes the drawing wrong — sometimes, extra touches spoil what is already perfect. You could even draw a beautiful snake together, giving your baby vibrant colors and gentle strokes.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 井底之蛙
fields.title_en: The Frog at the Bottom of the Well
fields.subtitle: 成长环境决定眼界
fields.subtitle_en: Our World Shapes Our Horizons
fields.content:
有一只青蛙住在一口枯井里，它太满意自己生活的这一方天地了，只要有机会，就会跟人吹嘘一番。
这天，青蛙蹲在井台上正闲得无聊，突然看见不远处有只大海龟在散步，就赶紧扯开嗓门招呼大海龟：“喂，海龟兄，请到这边来吧。”海龟听到招呼，就慢慢走过来了。刚到枯井边，青蛙显摆的冲动就来了。它对大海龟说：“海龟兄，你看这口井，这是我家。我的这个家简直是天堂，我想你从来都没见过这样宽敞的住所吧。今天算你运气好，我就领你参观一下吧。”
海龟探头看了一下井里，发现井底只有长满绿苔的浅浅一点儿泥水，还散发着阵阵臭气。它可不想进去参观，就把头缩了回来。但是青蛙仍然兴致勃勃地说：“我的这个地方真是舒服极了。傍晚我跳到井台上来乘凉，夜里就钻在井壁的窟窿里睡觉，热了就浸在水里，还能跳到泥里，打个滚运动运动。总之一切都很好，那些小虫子、螃蟹、蝌蚪什么的，没有一个能跟我比。”海龟脾气好，安静地听着。青蛙越说越得意，再次邀请海龟到它的家里参观，海龟不好意思推辞，就打算进去看看。可是它左腿还没全伸入井口呢，右腿就被井栏卡住了，只得作罢。海龟慢慢退出井栏。青蛙神气活现地表示遗憾：“真是遗憾，你找不到比这更好的地方了。”海龟看看青蛙，有点儿怜悯地问道：“你听说过大海没有？”青蛙摇摇头。海龟继续说：“大海无边无际，非常大，用千里不足以形容它的辽阔，用万丈也不足以表明它的深度。传说在4000多年前，大禹的时代，十年九涝海水都没有加深；后来到了商汤的时代，十年九旱，海水也没有减少。青蛙老弟，我就生活在大海中。比起你这一眼枯井，一坑死水来，你说哪个天地更广阔，哪个更让人快乐呢？”青蛙听得瞠目结舌。海龟走了，它还鼓着眼睛，半天回不过神来。它想：大海龟会不会是骗它呢？
fields.content_en:
# The Frog at the Bottom of the Well

There was once a frog who lived in a dried-up old well. It was so happy with its little corner of the world that whenever it got the chance, it would proudly boast to anyone who would listen.

One day, while the frog was lounging lazily on the edge of the well, suddenly it spotted a sea turtle strolling nearby. The frog quickly called out in a loud voice, "Hey, Mr. Turtle! Come over here!" Hearing the call, the turtle slowly made his way over. As soon as he reached the well, the frog's urge to show off kicked in. He said to the turtle, "Mr. Turtle, look at this well—it's my home! My little home is simply wonderful. I bet you've never seen such a spacious house in your life. You're very lucky today—I'll give you a little tour!"

The turtle poked his head down into the well and saw only a shallow puddle of muddy water covered in green moss, carrying a faint unpleasant smell. He certainly had no desire to go in, so he pulled his head back. But the frog went on excitedly, saying, "My little place here is truly wonderful. In the evening, I hop up to the edge of the well to enjoy the cool breeze. At night, I curl up in a little hole in the wall and sleep soundly. When it gets hot, I splash around in the water, or I roll around in the mud for a good exercise. Everything here is just perfect. None of those little bugs, crabs, or tadpoles can compare to me!" The turtle, being patient and gentle, listened quietly. The more the frog talked, the prouder he became. He invited the turtle again to come visit his home. Not wanting to be rude, the turtle agreed and tried to step inside. But before his left leg was even fully through the opening, his right leg got stuck on the well rim, so he had to give up. Slowly backing away from the well, the turtle watched as the frog said with a regretful air, "What a shame! You'll never find a better place than this."

The turtle looked at the frog and asked gently with a touch of pity, "Have you ever heard of the sea?" The frog shook his head. The turtle continued, "The sea stretches on endlessly, so vast that a thousand miles cannot describe its width, and ten thousand fathoms cannot measure its depth. Long ago, during the time of the great ruler Yu, it rained heavily for nine years out of every ten, yet the sea never rose higher. Later, during the reign of King Tang, there were droughts nine years out of every ten, yet the sea never shrank. Little frog brother, I myself live by the sea. Compared to your tiny dried-up well and stagnant pool, which world do you think is vaster? Which one brings more joy?" The frog's eyes widened in amazement. After the turtle left, the frog sat there with his eyes still bulging, completely speechless. He thought to himself: Could the sea turtle be trying to fool me?
fields.tips: 青蛙因为一直生活在井底，从没有看到过井外的世界，所以见识有限。如今怀孕了，有条件的准妈妈可以多出去见识见识，在身体舒服的时候出去旅游、去听音乐会、去欣赏美术展览……让自己的业余时间变得丰富多彩。这也是对胎宝宝进行最好的美育胎教。
fields.tips_en: The frog who lived all its life inside a well knew only a small circle of sky and never dreamed of the vast world beyond. Now that you are expecting, if you feel well, let yourself wander — travel to new places, listen to live music, visit art exhibitions. Let your days be rich and colorful; this is the most beautiful gift of aesthetic education you can offer your baby.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 东郭先生与狼
fields.subtitle: 同情心不可滥施
fields.subtitle_en: Compassion Must Be Wisely Shared
fields.content:
从前有一位书生叫东郭先生，一天他要到“中山国”去谋求官职。他牵着毛驴，毛驴驮着袋子，袋子里装着书简，在路上走了好几天了。这天他走到一片树林的边上，遇到两条岔路，迷路了。东郭先生站在岔路口东张西望，远远地看见有一处烟尘滚滚，好像是有大队人马在活动。这是晋国大夫赵简子在打猎。他们在追捕一只已经被他们射中的狼。
东郭先生还在犹豫到底走哪边，这只被赵简子射中的狼窜了出来。那只狼可怜兮兮地恳求东郭先生：“他们正在追我，请让我钻到你的袋子里躲一躲吧。只要我能活下来，以后一定会报答您的。”东郭先生虽然害怕把狼藏起来，得罪打猎的那群权贵，但是他有兼爱思想，不能见死不救。于是，他把书简都拿出来，把口袋腾空，要把狼装进去。装狼的时候，东郭先生总担心狼会不舒服，来来回回装了三次都没有成功。看着远处烟尘越来越近，狼着急了，就把自己蜷成一团，建议东郭先生把它四只脚捆住再往袋子里装。这一次非常顺利就装进去了。东郭先生刚把书简塞到袋子里，放到毛驴背上，赵简子他们就过来了。赵简子跟东郭先生打听狼的行踪，但是东郭先生什么也没说。赵简子很生气，愤怒地斩断了车辕。他威胁说谁敢知情不报，下场就跟车辕一样，但东郭先生仍然不肯说出狼的下落，赵简子只得走了。
当赵简子他们远去之后，装在口袋里的狼说：“多谢先生救命，现在可以放我出来了。请受我一拜吧。”东郭先生就把狼放出来了。可是狼一出口袋，态度就变了，它对东郭先生说：“我饿了，刚才你已经救我一命，就让我吃了你，再救我一次，救人救到底吧。”说着就张牙舞爪地向东郭先生扑了过去。东郭先生急忙躲开，绕着毛驴和狼兜起了圈子。已经转了好多圈了，东郭先生想这样下去可不是个办法。眼看太阳就要下山，一旦狼群出来，那就很难幸免了。于是他提议说：“我们这样办吧，去问3个人。如果3个人都说你应该吃我，那我也不躲，就给你吃了。如果3个人都说你不应该吃我，那你就放我走。”狼同意了。东郭先生和狼首先去问杏树。杏树说它对主人恩德不小，老了还要被他们卖到木匠铺去。东郭先生对狼恩德不重，应该被狼吃。东郭先生和狼又去问老牛，老牛说自己对主人恩德很重，到老了，还要被杀了卖肉。东郭先生对狼恩德不重，也应该被狼吃。东郭先生和狼最后问的是一个老人家。老人说狼不应该吃东郭先生，毕竟东郭先生对它有救命之恩。但狼狡辩说东郭先生救它的时候，把它的脚捆疼了，书简塞进去把它的身子也压麻了，还差点儿让它喘不过气来，并不是真的救它，所以一定要吃掉东郭先生。老人听完后，质疑说：“那么小的口袋能把你装进去，还又把书简塞进去，我不太相信。你如果能再让东郭先生把你装进去，我就能看到他是否会把你的脚捆疼，身子压麻了，给你做证，让你吃他。你说行吗？”狼一听就再次蜷成一团，让东郭先生把他捆上，装进了麻袋。狼刚进麻袋，老人迅速就把袋口扎紧了，和东郭先生一起把狼打死了。
fields.content_en:
**Mr. Dongguo and the Wolf**

Once upon a time, there was a kind scholar named Mr. Dongguo. One day, he set off on a journey to the State of Zhongshan in search of a government position. He led a donkey carrying a large sack filled with bamboo scrolls, and they walked for many days along the dusty road. One day, as he reached the edge of a forest, he came to a fork in the path and found himself lost. Mr. Dongguo stood at the crossroads, looking left and right. In the distance, he saw a great cloud of dust and smoke rising into the air — it seemed as though a large group of people was moving nearby. It was Zhao Jianzi, a nobleman of the Jin State, out hunting. His men were chasing a wolf that had already been wounded by an arrow.

While Mr. Dongguo was still deciding which path to take, the wounded wolf darted out from the woods. The poor wolf begged Mr. Dongguo in a trembling voice, "They are chasing me. Please let me hide in your sack. If you save my life, I will never forget your kindness and will repay you one day." Though Mr. Dongguo was afraid of angering the powerful hunters by hiding the wolf, his generous heart could not bear to leave the creature to die. So he took the scrolls out of the sack, emptied it, and tried to stuff the wolf inside. But the wolf was quite large, and no matter how Mr. Dongguo tried, he could not fit it in — he tried three times! Seeing the dust growing closer, the anxious wolf suggested that Mr. Dongguo tie its four legs together first, and then push it into the bag. This time, it worked, and the wolf was safely tucked inside. Just as Mr. Dongguo replaced the scrolls and placed the sack on his donkey, Zhao Jianzi and his hunters arrived. They asked Mr. Dongguo if he had seen a wolf, but he said nothing. Furious, Zhao Jianzi struck the pole of his carriage in anger. He warned that anyone who refused to speak would suffer the same fate — yet Mr. Dongguo still would not betray the wolf, and so Zhao Jianzi finally rode away.

Only after the hunters had disappeared far into the distance did the wolf speak from inside the sack: "Thank you, kind sir, for saving my life. May I come out now? Please let me bow to you in gratitude." Mr. Dongguo untied the sack and set the wolf free. But the moment the wolf stepped out, its attitude changed completely. It said cruelly to Mr. Dongguo, "I am so hungry. You have already saved my life once — now let me eat you and save you a second time. A true rescue should be carried through to the very end."说着就张牙舞爪地向东郭先生扑了过去。Mr. Dongguo quickly dodged aside, and the two of them went around and around the donkey and the wolf in circles. They had gone round and round many times when Mr. Dongguo realized this would not solve anything. The sun was beginning to set, and soon other wolves might come — he would surely be in grave danger. So he proposed, "Let us ask three people, and if all three say you should eat me, then I will not resist and will let you do so. But if all three say you should not eat me, then you must let me go." The wolf agreed.

First, Mr. Dongguo and the wolf asked a tree — an old apricot tree. The tree sighed and said, "I have been very useful to my master, shading his home and bearing sweet fruit for years. Yet when I grew old, he sold me to a carpenter. Since I was treated so poorly despite all I had given, and since Mr. Dongguo has done far less for me than I did for my master, it seems fair that you should eat him." Mr. Dongguo and the wolf then asked an old ox. The ox said sadly, "I worked hard for my owner all my life, plowing the fields from dawn until dusk. And yet when I grew too old to work, he had me slaughtered and sold for meat. If someone who has done so much can be treated this way, then Mr. Dongguo, who has given you so little, should certainly be eaten by you."

Finally, they asked an old man. The kind elder said the wolf should not eat Mr. Dongguo, for the scholar had clearly saved the wolf's life. But the clever wolf argued back, "He tied my legs so tightly that they were in pain! He stuffed heavy scrolls against my body until I could hardly breathe. He did not truly save me — he nearly harmed me instead! Therefore, I must eat him." Hearing this, the old man frowned and said, "I do not believe that a small sack could hold someone as large as you, nor the heavy scrolls as well. If you can fit yourself back into the sack so I may see it with my own eyes, then I will believe your story and witness that Mr. Dongguo did you wrong."

The wolf, eager once more, curled itself into a tight ball and allowed Mr. Dongguo to tie its legs and pack it back into the sack. The moment the wolf was inside, the old man swiftly tied the sack shut, and together with Mr. Dongguo, he struck the wicked wolf down. And so the kind but foolish scholar learned an important lesson — that not everyone who receives your help will remember your kindness.
fields.tips: 善良固然没有错，但是也要看对象，对本性凶残的对象，滥施同情反而害了自己。准妈妈在读这个故事的时候，可以跟准爸爸进行角色扮演，让故事画面更生动。
fields.tips_en: Kindness is a beautiful thing, but it should be given wisely — even to those who do not deserve it. Read this tale together and perhaps act it out with your partner, bringing the characters to life with warm voices. The story whispers a gentle lesson that even little ears can sense.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 狐假虎威
fields.title_en: The Fox Who Borrowed the Tiger's Might
fields.subtitle: 正确认识自己的价值
fields.subtitle_en: Understanding Your True Worth
fields.content:
战国时期，当楚国最强盛的时候，楚宣王询问北方各国的人后得知，他们都特别惧怕楚国的大将昭奚恤。他觉得很奇怪，就问朝中众大臣是怎么回事。一名叫江乙的大臣便跟他讲了个故事。这个故事就是《狐假虎威》。
有一只老虎住在一个山洞里。有一天老虎肚子饿了，便跑到外面去找食物。它走到一片茂密的树林里，发现了一只正在散步的狐狸。老虎一跃身扑过去，不费吹灰之力把狐狸擒住了。老虎兴奋地张开嘴就要把狐狸吃掉，却突然听到狐狸说话了。狐狸说：“你不能吃我，天帝已经命我为王中之王，命我管理百兽。你吃了我，天帝会严厉地惩罚你！”老虎听了狐狸的话，将信将疑。但它仔细观察，看狐狸一副镇定、傲慢的样子，又不像装出来的，就不敢造次了。狐狸一看老虎被唬住了，心想打铁还需趁热。于是它摆出更加嚣张的架势，盛气凌人地用爪子指着老虎的鼻子说：“怎么？你不相信我说的话？好，就让你见识见识，你跟在我后面走。我们出去，看看百兽见了我是不是都要回避？”老虎于是就跟着狐狸在树林里溜达开来。
狐狸大摇大摆地在前面走，到了树林里的一个小溪边。这里聚集了不少野兽，它们看到狐狸一副耀武扬威的样子都有些奇怪。它们正议论今天狐狸的架势怎么这么骄傲，突然看到它后面跟着一只大老虎，都大惊失色，迅速四散逃窜。看着百兽纷纷逃走，狐狸很得意地回头看了一眼老虎，轻蔑地哼了一声。老虎被吓得心惊胆战的，赶紧逃跑了。
其实，老虎不知道，百兽真正怕的是它，而不是狐狸，狐狸只是借了它的威势而已。
江乙讲完这个故事，跟楚宣王总结说：其实北方各国怕的并不是昭奚恤，而是楚宣王。楚宣王才是老虎，而昭奚恤只是借了虎威的狐狸。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Fox and the Tiger

A long, long time ago, during the days of the Warring States, the king of Chu wanted to know why the neighboring countries seemed so afraid of his great general, Zhao Xixu. He asked his wise minister Jiang Yi about it, and Jiang Yi told him a lovely story. And that story is called "The Fox and the Tiger."

Once upon a time, a tiger lived in a cozy cave. One day the tiger felt very hungry, so it wandered out into the forest to find something to eat. As it strolled through the tall, leafy trees, it spotted a little fox taking a peaceful walk. With one quick leap, the tiger caught the fox right away. The tiger opened its mouth wide, ready to eat, but then—amazement!—the fox began to speak. "You must not eat me!" said the fox bravely. "The King of Heaven has made me the ruler of all animals. If you eat me, he will be very displeased." The tiger paused, a little confused. But the fox stood there so calmly and proudly, looking as though it truly meant every word, and the tiger felt unsure about what to do.

Seeing that the tiger was puzzled, the fox thought, *Now is my chance.* So it stood even taller and pointed a paw at the tiger. "Don't believe me?" it said in a bold voice. "Come with me, and I will show you. Walk behind me, and see how all the other animals make way when they see me." And so the tiger followed the fox into the forest.

The fox marched confidently ahead, right up to a quiet little stream. Many animals were gathered there, and they noticed the fox walking with such pride and confidence. "How bold the fox looks today," they whispered among themselves. But then—oh dear—they looked behind the fox and saw the great tiger right there! The animals were startled and quickly ran off in every direction. Watching all the animals scamper away, the fox turned to the tiger with a proud little smile. The tiger, frightened all over, quickly ran away too.

But here is the secret the tiger did not know: the animals were really afraid of the tiger, not the fox at all. The fox was simply borrowing the tiger's mighty presence to look powerful.

When Jiang Yi finished his story, he smiled gently at the king and said, "Your Majesty, the northern countries are not truly afraid of General Zhao Xixu. They are afraid of you. You are the mighty tiger, and General Zhao is simply walking beside you, borrowing your great strength."

And so the king understood, and the story of the clever fox and the great tiger has been told ever since.
fields.tips: 故事中的狐狸虽然凭借一时的小聪明吓跑了其他动物，也欺骗了身后的老虎，但谎言总有戳穿的一天，到那时狐狸的处境就危险了。准妈妈读完故事不妨告诉胎宝宝，将来不要为了一时的风光而欺骗别人，真诚、友善地对待别人，才能获得别人的尊重。
fields.tips_en: Although the clever fox in the story frightened the other animals and deceived the mighty tiger trailing behind, the truth always comes out eventually — and when it does, the fox's predicament becomes very dangerous. After reading this story, dear mother, you might gently share with your little one: never deceive others just for a fleeting moment of glory. Treat others with sincerity and kindness, and their respect will follow naturally.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 亡羊补牢
fields.title_en: Mending the Pen After the Sheep Are Lost
fields.subtitle: 错误越早改正越好
fields.subtitle_en: The Earlier, the Better to Right a Mistake
fields.content:
从前，有一个人养了一大群羊，晚上把羊都圈在一个大羊圈里，早上再放出来。有一天，他早上把羊放出来，数了一下，少一只，再数一遍还是少一只。这个人就进到羊圈里查看还有没有没出来的。结果他发现羊圈的墙上破了一个大洞，大洞口上还有狼的脚印，地上有血。他想少了的羊一定是被狼叼走了。
邻居听他说了这件事，劝他赶快把羊圈修一修，把窟窿堵上。没想到这个人却说：“反正羊已经丢了，修羊圈，羊也回不来了，还修它干吗？”于是窟窿就留在那里没有管。到了晚上，羊照旧都圈在这个羊圈里。
第二天，这个人把羊从羊圈里再放出来的时候，一数又少了一只。看来狼又从窟窿里进来把羊又叼走了一只。这个人很后悔当初没有听邻居的劝告，否则也不会再丢一只羊了。于是他就赶快找东西把窟窿堵上了。
此后，狼再也钻不进羊圈里了，羊再也没丢过。
fields.content_en:
Title: Mending the Pen

Once upon a time, there was a man who owned a big flock of sheep. Every night, he kept them safe inside a large pen, and every morning, he let them out to graze. One morning, as he let the sheep out, he counted them and noticed one was missing. He counted again, and still, one was gone. The man went inside the pen to check if any sheep had stayed behind. That's when he saw a big hole in the wall of the pen. There were wolf tracks near the opening and a little blood on the ground. He knew the missing sheep had been taken by a wolf.

A neighbor heard about it and kindly told him, "You should fix the pen right away and block that hole!" But the man said, "The sheep is already gone. What good does it do to fix the pen now? It won't bring the sheep back." So he left the hole just as it was. That night, the sheep were folded back into the pen as usual.

The next morning, when the man let the sheep out again, he counted and found one was missing once more. The wolf had come back through the same hole and taken another sheep. The man felt very sorry that he hadn't listened to his neighbor's advice. If he had, he wouldn't have lost another sheep. So he quickly gathered materials and patched up the hole.

From that day on, the wolf could never squeeze into the pen again, and the man never lost another sheep.
fields.tips: 准妈妈可以告诉胎宝宝，在生活中我们不怕犯错误，犯了错误一定要勇于承认并积极改正。在讲这个故事的时候，准妈妈可以找个盒子做羊圈，再找两个玩偶，一个放在盒子里当羊，一个放在盒子外当狼。给胎宝宝演示一下狼怎样进到羊圈里把羊叼走。演示时重点介绍里、外这两个空间概念。
fields.tips_en: You can tell your baby that we should not fear making mistakes — the important thing is to courageously admit them and work earnestly to set things right. While telling this story, you might use a small box as a sheepfold and two little toys: one placed inside the box as a lamb, the other outside as a wolf. Act out how the wolf creeps into the pen and carries the lamb away. This is a lovely opportunity to introduce the wonderful concepts of "inside" and "outside."
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 愚公移山
fields.title_en: The Old Man Who Moved the Mountains
fields.subtitle: 精诚所至，金石为开
fields.subtitle_en: With Steadfast Devotion, Even Stone Yields
fields.content:
太行、王屋两座山，占地方圆七百里，高七八千丈，本来是矗立在冀州之南、黄河之北的。北山居住的人们被山阻隔，要出去很不方便。愚公一家也不例外。
这一年，愚公已将近90岁了，被山阻隔也有90年了，觉得不能再这样下去了。于是他就召集家人商量：“我打算跟你们一起把前面的两座大山铲除，这样道路就能直接通到豫州的南部，到达汉水南岸，出来进去就方便多了。你们同意吗？”大家纷纷表示赞成，只有愚公的妻子提出疑问：“凭借您一己之力，就是魁父这座小山都削减不了多少，又能把太行、王屋这两座大山怎么样呢？更何况挖出来的土石又往哪儿扔呢？”众人表示可以把土石扔到渤海边上，隐土北面。
愚公率领家里能干重活的3个人挑着担子上山了。他们把石头凿开，把土挖出，用簸箕装到筐里，然后运到渤海边上，倒入渤海。冬夏换季，他们才能往返一次。
邻居姓京城的寡妇有个孩子，才刚刚换牙，他也蹦蹦跳跳跑去帮忙。但是，河湾上有个叫智叟的老头讥笑愚公说：“你这样做也太蠢了，凭你残年余力，就是山上的一棵草都不见得能毁掉。这满山的泥土、石头，你能把它们怎么样？”愚公听了长叹一口气说：“你的想法真是顽固，顽固得不可改变。你连孤儿、寡妇都不如。我是风烛残年了，但是我死了，还有我儿子，我儿子会生孙子，孙子又生儿子，儿子再生孙子，子子孙孙是没有穷尽的。然而，这山却是固定不再长高了的。怎么会挖不平呢？”智叟无话可说了。
山里住的山神听说了这件事，怕他不停地干下去，到时候自己连住的地方都没有了，就将这件事禀告了天帝。天帝被愚公的诚心感动了。他叫来大力神夸娥氏的两个儿子，命令他们把王屋、太行两座山搬走，一座放在朔方的东部，一座放在雍州的南部。
从此，冀州的南部到汉水南岸就没有大山阻隔了，变成了一马平川的通途。
fields.content_en:
**The Old Man Who Moved the Mountains**

Two great mountains, Taihang and Wangwu, stretched seven hundred miles across and rose thousands of feet high. They once stood south of Jizhou and north of the Yellow River. The people living north of those mountains were blocked in and found it very hard to go anywhere. The old man's family felt this too.

One year, the old man was almost ninety years old. He had been blocked by the mountains for ninety years, and he felt he could not live like this anymore. So he gathered his family and said, "I want to remove those two big mountains right in front of us. Then our road will lead straight down to the south of Yu Province and reach the southern bank of the Han River. Coming and going will be so much easier. Do you agree?" Everyone agreed, but the old man's wife had a question. "You can barely chip away at that small hill, Kuifu," she said. "What could you possibly do to those two huge mountains? And where will all the dirt and stones go?" Everyone agreed they could throw them into the sea by the Bay of Bohai.

The old man led three members of his family who could do heavy work up the mountain. They cracked open the rocks, dug out the earth, scooped it into baskets, and carried it all the way to the Bay of Bohai to dump it in. Once a year, when winter turned to summer, they could make one round trip.

A neighbor, a widow with young teeth just starting to change, came hopping along to help. But a clever old man who lived by the river bend laughed at him and said, "How foolish you are! With your strength left, you could hardly even destroy a single blade of grass on the mountain. What can you do with all that dirt and stone?" The old man sighed and said gently, "Your mind is so closed. You are harder to convince than even a child or a widow. I am growing old, but when I die, my son will carry on. His son will have a son, and his son will have a son, and these sons and grandsons will go on forever. But the mountain will never grow any taller. How could we not dig it flat?" The clever old man had nothing more to say.

A mountain spirit heard about this and grew worried that the old man would keep digging forever until there was no room left for him. So he reported everything to the Emperor of Heaven. The Emperor was moved by the old man's sincere heart. He called upon two mighty sons of the deity Kua'e and ordered them to move the mountains. One mountain was placed east of Shuofang, and the other was placed south of Yongzhou.

From that day on, there were no more towering mountains blocking the land between the south of Jizhou and the southern bank of the Han River. Everything became wide, open, and peaceful.
fields.tips: “子子孙孙，无穷匮也”，这是繁衍的力量。准妈妈可以设想一下将来你的孩子生孙子，孙子又生孩子，将来四世同堂拍个大全家福的场景，一定会感动，现在怀孕的辛苦就不在话下了。
fields.tips_en: "Generations upon generations, without end" — this is the power of growth and continuation. Picture a future where your child grows up, has their own children, and soon there are four generations gathered together for a beautiful family portrait. It is a scene so heartwarming that every辛苦 of this pregnancy will seem a sweet price indeed.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 拔苗助长
fields.title_en: Pulling Sprouts to Help Them Grow
fields.subtitle: 自然规律必须尊重
fields.subtitle_en: The Natural Order Must Be Respected
fields.content:
古时候有个农夫性子特别急，什么都嫌慢。这年春天，他儿子在水田里插了些秧苗，他就每天围着这块水田转悠，隔一会就蹲下，用手量量秧苗长高了没有。秧苗自然不会长得那么快。每次量完，他就更着急了。
这个农夫就想办法要让秧苗长得快一些。他边转悠边想，还终于让他想出了一个办法，就是把秧苗拔高一点儿。说干就干，他蹲下身子一棵一棵地拔高秧苗。看着被拔高的秧苗，他越干越有劲，一口气就把整块田里的秧苗都拔高了一截。拔完，他高兴地站起来，发现腿都已经麻了。不过看着“长高”的秧苗，他是真高兴啊！
他拖着发麻的腿回到家，一进门就跟儿子嚷嚷：“我今天可干了件大事，累死我了。”儿子诧异地问：“爹你干什么大事了？”他非常得意地回答说：“我帮田里的秧苗都长高了一大截，不信你去看看。”儿子很纳闷儿，就拔腿往田里跑去。到田里一看，秧苗有的已经枯死，有的已经蔫了。这整片的水稻将颗粒无收。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Pulling the Sprouts to Help Them Grow**

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who was in such a hurry that everything felt too slow to him. One spring, his son planted some rice seedlings in the field, and the farmer walked around the field all day long, crouching down again and again to measure whether the seedlings had grown taller. But seedlings don't grow so fast, you see. Every time he measured them, he grew more and more worried.

So the farmer came up with a clever idea to help the seedlings grow faster. As he paced around, he thought and thought, and finally he hit upon a plan — he would gently pull each seedling up a little higher! And so he did. He crouched down and pulled each sprout up, one by one. The more he worked, the happier he became, and before long he had pulled up all the seedlings in the whole field. When he finished, he stood up proudly, though his legs were quite numb. But seeing his seedlings now much taller, he was truly overjoyed!

He trudged home on his tired, tingling legs and cried out the moment he walked through the door, "I did something wonderful today, though I'm all worn out!" His son asked in surprise, "What did you do, Papa?" And the father said with great pride, "I helped all the rice seedlings in the field grow much taller! You can go and see for yourself." His son was puzzled, so he ran as fast as he could to the field. When he got there, he saw that some of the seedlings had already withered and died, while others were drooping sadly. All the rice in that field would bring in no harvest at all.
fields.tips: 准妈妈现在就可以想想以后怎么教育胎宝宝，拔苗助长的想法要绝对杜绝。教育一定要遵循着孩子的成长规律、兴趣爱好来进行，别一心想着培养神童，否则最后会害了孩子。
fields.tips_en: Dear mother, now is the perfect time to begin thinking about how you will nurture your little one. The impulsive mindset of pulling up seedlings to force them taller must be firmly left behind. Every child grows at their own beautiful pace — follow their natural rhythm and genuine interests, and never rush to make a prodigy. Rushing only risks doing harm; patience and love bring the truest flourishing.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 刻舟求剑
fields.title_en: Marking the Boat to Find the Sword
fields.subtitle: 用发展的眼光看问题
fields.subtitle_en: Viewing Life Through Evolving Eyes
fields.content:
战国时，有个楚国人出门游历，随身带着一把宝剑。这一天他搭上了一条船，准备到江对面去。
船行到江心，突然晃了一下，这个楚国人立足不稳，失去了平衡，就把身上的剑掉入了江中。
一同搭船的人以及船家都感觉宝剑掉了很可惜，太遗憾了。没想到楚国人却一点儿也不着急，也没有遗憾的神色。只见他拿出一把小刀在船舷上刻了起来。众人不解，忙问他干什么呢？这个人回答道：“我刻个记号，我的宝剑是从这里掉下去的。等到了江边，我从这个记号这里跳下水，就能找到了。”众人愕然，但也没说什么。到了江边，众人纷纷下船。这个楚国人真的一头扎到了水里，去捞他掉落的宝剑。捞了半天，自然不见宝剑的影子。他觉得很奇怪，跟岸上的人说：“我的宝剑就是从这里掉下去的，我还做了记号，为什么找不到呢？”众人一听再也忍不住了，告诉他：“船一直在行进，你的宝剑沉入水底后不再移动，在这里自然是找不到你的宝剑的。”
fields.content_en:
# The Man Who Marked the Boat to Find His Sword

A long time ago, during the Warring States period, there was a man from the State of Chu who traveled with a beautiful sword by his side. One day, he boarded a boat to cross the river.

When the boat reached the middle of the river, it suddenly gave a little shake. The man lost his balance and his precious sword fell into the water with a soft splash.

Everyone on the boat, including the boatman, thought it was such a pity — what a shame! But the man from Chu did not seem worried at all. He simply took out a small knife and began to carve a mark on the side of the boat. The other passengers were puzzled and asked him what he was doing. He smiled and said, "I am making a note right here, because this is exactly where my sword fell into the water. When we reach the other side, I will jump in right at this mark and I will find my sword." Everyone looked at him in surprise, but no one said anything.

When the boat finally reached the far bank, all the passengers stepped onto the shore. The man from Chu immediately dove into the water to search for his sword. He looked and looked, but of course, he could not find the smallest trace of it. Confused, he swam back to the bank and said to the people standing there, "My sword fell from right here, and I even made a mark. Why can't I find it?" The people on the shore could hold back no longer. They gently told him, "Dear friend, the boat kept moving the whole time, but your sword settled at the bottom of the river and did not move at all. That is why you will never find it here."
fields.tips: 做胎教也要“与时俱进”，比如5个月时，胎宝宝有了听力，可以放些适合胎宝宝听的音乐；六七个月时胎宝宝对按压、触摸有反应，可以玩踢肚游戏……
fields.tips_en: Prenatal education should also grow and change alongside your little one! For instance, around five months, when your baby begins to hear, you might play gentle, soothing music for them. By six or seven months, when they start responding to touches and pressure, you can delight in playful games like gentle belly kicks. Adapt your bond to each new stage — your baby is always growing, always becoming someone new and wonderful.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 滥竽充数
fields.subtitle: 没有真本事迟早要被人识破
fields.subtitle_en: Without real skill, you'll eventually be found out
fields.content:
战国时，齐国的国君齐宣王特别喜欢音乐，尤其喜欢听吹竽。吹竽的乐手听说了，纷纷前去效力。齐宣王也来者不拒，手下共集结了300个吹竽手。齐宣王最喜欢听的是这300个人合奏。合奏声势浩大，场面热闹，特别能彰显自己的身份。
有一个叫南郭先生的人也跑到齐宣王那里，说自己吹竽的本事了得。据他自己说：“我吹竽的时候，听的人没有不被感动的，就连鸟兽也会跟着翩翩起舞，花草也会跟着节拍摆动。”齐宣王非常爽快就把他收下了，把他编进了吹竽人的队伍，跟着那些人一起吹竽。
其实南郭先生根本就不会吹竽，但是他知道齐宣王喜欢合奏，所以一点儿都不担心。每当演奏的时候，南郭先生就拿出自己表演的本事，手举着竽，根本不发出声音，只在动作、表情上做文章；别人摇晃身体他也摇晃身体；别人闭上眼睛，他也闭上；别人抬头低头，他也抬头低头。看上去吹得动情、忘我，真像一个吹竽高手。其实一点儿声音都没发出来。
南郭先生不会吹竽，在他身边演奏的人其实已经看了出来，只是大家都想不关己事，所以都懒得去拆穿他。这样南郭先生还真在这支吹竽的队伍里混了好些年，拿着和其他乐师一样多的薪水。
逍遥自在的好日子再长也不会一直延续下去。几年后，齐宣王死了，他的儿子齐湣王继承了王位。齐湣王和齐宣王不同，他不喜欢听合奏，觉得合奏一片吵闹，而喜欢叫乐师一个一个地单独吹竽给他听。这样更加悠扬动听。
齐湣王发了一道命令，命令这300个吹竽手都积极练习，做好准备，到时候会随机点名来演奏。乐师们接到命令，人人都积极准备，同时也在看南郭先生怎么办。南郭先生急得像热锅上的蚂蚁。这天齐湣王已经点了几个乐师进宫去演奏了，南郭先生一方面庆幸没有点到自己，但也明白真的混不下去了，就偷偷收拾行李，连夜逃走了。
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Man Who Pretended to Play**

A long, long time ago, in the Kingdom of Qi, King Xuan loved music very much. He especially loved listening to people play the yu, a beautiful wind instrument. When musicians heard this, they came from far and far away to play for the king. King Xuan welcomed them all, and soon he had three hundred yu players in his orchestra. His favorite thing was to hear all three hundred of them play together. The music was loud and grand, and it made the king feel very important.

One day, a man named Mr. Nanguo came to the king. "I am the best yu player in the world," he said proudly. "When I play, people are moved to tears. Even birds and animals dance to my music, and flowers and plants sway to my rhythm." The king was so impressed that he immediately welcomed Mr. Nanguo into the orchestra. Mr. Nanguo joined the three hundred players, ready to play along with them.

But here is the secret: Mr. Nanguo could not play the yu at all. However, he knew the king loved hearing everyone play together, so he was not worried. Whenever it was time to play, Mr. Nanguo would lift his yu to his lips and make all the right movements. He did not make a single sound. He only moved his hands, shook his body, closed his eyes, and nodded his head—just like everyone else. From the outside, he looked just like a true master, playing with all his heart. But no sound came out.

The other musicians could tell that Mr. Nanguo was not really playing. But everyone thought, "It is not my business," and no one wanted to speak up. So Mr. Nanguo kept pretending, year after year, earning the same pay as everyone else.

But happy days cannot last forever. After several years, King Xuan passed away, and his son, King Min, became the new ruler. King Min was very different from his father. He did not like the loud sound of the whole group playing together. Instead, he preferred to hear each musician play one by one, all alone. He said the music sounded sweeter and more beautiful that way.

King Min issued a decree: all three hundred yu players must practice hard and be ready, because he would call on them one at a time to play for him. The musicians all began practicing eagerly, and they all watched Mr. Nanguo to see what he would do. Mr. Nanguo was terrified. He felt like an ant on a hot pan. One day, the king had already called several musicians into the palace to play. Mr. Nanguo was glad it was not him—but he knew he could not hide forever. That night, while everyone was asleep, he quietly packed his things and slipped away in the darkness.
fields.tips: 每一个准妈妈都希望自己的胎宝宝出生后聪明伶俐、多才多艺，这也是现在准妈妈努力做胎教的出发点。讲这个故事的时候，准妈妈一定要告诉胎宝宝，不管做什么事情，都要有真才实学，没有本事的人或许能糊弄一时，但随着时间的推移，迟早会被周围人识破。
fields.tips_en: Every expecting mother dreams of a bright, gifted baby—that's exactly why so many begin prenatal bonding through storytelling. As you share this tale, gently remind your little one that true ability matters in everything we do. Someone without real talent might get away with it for a while, but sooner or later, the truth will show.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 掩耳盗铃
fields.title_en: Covering Your Ears to Steal a Bell
fields.subtitle: 自欺欺人
fields.subtitle_en: Don't fool yourself
fields.content:
现在流传下来的掩耳盗铃故事，是说一个人看到别人家的门口挂着一个铃铛，想偷走，但又担心被发现，于是就把自己的耳朵堵起来，自己听不到，以为别人也听不到了。然后他就放心地去摘铃铛，结果铃铛的声音惊动了主人，把他抓住了。
其实这个故事的原型是掩耳盗钟，具体是这样的：
传说春秋时期，晋国的世家赵家灭掉了范氏一族，有人就想趁火打劫，到范家去偷点儿东西。但是范家的财产已经被赵家搬运得差不多了，所以小偷什么都没找到。小偷要离开范家的时候，突然看到院子里有一口大钟，是用上等的青铜铸成的，他高兴极了。这么一口大钟能卖不少钱呢。于是他就决定把这口钟背回家去。
但是，大钟实在太大、太重了，小偷凭一己之力根本搬不动。他也不愿意去叫人帮忙，否则还得分给别人一份呢。小偷想了想，就找了一把大锤子，想把钟砸成小块卖，那也很值钱。小偷抡起锤子，拼命朝大钟砸去，没想到大钟发出“咣”的一声巨响，把小偷吓了一跳。他想，别人听到钟声就会跑来发现他的行径，吓得不敢再听，捂住了耳朵。
小偷捂住耳朵后发现声音小了。“哎，把耳朵捂住不就听不见钟声了吗？那样我砸烂钟就谁也不知道了。”于是小偷立刻从自己身上撕下两条布，团成团，塞到耳朵里去，然后试着再去砸钟。果然听不见了，小偷放心了。他放手用力砸起钟来，一下一下……小偷砸得高兴，钟声远远地传了出去。人们听到钟声不知道发生了什么事，纷纷赶来，一看原来是小偷在偷钟，迅速把他捉住了。
这么多人来了，小偷都没有发现。等到被捉住了，他还一脸诧异。他不明白明明自己已经把耳朵塞住了，别人怎么还能听到钟声呢？
fields.content_en:
**Title: Covering Ears to Steal the Bell**

The story of covering one's ears to steal a bell is about a man who saw a bell hanging at someone else's door and wanted to take it. But he was afraid of being discovered, so he plugged his own ears. Since he couldn't hear the bell himself, he thought no one else could hear it either. Then he went ahead and took the bell down. But the sound of the bell startled the owner, who came running out and caught him right away.

Actually, the original version of this story is about covering one's ears to steal a bell. Let me tell it like this:

It is said that during the Spring and Autumn period, the Zhao family in the State of Jin defeated the Fan family. A thief wanted to take advantage of the chaos and sneak into the Fan house to steal something. But the Zhao family had already carried away most of the Fan family's treasures, so the thief found nothing. Just as he was about to leave, he suddenly spotted a large bronze bell in the courtyard. He was overjoyed! Such a beautiful bell could be sold for a lot of money. So he decided to carry it home.

But the bell was far too big and heavy for one person to move. He didn't want to ask for help, either, because then he'd have to share the prize. After thinking about it, the thief found a large hammer and figured he could smash the bell into pieces to sell separately. He swung the hammer and struck the bell with all his might. *Clang!* The enormous sound terrified him. He thought, "If someone hears this bell ringing, they'll come and catch me." So he covered his ears tightly, hoping not to hear the sound.

After covering his ears, the noise did seem quieter. "Oh!" he thought. "If I plug my ears, I won't hear the bell at all. Then when I smash it, no one will ever know!" Immediately, he tore two strips of cloth from his clothes, rolled them up, and stuffed them into his ears. He tried hitting the bell again. Sure enough, he couldn't hear anything. Feeling safe, the thief began to smash the bell with all his might. Bang! Bang! Bang! He was so happy that he didn't notice the sound traveling far and wide. Hearing the strange noise, people gathered from everywhere. When they arrived, they found a thief smashing a great bell and quickly captured him.

The thief was so surprised when everyone showed up. He still couldn't understand how anyone could hear the bell when his own ears were completely plugged!
fields.tips: 怀孕5个月以后，胎宝宝有了听力，声音都会穿过准妈妈的肚皮到达胎宝宝的耳朵，所以准妈妈要远离声音嘈杂的环境。准妈妈觉得尚可接受的声音，对胎宝宝来说可能就有些大了，会让他感觉烦躁。
fields.tips_en: After five months of pregnancy, your baby can hear! Sound travels right through your belly to those tiny ears, so it's wise to stay away from noisy places. What feels comfortable to you may be too loud for your little one and could make them feel restless.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 自相矛盾
fields.subtitle: 万事无绝对
fields.subtitle_en: Nothing is absolute
fields.content:
楚国有个锻造矛和盾的人，他把打造好的矛和盾拿到市场上去卖。到了市场上，看着来来往往的人，他吆喝开了：“快来看我的矛。我的矛非常锐利，无论什么盾都挡不住它！”吆喝了几遍，见还没有人来买，又接着卖盾。他照样先夸宝：“快来看我的盾，我的盾非常坚固，任何矛都攻不破它！”
他这样吆喝来吆喝去，恰好这时有个特别好较真的人经过。那个人听了他的吆喝，就过来问：“你的矛很锐利，任何盾都挡不住，是吧？”叫卖的人说“是”。这个人又问：“你的盾很坚固，任何矛都穿不破，是吧？”叫卖的人说“当然”。这个人看看周围的人，又问了最后一个问题：“那么，用你的矛攻你的盾，会怎么样呢？”楚国人听完，瞠目结舌，一句话都说不出来了。他拿起矛和盾快速走出人群，没多久就消失不见了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Man Who Sold a Spear and a Shield

In the land of Chu, there was a man who made spears and shields. He brought his spears and shields to the market to sell them. At the market, watching people walk by, he began to call out, "Come look at my spear! My spear is so sharp that no shield in the world can stop it!" He called out several times, but when no one came to buy, he kept selling his shield. Just as before, he proudly praised his shield, "Come look at my shield! My shield is so strong that no spear can pierce it!"

He called out like this back and forth, and just then, a very careful man happened to pass by. Hearing his calls, the man came over and asked, "Your spear is very sharp, and no shield can stop it, right?" The salesman said, "Yes." The man asked again, "Your shield is very strong, and no spear can pierce it, right?" The salesman replied, "Of course." The man looked around at the people nearby, then asked one final question, "Then, if you use your spear to strike your shield, what will happen?" After hearing this, the man from Chu was speechless, with his eyes wide open. He picked up his spear and shield and quickly walked out of the crowd, disappearing soon after.
fields.tips: 楚国人夸下海口，最后难以自圆其说。准妈妈在讲这个故事的时候，可以拿一根小棍子，假装是矛，再拿一个枕头，当作是盾。矛说自己很尖锐，什么都能刺破；盾说自己很坚固，什么都刺不破。然后用棍子去攻击枕头。这样一边做游戏，一边给胎宝宝讲，会很有趣。
fields.tips_en: A man from Chu boasted so wildly he couldn't back it up. While telling this story, grab a small stick to pretend is a spear and a pillow to stand in for a shield. Let the spear boast it can pierce anything, and let the shield claim it can't be pierced by anything—then gently tap the pillow with the stick. Playful and fun, your baby will love it!
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 买椟还珠
fields.title_en: The Ornate Box and the Pearls
fields.subtitle: 各花入各眼
fields.subtitle_en: Beauty lives in the eye of the beholder
fields.content:
战国时候，有个楚国人急需一笔钱。他无处筹去，就想卖掉自己的一颗珍珠。这颗珍珠非常珍贵，但他还是担心卖不出好价钱，就想把珍珠好好包装一下，提高它的身价。
于是，这个楚国人买了一块名贵的木材，又请了一个手艺高超的工匠。工匠给他做了一个精致的盒子。盒子上雕刻着漂亮的花纹，用珠子和宝玉点缀，用翠鸟的羽毛镶了边，看上去精美绝伦，华光闪闪。
楚国人看这个盒子绝对配得上自己的珍珠了，就把珍珠放了进去，然后拿到市场上去卖。到了市场上，有一个郑国人特别钟爱，拿在手上翻来覆去地看，简直爱不释手，最后终于下定决心买了下来。
郑国人一手交钱，一手把盒子拿在手里走了。楚国人看珍珠卖出了好价钱，也很满意，准备回家了。楚国人没走几步，突然听到后面有人追赶他，回头一看是那个郑国人。他手里举着那颗珍珠。楚国人还以为是郑国人后悔了，正生气呢。他心想：我这么好的珠子还不值你这点儿钱吗？没想到郑国人追上他，把手里捏着的珍珠交给他，说：“先生，你把这颗珠子落在盒子里了，我特地拿回来还给你。”楚国人目瞪口呆地将珠子接过来，看着郑国人拿着盒子边欣赏边走远了。
楚国人站在原地，觉得十分尴尬，不知道该庆幸还是该懊恼：到底是珍珠更有价值，还是盒子更有价值呢？
fields.content_en:
Title: The Pearl and the Box

Long, long ago, during the Warring States period, there was a man from Chu who desperately needed money. He didn't know where to find any, so he decided to sell his precious pearl. The pearl was truly wonderful, but he worried it might not fetch a good price. So he thought, "If I wrap it in something beautiful, perhaps it will seem even more valuable."

So the man from Chu bought a piece of fine, expensive wood and hired a skilled craftsman. The craftsman made him a lovely little box. The box was carved with pretty patterns and decorated with pearls and jewels, and its edges were trimmed with bright bird feathers. It sparkled beautifully and looked absolutely stunning.

The man from Chu felt the box was worthy of his pearl. He placed the pearl inside and took it to the market. There, a man from Zheng was especially drawn to it. He picked it up and turned it over and over in his hands, simply loving it. In the end, he made up his mind and bought it.

The man from Zheng handed over the money and walked away with the box under his arm. The man from Chu was very pleased to have sold his pearl for such a good price and was getting ready to head home. But just a few steps later, he heard someone running after him. He turned around and saw it was the man from Zheng, holding the pearl high. The man from Chu was a bit cross at first, thinking the man had changed his mind. "Don't my lovely pearl deserve that much?" he thought to himself. But then the man from Zheng caught up and gently placed the pearl into his hand, saying, "Sir, you left this pearl inside the box. I brought it back just for you." The man from Chu stood there, wide-eyed, taking the pearl. He watched as the man from Zheng strolled away, admiring the box.

The man from Chu stood still, feeling rather embarrassed. He didn't know whether to feel glad or upset. Which was truly more valuable — the pearl, or the box?
fields.tips: 很多人在读完这个故事之后，都为郑国人感到遗憾，但其实对郑国人来说，真正珍贵的就是那个他爱不释手的盒子。各花入各眼，就像孩子一样，每个妈妈最能入眼的那个，无疑是自家的。所以准妈妈不用担心孩子将来是不是能让你满意。无论如何你都会义无反顾地爱上他。
fields.tips_en: Many readers feel sorry for the man from Zheng who kept the beautiful box and returned the pearls. But honestly—that gorgeous box was truly precious to him. Just as each flower speaks to a different eye, so too does each child shine brightest to their own mother. So don't worry about whether your baby will meet your expectations. However they turn out, you will love them unconditionally.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 塞翁失马
fields.title_en: The Old Man Lost His Horse
fields.subtitle: 祸福相依
fields.subtitle_en: Blessings and troubles walk hand in hand
fields.content:
靠近边塞居住着一个精通占卜的老人，他叫塞翁。有一天他的马无缘无故地跑到了胡人的领地。这个损失是很大的，人们都觉得他很不幸，过来安慰他。他却说：“这说不定是件好事呢。”人们对老人的态度都很不理解。
过了几个月，这匹马居然带着胡人的几匹骏马跑回来了。这是笔不小的意外之财，人们觉得他太幸运了，都来祝贺他。而他却说：“谁知道这就不能变成一件坏事呢？”人们想这老头怎么老喜欢跟别人唱反调啊。
胡人的马高大善跑，塞翁的儿子可喜欢了，经常骑着出去奔驰。有一次骑马的时候，儿子摔下来，摔折了腿。人们又来安慰了。老人却说：“这或许也是件好事。”人们想起前两次老人说的话，想也许有一定道理。
一年后，胡人大举侵犯边境，青壮年男子都被征兵，拿起弓箭去作战了，死了有十之八九。而他的儿子因为腿瘸了，不能上战场，幸而保全了一条命。
fields.content_en:
# The Old Man's Wise Words

Near the border lived a kind old man who was very good at predicting the future. His name was Sai Weng.

One day, his horse ran away and crossed into the territory of neighboring people. This was a big loss, and everyone felt sorry for him. They came to comfort him. But the old man just smiled and said, "You never know—maybe this is actually a good thing!" Everyone looked at each other in confusion.

A few months later, that same horse came back! And it brought with it several beautiful horses from the neighbors. What wonderful luck! Everyone came to celebrate with him. But the old man just shook his head and said, "Maybe this isn't so lucky after all. Who knows—maybe this will turn into something bad?" People thought the old man was just being stubborn and difficult.

The neighbor's horses were tall and fast, and Sai Weng's son absolutely loved them. He rode out again and again. But one day, he fell from a horse and broke his leg. Once again, people came to offer their sympathy. And once again, the old man said quietly, "Perhaps this will become a good thing." By now, people remembered his words from before and began to wonder if maybe there was some truth to them.

A year later, a great war broke out near the border. All the young men were drafted into the army and sent to fight. Most of them never came home. But Sai Weng's son—because his leg was still healing—was allowed to stay behind. And so, he was spared from the battle and survived.

And that is why people still tell this story today, about how sometimes what seems like bad luck may turn out to be good, and what seems like good luck may not always be so simple.
fields.tips: 准妈妈可以学学塞翁的思维方式，遇到好事不大喜过望，遇到坏事也不悲伤忧惧，总是着眼未来，可以避免情绪大起大落。
fields.tips_en: You can learn from the old man's calm wisdom—celebrate good news without losing your head, and face bad news without sinking into worry. Keeping your eyes on the future helps you stay emotionally balanced through all of life's twists and turns.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 武则天识青鹅
fields.title_en: Empress Wu Zetian and the Mystery of Qing'e
fields.subtitle: 拆字游戏
fields.subtitle_en: A Fun Character Puzzle
fields.content:
武则天坐上皇位、建立武周王朝以后，唐朝元老以及李家宗室诸人心里都不服。徐敬业是唐初名将李绩的孙子，他也在其列。
后来，徐敬业就在扬州起兵谋反，要推翻武则天，让李唐王朝复兴，骆宾王也帮他。徐敬业让骆宾王联络中书令裴炎做内应。骆宾王想必须有足够打动裴炎的理由，才能说服他，于是就编了一首童谣：“一片火，两片火，绯衣小儿殿上坐。”在京都和裴炎的家乡都传唱开来。
骆宾王去见裴炎，问裴炎有没有听说这首童谣。裴炎当然也听说了，只是不明白是什么意思，正好要问骆宾王呢。骆宾王就解释说：“‘绯衣’两个字合起来是‘裴’，而‘两片火’就是‘炎’，殿上坐自然就是说要称王了。所以，这首童谣的意思就是裴炎要做皇帝了，这是上天的意思。”裴炎一听自然心花怒放，很自然就答应了给骆宾王做内应。
裴炎答应做内应后，跟徐敬业有了比较紧密的联系。这被武则天的人察觉了。又一次，裴炎给徐敬业写了一封信，信用的是密语，上面只有“青鹅”两个字。这封信被武则天的人查获了。密信在朝堂上被公布开来，但没有人明白这两个字是什么意思，便拿给武则天看。武则天看过，沉思了一下便解释说：“‘青’是‘十二月’，‘鹅’则是‘我自与’。”这便是相约要在十二月起兵的意思，裴炎在那个时候就会做内应。
武则天据此便杀了裴炎，然后派兵追击徐敬业。徐敬业被其部下王那相杀死。王那相降了武则天。至此，徐敬业的谋反被平息了。
知识
lian
接
骆宾王是唐初诗人，出生寒微，但才华横溢。据传他7岁就可以作诗。著名的《咏鹅》就是他7岁时所作。后来他与王勃、杨炯、卢照邻被合称“初唐四杰”。而他的诗是4人中最多的。他最为人乐道的是替徐敬业写的《代李敬业传檄天下文》。这篇文章本来是讨伐武则天的，但后来他却折服了武则天。
fields.content_en:
Title: Wu Zetian Deciphers the Secret Message

After Wu Zetian took the throne and established her own dynasty, some elders from the old Tang dynasty and members of the Li royal family were not happy about it. One of them was Xu Jingye, the grandson of the great Tang general Li Ji.

Later, Xu Jingye raised an army in Yangzhou to fight against Wu Zetian, hoping to restore the Tang dynasty. His friend Luo Binwang helped him. Xu Jingye asked Luo Binwang to reach out to Pei Yan, an important government minister, to be a secret helper inside the palace. Luo Binwang knew he needed a good reason to convince Pei Yan, so he made up a little children's song: "One piece of fire, two pieces of fire, a child in crimson robes sits upon the throne." The song spread through the capital and also in Pei Yan's hometown.

When Luo Binwang met Pei Yan, he asked if he had heard the song. Pei Yan had heard it, but he did not understand what it meant — he was actually about to ask Luo Binwang! So Luo Binwang explained, "The word 'crimson' put together means the surname Pei. And 'two pieces of fire' makes the character for 'Yan.' Sitting on the throne means becoming emperor. So this song is telling us that you, Pei Yan, are destined to become emperor. It is the will of heaven." Pei Yan was overjoyed to hear this, and he readily agreed to be the secret helper.

After Pei Yan promised to help, he began communicating closely with Xu Jingye. Wu Zetian's spies noticed this. One day, Pei Yan wrote a letter to Xu Jingye using a secret code. The letter only had two words written on it: "Green Goose." The letter was discovered by Wu Zetian's people. It was shown openly in court, but no one could figure out what those two words meant. So they brought it before Wu Zetian. She looked at it thoughtfully for a moment and then said, "'Green' can be split into the word for twelve and the radical for moon — meaning the twelfth month. And 'goose' contains the characters for 'I myself will.' This means they plan to rise up in the twelfth month, and Pei Yan will be their helper inside the palace."

Based on this discovery, Wu Zetian had Pei Yan killed, and then sent soldiers to chase after Xu Jingye. Xu Jingye was killed by his own officer, Wang Naxiang, who then surrendered to Wu Zetian. In this way, Xu Jingye's rebellion was put to an end.

Knowledge

Luo Binwang was a famous poet of the early Tang dynasty. He was born into a poor family, but he was extraordinarily gifted. It is said that he could write poems when he was only seven years old. His most famous poem, "Ode to the Goose," was written when he was just seven. Later, he was grouped together with Wang Bo, Yang Jiong, and Lu Zhaolin as one of the "Four Outstanding Literati of the Early Tang." Among the four, he wrote the most poems. The thing he is best known for is the proclamation he wrote on behalf of Xu Jingye, calling on the whole world to rise up against Wu Zetian. Interestingly, although the article was meant to criticize Wu Zetian, even she was so impressed by its beauty that she admiringly acknowledged its brilliance.
fields.tips: 汉字的构成很有意思，尤其是会意字，比如“休”就是一个人靠着一棵树。准妈妈可以把感兴趣的字分析一下，看看有什么基本构成，想想为什么是这样的构成。
fields.tips_en: Chinese characters are beautifully crafted, especially the ideographs like 'rest' — it's simply a person leaning against a tree. Why don't you explore some characters together? Look at how they're built and discover the stories hidden inside them.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 鹬蚌相争，渔翁得利
fields.title_en: The Snipe and the Clam: A Story of Compromise
fields.subtitle: 该让步时需让步
fields.subtitle_en: Learning to Yield for Love
fields.content:
苏代是战国时期的纵横家。赵国要攻打燕国，苏代前往游说赵惠王。
到了赵惠王的王宫，苏代对他说：“我来的时候路过易水，在易水边看到有一只河蚌出来晒太阳。它刚刚把壳张开，就有一只鹬鸟飞过来，伸嘴到壳里要啄它的肉。鹬鸟刚伸嘴到壳里，河蚌就把壳合上了。这样鹬鸟和河蚌就对峙上了。”鹬鸟对河蚌说：‘今天不下雨，明天不下雨，小河蚌你就死定了。’但河蚌对鹬鸟说：‘今天你拔不出嘴去，明天拔不出嘴去，后天鹬鸟你就死定了。’河蚌和鹬鸟各不相让，就这样僵持着。这时有个渔夫路过，一眼就看到了这一鹬和一蚌，就把它们都捡起来了。
“现在赵国要攻打燕国，必然会造成燕国和赵国久久相持不下的局面，就像鹬鸟和河蚌一样。到时候强大的秦国就像渔夫一样，轻而易举就能把燕国和赵国都打败，尽收利益而去。希望大王再详加思量，三思而行啊！”
赵惠王被苏代说服了。他对苏代说：“你说得不错。”于是就取消了攻打燕国的打算。
fields.content_en:
# The Snipe and the Clam

Once upon a time, during the Warring States period, there was a wise advisor named Su Dai. The State of Zhao wanted to attack the State of Yan, and so Su Dai traveled to persuade King Hui of Zhao.

When Su Dai arrived at the king's palace, he said gently, "On my way here, I passed by the Yi River. There, I saw a little clam basking in the warm sun. Just as it had cracked open its shell, a snipe bird fluttered down and stretched its long beak right into the shell to peck at the clam's tender flesh. The moment the snipe's beak touched inside, the clam snapped its shell shut! So the snipe and the clam found themselves stuck, unable to move."

The snipe said to the clam, "If it doesn't rain today, and it doesn't rain tomorrow, little clam, you will dry up and perish!" But the clam replied, "If you cannot pull your beak out today, and cannot pull it out tomorrow, and cannot pull it out the day after, then you, poor snipe, will surely perish!" Neither would give in to the other, and they stayed locked in a stalemate. Just then, a fisherman happened to pass by. He spotted the snipe and the clam, stuck together, and he simply picked them both up.

Su Dai continued, "Right now, Zhao is preparing to attack Yan. This will only lead to a long, drawn-out standoff between your two states — much like the snipe and the clam. And when that happens, the powerful State of Qin will be like that fisherman, easily defeating both Yan and Zhao, and taking all the rewards for itself. I ask Your Majesty to please think carefully about this."

King Hui of Zhao was deeply moved by Su Dai's words. He said softly, "You are quite right." And so, he decided to cancel his plans to attack Yan.

And that is why we say — when two sides refuse to yield, a third party may come along and take the prize.
fields.tips: 鹬蚌相争，两败俱伤。准爸爸和准妈妈如果在生活中经常争吵，也会两败俱伤，而且更严重的是还会伤害腹中的胎宝宝。所以准妈妈和准爸爸要替胎宝宝多着想，有争执的时候该让步就要让步。
fields.tips_en: When the snipe and the clam refuse to let each other go, both end up harmed. If mom and dad argue too often, it can upset the little one growing inside. So let's remember our baby and choose kindness — sometimes letting go is the most loving thing we can do.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 杜甫智斗刁县令
fields.title_en: Du Fu Outsmarts the Difficult Magistrate
fields.subtitle: 有才能不怕刁难
fields.subtitle_en: Talent Shines Through Challenges
fields.content:
杜甫是我国唐代伟大的诗人，他50多岁时仕途不顺，携全家老小搬到了沙头镇生活。开始的时候杜甫靠弟弟和朋友接济，但这并非长久之计，于是就打算全家人开一家药铺。这家药铺取名为百草堂。此后全家就以卖药为生了。
百草堂卖的药货真价实，赚了不错的口碑。而且，杜甫一家人非常善良，有些穷人需要药，如果没钱就免费赠送了。不长时间，百草堂就受到了当地老百姓的爱戴。他们都赞不绝口地传诵杜甫的功德。这样一来，百草堂生意就很红火了。
当地几家药铺看百草堂是后来的，而且是外地人开的，生意这么好，就非常恼火。几家碰到一起一商量，决定联手将百草堂整垮，把杜甫赶出沙头镇。他们买通了县令，让县令来刁难杜甫。
这一天，下着小雨，药铺里人不多，很安静。伙计正在专心致志地抓药，突然门“咣当”一声响，被人撞开了。大家一看，进来的是个书吏。书吏在门口停顿了一下，横眉立目朝四下扫了一眼，径直来到柜台前，将一张药单甩到柜台上，傲慢地说：“这是县令大人急用的药，照单配来。如果配不来，你们就别想再卖药了！”伙计连忙把药单拿过来，一看就愣住了。只见药单上面写着：“行运早，行运迟，正行运，不行运。”这哪里是什么药名啊！旁边的一个老伙计赔着笑脸问：“这位大哥，不知道是哪位郎中开的药……”一句话还没说完，书吏就骂了起来，直接要求杜甫出来。他说，配不齐药就要砸药铺。
伙计赶忙拿着药单去后院找杜甫。杜甫拿过来一看，知道是县令故意为难。不过这点儿雕虫小技可难不倒他。杜甫在药箱子里取了三种药，又把桌上的一颗李子拿了，一并包在纸包里，走了出来。
杜甫出来向书吏施了一礼，问道：“这位大哥，不知县令大人有何见教？”书吏轻蔑地看了杜甫一眼，懒洋洋地回答道：“我们县令大人要你照单抓药，否则就要砸你的招牌。你就准备滚蛋吧，别想再卖药了！”杜甫笑了笑说：“哦，大哥请放心。县令大人要的药，本小铺都有。”书吏听了一愣。只见杜甫把手里的纸包放在柜台上，轻轻打开。纸包里的东西露出来了，是一片萝卜干、一块生姜牙、一个鲜李子和一颗干桃僵。书吏看了，得意地笑了：“我让你照单抓药，你这是什么？你想干什么？！”杜甫从容答道：“大哥请看，萝卜干是‘甘罗’之意。甘罗12岁当丞相，正是‘行运早’。这是不是药单中的第一味药？”书吏听了，的确如此，只好点头。杜甫再说：“生姜牙是‘姜子牙’的意思。姜子牙83岁遇到文王，是不是就是‘行运迟’？正是第二味药。”书吏只得再点头。杜甫继续说：“李子正是目前市场上的俏货，可以算得上是‘正行运’吧？”书吏还是只能点头。杜甫又指着桃僵说：“这是隔年的桃子，已经算不得鲜果了，没人再愿意吃，只能入药。是不是‘不行运’了？”书吏仍然无法反驳，只能拿着这几味药回去向县令交差了。
fields.content_en:
Title: Du Fu Outsmarts the Tricky Magistrate

Du Fu was one of China's greatest poets from the Tang Dynasty. When he was in his fifties, his career was not going well, so he moved his whole family to Shatou Town. At first, Du Fu relied on his younger brother and friends for help, but he knew that could not last forever. So he decided that the whole family should open a little medicine shop. They named it Baicaotang, which means "Hall of a Hundred Herbs." From then on, the family made their living by selling medicine.

Baicaotang sold only the best herbs at fair prices, and word of this spread. The people of Du Fu's family were also very kind-hearted. Whenever poor neighbors needed medicine but had no money, Du Fu gave it to them for free. Before long, the people of the town came to love Baicaotang. They praised Du Fu's goodness again and again. Soon, the shop was busier than ever.

The other medicine shops in town were very jealous. After all, Baicaotang was new and run by outsiders, yet it was doing so well. The owners met in secret and decided to work together to put Baicaotang out of business and drive Du Fu out of Shatou Town. They bribed the county magistrate to make things difficult for him.

One day, a light rain was falling. The shop was quiet with only a few customers. The shopkeeper's assistant was carefully measuring out herbs when suddenly the door burst open with a loud bang. Everyone looked up and saw a clerk walking in. He paused at the doorway, glared around the room with angry eyes, and strode straight to the counter. He threw a prescription onto the counter and said proudly, "These are medicines the magistrate urgently needs. Fill this order exactly. If you cannot, you will never be allowed to sell medicine again!" The assistant picked up the prescription and stared at it in surprise. Written on it were these words: "Luck comes early, luck comes late, luck comes now, and luck does not come at all." These were not the names of any herbs! A senior assistant stepped forward with a nervous smile and asked, "Sir, might I ask which doctor prescribed these medicines…?" He had not finished speaking when the clerk began to curse and demanded that Du Fu come out at once. He said the shop would be smashed if the medicines were not ready.

The assistant hurried to the back courtyard to find Du Fu. Du Fu took the prescription and understood immediately — the magistrate was deliberately making things hard for him. But this small trick could not fool him. Du Fu reached into his medicine chest and took out three items. Then he picked up a fresh plum from the table. He wrapped everything together in a piece of paper and walked back to the counter.

Du Fu bowed politely to the clerk and asked, "Good sir, what would the magistrate like to ask of us?" The clerk gave Du Fu a scornful glance and answered lazily, "Our magistrate wants you to fill this prescription, or he will smash your sign. You should prepare to leave and never sell medicine again!" Du Fu smiled gently and said, "Please do not worry, sir. The shop has everything the magistrate needs." The clerk was taken aback. Du Fu placed the paper bundle on the counter and carefully opened it. Inside were a piece of dried radish, a small chunk of ginger, a fresh plum, and a dried peach pit. The clerk looked at them and sneered. "I told you to fill the prescription! What is this? What do you think you are doing?!" Du Fu answered calmly, "Sir, please look. The dried radish represents 'Gan Luo.' When Gan Luo was twelve years old, he became prime minister. That means 'luck comes early.' Is this not the first herb on the list?" The clerk, though unwilling, had to nod. Du Fu continued, "This piece of ginger reminds us of 'Jiang Ziya.' Jiang Ziya was eighty-three years old when he met King Wen and finally found his fortune. That means 'luck comes late.' Is this the second herb?" The clerk could only nod again. Du Fu went on, "And this plum is the most popular fruit in market right now. It can certainly be called 'luck comes now.'" The clerk still had nothing to say but nodded. Finally, Du Fu pointed to the dried peach pit and said, "This is a peach from last year. It is no longer fresh, and no one wants to eat it. It can only be used as medicine. Does this not mean 'luck does not come'?" The clerk could find no answer and could only take the medicines back to report to the magistrate.
fields.tips: 从故事中可以看出杜甫的发散思维能力非常强，我们平时提到的联想记忆法也是发散思维方法的体现。准妈妈也可以试试用发散思维，当看到一样东西时就想想跟它有关系的事物，就将思维发散出去，锻炼脑力，增强记忆力。这对腹中的胎宝宝也有益啊。
fields.tips_en: Du Fu's wonderful imagination shows us the power of thinking outside the box. When you see something around you, try connecting it to other things — it's a delightful brain game that sharpens your mind and memory, and what a lovely gift for your baby!
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 曹冲称象
fields.title_en: Cao Chong and the Great Elephant
fields.subtitle: 孩子的潜能是无穷的
fields.subtitle_en: A Child's Limitless Potential
fields.content:
吴国的孙权送给曹操一头大象。曹操很想知道这头大象有多重，就叫他手下的官员想办法把大象称一称。
这可是一件难事。大象是很庞大的动物，怎么称呢？那时候没有那么大的秤，人也没有那么大的力气把大象抬起来。官员们都围着大象发愁，谁也想不出办法。
正在这个时候，跑出来一个小孩子，他站到大人面前说：“我有办法，我有办法！”官员们一看，原来是曹操的小儿子曹冲。他们嘴里不说，心里在想：哼！大人都想不出办法来，一个5岁的小孩子，会有什么办法？
可是千万别瞧不起小孩子，这小小的曹冲就是有办法。他想的办法，就连大人一时也想不出来。曹操说：“你有办法快说出来，让大家听听。”曹冲说：“我称给你们看，你们就明白了。”
曹冲叫人牵着大象，跟着他到河边去。曹操还有那些官员们都想看看他到底怎么称，于是一起跟着来到河边。河边正好有只空着的大船。曹冲说：“把大象牵到船上去。”大象上了船，船就往下沉了一些。曹冲说：“齐水面在船帮上画一道记号。”记号画好了以后，曹冲又叫人把大象牵上岸来。这时候大船空着，船身就往上浮起一些来。大家看着，一会儿把大象牵上船，一会儿又把大象牵下船，心里说：“这孩子在玩什么把戏呀？”
接下来曹冲叫人挑来石块，装到大船上去。挑了一担又一担，船身又慢慢地往下沉了。
“行了，行了！”曹冲看见船帮上的记号齐了水面，就叫人把石块又一担一担地挑下船来。这时候，大家明白了：石头装上船和大象装上船，那船身下沉到同一记号上，可见，石头和大象是同样的重量；再把这些石块称一称，把所有石块的重量加起来，得到的总和不就是大象的重量了吗？
大家都说，这办法看起来简单，可是要不是曹冲做给大家看，大人还真想不出来呢。他们都夸曹冲聪明。
知识
lian
接
曹操是历史上有名的大枭雄，也是大文豪。他写的《短歌行》可谓家喻户晓，诗歌慷慨激昂，准妈妈不妨朗诵一下并细品其中的意境。
短歌行
——曹操
对酒当歌，人生几何？
譬如朝露，去日苦多。
慨当以慷，忧思难忘。
何以解忧？唯有杜康。
青青子衿，悠悠我心。
但为君故，沉吟至今。
……
fields.content_en:
**Title: Cao Chong Weighs the Elephant**

The king of Wu, Sun Quan, sent Cao Cao a giant elephant. Cao Cao was very curious about how much the elephant weighed, so he asked his officials to come up with a way to weigh it.

This was quite a challenge. Elephants are enormous animals—how could anyone weigh such a creature? There were no scales big enough back then, and no person was strong enough to lift an elephant. The officials stood around the elephant, puzzled and worried, unable to think of any solution.

Just then, a little boy ran out and stood in front of the grown-ups. "I have a way! I have a way!" The officials looked and realized it was Cao Cao's youngest son, Cao Chong. They didn't say anything out loud, but inside they thought: *Hmph! Even the adults can't figure this out. What could a five-year-old child possibly know?*

But you should never look down on children. This small Cao Chong did indeed have a clever plan—a plan that even the grown-ups couldn't think of at the time. Cao Cao said, "Tell us your idea quickly, let's all hear it." Cao Chong replied, "I'll show you, and then you'll understand."

Cao Chong had someone lead the elephant and followed them to the riverbank. Cao Cao and all the officials wanted to see exactly how he would do it, so they all followed along to the riverside. Luckily, there was a large empty boat right there. Cao Chong said, "Lead the elephant onto the boat." As the elephant climbed aboard, the boat sank a little lower into the water. Cao Chong said, "Mark the water level on the side of the boat." After the mark was made, Cao Chong had the elephant led off the boat again. Now that the boat was empty, it floated higher in the water. Everyone watched as the elephant was led on and off the boat, and they wondered, "What trick is this child playing?"

Next, Cao Chong had people carry loads of stones and place them onto the boat. One load after another was carried over, and the boat slowly sank lower and lower.

"Enough, enough!" Cao Chong said when the stones reached the mark on the boat. He told everyone to carry the stones off the boat, one load at a time. And then everyone understood: when the stones were on the boat and the elephant was on the boat, the vessel sank to the exact same mark. That meant the stones and the elephant weighed the same! And if they weighed all the stones and added up their total weight—that would be the weight of the elephant!

Everyone agreed that although the method seemed simple, the adults truly would never have thought of it if Cao Chong hadn't shown them. They all praised Cao Chong for being so clever.

**A Little Knowledge**

Cao Cao was a famous historical leader and also a great poet. His poem *Short Song Style* is known by many people. Its verses are bold and full of feeling—perhaps a future mother might like to read it aloud and savor its beautiful meaning.

*Short Song Style*
—Cao Cao

Sing while you drink, for how long is life?
Like morning dew, too many days have passed.
Sing with all your heart, for worries linger on.
What can ease these worries? Only wine can help.

Your black collar keeps lingering in my heart.
Because of you, I've hummed this tune till now.
...
fields.tips: 小孩子的潜能是无穷的，人在孩童时期的想象力可能是成人后的许多倍。宝宝能把日常生活中的某些行为用到游戏中去，比如，用小凳子当汽车开等。准爸爸准妈妈要注意开发胎宝宝的潜能啊。
fields.tips_en: Children's imaginations are truly boundless! They turn everyday objects into extraordinary adventures — a small stool becomes a roaring car, a blanket becomes a magical cape. Let's nurture those wonderful sparks in our baby's budding mind.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 雍正的冷笑话
fields.subtitle: 皇帝的另一面
fields.subtitle_en: The Emperor's Playful Side
fields.content:
雍正在大多数人的印象里都是冷漠、不苟言笑的，但他批示的折子却体现出他其实是个制造冷笑话的高手，非常睿智、幽默。
有个官员犯了罪，被关在狱中。在狱中他给雍正上了个悔罪的折子，希望能够得到赦免或者减轻刑罚。里面有两句话“辜负天恩，羞惧交并”，雍正在这两句话边批示道：“知儒惧死实甚，然羞则未也。”意思是说我知道你怕死怕得要命，不过羞愧就未必了。
雍正给另一个官员的折子的批示就更直接了，读起来感觉这些字都是带着表情的：“汝以朕为可欺乎？汝忘朕即位之时，已年过四十矣，官吏情伪朕尽知之。朕在藩邸时，即知汝名曾列弹章，汝又送朕礼物，冀朕在大行皇帝前转圜。汝此后其小心谨慎，一举一动，不能逃朕之洞鉴也。”意思是说你以为我好骗吗？你忘了我登基之时已经年过40了吗？我对你们这些官吏的情况都知道得详详细细的。我还是王爷的时候，你弹劾过我，还送过我礼物，希望我在先帝面前给你说好话。此后，你虽然小心谨慎，但一举一动，都没逃过我的眼睛。这个批示把这个官员的老底揭了个干净。想必这个官员看过之后，一定是脊背冒冷汗了。
因为宫里传召了一个戏班子，要搭台唱戏，有一个官员觉得此举不合规矩，就上折子阻止，接连上了3个。开始雍正也都没说什么，最后不耐烦了，在折子上批示道：“尔欲沽名，三折足矣。若再琐渎，必杀尔。”说你要博个美名，有这3个折子就足够了。如果再来啰唆，我就杀了你。
雍正还没有当皇帝的时候，经常微服出行。有一次到杭州，在涌金门看到一个书生在卖字，笔法非常精练老到，就站着多看了一会儿，最后还让书生给自己也写一副对联。对联里有个“秋”字，本来在右边的“火”字，书生却写到了左边。雍正纳闷儿，就问是不是写错了。书生不以为然，拿出一本名帖翻开给雍正看，里面的“秋”就是这样写的。雍正看他挺博学的，就问他为什么不考功名，反而在这里卖字。书生告诉雍正说自己家贫，妻儿老小都养不过来，根本没能力去考功名。雍正听后，慷慨解囊，赠送了书生一笔钱，让他别卖字了，去考个功名。临分别时，雍正还开玩笑说考了功名别忘了他。
书生谢过雍正后，就拿着钱进京了。后来他果真考中了，并且入翰林院供职。此时的雍正已经是皇帝了。他从名册上看到书生的名字，立刻想起了涌金门买字赠金的事，就召这个书生入宫。书生入宫后，雍正写了个“和”字，但是把“口”写在了左边，让人拿给书生看。书生不明就里，就说这是个错字。雍正什么也没说，只是给书生一道诏书，让他拿着去找浙江巡抚。
书生遵旨到了浙江巡抚处，将诏书给了浙江巡抚。浙江巡抚展开一看，上面写着让书生在涌金门再卖3年字，然后来翰林院供职。至此，书生才恍然大悟，当年那个资助自己的人正是雍正。雍正写个“和”字就是为了让他想起当年写的那个“秋”字以及当年那个资助他的人。可惜自己没想起来，还得再卖3年字。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Yongzheng's Cold Jokes**

Yongzheng is remembered by most people as cold and serious, but the notes he wrote on memorials show he was actually quite clever and had a wonderful sense of humor.

There was once an official who broke the law and was thrown into prison. While in jail, he wrote a memorial begging for forgiveness or a lighter sentence. He wrote two phrases: "I have failed the Emperor's grace, and shame and fear grip my heart." Yongzheng wrote beside these words: "I understand that you are very much afraid of death. But as for feeling ashamed—that is not so certain."

Yongzheng's note to another official was even more direct, so lively it feels as if the words themselves have expressions on their faces. He wrote: "Do you think I am easy to fool? Have you forgotten that I was already over forty when I became emperor? I know all about you officials and your tricks. Even back when I was still a prince, you wrote a letter criticizing me and also sent me gifts, hoping I would speak well of you to the late emperor. From now on, be careful. Every single thing you do will be seen clearly by me." This note laid the official bare. No wonder that man must have felt a chill run down his back after reading it.

Once, a theater troupe was invited into the palace, and an official worried this was against the rules, so he sent three separate memorials trying to stop it. At first, Yongzheng said nothing. But finally, grown impatient, he wrote on the last one: "If you want to win a reputation for honesty, these three memorials are enough. If you bother me again with more nonsense, I will have you killed."

Before he became emperor, Yongzheng often traveled incognito. One time in Hangzhou, at the Jiongin Gate, he saw a scholar selling calligraphy.
