Once upon a time, there was a little shepherd boy. No matter what questions people asked him, he always had a clever answer, and his fame traveled far and wide. When the king heard about him, he didn't believe someone could be so wise, so he invited the shepherd boy to the palace. The king said to him, "If you can answer my three questions, I will accept you as my own son." The boy asked, "What are the questions?"

The king said, "The first is: how many drops of water are in the sea?" The little shepherd boy replied, "Honored Majesty, please order all the rivers in the world to be blocked, so not a single drop of water flows into the sea, until I finish counting. Then I will tell you exactly how many drops are in the ocean."

The king then said, "The second question is: how many stars are in the sky?" The boy asked for a large white sheet of paper. Then he used a pen to poke many tiny dots on it, so small they were nearly invisible and impossible to count. Anyone who stared at it would grow dizzy. Then the shepherd boy said, "The stars in the sky are just as numerous as these dots on my paper. Please count them if you can." But no one could count them all.

The king could only ask his final question: "How many seconds are in eternity?" The boy answered, "In Pomerania there is a diamond mountain. It is two miles high, two miles wide, and two miles deep. Every hundred years a bird comes and pecks at the mountain with its beak. When the entire mountain has been worn away, only then will the first second of eternity have passed."

The king said, "You have answered my questions like a true wise man. From this day forward, you may live in the palace, and I will treat you as my very own son."

(From *Grimm's Fairy Tales*)
fields.tips: 国王的问题近乎刁难。遇到这种情况的时候，就要采取巧妙的方法回答。故事里聪明的小牧童不但避开了正面回答国王的难题，反而给国王出了难题。相信在妈妈肚子里就听着这些故事长大的小宝宝，长大后肯定也会善于观察、善于思考，能聪明地解决各种各样的难题。
fields.tips_en: The king's question was nearly a trick. When faced with such a challenge, the key is to respond with wit and grace. The clever young shepherd in the story not only avoided answering the king's hard question head-on, but he turned it around and posed a challenge of his own. We believe that the little one growing inside you, listening to stories like these, will grow up to be observant, thoughtful, and skilled at solving all sorts of problems.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 最好的礼物
fields.subtitle: 用心的礼物最有情意
fields.subtitle_en: Thoughtfulness Makes the Greatest Gift
fields.content:
小花狗生病了，大伙儿带来了最好的玩具，希望能够给小花狗解解闷儿。
小猫咪咪也来了。小黑猪偷看着咪咪，咪咪的手里什么也没有。大伙儿开始送玩具了。哇，有遥控飞碟，有声控老鼠，还有精致华贵得让人不敢碰的小轿车……
轮到咪咪了。大伙儿都把眼睛瞪得大大的，看着两手空空的咪咪。小黑猪更是眼睛一眨也不眨。没想到咪咪却说：“大伙儿都把眼睛闭上，我才好把玩具拿出来！”
大伙儿互相看看，只好把睁大的眼睛闭上。
一会儿，咪咪说：“睁开吧。”小黑猪睁眼一瞧，咪咪手里捧着个花花绿绿的小东西，毛茸茸的，又有趣又可爱。大伙儿都把脖子伸得长长的，想看个清楚。
咪咪手里的小东西十分灵活，东一蹦，西一跳，总往咪咪身后跑。咪咪想抓住它，可转了100圈还是没抓住。急得咪咪直朝大家吐舌头，那副滑稽相，逗得小花狗它们哈哈大笑。
表演结束了，大伙争着问咪咪玩具是从哪儿买来的。
这时，咪咪从地上站起来，拍拍裙子说：“这个玩具一分钱也没花，它就是我自己的尾巴呀！”
啊，大伙儿谁也没想到！
咪咪说：“这个玩具是我为小花狗精心设计的。我在尾巴上涂了颜色，卷成彩球的样子。看见小花狗那么开心地笑，我真高兴！”
躺在床上的小花狗说：“谢谢你，咪咪，你真好！”
小黑猪不好意思地挠挠头，嘿嘿地笑着说：“咪咪，可真有你的！这玩具可真有趣呀。”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Best Gift

Little Flower Dog was sick, so everyone brought their very best toys, hoping to cheer him up.
Little Kitty Mimi came too. Little Black Pig peeked at Mimi, but Mimi had nothing in her hands. Everyone else started giving their presents. Wow, there was a remote-controlled flying saucer, a voice-controlled mouse, and a delicate, beautiful little car that looked too fancy to even touch…
Then it was Mimi's turn. Everyone stared with their eyes wide open, watching Mimi with empty paws. Little Black Pig didn't even blink. But unexpectedly, Mimi said, "Everyone, close your eyes first. I need to get my toy!"
Everyone looked at each other and, well, closed their big, wide eyes.
After a moment, Mimi said, "Open them now." Little Black Pig opened his eyes and looked—Mimi was holding a colorful little thing, fluffy and fun and cute. Everyone stretched their necks out to see it clearly.
The little thing in Mimi's paws was very lively. It hopped here, jumped there, always running behind Mimi. Mimi tried to catch it, but after spinning around a hundred times, she still couldn't grab it. Mimi stuck out her tongue in frustration, and that silly look made Little Flower Dog and everyone laugh out loud.
When the show was over, everyone crowded around asking Mimi where she had bought the toy.
At that moment, Mimi stood up from the ground and patted her dress. "This toy cost not a single penny. It's my own tail!"
Ah, no one had thought of that!
Mimi said, "I designed this toy especially for Little Flower Dog. I painted colors on my tail and curled it up like a rainbow ball. Seeing Little Flower Dog smile so happily makes me truly glad."
Lying in bed, Little Flower Dog said, "Thank you, Mimi. You are so kind."
Little Black Pig scratched his head, embarrassed, and chuckled. "Mimi, you really are something! This toy is truly fun."
fields.tips: 最好的礼物一定是有趣的、用心的、真挚的。就好像准爸爸准妈妈现在充满爱意做的胎教。它或许不是最昂贵的，但却是最用心的，是送给胎宝宝最好的礼物。
fields.tips_en: The best gifts are always fun, heartfelt, and sincere. Just like the loving prenatal moments you and Daddy are sharing right now. It may not be the most expensive thing in the world, but it is made with so much love — and that makes it the very best gift you could ever give your little one.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 红青蛙
fields.subtitle: 爱惜本来的自我
fields.subtitle_en: Embracing Your True Self
fields.content:
小青蛙住在青蛙小院里，这里所有的青蛙都穿绿衣裳。小青蛙觉得这衣服很一般，一点儿都不美。小青蛙看见院子里的美人蕉，花儿是火红的，像火焰一样，真美！小青蛙找出画画用的红色水彩颜料，涂在自己身上，除了一对亮亮的眼睛，身子全都涂上了红色！
空中飞过一只小燕子，它惊奇地叫着：“看哪！荷叶上蹲着一只红青蛙，多美呀！”听了小燕子的赞美，小青蛙可乐啦，大声喊道：“我是一只与众不同的红青蛙！”
小青蛙肚子饿了，去捉绿蚱蜢。绿蚱蜢眼睛尖，看见一只红青蛙过来，“噗”的一声，跳进草丛里不见啦。“逃了一只绿蚱蜢，去捉一只大蝼蛄！”小青蛙悄悄地跳过来。那大蝼蛄真调皮，看见红青蛙来了，一声不响地钻进泥地里。小青蛙感到奇怪，喃喃地说：“怎么搞的，这些虫子都变得聪明啦？”小青蛙忙了一阵，没捉到虫子。“唉，今天运气真不好！”
突然，传来一阵“啪啦、啪啦”的响声。小青蛙转身一看，愣住了：“哎哟，一条大青蛇游来了！”大青蛇昂着头，吐着舌头，想吞吃小青蛙。小青蛙吓坏了，拼命地逃。它看见前面有个池塘，“扑通”一声，跳了下去。
小青蛙在池塘里游啊游，身上涂的红颜色洗掉了，变回了原来的绿衣裳。小青蛙这才明白，都怪自己。穿这件红衣裳，暴露目标，真显眼啊！
这时，只听见“扑通”一声，青蛙妈妈跳下池塘，游了过来。“孩子，你怎么啦？”青蛙妈妈问。小青蛙回答：“妈妈，你给我穿的绿衣裳真好，跟青草的颜色一模一样，是一种最佳‘保护色’。”
青蛙妈妈和小青蛙乐得呱呱叫。
知识
lian
接
青蛙是一种可爱的、对人类有益的小动物。在夏天的夜里，它们会一直“呱呱”地唱歌。青蛙有很多特别的地方：
青蛙在吞咽食物时会眨眼睛；
青蛙头上的两侧各有一个略微鼓着的小包包，那是它的耳膜。青蛙可以通过它听到声音；
青蛙是卵生的。卵孵化成蝌蚪，最后才变成青蛙；
青蛙的眼睛很特别，在迅速飞动的各种形状的小动物里，可以立即识别出它最喜欢吃的苍蝇和飞蛾，而对其他飞动着的东西和静止不动的景物都毫无反应；
青蛙是捉虫能手，一只蚊子飞过来，青蛙身子猛地向上一蹿，舌头一伸一缩，又落在地上，蚊子不见了，被青蛙吞进了肚子里，吃完它又原样坐好，等待着下一只害虫的到来；
青蛙是变温动物，体温会随着外界温度的变化而变化。
fields.tips: 青蛙是伪装高手，除了肚皮是白色的以外，头部、背部都是黄绿色的，很光滑、很软，还有花纹，可以使它隐藏在草丛中，捉害虫更容易些，也可以保护自己不被敌人发现。故事里的小青蛙幸亏洗掉了红衣裳，才避免了饿肚子。爸爸妈妈在培养宝宝的过程中，也要注意保护宝宝的儿童本性哦。
fields.tips_en: Frogs are masters of disguise! Apart from their white bellies, their heads and backs are yellow-green — smooth, soft, and patterned — allowing them to blend right into the grass. This helps them catch insects more easily and keep safe from danger. In the story, the little frog was lucky to wash off the red clothes and avoid going hungry. As you raise your child, remember to cherish and protect their natural, childhood spirit.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小黄鹂
fields.subtitle: 生活的意义
fields.subtitle_en: The Meaning of Life
fields.content:
一只小黄鹂第一次离开妈妈，自己外出捕虫。
当小黄鹂飞了一天，疲倦地回到家里时，妈妈问它都看到、听到些什么。
小黄鹂说：“除了虫子，我什么也没看到。”
妈妈失望了，说：“我们不是光为了虫子而生活的。”
小黄鹂想了想妈妈的话，若有所悟地睡着了。第二天它飞出去捕虫，又疲倦地飞回来了。
妈妈问它看到、听到些什么。
小黄鹂说：“我看到一只老白头翁真可怜，它老得已经不能捕虫了，我把捕到的虫子送给了它。”
“我还看到一只小百灵鸟，它的歌声真好听，我听了半天。我想，将来我也许会唱得比它更好听的。”
妈妈高兴极了，说：“你开始懂得怎样生活了！”
知识
lian
接
黄鹂是一种非常美丽的鸟，历来备受人们的喜爱。它以昆虫为主食，也是一种有益于园林的鸟，是人类的好朋友。黄鹂科鸟类以其艳丽的羽饰和悦耳的鸣声，构成大自然的点缀。
fields.content_en:
# Little Yellow Oriole

Once, a little yellow oriole left home by itself for the first time to find insects to eat.

When the little oriole flew all day and returned home tired, its mother asked what it had seen and heard.

The little oriole said, "I only saw insects."

Mother was disappointed. She said, "We do not live only for insects."

The little oriole thought about its mother's words and fell asleep with a quiet understanding. The next day it went out again to find insects and came back just as tired.

Mother asked what it had seen and heard.

The little oriole said, "I saw an old white-headed bird. It was so pitiful because it was too old to catch insects anymore, so I gave it the insects I had caught."

"I also saw a little lark, and its song was so beautiful that I listened to it for a long, long time. I thought, perhaps one day I can sing even more beautifully than it does."

Mother was overjoyed and said, "Now you are beginning to understand how to live!"

---

**Did You Know?**

The yellow oriole is a very beautiful bird, always loved by people. It eats mostly insects and helps protect gardens, making it a wonderful friend to humans. Oriole birds, with their bright colorful feathers and sweet songs, add beauty to our natural world.
fields.tips: 生活的意义并不是为了活着，而应该有广阔的天地，有梦想、有爱心，可以做许许多多喜欢的事情。“我们不是光为了虫子而生活的”，小黄鹂妈妈的话包含了一位母亲的期待。准爸爸准妈妈也应该让胎宝宝体会到更多生活的美妙之处。
fields.tips_en: The meaning of life is not simply to survive, but to explore a wide and wonderful world, to have dreams and a loving heart, and to do many things that bring us joy. As the little oriole's mother wisely said, 'We are not here only for worms.' Those words carry a mother's deepest hopes and wishes. Expecting parents can also help their baby feel the beauty and richness of life from within the womb.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 小马过河
fields.title_en: The Little Horse Crosses the River
fields.subtitle: 实践出真知
fields.subtitle_en: True Knowledge Comes Through Experience
fields.content:
有一天，妈妈把小马叫到身边说：“小马，你已经长大了，可以帮妈妈做事了。今天你把这袋粮食送到河对岸的村子去吧。”小马非常高兴地答应了。
小马驮着粮食飞快地来到了小河边。可是河上没有桥，只能自己蹚过去，可又不知道河水有多深。犹豫中的小马一抬头，看见了正在不远处吃草的牛伯伯。小马赶紧跑过去问道：“牛伯伯，您知道那河里的水深不深呀？”
身材高大的牛伯伯笑着说：“不深，不深，才到我的小腿。”小马高兴地跑回河边准备蹚过河去。它刚一迈腿，忽然听见一个声音说：“小马，小马，别下去，这河可深啦。”
小马低头一看，原来是小松鼠。小松鼠翘着它漂亮的尾巴，睁着圆圆的眼睛，很认真地说：“前两天我的一个伙伴不小心掉进了河里，河水就把它卷走了。”
小马一听没主意了。牛伯伯说河水浅，小松鼠说河水深。这可怎么办呀？只好回去问妈妈。马妈妈老远就看见小马低着头驮着粮食又回来了，心想它一定是遇到困难了，就迎过去问小马。小马哭着把牛伯伯和小松鼠的话告诉了妈妈。妈妈安慰小马说：“没关系，咱们一起去看看吧。”
小马和妈妈又一次来到河边。妈妈这回让小马自己去试探一下河水有多深。小马小心地试探着，一步一步地蹚过了河。噢，它明白了，河水既没有牛伯伯说的那么浅，也没有小松鼠说的那么深。只有自己亲自试过才知道。
小马深情地向妈妈望了一眼，心里说：“谢谢你了，好妈妈。”然后它转头向村子跑去，心里别提有多高兴了。
知识
lian
接
在我国传统文化中，不同的称呼通常代表不同类型的马：
儿马——公马
骒——母马
驹——小马
骠——黄色的马
骝——黑鬃、黑尾的红色马
骃——浅黑带白色的马
骅——枣红色的马
骊——黑色的马
骐——有青黑色纹理的马
骓——白蹄的黑马
骢——青、白杂毛的马
龙——纯白色的马
骁——强壮的马
骏——走得快的好马
骥——老马
fields.content_en:
Title: Little Horse Crosses the River

One day, Mama called little horse over and said, "Little horse, you've grown so big. Now you can help Mama with a task. Please carry this sack of grain across the river to the village on the other side." Little horse happily agreed.

Carrying the grain on his back, little horse trotted quickly to the edge of a small river. But there was no bridge—only the water, and little horse didn't know how deep it was. Just then, he looked up and saw Uncle Cow grazing nearby. Little horse hurried over and asked, "Uncle Cow, do you know if the river is deep or shallow?"

Uncle Cow, tall and kind, smiled and said, "Not deep at all! The water only reaches my lower legs." Little horse was delighted and trotted back to the riverbank, ready to wade across. But just as he lifted one leg, a voice called out, "Little horse, little horse—don't go in! The river is very deep!"

Looking down, little horse saw little squirrel. Squirrel held her beautiful tail high, her round eyes wide and serious. "Two days ago, my friend accidentally fell into the river, and the water swept him right away," she said.

Little horse felt lost. Uncle Cow said the water was shallow, but squirrel said it was deep. What should he do? There was only one thing to do—he had to go back and ask Mama.

Far away, Mama horse spotted little horse returning, head lowered and still carrying the grain. She knew something was troubling him, so she walked over to meet him. Little horse tearfully told Mama everything Uncle Cow and little squirrel had said. Mama gently comforted him and said, "It's all right, dear. Let's go take a look together."

Once again, Mama and little horse came to the riverbank. This time, Mama encouraged little horse to test the water himself. Carefully, step by step, little horse waded across. Oh—now he understood. The river was neither as shallow as Uncle Cow said, nor as deep as little squirrel said. You have to try for yourself to know the truth.

Little horse glanced affectionately at his Mama and thought to himself, "Thank you, dearest Mama." Then he turned and trotted toward the village, his heart overflowing with joy.

Knowledge:
In our traditional culture, different names are used for different kinds of horses:

Gong ma—stallion (male horse)
Ke ma—mare (female horse)
Ju—foal (young horse)
Piao—yellow horse
Liu—red horse with black mane and black tail
Yin—light black horse with white markings
Hua—chestnut-colored horse
Li—black horse
Qi—horse with bluish-black stripes
Zhui—black horse with white hooves
Cong—gray and white speckled horse
Long—pure white horse
Xiao—strong and brave horse
Jun—fast and fine horse
Ji—wise old horse
fields.tips: 小马过河的故事告诉我们很重要的一点：每个人都是独立的个体，别人的经验不一定适合自己。爸爸妈妈在养育孩子的时候也要注意这一点，别人的经验不能完全采纳，要通过判断才能借鉴，最终摸索出最适合自己教养孩子的方式。
fields.tips_en: The story of the little horse crossing the river teaches us an important lesson: everyone is unique, and what works for others may not work for you. When it comes to raising your child, remember that advice from others should be thoughtfully considered rather than simply copied. Every family will discover its own special way of nurturing and loving their little one.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 贤明的县令
fields.subtitle: 善恶分明来断案
fields.subtitle_en: Seeing Clearly the Difference Between Good and Evil
fields.content:
一天早晨，一个农夫挑了一担菜进城去卖。在街上，农夫拾到一袋钱，他数了一下，一共有15块银元。
回家后，农夫把15块银元交给了母亲。母亲说：“孩子，人家丢了钱，一定很着急，我们怎么能要人家的钱呢？赶快送还失主。说不定人家正找得着急呢！”这个农夫按照母亲的吩咐，赶回拾钱的地方，等待失主来领。
在前面不远处，农夫发现有一个人好像低着头在地上寻找什么东西，便连忙上前问他：“老弟，你丢钱了吧？我拾到了，现在还给你吧。”不等那人回答，农夫便将15块银元全都给了那个人。这时，有一些人围了上来。见此情景，有人提出，失主应给农夫一些赏钱。不料，这个人却十分吝啬地说：“我原本丢失的是30块银元，现在只找回来一半。我怎么能再分一些钱给他呢？”
农夫觉得那个人太不讲理了。自己如数将钱归还给他，他不但不谢，反而有诬蔑自己贪了一半的意思。农夫实在气愤不过，便跟那个人争吵起来。两个人互相扭打着来到县衙门的堂上。他们各自向县令叙说事情的缘由。
县令听后，心里已有几分底了。他对那个丢钱人的行为颇为生气。县令派人将农夫的母亲叫来，当面对质核实，证明农夫说的情况属实。接着，县令让农夫和那个丢钱人各自写下自己捡到和丢掉的钱数。于是他们分别写道：“我的确拾到15块银元”，“我确实丢了30块银元”。县令将两张纸捏在手上，对失主说：“你丢的是30块银元，而他拾到的是15块银元，可见这钱不是你的钱，而是上天赐给这位贤良母亲的养老钱。假若他拾到的是30块银元，那就是你的了。你到别的地方去找你的钱吧！”
那个人知道自己撒谎，自觉理亏，便也不敢再作狡辩，灰溜溜地离开了县衙。于是，县令把15块银元交给农夫的母亲，说：“你是位贤德的母亲，这钱就归你了！”
人们听说后都拍手叫好。
知识
lian
接
这位贤明的县令不愧是老百姓爱戴的清官。在我国历史上，也有一位以清正刚直著称的清官，名字叫包拯。由于他廉洁公正、不攀附权贵，故有“包青天”及“包公”之名。后世将他奉为神明崇拜，认为他是文曲星转世。
在影视剧中，包拯常被塑造为面部黝黑的形象，额上挂有一弯苍白明月，常被称为“包黑子”“包黑炭”。其实在历史上，他的皮肤并不黑。
fields.content_en:
**The Wise County Magistrate**

One morning, a farmer carried a basket of vegetables into town to sell. On the street, he found a bag full of money. He counted it and found fifteen silver coins.

When he got home, the farmer handed the fifteen silver coins to his mother. His mother said, "Child, whoever lost that money must be very worried. How can we keep someone else's money? You must take it back and return it to its owner. They are probably searching for it right now!" So the farmer rushed back to the place where he had found the money and waited for the owner to come claim it.

Not far ahead, the farmer noticed a man with his head bowed, searching the ground for something. He hurried over and asked, "Brother, did you lose some money? I found it. Let me give it back to you." Before the man could answer, the farmer handed him all fifteen silver coins. At that moment, a crowd gathered around. Seeing what happened, someone suggested that the owner should give the farmer some reward money. But surprisingly, the man said very stingily, "I originally lost thirty silver coins, and I have only found half. Why should I give any of my money to him?"

The farmer felt the man was being completely unreasonable. He had returned the money in full, and instead of saying thank you, the man seemed to accuse him of keeping half. The farmer was so angry that he began to argue with the man. The two of them grappled and eventually went together to the county magistrate's court. Each one told the magistrate what had happened.

After hearing both sides, the magistrate already understood something. He was quite displeased with the money-loser's behavior. The magistrate sent for the farmer's mother and had her confront the man face to face to verify the truth. It was confirmed that the farmer was telling the truth. Then the magistrate asked both the farmer and the money-loser to write down, respectively, how much they had found and how much they had lost. So they each wrote: "I truly found fifteen silver coins," and "I truly lost thirty silver coins." The magistrate held both pieces of paper in his hand and said to the loser, "You say you lost thirty silver coins, but he found only fifteen. This means this money is not yours. It is a gift from heaven — a pension for this good woman who raised such a virtuous son. Had he found thirty coins, then it would have been yours. Go look for your money elsewhere!"

The man knew he had lied and felt guilty. He did not dare to argue further and slinked away from the courthouse. So the magistrate handed the fifteen silver coins to the farmer's mother and said, "You are a wise and virtuous mother. This money belongs to you!"

When people heard about this, they all clapped and cheered.

**A Little Knowledge**

This wise magistrate was truly a fair and honest official loved by the people. In Chinese history, there was another famous upright and incorruptible judge named Bao Zheng. Because he was honest, just, and refused to flatter powerful people, he was known as "Judge Bao" or "Lord Bao." Later generations came to honor him almost like a god, believing he was the reincarnation of a star of wisdom.

In TV shows and movies, Bao Zheng is often shown with dark skin and a pale crescent moon on his forehead, which is why people nicknamed him "Black Bao." But in real history, his skin was not actually dark.
fields.tips: 那位贤良的母亲教儿子将拾来的钱交还失主，反遭讹诈；贤明的县令机智地将钱判给这位母亲，而那个讹诈、负心的人却不得好下场。人们都有自发的善心，对恶人有厌恶之心，对好人有怜悯之心。这是非常朴素、自然的感情。胎宝宝也能随着准妈妈的感受体会到这一点，将来他会成长为一个善恶分明的人。
fields.tips_en: A kind-hearted mother taught her son to return money he had found, but instead he was falsely accused. The wise magistrate cleverly gave the money to her, and the dishonest man met his just reward. Deep within every one of us is a natural sense of compassion for the good and disapproval of the bad. Your baby can feel these gentle emotions through you, growing up with a heart that knows right from wrong.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 有远见的母老鼠
fields.subtitle: 人无远虑必有近忧
fields.subtitle_en: Those Who Plan Ahead Need Not Worry
fields.content:
两只老鼠在屋梁上戏耍，一不小心，双双掉下来，落到一个大青缸里。真是因祸得福，大青缸里有很多米，两只老鼠立刻大吃起来。开始，老鼠还担心主人来，一吃饱就跳到缸外躲藏，饿了再跳进缸里吃米。两只老鼠一连吃了几天，也不见半个人影，它们就渐渐壮起胆儿，吃饱后躺在缸里睡大觉，不再出来躲藏了。
也许是主人故意让老鼠吃米，或者这缸米根本就没有主人，反正一直没有人来。两只老鼠天天在米缸里吃了睡、睡了吃，无忧无虑。缸里的米被一点儿一点儿吃下去，老鼠的身体一点儿一点儿肥大起来，最后竟大得像两只猫，完全失去鼠类的模样了。
舒服的日子过久了也会腻歪。有一天，母老鼠说：“我们到外面走走吧，很久不出去了。”公老鼠说：“好，我想出去看看那些穷哥们。”两只老鼠纵身一跳，以为轻易就能跳到缸外，谁知却听见“噗噗”两声，双双撞在缸壁上，落回缸里。两只老鼠使出全身力气再跳一次，结果更惨，不但又一次重重地撞在缸壁上，鼻子还流了很多血。以前稍一用力就能跳出去的，今天怎么跳不出去了呢？
两只老鼠仰头望望缸口，又互相对看一眼，发现大青缸比以前高多了。而它们，因为太肥胖，跳跃的高度已不及原来的三分之一。母老鼠问：“这可怎么办呢？”公老鼠说：“反正缸里有的是米，不出去了。”
母老鼠却不想一辈子待在缸里。它开始减少食量，每天只吃一餐，每餐只吃半饱，还不睡觉，一天到晚跳个不停，撞在缸壁上“噗噗”作响，弄得浑身是伤。公老鼠问它为什么要折磨自己。母老鼠说：“我在节食减肥，我还想跳出去。”公老鼠照样大吃大睡，还嘲笑母老鼠有福不会享。
母老鼠一天天消瘦，它的弹跳力却一天天增强，跳得越来越高。终于有一天，它奋力一跃，奇迹般地跳出了米缸！这时候，缸里已经没有多少米了。公老鼠也迫不及待地想跳出去，可它早已臃肿得像一头小猪。别说跳，连走路都必须像皮球一样慢慢滚动。
结果公老鼠吃完缸里的米后，就活活饿死在大青缸里了。母老鼠虽然历尽艰辛，遍体鳞伤，却成功地回到了外面的世界。
知识
lian
接
“鼠”字在甲骨文里像一只小老鼠张着嘴在咬东西；象形的鼠字，在从商朝到秦朝的演变、发展过程中，变化不少。在秦朝小篆中已趋向符号线条化；隶书的鼠字是在小篆的基础上演变来的，鼠头变成方形，鼠脚和鼠尾还有点象形，但鼠的形象已不明显了；楷书的鼠字吸收了隶书鼠字的特点，这也是今天所用的“鼠”字；草书则多见于艺术书画作品。
fields.content_en:
The Visionary Mother Mouse

Two mice were frolicking on the roof beam when, by accident, they both tumbled down into a large green ceramic jar. Fortunately, the jar was full of rice, so the two mice immediately dug in and began to eat their fill. At first, they worried the owner might come, so they would eat their fill and then jump out to hide, only to jump back in when they felt hungry again. But after days of eating, not a single person appeared, and they gradually grew bolder. After eating their fill, they would lie down in the jar and sleep soundly, no longer bothering to hide.

Perhaps the owner was deliberately letting the mice eat the rice, or perhaps this jar of rice didn't belong to anyone at all. Whatever the reason, no one ever came. Day after day, the two mice slept and ate and ate and slept in the rice jar, carefree and happy. The rice in the jar slowly disappeared grain by grain, and the mice grew fatter and fatter, until they were as big as two cats and had completely lost their mouse-like appearance.

Comfortable days can grow tiresome after a while. One day, the mother mouse said, "Let's go outside for a walk. We haven't been out in a long time." The father mouse said, "Good idea! I'd like to go see those poor buddies of mine." The two mice leaped as high as they could, thinking they could easily jump out of the jar. But instead, they heard two soft thuds as they bounced off the smooth sides and fell back into the jar. They gathered all their strength for another jump, but it was even worse this time—they slammed hard against the wall once again, and their noses started bleeding. How could they not get out today when they used to jump out so easily?

The two mice looked up at the opening of the jar, then glanced at each other, and realized the jar had grown much taller. Meanwhile, because they were so overweight, they could only jump about one-third of their original height. The mother mouse asked, "What should we do?" The father mouse replied, "Oh well, there's plenty of rice in the jar. Let's just stay in and eat."

But the mother mouse did not want to live her entire life in the jar. She began to eat less, having only one meal a day, and even then, only half-full. She skipped naps and spent the whole day jumping constantly, bouncing against the jar walls with soft thuds, covering herself in bruises and scratches. The father mouse asked her why she was punishing herself. The mother mouse said, "I'm dieting and exercising so I can jump out of here." The father mouse continued eating and sleeping as before, laughing at the mother mouse for not enjoying her good fortune.

Day by day, the mother mouse grew thinner, and her jumping ability grew stronger. She was able to leap higher and higher. Finally, one day she took a mighty leap—and to everyone's amazement—she jumped right out of the rice jar! By then, there was very little rice left in the jar. The father mouse, desperate to escape too, tried his best, but he was now so swollen and heavy that he resembled a little pig. He couldn't even jump anymore. All he could do was slowly roll along the ground like a ball.

In the end, the father mouse ate all the remaining rice and starved to death inside the jar. The mother mouse, though exhausted and covered in bruises and scratches, had made it back out to the world outside.

Knowledge
Character Note

The ancient Chinese character "鼠" (mouse/rat) in oracle bone script resembles a small mouse with its mouth open, biting on something. Throughout the evolution from the Shang Dynasty to the Qin Dynasty, the pictographic character changed considerably. By the time of the Qin Dynasty's small seal script, the character had begun to take on more symbolic, linear forms. The clerical script version of "鼠" evolved from the small seal script—the head became square-shaped, while the feet and tail still retained some pictographic quality, though the overall image of the mouse was no longer obvious. The regular script version of "鼠" absorbed features from the clerical script, and this is essentially the form used today. The cursive script style is most often seen in artistic calligraphy and paintings.
fields.tips: “人无远虑，必有近忧”。这个道理虽然古朴，但仍然很实用。掉在米缸里的两只老鼠，一只安于现状，另外一只开始为未来忧虑。最终有远虑的母老鼠得救了，公老鼠因为追求安逸，却丧失了性命。准爸爸准妈妈也一样，在胎宝宝到来之前就做好了准备，等怀孕后，一切便有条不紊地进行。夫妻之间的感情也不会因为胎宝宝的到来而受到影响。
fields.tips_en: 'Those who plan ahead need not worry about troubles near at hand.' Though this wisdom is old, it remains truly valuable. Two mice fell into a rice jar—one was content with the present, while the other began planning for the future. In the end, the thoughtful mother mouse was saved, while the one who sought only comfort lost everything. Similarly, when expecting parents prepare lovingly before their baby arrives, everything unfolds smoothly and naturally, and the bond between husband and wife grows even stronger.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 两只毛毛熊
fields.subtitle: 巧妙利用他人的好胜心
fields.subtitle_en: Cleverly Guiding a Competitive Spirit
fields.content:
有两只毛毛熊，一只是白色的，一只是黑色的。白色的叫小白，黑色的叫小黑。它俩都会捉鱼。为了比比谁更勤劳，它们还把自己捉的鱼挂在了屋檐下。意思是说：看看吧！看谁捉得多！
狡猾的小狐狸猜到了它俩的心思，就悄悄地找到小白，说：“这样吧，我来帮你一把。每天我都把小黑的鱼偷吃掉两条，这样一数鱼，保证你比它多！”小白听了快活得直蹦：“好！就这样！我一定为你保密！”
果然，第二天比赛时，小白胜了。可是，第三天比赛时，小白的鱼却比小黑的鱼少了一条。原来，狡猾的狐狸也找了小黑，对它说：“这样吧！我来帮你一把，我每天都把小白的鱼偷吃掉两条，这样一比，保证你多！”小黑也高兴得直蹦：“好！就这样！就这样！我一定为你保密！”
就这样，狡猾的小狐狸一会儿帮帮这个，一会儿帮帮那个，天天把肚子撑得圆滚滚的。而两只毛毛熊却一直蒙在鼓里。后来，当它们终于明白了这一切，要找小狐狸算账时，狡猾的小狐狸早就跑得无影无踪了。
fields.content_en:
**Title: Two Fluffy Bear Cubs**

Once upon a time, there were two fluffy bear cubs—one white and one black. The white one was named Xiao Bai, and the black one was named Xiao Hei. Both of them knew how to catch fish. To see who was harder working, they hung the fish they caught under the eaves of their houses. It was as if to say: Look! See who caught more!

A clever little fox guessed what they were thinking. He quietly went to Xiao Bai and said, "How about this? I'll give you a hand. Every day I'll sneak over and eat two of Xiao Hei's fish. Then when you count your catch, you'll surely have more than him!" Xiao Bai was so happy he could barely contain himself. "Great! That's perfect! I'll keep it a secret, I promise!"

Sure enough, on the second day's competition, Xiao Bai won. But by the third day, Xiao Bai actually had one fewer fish than Xiao Hei. It turned out the sly fox had also visited Xiao Hei. He said, "Let me help you! Every day I'll steal and eat two of Xiao Bai's fish. Then you'll definitely come out ahead!" Xiao Hei jumped for joy too. "Wonderful! That's wonderful! I'll keep it to myself, I promise!"

And so, the tricky little fox went from one to the other, helping this side one day and that side the next, until his belly was as round as a ball. Meanwhile, the two fluffy bear cubs remained completely in the dark. By the time they finally figured it all out and went looking for the fox to settle the score, the cunning little fox had long since vanished without a trace.
fields.tips: 故事里的小狐狸很狡猾，准爸爸准妈妈要告诉胎宝宝：可不能像狐狸那样干损人利己的事情哦。为了贪慕虚荣而损害别人的利益就更不可取了。
fields.tips_en: The clever fox in this story may seem clever, but expecting parents should share with their little one that being kind is far better than being cunning. It is never right to harm others just to satisfy one's own pride or desires. Let us raise our children with gentle hearts and honest intentions.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 三个和尚
fields.subtitle: 齐心协力才能成事
fields.subtitle_en: Unity Brings Success
fields.content:
山上有座小庙，庙里有个小和尚。他每天挑水、念经、敲木鱼，给观音菩萨案桌上的净水瓶添水，夜里不让老鼠来偷东西，生活过得安稳自在。
不久，来了个高个子和尚。他一到庙里，就把半缸水喝光了。小和尚叫他去挑水，高个子和尚心想一个人去挑水太吃亏了，便要小和尚和他一起去抬水。两个人只能抬一只水桶，而且水桶必须放在扁担的中央，两人才心安理得。这样总算还有水喝。
后来，又来了个胖和尚。他也想喝水，但缸里没水。小和尚和高个子和尚叫他自己去挑。胖和尚挑来一担水，立刻独自喝光了。从此谁也不挑水，三个和尚就没水喝了。
大家各念各的经，各敲各的木鱼。观音菩萨面前的净水瓶也没人添水了，花草枯萎了。夜里老鼠出来偷东西，谁也不管。结果老鼠猖獗，打翻烛台，燃起大火。三个和尚这才一起奋力救火。大火扑灭了，他们也觉醒了。从此三个和尚齐心协力，自然也就有水喝了。
知识
lian
接
《三个和尚没水喝》的民间故事家喻户晓，也因此被改编后拍成了动画片。动画片的片名就叫《三个和尚》。它形式异常鲜活、有趣，特别适合孕期准妈妈观看。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Three Monks

On the hill there was a small temple, and in the temple lived a little monk. Every day he carried water, chanted scriptures, and struck the wooden fish, refilling the pure-water vase on Guanyin Bodhisattva's table and chasing away the mice at night. His life was peaceful and carefree.

Soon, a tall monk arrived. The moment he got to the temple, he drank half a jar of water in one go. The little monk asked him to go carry water, but the tall monk thought it wasn't fair to go alone, so he asked the little monk to help him carry water in a bucket. The two could only lift one bucket at a time, and they only felt comfortable when the bucket sat right in the middle of the carrying pole. But at least there was still water to drink.

Later, a chubby monk came too. He also wanted some water, but the jar was empty. The little monk and the tall monk told him to go fetch it himself. The chubby monk brought back a load of water, then drank it all by himself. From then on, no one went to carry water anymore, and the three monks had no water to drink.

Each one read his own scriptures and struck his own wooden fish. No one refilled the pure-water vase in front of Guanyin Bodhisattva, and the flowers and plants began to wither. At night the mice came out to steal food, and no one cared. Soon the mice ran wild, knocking over a candle stand and starting a big fire. Only then did the three monks work together to fight the flames. After the fire was put out, they finally woke up to the truth. From that day on, the three monks worked as one, and there was always water to drink.

Knowledge

The folk tale "The Three Monks Had No Water to Drink" is well-known by everyone, and it was adapted into an animated film called *The Three Monks*. Its lively and fun style makes it especially wonderful for an expectant mother to watch during pregnancy.
fields.tips:
一个呀和尚挑呀么挑水喝，
嘿嘿，
挑呀么挑水喝。
咿咿，
挑呀么挑水喝。
……
准妈妈孕期不妨听听这首儿时就耳熟能详的欢快歌曲，相信胎宝宝会喜欢这快活的旋律。
fields.tips_en: One little monk goes fetching water, hee hee, fetching water for him to drink. Yi yi, fetching water for him to drink. …… During your pregnancy, dear mom-to-be, why not hum along to this cheerful childhood tune? Your little one will surely delight in its bright, bouncy melody.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 以德报怨
fields.subtitle: 坏事可能变成好事
fields.subtitle_en: A Bad Turn Can Become a Good One
fields.content:
魏国的大夫宋就被派到一个小县去担任县令。这个县正好位于魏国与楚国的交界处，这地方盛产西瓜。虽然同处一地，可是两国村民种西瓜的方式和态度却大不一样。
魏国这边的村民种瓜十分勤快，他们经常担水浇瓜，所以西瓜长得快，而且又甜又香。楚国这边的村民种瓜十分懒惰，又很少给西瓜浇水，所以他们的瓜长得又慢又不好。楚国这边的县令看到魏国的西瓜长得那么好，便责怪自己的村民没有把瓜种好。而楚国的那些村民却没有从自己身上找原因，只是一味怨恨魏国的村民，嫉妒他们把瓜种得那么大、那么香甜。于是，楚国这边的村民就想方设法去破坏魏国村民的劳动成果。每天晚上，楚国村民轮流摸到魏国的瓜田，踩他们的瓜，扯他们的藤，这样，魏国村民种的瓜每天都有一些被毁掉了。
魏国村民发现这个情况后，十分气愤，他们也打算夜间派人偷偷过去破坏楚国的瓜田。一位年纪大的村民劝阻大家说：“我们还是把这件事报告给县令宋就，向他请示该怎么办吧？”
大家来到宋就的县衙。宋就耐心地劝导本国的村民说：“为什么要这么心胸狭窄呢？如果你来我往没完没了地这般闹下去，只会结怨越来越深，最后把事态闹大，引起祸患。我看最好的办法是，你们不计较他们的无理行为，每天都派人去给他们的西瓜浇水。最好是在夜间悄悄进行，不声不响地，不要让他们知道。”
魏国村民依照宋就的话去做了。于是，从这以后，西边楚国的瓜一天天长得好起来。楚国村民发现，自己的瓜田像是每天都有人浇过水，感到很奇怪。互相一问，谁也不知道是怎么回事。于是他们开始暗中观察，终于发现为他们的西瓜浇水的正是魏国的村民。楚国的村民大受感动。
很快，这件事情被楚国县令知道了，他既感激、高兴，又自愧不如魏国县令。他把这些情况写下来报告给了楚王。楚王也同样很受感动，同时也深感惭愧和不安。
后来，楚王备了重金派人送给魏王，希望与魏国和好。魏王欣然同意了。此后，楚、魏两国开始友好起来，边境的两国村民也亲如一家。两边种的西瓜都同样又大又甜。
（选自《中国古代寓言故事》）
知识
lian
接
魏国和楚国均为战国七雄之一，春秋时期和战国时期无数次战争使诸侯国的数量大大减少。到战国后期，仅剩下七个实力较强的诸侯国，分别为齐、楚、燕、韩、赵、魏、秦，合称为“战国七雄”。
战国时期，出现了诸子百家。这是中国思想、学术发展的黄金时期，史称“百家争鸣”，是各种文化百花齐放的一个历史阶段。
fields.content_en:
Title: Repaying Injury with Kindness

The great minister Song Jiu from the State of Wei was sent to serve as the magistrate of a small county. This county happened to sit right on the border between the States of Wei and Chu, and the land there was perfect for growing watermelons. Even though the villagers on both sides lived in the same region, the way they grew their watermelons was completely different.

On the Wei side, the villagers worked very hard at farming. They often carried water to irrigate their melon patches, so their watermelons grew quickly and were sweet and delicious. On the Chu side, the villagers were much lazier and rarely watered their fields, so their melons grew slowly and were not very good. The Chu county magistrate saw how wonderful the Wei watermelons were and scolded his own villagers for not taking better care of the crops. But instead of looking at what they could do better themselves, the Chu villagers simply blamed the people of Wei and grew jealous that their melons were so big and sweet. So the Chu villagers came up with ways to ruin the labor of the Wei farmers. Every night, they would take turns sneaking into the Wei melon fields, stepping on their plants and pulling at their vines, so that some of the Wei villagers' melons were destroyed each day.

When the Wei villagers discovered what was happening, they were very angry and decided to sneak out at night to destroy the Chu melon fields in return. An elder among them stopped everyone and said, "Let us report this to Magistrate Song Jiu and ask him what we should do."

So the villagers went to Magistrate Song Jiu's office. Song Jiu patiently counseled his own people, saying, "Why be so narrow-minded? If we keep responding to each other with harm after harm, the resentment will only grow deeper and deeper, and the trouble will only get bigger. I think the best thing to do is simply let go of their unkind behavior. Every night, send someone to water the Chu villagers' melon patch for them. Do it quietly at night, without making a sound, so they never even know who is doing it."

The Wei villagers followed Magistrate Song Jiu's advice. From that day on, the melons on the Chu side grew better and better each day. The Chu villagers noticed that their fields seemed to be watered every day, and they were very puzzled. They asked each other, but no one knew the answer. So they began to watch secretly, and eventually discovered that it was the Wei villagers who were watering their melon patch after all. The Chu villagers were deeply moved.

Soon, the Chu county magistrate heard about this. He felt grateful and happy, but also somewhat ashamed compared to the magistrate of Wei. He wrote everything down and reported it to the King of Chu. The king was equally touched, and he felt a deep sense of shame and regret as well.

Later, the King of Chu prepared a heavy gift and sent it to the King of Wei, hoping to make peace with the State of Wei. The king of Wei gladly agreed. From then on, the States of Chu and Wei became friendly toward each other, and the villagers on both sides of the border lived together like family. The watermelons grown on both sides were equally big and sweet.

---

About this story

The States of Wei and Chu were both among the Seven Warring States. The countless wars during the Spring and Autumn Period and the Warring States Period greatly reduced the number of kingdoms. By the late Warring States Period, only seven powerful states remained: Qi, Chu, Yan, Han, Zhao, Wei, and Qin.

During the Warring States Period, many great schools of thought emerged in China. It was a golden age of ideas and learning, known as the "Hundred Schools of Thought," when many different philosophies and cultures flourished together.
fields.tips: 不要采取“以眼还眼，以牙还牙”的态度去激化矛盾。宽宏大量，以德报怨，反而会促使矛盾缓解，使坏事变成好事。准妈妈也一样，要常怀一颗乐观的心，即使生活中遇到不愉快的事情，也不要过于较真，也许多一点儿爱心与耐心，会让自己收获一份好心情。这对胎宝宝的发育很有好处。
fields.tips_en: Instead of escalating conflict with a tit-for-tat attitude, choose generosity and kindness—it can ease tensions and turn difficult moments into something beautiful. Similarly, dear mom-to-be, keep a hopeful and optimistic heart. When life brings unpleasant moments, try not to dwell on them too heavily. A little extra love and patience can fill you with warmth and joy, which is wonderful for your baby's development.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 知识的光亮
fields.subtitle: 学习永远也不晚
fields.subtitle_en: It's Never Too Late to Learn
fields.content:
晋平公是春秋时期晋国的国君，他政绩不凡，学问也很好。在70岁的时候，他依然还希望多读点儿书，多长点儿知识，总觉得自己所掌握的知识实在是太有限了。可是70岁的人再去学习，困难是很多的。晋平公对自己的想法总是不自信，于是他去询问他的一位贤明的臣子师旷。
师旷是一位双目失明的老人，他博学多智。虽然他的眼睛看不见，但心里亮堂着呢。晋平公问师旷：“你看，我已经70岁了，年纪的确老了，可是我还很希望再读些书，长些学问，又总是没有信心，总觉得是否太晚了呢？”
师旷回答说：“您说太晚了，那为什么不把蜡烛点起来呢？”
晋平公不明白师旷在说什么，便说：“我在跟你说正经话，你跟我瞎扯什么？哪有做臣子的随便戏弄国君的呢？”
师旷一听，乐了。他连忙说：“大王，您误会了。我这个双目失明的臣子，怎么敢随便戏弄大王呢？我也是在认真地跟您谈学习的事呢。”
晋平公说：“此话怎么讲？”
师旷回答说：“我听说，人在少年时代好学，就如同获得了早晨温暖的阳光一样。那太阳越照越亮，时间也长久。人在壮年的时候好学，就好比获得了中午明亮的阳光一样，虽然中午的太阳已走了一半，可它的力量很强、时间也还有许多。人到老年的时候好学，虽然已日暮，没有了阳光，可他还可以借助蜡烛啊。蜡烛的光亮虽然不怎么明亮，可是只要获得了这点儿烛光，尽管有限，也总比在黑暗中摸索要好多了吧。”
晋平公恍然大悟，高兴地说：“你说得太好了，的确如此！我有信心了。”
诚然，不爱学习，即使大白天睁着眼睛，也只能两眼一抹黑；只有经常学习，不论年少年长，学问越多心里越亮堂，才不至于盲目处事、糊涂做人。
（选自《中国古代寓言故事》）
fields.content_en:
Title: The Light of Knowledge

King Jin Ping was a ruler of the State of Jin during the Spring and Autumn period. He was known for his excellent leadership and his love of learning. Even at the age of seventy, he still wished to read more and learn more, always feeling that what he already knew was too little. But learning at seventy is not easy, and the King often felt unsure about his desire to keep studying. So he went to ask his wise minister, Shi Kuang, for advice.

Shi Kuang was an old man who could not see, but he was full of knowledge and wisdom. Though his eyes were dark, his heart was bright. The King asked him, "I am already seventy years old. I still want to read and learn, but I have no confidence. Do you think it is too late?"

Shi Kuang replied, "If you think it is too late, then why not light a candle?"

The King did not understand. He said, "I am speaking to you seriously. Why are you joking with me? How dare a minister tease his ruler?"

Shi Kuang smiled gently. He quickly said, "Great King, you misunderstand. How could a blind minister like me ever dream of teasing you? I am being very serious about learning, just as you are."

The King asked, "Then what do you mean?"

Shi Kuang answered, "I have heard that when a young person loves to learn, it is like the warm sunshine of early morning. The sun shines brighter and brighter, and it has many hours ahead. When a strong adult loves to learn, it is like the bright noon sun. Though the day is already halfway over, the sun is still powerful and there is still much time. And when an old person loves to learn, though the sun has set, they can still light a candle. The candlelight may not be very bright, but even a little light is far better than groping around in total darkness, isn't it?"

The King's face lit up with understanding. He happily said, "You are so right! Now I feel confident indeed."

And truly, without the love of learning, even with our eyes wide open in broad daylight, we would still see nothing but darkness. But those who keep learning—whether young or old—find their hearts growing brighter and brighter, and they can face life with clarity and kindness.

(Based on "Ancient Chinese Fables")
fields.tips: 知识可以给人指引前进的方向。准爸爸准妈妈给胎宝宝讲故事，就是给胎宝宝灌输知识，给胎宝宝多一些有益的刺激，让宝宝以后的人生之路更顺利。活到老学到老，人的一生，都不应该放弃学习。
fields.tips_en: Knowledge lights the path ahead. When mom and dad read stories to their little one, they are sharing knowledge and offering gentle, meaningful stimulation that can help make the journey of life smoother. From childhood to old age, learning is a gift we carry forever—never set it down.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 靠什么取暖
fields.subtitle: 知识比蜡烛更温暖
fields.subtitle_en: Knowledge Is Warmer Than Candlelight
fields.content:
有一年冬天，天气寒冷，阿凡提与几位朋友打赌说，他能在这冰天雪地里，在野外过上一夜而不被冻死。
“阿凡提，如果你真能这样，我们将给你两枚金币。”朋友们说道。
“一言为定！”阿凡提说。
当晚，阿凡提带上一本书和蜡烛，到野外度过了一个对他来说最寒冷的夜晚。
天亮后，阿凡提哈着气、搓着手跑回村里向朋友们索要打赌钱。朋友们惊诧地问他：“阿凡提，难道你没有用任何取暖的东西吗？”
“没有哇！”阿凡提耸耸肩膀说。
“连一支蜡烛也没点吗？”朋友们又问。
“我是点了一支蜡烛，可我是用它来照明看书的！”阿凡提说。
“蜡烛不仅可以照明，它也有热度，你肯定用它取暖了，这样不能算你赢。”朋友们耍赖道。
阿凡提没有争辩，默默地走了。过了一个月，阿凡提请这几位朋友到家吃饭。可朋友们坐在客厅里等了好几个小时，肚子饿得咕噜噜直叫，阿凡提还是不端饭来招待。朋友们等得不耐烦了，出去想看个究竟。他们拥进厨房，发现阿凡提架了一口大锅，锅底下点着一支蜡烛正烧着。锅里一点儿热气都不冒。
“阿凡提，用蜡烛能做熟饭吗？”朋友们取笑他说。
“你们说蜡烛有热度，我从一大早就用蜡烛烧饭，可到现在都做不熟，我也感到非常奇怪。”阿凡提回答道。
（选自《阿凡提的故事》）
fields.content_en:
# Title: What Did He Use to Stay Warm?

One winter, the weather was bitterly cold. Afanti made a bet with some friends, saying he could spend the night out in the frozen wilderness without freezing to death.

"If you can really do that, we'll give you two gold coins," his friends said.

"It's a promise!" Afanti replied.

That night, Afanti took a book and a candle and spent the coldest night of his life out in the wild.

When morning came, Afanti ran back to the village blowing on his hands and rubbing them together to ask his friends for the wager money. His friends were amazed. They asked, "Afanti, didn't you use anything to keep warm?"

"No, I didn't!" Afanti shrugged his shoulders.

"Didn't even light a candle?" his friends asked again.

"I did light a candle, but only to read by!" Afanti said.

"Candles give light, but they also give off heat. You definitely used it to stay warm. That doesn't count as you winning!" his friends argued.

Afanti didn't argue back and quietly walked away. A month later, Afanti invited those friends over for a meal. But hours passed while his friends waited in the living room, their bellies rumbling with hunger, and still Afanti brought no food. Growing impatient, they went out to see what was going on. They rushed into the kitchen and found Afanti with a large pot on a stand, a single candle flickering underneath it. Not a single wisp of steam rose from the pot.

"Afanti, can you cook a meal with just a candle?" his friends teased him.

"You said candles give off heat, so I've been cooking with a candle since early morning. But the food still isn't done, and I'm very puzzled too," Afanti answered.

(From *The Stories of Afanti*)
fields.tips: 烛光可以让准妈妈的心情变得柔和。在冥想的时候，准妈妈可以使用一些适合孕期使用的熏香蜡烛，效果会特别好。但是一定要记得在使用熏香的时候，要咨询医生和专业人士，因为很多熏香在孕期使用会对胎宝宝造成伤害。
fields.tips_en: The soft glow of a candle can soothe a expectant mother's heart. During quiet meditation, using pregnancy-safe scented candles can be especially calming. But always remember to consult your doctor or a specialist before using any aromatherapy candles, as some fragrances may not be safe during pregnancy.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 勇敢的鹦鹉
fields.subtitle: 学会借助外力
fields.subtitle_en: Learning to Ask for Help
fields.content:
有一只鹦鹉，离开家去看外面更广阔的世界。飞了几天，它又累又饿地来到了一座山林，打算暂时在这里安身。一只小松鼠看到了这只来自异乡的鹦鹉，马上蹦蹦跳跳地跑遍了整个山林，把这个消息告诉给所有的动物：“快去看呢，来客人了，来客人了！”动物们为鹦鹉举行了盛大的欢迎仪式：鸟儿们唱起动听的歌，小鹿们翩翩起舞，小猴们为鹦鹉采来了好多好多美味的浆果，让它吃了个饱。鹦鹉对此十分感动。
在接下来的几个月中，所有的飞禽走兽都待鹦鹉特别好，鹦鹉也尽自己的能力为大家做事，大家都很喜欢它。
虽然生活得很快乐，但是时间一长，鹦鹉不禁思念起自己的家乡来。于是它向大家告别说：“大家这么多天对我的照顾，我非常感激，但我必须回家去了。希望你们多多保重。”动物们依依不舍地把鹦鹉送了一程又一程，还是不得不分手了。
过了些日子，不幸的事情发生了。这座山林忽然起了大火。这场火烧得可厉害了，烈焰滚滚，映红了半边天，百里之外都看得见。山林中的动物们无处可逃，死伤无数，情景让人惨不忍睹。
鹦鹉远远地望见了这边的大火，心中暗叫“不好”。它飞去求助天神，并不辞劳苦地日夜赶路，赶到了着火的山林边。它一次次地飞到附近的河边，将羽毛在水中沾湿，然后把水洒向山林。也不知这样来来回回飞了多少趟，鹦鹉累得头昏眼花，几次险些被热浪吞没，身上的羽毛也被烧焦了。但是火势一点儿也没有减弱，反而越烧越旺。鹦鹉毫不气馁，还是不断地洒着水。
天神对鹦鹉说：“你也太自不量力了，凭你用羽毛洒的那一点儿水，是根本扑灭不了山火的，你这是何必呢？搞不好还会把自己的性命都搭进去！”鹦鹉回答说：“我知道我也许帮不了什么忙，但您可以帮助我。我曾经寄住在这里，这里所有的动物都非常善良，待我非常好。无论如何，我一定要为它们竭尽全力，绝不能眼睁睁地看着它们活活被烧死！”
天神听了这番话，很受感动，立即扑灭了山林大火。鹦鹉的朋友们终于得救了。
（选自《中国古代寓言故事》）
知识
lian
接
鹦鹉的“口技”在鸟类中的确是十分超群的。人们对鹦鹉最为钟爱的技能当属效仿人言。事实上，这是一种条件反射、机械模仿而已。这种仿效行为在科学上也叫效鸣。由于鸟类没有发达的大脑皮层，因而它们没有思想和意识，不可能懂得人类语言的含义。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Brave Parrot

Once there was a parrot who left home to see the wider world. After flying for several days, tired and hungry, it arrived at a mountain forest and decided to stay there for a while. A little squirrel spotted the parrot from a faraway land and immediately hopped all through the forest to share the news with every animal: "Come and see! A guest has arrived!" The animals threw a grand welcome party for the parrot. The birds sang beautiful songs, the deer danced gracefully, and the monkeys gathered plenty of delicious berries so the parrot could eat its fill. The parrot was deeply moved.

Over the next few months, all the birds and beasts treated the parrot very well, and the parrot did everything it could to help everyone. Everyone loved it.

Although life was happy, the longer it stayed, the more the parrot began to miss its hometown. So it said goodbye to everyone: "Thank you all so much for taking such good care of me. But I must go home now. Please take good care of yourselves." The animals reluctantly walked with the parrot as far as they could before they had to part.

Some days later, something terrible happened. A huge fire broke out in the mountain forest. The flames were so fierce, painting half the sky red, that they could be seen from miles away. The animals in the forest had nowhere to run, and many were killed or injured. It was a heartbreaking scene.

The parrot saw the fire from afar and knew right away something was terribly wrong. It flew to seek help from the gods, traveling day and night without rest, until it reached the burning forest. It flew again and again to a nearby river, wetting its feathers with water, and then sprinkled the water toward the forest. No one knows how many times it flew back and forth. The parrot grew dizzy and nearly lost its life several times to the scorching heat, and its own feathers were singed. But the fire showed no sign of weakening — it only grew fiercer. Still, the parrot refused to give up and kept sprinkling water.

The gods said to the parrot, "You are far overestimating yourself. That little water on your feathers can never put out a forest fire. Why are you doing this? You could easily lose your own life!" The parrot replied, "I know I may not be able to help, but you can help me. I once stayed here, and all these animals were so kind to me, treating me with such warmth. No matter what, I must do everything I can for them. I cannot simply stand by and watch them burned alive!"

Moved by these words, the gods immediately extinguished the forest fire. The parrot's friends were finally saved.
fields.tips: 故事中的鹦鹉是重感情、机智勇敢、知恩图报等美德的化身。在朋友、亲人遇到危险或困难的时候，我们应该伸出援助之手。不过，要权衡自身的力量，不要做自身力所不能及的事情。故事中的鹦鹉借助天神的外力很对，但冒着丢掉生命的危险，是对自身的不负责任。准爸爸准妈妈可以教给胎宝宝，应学习鹦鹉重感情、知恩图报的美德，但有危险时，要先自救再救人，同时要求助身边那些有能力帮助自己的人。
fields.tips_en: The parrot in our story embodies loyalty, wisdom, courage, and gratitude. When friends or family face danger or hardship, we should reach out a helping hand. Yet we must also be wise about our own limits and avoid taking on more than we can handle. The parrot was right to call upon heavenly help, but risking its own life would have been careless. Dear parents, you can share with your little one the parrot's beautiful qualities—loyalty and gratitude—while also teaching that when danger comes, it's important to stay safe first and then seek help from those who can truly assist.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 谁更有力量
fields.subtitle: 让人臣服的不是暴力
fields.subtitle_en: It Is Not Force That Wins Hearts
fields.content:
关于太阳和风谁更有力量的问题，它们之间发生了多次争吵。
这一天，它们又为此争吵起来。为了给这个问题以明确的答案，最后它们决定，拿一个路人来测试它们的力量。就是看谁能脱下那个路人的斗篷，最先让行人脱下者，自然就是胜利者。
风首先开始了。只见狂风骤起，转眼间，山上的树木一棵棵被连根拔起，森林几乎变成了一片废墟。那位路人见狂风大作，急忙跑到山脚下，躲避起来。随后，那斗篷被他更结实地系在了身上。哦，风使出了全力，可一切全是白费。
轮到太阳上场了。在天空，它透过一片云，将异常炽热的光线朝那可怜的路人身上汇聚。哦，那路人简直要被烤化了。“啊，太热了！热死了！”他痛苦地说，“简直就像是在火炉里，叫人没法忍受！”于是，他不得不脱下了斗篷，跑到大树下去乘凉。
（选自《伊索寓言》）
fields.content_en:
Title: Who Is Stronger?

About whether the sun or the wind is stronger, they had many arguments back and forth. One day, they started arguing about it again. To find a clear answer, they finally decided to test their strength on a traveler—whichever could make the traveler take off his cloak first would be the winner.

The wind went first. A fierce storm suddenly rose, and in a blink, the trees on the mountain were torn up by their roots, and the forest was nearly turned into ruins. The traveler saw the wild wind and hurried to the foot of the mountain to take shelter. Then he tied his cloak even more tightly around himself. Oh, the wind used all its might, but everything was in vain.

It was the sun’s turn now. In the sky, it shone through a cloud, focusing its very warm light onto the poor traveler. Oh, the traveler felt like he was being roasted. "Ah, it's so hot! So hot!" he said in pain. "It feels like standing inside an oven—I can't stand it!" So he had no choice but to take off his cloak and ran to sit under a big tree to cool off.

(Picked from Aesop's Fables)
fields.tips: 其实太阳和风都有力量，只是看用在什么地方。因此，不要盲目地和别人比较。别人的强项也许是自己的弱项，而自己的强项别人也不一定能比得上。爸爸妈妈也不要将自己的孩子和别的孩子做无谓的比较啊。
fields.tips_en: Actually, both the sun and the wind have their own strength—it simply depends on how they are used. So, there is no need to blindly compare yourself with others. What another person excels at might be your weakness, while your own strengths may be something others cannot match. Mom and Dad, please also avoid making unnecessary comparisons between your child and other children.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 谁是好人
fields.subtitle: 别从表面判断好坏善恶
fields.subtitle_en: Do Not Judge Good or Evil by Appearances
fields.content:
一天，小老鼠趁着妈妈不注意，又偷偷地溜出了家门，直到中午才回来。一到家，它就兴奋地对妈妈说：“妈妈，我刚刚出去玩儿的时候，看到两个奇怪的动物！”
鼠妈妈微笑着对小老鼠说：“是这样吗？你就讲给我听听吧。”
小老鼠点了点头，说：“我出了家门以后，跑得飞快，一直跑到了院子里。在那里，我看见了第一只可怕的动物！它长着花花绿绿的毛，伸着脖子，发出难听的‘喔喔喔’的声音，吓得我直打哆嗦！”
鼠妈妈对小老鼠说：“这是院子里的那只小公鸡！”
小老鼠又说：“这个奇怪的家伙使劲儿拍打着翅膀，可把我给吓坏了。我急忙就跑了。刚跑没多远，在院子里的窗台上，我又看见了一个可爱的动物！它身上有着柔软的毛和漂亮的斑纹，还有一条长长的尾巴，叫声也非常温柔。”
鼠妈妈赶紧问：“这个‘可爱’的动物的叫声是不是‘喵喵喵’的？”
小老鼠高兴地接着说：“对呀！对呀！您也认识它吗？我还想和它打招呼呢，但看见小公鸡凶恶的样子就赶快跑了！”
鼠妈妈气得哭笑不得，抱起可爱的小老鼠，对它说：“我可爱的儿子，你知道吗，那个‘喵喵’叫的家伙是猫，它是我们老鼠的天敌。你要是去和它打招呼，它肯定会毫不犹豫地一口把你吃掉。而那个公鸡是个很温顺的动物，它是不会伤害我们的。记住，下次看到猫一定要掉头就跑。”
小老鼠听了妈妈的话，似懂非懂地点了点头，它以后再也不乱跑了，而是跟在妈妈身后，努力地学习本领。
fields.content_en:
# Who Is the Good One?

One day, the little mouse sneaked out of the house while his mom wasn't looking, and didn't come back until noon. As soon as he got home, he excitedly told his mom, "Mom, I saw two strange animals when I went out to play!"

Mommy mouse smiled and said, "Is that so? Tell me all about it."

The little mouse nodded and said, "After I left home, I ran super fast, all the way into the yard. That's where I saw the first scary animal! It had colorful feathers, stretched out its neck, and made a terrible 'cock-a-doodle-doo' sound. It scared me so much I shivered!"

Mommy mouse said, "That's the little rooster from the yard!"

The little mouse went on, "This strange creature was flapping its wings so hard — it really scared me! I ran away as fast as I could. Not long after, by a windowsill in the yard, I saw another lovely animal! It had soft fur and pretty stripes, and a long tail, and its voice was so gentle."

Mommy mouse quickly asked, "Does this 'lovely' animal go 'meow, meow, meow'?"

The little mouse happily continued, "Yes, yes! You know it too? I wanted to say hello, but I saw how fierce the rooster looked, so I ran right away!"

Mommy mouse was so exasperated she didn't know whether to laugh or cry. She hugged her dear little mouse and said, "My sweet boy, did you know that the 'meow-meow' creature is a cat? Cats are our mouse greatest enemy. If you went to say hello, it would eat you without a second thought. But the rooster is a gentle creature — it would never hurt us. Remember, next time you see a cat, turn around and run!"

The little mouse listened to his mom's words and nodded with a half-understood expression. After that, he never wandered off again. Instead, he stayed close to his mom and worked hard to learn important skills.
fields.tips: 这个故事告诉我们：好坏善恶并不能从表面上看出来。因为看起来很凶的公鸡，不会伤害小老鼠，但看起来温柔的猫咪，却是要一口吃掉小老鼠的哦。
fields.tips_en: This story teaches us that goodness and wickedness cannot always be seen from the outside. The rooster, who looks fierce, will never harm the little mouse, but the cat, who appears gentle, is the one who wants to eat the mouse in one bite.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 花环属于谁
fields.subtitle: 名次并不是最重要的
fields.subtitle_en: Rank Is Not the Most Important Thing
fields.content:
森林之王大象爷爷决定在森林里举行一次盛大的动物运动会，消息一传开，小动物们非常踊跃地到报名处报名。
赛道上，跑得最快的是小猴子和小白兔，它们像离弦的箭一样跑了出去，连蹦带跳。两旁的小动物们都看不清到底谁快谁慢。
它们跑啊跑啊，忽然看见一只小松鼠在树下直哭。小白兔想：这小松鼠干吗哭呢？上去问问吧！可是现在是赛跑啊，要是输给了小猴，就会被别人看不起。还是不理小松鼠了，第一名重要！小白兔继续往前跑。小猴子想：小松鼠哭了，一定有伤心事，去安慰安慰它吧。可是现在是赛跑啊。
小猴子想起了妈妈对它说的话：“无论在什么时候、什么地方都应该互相帮助。”对，一定要帮助小松鼠。小猴子马上走向小松鼠，问道：“小松鼠，你干吗哭呀？”
小松鼠说：“小猴子哥哥，前几天我到遥远的外婆家去，今天回来了。可回到家，爸爸妈妈都不见了。我急急忙忙地跑出来找，可是迷路了。”小松鼠说完，又大哭起来。
小猴子笑着说：“小松鼠，你不要哭。今天举行动物运动会，全森林里的小动物都来观看了。我是个赛跑运动员，刚刚从这里经过。这条路我熟悉，不要哭了。”
小松鼠听了，抬头看着小猴子。只见它身上穿着运动衣，满头大汗，小松鼠就说：“你还不快跑，你会输的！”小猴子说：“不要紧，你家在哪儿？我先送你回家，你乖乖在家待着，你爸爸妈妈很快就会回来的。”
小猴子把小松鼠送回家，就继续往终点跑。但它跑到终点的时候，看见小白兔戴着花环，在大伙儿中间有说有笑。大伙儿看见了小猴子，说：“小猴子，你怎么跑得这么慢呀，大概在半路睡觉了吧？”
小猴子听了，甭提心里有多难受了！它躲到一边，伤心地哭了。哭着，哭着，它感觉到自己的脖子被什么东西套住了，一摸，原来是个花环。它猛一回头，惊喜地看见小松鼠微笑着向它点头。大象爷爷摸着小猴子的头，说：“好孩子，花环应该是你的。”
fields.content_en:
Title: Who Does the Wreath Belong To?

Grandpa Elephant, the king of the forest, decided to hold a grand animal sports meeting in the forest. As soon as the news spread, all the little animals eagerly signed up at the registration desk.

On the track, the fastest runners were the little monkey and the white rabbit. They shot forward like arrows, hopping and skipping along the way. The little animals on both sides couldn't even tell who was faster and who was slower.

They ran and ran when suddenly they saw a little squirrel crying under a tree. The white rabbit thought, "Why is that little squirrel crying? Maybe I should go ask!" But this was a race. If he lost to the little monkey, everyone would look down on him. Better not bother with the squirrel. First place is what matters! The white rabbit kept running forward. The little monkey thought, "The little squirrel is crying. Something must be wrong. I should go comfort it." But this was a race after all.

The little monkey remembered what his mom had always told him: "No matter when or where, we should always help each other." That's right. He must help the little squirrel. The little monkey immediately walked over and asked, "Little squirrel, why are you crying?"

The little squirrel said, "Brother Monkey, I went to visit my grandma's house a few days ago, and today I came back. But when I got home, my mommy and daddy were gone. I hurried out to look for them, but I got lost." After saying that, the little squirrel burst into tears again.

The little monkey smiled and said, "Little squirrel, don't cry. Today is the day of the animal sports meeting, and all the little animals in the forest have come to watch. I'm a runner and I just passed by here. I know this road well. Don't cry anymore."

Hearing this, the little squirrel looked up at the little monkey. She saw that he was wearing sports clothes and was covered in sweat. She said, "Shouldn't you go race? You'll lose!" The little monkey said, "It's all right. Where is your home? I'll take you there first, then you stay home nicely. Your mommy and daddy will be back soon."

The little monkey walked the little squirrel home, then continued running toward the finish line. But when he arrived, he saw the white rabbit wearing a flower wreath, laughing and chatting among the crowd. When the crowd spotted the little monkey, they said, "Little monkey, why did you run so slowly? You must have taken a nap halfway!"

The little monkey felt so sad he couldn't even put it into words. He hid to one side and cried sadly. Crying and crying, he felt something wrap around his neck. He reached up and touched it—it was a flower wreath! He turned around quickly and saw the little squirrel smiling and nodding at him. Grandpa Elephant patted the little monkey on the head and said, "Good child, the wreath belongs to you."
fields.tips: 准爸爸准妈妈要告诉宝宝，世界上很多东西都比名次重要。有的时候，我们帮助别人只是举手之劳，但却能因此得到意外的机会和收获。
fields.tips_en: Dear Mom and Dad, tell your baby that many things in this world are far more important than rankings. Sometimes, helping someone is as easy as raising your hand, yet it can bring unexpected opportunities and rewards.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 猫与肉
fields.subtitle: 让事实说话
fields.subtitle_en: Let the Facts Speak for Themselves
fields.content:
阿凡提是最聪明的人，什么事都难不倒他，也别想骗到他。
有一天，阿凡提买了3斤肉回来，吩咐妻子用这些肉做一顿饺子，打算两个人美美地吃一顿。妻子满口答应，把肉接了过去。
没想到，阿凡提的妻子特别馋，又有点儿懒，她不想做饺子，又急着想吃肉，就把肉炒熟，自己全部吃掉了，而后和了面，擀了一叠饺子皮放在碗里。
晚上阿凡提回来了，要饺子吃。妻子就把那碗饺子皮端了过来，放到阿凡提的面前。阿凡提奇怪地看着饺子皮，问道：“饺子呢？”妻子说：“我切好肉，和好面，就擀饺子皮了。谁知道我擀饺子皮的时候，你那只该死的猫，把肉全部吃光了。”阿凡提一副恍然大悟的表情。他“哦”了一声，就吩咐妻子把猫抓来，自己则拿来了一杆秤。
妻子把猫抓来了，阿凡提把它放到秤上，不多不少正好3斤。阿凡提紧紧盯着妻子，一脸疑惑地问妻子：“我的妻呀，如果这是猫的话，肉在哪里？如果这是肉的话，那么猫在哪里？”妻子看阿凡提已经猜到自己撒谎了，讪讪地笑了。
（选自《阿凡提的故事》）
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Cat and the Meat**

Nasreddin was the smartest man who ever lived. Nothing could stump him, and no one could ever trick him.

One day, Nasreddin came home with three pounds of meat. He told his wife to use it to make dumplings so they could both enjoy a wonderful meal. His wife agreed at once and took the meat.

But Nasreddin's wife had a little something of a craving—and she was a bit lazy too. She didn't feel like making dumplings, but she really wanted to eat that meat. So she fried it all up and ate it herself. Then she mixed some dough and rolled out a pile of empty dumpling wrappers and put them in a bowl.

That evening, Nasreddin came home and asked for his dumplings. His wife brought over the bowl of wrappers and set it in front of him. Nasreddin looked at the wrappers in surprise. "Where are the dumplings?" he asked. She said, "I cut the meat, made the dough, and rolled the wrappers. But while I was rolling, that pesky cat of yours ate all the meat!" Nasreddin's face showed that he suddenly understood. He said "Oh," and asked his wife to bring the cat. He then fetched a scale.

His wife brought the cat, and Nasreddin placed it on the scale—exactly three pounds, not a bit more or less. He looked closely at his wife and asked with a puzzled smile, "My dear wife, if this is a cat, then where is the meat? And if this is meat, then where is the cat?" His wife saw that he already knew she had been lying, and she just gave a little embarrassed laugh.

(From *The Stories of Nasreddin*)
fields.tips: 阿凡提处理事情的方法都很特别，采取旁敲侧击的方法，巧妙地避免了正面冲突。这样比较容易维持家庭和睦。当自己家有了矛盾的时候不妨也试试旁敲侧击法。有关阿凡提的故事有很多，准妈妈不妨找来读一读，可以潜移默化地启迪胎宝宝的智慧啊。
fields.tips_en: Nafta always handles situations in his own special way, using clever indirect approaches to skillfully avoid direct confrontation. This method helps maintain harmony in the family. When conflicts arise at home, why not try this gentle, roundabout approach? There are many wonderful Nafta stories out there—expectant mothers, why not find some to read? They can quietly awaken your baby's wisdom.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 聪明法官嫁女
fields.title_en: The Clever Judge's Daughter Gets Married
fields.subtitle: 学会辨识真正的财富
fields.subtitle_en: Learning to Recognize True Wealth
fields.content:
从前，有3个聪明的法官，他们是好朋友。他们之中，有一个是最聪明、最受人尊敬的，其他两位法官有什么疑难，也要向他请教。
最聪明的法官有一个美丽、聪慧的女儿。而他那两位法官好朋友，各有一个年轻英俊的儿子。这3个孩子从小一起长大，彼此关系都很好。终于到了年轻人要结婚的年龄，两个小伙子的父亲都在不约而同地考虑提亲的事。一天，一个法官朋友派人来对美丽姑娘的父亲说，请把他的女儿嫁给自己的儿子。
最聪明的法官没有立即答复。他吩咐仆人备饭款待这个提亲的人。正在这时候，另一位法官朋友也派人来提亲了。最聪明的法官还是没有直接答复，也吩咐备饭款待。
第二个派来提亲的人吃饭的时候，第一个人已经吃饱了。他向最聪明的法官告别，同时重复了一遍他的请求。
“很好……为什么不呢？告诉你的主人，就约定3个月的期限吧，请他在这个时间内做好迎娶我女儿的准备。”
第一个派来提亲的人走了。第二个人得到的也是同样的回答，也走了。
两个派来提亲的人回去后，把姑娘的父亲——那位最聪明的法官的回答转告给各自的主人：法官说，在3个月内做好结婚的准备。
其中一个提亲的法官想：“他以为我猜不到他的意图？结婚的准备……”他立即吩咐他的儿子：“孩子，3个月不是很长的期限，赶紧去买块好地，盖栋好房子，这可以让你和心爱的姑娘舒舒服服地住进去，而且能体面地招待客人。”他自豪地说：“没有我不懂的事。这老滑头的意图我一猜就中！”
而另一个法官却是这样对儿子说的：“聪明人的智谋无穷无尽，但是这些话的意思我还是清楚的。我的孩子，带些钱到各地去见见世面、广交朋友吧。你现在虽然有许多朋友，但是还不够。‘做好准备’的含义可能就在这里。”
3个月很快就过去了，约定的日子到了。这两个法官都派人对最聪明的法官说自己已经准备好了。最聪明的法官把这两位法官朋友请到家里做客，安排丰盛的酒席招待，然后说：“我只有一个女儿，可你们都向我提出同样的要求，让我把女儿嫁给自己的儿子。我太为难了，所以想请你们告诉我，我女儿该嫁给哪个年轻人？”
两个法官都说：“这件事真是难办啊。平常我们有什么问题都得向你请教，我们也没有什么主意。”
最聪明的法官继续说：“我跟两个年轻人约定了一个日子，就是今天。他们都说做好了结婚的准备工作。一个年轻人买了土地，给自己和客人盖了一栋宽敞的房子。另一个年轻人出门结交了许多新朋友。你们说，谁的准备工作做得好？我女儿该嫁给谁呢？”
“我们不知道。”两个法官都说。
最后，最聪明的法官说：“房屋有什么意义？风暴可以刮倒，大火可以烧掉，洪水也可以吞没，一切都是不可预测的。可是友谊却不同了，当你面临困难时，珍贵的友谊会给你很大帮助。朋友多的人是最富有的人。我的女儿要嫁给这样的小伙子。”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Wise Judge and His Daughter's Marriage

Long ago, there were three clever judges who were good friends. Among them, one was the wisest and most respected, and the other two judges would come to him whenever they had difficult questions.

The wisest judge had a beautiful and clever daughter. His two judge friends each had a young and handsome son. The three children grew up together and were very close. When the young people reached marriageable age, the fathers of the two boys both began thinking about asking for their daughters' hands in marriage. One day, one of the judge friends sent a messenger to the father of the beautiful girl, asking him to give his daughter in marriage to his son.

The wisest judge did not answer right away. He told his servant to prepare a meal to host the messenger. Just then, another judge friend also sent someone to ask for the girl's hand. The wisest judge still did not give a direct answer; he also ordered a meal for this visitor.

While the second messenger was eating, the first had already finished his meal. He said goodbye to the wisest judge and repeated his request.

"Very well... why not? Tell your master that we shall set a period of three months. Please ask him to make all the preparations for marrying my daughter within that time."

The first messenger left. The second one received the same reply and also left.

After returning home, both messengers told their masters what the judge—father of the girl—had said: the judge asked them to make preparations for the wedding within three months.

One of the judges who sent a messenger thought, "He thinks I won't guess his meaning? Preparing for marriage..." He immediately told his son, "My child, three months is not a long time. Hurry and buy a fine piece of land and build a good house, so you and your beloved girl can live comfortably and receive guests with honor." He said proudly, "There is nothing I don't understand. I've guessed the old cunning man's intention perfectly!"

But the other judge said to his son differently: "The wise man's wisdom is endless, but I still understand what these words mean. My child, take some money and travel to different places to see the world and make many new friends. Although you have many friends now, it may not be enough. Perhaps that is what 'making preparations' means."

The three months passed quickly, and the agreed day arrived. Both judges sent word to the wisest judge that they were ready. The wisest judge invited his two judge friends to his home for a visit, prepared a grand feast, and then said, "I have only one daughter, yet you both asked me to marry her to your son. I am quite puzzled, so I would like you to tell me—which young man should my daughter marry?"

Both judges said, "This is indeed a difficult matter. We usually come to you for advice on every problem, but we have no idea ourselves."

The wisest judge continued, "I set today as the day to meet with both young men. They both said they have made their wedding preparations. One young man bought land and built a spacious house for himself and his guests. The other young man traveled and made many new friends. Tell me, whose preparations are better? Who should my daughter marry?"

"We do not know," both judges said.

Finally, the wisest judge said, "What use is a house? A storm can blow it down, a fire can burn it to the ground, a flood can swallow it—all things are unpredictable. But friendship is different. When you face difficulties, precious friends will give you great help. He who has many friends is the richest of all men. My daughter shall marry this young man."
fields.tips: 看完这个故事，准妈妈可以对胎宝宝说：“宝宝啊，平凡的人积累有形资产，聪明的人积累无形资产。比有形资产更重要的是一辈子也不会失去的无形资产，比如友谊。宝贝长大后，要交很多要好的朋友哦。”
fields.tips_en: After hearing this story, you can softly say to your baby: 'My dear child, ordinary people accumulate visible wealth, but wise people gather invisible treasures. More precious than any material possession is the wealth you will never lose—not even for a day—such as friendship. My darling, when you grow up, make many dear friends.'
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 皇帝吃鲫鱼
fields.title_en: The Emperor Tastes the Crucian Carp
fields.subtitle: 改变思路巧解难题
fields.subtitle_en: A Clever Change of Approach Solves the Problem
fields.content:
有一天，皇帝上完朝后，留下4位大臣，问他们鲫鱼身上到底哪块肉更好吃。第一位大臣说鲫鱼的头好吃，因为肉香；第二位大臣说鲫鱼的尾巴最好吃，因为是活肉；第三位大臣说脊背肉最好吃，因为这里肉厚；第四位大臣说鱼肚子的肉最好吃，因为没刺。四位大臣各执一词，争执不下，弄得皇帝也不知道到底该吃哪块鱼肉了。于是皇帝就传旨让大臣去找个渔翁，带到皇宫来问一问。
4位大臣回家后，都希望明天找到的渔翁能够跟自己说法一致，就都跟皇上派出找渔翁的人打听渔翁的住址，然后各自带10两银子到城外去找渔翁。这个渔翁一天之内连续接待了4位大臣，分别得到了他们送来的10两银子。渔翁也都分别答应了他们的要求，说到了皇上跟前一定跟他们保持一致的说法。
第二天渔翁来到殿上，一看4位大臣都在呢。这是老渔翁没有想到的。现在按照哪位大臣的说法说都不对，否则一定会得罪另外3位大臣。老渔翁心里打鼓，后悔不该收人家的银子。这时只听皇上迫不及待地问：“老渔翁，鲫鱼究竟哪块肉最好吃啊？”老渔翁抬眼朝4位大臣一一看去，看见他们都在热切地注视着自己呢。他突然灵机一动，对皇上说：“我主万岁，鲫鱼其实是季节性很强的鱼，要按季节吃。不同的季节好吃的部位是不同的。”皇上惊讶地问：“怎么分季节的，快快说。这样的事还是头一次听说呢。”老渔翁不慌不忙地答道：“鲫鱼哪块肉最好吃呢？春天头最好吃，夏天尾巴最好吃，秋天脊背最好吃，冬天肚子的肉最好吃。”
皇上对老渔翁的回答很满意，不但赏赐了渔翁，还加封了4位大臣。老渔翁拿着赏赐，看看各位大臣，也狡黠地笑了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Emperor and the Crucian Carp

One day, after attending court, the emperor asked his four ministers, "Which part of the crucian carp tastes the best?" The first minister said, "The head, because the meat is fragrant." The second minister said, "The tail is the best, because it is lively meat." The third minister said, "The back is the best, because the flesh is thickest there." And the fourth minister said, "The belly is the best, because it has no bones." Each minister stuck to his own opinion, and the argument went on and on, leaving the emperor quite unsure of which part to choose. So the emperor issued an order for the ministers to find an old fisherman and bring him to the palace to ask him.

When the four ministers returned home, each one hoped the fisherman he would meet the next day would agree with his own view. They all managed to find out from the man sent by the emperor where the fisherman lived, and each of them brought ten taels of silver to see him outside the city. That same day, the old fisherman received visits from all four ministers in a row, and each one gave him ten taels of silver. He agreed to all of their requests, promising that when he spoke before the emperor, he would support whichever view each minister had offered.

The next day, the fisherman arrived at the palace and saw that all four ministers were already there. This was not what the old fisherman had expected. Whichever minister's opinion he chose to repeat would be the wrong one, and he would surely offend the other three. His heart began to race, and he regretted ever accepting their silver. Just then, the emperor impatiently asked, "Old fisherman, which part of the carp truly tastes the best?" The old fisherman raised his eyes and looked at each of the four ministers in turn, seeing them all watching him with eager expectation. Suddenly, a clever idea came to him. He said to the emperor, "Your Majesty, the crucian carp is a fish that changes with the seasons, and the best part to eat depends on the season." The emperor asked in surprise, "How do you divide it by season? Please tell me quickly. I have never heard of anything like this before." Calmly, the old fisherman replied, "Spring is the best time to eat the head, summer the tail, autumn the back, and winter the belly."

The emperor was very pleased with the fisherman's answer. He not only rewarded the old fisherman but also promoted all four ministers. The fisherman took his reward, glanced at the ministers, and gave a sly little smile.
fields.tips: 渔翁按季节吃鱼的说法，不但让皇帝满意，也让4位大臣满意。准妈妈在工作和生活中遇到较难解决的问题时，也不妨拓宽自己的想象空间，变换思路，寻求合理的解决方法。
fields.tips_en: The fisherman's suggestion of eating carp according to the season pleased not only the emperor but also all four ministers. Expecting mothers, when faced with difficult challenges at work or in daily life, might also try broadening their imagination and shifting their perspective to find a wise and reasonable solution.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 不合格的烟囱
fields.subtitle: 提前防范胜过事后补救
fields.subtitle_en: It's always kinder to prevent trouble before it happens than to fix it after.
fields.content:
有一户人家盖了新房子，但厨房没有安排好，烧火的土灶烟囱砌得太直，土灶旁边堆着一大堆柴草。
一天，这家主人请客。有位客人看到主人家厨房的这些情况，就对主人说：“你家的厨房应该修改一下。”
主人问道：“为什么呢？”
客人说：“你家烟囱砌得太直，柴草放得离火太近。你应将烟囱砌得弯一些，柴草也要搬远一些。不然的话，容易发生火灾。”
主人听了，笑了笑，不以为然，没放在心上。他不久就把这事忘到脑后去了。后来，这户人家果然着火了。左邻右舍立即赶来，有的浇水，有的撒土，有的搬东西。大家一起奋力扑救，大火终于被扑灭了。除了将厨房里的东西烧了一小半外，总算没酿成大祸。
为了酬谢大家的全力救助，主人杀牛、备酒，办了酒席。席间，主人热情地请被烧伤的人坐在上席，其余的人也按功劳大小依次入座，唯独没有请那个建议改修烟囱、搬走柴草的人。
大家高高兴兴地吃着、喝着，忽然有人提醒主人说：“要是当初您听了那位客人的劝告，改建烟囱、搬走柴草，就不会造成今天的损失，也用不着杀牛买酒来酬谢大家了。现在，您论功请客，怎么可以忘了那位事先提醒、劝告您的客人呢？难道提出防火的没有功，只有参加救火的人才算有功吗？我看您应该把那位客人请来才对呀！”
主人听了，这才恍然大悟，赶忙把那位客人请来，不但说了许多感激的话，还真的请他坐了上席。众人也都拍手称好。
事后，主人新建厨房时，就按那位客人的建议做了，把烟囱砌成弯的，柴草也放到安全的地方去了。因为以后的日子还长着呢。
做什么事情都要有预见性，如果自己没意识到，听听别人的建议也是好的。防患于未然总比出了险情再去补救更为重要。
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Chimney That Wasn't Right**

There was a family that had just built a new house. But they hadn't arranged the kitchen properly. The chimney of the dirt stove went straight up, and there was a big pile of firewood and hay stacked right next to the stove.

One day, the host invited guests over. One guest noticed the kitchen situation and said to the host, "You should fix your kitchen."

The host asked, "Why?"

The guest said, "Your chimney is too straight, and the firewood is placed too close to the fire. You should make the chimney curve, and move the firewood farther away. Otherwise, it's easy to catch fire."

The host listened, smiled, and didn't take it seriously. Soon after, he forgot all about it. Later, this family indeed had a fire. The neighbors all came running right away. Some brought water, some threw dirt, and some moved things out of the way. Everyone worked hard together to put out the flames, and the big fire was finally put out. Besides burning about half of what was in the kitchen, they were lucky that it didn't turn into a major disaster.

To thank everyone for their help, the host killed a cow, prepared wine, and held a feast. During the meal, the host warmly invited those who had been burned to sit in the seat of honor, and everyone else took their places according to their contributions. But the guest who had suggested fixing the chimney and moving the firewood was not invited at all.

Everyone was happily eating and drinking when suddenly someone reminded the host, "If only you had listened to that guest back then, fixed the chimney, and moved the firewood, you wouldn't have suffered these losses today. You wouldn't need to kill a cow and buy wine to thank everyone either. Now that you're honoring people by their contributions, how can you forget the guest who warned you beforehand? Is it possible that preventing a fire has no merit, and only those who fight the fire are rewarded? I think you ought to invite that guest!"

The host finally understood, quickly invited the guest over, said many words of gratitude, and truly offered him the seat of honor. Everyone clapped and cheered.

After that, when the host rebuilt the kitchen, he followed the guest's advice. He built a curved chimney and placed the firewood in a safe spot far away — because there were still many long days ahead.

No matter what we do, it's good to be forward-looking. If we don't realize a problem ourselves, listening to others' suggestions is always a wise thing to do. Preventing trouble before it happens is always more important than trying to fix things after the danger has already come.
fields.tips: 父母是孩子的领路人，对自己生活中的一些不良习惯，不要想着等孩子出生后再改不迟。如果你希望孩子做到什么，你自己就要提前做到什么。
fields.tips_en: Parents are their children's guides. Don't wait until your baby arrives to start changing those bad habits — if you want your child to do something, show them the way by doing it yourself first.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 谁来看守马
fields.subtitle: 善于找对自己有利的说辞
fields.subtitle_en: Good at finding the angle that works in their favor
fields.content:
国王派一位丞相和阿凡提到外地办事。阿凡提骑的是一匹黑色的老马，丞相的坐骑是一匹白色的骏马。
到了傍晚，他俩来到一个前不着村后不着店的野外，决定露宿。丞相对阿凡提说：“阿凡提，这里常有野兽出没，还可能会有强盗，今晚请你看守这两匹马。”
“不，我不看，你自己看吧。我的马是黑色的，夜里野兽和强盗根本看不见它。”阿凡提说。
丞相一听阿凡提说得有道理，便对他说：“如果那样，我们俩把马调换一下。我的这匹白色骏马归你，你的黑色老马归我。”
阿凡提高兴地与丞相调换了马，然后对丞相说：“太好了，今夜就请您守护这两匹马吧！”
“为什么？”丞相问。
“现在您的马是黑色的了，这黑咕隆咚的深夜，您也看不清您的马是被狼吃了还是强盗偷走了。我现在的马是白色的，我一眼就能看清它是否安在。”阿凡提说完便睡觉去了。丞相只好守了一夜。
（选自《阿凡提的故事》）
fields.content_en:
# Who Will Watch the Horses?

The king sent a prime minister and Afanti on a trip to another place. Afanti rode a dark black old horse, and the prime minister rode a beautiful white horse.

In the evening, they arrived in the middle of nowhere—no village in sight, far from any home—and decided to sleep outdoors. The prime minister said to Afanti, "Afanti, wild animals often come around here, and bandits might too. Please watch both horses tonight."

"No, I won't watch them. You watch them yourself. My horse is black, and at night neither wild animals nor bandits can see it," Afanti said.

The prime minister thought this made sense and said, "Then let's swap horses. I'll give you my white horse, and you give me your black horse."

Afanti happily swapped horses with the prime minister and said, "Wonderful! Tonight you guard both horses, please!"

"Why?" asked the prime minister.

"Now your horse is black, and in this dark, pitch-black night, you won't be able to tell if a wolf ate it or a bandit stole it. But my horse is white now, and I can see it at a glance to know if it's safe," said Afanti. Then he went to sleep. The prime minister had no choice but to stay awake all night.

*(From The Stories of Afanti)*
fields.tips: 有关阿凡提的故事流传很广。在这个故事中，马没有变，变的只是阿凡提的说辞，因为善于寻找对自己有利的说辞，阿凡提避免了守着马过夜。准爸爸和准妈妈可以把这个故事一起讲给胎宝宝听，一个扮成阿凡提，一个扮成丞相。这样会更加生动。
fields.tips_en:
The story of Afanti is widely loved. In it, the horse never changes—only Afanti's words do. Thanks to his clever way of finding just the right words to suit his favor, Afanti manages to avoid spending the night guarding the horse. 

Future dad and mom can read this story together to their little one—one playing Afanti and the other playing the minister. It'll bring the tale to life in a warm and lively way! 🌟
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 馕是什么东西
fields.subtitle: 不要把简单问题复杂化
fields.subtitle_en: Don't Make Simple Things Complicated
fields.content:
几位哲学家、逻辑学家和法律学家正在王宫讨论某一个问题，他们各自提出自己的见解，可谁也不服谁就争论起来。无休止的争论使阿凡提头昏脑涨，他站出来说道：“你们都是一群糊涂虫！”阿凡提的这句话冒犯了这些学者，学者要求国王惩治他。国王唤来打手，命令鞭打阿凡提50下。
“且慢，贤明的国王陛下，”阿凡提不慌不忙地站出来说，“我提出一个问题让这些学者回答。如果他们回答得正确，我甘心情愿挨罚。”
“好吧，请提出你的问题！”国王说。
“先拿纸和笔来！”阿凡提说。
纸和笔拿上来了，阿凡提把纸和笔分给了这些学者，然后说道：“馕是什么东西？请你们在纸上分别写出这个问题的答案。”
学者们写好答案后交到国王手里，国王开始宣读答案：
第一份答案说：“馕是一种食品。”
第二份答案说：“馕是面粉和水的混合物。”
第三份答案说：“馕是真主的恩赐。”
……
第七份答案说：“没有人能真正知道它到底是什么。”
国王宣读完答案，问阿凡提：“阿凡提，你看他们回答得怎么样？”
“回答得不怎么样，本来很简单的问题，他们回答得一个比一个复杂，而且都没答到点子上！”阿凡提说，“非常简单，馕是吃的东西！”
国王觉得有理，就取消了对阿凡提的处罚。
（选自《阿凡提的故事》）
fields.content_en:
Title: What Is Naan?

Several philosophers, logicians, and lawyers were discussing a certain question in the palace. They each shared their own ideas, but no one could convince the others, so they started arguing. The endless debate made Avanti dizzy, so he stepped forward and said, "You are all a bunch of confused fools!" His words offended the scholars, who asked the king to punish him. The king called in his guards and ordered that Avanti be whipped fifty times.

"Wait, wise King," Avanti said calmly. "Let me ask these scholars a question. If they answer correctly, I will gladly accept my punishment."

"Very well, please ask your question!" said the king.

"Bring paper and pens first!" said Avanti.

Paper and pens were brought. Avanti handed them out to the scholars and said, "What is naan? Please write your answers on the paper."

After the scholars finished writing, they handed their answers to the king, who began to read them aloud:

The first answer said, "Naan is a kind of food."

The second answer said, "Naan is a mixture of flour and water."

The third answer said, "Naan is a blessing from God."

...

The seventh answer said, "No one can truly know what it is."

After the king finished reading, he asked Avanti, "Avanti, how do you think they did?"

"Not very well," said Avanti. "It was such a simple question, but they each answered in a more and more complicated way, and none of them hit the point. Very simply put — naan is something you eat!"

The king agreed and cancelled the punishment.

(From *The Stories of Avanti*)
fields.tips: 简单是一种智慧。聪明人能够把复杂的事情简单化。孕期准妈妈想的问题很多，常常让自己情绪变得不好。其实准妈妈只要想想孕育本是平常事，千百年来人们都是如此繁衍后代，就不会有太多的顾虑与担忧了。
fields.tips_en: Simplicity is a kind of wisdom. A clever person knows how to make complicated matters simple. During pregnancy, expecting mothers often carry many worries, which can weigh on their emotions. Remember — creating new life is a natural and ordinary journey that has continued for thousands of years. Keeping this in mind can help ease your fears and bring peace of mind.
fields.source: 每天10分钟胎教故事（付娟娟）

fields.title: 想飞的小象
fields.title_en: The Little Elephant Who Wanted to Fly
fields.content:
有一只可爱的象宝宝，终于来到了这个美丽的世界。他刚刚出生，却已经摇摇晃晃地站起来了。小象宝宝对这个世界充满了好奇，他看着周围的一切，眼里充满了惊喜。
第一天，象爸爸带小象宝宝去散步，小象宝宝认识了许多鲜艳的花儿，嫩绿的草儿，茁壮的大树。第二天，象爸爸带小象宝宝到了河边，他看见了清澈的河水，巍峨的高山，圆润的鹅卵石。第三天，象爸爸带着小象宝宝认识了许多小动物。小象开心地说：“世界可真大啊！”
这时，一只小鸟在天空自由地飞翔着。小象看着好羡慕，他想：“要是我也会飞，就可以在高高的空中看到更多的东西了，那该多好啊……” 于是，小象辛苦地爬到树上想学飞，可他一松手就“哎哟”一声，重重地摔在了地上。这一下，惊醒了在一旁午睡的小蛇。小蛇笑着说：“小象，你别费劲啦！我们都有自己的本事，你看我也不会飞，可我会爬到树上睡大觉！”小蛇正说着，小狮子和小老虎也悠闲地走了过来。小狮子说：“你看，我也不会飞，可是我能跳过宽宽的大河！”小老虎紧跟着说：“我也不会飞，可那又有什么关系，我会游泳呢！”小象似乎明白了，他若有所思地点点头说：“可是，我会什么呢……”这时，象爸爸走了过来用鼻子轻抚着小象说：“我们大象力气可大了，这可是小鸟完全做不到的啊！”
于是，小象开始跟着爸爸用鼻子工作，他跟着爸爸学着搬运木头。只见小象用长鼻子轻松一钩，大木头就搬起来了。小象开心极了，觉得自己很有本事，大家都喜欢他。象爸爸看到小象这么有成就，用大鼻子轻抚着小象的后背，温柔地说：“每种动物都有自己的优点和长处，都是独一无二的，一定要学会用自己的特点做适合自己的事情。”小象高兴地对爸爸说：“做一个大力气的小象，真幸福！”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Elephant Who Wanted to Fly

There was a cute little elephant who had just arrived in this beautiful world. He had only just been born, but he was already wobbling to his feet. Little Elephant was full of curiosity about the world. He looked at everything around him, his eyes sparkling with wonder.

On the first day, Elephant Dad took Little Elephant for a walk, and Little Elephant learned about bright and colorful flowers, soft green grass, and tall, strong trees. On the second day, Elephant Dad took Little Elephant to the riverbank, where he saw clear, shimmering water, towering mountains, and smooth, round stones. On the third day, Elephant Dad introduced Little Elephant to many little animals. Little Elephant said happily, "The world is so big!"

At that moment, a little bird flew freely in the sky. Little Elephant watched with envy and thought, "If only I could fly too, I could see so many more things from high up in the air. How wonderful that would be…" So Little Elephant carefully climbed up a tree to try learning to fly, but the moment he let go, "Ouch!" he fell heavily to the ground. The noise woke up a little snake who was napping nearby. The snake chuckled and said, "Little Elephant, don't bother! We all have our own special talents. Look, I can't fly either, but I can climb trees and sleep on them!" As the snake was speaking, Little Lion and Little Tiger strolled over lazily. Little Lion said, "See, I can't fly, but I can leap across wide rivers!" Little Tiger added, "I can't fly either, but what does that matter? I can swim!" Little Elephant seemed to understand. He nodded thoughtfully and said, "But then, what can I do…?" Just then, Elephant Dad came over and gently stroked Little Elephant with his trunk, saying, "We elephants are very strong, and that is something birds can never do!"

So Little Elephant began to learn from Dad, using his trunk to work. He followed his dad and practiced carrying logs. With a easy hook of his long trunk, Little Elephant lifted a big log right up. Little Elephant was overjoyed. He felt so proud and knew everyone would like him. Seeing how accomplished Little Elephant was, Elephant Dad gently stroked his back with his big trunk and said softly, "Every animal has its own strengths and special gifts. We are all unique. Always learn to use your own wonderful traits to do the things that are right for you." Little Elephant smiled happily at his dad and said, "Being a strong little elephant is such a happy thing!"
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 春笋大力士
fields.content:
“哗啦啦，哗啦啦……”春天的雨水就是多，刚才还是好好的天，一会儿就下起了大雨。不一会儿，雨停了，太阳又在蓝蓝的天上露出了笑脸。
小兔提着篮子蹦蹦跳跳地向小树林走去，他想采蘑菇。小兔刚走到竹园，就听见了“咕噜噜”的声音，原来是一块大石头滚下来挡在了小路上。小兔想，这块大石头挡住了路，我来把它搬走。
小兔使劲地搬，“嗨哟嗨哟”，他使出了很大的力气，可大石头一动也不动。
小狗路过竹园，看见大石头便走上前去帮小兔一起搬。“嗨哟嗨哟”，他们俩使劲地搬着，可大石头还是一动也不动。
小黑熊来了，他的个头真大，胳膊好粗好粗的。小黑熊拍拍巴掌，抱住大石头使劲地搬着，可大石头还是一动也不动。
小兔说：“要是我们三个一起用劲推，也许会推动大石头的。”于是，三个小伙伴一起使劲地推大石头。大石头真重啊，他们累得呼哧呼哧直喘气，大石头还是一动也不动地挡在路上。
怎么办呢？突然，小兔尖叫了起来：“哎呀，动了！你们瞧，大石头动了！”叫声把小狗和小黑熊都吓了一跳。
小黑熊说：“胡说，没有人搬它，大石头怎么会……”话还没说完，小黑熊也看到大石头动了一下，这是怎么回事呢？三个小伙伴吓坏了，赶紧躲进竹林里。
大石头真的在动，它的一边在一点儿一点儿慢慢地往上抬，越抬越高。“咕噜”一下，大石头翻了个身，滚到了路边。
小兔他们这才跑上前去看，只见小路上冒出了一根新长出来的竹笋，又粗又壮。
“哎呀，原来是竹笋把大石头顶翻的。”小狗说。
“竹笋的力气可真大呀！”小兔说。
“都说我是个大力士，真正的大力士应该是竹笋！”小黑熊佩服地说。
