fields.content_en:
# Spring Bamboo Shoot Strongman

"Rattle-rattle, rattle-rattle…" Spring rains are so plentiful. Just a moment ago the sky was clear, and then suddenly a heavy rain began to fall. Soon after, the rain stopped, and the sun peeked out again with a smile in the blue sky.

Little Rabbit carried a basket and hopped along toward the little woods. He wanted to pick mushrooms. When Little Rabbit reached the bamboo grove, he heard a "roll-loom" sound. A big stone had rolled down and blocked the path. Little Rabbit thought, This big stone is blocking the way—I'll move it.

Little Rabbit pushed with all his might—"heave-ho, heave-ho!"—but the big stone didn't budge at all.

Little Dog passed by the bamboo grove, saw the big stone, and went over to help Little Rabbit push. "Heave-ho, heave-ho!" They both pushed hard, but the big stone still didn't move.

Then Little Black Bear came. He was so big, with arms thick and strong. Little Black Bear clapped his paws together, wrapped his arms around the stone, and pushed with all his might. But still, the big stone didn't move.

Little Rabbit said, "What if the three of us push together? We might be able to move it." So all three friends pushed together with all their strength. The big stone was so heavy that they panted and wheezed, but the stone still sat right there, unmoved, blocking the road.

What should they do? Suddenly, Little Rabbit let out a cry: "Oh! It's moving! Look, the big stone moved!" The shout startled Little Dog and Little Black Bear.

Little Black Bear said, "Nonsense, no one is pushing it—how could the big stone…" But before he finished, he also saw the stone shift a little. What on earth was happening? The three friends were frightened and quickly hid inside the bamboo grove.

The big stone really was moving. One side slowly lifted higher and higher, bit by bit. With a "rumble," the big stone tipped over and rolled to the side of the path.

Little Rabbit and his friends ran over to take a closer look. There, rising from the path, was a fresh new bamboo shoot, thick and strong.

"Oh, so it was the bamboo shoot that tipped over the stone," said Little Dog.

"The bamboo shoot is so strong!" said Little Rabbit.

"I always thought I was the strong one," said Little Black Bear in admiration. "But the real strongman is the bamboo shoot!"
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 淘气包哥哥
fields.content:
朵朵的哥哥是一个淘气包，常常惹得她又哭又笑。
朵朵有一头漂亮的长发，乌黑柔软。她最常见的发型就是妈妈为她梳的两条小辫子——发梢用皮筋绑紧，微微翘起，额前别一只漂亮的向日葵发卡，别提多可爱了。邻居的爷爷奶奶们见了，都会捏捏她的脸蛋，夸她是一个漂亮的小姑娘。但朵朵的哥哥可不这么想，如果他也觉得妹妹可爱漂亮，就不会三番五次地揪她的小辫子了。
这天，哥哥又揪她辫子了。更过分的是，他还将两根皮筋捋了下来，揪疼她了不说，辫子也被弄散了，头发变得乱糟糟的，朵朵放声哭了起来。哥哥“哼”了一声，丢下哭泣的妹妹，嘟着嘴走开了。过了一会儿，哥哥跑了回来，额角还挂着汗珠，手里握着两根棒棒糖，他没好气地把棒棒糖塞进朵朵怀里。看到哥哥用平时攒的零用钱给自己买糖吃，朵朵止住哭声，美滋滋地吃了起来。
这天，朵朵歌唱家般嘹亮的哭声响彻了整个小区。原来又是那个淘气包哥哥，他不小心将沙子扬进了她的眼睛里。哥哥先是一脸不耐烦，直说朵朵是个“爱哭鬼”，接着又故技重施，跑去买了两根棒棒糖送给妹妹，并小声说了句“对不起”。朵朵止住哭声，揉揉眼睛，甜甜地笑了。这时，另一个淘气包金刚突然从一边蹦出来，抢走了朵朵的棒棒糖。朵朵的眼泪又像断了线的珠子一样，稀里哗啦地滚落下来。
哥哥也不知哪来的力气，一把抓住比他高出半个头的金刚，夺回了棒棒糖，放进妹妹的手心。金刚不服气地说：“你不是也常常欺负你妹妹？！”“我的妹妹只有我可以欺负，别人不行！”哥哥大声喊道。金刚撇撇嘴，走开了。朵朵的心里甜甜的，大大的笑容在脸上绽开。
这天，朵朵又哭啦！淘气包哥哥做了一把弹弓，瞄准这儿，瞄准那儿，结果将朵朵放在花盆边的泡泡瓶打翻了，肥皂水流得干干净净，一滴也不剩。听到朵朵的哭声，哥哥捂住了耳朵，皱着眉头转身回到了自己的房间。他踮着脚将存钱罐拿下来，跑去了小卖部。只是这次，棒棒糖也没能将朵朵的眼泪收回去。哥哥红了脸，将弹弓丢到一边，捡起泡泡瓶跑到厨房，将洗洁精倒进瓶子里，又加满了水，然后牵着朵朵的小手来到公园里的一座石桥上。
哥哥用吸管蘸了一下自制的“洗洁精泡泡水”，用心地吹了起来。一个、两个、三个……圆圆的气泡慢慢膨胀、升空，泛着五颜六色的光芒，就像魔幻彩球一样，漂亮极了。
兄妹俩一起站在小石桥上，吹着泡泡，非常开心。朵朵睁大眼睛瞧着泡泡，心想：我的哥哥可真了不起。
fields.content_en:
Title: My Mischievous Big Brother

Duo Duo's big brother is quite a rascal, and he always manages to make her cry and laugh by turns.

Duo Duo has beautiful long hair, soft and as dark as ink. Her most common hairstyle is two little pigtails that her mom brushes for her — tied at the ends with little rubber bands that curl up slightly, and a pretty sunflower hair clip tucked in front. Everyone says how adorable she is, and the neighboring grandparents love to pinch her cheeks and call her a lovely little girl. But Duo Duo's brother doesn't quite see it that way. If he thought his little sister was cute and pretty, he certainly wouldn't keep pulling on her little braids again and again.

One day, her brother pulled her braids again. Even worse, he took off both rubber bands. Not only did it hurt her, but her braids got all tangled and messy, and Duo Duo burst into tears. Her brother just "hmphed," left his crying sister behind, and stomped off with a pout. But after a while, he ran back, sweat glistening on his forehead, holding two lollipops in his hand. He grumpily shoved them into Duo Duo's arms. Seeing that her brother had used his own saved pocket money to buy her candy, Duo Duo stopped crying and happily began to enjoy it.

That day, Duo Duo cried with a voice as loud and clear as a little singer, and her wailing echoed all through the neighborhood. It was that mischievous brother again — he had accidentally kicked sand right into her eyes. At first, her brother looked very impatient and kept telling Duo Duo she was such a "crybaby." Then, just like before, he ran off and came back with two lollipops for his little sister, quietly whispering, "I'm sorry." Duo Duo wiped her eyes and gave a sweet smile. Just then, another rascal named Jin Gang suddenly popped out from somewhere and snatched Duo Duo's lollipop. Tears streamed down her face again like beads spilling from a broken string.

No one knows where her brother found such strength, but he grabbed Jin Gang, who was half a head taller than him, took the lollipop back, and placed it right into his little sister's palm. Jin Gang protested, "Aren't you always bullying your own sister?!" "Only I can bully my little sister! Nobody else!" her brother shouted loudly. Jin Gang pursed his lips and walked away. Duo Duo's heart felt warm and sweet, and a big smile bloomed on her face.

That day, Duo Duo cried again! Her mischievous brother had made a slingshot, aiming here and aiming there, and accidentally knocked over Duo Duo's bubble bottle placed beside a flowerpot. All the soapy water spilled out — not a single drop was left. Hearing Duo Duo's crying, her brother covered his ears, frowned, and turned around to go back to his room. Then he tiptoed over, grabbed his piggy bank, and ran to the little shop. But this time, even a lollipop couldn't stop Duo Duo's tears. Blushing, her brother tossed the slingshot aside, picked up the bubble bottle, ran to the kitchen, poured in some dish soap, filled it with water, and then held Duo Duo's small hand as they walked to a stone bridge in the park.

Using a straw to dip into their homemade "soapy bubble water," her brother blew with all his heart. One bubble, two bubbles, three bubbles… round bubbles slowly swelled up and floated into the sky, shimmering with all colors of the rainbow, just like magical glowing balls. They were so beautiful.

Standing together on the little stone bridge, the brother and sister blew bubbles and had a wonderful time. Duo Duo stared wide-eyed at the floating bubbles and thought to herself: My big brother is really amazing.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 荷花公主
fields.content:
六月出生的我对荷花总有着特殊的感情。也许因为小时候妈妈总会指着荷花说：“宝贝，知道为什么妈妈在六月生下你吗？因为这个季节属于荷花。荷花是最美的花儿，像花中之公主，艳丽芬芳，却让人敬而远之，出淤泥而不染，总是骄傲地绽放着。”所以，我一直觉得荷花是我的幸运花。
在意大利的小镇旅游的时候，我幸运地买到了一个精致可爱的水晶荷花小挂坠，于是一直得意地戴在脖子上。在我忧伤、忐忑、孤独的时候，只要摸着小挂坠，内心都会觉得温暖。我总像孩子一样幻想着，也许有那么一个神奇的地方，全是世界上各种各样美丽的花，每一种花都有自己的国度，而我就是荷花国中的一朵，而且是最美的那一朵，我一定会是荷花公主吧……
大学毕业以后我来到北京工作，繁忙而紧张的生活有时令人喘不过气来，对家乡和妈妈的思念也会经常浮于脑海。夏天的清早，能去到离我家不远的颐和园看荷花，是最令我开心和放松的事情了。
这一天，我像往常一样走近充满清香的荷花池。清晨的薄雾还没散去，淡淡地、一缕缕地环绕着池子，大朵怒放的荷花敞开着灿烂的花瓣，嫩白的花瓣尖上淡淡的粉红色娇艳欲滴，像是一位国画高手在花瓣尖上点缀的粉墨汁，淡淡地溢了开来。在嫩黄的花蕊上的是一个跳舞的小精灵吗？哦，那是一只翅膀闪动着晶莹的光亮的大蜻蜓，在硕大的花间轻跳曼舞着。荷花那笔直纤细的花茎骄傲地挺立着，就像一个绅士，只在风中微微摇曳。那水面上挨挨挤挤的大圆盘似的碧绿饱满的荷叶，快乐地拥挤着，铺满池塘，怎么看都像是一群群慕名来欣赏荷花的使者，满满地挤在荷花的下面，静静陪伴着水中的仙子。可爱的莲蓬却像是一个个可爱的孩子，饱满的小绿色脸儿对着阳光，充满了希望。
忽然间，被美景迷惑的我真想也变成那只幸运的蜻蜓，变成一个小小的人儿，踮着脚尖站在嫩嫩的花蕊间，跳着芭蕾。我像蝶儿一样轻盈，从这一朵一跃到那一朵上，再从荷花上跳到宽大的荷叶上。我在这花的舞台上旋转，奔跑，所有的荷花都为我伴舞，所有荷叶为我鼓掌。没错，清澈的湖水倒影里，我俨然一位美丽的荷花公主正在自己的国度里翩翩起舞……接着，远处走来一个熟悉的身影，是妈妈，她也来看荷花了，我使劲在花上向妈妈招手，可她似乎看不见我，也许我太小了，我着急了，又跳起来大喊着妈妈……再接着，我就醒了。
这是一个荷花池边的甜蜜的梦，只属于我的，荷花公主的梦。
fields.content_en:
# The Lotus Princess

I have always had a special feeling for lotus flowers, since I was born in June. Maybe because when I was little, my mom would point to the lotuses and say, "Sweetheart, do you know why I had you in June? Because this season belongs to the lotus. It is the most beautiful flower, like a princess among flowers—gorgeous and fragrant, yet kept at a distance, rising pure from the mud, always blooming proudly." So I have always felt that the lotus is my lucky flower.

When I was traveling in a small town in Italy, I was lucky enough to find a delicate and lovely crystal lotus pendant, and I wore it happily around my neck ever since. On days when I felt sad, worried, or lonely, touching that little pendant always made my heart feel warm. I would daydream like a child, hoping there might be some magical place filled with all the beautiful flowers in the world, where every kind of flower had its own kingdom. And I would be a flower in the kingdom of lotuses—the most beautiful one of all. I would surely be the Lotus Princess...

After university, I came to Beijing to work. Life there was busy and stressful, sometimes making it hard to breathe. I often thought about home and my mother. In summer mornings, going to the Summer Palace near my house to see the lotus flowers was the thing that made me happiest and most at ease.

One day, I walked to the lotus pond as usual, breathing in its sweet fragrance. The morning mist had not yet lifted, drifting softly in thin strands around the pond. Big lotus flowers stood wide open with brilliant petals, their pale white tips tinged with a soft pink that looked as though a master Chinese painter had gently brushed them with rosy ink. Was that a tiny dancing fairy on the tender yellow stamens? Oh, it was a large dragonfly, its wings sparkling with bright light, leaping and dancing gracefully among the great blossoms. The lotus stems stood tall and straight, proud as a gentleman, swaying only slightly in the wind. The broad green lotus leaves floated on the water's surface, crowded together cheerfully and covering the pond like messengers who had come from far away just to admire the lotuses, quietly keeping watch below the water's fairy. And the cute little lotus pods looked like adorable children, their plump green faces turned toward the sunshine, full of hope.

Suddenly, so enchanted by the beauty around me that I really wished I could become that lucky dragonfly, a tiny person standing on my tiptoes among the soft yellow stamens, dancing ballet. I would leap lightly from one flower to another like a butterfly, then dance from the lotus petals onto the broad green leaves. I spun and ran across this stage of flowers, all the lotuses dancing with me, all the lotus leaves clapping for me. Yes, looking at my reflection in the clear water, I was beautiful—a Lotus Princess dancing gracefully in my own kingdom... Then, someone familiar appeared in the distance. It was Mom! She had come to see the lotuses too. I waved at her as hard as I could from atop the flower, but she couldn't see me. Perhaps I was just too small. I got worried, jumped up and down, and shouted, "Mom!"... And then, I woke up.

It was a sweet dream by the lotus pond, a dream just for me—the dream of the Lotus Princess.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 海底世界
fields.content:
你可知道，大海深处是怎么样的吗？
海面上波涛汹涌的时候，海底依然很宁静。最大的风浪也只能影响到海面以下几十米深。而在阳光照射不到的海底，水越深光线越暗，五百米以下就完全黑了。在这一片黑暗的深海里，却有许多光点像闪烁的星星，那是有发光器官的深水鱼在游动。
海底是否一片寂静，没有一点儿声音呢？不是的。海底的动物常常在窃窃私语。你用水中听音器一听，就能听见各种声音：有的像蜜蜂一样嗡嗡作响，有的像小鸟一样啾啾欢叫，有的像小狗一样汪汪不停，还有的好像在打鼾一般……它们吃东西的时候发出一种声音，行进的时候发出另一种声音，遇到危险还会发出警报。
海里的动物，人类已经知道的大约有三万种。它们各有各的活动方法。海参靠肌肉伸缩爬行，每小时只能前进四米。有一种鱼的身体像梭子，每小时能游几十公里，攻击其他动物的时候，比普通的火车还快。乌贼和章鱼能突然向前方喷水，利用水的反推力迅速后退。还有些贝类自己不动，干脆就扒在轮船底下做免费的长途旅行。
海底有山，有峡谷，也有森林和草地。海底植物的色彩多种多样，有褐色的，有紫色的，还有红色的。最小的单细胞海藻，要用显微镜才能看清楚。最大的海藻长达二三百米，是地球上最长的生物。
海底当然还蕴藏着丰富的煤、铁、石油和天然气，并拥有陆地上蕴藏量很少的稀有金属。 海底真的是一个景色奇异、物产丰富、神奇无比的世界。
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Underwater World**

Do you know what the deep sea looks like?

When the ocean waves are churning and wild above, the seafloor stays very calm and quiet. The biggest storms only reach a few dozen meters down. In the parts where sunlight never finds its way, the water gets darker the deeper you go—below five hundred meters, it’s completely black. Yet in this dark underwater world, there are many glowing specks that twinkle like stars. Those are deep-sea fish with their own special lights, swimming through the night.

Is the seabed completely silent, with not a single sound? Not at all. The animals of the sea often whisper to one another. If you listen with a special underwater microphone, you can hear all sorts of sounds: some go buzz like bees, others chirp like little birds, some bark like puppies, and a few even sound like they’re snoring! They make different sounds when they eat, when they swim along, and even warning signals when danger is near.

Scientists already know about thirty thousand kinds of animals that live in the sea. Each one moves in its own special way. Sea cucumbers crawl along using their muscles, moving only about four meters an hour. Some fish are shaped like spindles and can swim dozens of kilometers each hour—faster than an ordinary train when they chase their food. Squid and octopuses shoot water backward to zoom forward quickly, while certain shellfish simply cling to the bottom of ships and enjoy a free ride to distant places.

On the seafloor, there are mountains and valleys, forests and meadows. The plants come in all sorts of colors—brown, purple, and red. The tiniest seaweeds are so small you need a microscope to see them, but the largest seaweeds grow two or three hundred meters long, making them some of the longest living things on Earth.

Beneath the sea, too, lie rich stores of coal, iron, oil, and natural gas, as well as rare metals that are hard to find on land. The ocean floor truly is a wondrous place—full of wonder, full of life, and full of treasures waiting to be discovered.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 金色花
fields.subtitle: 选自泰戈尔《新月集》（郑振铎译）
fields.subtitle_en: From Tagore's Crescent Moon (translated by Zheng Zhenduo)
fields.content:
假如我变成了一朵金色花，为了好玩，长在树的高枝上，笑嘻嘻地在空中摇摆，又在新叶上跳舞，妈妈，你会认识我吗？
你要是叫道：“孩子，你在哪里呀？” 我会暗暗地在那里匿笑，却一声儿不响。
我要悄悄地开放花瓣儿，看着你工作。
当你沐浴后，湿发披在两肩，穿过金色花的林荫，走到做祷告的小庭院时，你会嗅到这花香，却不知道这香气是从我身上来的。
当你吃过午饭，坐在窗前读《罗摩衍那》，那棵树的阴影落在你的头发与膝上时，我便要将我小小的影子投在你的书页上，正投在你所读的地方。
这时你会猜得出这就是你孩子的小小影子吗？
当你黄昏时拿了灯到牛棚里去，我会突然地再落到地上来，又变成了你的孩子，求你讲故事给我听。
你一定会说：“你到哪里去了，你这淘气的孩子？”
“我不告诉你，妈妈。”因为我还要偷偷做一朵芳香迷人的金色花，悄悄陪伴着你，我亲爱的妈妈。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Golden Flower

If I became a golden flower, just for fun, growing on a high branch of a tree, swaying and giggling in the breeze, dancing on the fresh green leaves, would you recognize me, Mama?
If you called out, "Child, where are you?" I would hide and giggle quietly, without making a sound.
I would softly open my petals and watch you work.
After your bath, with your wet hair draped over your shoulders, walking through the golden-flowered path to the little courtyard where you pray, you would smell this fragrance, though you wouldn't know it came from me.
After lunch, when you sit by the window reading the Ramayana, and the shadow of the tree falls on your hair and your knees, I would gently drop my tiny shadow onto your book, right on the page you're reading.
Would you guess that this is your child's little shadow?
When you carry the lamp to the cowshed at dusk, I would suddenly fall back to the ground and become your child once more, asking you to tell me a story.
You would surely say, "Where have you been, you naughty child?"
"I won't tell you, Mama." Because I want to keep being a sweetly fragrant golden flower, quietly staying by your side, my dear Mama.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 小蚂蚁回家
fields.content:
美丽的秋天到了，大自然变成了另一番景象。金黄的树叶，沉甸甸的果实，处处都洋溢着果香。小蚂蚁在这个时候可没闲着，为过严冬做准备，小蚂蚁和大家一起出动寻找食物。
小蚂蚁忽然闻到了一股香味，于是他离开了长长的队伍，顺着随风飘来的阵阵香味，来到一棵茂盛的桂花树旁。小小的、金灿灿的桂花开满了整棵桂花树，小蚂蚁抬头望着那些飘着甜蜜香味的桂花，被深深吸引了。
于是，小蚂蚁开始爬树了。他爬呀爬，沿着树干不知爬了多长时间，才爬到树顶枝的花瓣上。这一刻，小蚂蚁仿佛来到了一个香喷喷的黄金世界，浓郁的香味快把他熏晕了，他全身都沾满了桂花的浓香。
小蚂蚁高兴极了。太阳光像一条金色的被子，盖在身上暖洋洋的，特别舒服。就这样，他不知不觉地、幸福地睡着了。小蚂蚁一觉醒来，一看天色不早了，就急急忙忙往家走。他看到了自己的窝，看到了窝口的两个小伙伴。小蚂蚁连忙打招呼：“喂，你们好啊！”不料，那两个小伙伴奇怪地望了望他，好像从来没见过他一样，完全不理睬。小蚂蚁也没在意，他多么想快点回到窝里去呀！
可是他往前一爬，那两个小伙伴竟把他当敌人，张开嘴，恶狠狠地朝他扑过来。这下可把小蚂蚁吓了一大跳。“这是怎么回事啊？”还没等小蚂蚁回过神来，紧接着窝里又冲出一群蚂蚁，他们可全是他的好伙伴啊，但是现在，居然全都翻脸啦！
“到底发生了什么事？！”小蚂蚁边逃边喊，“是我啊！我是小蚂蚁呀！”可是无论他怎么解释，那群蚂蚁始终凶恶地追着他，差点就要咬到他了。小蚂蚁只能拼命往前跑，一直跑啊跑，直到伙伴们离远了，不再追了，他才停了下来。小蚂蚁站在小河边伤心地哭了。
小蚂蚁多么孤独！他实在不明白，自己到底做了什么错事呢？小伙伴们为什么要这么对他？他们恨他，想咬他，要赶走他……小蚂蚁很难过，也很沮丧。他歪着脑袋想啊想，忽然，小蚂蚁想起了小时候妈妈说的话：“孩子，你要记住一件事，我们每一群蚂蚁就是一个大家族，都有一种特殊的气味。要是你失去这种气味，家里人就不认识你了，就会把你当敌人，非赶走你不可！”
“哦，原来是这样啊……”小蚂蚁恍然大悟，“刚才我身上沾了花香，花香遮盖了原来的气味，别的蚂蚁分辨不出来了！怪不得这些熟悉的伙伴们都翻了脸呢！”
想到这里，小蚂蚁真后悔呀，光顾着在甜美的桂花树上睡觉了，这下可怎么办呢？如何回家啊？
这时，一只可爱的小绿青蛙跳了过来，他看着小蚂蚁自言自语了好久，于是对他说：“呱呱呱！小蚂蚁，别烦恼了，快跟我一起跳到河里洗个澡吧！”小蚂蚁心里一亮：“对啊，洗个澡不就可以把身上的香味洗掉了吗？”小蚂蚁爬到好心的青蛙背上，一下跳进水里，痛痛快快地在河里洗了一个澡。
小蚂蚁回了窝，小伙伴们对他可亲热啦，完全不像刚才的阵势了。他们一个个主动向小蚂蚁打招呼：“喂，小家伙，你去哪儿了？怎么这么晚才回来？好长时间没见到你了！”“是啊，你上哪儿去了？”“我们可惦记你呢！”
小蚂蚁笑着晃着触角，心想：“哎，以后可不能再到有特殊气味的地方去睡觉了！”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Ant Goes Home

The beautiful autumn had arrived, and nature had changed into something new. Golden leaves everywhere, heavy fruits hanging from the branches, and sweet fragrance floating in the air. The little ant was very busy at this time, getting ready for the long winter ahead. The little ant went out with everyone to find food.

Suddenly, the little ant smelled a wonderful fragrance. So he left the long line of ants and followed the sweet smell carried by the wind until he came to a big, leafy osmanthus tree. Tiny golden flowers covered the whole tree. The little ant looked up at those sweet-smelling flowers and was deeply attracted.

So the little ant started climbing the tree. He climbed and climbed, along the trunk for what felt like a very long time, until he reached the petals at the very top. At that moment, the little ant felt like he had arrived in a fragrant, golden world. The rich perfume was almost too much, and his whole body became covered in the sweet scent of osmanthus flowers.

The little ant was so happy. The sunlight fell on him like a warm golden blanket, and he felt cozy and comfortable. Before he knew it, he fell into a happy, peaceful sleep. When the little ant woke up, he saw that it was already late, so he hurried home. He saw his nest and two friends standing at the entrance. The little ant quickly called out, "Hello there!" But those two friends looked at him strangely, as if they had never seen him before, and completely ignored him. The little ant didn't mind too much because he so badly wanted to get inside the nest!

But when he took one more step forward, those two friends treated him like an enemy. They opened their mouths and ferociously lunged toward him. This gave the little ant a huge scare. "What is going on?!" Before the little ant could figure it out, a whole group of ants rushed out of the nest. They were all his good friends! But now, they had all turned against him!

"What's happening?!" the little ant cried while running away. "It's me! I'm the little ant!" But no matter how much he explained, the group of ants kept chasing him fiercely, almost close enough to bite him. The little ant could only run as fast as he could, running and running, until his friends were far behind and no longer chasing him. Then he stopped. The little ant stood by the riverbank and cried sadly.

The little ant felt so lonely! He truly couldn't understand what mistake he had made. Why were his friends treating him this way? They hated him, wanted to bite him, wanted to drive him away... The little ant was very sad and discouraged. He tilted his head and thought and thought. Suddenly, he remembered what his mommy had told him when he was little: "Child, remember this. Every group of ants is like one big family, and we all have a special smell. If you lose that smell, your family won't recognize you anymore. They'll treat you like an enemy and chase you away!"

"Oh, so that's what happened..." The little ant suddenly understood. "Just now, my body got covered in the flower scent. That sweet smell covered up my original scent, and the other ants couldn't tell it was me! No wonder those familiar friends turned against me!"

Thinking about this, the little ant really regretted it. He had been so busy sleeping on that sweet-smelling osmanthus tree that he hadn't thought about anything else. But what should he do now? How could he go home?

At that moment, a cute little green frog hopped over. It watched the little ant talking to himself for a long time, then said to him, "Ribbit, ribbit! Little ant, don't worry anymore. Come jump into the river with me and take a bath!" The little ant's eyes lit up. "That's right! If I take a bath, I can wash the smell off my body!" The little ant climbed onto the kind frog's back, and down they jumped into the water. The little ant had a wonderful swim and washed himself clean in the river.

When the little ant returned to the nest, his friends were so friendly toward him now—nothing like the scary scene from before. One by one, they warmly greeted him. "Hey there, little guy! Where have you been? Why did you come back so late? We haven't seen you for such a long time!" "Yeah, where did you go?" "We were all worried about you!"

The little ant smiled and wiggled his antennae, thinking to himself, "Oh dear, I must never go sleep in a place with such a strong smell again!"
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 猫与猫寻
fields.title_en: The Cat and the Kitten's Search
fields.content:
奥娜是一个爱猫的孩子。作为动物保护者的妈妈，总会带回一些流浪猫，而这些猫成了奥娜最好的玩伴。奥娜慢慢长大，猫也跟着长大，她和猫的缘分也在继续。在一次夏令营中，她经历了一段奇妙旅程。
奥娜在郊外看到了一只脖子上戴着铃铛的可爱白猫，喜欢猫的她就跟了上去。阳光下的郊外，微风吹拂，猫尾草左右摇摆，真的像猫猫的尾巴一样。猫猫不时地回头看看奥娜，仿佛催促奥娜一般。穿过一片猫尾草，奥娜来到了一座废旧工厂，她跟着猫走上走下。奥娜穿过废弃的机器，走上有青苔的楼梯，这时猫猫顺着传送带滑了下去。奥娜正在考虑要不要跟上去的时候，不知从哪里传来了呼唤声。她一步没站稳，趴在传送带上急速滑了下去。
奥娜不知滑落了多久，突然眼前一亮，亮得她睁不开眼睛——棉花糖的云彩，七彩果冻的彩虹，面包的森林，两条河并行消失在远处，仔细看原来是牛奶河和巧克力河。当她睁开眼睛的时候，她坐在一个到处都是猫尾草的地方，带她来的猫站了起来，奥娜发现猫竟然和她的身高差不多了。
“你怎么变大了？”
“是你变小了。奥娜，欢迎来到猫的世界，喵之国欢迎你。”
“啊……你怎么会说话？”
“你教的啊。”
“我教的？！”
“你小时候，教过我们很多事的，跟我走。”
穿过猫尾草，是一条波光粼粼的河，不时有快乐的鱼儿跃出河面，对奥娜说：“欢迎欢迎，我们的小公主。”
“鱼也能说话？”奥娜吃惊地说，“小猫咪，你叫啥啊？”
“奥娜公主，你给我起过名字啊。我叫小白。”
“……你在说什么？”
“奥娜，你跟我走吧，你会看到很多老朋友的。”
桥对面是一座古老的城堡，小白推开门走了进去，奥娜被这古香古色的古堡吸引住了。她站在大厅中央，眯眼睛双手伸向天，仿佛她就是这座古堡的主人一样。
她睁开眼，发现小白也不见了。“小白，你在哪儿啊？”奥娜的声音在古堡里久久回荡。她走向前面更大的门，但推开门的一瞬间她就震惊了。
屋子里有许多糖果做的猫窝和一个糖果做成的滑梯，奥娜来到了她梦中的仙境。好几只猫，一起捧着生日蛋糕，对她唱着猫声猫气的生日快乐歌。奥娜愣了。
小白喊道：“奥娜公主生日快乐。”
“今天是我生日？”
“是啊，我们每一只猫都曾陪你过过生日。你还给我们吃好吃的蛋糕。今年我们一起陪你度过这个生日。”
奥娜脑海里浮现出以前每一个和猫猫们过的生日。那时的她和猫笑得都好开心。猫猫们送给奥娜的生日礼物，多得她都快抱不下了。一个个美丽精巧的礼盒，都打着可爱的蝴蝶结，她开心得仿佛像在过圣诞节般。
奥娜打开蛋糕盒，发现偌大的蛋糕只剩下了一个空壳，里面一个可爱的胖豚鼠睡得香甜。所有人都震惊了。豚鼠揉着睡眼醒了，打了一个哈欠。“好可爱的老鼠啊！”奥娜说道。
“我不是老鼠，我是豚鼠。”小胖子愤愤地说。“你这个贼，吃我们公主的蛋糕。”猫猫们生气了。“我没有偷，就是路过吃一口。”小豚鼠拍拍屁股。“你就是偷东西的贼。”“我才不是。”豚鼠也瞪起了小圆眼睛。
这时一直打鼾的大肥花猫，忽然吹破了一个鼻涕泡，他的动作和小豚鼠竟然出奇地一致。他完全看不出发生了什么，别的猫继续在争论，他听完后摇摇头又缩成一团继续睡去。
一只小黄猫对奥娜说：“奥娜，对不起，我得要回我的礼物了。”说完他打开了礼物盒，取出一团线球。在其他几只猫的帮助下，把小胖子绑了起来。
奥娜哭喊道：“你们干吗啊？”
“奥娜，他是贼，我们必须把他抓起来。”
“可他这么可爱，不就是一个蛋糕吗？我们一起过生日也算上他一起呗，蛋糕没有也没关系，我能再看到你们就很开心了。”
“奥娜，我们的世界容不得不爱劳动，偷东西的人。”
“这个豚鼠能做什么啊？”奥娜问道。
“我可以和那个胖猫一起工作，他能做什么我就能做什么。”小胖子回答。
大肥花猫眼睛眯成一道缝，打着哈欠说：“要不让他跟着我吧，我俩都很有力气，能干很多活儿，但是白天我们得睡觉。”
“奥娜，你觉得怎么样啊？”奥娜用力地点了点头：“嗯。”
小黄猫不情愿地解开了绳索，小胖子和所有的猫玩在了一起。奥娜和猫猫们玩起了躲猫猫、老鹰捉小鸡、真心话大冒险。猫猫们连他们好吃的藏哪里都说了，小豚鼠在一旁嘿嘿地笑着。他们的笑声送走了太阳，迎来了月亮。
奥娜在棉花糖做的被子里甜甜睡去。
当她缓缓睁开眼时，发现自己躺在刚才那片猫尾草上，暖暖的阳光很是温暖。
奥娜坐上车，口袋里仿佛有东西急着要出来。她打开口袋，小胖子露出了头，对奥娜做出“嘘”的手势。这是奥娜这些年来最有意思的一个生日。晚饭时妈妈买的蛋糕很好吃，小胖子埋头在他的饭盒里吃得满脸都是奶油。
“妈妈，你说猫会说话吗？”
“你小时候就总和猫猫说话，你忘了吗？”
时间再次回到那个时候，奥娜点着一群小猫的头说：“记住我是你们的小公主，你们要一直记得我的生日哦，本公主赏你一块蛋糕。”小白猫喵喵地叫着，脖子上的小铃铛发出悦耳的声音。
“小胖子，你别吃了……”夜很静，奥娜的声音却很清晰。那只大肥花猫远远看了一眼奥娜的房间，团成一团沉沉睡去。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Cat Who Found a Friend

Oona was a child who loved cats. Her mom, an animal protector, would always bring home stray cats, and these cats became Oona's best companions. As Oona slowly grew up, the cats grew up too, and her bond with them continued. During a summer camp, she experienced a wonderful journey.

Oona saw a cute white cat wearing a bell around its neck in the suburbs, and being a cat lover, she followed it. Under the sunshine in the countryside, a gentle breeze blew, and foxtail grass swayed left and right, truly looking like cat tails. The little cat kept looking back at Oona, as if urging her to hurry along. After passing through a field of foxtail grass, Oona arrived at an abandoned factory, following the cat up and down the stairs. She walked past old machines and climbed mossy steps, when suddenly the cat slid down a conveyor belt. Before Oona could decide whether to follow, she heard a call from somewhere. One unsteady step and she tumbled onto the conveyor belt, sliding down rapidly.

Oona didn't know how long she had been sliding when suddenly, bright light flooded everywhere—so bright she couldn't even open her eyes. Clouds made of cotton candy, a rainbow like colorful jelly, a forest made of bread, and two rivers running side by side that disappeared into the distance. On closer look, they were a milk river and a chocolate river. When she finally opened her eyes, she found herself sitting in a place covered all around with foxtail grass. The cat that had brought her stood up, and Oona noticed that the cat was now about the same height as her!

"Why have you gotten so big?"
"You've gotten smaller, Oona. Welcome to the world of cats! We, the Kingdom of Meow, welcome you."
"Ah... how can you talk?"
"You taught us."
"You taught me?!"
"When you were little, you taught us so many things. Come with me."

Past the foxtail grass ran a sparkling river, where happy fish occasionally leaped out of the water, saying to Oona, "Welcome, welcome, our little princess."
"Can fish talk too?" said Oona in surprise. "Little kitty, what's your name?"
"Princess Oona gave us names. I'm called Little White."
"...What are you talking about?"
"Oona, come with me, and you'll see many old friends."

On the other side of the bridge stood an ancient castle. Little White pushed open the door and walked inside. Oona was captivated by the castle's vintage charm. She stood in the center of the hall, squinting and reaching her hands toward the sky, as if she were truly the owner of this castle.

When she opened her eyes again, she found Little White was nowhere in sight. "Little White, where are you?" Oona's voice echoed throughout the castle for a long time. She walked toward a bigger door in front, but the moment she pushed it open, she was stunned.

The room was filled with candy-made cat houses and a candy slide. Oona had arrived in the fairy tale land she had always dreamed of. Several cats held a birthday cake together and sang a meowy version of "Happy Birthday" to her. Oona stood frozen.

Little White called out, "Happy Birthday, Princess Oona!"
"Is today my birthday?"
"Yes, every one of us has celebrated your birthday with you. You used to feed us delicious cake. This year, we'll celebrate with you together."

Images of past birthdays spent with the cats came flooding into Oona's mind. Back then, she and the cats had laughed so happily. The birthday gifts the cats gave Oona were so many she could barely hold them all. Beautiful, delicate gift boxes tied with cute ribbons made her feel as joyful as if it were Christmas.

Oona opened the cake box and discovered that the huge cake was nothing but an empty shell. Inside, a cute chubby guinea pig slept soundly. Everyone was shocked. The guinea pig rubbed its sleepy eyes awake and let out a yawn. "What a cute little mouse!" Oona said.
"I'm not a mouse, I'm a guinea pig," said the little chubby one indignantly. "You thief! You ate our princess's cake!" the cats exclaimed angrily. "I didn't steal it, I was just passing by and took a bite," the little guinea pig said, patting its bottom. "You're a stealing thief!" "I'm not!" the guinea pig retorted, staring back with its little round eyes.

At that moment, a large fat calico cat that had been snoring blew up a snot bubble. Its action was surprisingly similar to the guinea pig's. It had no idea what was happening. The other cats continued arguing, and after listening for a bit, the fat cat shook its head, curled up, and went back to sleep.

A little yellow cat said to Oona, "Oona, I'm sorry, but I need my gift back." Saying this, he opened the gift box and took out a ball of yarn. With the help of the other cats, they tied up the chubby little one.

Oona cried out, "What are you doing?"
"Oona, he is a thief. We must catch him!"
"But he's so cute. It's just a cake, right? Let's include him in our birthday celebration. It's okay if the cake is gone. I'm so happy just to see you all again."
"Oona, our world doesn't tolerate lazy, stealing people."
"What can this guinea pig do?" Oona asked.
"I can work alongside that fat cat. Whatever he can do, I can do too," the chubby one replied.
The large fat calico squinted its eyes and, yawning, said, "How about you let him follow me? The two of us are strong and can do lots of work, but we sleep during the day."
"Oona, what do you think?" Oona nodded firmly. "Mm-hmm."

Reluctantly, the little yellow cat untied the rope, and the chubby guinea pig began playing with all the cats. Oona and the cats played hide-and-seek, catch-the-chicken, and truth or dare. The cats even told them where they hid their favorite treats, and the little guinea pig chuckled happily nearby. Their laughter saw the sun set and the moon rise.

Oona fell into a sweet sleep wrapped in a quilt made of cotton candy.

When she slowly opened her eyes, she found herself lying on that patch of foxtail grass again, with warm sunlight gently caressing her.

Oona got into the car, and something in her pocket seemed eager to come out. She opened her pocket, and the chubby guinea pig poked its head out, putting a finger to its lips in a "shhh" gesture. This was the most wonderful birthday Oona had ever had in all these years. At dinner, the cake her mom bought was delicious. The chubby one buried its face in its lunchbox, eating until its face was covered in cream.

"Mom, do you think cats can talk?"
"You used to talk to cats all the time when you were little. Don't you remember?"

Time returned to those moments once again. Oona pointed at the group of kittens and said, "Remember, I am your little princess. You must always remember my birthday. I'll reward you with a piece of cake." The little white cat meowed, and the small bell around its neck made a pleasant tinkling sound.

"Little Fatty, stop eating..." the night was very quiet, and Oona's voice rang clear and soft. Far away, the large fat calico cat glanced toward Oona's room, curled itself into a ball, and fell into a deep sleep.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 灵感
fields.subtitle: 林徽因
fields.subtitle_en: Lin Huiyin
fields.content:
是你，是花，是梦，打这儿过，
此刻像风在摇动着我；
告诉日子重叠盘盘的山窝；
清泉潺潺流动转狂放的河；
孤僻林里闲开着鲜妍花，
细香常伴着圆月静天里挂；
且有神仙纷纭的浮出紫烟，
衫裾飘忽映影在山溪前；
给人的理想和理想上
铺香花，叫人心和心合着唱；
直到灵魂舒展成条银河，
长长流在天上一千首歌！
是你，是花，是梦，打这里儿过，
此刻像风在摇动着我；
告诉日子是这样的不清醒；
当中偏响着想不到的一串铃，
树枝里轻声摇曳；金镶上翠，
低了头的斜阳，又一抹光辉。
难怪阶前人忘掉黄昏，脚下草，
高阁古松，望着天上点骄傲；
留下檀香，木鱼，合掌
在神龛前，在蒲团上，
楼外又楼外，幻想彩霞却缀成
凤凰栏杆，挂起了塔顶上灯！
fields.content_en:
Title: Inspiration

It's you, it's flowers, it's dreams, passing right by,
Right now swaying me like wind;
Tell the days nestled in winding mountain hollows,
Clear springs babbling into a wild, rushing river;
In a quiet forest, fresh flowers bloom at their leisure,
Their sweet scent often accompanying the round moon hanging in the still sky;
And immortals rise gently from swirling purple mist,
Their flowing robes shimmering, shadows dancing by the mountain stream;
Laying fragrant blossoms upon our ideals,
So that hearts sing together as one;
Until a soul unfolds into a gentle galaxy,
Flowing long across the sky, a thousand sweet songs!

It's you, it's flowers, it's dreams, passing right by,
Right now swaying me like wind;
Telling me that the days are soft and hazy,
With an unexpected little ring of bells chiming in between,
A gentle rustle among the branches; gold kissed with green,
The sunset bowing low, then glowing once more.

No wonder those standing on the steps forget about twilight,
The grass beneath their feet,
The ancient pines on the tall tower gazing proudly toward the sky;
Leaving behind sandalwood, wooden fishes, palms pressed together,
Before the shrine, upon the cushioned mat,
Layer after layer, fantasies woven into rainbow clouds become
A phoenix railing, hanging lanterns from the tower's peak!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 秋叶
fields.content:
金色
总是在秋天落入人间
带着最温暖的太阳跃入树林
树林
最先感受秋日的凉爽
悄悄留着余温包裹着自己
风儿
让叶子们背上降落伞
穿着闪亮的金纱不停地飘摇
松鼠
是一群顽皮的小精灵
带着欢笑躲进金色的帐篷
披着树叶滑翔在日落的树林
秋叶
像红的，黄的，彩色的小手儿
是精灵们欢乐的玩具
是孩子们温暖的被子
是宝贝们柔软的地毯
是淘气包们神秘的窝
是大自然轻盈的幸福天堂
fields.content_en:
**Title: Autumn Leaves**

Golden
always fall to earth in autumn
leaping into the forest with the warmest sunlight
The forest
feels the coolness of autumn first
quietly holding onto its warmth, wrapping itself snug
The wind
lets the leaves carry tiny parachutes
dressing them in shimmering golden gossamer, drifting on and on
Squirrels
are a troop of playful little spirits
tittering as they hide inside golden tents
gliding through the evening woods on leaf-beds
Autumn leaves
like tiny hands in red, yellow, and every color
are the playful toys of these little spirits
are warm blankets for children
are soft carpets for little ones
are secret little dens for the mischievous
are nature's light, happy paradise
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 妈妈的爱
fields.content:
是眼角的皱纹
是渐渐昏花的眼神
是颤巍巍的手指
和纤小的缝衣针
是曾经柔柔的歌谣
领着我感知这个世界
妈妈的爱
是稀松的牙齿
就像我曾经记忆中的乳汁
品味这个世界的甘甜
妈妈
我想做你的双腿
跨越整个世界
我想做你记忆的天使
陪伴你生活中的点滴
我想做你清澈的眼睛
找到最明亮的星星
妈妈
我想扶着你
爬上每一段艰难上下的楼梯间
走过每一根拐杖敲击湿滑的地面
妈妈
我想依偎着你
在你怀中幽幽细语
就像我曾经的牙牙学语
fields.content_en:
**Title: Mama's Love**

The lines around your eyes
The eyes that see less clearly now
The trembling fingers
And the tiny needle for mending clothes
The gentle songs you sang
That led me to understand this world

Mama's love
Is your soft teeth
Like the milk I once knew
Tasting all the sweetness of life

Mama
I want to be your legs
To carry you across the whole world
I want to be the guardian of your memories
To watch over every moment of your days
I want to be your clear eyes
To find the brightest stars in the sky

Mama
I want to hold you as you climb
Every difficult staircase
To walk beside you as your cane taps
On the wet, slippery ground

Mama
I want to curl up against you
And whisper softly in your arms
Just like I once babblingly learned to speak
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 盲人摸象
fields.title_en: The Blind Men and the Elephant
fields.content:
有一天，四个盲人坐在树下乘凉。有个人牵着大象走了过来，口中大声喊着：“象来了，请让开一点儿！”
一个盲人说：“象是什么样子的？让我们摸一摸吧！”
另外三个盲人也说：“对，摸一摸就知道象是什么样子了。”
牵象的人把象拴在树上，他们就去摸。
一个盲人摸着了象的身子，就说：“我知道了，象原来像一堵墙。”
一个盲人摸着了象的鼻子，就说：“象跟又圆又光滑的棍子一样。”
第三个盲人摸着了象的腿，就说：“你们俩说的都不对，象跟柱子差不多。”
最后一个盲人摸到了象的尾巴，就大叫起来：“你们都错了！象其实跟绳子一个样！”
四个盲人你争我吵，都说自己对，谁也不服谁。牵象的人对他们说：“你们都没有说对。你们每个人只摸到了象的一部分，怎么能断定象是什么样子呢？”
最后，四个人都认真地摸了整头大象。这回，大家都高兴地说：“原来大象有着又圆又光滑的鼻子，有着像柱子一样的腿，有着像绳子一样的尾巴，还有着像墙一样的身体……大象真大啊！”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Blind Men and the Elephant

One day, four blind men were sitting under a tree, enjoying the cool shade. A man walking by led an elephant past them, calling out loudly, "The elephant is coming! Please make some room!"

One blind man asked, "What does an elephant look like? Let's touch it and find out!"

The other three agreed, "Yes, let's feel it and we'll know what it's like!"

The man tied the elephant to the tree, and the four blind men went over to touch it.

One blind man touched the elephant's body and said, "I know! An elephant is like a big wall."

Another touched the elephant's trunk and said, "An elephant is like a round, smooth stick."

The third blind man touched one of its legs and said, "You're both wrong. An elephant is more like a pillar."

The last blind man touched the elephant's tail and called out, "You're all wrong! An elephant is actually like a rope!"

The four men argued and disagreed, each insisting he was right. The elephant keeper told them, "None of you is quite right. Each of you only felt part of the elephant. How can you know what the whole elephant looks like?"

Finally, the four men carefully felt every part of the elephant. This time, they all happily said, "So an elephant has a round, smooth trunk, legs like pillars, a tail like a rope, and a body like a wall... An elephant is truly so big!"
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 海
fields.content:
大海，对我总是有着深深的魔力。并不是我喜欢在大海里畅游，因为我几乎不会进到海里。深深吸引我的，是美丽多变的海滩。
每每来到大海边，我几乎都会忘记自己的身体，忘记自己的存在，我会用心来感受大海。也许正是如此，我才会感受得如此细腻和真切。我总是尽力珍惜自己的每一个感官去体会的感觉，体会那飘着淡淡咸味的海风，那变幻无常、色彩斑斓的厚重的云，那形态奔放、汹涌滚滚的层层海浪，那丝丝柔滑、温柔缠绕的海草，那深深包裹着我的脚丫的金黄柔软的沙滩，那一处处迷你而壮观的沙雕，那迅速而可爱的横冲直撞的小海蟹，那形状各异的贝壳，那瞬间跃入海平面的夕阳……
一切的美好感受刺激着我的每一个细胞。我总会恍惚，自己就犹如这一阵海风，一朵浪花，一缕海草，一片细沙，一只小海蟹，一只小海螺，一束阳光……深深地，深深地融入这海边的一切。
每每震撼我的，更是那呼啸的风与风的合唱，时而畅快，时而悲沉，时而清朗，时而暗啸……而我，总会随风吟唱。
海滩，就是大海的一扇神奇的门，我要站在门口，呼唤充满魔力的大海。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Sea

The sea has always held a deep magic for me. It's not because I love swimming in it — I hardly ever go into the water at all. What truly draws me in is the beautiful, ever-changing beach.

Every time I visit the seaside, I seem to forget my body, forget myself entirely, and let my heart feel the sea. Perhaps that is why I can sense it so gently and so deeply. I always try to treasure every feeling my senses bring me — the sea breeze carrying a soft saltiness, the thick clouds shifting colors and shapes above me, the wild rolling waves crashing again and again, the silky seaweed wrapping gently around my toes, the warm golden sand hugging my little feet, the tiny yet grand sand sculptures scattered about, the playful little crabs scuttling swiftly back and forth, the shells in all sorts of strange and lovely shapes, the sunset leaping into the sea in a single bright moment…

All these beautiful sensations stir every part of me. I often feel as if I've become the sea breeze itself, a splash of wave, a strand of seaweed, a grain of fine sand, a little crab, a small conch shell, a ray of warm sunlight… blending deeply, ever so deeply, into everything by the shore.

What moves me most, though, is the wind — howling and singing at once, now joyful and free, now low and solemn, now clear and bright, now whispering softly in secret… And I always sing along with it.

The beach is like a wonderful door to the sea, and I stand at its opening, calling out to the magical sea.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 你的笑
fields.subtitle: 林徽因
fields.subtitle_en: Lin Huiyin
fields.content:
笑的是你的眼睛，口唇，
唇边浑圆的旋涡。
艳丽如同露珠，
朵朵的笑向
贝齿的闪光里躲。
那是笑——神的笑，美的笑：
水的映影，风的轻歌。
笑的是你惺松的鬈发，
散乱地挨着耳朵。
轻软如同花影，
痒痒的甜蜜
涌进了你的心窝。
那是笑——诗的笑，画的笑：
云的留痕，浪的柔波。
笑的是你轻微的震动
仿佛生命的气息
带动我的心跳
阵阵的幸福
溢满我们的心
那是笑——爱的笑，心的笑：
光的照射，精灵的呼唤。
fields.content_en:
# Your Smile

Your eyes smile, your lips smile,
and the round little dimples by your mouth.
Bright as morning dew,
your little blossoms of laughter
hide behind the gleam of your tiny teeth.
That is a smile—divine, beautiful:
a reflection of water, a soft song of the wind.

Your sleepy, curly hair smiles too,
tousled and resting gently against your ears.
Soft as flower shadows,
a ticklish sweetness
pours into your little heart.
That is a smile—poetic, painted:
the trace of clouds, the gentle ripple of waves.

Your gentle trembling smiles as well,
like the breath of life itself,
stirring my heartbeat,
wave after wave of happiness
overflowing our hearts.
That is a smile—loving, heartfelt:
the glow of light, the call of little spirits.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 奇怪的镜子
fields.content:
美丽的池塘里住着一条漂亮的小红鱼。他快快活活地玩了一天，觉得累了，正想找一个舒服的地方休息一会儿。忽然，小红鱼发现有一样东西在一闪一闪的，他睁大眼睛一看，不禁叫了起来：“好大好亮的镜子啊！”小红鱼想：“要是把这面大镜子搬到家里，让大家都能照一照该多好啊！”这么想着，小红鱼轻轻地游到那镜子边，还没碰着，“镜子”就碎成一块块小片儿了。小红鱼心里挺伤心的，但是不一会儿，那面亮亮的“镜子”又重新圆了起来。
于是，小红鱼急急忙忙找来了正在河边唱歌的小青蛙。“青蛙弟弟，我找到了一面又大又圆的镜子，请你帮我抬回家好吗？”小青蛙一口答应了。小青蛙刚想用宽宽的大嘴巴轻轻衔住镜子，只见“镜子”又碎成一块块小片了。小红鱼和小青蛙都很失落。但是不一会儿，那面神奇的“镜子”再次圆了起来。
于是，小红鱼接着赶紧找来了正在水中跳舞的河蚌。“河蚌姐姐，请你帮我把大镜子抬回家好吗？”河蚌一口答应了，跟着小红鱼来到镜子边。河蚌刚想用两片蚌壳轻轻地夹住镜子，可是“镜子”又碎了。小红鱼、小青蛙、河蚌都很难过。但是很快，那面大大的“镜子”又圆了起来。
小红鱼这回找到了正在水藻中吹泡泡的螃蟹。“螃蟹哥哥，我找到了一面又大又圆的镜子，请你帮我抬回家好吗？”螃蟹一口答应了。他刚想用两只大大的螯轻轻地钳住镜子，可是“镜子”又碎了，成了一块块的小片儿。大家全都很无奈，可是又感到很奇怪：这到底是怎么回事呢，镜子在跟我们开玩笑吗？
这时，只听见一阵“哈哈哈——”的笑声，虾公公拖着长长的胡子来了：“傻孩子们，这哪是什么镜子，这是天上的月亮在水里的影子啊！”小红鱼、小青蛙、河蚌、螃蟹都抬起了头，大家看看天，又看看水面，都哈哈地笑了起来，连池塘里的月亮也笑了呢！
fields.content_en:
Title: The Strange Mirror

In a beautiful pond lived a lovely little red fish. He had played happily all day and felt tired, just looking for a cozy spot to rest. Suddenly, the little red fish noticed something sparkling and shimmering. He opened his eyes wide and exclaimed, "What a big and bright mirror!" The little fish thought, "How wonderful it would be if I could carry this big mirror home so everyone could look into it!" So he swam gently toward the mirror, but before he could even touch it, the "mirror" shattered into tiny pieces. The little fish felt quite sad, but soon enough, the shining "mirror" came back together again.

Then the little red fish hurriedly went to find a little frog who was singing by the riverbank. "Little frog brother, I found a big, round mirror. Could you please help me carry it home?" The little frog agreed at once. But just as he was about to gently hold the mirror in his wide mouth, the "mirror" shattered into pieces again. Both the little fish and the little frog felt very disappointed. Yet, shortly after, the magical "mirror" rounded itself out once more.

So the little red fish quickly went to find a river clam who was dancing in the water. "Miss Clam, could you please help me carry the big mirror home?" The clam agreed right away and followed the little fish to the mirror. But the moment she tried to gently pinch the mirror between her two shells, it broke into pieces once more. The little fish, the little frog, and the clam were all very sad. But soon, the big "mirror" came together again.

This time, the little red fish found a crab blowing bubbles among the water weeds. "Brother Crab, I found a big, round mirror. Please help me carry it home, okay?" The crab agreed without hesitation. But as soon as he tried to gently hold the mirror with his two big claws, it broke into small pieces again. Everyone felt helpless, yet also very puzzled: What was going on? Was the mirror playing tricks on them?

Just then, a hearty "Hahaha—" laugh echoed through the water. Grandpa Shrimp, with his long whiskers trailing behind him, swam over. "You silly little ones, that is not a mirror at all! It is the shadow of the moon in the sky, reflected on the water!" The little fish, the little frog, the clam, and the crab all lifted their heads, looked up at the sky, and then looked down at the water. They all burst into laughter, and even the moon in the pond seemed to laugh too!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 迷人的森林
fields.content:
我走过了太多美丽的地方，而在大自然的所有壮观景象里，我最爱迷人的森林。
森林是可以融入的风景，是所有生命的源泉，是一幅最多彩的水粉画，是探险者最眷恋的家园。
每当清晨悄悄露出一道白曦，袅袅薄雾就环绕了整个森林。钻石般晶莹的露珠，紧紧地挨在一起，点缀着大地。彩色的鸟儿仿佛是森林的音乐家，它们穿越林间的歌声此起彼伏，还有比那更美妙的合唱吗？静静的河水潺潺流过，清澈而闪亮。在晨雾的覆盖中，人们永远不知道它从何而来，去向何处。
湛蓝的天空下是黛色的山峦，葱葱郁郁的树林环绕着，山脉显得格外深邃悠远。五彩斑斓的野花儿竞相怒放着，好像有用不尽的颜色，绽放不完的芳香。艳丽的玫瑰，娇嫩的丁香，星星点点的小野菊，茂密的紫藤，淡雅的曼陀罗……在明媚的阳光下陪伴着翠绿的森林。
瀑布，深潭，绵绵的小溪，滋养着森林里的所有生命。
小松鼠在树干上忙上忙下，猴子在树枝上荡着秋千，小鹿在水边静静饮水，兔子在草丛里蹦来蹦去，小刺猬忙着背果子，萤火虫如精灵般飞舞……这是一幕多么生动的画面啊！
夜晚的森林深邃而神秘，明亮的月光透过树叶，斑驳地洒在地上，星星点点的，有一批夜晚的使者忙碌地延续着白天的热闹，虫儿们起劲地鸣叫着，青蛙在水边唱歌，安静的猫头鹰在树梢注视着一切……
迷人的森林总是充满了快乐的精灵，源源不断地绽放着生命的色彩！
fields.content_en:
# The Enchanting Forest

I have walked through so many beautiful places, but among all the wondrous sights of nature, I love the enchanting forest the most.

The forest is a landscape you can become part of, the source of all life, the most colorful watercolor painting, and the home that adventurers never want to leave.

Every morning, as the first white light quietly peeks through, a delicate mist wraps around the whole forest. Dewdrops, clear and bright like diamonds, nestle close together, adorning the earth. Colorful birds are like the musicians of the forest, their songs rising and falling among the trees. Can there be any lovelier chorus? The quiet river flows gently, clear and sparkling. Covered in morning mist, no one ever knows where it comes from or where it goes.

Beneath the deep blue sky lie dark green mountains, ringed by lush woods, making the ranges seem especially deep and faraway. Colorful wildflowers bloom in joyful competition, as if they had endless colors and unfailing fragrance. Bright roses, tender lilacs, tiny daisies dotted here and there, thick wisteria, and gentle daturas… accompany the emerald forest in the warm sunshine.

Waterfalls, deep pools, and endless little streams nourish all the lives within the forest.

Little squirrels busy themselves up and down the tree trunks, monkeys swing on branches like on a swing, deer drink quietly by the water's edge, rabbits bounce through the grass, hedgehogs hurriedly carry fruits on their backs, and fireflies dance through the air like little spirits… What a lively picture!

At night, the forest grows deep and mysterious. Bright moonlight filters through the leaves, falling in dappled spots on the ground. A band of nighttime messengers busily carries on the excitement of the day. Insects chirp cheerfully, frogs sing by the water, and the quiet owl watches over everything from the treetops.

The enchanting forest is always filled with joyful spirits, endlessly blooming with the colors of life!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 奇怪的尾巴
fields.content:
炎热的夏天总是让人难熬，连动物们都要躲在某个地方凉快凉快。有一天，一条蚯蚓正在大树荫下舒服地乘凉。一只小壁虎爬过来了，招呼蚯蚓：“蚯蚓兄弟，你好！”
“你好啊，小壁虎。”蚯蚓问，“你从哪儿来呀？”小壁虎说：“刚才我在墙根儿下捉苍蝇，一只老花猫猛扑过来，想抓我……”
蚯蚓急忙说：“啊呀，真危险，猫爪子可厉害了，让他抓住可没命啦！”小壁虎一脸不在乎地说：“不要紧，我有办法对付他！你看，我的尾巴可是我的秘密武器。”
蚯蚓往小壁虎身后一看，惊讶地叫道：“哎呀，你的尾巴怎么没有啦 ？尾巴呢？尾巴哪儿去了？”小壁虎挺得意地说：“我只要丢掉尾巴，我的命就能保住啦！”蚯蚓这回更觉得奇怪了：“干吗要把尾巴丢掉呢？没了尾巴多难看啊！”
小壁虎聚精会神地解释着：“我一看老花猫扑过来，就连忙把尾巴甩掉了，然后往草堆里一钻。那时候我的尾巴掉在地上还一摆一摆地动弹呢，老花猫都看呆了，趁他没注意，我就溜走了！”
蚯蚓想了想又有点担忧地说：“噢，是这么回事啊！那你没尾巴了怎么办呢？”小壁虎神秘地笑着说：“不要紧，过不了几天，我会再长出一条新尾巴来！”
“那你跟我们蚯蚓可是一样的了！”蚯蚓听完连忙说，“我们蚯蚓就是身子断了还能再生呢！你知道吗？上回有两只小鸡把我扯成了两截了，还没来得及吃哩，就听一个小孩儿喊：‘小鸡，蚯蚓会耕地，你们不能伤害他！’说着，他就把小鸡赶跑了。没过几天，我的前半截就长出了尾巴，后半截也长出了脑袋……嘿！我就变成了两条啦！”
壁虎听了很高兴地说：“太好啦，蚯蚓兄弟，你的身子断成两截能变成两条蚯蚓，我的尾巴断了，还能长出一条新尾巴。咱们有这样的本事，就要把自己保护好，多为大自然做好事呢。”蚯蚓说：“对啊，你要多多地消灭害虫。我呢，可以松土，造肥，让生长在地里的庄稼长得更好，是不是很棒呢？”
壁虎连声说：“哈哈，我也是这么觉得的！那再见了，蚯蚓兄弟，我接着抓害虫去了！”
“再见！小壁虎！”蚯蚓也开心地说。
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Strange Tail**

Hot summers can be really tough, and even the animals need to find a cool place to hide. One day, a little earthworm was enjoying the shade under a big tree. A small gecko crawled over and said hello, "Hello there, Mr. Earthworm!"

"Hello, little gecko," said the earthworm. "Where have you been?" The gecko replied, "I was catching flies near the wall when suddenly an old cat pounced at me, trying to grab me..."

The earthworm gasped, "Oh my goodness, that sounds so dangerous! Cat claws are very sharp. If he had caught you, it would have been terrible!" But the gecko just smiled carelessly and said, "It's okay, I have a way to handle him! Look, my tail is my secret weapon."

The earthworm looked behind the gecko and exclaimed in surprise, "Oh dear, where is your tail? It's gone! Where did it go?" The gecko puffed out his chest proudly and said, "If I lose my tail, I can save my life!" Now the earthworm was even more puzzled. "Why would you throw away your tail? That must look so silly without it!"

The gecko explained with great focus, "When I saw the old cat pouncing at me, I quickly dropped my tail and hid in the haystack. My tail was still wiggling on the ground, and the cat was so surprised he just stared at it. While he was distracted, I sneaked away!"

The earthworm thought for a moment and said worriedly, "Oh, I see! But what will you do without a tail?" The gecko smiled mysteriously and said, "Don't worry, in just a few days, I'll grow a brand new tail!"

"Then you're just like us earthworms!" the earthworm quickly said. "We earthworms can grow new parts even if our bodies get broken in two! Did you know? Once, two little chicks pulled me into two pieces before they could eat me. Then a little boy shouted, 'Chicks, earthworms help plow the fields! You can't hurt him!' And he chased the chicks away. Before long, my front half grew a tail, and my back half grew a head... Hey, I became two earthworms!"

The gecko listened happily and said, "That's wonderful, Mr. Earthworm! Your body can split into two earthworms, and my tail can grow into a brand new tail. Since we have such special abilities, we should protect ourselves and do good things for nature." The earthworm agreed, "Yes! You can catch many harmful insects. I can loosen the soil and make fertilizer, helping the crops grow better. Isn't that wonderful?"

The gecko laughed and said, "Haha, I think the same thing! Well, goodbye, Mr. Earthworm. I'm going to continue catching bugs!"

"Goodbye, little gecko!" said the earthworm happily.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 小青虫变蝴蝶
fields.content:
冬爷爷刚慢悠悠地离开，春姑娘就急忙忙地赶来了。
春姑娘头上戴着用红花、白花、黄花编成的帽子，身上穿着绿色的衣裳，打扮得可漂亮了！她张着像薄纱一样的大翅膀飞呀飞，飞到了田野里的一棵大树旁边。春姑娘看见树枝上挂着一个褐色的两头尖尖的小包包，风儿轻轻一吹，小包包就随着风儿摇摇摆摆。这是什么呢？春姑娘停下来看了看。哦！原来这个小包包是小青虫变的。
小青虫已经睡了一个冬天了。去年秋天，小青虫变成了这个小包包后就睡着了，一直睡到现在还没醒呢。
春姑娘看着这个褐色的小尖包包，心里想：嗯，小青虫快要醒了。我得趁这个时候把这个世界变个样儿，那样小青虫醒来一定会大吃一惊，完全不认识这个世界了！春姑娘一想到这儿就觉得特别有趣，于是她快活地忙碌了起来。
春姑娘轻抚着小草说：“小草呀小草！我要把世界变得更美丽，让小青虫醒来的时候觉得很吃惊。小草，你帮帮忙吧！”
小草听了春姑娘的话，立刻从土里伸出头来。嗬，大地马上变成了一片绿色，好像铺上了嫩绿光滑的丝绒地毯，漂亮极啦！可是，小青虫还睡着呢，一点也不知道。
接着春姑娘又飞到结着薄冰的小河边儿，温柔地对小河说：“小河呀小河！我要把世界变得更美丽，让小青虫醒来一看觉得很惊喜。小河，你能帮帮忙吗？”
小河微微笑了笑，河里的冰就化了，河水“哗哗”地唱着歌，欢快地跑着。可是，小青虫还睡着呢，一点儿都不知道。
春姑娘又对冻僵了的树和藏起来的花儿说：“树啊！花儿啊！我要把世界变得更美丽，让小青虫醒来一看觉得非常惊喜。你们帮帮忙，行吗？”
树和花儿点了点头：“行啊，行啊！”看那儿！树上冒出了绿色的小嫩叶子，各种各样的小花儿星星点点地开放了，就像彩色的星星布满了大地，真是美极了！
春姑娘飞到小青虫那儿，对着小包包轻柔地说：“小青虫，你该醒醒了，快来看看外面的世界，一定吓你一跳呢！”可是，春姑娘叫了半天，小青虫也没说话。她再仔细一看，咦？小尖包包早就空了，小尖包包上有一个小缝缝，小青虫不见啦！
春姑娘觉得好奇怪啊，小青虫去哪了？她东瞧瞧，西看看……啊，有一只五彩的大花蝴蝶正在花丛里欢快地飞来飞去，高兴地跳舞呢！
这只蝴蝶真漂亮啊，她的翅膀上好像镶着各种颜色的小珍珠，在金色阳光的照耀下，小珠子闪闪发光。美丽的蝴蝶一会儿飞到东，一会儿飞到西，她欣喜地听着小河欢唱。她飞过柔软碧绿的小草，闻闻甜蜜的花香，绕过满是嫩芽的树木……蝴蝶兴奋极了：“世界怎么变样了呢？”
小河、小草、花儿和树也都看见了这只蝴蝶，惊叹地说：“哟！多漂亮的一位小姑娘啊！她是谁呀？”
春姑娘笑了：“你们不认识她吗？她就是挂在树上的那个小尖包包里的小青虫变的，她的名字叫‘蝴蝶’啊！”
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Green Caterpillar Becomes a Butterfly

Grandpa Winter had just slowly drifted away when Miss Spring hurried right along behind him.

Miss Spring wore a hat woven from red, white, and yellow flowers, and a beautiful green dress. How lovely she looked! She spread her sheer, gossamer wings and fluttered all the way to a big tree in the fields. There, hanging from a branch, was a small brown pouch with pointed ends on both sides. The wind blew gently, and the little pouch swayed back and forth. What could it be? Miss Spring paused to take a closer look. Oh! That little pouch was a little green caterpillar.

The little green caterpillar had been sleeping through the whole winter. When autumn came last year, it turned itself into that little pouch and fell asleep, and it had been sleeping until right now.

Miss Spring looked at the little brown pointed pouch and thought, "Hmm, the little green caterpillar is about to wake up. I'll change the world while I can, so when it wakes up, it will be so surprised it won't even recognize anything!" The thought made her very happy, and she set to work with a bright heart.

Miss Spring gently touched the grass and said, "Little grass, oh little grass! I want to make the world more beautiful so the little green caterpillar will be very surprised when it wakes up. Will you help me?"

The little grass heard Miss Spring's words and immediately popped its head out of the soil. Hey! The whole earth turned green at once, as if someone had laid down a soft, smooth carpet of tender green velvet. It was so pretty! But the little green caterpillar was still fast asleep and had no idea at all.

Then Miss Spring fluttered to the riverbank, where a thin layer of ice still covered the water. She spoke softly to the river, "Little river, dear little river! I want to make the world more beautiful so the little green caterpillar will be filled with wonder when it wakes up. Can you help me?"

The river smiled gently, and the ice melted away. The river water went "rush, rush," singing its happy song as it ran along. But the little green caterpillar was still asleep, not knowing a single thing.

Miss Spring then spoke to the frozen trees and the hidden flowers: "Trees, oh trees! Flowers, dear flowers! I want to make the world more beautiful so the little green caterpillar will be truly amazed when it wakes up. Will you help, please?"

The trees and flowers nodded and said, "Yes, yes, of course!" Look there! Green, tender leaves were sprouting from every branch, and little flowers of every color were blooming one by one, like colorful stars scattered across the earth. It was absolutely beautiful!

Miss Spring fluttered over to the little green caterpillar and softly whispered to the pouch, "Little green caterpillar, it's time to wake up! Come see the world outside — you will be so surprised!" But Miss Spring called and called, and the little green caterpillar did not answer. She looked more carefully and... oh! The little pointed pouch was empty. There was a tiny little slit in it, and the little green caterpillar was gone!

Miss Spring felt quite puzzled. Where had the little green caterpillar gone? She looked left and she looked right... Ah! A beautiful rainbow butterfly was dancing joyfully among the flowers!

That butterfly was truly gorgeous. Its wings seemed to be adorned with tiny pearls of every color, sparkling and shining under the golden sunlight. The beautiful butterfly fluttered here and there, happily listening to the river's cheerful singing. It flew over the soft green grass, smelled the sweet fragrance of the flowers, and skimmed past the trees full of tender buds... The butterfly was thrilled. "How has the whole world changed!"

The river, the grass, the flowers, and the trees all saw the butterfly too, and they marveled, "Oh! What a lovely little lady! Who could she be?"

Miss Spring laughed and said, "Don't you recognize her? That little green caterpillar who was hanging in the pointed pouch on the tree — she has become a butterfly!"
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 博物馆的幻想
fields.content:
我特别喜欢去博物馆，因为那里像一个神奇的时光穿越机器，让我感觉进入了漫长的历史长河中，随着那些无声无息的历史珍宝和建筑，回到那远久的古老过去。每次去博物馆都像进行一次长途的时光旅行，我的心和思绪会跟着飞向历史的每一个角落。
我去过的最棒的博物馆就要数纽约的大都会博物馆了。那里面有特别多的世界各国的珍宝和艺术品，还有很多代表历史和文化的古文物，很令人增长知识。其中我最喜欢的是各个国家古代的盔甲和刀剑，既精致又漂亮，而且威风凛凛。
每每在此刻，我就会浮想联翩，一边欣赏一边想象自己穿上这样的盔甲，佩带着宝剑，骑着骏马飞奔在古战场上，带领着千军万马作战。就像最勇敢的少女战士，机智、灵活而又充满斗志。周围是辽阔的无边无际的旷野，河水弯曲得像丝带一般和远处无数的山峰交错在一起。一场恢宏的战役之后总会是一片阴暗凄凉的景象，悲啸的寒风，日色昏黄，蓬蒿也断落，野草萎枯，寒气凛冽有如降霜的冬晨。而我，却依然傲宇马上，英姿飒爽。
在博物馆里看着珍贵的展品，同时畅游在自己的幻想世界里，也许是我最爱博物馆的原因吧，因为有时候想象的世界远比真实的世界更精彩。
fields.content_en:
# The Museum's Fantasy

I really love going to the museum, because it's like a magical time machine that carries me along the long river of history, returning to those distant ancient times together with the silent treasures and buildings. Every visit to the museum feels like a long journey through time, and my heart and thoughts fly to every corner of history.

The very best museum I have ever visited is the Metropolitan Museum in New York. It has wonderful treasures and artworks from all over the world, as well as many ancient artifacts that represent history and culture, teaching me so much. Among them, my favorite are the ancient armors and swords from different countries—so delicate and beautiful, yet full of pride and courage.

Every time, my imagination soars. While admiring them, I imagine myself wearing such armor, carrying a sword, riding a proud horse across an ancient battlefield, leading thousands of soldiers into battle. Just like the bravest young warrior girl—clever, quick, and full of fighting spirit. Around me lies an endless wide wilderness, with rivers winding like ribbons, meeting countless distant mountains. After a great battle, darkness and sorrow fill the land. A howling cold wind blows, the sky turns dim and yellow, plants wither and wild grass dries up, and the biting chill is like a frosty winter morning. And yet, I still sit tall upon my horse, brave and proud.

Looking at those precious exhibits in the museum while wandering in my fantasy world—perhaps this is why I love the museum so much. Because sometimes, the world of imagination is far more wonderful than the real world.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 数星星的孩子
fields.title_en: The Little One Who Counts the Stars
fields.content:
晚上，满天的星星像无数珍珠撒在夜空中。一个孩子坐在院子里，靠着奶奶，仰着头，数着天空的星星。一颗、两颗……一直数到几百颗。
奶奶笑着说：“傻孩子，又在数星星了。那么多星星，一闪一闪地乱动，眼都看花了，能数得清吗？”
孩子说：“奶奶，能看得见，就能数得清。星星是在动，可不是乱动。您看，这颗星和那颗星总是离得那么远。”
爷爷走过来说：“孩子，你看得很仔细。天上的星星是在动，可它们之间的距离是不变的。我们的祖先把它们分成一组一组，还给起了名字。”爷爷停了停，指着北边的天空说：“你看，那七颗星，连起来像一把勺子，叫北斗星。离它们不远有颗最亮的星，叫北极星。北斗星总是绕着北极星在转。”
爷爷说的话是真的吗？这个孩子一夜没睡好，几次起来看星星。他看清楚了，北斗星果然绕着北极星慢慢地转动。
这个数星星的孩子叫张衡，是汉朝人。他长大以后，刻苦钻研，发明了浑天仪。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Child Who Counted Stars

At night, the sky was full of stars, like countless pearls scattered across the darkness. A child sat in the courtyard, leaning against his grandmother, looking up and counting the stars. One, two... all the way to hundreds.

Grandma smiled and said, "Silly child, counting stars again? There are so many, twinkling and moving about. Your eyes will get tired. Can you really count them all?"

The child replied, "Grandma, if I can see them, I can count them. The stars do move, but not in a messy way. Look, this star and that star are always far apart."

Grandpa walked over and said, "Child, you observe very carefully. The stars in the sky do move, but the distance between them stays the same. Our ancestors grouped them together and gave them names." Grandpa paused, then pointed to the northern sky. "Look at those seven stars connected like a ladle. We call it the Big Dipper. Not far from it is the brightest star, called Polaris. The Big Dipper always circles around Polaris."

Were Grandpa's words true? The child couldn't sleep well that night, getting up several times to look at the stars. He saw clearly that the Big Dipper did indeed slowly revolve around Polaris.

This child who counted the stars was named Zhang Heng. He lived during the Han Dynasty. When he grew up, he studied hard and invented the armillary sphere.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 海豚女孩
fields.content:
在一个寒冷的冬天，一个北京的小女孩跟着妈妈来到了依然是盛夏的悉尼看望姥爷。在冬天里过夏天，没有什么比这个更让小女孩快乐了。小爱，是这个小女孩的名字。这里有太多让小爱喜欢的理由了：蓝天白云，明媚的阳光，茂密的树林，绿草茵茵。也许最让小爱心动的是那无边的大海和总也走不完的海岸线。去海边，是小爱每天都要干的事。直到有一天，一个神秘的朋友在这里和她相遇了。
这是一个明媚的早晨，小爱依然提着她心爱的沙滩小桶来到海边，心里想着：今天会捡到什么有趣的东西呢？没想到她居然遇到了一只海豚！其实这只海豚早就认识小爱了，因为她是小海豚唯一见过拥有像黑夜一样的头发和眼睛的小女孩。小海豚特别喜欢看小爱，它总是离得远远的，偶尔跳出海面，望一眼沙滩上的小爱。
小爱来到一块巨大的礁石旁，她想看看这些礁石旁会有什么新发现。没想到，她看见了一只抬起头正微笑看着她的可爱海豚！小爱被眼前的画面惊呆了，真的是一只海豚在看着她呢！小爱激动得说不出话来，她慢慢趴在礁石边，使劲伸出手臂，轻轻地抚摸到了小海豚的头。没想到，海豚特别乖，依然微笑着让小爱摸着它的头，还张开了嘴发出愉快的声音。这一刻，小爱相信了，眼前的一切都是真的，不是在做神奇的梦！
“我叫小爱，你有名字吗？”
“好吧，我就叫你小海豚吧，说不定你能听懂我说的话呢！”
“你真漂亮，能在海里自由自在地游泳很开心吧？我也想跟你一起玩儿，跟你一块儿游泳……”小爱摸着小海豚自言自语着，可是小海豚就像能听明白小爱的话一样，不停地点着头，发出悦耳温柔的声音，摆动着尾巴欢快地一头扎进大海，又很快跃出海面。
“你是想让我跟你一起玩吗？真的吗？哈哈，那我也跳进去跟你一起游泳吧！我妈妈教过我游泳，我也是很厉害的呢！”小爱似乎感受到了小海豚来自大海的召唤，情不自禁脱掉鞋子，毫不犹豫地跳入了大海。很快，小爱就被什么托出了海面，没错，就是那只小海豚！小爱这回真的紧紧抱住了她的新朋友，真的畅游大海了！
这不是梦，却像梦一样神奇！小爱骑在小海豚的背上，快乐得像一条小美人鱼，更像一个美丽的海豚女孩。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Dolphin Girl

On a cold winter day, a little girl from Beijing traveled with her mom to Sydney, where summer still reigned, to visit her grandpa. There was nothing that made the little girl happier than experiencing summer in the middle of winter. Her name was Xiao Ai. There were so many reasons here to love: blue skies and white clouds, bright sunshine, dense forests, and lush green grass. But perhaps what captured her heart the most was the endless ocean and the coastline that seemed to stretch on forever. Going to the beach became something Xiao Ai did every single day. And then one day, a mysterious friend met her there.

It was a bright morning, and Xiao Ai carried her beloved little beach bucket to the seaside, wondering what interesting things she might find today. To her surprise, she actually met a dolphin! In fact, this dolphin had known Xiao Ai for a while already, because Xiao Ai was the only little girl the dolphin had ever seen with hair and eyes as dark as the night. The little dolphin loved watching Xiao Ai from afar, occasionally leaping out of the water just to catch a glimpse of her on the beach.

Xiao Ai came to a huge reef and wanted to see if there were any new discoveries around it. To her amazement, she saw a cute little dolphin raising its head and smiling at her! Xiao Ai was speechless—this was really a dolphin looking at her! She slowly leaned by the reef and gently reached out her arm to pet the little dolphin's head. The dolphin was so sweet, still smiling as Xiao Ai stroked its head, and even opened its mouth making happy sounds. In that moment, Xiao Ai knew everything was real, not some magical dream!

"My name is Xiao Ai, do you have a name?"
"Well, I'll call you Little Dolphin. Maybe you can understand what I'm saying!"
"You're so beautiful. It must feel wonderful to swim freely in the sea, right? I want to play with you and swim with you…" Xiao Ai whispered to herself while petting the dolphin, and Little Dolphin seemed to understand every word. It nodded continuously, made sweet gentle sounds, and joyfully dove into the sea with a flick of its tail, then quickly leaped back out of the water.

"Do you want me to play with you? Really? Haha, then I'll jump in and swim with you! My mom taught me how to swim—I'm pretty good at it!" Feeling the call of the sea from her new friend, Xiao Ai couldn't help herself. She took off her shoes and jumped into the ocean without hesitation. Soon, something lifted her above the surface. It was Little Dolphin! Xiao Ai held onto her new friend tightly and truly swam in the vast sea!

This wasn't a dream, but it felt as magical as one! Riding on the back of the little dolphin, Xiao Ai was as happy as a little mermaid, even more like a beautiful dolphin girl.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 小熊过桥
fields.content:
有一只特别乖的小熊，他每天和妈妈生活在一起，无忧无虑的。熊妈妈把小熊照顾得无微不至，随着小熊一天天长大，熊妈妈觉得小熊该自己学着做些事了。于是有一天，熊妈妈对小熊说：“宝贝，你想姥姥吗？”小熊马上回答：“特别想！我好些日子没见到姥姥了，我想去看望姥姥！”妈妈接着说：“好啊，那你去的时候，把咱们那束鲜花送给姥姥，把点心也拿去给姥姥尝尝吧！”
小熊疑惑地看着妈妈：“这一次，是我自己一个人去吗？”妈妈微笑着说：“是啊，你是一个大孩子了，可以帮妈妈分担很多事了，今天妈妈很忙，看望姥姥这件事就由你代替妈妈完成吧！可以吗，我的宝贝？”
“当然可以啦！”小熊说着抱起点心盒子，抱起鲜花，“妈妈，那我走啦！”
小熊离开家，走着走着来到一条小河边上。河上有一座桥，这桥是用竹子搭的。以前都是小熊跟着妈妈一起过桥，而且有时妈妈还拉着小熊的手。可是这回，小熊刚走了没两步，就站在上面不敢动了，因为这桥走起来左一摇右一晃的，感觉很危险。而且桥下的河水流得很急，哗哗作响！
小熊有点紧张，也有点害怕了，就在这时，天上飞过来一只乌鸦。小熊满眼期待地望着乌鸦，以为他能给自己一些帮助。没想到这乌鸦不但不帮助小熊，反倒吓唬他。乌鸦高声喊道：“呱——呱——呱——坏啦，坏啦！快来看啊，小熊要掉下河啦，小熊要掉下河啦！”乌鸦刺耳的叫声一直在小熊耳边回响着。
小熊本来就害怕，被乌鸦这么一吓唬，就更不敢抬脚了，觉得紧张极了。他低头一看河水，连河水也在笑话他：“哗哗哗哗，小熊小熊，你怎么这么不勇敢呢？小竹桥都不敢过！这么胆小，太没出息啦 ！太没出息啦！”
“乌鸦吓唬我，河水笑话我，这、这可怎么办呢？我真的不敢往前走啊！”小熊着急得哭了，而且觉得竹桥似乎越来越摇晃了，好像就快把自己晃下桥了！小熊不由自主地大声叫着：“妈妈，妈妈，快来呀！”可是，妈妈离这儿那么远，怎么听得见呀？
熊妈妈听不见，可是水里的小鱼儿却听见了，他们“扑噜、扑噜”从水里钻出头来，其中有一条善良的大鲤鱼，他大声地对小熊说：“小熊，小熊，你别害怕！”小熊听见大鲤鱼的话，心里充满感激。大鲤鱼接着说：“这座竹桥一点都不危险，以前你和你的妈妈一起过都没事！你现在把眼睛往前瞧，别往水下看。你挺起胸，直起腰，迈开步，一二，一二，就过去啦！”
在小熊最害怕的时刻，大鲤鱼的这番话似乎特别有作用，小熊觉得内心温暖起来了。他听大鲤鱼的话，抬起头，眼睛向前看，挺起胸，直起腰，迈开大步，一二，一二……嘿，真过去啦！
小熊到了岸边回头一看，自己这么快就过来了，这座竹桥一点儿都不危险嘛！眼泪还没干的小熊就高兴地笑了。他回头冲着大鲤鱼直点头：“大鲤鱼，谢谢你，我做到了！再见吧！”
小鱼儿们一看小熊平平安安地过去了，都非常高兴，“咕咚、咕咚”全都钻到水里去了。
fields.content_en:
Title: Little Bear Crosses the Bridge

There was a very well-behaved little bear who lived with his mother every day, carefree and happy. Mother Bear took wonderful care of him, but as Little Bear grew bigger each day, she felt he should start learning to do things on his own. So one day, Mother Bear said to him, "Dear, do you miss Grandma Bear?" Little Bear immediately answered, "I miss her so much! I haven't seen Grandma in quite a while, and I want to visit her!" Mother Bear went on, "That's lovely. When you go, take our bouquet of flowers to Grandma, and bring some pastries for her to taste as well!"

Little Bear looked at Mother Bear in surprise. "Am I going all by myself this time?" Mother Bear smiled gently. "Yes, you are such a big boy now. You can help Mommy with many things. Today Mommy is very busy, so why don't you go to visit Grandma on my behalf? Could you do that for me, my dear?"

"Of course I can!" Little Bear said, picking up the pastry box and the bouquet of flowers. "Goodbye, Mommy! I'm off now!"

Little Bear left home and soon came to the edge of a small river. There was a bridge across it, made of bamboo. In the past, Little Bear always crossed the bridge with his mother, and sometimes she even held his hand. But this time, he had only taken two steps when he stopped, too frightened to move further. The bridge swayed left and right, feeling very unsafe. And the river water below was rushing swiftly, roaring noisily!

Little Bear was already a bit nervous and quite scared. Just then, a crow flew overhead. Little Bear looked at the crow with hopeful eyes, hoping it could offer him some help. But instead of helping, the crow only frightened him more. The crow called out loudly, "Caw—caw—caw! Oh no, oh no! Come and see, the little bear is going to fall into the river! The little bear is going to fall into the river!" The crow's harsh cries kept echoing in Little Bear's ears.

Little Bear was already afraid, and now the crow's scaring made him even more frozen with fear. He looked down at the river, and even the water seemed to be mocking him: "Splash, splash, splash, little bear, little bear, why aren't you brave? You're too scared to cross a little bamboo bridge! So timid, so weak! So weak!"

"The crow is scaring me, and the river is making fun of me… What should I do? I really don't dare to move forward!" Little Bear cried out in worry. He felt the bamboo bridge growing more and more wobbly, as if it were about to shake him right off! Little Bear couldn't help but call out loudly, "Mommy! Mommy, come quickly!" But Mother Bear was so far away—how could she possibly hear him?

Mother Bear couldn't hear, but the little fish in the water could. They popped their heads up from the water with glug-glug sounds. One kind big carp spoke out to Little Bear, "Little bear, little bear, don't be afraid!" Hearing these words from the big carp filled Little Bear with gratitude. The carp continued, "This bamboo bridge is not dangerous at all. You and your mother crossed it safely before! Now, look ahead, don't look down at the water. Stand up tall, straighten your back, take your steps—one, two, one, two—and you'll make it across!"

At the moment Little Bear was most afraid, the big carp's words seemed to work like magic. Little Bear felt warmth spreading through his heart. He followed the carp's advice: he lifted his head, looked forward, stood up tall, straightened his back, and marched forward with big steps—one, two, one, two… Hey, he actually made it across!

When Little Bear reached the other side and looked back, he couldn't believe how quickly he had crossed. This bamboo bridge wasn't dangerous at all! Even with still-wet tears, Little Bear broke into a happy smile. He turned and nodded gratefully to the big carp, "Big carp, thank you! I did it! Goodbye!"

Seeing Little Bear had crossed safely, all the little fish were overjoyed and happily splashed back underwater with glug-glug sounds.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 捉迷藏
fields.content:
月亮用长长的手帕，
把太阳的眼睛蒙起来了。
趁着他还在数着：
一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八……
颜色们
赶快找一个自己喜爱的地方，
静悄悄地，躲在里面。
绿色太多了，挤不下。
有的躲在树叶里；
有的躲在小草里。
黄色躲在菊花里；
白色躲在云朵里；
蓝色躲在天空里；
红色躲在玫瑰里。
大家都躲好了，
月亮就把手帕解开，
太阳睁开眼睛，
一下子就把所有颜色都找出来啦！
fields.content_en:
**Hide and Seek**

The moon used her long handkerchief to cover the sun's eyes.
While he was still counting:
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight…
The colors
Rushed to find their favorite places to hide,
Silently tucking themselves away.
There were so many greens, there wasn't enough room!
Some hid inside the leaves;
Some hid in the tiny grass blades.
Yellow hid inside chrysanthemums;
White hid inside clouds;
Blue hid inside the sky;
Red hid inside roses.
When everyone was safely hidden,
The moon untied her handkerchief,
The sun opened his eyes,
And in a flash, found every color!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 星星树
fields.content:
亮亮的叶子
闪闪的花儿
墨蓝的夜空下
长着一棵星星树
这是爷爷的星星树
爸爸在树下
数着星星，看着月亮
慢慢长大
这是爸爸的星星树
宝宝在树下
说着儿歌，听着故事
快乐长大
这是宝宝的星星树
蟋蟀在打架
蝈蝈在唱歌
毛毛虫在睡觉
爸爸陪着宝宝，数星星
这是全家人的星星树
每个家人
就像每颗星星
闪着故事
亮着温暖
透着爱
fields.content_en:
Title: The Star Tree

Leaves that shine
Flowers that sparkle
Beneath the deep blue night sky
Grows a Star Tree
This is Grandpa's Star Tree
Baba stood under that tree
Counting stars, watching the moon
Growing up slowly
This is Baba's Star Tree
Baby stands under that tree
Singing nursery rhymes, listening to stories
Growing up with joy
This is Baby's Star Tree
Crickets are fighting
Katydids are singing
Caterpillars are sleeping
Baba keeps Baby company, counting stars
This is our whole family's Star Tree
Every family member
Is like every star
Telling stories
Shining warm
Full of love
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 摇篮曲
fields.content:
藤摇篮，竹摇篮，
好像一只小小船。
乖宝贝，闭上眼，
我们坐船出去玩。
漂过洋，漂过海，
不用摇橹不用帆。
蓝的夜，亮的星，
片片白云似轻纱。
柔的风，细的语，
甜蜜的呢喃耳边绕。
小绿岛，草幽幽，
繁花密叶荡清波。
乖宝宝，闭着眼，
妈妈的怀中微微笑。
fields.content_en:
Lullaby

A wicker cradle, a bamboo cradle,
Like a little tiny boat.
Sweet baby, close your eyes,
Let's sail away together.

Sailing over oceans, sailing over seas,
No need for oars, no need for sails.

Blue night, bright stars,
Soft white clouds like gentle gauze.
Gentle wind, quiet whispers,
Sweet murmurings环绕 around your ears.

Little green island, soft green grass,
Flowers and leaves swaying in the clear waves.

Sweet baby, eyes closed,
Smiling softly in mom's warm arms.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 外婆家的夏天
fields.subtitle: 是玉米糊糊和炸咸鱼的味道，那永远定格在记忆深处的味道。
fields.subtitle_en: It was the scent of corn porridge and fried salted fish, a fragrance forever preserved in the depths of memory.
fields.content:
所有夏天应该有的样子，全都是外婆家夏天的样子。
外婆一手提着藤条编成的篮子，一手牵着比篮子还要圆的我，去采桑葚啦！粗糙的柏油路两边，长满了一人高的波斯菊。当然不是像我那么高，有外婆那么高呢！
夏天的风是懒的，花儿也是懒的。风温吞吞地吹过来，温吞吞地吹过去，也不见花儿动弹一下。
外婆说波斯菊都有八片花瓣。我问：“会不会有七片的？”外婆说：“找到七片的会有好运气呢！”
小手接过大手递来的一朵七瓣波斯菊，大大的笑容在脸上绽开，像花儿一样。
那时候的快乐太简单，好运气的孩子满手满嘴都是紫色的桑葚汁，又怎么会留意到，其中两片花瓣之间的距离好像太大了一点呢？
外婆一手端着洗衣盆，一手牵着能装进洗衣盆的我，去洗衣服啦！河岸边满是高大翠绿的树，我叫不上大树们的名字，但是鸟儿和蝉儿应当知道，因为那是它们的树妈妈。
鸟啼蝉鸣，伴着潺潺的流水声，我还嫌不够闹，光着屁股“扑通”跳进河里。溅起的水花打湿了外婆的衣襟，外婆一点儿也不恼，倒柔声地说了句：“真凉快！”
火热的阳光透过树叶间的缝隙打在河面上，河水清亮见底，五颜六色的鹅卵石泛着可爱的光泽。小脚丫踩在上面掐腰站立，水深也才没腰而已。旁边的孩子肩上挂着天蓝色的游泳圈，上面的海豚可真好看。听到外婆呼唤的时候，我已经盯了许久吧。
外婆可真有办法，她将刚洗完的裤子扎紧裤脚，再把裤腰投进河里，出不去的空气一时被堵进裤腿儿，鼓胀起来。我抱着鼓鼓的裤腿儿，小脚丫在身后扑腾，浮起来啦！
外婆一手拎着一根棍子，一手牵着还没有棍子高的我，去采蘑菇啦！
我问外婆：“为什么要带棍子啊？”
外婆答：“敲敲打打，别被长虫咬了手！”
我说：“外婆，太热啦！我要脱衣服。”
外婆答：“山上毒草虫子多，可不要脱外套！”
我说：“外婆，我好累，想回家。”
外婆说：“宝宝乖，再采十朵，就带你回家。”
后来外婆采了十朵、二十朵、三十朵……我在一旁安安静静的，看着蹦蹦跳跳地穿梭在树枝间的小松鼠，看得入了神。
“宝宝，回家啦！”外婆一手提着装满蘑菇的篮子，一手牵着我，穿过下山的小径，过清澈的小河，穿过波斯菊环绕的乡间柏油路。
夏日的黄昏，空气闷热依然。
“外婆，我渴。”
“宝宝去买冰棍吃。”
小手接过大手递过来的一枚凉凉的硬币，大大的笑容在脸上绽开，像花儿一样。汗珠儿顺着圆圆的脸蛋淌了下来，我用大拇指和食指捏着冰棍，一边吸溜着，一边顺着路边的花坛向外婆家的方向慢悠悠地走，看着花花草草，蜜蜂蝴蝶。
夕阳西斜，身子小小，影子长长，恰好饥肠辘辘。
粉色点点的水鞋停在了外婆家门口，因为一股香味而定住细嗅
fields.content_en:
Title: Summer at Grandma's House

Every summer should look exactly like summers at Grandma's house.
Grandma carried a woven rattan basket in one hand and held my hand with the other—I was rounder than the basket!—as we went to pick mulberries. On both sides of the rough asphalt road grew Persian marigolds as tall as a person. Of course, not as tall as me, but as tall as Grandma!

The summer wind was lazy, and so were the flowers. The breeze blew gently this way and gently that, and the flowers didn't stir at all.

Grandma said Persian marigolds had eight petals. I asked, "Could there be one with seven?" Grandma said, "If you find one with seven petals, you'll have good luck!"

I received a seven-petaled flower from her large hand with my small one, and a big smile blossomed on my face, just like a flower.

Back then, happiness was so simple. A lucky child with hands and mouth stained purple from mulberry juice—who would notice that the distance between two petals seemed just a little too wide?

Grandma carried a washbasin in one hand and held me, small enough to fit inside the basin, in the other, as we went to do laundry. The riverbank was lined with tall, lush green trees. I couldn't name the trees, but the birds and cicadas must have known, for they were their tree mothers.

Birdsong and cicada chirping mixed with the gentle sound of flowing water, yet I thought it wasn't noisy enough and splashed into the river naked, making a big splash. The water soaked Grandma's clothes, but she wasn't angry at all. Instead, she softly said, "So refreshing!"

Hot sunlight filtered through the leaves and sparkled on the river surface. The water was clear as glass, and colorful pebbles glowed cutely. I stood with my hands on my hips, my little feet stepping on them, and the water barely reached my waist. Nearby, a child wore a sky-blue swim ring with a lovely dolphin on it. By the time Grandma called me, I must have been staring at it for a long time.

Grandma was so clever. She tied the legs of the freshly washed pants tightly, then tossed the waist into the river. The trapped air puffed up the legs like a balloon. I hugged the swollen pant legs, kicking my little feet behind me, and—wow, I floated!

Grandma carried a stick in one hand and held my hand with the other—I was still shorter than the stick—as we went to pick mushrooms.

I asked Grandma, "Why do we need a stick?"
Grandma replied, "To poke around. That way you won't get bitten by snakes!"
I said, "Grandma, it's so hot! I want to take off my clothes."
Grandma answered, "There are poisonous plants and bugs on the mountain. Don't you dare take off your jacket!"
I said, "Grandma, I'm so tired. I want to go home."
Grandma said, "Be good, baby. Pick ten more mushrooms, and then I'll take you home."

Later, Grandma picked ten mushrooms, twenty mushrooms, thirty mushrooms… I sat quietly beside her, watching a little squirrel hop among the branches, completely enchanted.

"Baby, let's go home!" Grandma carried the basket full of mushrooms in one hand and held mine in the other as we walked down the mountain path, crossed the crystal-clear stream, and passed through the country road surrounded by Persian marigolds.

The summer evening air was still warm and heavy.
"Grandma, I'm thirsty."
"Let's go buy you a popsicle, baby."

My small hand received a cool coin from her large hand, and a big smile blossomed on my face, just like a flower. Sweat trickled down my round cheeks. Pinching the popsicle between my thumb and index finger, I sipped it slowly while strolling along the flowerbeds toward Grandma's house, watching the flowers, grass, bees, and butterflies.

The sun dipped low in the sky. My body was small, my shadow was long, and my tummy was wonderfully rumbling.

My pink polka-dot water shoes stopped at Grandma's door, frozen by a wonderful aroma wafting from within.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 美丽的家园
fields.subtitle: 选自海伦·凯勒《假如给我三天光明》
fields.subtitle_en: Adapted from Helen Keller's Three Days to See
fields.content:
我们的家在美国南方的一所不大的房子里，房子虽小，却美丽而温馨。这所房子被包围在一片蔷薇和金银花架中，成了蜂鸟和蜜蜂的乐园。旁边的老宅也被一片树木和藤蔓包围着，我们喜欢称它为“绿色家园”。虽然我既看不见也听不见，我依然常常独自摸索着走到庭院里，尽情享受紫罗兰和百合花诱人的芬芳。当心情不好时，这里也成了我的避难所。花园里还有一种罕见的蝴蝶荷，它的花瓣像蝴蝶的翅膀，很容易掉落。还有最美丽的蔷薇，爬满了花园的每一个角落，散发着清香。
那时，我有两个形影不离的好朋友：玛莎·华盛顿和老猎犬贝尔。玛莎是厨师的孩子，一个黑人小女孩。她能看懂我的手势，而且对我绝对服从。我和玛莎在厨房里度过很多美好时光。我们一起揉面团、做冰激凌、喂火鸡。火鸡不怕人，会在我们手上抢东西吃。有一次我们还拿走了厨房刚刚烤好的蛋糕，躲在木材堆里好好享受了一番，但不久就闹肚子了，这可能就是偷东西吃的下场。
我们还到很深的花丛里去找珍珠鸡刚下的蛋。我用双手合成圆形，放在地上，示意玛莎去草丛里找蛋，玛莎一看就明白了。谷仓、马棚、牛奶场，都是我和玛莎的乐园，我们成了其中无忧无虑的天使。
准备圣诞节的食物也是一件很快乐的事情。家人会让我们磨香料、挑选葡萄干、舔舔勺子上的食物残渣，不过我对装着礼物的袜子倒不是很感兴趣。
我和玛莎还喜欢恶作剧。有一次我们坐在阳台的台阶上，拿着剪刀剪纸娃娃，后来百无聊赖，就开始剪金银花叶子。突然，玛莎那一头卷曲的螺丝锥一样的头发引起了我的注意，刚开始她不让我剪，后来慢慢屈服了。当然，我的头发也没能幸免，差点被剪了个精光，幸亏母亲跑来解救。
我的老猎犬贝尔总是懒洋洋地躺在暖炉旁睡懒觉，一点儿也不听我的指挥。偶尔它会跳起来狂奔，像是看见了猎物一样，我也不明白它为什么会这样。大多数时候我不会理睬它，而是去找玛莎玩。童年的生活就是这样，寂静而无忧无虑，我在黑暗中感受着这个世界，一样的清晰和生动。
曾经有一次我爬树受伤了，这使我很长时间都不敢爬树，恐惧还残留在我的心中。直到有一天，我再也抵制不了含羞树诱人的芳香。春天的一个晴朗的早晨，我独自一人在凉亭里看书，突然，一阵淡淡的香气吸引了我。我循着香气来到花园的尽头，含羞树开满了花朵，树枝被压得垂到了青草上。只要轻轻碰一下树枝，花儿就如雨点般纷纷落下。我穿过花雨，来到含羞树前，犹豫了一下，便两手抓住树干开始往上爬。树干太粗，几乎抱不住，而且树枝和树皮已经剥落了，我的手也受伤了。尽管爬得很费劲，但我觉得自己在做一件精彩而非同寻常的事，因此就鼓足劲往上爬，直到爬上了一个舒适的座位。这个座位是很久以前用小椅子砌的，日久天长，已成了大树的一部分。我在上面待了很长时间，好像云端的仙女一样。从那以后，我常常爬到这棵“天堂之树”上玩耍，浮想联翩，遨游在美妙的梦境中。
对于我这样的孩子，童年真的已经很快乐了，有温暖的家人，有亲密的朋友，有智慧的老师，有美丽的家园，幸福也就该是这样子吧。
fields.content_en:
Title: Beautiful Home

Our home is in a small house in the southern part of America. Though small, it is beautiful and cozy. The house is surrounded by rose bushes and honeysuckle trellises, making it a paradise for hummingbirds and bees. The old house next door is wrapped in trees and vines, and we like to call it our "Green Home." Though I cannot see or hear, I often wander by myself into the garden, happily breathing in the sweet fragrance of violets and lilies. When I feel sad, this becomes my safe haven too. There is also a rare butterfly plant in the garden, its petals like butterfly wings that easily fall away. And the most beautiful roses grow everywhere in the garden, spreading their lovely scent.

Back then, I had two inseparable friends: Martha Washington and an old hunting dog named Bell. Martha was the cook's daughter, a little Black girl. She understood my hand signals perfectly and always obeyed me. I spent many wonderful hours with Martha in the kitchen. Together we kneaded dough, made ice cream, and fed the turkey. The turkey was not afraid of people at all and would take food right from our hands. Once we even took a cake that had just come out of the oven and hid in the woodpile to enjoy it. But soon afterward, our stomachs hurt—a lesson, perhaps, in stealing snacks.

We would also go deep into the flower beds to look for eggs that guinea fowl had just laid. I would form a circle with my hands and place them on the ground, showing Martha where to search for the eggs in the grass, and she understood right away. The barn, the stable, and the dairy were all our playgrounds, and we became carefree angels there.

Getting ready for Christmas food was such a joyful task. Our family let us grind spices, pick raisins, and lick the leftover food off spoons. I was not very interested in the stockings filled with gifts, though.

Martha and I also loved playing pranks. Once we sat on the steps of the balcony, cutting paper dolls with scissors. Bored after a while, we started cutting honeysuckle leaves instead. Suddenly, I noticed Martha's curly hair, which looked like little corkscrews. At first she did not let me cut it, but slowly she gave in. Of course, my own hair did not escape either—I almost lost it all until Mother came running to rescue me.

Our old hunting dog Bell always lay lazily by the stove, sleeping and paying no attention to me. Sometimes he would suddenly jump up and run wildly, as if he had seen prey. I never understood why he did that. Most of the time I ignored him and went to find Martha instead. That was my childhood—quiet and carefree. In my darkness, I felt the world just as clearly and vividly as anyone else.

Once I fell while climbing a tree, and for a long time I was too scared to climb again. That fear stayed inside me. Until one day, I could no longer resist the tempting fragrance of a mimosa tree. On a clear spring morning, I was reading alone in the gazebo when a soft, sweet scent drew me in. Following it, I came to the edge of the garden, where the mimosa tree was covered in blossoms, its branches heavy and drooping to the grass below. With just a gentle touch, the flowers fell like rain. Walking through that blossom shower, I came to the mimosa tree, hesitated for a moment, and then grabbed the trunk with both hands and began to climb. The trunk was too thick to wrap my arms around, and the bark was peeling, so my hands got hurt. But even though it was hard, I felt I was doing something wonderful and extraordinary, so I gathered my strength and climbed higher and higher until I reached a comfortable seat. It had been built long ago from small chairs and had become part of the tree over the years. I stayed there for a long time, like a fairy among the clouds. From then on, I often climbed this "Tree of Heaven" to play, lost in wonderful dreams.
