For a child like me, childhood was truly joyful—surrounded by loving family, close friends, wise teachers, and a beautiful home. Perhaps this is what happiness looks like.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 带翅膀的孩子
fields.subtitle: 红、紫、绿、蓝……这一定是大自然魔术师的神奇魔法。
fields.subtitle_en: Red, purple, green, blue... this must be the wonderful magic of nature's wizard.
fields.content:
我有一个秘密的世界，在这个世界里，我是不一样的我。我曾经悄悄地告诉妈妈，在那个世界里我长着一双雪白的翅膀，像天使一样美丽。
那天晚上，我去到了另一个世界，那双美丽的翅膀从背后伸出来，我的骨血融进了每一片羽翼。当大脑发出“飞”的指令，身体一用力，它们真的扑扇了起来，带起了风，带起了地上的尘土，带起了树梢的叶子。我摸到了天上的云，天上的鸟，还有天上的风筝。我感觉太阳离我更近了，因为眼前似乎出现了一道火红的光亮，透过薄薄的眼皮，投进了我的瞳孔。
它们带我飞到了长城，那座饱经风霜的古老建筑。它像一条尊贵威严的长龙，盘踞在崇山和绿树的环抱之中。我仿佛看到了冷兵器时代的古城边关，金戈铁马，长河落日。
它们带我飞到了马尔代夫，那个印度洋上的世外桃源。那里水清沙白，有蓝天白云，椰林树影，七彩缤纷的珊瑚，目不暇接的热带鱼群，充满着赤道活力的原始海洋，热情如火的风土人情……这是小猪麦兜的想象，此刻却如此真实地出现在我的眼前。
它们带我飞到了潘帕斯草原，那颗南美洲的明珠。草原的天空那么蓝，像是用深蓝色的水彩泼过一般。草原和蓝天相接，一碧万顷，辽阔到让人遗忘了自己的存在，遗忘了世间所有的琐碎与烦忧。这里没有高楼，没有汽车，没有喧嚣。草原上这里几头牛，那里几只羊，悠闲地吃着草，远处的牧民骑马掠过，英姿飒爽。
他们带我飞到了北极，世界上最冷的地方。雪原和坚冰一望无际，在破冰的水里，憨态可掬的北极熊笨拙地摆动着前爪，像是在跟我招手。晴朗的夜里，繁星眨着眼睛，我也做了一次数星星的孩子，最后还是数花了眼。一道白色的光线划过天际，那是银河吗？哪知“银河”越来越宽，在移动中渐渐地变了颜色原来这里的世界是那么大，那么美，那么神奇，那么可爱。
虽然这个世界里只有我自己知道，但是我一点也不寂寞，内心充满了快乐与满足。下回，我要带妈妈一起去我的秘密世界里，我要这双翅膀陪着我们，继续飞翔。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Child with Wings

I have a secret world, where I am a different version of myself. I once quietly told Mama that in that world, I grew a pair of snowy white wings, beautiful as an angel's.

That night, I went to another world. Those beautiful wings sprouted from my back, and my very bones and blood melted into every feather. When my mind sent the signal to "fly," my body tensed, and they truly began to flap, stirring the wind, lifting dust from the ground, and rustling the leaves at the tips of trees. I touched the clouds above, the birds in the sky, and kites flying high. I felt the sun draw closer, for a fire-red glow seemed to appear before my eyes, shining through my thin eyelids and into my pupils.

They flew me to the Great Wall, that ancient structure weathered by time. It looked like a noble and majestic dragon coiled among towering mountains and green forests. I could almost see the old border towns of the age of cold weapons—swords gleaming, horses galloping, the long river, and the setting sun.

They flew me to the Maldives, that paradise hidden in the Indian Ocean. Crystal-clear water, white sand, blue skies and fluffy clouds, coconut groves casting their shadows, colorful coral reefs, schools of tropical fish in every hue—too many to count—all teeming with the wild energy of the equator, and people warm and welcoming as fire... It was what the little pig McDull once imagined, yet here it appeared so real before my eyes.

They flew me to the Pampas grasslands, the shining jewel of South America. The sky above the grassland was so blue, as if splashed with deep blue watercolor. The grassland met the blue sky in one endless stretch of green, so vast that I forgot myself, forgot all the trivial worries of the world. There were no tall buildings, no cars, no noise. Here a few cows, there a few sheep, grazing peacefully. Far away, a herdsman rode past on horseback, brave and splendid.

They flew me to the North Pole, the coldest place on Earth. Snowfields and solid ice stretched as far as the eye could see. In the broken ice water, an adorable polar bear waved its front paws clumsily, as if waving hello to me. On a clear night, the stars twinkled like eyes. I too became a child who counted stars, and in the end, I could hardly see through my own dazzled gaze. A white streak flashed across the sky—was that the Milky Way? But the "river" grew wider and shifted colors as it moved. I realized the world here was so big, so beautiful, so magical, so lovely.

Even though only I know about this world, I am never lonely. My heart is full of joy and contentment. Next time, I will take Mama into my secret world too, and these wings of mine will carry us both, soaring ever onward.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 爸爸去哪了
fields.content:
在城市的边上不远处，有一片秘密的树林，背靠着连绵的青山。在青山的脚下，有不少座大大小小的房子。其中一座不太大的红砖房子就是坤宝的家。在这里住着坤宝一家和姥姥、姥爷。
坤宝一家以前住在城市里，可是他是个特别喜欢大自然的孩子，每天从幼儿园回来只能在楼下那个小得可怜的花园里玩玩，骑骑车，实在没意思透了。楼下的小区说是个花园，其实不过就是有几棵树，有一小片绿地，但是被来来往往的人踩得几乎长不出草，很多地方都秃秃的。对于坤宝这样渴望大自然的孩子来说，真是很郁闷呢。
终于，为了坤宝的美丽童年，妈妈决定全家搬到城边上的姥爷家去。于是，坤宝幸福的日子开始了。他每天都可以去树林里玩，在草地上来回奔跑，抓各种有意思的小虫子，用大网子追蝴蝶，过得不亦乐乎。可是很快，坤宝的烦恼又来了，爸爸总是不陪他玩。坤宝很想让爸爸陪他一起在草地上踢球，一起追蝴蝶，一起去不远的小河边捞虾，捞蝌蚪，扶着他爬上树……有太多事情坤宝希望爸爸一起帮助他，可是爸爸真的好懒啊！他不是在看电脑，就是在看手机，要么就是在睡觉，或者一回到家就说自己实在太累了，只想在沙发上躺着休息看电视。坤宝很生气，因为爸爸总说下次下次！
一个周末的中午，吃过午饭后，爸爸再次拒绝了坤宝一起出去骑车的请求，匆匆忙忙地出门加班了。坤宝很不开心地骑着自己的小自行车来到小树林，当他把车靠在一棵树边的时候，发现树下的草丛里有一个漂亮的小盒子，盒子的外面有着亮亮的彩色小玻璃装饰，像一个小宝盒一样精致。坤宝打开盒子发现里面除了一个小纸条什么都没有。幸亏坤宝跟妈妈学习，认识了不少字，只见上面写着：“把让你伤心的人装进盒子。”背面还有一行：“咒语……解咒语……！”坤宝看了这个字条兴奋极了，觉得太不可思议了，难道童话书里的事情真的发生了吗？于是坤宝抱着小盒子坐在树下开始想，到底把谁装进这个盒子里……忽然，他想起一个人——爸爸！没错，就是爸爸，他太让我伤心了，总是不陪我玩，还老是不讲信用，我要把他关进小盒子里好好反省一下！
于是，坤宝把小盒子放在一堆不起眼的草丛里，带着纸条一边往回骑车一边想：我可真的要把爸爸装进盒子了，好紧张啊！在快到家门口时，坤宝终于下定决心，拿出纸条，念了咒语……进了家门，他发现爸爸果然不在家，妈妈说爸爸还没回家呢。坤宝于是在家接着看书、玩玩具，似乎把这件事很快就忘了。到了吃晚饭的时间，大家都坐在桌前，只有爸爸还没在。妈妈轻松地说，估计又是加班吧，咱们先吃吧。因为是周末，妈妈允许坤宝看一部动画电影，这是坤宝每周最期待的时刻，他全情投入地看着电影，早把咒语和爸爸的事忘得一干二净了。
直到睡觉的时候，家人才觉得奇怪，爸爸怎么还没回来呢？这时候坤宝有点着急和不安了，难道爸爸真的被装进盒子了？他躺在床上，翻来覆去睡不着，再看表，竟然已经快夜里十二点了。坤宝有些难过了，爸爸要真是被装进小盒子了，一定没吃饭吧，而且他变小了估计也打不开盒子了，会不会也没有空气啊……其实爸爸也挺好的，总给我买玩具，还经常把我举得特别高转圈玩！家里人似乎都在担心爸爸呢，妈妈好像正在打电话，可是爸爸的电话也打不通。哎，坤宝忽然难受了起来，觉得自己太不好了，一定要把爸爸放出来！他连忙起身找那个纸条，然后悄悄躲进卫生间念了解咒语，然后又回到床上听着门外的声音，焦急地等着爸爸回家。
没过一会儿，爸爸果然回来了！妈妈责备爸爸怎么联系不上，爸爸解释说开车快到家的时候，忽然觉得特别困，就在路边停下来睡着了。不知不觉睡了很久，刚刚醒来。妈妈似乎对这个理由充满了怀疑，可是坤宝知道，爸爸说的是真的。因为在他睡着的时候，其实就是被装进了那个神奇的盒子……
fields.content_en:
**Where Did Daddy Go?**

Not far from the edge of the city, there was a secret little forest backed by rolling green hills. At the foot of those hills stood many houses of all sizes. One small red brick house was Kunbao's home, where he lived with his family, his grandma, and his grandpa.

Kunbao's family used to live in the city, but Kunbao was a child who loved nature deeply. Every day after kindergarten, he could only play in the tiny garden downstairs — riding his bike around, which was really boring. The community called it a garden, but it really just had a few trees and a small patch of green grass that was mostly worn bare by people walking back and forth. For a child like Kunbao, who longed for nature, that was quite frustrating.

Finally, for Kunbao's happy childhood, Mom decided the whole family would move to Grandpa's house by the edge of the city. And so, Kunbao's wonderful days began. He could go into the forest every day, run back and forth on the grass, catch all sorts of interesting little bugs, chase butterflies with a big net — he was having the time of his life. But soon, Kunbao's worries came again. Daddy never played with him. Kunbao really wanted Daddy to kick a ball with him on the grass, chase butterflies together, go to the little river nearby to catch shrimp and tadpoles, hold his hand while climbing a tree… There were so many things Kunbao wished Daddy could help him with, but Daddy was just too lazy! He was either looking at the computer or his phone, or sleeping, or as soon as he got home he'd say he was so tired and just wanted to lie on the sofa and watch TV. Kunbao was very upset because Daddy always said, "Next time, next time!"

One weekend noon, after lunch, Daddy turned down Kunbao's request to ride bikes together once again and hurried out to work overtime. Unhappy, Kunbao rode his little bicycle to the small forest. When he leaned his bike against a tree, he noticed a pretty little box in the grass underneath. The outside of the box was decorated with shiny, colorful little glass pieces, as delicate and lovely as a tiny treasure chest. Kunbao opened the box and found nothing inside except a small piece of paper. Luckily, Kunbao had learned to read from his mom, and the note said: "Put the person who makes you sad inside the box." On the back was another line: "Magic spell… anti-magic spell…!" Kunbao was so excited reading the note — it was incredible! Could things from fairy tales really be happening? So Kunbao held the little box and sat under the tree, thinking about who he should put inside… Suddenly, he thought of someone — Daddy! That's right, it was Daddy. Daddy made him so sad, never playing with him and always breaking his promises. He'd lock him in the little box to reflect on his ways!

So Kunbao placed the little box in an unnoticeable patch of grass and, riding his bike back home, kept thinking to himself: I'm really going to put Daddy in the box! How nerve-wracking! When he was almost at the door, Kunbao finally made up his mind, took out the paper, and read the magic spell aloud… He went inside and found Daddy wasn't home. Mom said Daddy hadn't come back yet. So Kunbao stayed home, read books and played with his toys, and seemed to forget about it pretty quickly. When it was time for dinner, everyone sat at the table except Daddy. Mom casually said he was probably working overtime again and that they should start eating. Since it was the weekend, Mom let Kunbao watch an animated movie — this was his most anticipated moment every week. He was completely absorbed in the movie and had forgotten all about the magic spell and Daddy by then.

It wasn't until bedtime that the family realized something was odd — why hadn't Daddy come home yet? Kunbao started to feel worried and uneasy. Had Daddy really been put inside the box? He lay in bed, tossing and turning, unable to sleep. Looking at the clock, it was already nearly midnight. Kunbao felt sad. If Daddy was truly in the little box, he must be hungry and wouldn't have eaten, and if he'd become small he probably couldn't open the box either — would there even be air inside?… Actually, Daddy wasn't so bad. He always bought Kunbao toys and often lifted him high up and spun him around for fun! Everyone in the family seemed to be worrying about Daddy. Mom appeared to be on the phone, but Daddy's phone wouldn't go through. Sigh, Kunbao suddenly felt awful and thought he was being very naughty. He had to let Daddy out! He quickly got up, found the note, quietly hid in the bathroom, and read the anti-magic spell. Then he returned to bed, listening at the door, anxiously waiting for Daddy to come home.

And sure enough, not long after, Daddy came home! Mom scolded him for being unreachable, and Daddy explained that when he was driving almost home, he suddenly felt very sleepy, so he pulled over and fell asleep. He hadn't realized how much time had passed and had just woken up. Mom seemed full of doubt about this excuse, but Kunbao knew Daddy was telling the truth — because while he was asleep, he had actually been put inside that magical little box…
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 菲比和巴尼
fields.subtitle: 不是很奇怪吗？
fields.subtitle_en: Isn't That Peculiar?
fields.content:
菲比有一头闪亮的金发，像是冥冥中注定一般，她养的那只小兔子巴尼，头顶竟然也有一撮金黄色的毛。白兔长金毛巴尼是菲比见过的最懒的兔子，它天性不在意自由，即便菲比打开兔笼将它放出来，也不见它跳跃撒欢，只半眯着眼躺在草地上晒太阳。巴尼圆滚滚的身子显得可爱又滑稽，两只长耳朵便是它身上唯一秀气纤细的地方了。巴尼时而将一边的叶子扒拉到跟前嚼上几口，随即便又眯上眼睛，靠在一旁不动了。
菲比常常想，这只笨兔子跟乌龟赛跑，保准输定了。
这天晴空万里，天上飘着零星的几丝云彩，像被扯散的棉花糖，仿佛伸手捻过来吸进嘴里，就会立即化掉。菲比站在院子里，想象着云彩的味道。
“菲比，推上你的小车，去后山给巴尼割些苜蓿回来。”
“好的，妈妈。”
菲比蹬上小胶靴，推上小推车，装上小镰刀，想了想，把巴尼也装进推车里。巴尼圆溜溜的双眼打开一条缝，既不雀跃也不抗拒，一副任君摆布的样子。“臭巴尼，我辛辛苦苦为你准备食物，你从来都不陪我玩。今天不给你割苜蓿啦！带你到后山，你自己吃好了。”
菲比推着小推车向不远处的后山走去，和暖的微风吹起她的裙摆，也吹起她金色的长发。巴尼趴在车里，头顶的金毛一颤一颤，小镰刀的刀刃差点碰到它短小的尾巴，菲比赶忙将镰刀挂得远一些。
后山的秋天是颜色最多的时候，金色的银杏，火红的枫树，苍翠的青松，嫩黄的菊花，银白的飞瀑……像是哪位画家打翻了调色盘。菲比停在一片苜蓿繁茂的地方，将巴尼抱下来放在地上，巴尼的双眼霎时滴溜溜瞪起来。菲比心想：这只馋兔子。
巴尼却迟迟没有下嘴，反而一扭头，朝上山方向的一条小径狂奔了起来。菲比吃了一惊：原来这只兔子会跑呀！菲比没做多想，也紧跟着巴尼，朝山上跑去。
菲比不知跑了多久，最后停在一条飞瀑前。流水从高处落下，砸进绿幽幽的深潭里，轰隆隆的。飞瀑两边是茂密的丛林，合抱的老树盘根错节，枝桠不规则地到处伸长。林中不时传来蝉和布谷鸟不急不忙的叫声，像是在召唤菲比向更深处去。菲比有些怕，但巴尼小小的身子几个跳跃，便拐进瀑布后的丛林里，没了踪影。菲比咬咬牙，快步跟了上去。
菲比转过飞瀑，却没看到巴尼，这时她张大了嘴巴，一脸吃惊：在她面前有一个巨大的山洞，里面一片漆黑，不知道通向什么地方。菲比四下寻找，放低声音呼唤巴尼的名字，回答她的却只有山洞里传出的回音。菲比紧张极了，生怕从里面钻出什么可怕的怪物将她吃掉，可是她无法丢下巴尼不管，她犹豫了一会儿，一狠心便硬着头皮大步迈了进去。
山洞里一丝光亮也没有，只有石壁上掉下的水珠砸在地上的啪嗒声。菲比一手扶着墙壁，一手向前探，低声叫着巴尼。忽而眼前闪过一道金光，菲比大叫一声，却并没有预想中的危险发生。借着金色的光亮，菲比看见两只洁白的长耳朵，是巴尼！原来金色的亮光是巴尼头顶的金毛发出的。
“巴尼，你怎么跑到这里来了，我抱着你，咱们出去吧。”菲比小声说道，蹲下身试图抱起巴尼，哪知巴尼缩起球一样的身子滚到前面，不让菲比抱。
“巴尼，我们回家啦！”
金色的亮光倏地躲远，又向着黑暗的前方移动。
菲比一路跟随，终于在将要筋疲力尽的时候看见了一抹属于太阳的光亮。
洞口很窄，巴尼一跃蹿跳出去，转回身望着洞内。
菲比跪下身来，缩着肩膀，一点一点向外挤。树枝划伤了她的脸颊，杂草刮乱了她的金发，终于，她爬出来了，和巴尼一起站在明亮的阳光下。
这是怎样美丽的一幅景象，菲比张大嘴巴，惊讶得说不出话：
彩云桥架在一条清澈的小河上，河水泛着淡粉色的光，飘散出甜甜的蜜桃味儿；胡萝卜有七种颜色，最神奇的是，它们长在了树上；大片大片的苜蓿田一直延伸到远处的山坡，仔细瞧瞧，居然都是四片叶子；道路两边是两排整齐干净的矮木房，从门里走出来的不是矮人，不是精灵，竟然是一只只蹦蹦跳跳的兔子——而且菲比发现，它们的头顶，都有一撮金色的毛。
“巴尼，这是你的家乡吗？”
巴尼当然不会回答，它只是走近，用头蹭了蹭菲比的靴子。
兔子王国热情招待了它们的人类朋友。菲比尝到了苜蓿花蜜酿的酒、紫色胡萝卜做的馅饼，而且这里的云彩真的是可以吃的，味道比棉花糖要好。
夜里，兔子王国繁星璀璨。菲比从没见过这么多星星，而且这些星星都好大，仿佛伸手就能摘到一样。她试着伸了伸手，却摸到了什么冰凉柔软有弹性的东西，原来星星的触觉像果冻一样！
菲比将这颗星星小心翼翼地摘下，她发现原来星星并不是五角的，而是圆溜溜的，像水晶魔法球一样。身边的兔子们为她摘下了星星而欢呼雀跃，跳起舞来。菲比想起在学校学的《兔子舞》，便也开心地跟着它们一起跳。
跳着跳着，菲比突然踩了空，从高空落下。她一跃坐起，梦醒了。
晨光熹微，透过淡蓝色的窗帘照进来，菲比发现自己在房间的小床上。
她跳下床跑出去，跑进院子，跑到兔笼前。
巴尼露出肉呼呼的肚皮，躺在笼子里呼呼大睡。菲比伸手抚摸它头顶金色的毛，小小的笼子里泛起淡淡的黄色光晕。巴尼缓缓抬起眼皮，瞥了眼菲比，又懒懒地睡去了。菲比却幸福地微笑着，真是一个无比快乐的梦……
fields.content_en:
**Title: Phoebe and Barney**

Phoebe had shining golden hair, and as if by some quiet destiny, her little rabbit Barney also had a tiny golden tuft of fur on top of his head. White rabbit with golden hair—Barney was the laziest rabbit Phoebe had ever seen. He didn't care much for freedom at all. Even when Phoebe opened his cage to let him out, he never hopped or played. Instead, he would lie on the grass half with his eyes closed, basking in the sun. Barney's round, chubby body looked cute and funny, and his two long ears were the only delicate, graceful part of him. Sometimes he would drag a leaf over with his paws and chew a few bites, then close his eyes again and lean against something, motionless.

Phoebe often thought that if this silly rabbit raced a turtle, he would surely lose.

One day the sky was clear and blue, with a few wisps of clouds floating gently, like cotton candy pulled apart. It was as if you could reach out and pinch one and pop it into your mouth, and it would melt away in an instant. Phoebe stood in the yard, imagining what the clouds might taste like.

"Phoebe, push your little cart and go to the back hill to cut some clover for Barney."

"Okay, Mama."

Phoebe pulled on her little rubber boots, pushed her small cart, and picked up her little sickle. After a moment's thought, she placed Barney inside the cart too. Barney opened his round eyes just a slit, neither excited nor resistant, perfectly content to be at the mercy of others. "Stinky Barney, I work so hard preparing food for you, and you never play with me. Today I won't even cut clover for you! I'll take you to the back hill, and you can eat whatever you find."

Phoebe pushed the cart toward the nearby back hill. A warm, gentle breeze lifted the hem of her dress and ruffled her long golden hair. Barney lay curled in the cart, the golden tuft on his head trembling with each bump. The blade of the sickle nearly touched his short little tail, so Phoebe quickly hung it farther away.

Autumn on the back hill was the most colorful season of all—golden ginkgo trees, fiery red maples, deep green pines, tender yellow chrysanthemums, and silvery white waterfalls cascading down. It was as if some painter had knocked over their palette. Phoebe stopped at a patch where the clover grew especially thick. She lifted Barney out and set him on the ground, and his eyes instantly went wide and sparkling. Phoebe thought to herself: *What a greedy little bunny.*

But Barney didn't start eating right away. Instead, he turned his head and sprinted down a narrow path leading up the mountain. Phoebe was surprised—so this rabbit *could* run! Without thinking too much, she followed close behind and ran up the hill after him.

Phoebe ran for what felt like a long time before finally stopping in front of a waterfall. Water rushed down from high above, crashing into a deep, emerald-green pool below with a soft thundering sound. On both sides of the falls grew thick jungle, with ancient trees whose roots twisted together and branches reaching in every direction. Cicadas and cuckoos called lazily from somewhere in the forest, as if inviting Phoebe to venture even deeper. Phoebe felt a little afraid, but Barney's small body bounded through the leaves and disappeared behind the waterfall. Gritting her teeth, Phoebe quickened her pace and followed.

Phoebe passed behind the waterfall but couldn't see Barney anywhere. Then her mouth fell open in wonder—right in front of her was a huge cave entrance, dark within, leading to who knew where. Phoebe looked all around and called out Barney's name in a soft voice. The only answer was her own echo bouncing back from inside the cave. Phoebe was very nervous, afraid some terrible monster might come rushing out to devour her. But she couldn't possibly leave Barney behind. After a moment's hesitation, she steeled herself and stepped boldly inside.

There was not a single ray of light in the cave, only the sound of water drops falling from the rocky walls and pattering onto the ground. Phoebe kept one hand on the wall and reached forward with the other, calling for Barney softly. Suddenly, a golden glow flashed before her eyes. Phoebe cried out, but no danger came. In the golden light, she saw two pure white long ears—Barney! The bright golden shimmer was the fur on top of his head.

"Barney, how did you get all the way here? Let me pick you up, and we'll go home," Phoebe whispered, crouching down to try and lift him. But Barney curled himself into a little ball and rolled forward, letting her not hold him.

"Barney, let's go home!"

The golden glow darted a little farther away and then continued moving forward into the darkness.

Phoebe followed along the entire way, and just as she was about to collapse from exhaustion, she finally spotted a sliver of sunlight belonging to the world above.

The cave opening was very narrow. Barney leaped right out, then turned around to look back inside.

Phoebe dropped to her knees, hunched her shoulders, and inch by inch worked her way out. Branches scratched her cheek, and wild grass tangled her golden hair. Finally, she crawled free and stood in the bright sunshine alongside Barney.

What a beautiful sight unfolded before her! Phoebe stood with her mouth wide open, too amazed to speak.

Rainbow-colored bridges arched over a crystal-clear little river. The water shimmered with a soft pink glow and carried the sweet scent of ripe peaches. Carrots grew in seven different colors, and the most wonderful thing was that they grew right on trees! Huge fields of clover stretched all the way to the distant hillsides, and when Phoebe looked closely, every single clover had four leaves. Lining the road were two neat rows of tidy little wooden houses. Stepping out of the doors weren't dwarfs or elves, but bunny after bunny, hopping and skipping happily—and Phoebe noticed that each of them had a tiny tuft of golden hair on top of their heads.

"Barney, is this your hometown?"

Barney couldn't answer, of course. He simply walked over and nuzzled his head against Phoebe's boot.

The Rabbit Kingdom welcomed their human friend with great warmth. Phoebe tasted wine brewed from clover flower honey and pies made from purple carrots. And the clouds really *were* edible—tasting even better than cotton candy.

That night, the Rabbit Kingdom sparkled with countless bright stars. Phoebe had never seen so many stars before, and they all looked so large, as if she could reach out and pluck them from the sky. She tried stretching her hand toward one, but her fingers brushed something cool, soft, and bouncy. The stars felt just like jelly!

Phoebe carefully plucked the star and discovered that it wasn't five-pointed at all—it was perfectly round, like a magical crystal ball. The rabbits around her cheered and danced with joy. Remembering the "Rabbit Dance" she had learned at school, Phoebe happily joined in.

But mid-dance, Phoebe suddenly missed a step and tumbled through the air. She jolted upright—she had woken from her dream.

Soft morning light filtered through the pale blue curtains. Phoebe found herself on her little bed in her room.

She jumped out of bed and ran outside, out into the yard, all the way to the rabbit cage.

Barney lay on his fluffy belly, fast asleep in his cage. Phoebe reached out and stroked the golden fur on top of his head, and a soft yellow glow seemed to rise in the tiny cage. Barney slowly opened his eyelids, glanced at Phoebe, and then drifted back to sleep. But Phoebe smiled blissfully. What a wonderfully happy dream it had been…
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 冬日的猫头鹰
fields.content:
一个影子
安静地停留在树梢
一轮圆月
默默地照亮在远方
冬日的寒气
凝结在密密的羽毛间
远处的啼鸣
躲藏在清冷的夜空中
一束冷淡的目光
直直地投向雪夜里孤独的身影
一道松软的雪印
长长地留在强壮男人的背后
一窝雏鸟相偎着
等待着雪松枯枝上的猫头鹰
一处温暖的木屋
壁炉的微火留给正在归家的父亲
冬日的夜晚，依然清冷
明朗的冷月，依然清晰
垂雪的松柏，直立盎然
寒气下高高低低的黑影啊
跳动着呵护的心
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Winter Owl**

A shadow
quietly resting on the treetop
a round moon
shining silently in the distance
the winter chill
settles deep within the thick feathers
a distant hooting call
hiding in the clear, cold night sky
a pair of calm eyes
gazing straight at the lonely figure in the snow
a trail of soft footprints
stretching long behind the strong man
a nest of little chicks snuggled close together
waiting for the owl on the pine branches
a cozy wooden house
the gentle glow of the fireplace waiting for father coming home
Winter nights are still cold
the bright clear moon still shines so clearly
the snow-dusted evergreens stand tall and green
those dark shadows rising high and low in the cold
beat with loving, caring hearts
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 荒岛梦
fields.content:
这一次，我和女儿的小破船是真真切切地被海浪推到了这一个岛上。我拉着女儿蹒跚地爬出小船，定睛仔细看了看，没错，是荒岛，真的是一座看不见人烟的荒岛！女儿很兴奋，完全没了刚才晕船的痛苦，欢快地在海滩上飞奔了起来，并且兴奋地发出各种奇怪的声音。我心情就复杂多了，忐忑，紧张，茫然，不知所措。我毫无力气地瘫坐在沙滩上，一种孤零零的感觉油然而生。完蛋了，我们在一座荒岛上！只有我和我的女儿！
渐渐地我似乎回过神来了，把依然在疯跑的女儿召唤回来。我们开始回忆，刚才在船上我们的食物呢，好像还有面包和石榴汁。对了，爸爸呢？爸爸去哪了？他刚才不是还给我们拍照片呢吗？哦，天啊！他难道掉进海里了！不对啊，还有船上别的人呢，明明是一艘大游轮的，怎么变成一只小破船了呢？其他人都去哪了？水！我记得女儿晕船时我们还有矿泉水的，去哪里了？
……
这一切似乎都引不起女儿的担忧，她貌似开始计划爬椰子树了！她很高兴自己的攀岩鞋依然在，并且满含期待地问我，想喝嫩一些的椰子汁还是老一些的。我离开一无所获的破船然后看着女儿说：“你真以为这是巴厘岛或者马尔代夫吗？”女儿一边走向椰子树一边说：“不管这是哪，至少我可以自己爬树摘椰子！”
好吧，我不得不佩服我的女儿，她总是不在乎很多事，她会把一切困难当作好玩的事情去解决。可是，宝贝，这一回是来真的了！我无奈地看着她像猴子一样敏捷地抱着树干往上蹬，心里竟然慢慢地开始不再那么担忧了。是啊，想那么多干什么，先找些吃的喝的。我很庆幸贴身的腰包依然在，而且那把功能很全的瑞士军刀居然也在。我正琢磨着在破船里再找些什么，我的女儿居然抱了一个椰子跑过来啦，大叫着：“妈妈，这个椰子真是熟透了，一拽就下来啦！”
当我们用石头费劲地打开椰子，喝着椰汁，用军刀切着椰肉吃的时候，忽然听到海面传来很大的汽笛声，居然有船！女儿首先放下椰子立刻奔向海边大喊起来，我也赶忙起身和她一起叫喊，多希望船会开过来。虽然呼啸的海风几乎要淹没我们的声音，但是船居然开过来了，还是一艘好大好大的船啊！而且，这不是一艘一般的船，而是一艘海盗船！我赶紧捂住女儿的嘴，可是，船上的人已经看见我们了，飘着海盗旗的大船几乎停在了我的面前。
正在我紧张错愕的时候，船上下来了一个人，这个人越走越近，我紧紧地搂着女儿。当这个人停在我面前时，我终于看清了，我认识他，这个戴着船长帽的海盗男人，就是刚刚失散的女儿的爸爸！就在我还在张着大嘴惊讶得没回过神的时候，女儿的爸爸突然举着个大铃铛在我耳边拼命地摇啊摇，铃声是那么的吵、那么的大！
好吧好吧！讨厌的闹铃！我起床啦……
fields.content_en:
Title: Island Dream

This time, my daughter and I really did wash ashore on this island in our little battered boat. I held my daughter's hand and we stumbled out of the boat. I looked around carefully. Yes, it was an uninhabited island—a real deserted island with nobody in sight! My daughter was so excited she completely forgot about her seasickness. She ran happily along the beach, making all kinds of silly sounds. I felt much more complicated emotions—worried, nervous, lost, and unsure of what to do. I collapsed weakly onto the sand, a lonely feeling welling up inside me. We were in trouble! We were stuck on a deserted island! Just me and my daughter!

Slowly, I began to come to my senses and called my daughter, who was still running wild, back to me. We started to remember—what had happened on the boat? Where was our food? I thought we still had bread and pomegranate juice. And where was Dad? Where had he gone? Wasn't he just taking photos of us? Oh, my goodness! Had he fallen into the sea? But wait—what about the other people on the boat? It had been such a big cruise ship. How did it become such a small, battered boat? Where had everyone else gone? And water! I remembered there had been bottled mineral water when my daughter got seasick. Where had that gone?

...

None of this seemed to worry my daughter at all. She was already planning to climb a coconut tree! She was very glad her climbing shoes were still with her, and she asked me eagerly, "Do you want young tender coconut juice or older, thicker coconut juice?" I left the empty, broken boat and looked at my daughter. "Do you really think this is Bali or the Maldives?" she replied, walking toward the coconut tree. "Wherever this is, at least I can climb the tree and pick coconuts myself!"

Well, I had to admire my daughter. She never worried about many things. She treated every difficulty as a fun challenge to solve. But, darling, this time it was really real! I watched helplessly as she climbed the tree trunk as agile as a little monkey. Slowly, my worries began to ease. Yes, why worry so much? Let's just find some food and water first. I was so glad my small waist bag was still here, and that my multi-functional Swiss army knife was in it too. I was wondering what else I could find in the broken boat when my daughter ran over with a coconut, shouting, "Mama! This coconut is perfectly ripe! It came right off with a pull!"

When we struggled to crack open the coconut with stones, drinking the fresh coconut juice and slicing the sweet meat with our pocket knife, we suddenly heard a loud ship horn from the sea! A ship! My daughter dropped the coconut immediately and ran toward the shore, shouting. I quickly got up and joined her. How we wished the ship would come closer. Although the roaring sea wind almost drowned out our voices, the ship actually came toward us—and it was a very, very big ship! And not just any ordinary ship—it was a pirate ship! I quickly covered my daughter's mouth, but the people on board had already spotted us. The ship flying the pirate flag came to a near stop right in front of me.

Just then, as I stood there紧张和惊讶, someone came down from the ship. He walked closer and closer, and I held my daughter tightly. When he stopped right in front of me, I finally saw clearly—I knew him! This pirate captain was none other than my daughter's dad, who had just separated from us! Before I could even process my surprise with my mouth wide open, my daughter's dad suddenly shook a big alarm bell right next to my ear, ringing it as loudly as he could!

Okay, okay! Annoying alarm clock! I'm up...
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 一枚雪花
fields.content:
去年的冬天，依然毫无悬念地降了几场大雪，白色厚重地压着整个世界。夜晚变得再也不寂寞了，黑色几乎消失在冬夜里。我喜欢有雪的冬天，那时候的屋子格外的温暖。穿着蕾丝的长睡袍，抱着一杯热可可，贴在凉凉的窗户上看雪景，真是件美丽的事儿。
当皑皑的大雪渐渐被太阳带走的时候，有一枚剔透晶莹的雪花，似乎迟迟不肯离去，暧昧地亲吻着我的窗户，执着地留恋着开始温暖的冬日。不知道是不是因为我每日与它呢喃细语，无限温存，还是听惯了我吐露各种情怀思念、纠结郁闷，偶尔，我会把这枚雪花当作有生命的冰花小人儿，情意绵绵。
终于在春天就快来的时候，我小心翼翼地把它装进了一个漂亮的瓶子里。我知道，这是一枚很特别的雪花，它特别大，特别有型，像水晶一样透着五彩的颜色。最神奇的是，它居然一直一直没有融化，就那样乖乖地在我的瓶子里安静地住着，好像在等着今年冬天的来临，在等新一季雪的召唤，等待再一次的璀璨绽放。
直到有一天的夜里，这片安静了一年的雪花，忽然静静地苏醒，在昏暗的房间里悄悄地忽隐忽现。它似乎在期待着什么，又似乎要发生什么变化。一整夜，这片雪花都不容我片刻安心入眠，它那么像淘气的小精灵，一闪一闪，调皮地闪动身上的小水晶，点点光亮跳跃在黑暗的夜里。原本温暖的屋子，渐渐地变得不再那么温暖了，我几乎感到那丝丝的凉意袭上身来。我拉了拉垂下床角的被子，再次把头缩进厚厚的大枕头里，在床上蜷曲成一只猫。当我再次歪头瞟了一眼那不安的雪花时，它居然像一只点着的水晶雕花灯，浑身绽放着晶莹剔透的绚丽色彩，光芒四射。
等等，它是在移动吗？瞬间，我仅存的睡意也消失了，我猛地坐起身子定定地看着这枚不断给我意外的雪花。真的，真的在动，这枚雪花真的在移动呢！它就像一只透明美丽的蜘蛛，悄无声息的，缓缓地向瓶口挪动，用几乎发现不了的速度，缓缓地挪动着。这枚雪花想出来！我迅速从床上爬起来，跳到窗前，猛地大力拉开沉重的丝绒窗帘……一片纯白瞬间射中了我的眼。好大的一场雪，今天第一场幸福的雪早早地来了！我回头转向那枚神秘的雪花，知道啦，你想妈妈啦！想出来和家人一起玩啦！
再一次，我小心翼翼把它放回窗户上。我的窗户上又有了一枚美丽的，大大的，晶莹剔透的雪花了，它在朝我笑呢……
fields.content_en:
Title: A Single Snowflake

Last winter, as expected, there were several heavy snowfalls, and a thick white blanket covered the whole world. The nights were no longer lonely; the darkness seemed to fade away in the winter evenings. I love winters with snow, because then our house feels especially warm. Wrapped in my lace nightgown, holding a cup of hot cocoa, and pressed against the cool window watching the snow fall—what a lovely thing that is.

When the bright white snow was slowly carried away by the sun, one single crystal-clear snowflake seemed reluctant to leave. It gently kissed my window, clinging on, lingering in the warming days of winter. Perhaps because I whispered sweetly to it every day, or perhaps because I had shared all my feelings, thoughts, worries, and sadness with it—I sometimes imagined that snowflake as a little living ice spirit, full of tenderness and charm.

Finally, just as spring was about to arrive, I carefully placed it inside a pretty little bottle. I knew this was a very special snowflake—it was unusually large, beautifully shaped, and shone like crystal with rainbow colors. The most magical thing was that it simply never melted. It sat quietly in my bottle, as if waiting for winter to come again, listening for the call of a new season's snow, hoping to bloom once more in all its brilliant beauty.

Until one night, the snowflake that had been still for a whole year suddenly awakened. In the dim room, it flickered softly in and out of sight. It seemed to be waiting for something, or perhaps about to change. That entire night, it would not let me rest. It was like a playful little sprite, twinkling and flashing the tiny crystals on its body, dots of light dancing through the dark. The warm room gradually felt cooler, and I could almost feel a chill wrapping around me. I pulled up the blanket hanging off the edge of the bed, tucked my head deep into my fluffy pillow, and curled up like a cat. When I glanced once more at the restless snowflake, it had transformed into something like a crystal lantern, glowing with shining, brilliant colors in every direction.

Wait—is it moving? In that moment, all my sleepiness disappeared. I sat straight up and stared at this surprising snowflake. It was true! It was really moving! The snowflake was gliding slowly and silently toward the mouth of the bottle, like a beautiful透明蜘蛛. It wanted to come out! I quickly jumped out of bed, ran to the window, and pulled open the heavy velvet curtains with all my might… A flash of pure white hit my eyes. What a beautiful snowfall! The first happy snow of the day had arrived early! I turned back to look at my mysterious snowflake and said, I know—you miss your mommy! You want to go out and play with your family!

Once again, I gently placed it back on my windowsill. And there on my window, another beautiful, big, crystal-clear snowflake appeared, smiling at me…
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 贝壳兔子传声筒
fields.content:
米可是一个在海边长大的孩子。
她喜欢海边的清晨。喜欢太阳藏在海平面以下的时候，天边火焰一样的深红色。海鸥飞得高高的，动听的鸣叫声从很远的地方传来。
她喜欢海边的午后。喜欢湛蓝的海水打在肩膀上的凉爽，泳圈上的小蓝鲸在洁白的浪花里翻滚跃动，像活了一样。沙滩上的爸爸和孩子一起砌沙雕，巨浪打来，沙雕被打翻，他们便离海岸远了点，重新盖一座城堡。
她喜欢海边的傍晚。远处的灯塔一闪一闪，不仔细看，还以为是一颗明亮的星星。没有了白天的喧哗热闹，耳畔回荡的都是海浪拍打礁石的声音。米可光着脚丫，把人字拖收进随身的帆布挎包里。一步、两步、三步……米可听着海浪声，用步伐来丈量它敲打礁石的频率。
脚底传来一阵痒痒的痛感，米可被什么东西硌了脚，借着夕阳的余晖拾起，是一颗晶莹的贝壳。沙滩上有一位戴帽子的大叔，他盘腿坐着，手上正编织着什么，四周散落着奇形怪状的贝壳。
“你在做贝壳工艺品吗？”
“是的，你要选一个吗？”
“可以吗？但是我没有钱。”
“不要钱。”
米可蹲下身，捏起这个瞅瞅，抓起那个看看，它们都好美，该选哪一个呢？
“这个好吗？”大叔拾起角落里一只雪白的“兔子”，问米可。
那真是一个栩栩如生的、令人惊叹的作品，贝壳上整齐的横纹就像兔子柔顺的毛；那两只“长耳朵”，大叔也不知从哪里找来那么相似的两片贝壳；就连红色眼睛，都找来颜色相似的砂石粘上去。
大叔摆摆手，憨憨地笑，米可接过小兔子，也咧开嘴笑着谢大叔。然后她趿拉上人字拖，满心欢喜地跑回家。
夜深了，米可爬上床，小手捧着小兔子贴在耳畔，沉沉睡去了。
好奇怪啊，卧室里为什么会有海边的涛声呢？米可心里数着：一秒、两秒、三秒……涛声的频率和用脚步丈量出来的一模一样。是在做梦吗？
“米可……哗啦啦啦……我喜欢你……哗啦啦啦……因为你像我一样喜欢大海……哗啦啦啦……”
米可试图睁大眼睛寻找声音的来源，眼前只有一片氤氲的乳白色烟雾，恍惚间，一头巨大的蓝鲸翻过一片巨浪，背上的水柱像喷泉一样直冲云霄。
米可却突然醒来了，手里还紧紧捧着那只贝壳兔子，壁灯泛着幽黄的光，耳边只剩蟋蟀有规律的叫声。
米可生日那天，全家人开着游艇去海上游玩。
碧海蓝天，海鸥在头顶结伴飞过。夏天的风吹得人懒懒的，爸爸妈妈躺在榻上休息，米可捧着蛋糕和果汁跑来跑去，贝壳小兔子被她用绳子穿起挂在胸前，随着她活泼的脚步左摇右摆。
突然，海上出现了一道望不到顶的水柱，激起了洁白的水花，米可跑上前看。
她不禁发出又惊又喜的赞叹，这是梦里的那只蓝鲸吗？
这时候，胸前的小兔子震动起来，又是那个熟悉的声音：
“米可……哗啦啦啦……我喜欢你……哗啦啦啦……因为你像我一样喜欢大海……哗啦啦啦……”
米可将小兔子贴在耳畔，声音更清楚啦！原来小兔子是她和蓝鲸之间的“传声筒”吗？米可对着小兔子大声说：
“我也喜欢你！蓝鲸，我们可以做朋友吗？”
游艇旁响起一阵愉悦的叫声，那道高耸的水柱被午后的阳光折射出彩虹的颜色，美丽极了！
fields.content_en:
# The Seashell Rabbit Talking Tube

Mika is a child who grew up by the sea.

She loves the beach in the morning, when the sun hides just below the horizon and the sky glows deep red like fire. Seagulls fly high above, their sweet calls drifting in from far away.

She loves the beach in the afternoon. She loves the cool splash of blue water on her shoulders, the little blue whale on her swim ring rolling and jumping through white foam, as if truly alive. On the sand, fathers and children build sandcastles together. A big wave comes and knocks them over, so they step farther from the water and build a new castle.

She loves the beach at dusk. The lighthouse in the distance flickers on and off. If you don't look closely, you might think it is a bright star. The noise of the day has faded, and all she hears is the sound of waves beating against the rocks. Mika takes off her flip-flops and puts them in her canvas bag. One step, two steps, three steps… She listens to the waves and counts out their rhythm with her feet.

A ticklish little sting comes from the soles of her feet. Mika has stepped on something. In the golden sunset light, she picks it up — it is a shining seashell. On the beach sits an uncle wearing a hat, cross-legged, weaving something in his hands. Strange and wonderful shells are scattered all around him.

"Are you making seashell crafts?"

"Yes, would you like to choose one?"

"Can I? But I don't have any money."

"No money needed."

Mika squats down, picking one up to look, then another, admiring them all. They are all so beautiful. Which one should she choose?

"How about this one?" The uncle picks up a snowy white "rabbit" from a corner and asks Mika.

It is truly a breathtaking work of art. The neat lines across the shell look just like soft rabbit fur. Those two "long ears" are made from two shells that match perfectly — the uncle must have searched far and wide to find them. Even the red eyes are little grains of colored sand, carefully stuck in place.

The uncle waves his hand and gives a silly, sweet smile. Mika takes the little rabbit and grins back at him, thanking him. Then she slips on her flip-flops and runs all the way home, her heart full of joy.

Night falls. Mika climbs into bed, cups the little rabbit in her small hands, and presses it gently against her ear. Soon she is fast asleep.

How strange. Why can she hear the sound of ocean waves in her bedroom? Mika counts in her head: one second, two seconds, three seconds… The rhythm of the waves is exactly the same as the one she counted with her footsteps. Is she dreaming?

"Mika… splash, splash, splash… I like you… splash, splash, splash… because you love the sea just like I do… splash, splash, splash…"

Mika tries to open her eyes wide and find where the sound is coming from. All she sees is a soft, milky white mist. And then, in a daze, a giant blue whale leaps over a towering wave, its spout shooting up like a fountain straight into the sky.

But suddenly Mika wakes up. She is still holding the seashell rabbit tightly. The bedside lamp glows a warm yellow, and all she hears is the steady chirping of crickets.

On Mika's birthday, her whole family takes a yacht out to sea.

The sky and sea are both a beautiful blue. Seagulls fly past overhead in pairs. The summer breeze makes everyone feel drowsy and calm. Mama and Papa rest on lounge chairs while Mika runs about with the cake and juice. The little seashell rabbit hangs from a string around her neck, swaying left and right with her happy steps.

Suddenly, a towering column of water rises from the sea, sending white spray flying. Mika runs over to take a look.

She gasps with surprise and delight. Is it the blue whale from her dream?

At that moment, the little rabbit on her chest begins to vibrate. That familiar voice comes again:

"Mika… splash, splash, splash… I like you… splash, splash, splash… because you love the sea just like I do… splash, splash, splash…"

Mika presses the rabbit to her ear, and the voice is even clearer! Could the little rabbit be a talking tube between her and the blue whale? Mika speaks loudly into it:

"I like you too, blue whale! Can we be friends?"

A joyful cry echoes beside the yacht. The tall spray of water catches the afternoon sunlight and shines with the colors of a rainbow. It is so beautiful!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 羊爱上猫
fields.title_en: The Sheep Who Loved a Cat
fields.content:
小羊莱特爱上了“万人迷”艾米丽。
艾米丽是一只金毛碧眼的猫咪，身段姣好，四肢修长匀称，尾巴翘起一个好看的弧度，走路时步伐优雅，从容不迫。艾米丽的爱慕者可以从街头的电话亭排到街尾的快餐店，小羊莱特也是其中一个。
获得佳人芳心的方法是什么？莱特已经坐在电脑前“谷歌”了一上午，得出了结论：喜欢一个人，就给她她想要的。
于是莱特去临街的“哞哞花店”买了一束玫瑰，又在心里默背了一遍告白词，便向艾米丽家走去。路上莱特碰到了小猪伟兹，他带了一束香水百合，想也是去艾米丽家告白。莱特不觉加快了步伐，想赶在伟兹前面敲开艾米丽的门，伟兹也毫不让步。就这样，一羊一猪在路上狂奔了起来，到了艾米丽家门口的时候，他们已经累得气喘吁吁的。
“咚咚”，莱特和伟兹一同敲响了艾米丽的门。过了许久，门才被打开。“有事吗？”艾米丽问。“艾米丽！”莱特和伟兹一同说道，“请接受我的鲜花。”“谢谢。”艾米丽接过了玫瑰和百合，眨眨碧绿的大眼睛，莞尔一笑，随即关上了门，没有给他们告白的机会。
莱特不灰心。第二天，他去斜对面的“喵喵鱼市”买了一条金鱼，又在心里默背了一遍告白词，便急急向艾米丽家走去。莱特在路上碰到了小马托尼，他带了一只小仓鼠。于是，莱特和托尼也开始赛跑，到了艾米丽家门口的时候，他们都累得上气不接下气。
“咚咚”，莱特和托尼一同敲响了艾米丽的门。过了许久，门才被打开。“有事吗？”艾米丽问。“艾米丽！”莱特和托尼一同说道，“请接受我的礼物。”“谢谢。”艾米丽接过了金鱼和老鼠，翘翘高傲的尾巴，莞尔一笑，随即关上了门，没有给他们告白的机会。
莱特郁闷地回到家，又坐在电脑前研究“求爱秘籍”。这次他得出结论：喜欢一个人，就给她自己所拥有的最好的东西。
第三天，莱特背着一卷羊毛毯子，来到了艾米丽家门口。今天没有其他的“情敌”出现，莱特松了口气。艾米丽正在家里唱歌，悠扬的歌声透过门板传到莱特的耳朵里，让他的爱慕之情更加浓厚了。
“咚咚”，莱特敲开了艾米丽的门，鼓起所有的勇气说道：“艾米丽，请接受我的爱意吧。”艾米丽望着光秃难看的莱特，眼中流露出了愧疚而又无奈的神情。莱特剪掉了自己身上所有的毛，为艾米丽编织了一条柔软温暖的毯子。但是艾米丽还是婉拒了莱特的求爱。
莱特很伤心，忧郁的他独自走到了郊外，靠在一棵老树下暗自伤怀。“小羊，你在难过什么呀？”满脸皱纹的树伯伯慢悠悠地问道。“我给了艾米丽她最喜欢的东西，还有我最好的东西，可她为什么还是不喜欢我呢？”莱特闷闷地说。“她喜欢的和你最好的，未必是她需要的啊。这世上不缺锦上添花，缺的是雪中送炭。”树伯伯说完，缓缓闭上眼，睡着了。
莱特似懂非懂，但树伯伯的话让他的心里舒服了许多。
许多天过去了，艾米丽的家门口再没有排着长队的爱慕者了。因为在一场大火中，艾米丽为了救一只小猫，颈上的金毛被烧掉了。她不再美丽，甚至因为伤痛，不再自信，失去了往日的优雅。因此，往日的爱慕者们都望而却步，见异思迁了。
这一天，莱特又背着一卷什么东西，敲开了艾米丽家的门。“艾米丽，这个一定非常适合你！”原来，莱特用新长出的毛为艾米丽编织了一条围巾，刚好可以遮住她的伤疤。望着依旧光秃秃的莱特，艾米丽的眼眶湿润了。
莱特张开怀抱，艾米丽轻轻地靠在他的怀里，温柔地笑了。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Lamb Who Loved the Cat

Little Lamb Wright fell in love with the wonderful Emily.
Emily was a cat with golden fur and bright blue eyes, with a graceful figure and long, slender legs. Her tail curled up in a lovely arc, and she walked with elegant, unhurried steps. Her admirers could line up from the phone booth on the street corner all the way to the fast-food restaurant at the end. Little Lamb Wright was one of them.

So what's the way to win a lady's heart? Wright had been sitting in front of the computer "Googling" all morning, and he came to a conclusion: if you like someone, give them what they want.
So Wright went to the "Moo Moo Flower Shop" across the street and bought a bouquet of roses. He practiced his confession words in his head and set off toward Emily's home. On the way, Wright ran into little pig Weiz, who was carrying a bunch of fragrant lilies, apparently also heading to Emily's to confess his feelings. Wright quickened his pace, wanting to beat Weiz to Emily's door. Weiz wouldn't back down either. And so, a lamb and a pig raced all the way down the road. By the time they reached Emily's doorstep, both of them were out of breath.

"Knock, knock," Wright and Weiz knocked on Emily's door together. After a long while, the door finally opened. "What is it?" asked Emily. "Emily!" Wright and Weiz said together. "Please accept my flowers." "Thank you," Emily said, taking the roses and lilies. She blinked her big green eyes and gave a gentle smile, then closed the door without giving them a chance to confess.

Wright wasn't discouraged. The next day, he went to the "Meow Meow Fish Market" across the street and bought a goldfish. He practiced his confession words again in his head and hurried toward Emily's house. On the way, Wright ran into little horse Tony, who was carrying a small hamster. So Wright and Tony started racing each other, and by the time they reached Emily's door, both were completely winded.

"Knock, knock," Wright and Tony knocked on Emily's door together. After a long while, the door opened. "What is it?" asked Emily. "Emily!" Wright and Tony said together. "Please accept my gift." "Thank you," Emily said, taking the goldfish and the hamster. She flicked her proud tail, gave a gentle smile, and then closed the door—without giving them a chance to confess.

Wright went home dejected and sat back in front of the computer to study his "love secrets." This time, he came to a new conclusion: if you like someone, give them the very best of what you have.
On the third day, Wright carried a rolled-up wool blanket and arrived at Emily's doorstep. No other "rivals" appeared that day, so Wright breathed a sigh of relief. Inside, Emily was singing, her sweet melody drifting through the door and filling Wright's heart with even deeper affection.

"Knock, knock," Wright knocked on Emily's door and, gathering all his courage, said, "Emily, please accept my love." Emily looked at the bare and scraggly Wright, and her eyes showed a look of guilt and helplessness. Wright had sheared off all the wool from his own body and woven it into a soft, warm blanket for Emily. But Emily still gently turned him down.

Wright was very sad. The gloomy lamb wandered out to the countryside alone and leaned against an old tree, quietly moping. "Little lamb, what are you sad about?" asked Grandpa Tree, his face full of wrinkles, in his slow, leisurely voice. "I gave Emily her favorite thing, and the very best of what I have, so why doesn't she like me?" Wright mumbled. "What she likes and what is your best aren't necessarily what she needs. This world doesn't lack people who add flowers to the brocade—it lacks those who bring charcoal in the snow." After saying this, Grandpa Tree slowly closed his eyes and fell asleep.

Wright didn't fully understand, but Grandpa Tree's words made him feel a little better inside.

Many days passed, and no long line of admirers waited outside Emily's door anymore. Because in a great fire, Emily had lost the golden fur on her neck while saving a kitten. She was no longer beautiful, and because of her pain, she had lost her confidence and her former elegance. The admirers of yesterday stepped back and moved on.

One day, Wright knocked on Emily's door again, carrying something rolled on his back. "Emily, this will suit you perfectly!" It turned out that Wright had woven a scarf from his newly grown wool, just right to cover her scar. Looking at the still-bare Wright, Emily's eyes grew teary.

Wright opened his arms, and Emily gently leaned into them and smiled softly.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 神笔诺伊
fields.subtitle: 竹子做成的笔杆，兔毛做成的笔头。大家都说，那是一支神笔。
fields.subtitle_en: A bamboo handle, a rabbit-hair tip. Everyone said it was a magical brush.
fields.content:
诺伊有一支画笔盛夏的正午，烈日炙烤着大地，这是一天当中影子最短的时候。一顶大檐帽，一袭英挺的警服，一副洁白的手套，他是城市道路的守护者——交警叔叔。晶莹剔透的汗珠连成了串，顺着他帅气的侧脸滑下，掉在被太阳晒得锃亮的柏油路上，即刻就蒸发。诺伊口袋里的画笔“嘀嘀”作响——开工啦！
诺伊用白色画云彩，大朵的云彩飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘上天空，遮住了烈日。
诺伊用黑色画树荫，大片的树荫飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘进路边，带来了阴凉。
诺伊又蘸了绿色的水彩，这下画什么呢？软毫轻转，徐徐涂抹，是一支冰凉甜美的绿豆雪糕。雪糕飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘进诺伊的手里，诺伊将它剥开，送给了交警叔叔。
深秋的公园，寒霜打蔫了花草，未及南飞的鸟儿在寒风里瑟瑟发抖，落叶一层覆一层，怎么也落不完似的。放风筝的老人，嬉戏打闹的孩子，统统躲回了家，这是一个安静的季节。诺伊口袋里的画笔“嘀嘀”作响——开工啦！
诺伊用黄色画菊花，淡雅的菊花飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘进了花坛，成了公园里的最后一朵花。
诺伊用棕色画鸟窝，结实的鸟窝飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘到了树上，孤单的鸟儿有了家。
诺伊又蘸了绿色的水彩，这下画什么呢？软毫轻转，细细勾勒，是一片绿色的银杏叶。银杏叶飘出画纸，飘啊飘，随风打了几个卷儿，落进满地的黄叶里，被一个眉眼弯弯的长发女孩拾起，悉心放进了随身的笔记本里。
新年的早晨，诺伊被妈妈从暖和的被窝里拽了起来。早餐的香气悠悠钻进尚还朦胧的意识里，诺伊挣扎着穿衣叠被，收起的窗帘露出黯淡的天光。“妈妈，再让我睡一会儿吧，天还没亮哪！”“不是天没亮，那是烟火放得太多，有了雾霾。天不早啦！”诺伊吃完早餐，戴上口罩出门。口袋里的画笔“嘀嘀”作响——开工啦！
诺伊用蓝色画天空，澄澈的蓝天飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘过头顶，飘过高楼，天色不再黯淡。
诺伊用红、橙、黄、绿、青、蓝、紫画彩虹，绚丽的彩虹飘出画纸，飘啊飘，飘到天边，路上的行人惊叹连连，彩虹比烟火好看多啦！
诺伊又蘸了绿色的水彩，这下可画什么好呢？
不画啦！不画啦！我等春姑娘来。
fields.content_en:
Title: Noe's Magic Paintbrush

On a midsummer noon, the fierce sun baked the earth. It was the time of day when shadows are shortest. A wide-brimmed hat, a crisp police uniform, white gloves — he was the guardian of the city roads, the traffic policeman uncle. Crystal-clear beads of sweat formed strings, sliding down his handsome cheek, falling onto the sun-baked asphalt road, and evaporating in an instant. The paintbrush in Noe's pocket went "beep beep" — time to get to work!

Noe painted white clouds, and big fluffy clouds floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, up into the sky, covering the fierce sun.

Noe painted dark tree shade with black, and大片 of cool shade floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, settling along the roadside, bringing relief from the heat.

Noe dipped the brush again in green watercolor. What to paint now? The soft bristles swirled gently, and stroke by stroke, a cool, sweet green bean ice cream appeared. The ice cream floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, right into Noe's hand. Noe unwrapped it and gave it to the traffic policeman uncle.

In the deep autumn park, frost had wilted the flowers and plants. Birds that hadn't yet flown south shivered in the cold wind. Fallen leaves piled layer upon layer, as if they would never stop falling. Old men flying kites and playing children had all gone back indoors. It was a quiet season. The paintbrush in Noe's pocket went "beep beep" — time to get to work!

Noe painted yellow chrysanthemums, and delicate blossoms floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, settling into the flower bed, becoming the last flowers in the park.

Noe painted brown bird nests, and sturdy nests floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, landing in the trees. The lonely birds now had a home.

Noe dipped the brush again in green watercolor. What to paint this time? The soft bristles danced gently, tracing fine lines, and a green ginkgo leaf appeared. It floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, curling with the wind before settling among the golden leaves on the ground. A long-haired girl with smiling eyes picked it up and carefully placed it in her notebook.

On a New Year morning, Noe was pulled from the warm blankets by mommy. The scent of breakfast drifted into his still-drowsy mind. Noe struggled to dress and fold the blankets. The drawn curtains revealed a dim gray light. "Mommy, let me sleep a little longer. It's not even dawn!" "It's not dawn that's missing, darling. Too many fireworks have filled the air with haze. It's getting late!" After breakfast, Noe put on a mask and headed outside. The paintbrush in his pocket went "beep beep" — time to get to work!

Noe painted the sky in blue, and a clear blue sky floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, rising above heads and over tall buildings. The sky was no longer dull.

Noe painted a rainbow with red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, and purple. A brilliant rainbow floated out of the paper, drifting and drifting, reaching to the horizon. Passersby on the street gasped in wonder. The rainbow was so much more beautiful than fireworks!

Noe dipped the brush again in green watercolor. What should he paint now?

Not this time! Not this time! I'll wait for Miss Spring to arrive.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 小鳄鱼香香
fields.content:
小爱跟自己的好朋友一匹小马、双胞胎狐狸姐妹小左和小右一起在丛林里赶路，他们急着去小马的家乡——内蒙古大草原。这匹蒙古小马叫小卡，他的家乡遭到了沙鼠的侵害，大草原已经都快秃了，很多马都要远离家乡去新的地方找草源。小爱和小左、小右就是一起去帮助小卡赶走沙鼠的。
几个好朋友忙着赶路，这时在低矮的灌木边出现了一片沼泽，水面上漂着绿色的浮萍和白色的睡莲。一只看上去挺可爱的小鳄鱼露出了半个身子，慢慢爬到岸上。“好可爱的一只小鳄鱼呀，可她看起来好像很不开心的样子。”小爱说。
只见小鳄鱼来到一棵树下默默地哭了起来。“呜呜，哥哥们好讨厌……”小爱走过去轻声问：“你为什么哭呢？”
“她叫香香，最爱哭了，他们家只有她一个小女孩。”小左抢着说。
“为什么我有那么多哥哥呢！”香香有点愤愤地说，“他们都爱欺负人，我真想有小妹妹和我一起玩。”
“大概你妈妈不喜欢女宝宝吧……”小左朝她做了个鬼脸。“才不是呢！妈妈可喜欢我了。”香香着急地反驳。
小爱认真地想了想说：“也许，我可以帮你这个忙。”
“真的吗？”香香半信半疑又充满期待地看着小爱。
“哈哈，小爱，你难道要给她变出个妹妹来吗？”小右不相信地大笑着说。小左和小马他们也很疑惑地看着小爱。
小爱问香香：“你妈妈正在孵蛋吗？”
“现在不在，哥哥们在打架，妈妈去管他们了。”香香指着远方说，“哥哥们一天到晚又吵又闹，妈妈总得为他们操心！”
“那你能带我去看看那些蛋吗？”小爱问。“可以，但我们一定要快点，妈妈很快就会回来的，要是她看到我们围在这儿一定会很生气的！”大家跟着香香来到一个窝边，里面都是鳄鱼蛋。
“我妈妈是一个生物学家，她给我讲过，鳄鱼妈妈如果把蛋生在温暖的地方，出生的就会是男宝宝，要是把蛋生在阴凉的地方，出生的就是女宝宝。”大家听了小爱说的话都恍然大悟。“你们看，那边有一块大石头，我们把它挪到窝边上，这样就可以挡住阳光了，温度就会变低一些。”小爱指着不远处说。
香香一下子兴奋起来：“那我很快就可以有妹妹了？”“对呀，耐心等待吧，你妈妈会给你带来好几个小妹妹呢！”小爱也很开心地说。于是大家一起把石头小心地搬到了窝边。
香香激动得坐在石头上欢呼：“我要和妈妈一起等妹妹出生，我就要有妹妹啦！哈哈！”
“一定要当个好姐姐呀！”小爱说完又和朋友们一起赶路了。
fields.content_en:
Title: Little Crocodile Xiangxiang

Xiao Ai was traveling through the jungle with her best friends — a little horse and the twin fox sisters, Xiao Zuo and Xiao You. They were in a hurry to reach the little horse's hometown, the vast grasslands of Inner Mongolia. The Mongolian pony, named Xiao Ka, had a problem: his homeland was being overrun by gophers, and the grasslands were nearly bare. Many horses had to leave home to find new grazing lands. Xiao Ai, Xiao Zuo, and Xiao You had come to help Xiao Ka drive the gophers away.

The good friends were busy on their journey when, beside some low bushes, a marsh appeared — its surface dotted with green duckweed and white water lilies. A cute-looking little crocodile poked half her body out of the water and slowly crawled onto the shore. "What a cute little crocodile," said Xiao Ai. "But she looks rather unhappy."

The little crocodile walked over to a tree and began to cry silently. "Waaah, my brothers are so annoying..." Xiao Ai walked over and gently asked, "Why are you crying?"

"Her name is Xiangxiang," said Xiao Zuo quickly. "She cries all the time. She's the only girl in her family."

"Why do I have so many brothers!" Xiangxiang said, a little crossly. "I wish I had a little sister to play with."

"Maybe Mama doesn't like baby girls..." Xiao Zuo made a silly face at her. "That's not true! Mama loves me!" Xiangxiang protested eagerly.

Xiao Ai thought carefully for a moment and said, "Maybe I can help you with that."

"Really?" Xiangxiang looked at Xiao Ai with half-belief and great hope.

"Haha, Xiao Ai, are you going to conjure a little sister for her?" Xiao You laughed loudly in disbelief. Xiao Zuo and the little horse also looked at Xiao Ai with puzzled expressions.

Xiao Ai asked Xiangxiang, "Is your mama sitting on her eggs right now?"

"Not right now. My brothers are fighting, and Mama went to scold them." Xiangxiang pointed into the distance. "My brothers吵 and闹 all day long, and Mama always has to worry about them!"

"Can you take me to see those eggs?" asked Xiao Ai. "Yes, but we have to be quick. Mama will be back soon, and she'll be very angry if she sees us gathered here!" Everyone followed Xiangxiang to a nest, which was full of crocodile eggs.

"My mama is a biologist," Xiangxiang explained. "She told me that if a mama crocodile lays her eggs in a warm place, the babies will be boys. If she lays them in a shady place, the babies will be girls." Everyone nodded as they finally understood what Xiao Ai meant.

"Look over there," said Xiao Ai, pointing. "There's a big stone. If we move it next to the nest, it will block the sunlight and make the temperature a little cooler."

Xiangxiang's eyes lit up with excitement. "Will I have a little sister soon?"

"Yes," said Xiao Ai happily. "Just be patient, and your mama will bring you several little sisters!" Together, everyone carefully moved the stone next to the nest.

Xiangxiang sat on the stone, cheering with joy. "I'm going to wait with Mama for my sisters to be born! I'm really going to have a sister! Haha!"

"Be a good big sister, okay?" said Xiao Ai. Then, with her friends, she continued on their journey.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 秋千
fields.content:
我想在轻柔的风中
吹散美丽的蒲公英
让所有飞舞的小伞
送去生命的种子
我望着傍晚的红日
摇晃着低低的秋千
每一下飞荡的起伏
都是你小小的身影
我要当一名勇敢的船长
用结实的手臂保护你
让拴着绳子的小木板
带你去天上摸夕阳
我想做一只强壮的大鸟
把你精灵般的笑声
送到最远的夜空
化成一颗颗的小星星
或者
我还是做一个木头秋千吧
垫在你软软的身体下
听树叶沙沙作响
看太阳慢慢下沉
就这么安静地陪着你
一起飘荡
一起长大
一起看暖阳
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Swing**

I want to blow the beautiful dandelions
in the gentle wind
and let all the tiny flying parachutes
carry seeds of life away.

I gaze at the red evening sun
swaying on the low swing.
Every rise and fall
is your little silhouette.

I want to be a brave captain
with strong arms to hold you safe
and let that little wooden board on ropes
carry you up to touch the sunset in the sky.

I want to be a mighty bird
and carry your elfin laughter
to the furthest night sky,
turning it into little stars.

Or maybe
I'll just be a wooden swing
placed beneath your soft little body,
listening to the leaves whisper
and watching the sun slowly sink.

Just quietly staying with you,
drifting together,
growing together,
watching the warm sun together.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 那年的夏天
fields.content:
还是那间小木屋
还是屋外茂密的榕树
还是树上那阵阵蝉鸣
却不见了你的微笑
依然是炎热的
水面泛着金光
风儿丝丝掠过
我在倒影中寻觅夏天
那年的天特别蓝
你说我的眼睛里都是天
那年的云像棉花
你说要抱着我躺在云间
那年的太阳很刺眼
你说就像我笑起来嘴角的灿烂
还是那条窄窄的木船
孤独地漂荡着
还是那扇依偎的窗栏
留我独自倚靠
一切都那么遥远
像会飘的梦
一切都那么清晰
就在我眼前
是那年的夏天
fields.content_en:
Title: That Summer

That little wooden cabin still stands,
That thick banyan tree outside the door,
Those cicadas singing in the branches—
But your smile is gone.

It is still hot and bright,
The water shimmers with golden light,
A gentle breeze brushes past,
And I search for that summer in its reflection.

The sky that year was so blue,
You said my eyes held all that blue.
The clouds that year looked like cotton,
You said you'd hold me and lie among them.
The sun that year was bright and warm,
You said it matched the brightness of my smile.

That narrow wooden boat still drifts alone,
That window frame where we once leaned together
Still leaves me leaning by myself.

Everything feels so far away,
Like a drifting dream.
Yet everything is so clear,
Right before my eyes.
It is that summer.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 夜里的花和草
fields.content:
暑假的夜晚，深蓝色的星空澄澈高远，银河像一条洁白的丝带，横贯天际。
露露和莫兰坐在院子里的小板凳上吃西瓜，一轮皎洁的明月当空高挂。露露望着浩瀚的夜空，一脸向往地说道：“月亮可真美。莫兰，所有的植物都离不开阳光，但有没有植物是需要月光的照射才能生长的呢？”莫兰想了想，回答道：“我听说有种花叫昙花，只在夜间开放，白天就谢了。”
“你这么一说，我倒想起了另一种花，叫夜来香，到了夜晚香气会特别浓。”露露说完，深吸了口气，仿佛闻到了夜来香的香味一样。
“看来月光对植物的生长还真能发挥作用哪！”月亮像是听懂了一般，将柔和的月光轻轻照在两人身上，在地上投射出她们可爱的小影子。
“不知道可不要乱说哦。”莫兰的爸爸从屋里走出来，手里的蒲扇摇摇晃晃，赶走了围绕着孩子们的蚊虫。
“爸爸，给我们讲讲月光的奥秘吧！”莫兰扒着爸爸的腿，急切地想知道答案。
“月亮本身是不会发光的，我们看到的月光，是月球将太阳照射到它身上的光线反射到地球上的。当月球、地球、太阳连成一线的时候，太阳的光线被地球挡住，照射不到月球上，这就形成了我们平时所说的‘月食’。”莫兰的爸爸顿了顿又说，“所以，月亮是不发光的，那又何来月光对植物生长的作用呢？”
露露皱了皱眉头，似有不服，又提出了疑问：“那要怎么解释昙花在夜间开放，夜来香在夜里变得更香的现象呢？”莫兰爸爸笑着回答道：“昙花有一个很好听的名字，叫‘月下美人’，但这可不代表它是因为月光才开花的。昙花的原产地在遥远的中美洲大陆——墨西哥至巴西的热带沙漠中，那里的气候又干又热，但到晚上就凉快多了。晚上开花，可以避开强烈的阳光曝晒，缩短开花时间，又可以大大减少水分的损失，有利于它的生存，使它的生命得到延续。于是天长日久，昙花在夜间短时间开花的特性就形成了，代代相传至今。”
“原来是这样，看来植物和人一样，虽然离不开阳光，但是太过强烈的曝晒也无法承受。”露露赞同地点头。
“那夜来香呢？它在夜里会变得更香，这是为什么啊？”莫兰按捺不住，紧接着问道。
“夜来香的花瓣与一般白天开放的花的花瓣构造不一样，夜来香花瓣上的气孔有一个特点，一旦空气的湿度大，它就张得大，气孔张大了，蒸发的芳香油就多。夜间因为没有了太阳照晒，空气中的水蒸气蒸发得比较少，因此湿度就比白天要大。这样一来，它的气孔就张得更大了，释放出的香气也就特别浓。你们可以养一株夜来香观察一下，就会发现不仅在夜晚，在阴雨天，它的香气也比晴天要浓。”
两人一脸崇拜地望着莫兰爸爸，又扬起圆圆的脑袋瓜，同样一脸崇拜地望着深邃的夜空。大自然中可真是有千千万万的奥秘，等着她们去揭晓呢。
fields.content_en:
# The Flowers and Grass at Night

On a summer evening, the deep blue sky was clear and high, the Milky Way stretching across the heavens like a white ribbon. Lulu and Moran sat on small stools in the courtyard, eating watermelon, with a bright round moon hanging high above. Lulu gazed at the vast night sky and said longingly, "The moon is so beautiful. Moran, all plants need sunlight to grow—but are there any plants that need moonlight instead?"

Moran thought for a moment and answered, "I've heard of a flower called the queen of the night—it only blooms at night and withers by dawn."

Hearing this, Lulu remembered another flower. "That reminds me of the evening primrose, whose scent becomes especially strong at night." She finished speaking and took a deep breath, as if she could already smell the fragrant blossom.

"It seems moonlight really does play a role in how plants grow!" The moon, as though it understood, gently shone its soft light upon the two girls, casting their cute little shadows on the ground.

"Don't say things you're not sure about," Moran's father came out of the house, his palm-leaf fan swaying back and forth, shooing away the mosquitoes buzzing around the children.

"Dad, tell us about the secrets of moonlight!" Moran clung to her father's leg, eager to know the answer.

"The moon itself doesn't produce light. What we see as moonlight is sunlight that has bounced off the surface of the moon and traveled to Earth. When the moon, Earth, and Sun line up in a row, the Earth blocks the Sun's rays from reaching the moon—that's what we call a lunar eclipse." Her father paused before adding, "So if the moon doesn't produce light, how can there be any effect of moonlight on plant growth?"

Lulu frowned slightly, unconvinced, and asked another question, "Then how do we explain the phenomenon of the queen of the night blooming at night and the evening primrose becoming more fragrant after dark?"

Moran's father smiled and replied, "The queen of the night has a lovely name—'beauty under the moon'—but that doesn't mean it blooms because of moonlight. The queen of the night is originally from the tropical deserts of Central America, from Mexico to Brazil. There, the climate is both dry and hot, but it becomes much cooler in the evening. Blooming at night helps it avoid the intense sunlight, shortens the time the flower is open, and greatly reduces water loss, which helps it survive and continue its life. Over time, this trait of blooming briefly at night was passed down from generation to generation."

"I see," Lulu nodded in agreement. "So just like us, plants can't handle too much intense exposure even though they can't live without sunlight."

"What about the evening primrose? Why does it become more fragrant at night?" Moran couldn't hold back and asked immediately.

"The structure of the evening primrose's petals is different from flowers that bloom during the day. The pores on the evening primrose's petals have a special feature—they open wider when the humidity in the air is high. When the pores open wider, more aromatic oil evaporates. At night, without the sun's heat, less water vapor evaporates into the air, so the humidity becomes higher than during the day. This causes the pores to open even wider, releasing especially strong fragrance. You can grow an evening primrose and observe it—you'll find that not only at night, but also on rainy days, its fragrance is stronger than on sunny days."

The two girls looked at Moran's father with admiration, then lifted their round little heads to gaze once more at the profound night sky. There were truly countless mysteries in nature, waiting for them to uncover.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 勇敢的野牛
fields.content:
广袤的东欧大草原上，水草丰茂，来自黑海和里海的暖风不远千里奔袭而至，带来了充沛的雨水。动物们为上天的恩赐欢欣鼓舞，草原上到处一派和谐繁荣。
然而，野牛族长安德烈最近却一脸愁容，常常在饮水食草的时候唉声叹气。这一切都被聪明细心的约克看在眼里，约克细细琢磨缘由，似是有所领悟了。
这一天，安德烈捉了一只野兔回来，族人围在一起，都十分疑惑不解：欧洲野牛虽然体型庞大，健壮勇猛，但却是食草性动物。族长什么时候养成了吃肉的怪癖，捉只野兔回来是要做什么呢？
安德烈将野兔放在地上，清了清嗓子，向大家道出了他最近一直烦恼的事情：前些日子，人类的偷猎者频频来犯，大肆捕杀草原上的狼群。一系列“血腥事件”发生之后，草原上悄悄出现了变化，虽然大伙儿都没发现，但逃不过德高望重的野牛族长安德烈的眼睛。原来，狼的数量渐少，作为狼的主要食物的野兔，因为少了天敌的攻击和捕食，开始大量繁殖。安德烈烦恼的事情就在于，数量剧增的野兔成为了他们的竞食者。草木虽然能再生，但终究抵不过野兔的繁殖速度。这样一来，就会对野牛族的生存造成威胁。
经族长一提点，大伙儿才发现，草原的面积还真是在明显地减少，这的确是一个严峻的问题。大伙儿面面相觑，脸上也都挂上了愁容。而被安德烈捉来的野兔，则满脸不屑地趴在一旁啃着青草，似是在说：“你们能把我怎么样？还能把我吃了不成？”这时候，一直沉默的约克开口说道：“我倒是有一个办法，也许能奏效，只是需要大伙儿的配合。”大伙儿一听，连声附和。约克是族里最聪明的牛，这一点没有牛不赞同。安德烈点点头，示意约克说下去。
“大伙儿分成两队，一队埋伏在草原入口的山坡后面，一旦猎狼的坏蛋进入，就撞翻越野车，顶飞猎枪，让偷猎者屡战屡败，再也不敢侵犯草原；另一队去野兔聚居的地方，将他们赶到狼群和虎群集中的地方，帮助他们捕猎。虽然我们不吃野兔，但狼和虎是吃的嘛。”
约克说完，大伙儿纷纷表示赞同。安德烈的眉头渐渐舒展开来，爽朗地大笑了几声，然后说道：“就这么办！”
于是正义勇敢的野牛族展开了旷日持久的草原保卫战，他们打退了违法犯罪的偷猎者，抑制了野兔的飞速繁殖。不过提起狼虎捕杀野兔的血腥场面，有些野牛还是会露出胆战心惊的表情，觉得太过残忍。安德烈安慰大家说：“物竞天择，适者生存。我们帮助狼群压制野兔，也是在帮助我们自己，更是在保护自然。自然环境只有维持平衡，动物们才能永久地生存下去，生态平衡一旦被破坏，遭殃的将是整个草原。”
来自黑海、里海的暖风依旧缓缓吹着，草原又恢复了往日的宁静，那是大自然和谐的真正宁静。
fields.content_en:
Title: The Brave Wild Buffalo

On the vast steppes of Eastern Europe, where grass was thick and green, warm winds from the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea traveled for many miles to bring plentiful rain. The animals were overjoyed for this gift from the sky, and the grasslands were full of peace and prosperity.

But Andrew, the leader of the buffalo clan, had been looking worried lately. He would often sigh while drinking water and eating grass. His clever and careful friend York noticed everything and began to think about what might be troubling him.

One day, Andrew brought back a wild rabbit. The rest of the clan gathered around, very puzzled. European buffaloes may be large and strong, but they are herbivores. When had their leader developed such a strange habit of catching rabbits, and what did he intend to do with it?

Andrew placed the rabbit on the ground and cleared his throat. He explained the worry that had been weighing on him. Recently, human poachers had been coming to the grassland again and again, hunting the wolf packs. After a series of troubling events, quiet changes had begun to appear on the grassland. Most of the animals had not noticed, but Andrew, who was respected by all, saw them. The number of wolves was decreasing, and since rabbits were the main food of wolves, the rabbits had no natural predators anymore. They began to multiply rapidly. And that was exactly what troubled Andrew—the growing number of rabbits was becoming a competitor for the food that the buffalo clan relied on. The grass could regrow, but not as fast as the rabbits reproduced. This would eventually threaten the survival of their whole clan.

When Andrew pointed this out, everyone realized that the grassland was indeed shrinking. It was a serious problem. The animals looked at each other with worried faces. Meanwhile, the rabbit that Andrew had caught lay nearby, nibbling on grass with a look of defiance, as if saying, "What can you do about me?" Then York, who had been silent, spoke up. "I have an idea that might work, but we will all need to work together." Everyone agreed at once. No buffalo in the clan doubted that York was the smartest of them all. Andrew nodded and invited York to continue.

"Let's divide into two groups," York said. "One group will hide behind the hill at the entrance of the grassland. When the poachers arrive, we will overturn their vehicle and knock away their guns, so they will never dare to return. The other group will drive the rabbits toward the areas where wolves and tigers live, helping them hunt. We may not eat rabbits ourselves, but wolves and tigers certainly will."

Everyone agreed with York's plan. Andrew's worried expression slowly softened, and he let out a warm laugh. "Let's do it!" he said.

And so the brave and just buffalo clan began a long battle to protect their grassland. They drove away the poachers and slowed the rapid growth of the rabbit population. Still, some buffaloes felt uneasy when they thought about the wolves and tigers hunting rabbits, finding it a bit frightening. Andrew comforted them gently. "Nature has its own balance," he said. "By helping the wolves control the rabbits, we are helping ourselves and protecting nature. Only when the natural world stays in balance can all animals live peacefully. If that balance is broken, the whole grassland will suffer."

The warm winds from the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea continued to blow softly, and the grassland returned to its peaceful quietness—the true, harmonious calm of nature.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 艾莉的梦
fields.content:
艾莉是一个特别爱做梦的小女孩，她在白天的时候就很喜欢发呆，其实，也不是在发呆，照她自己的说法就是：“我在放空我的大脑啊，这样才可以让神奇的事情进到我的脑海里来。”
白天艾莉最爱做的事就是在自家的后花园里，静静地观察各种各样的小昆虫。初夏就是个好季节，大大小小的花儿开满了整个庭院，肥肥瘦瘦的绿植叶子也铺满了墙壁，这些都是昆虫们最舒适的家园。看着蝴蝶高高低低、缓缓地扑腾着，艾莉忽然觉得好乏好困啊，不知道是不是因为看了太多小小的虫子，眼睛都累了。好吧，就这样歪在院子里的藤椅上，睡一会儿吧。这一睡不要紧，艾莉居然又做梦了，这一回，是她一直一直想要的梦境……
艾莉慢慢睁开眼，拨开一片巨大的挡着视线的叶子，定睛看了看眼前这个世界。哦，不！这是怎么了？艾莉发现周围的世界突然变得很不可思议：草长得像树一样高大，巨大的七星瓢虫正好奇地盯着艾莉，像火车一样的毛毛虫就从艾莉的身边爬过。一只黑寡妇蜘蛛正在他们头顶织一张大网，一只漂亮的红蜻蜓跟艾莉一样高，停在一根大草上，瞪着圆眼睛看着艾莉，艾莉也似乎要从他的眼睛里看见成千上万的自己。这回，蜗牛的壳看起来真的像是个屋子了，估计艾莉也能住进去。
最神奇的是那些花花草草，平时也就是鲜艳而已，可现在居然都透着荧光，好像全被萤火虫施了魔法，沾满了萤光粉闪着光亮。天黑得好快啊，但是阳光在这个世界已经不重要了，因为在这里，每一只昆虫，每一株植物，都像覆盖了精灵仙子的魔咒，散发着神奇诡异的光亮。而且他们都与艾莉心灵相通，只觉得她是一位意外的访客。
艾莉依然茫然：到底是自己变小了，还是这个世界变大了？但是这一刻，什么都不重要了！重要的是，这一刻，艾莉终于可以和她最爱的昆虫们在一起，那么近那么近……
fields.content_en:
Title: Ellie's Dream

Ellie was a little girl who loved dreaming more than anything else. During the day, she often sat quietly and gazed into the distance. It wasn't really doing nothing, she liked to say: "I'm clearing my mind, so that wonderful things can come in."

Ellie's favorite thing to do during the day was sit in her family's backyard garden, quietly watching all kinds of little bugs. Early summer was such a lovely season. Big and small flowers bloomed all over the yard, and chubby green leaves covered the walls — a perfect little home for insects. Watching the butterflies flutter up and down slowly, Ellie suddenly felt so sleepy. Maybe her eyes were tired from looking at too many tiny creatures. Well, she decided to lean back in the wicker chair in the yard and take a little nap. And as soon as she closed her eyes, Ellie fell into a dream — this time, it was the very dream she had always longed for...

Ellie slowly opened her eyes and pushed aside a giant leaf that was blocking her view. She blinked and looked around at the world before her. Oh no! What was going on? Ellie noticed that everything around her had suddenly become magical: the grass grew as tall as trees, a huge ladybug curiously stared at her, and a caterpillar as big as a train crawled right past Ellie. A black widow spider was weaving a giant web above their heads, and a beautiful red dragonfly, as tall as Ellie herself, perched on a blade of grass and gazed at her with round eyes. Ellie felt like she could see thousands of herself reflected in those shiny eyes. Even the snail's shell looked just like a tiny house now — Ellie thought she might even be able to climb inside.

The most wonderful thing was the flowers and plants. Usually they were only bright and colorful, but now they glowed with a soft, shimmering light, as if fairies had sprinkled them with glittering dust. Night fell quickly, but sunlight no longer mattered in this world, because here every insect and every plant seemed covered in a gentle spell, radiating a mysterious and magical glow. And they all seemed to feel connected to Ellie, welcoming her as a sweet and unexpected visitor.

Ellie was still a little confused — had she become tiny, or had the whole world grown big? But at that moment, none of that mattered! What mattered was that Ellie could finally be with her favorite little bugs, so close, so very close...
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 年少的我
fields.content:
离开很久了
只有在梦里
我依然看见自己年少的身影
放肆地笑着
欢快地叫着
勇敢地跑着
年少的我
很想再回去
轻松的自己
在简单的烦恼里傻傻地释怀
青涩的话语
懵懂的爱情
稚嫩的心绪
年少的我
依然在心中
偶尔地澎湃
在成熟的困惑中无惧地微笑
自信地浅吟
执着地追随
坚定地前行
年少的我
从未离开
那份情怀
伴我一生
fields.content_en:
Title: The Young Me

It has been a long time
But only in my dreams
Do I still see myself as young
Laughing freely
Chirping joyfully
Running bravely

The young me
Longs to go back again
To that easy self
Letting simple worries fade with a foolish smile
Unsure words
Innocent love
A tender heart

The young me
Still lives in my heart
Occasionally surging
Smiling fearlessly through grown-up confusion
Singing softly with confidence
Chasing what I believe in
Walking forward with strength

The young me
Has never left
That feeling
Will stay with me for life
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 丛林里的精灵
fields.subtitle: 叶芝《失窃的孩子》
fields.subtitle_en: From W.B. Yeats' "The Stolen Child"
fields.content:
湖中的丛林
向着湖心低低倾斜
一座枝叶茂盛的小岛
苍鹭拍打着翅膀
把瞌睡的小鼠惊醒
那里隐藏着精灵的木桶
装满了草莓
和偷来的鲜红樱桃
来吧，人间的孩子
拉起精灵的小手
走向旷野和溪流
不要让充满泪水的世界打扰你
那里有银波轻漾的月光
朦胧的灰色沙滩
在那最遥远的地方
我们频频欢笑
飘动着快乐的舞影
我们交换着稚嫩的小手
兴奋溢满眼波
跟着精灵追赶着月亮
蹦跳着踩一个个泡泡
去到那芦苇成堆的水塘
寻找熟睡中的鲈鱼
和沐浴在水中的星星
走吧，人间的孩子
拉起精灵的小手
走向旷野和溪流，
不要让充满烦恼的世界扰乱你
来吧，人间的孩子
和精灵一起，快乐于丛林
fields.content_en:
**Title: The Spirits of the Jungle**

In the jungle of the lake,
Leaning low toward the heart of the water,
A small island thick with leaves and branches,
A heron flaps its wings
And startles a sleepy little mouse.
There hides a spirit's wooden barrel,
Filled with strawberries
And stolen bright red cherries.

Come, child of the world,
Take the spirit's little hand,
And walk toward the open fields and streams.
Do not let a tear-filled world disturb you.
There is moonlight shimmering on silver waves,
A soft gray sandy shore.
In that faraway place,
We laugh again and again,
Our joyful dance shadows fluttering,
We trade little hands,
Excitement shining in each other's eyes,
Chasing the moon with the spirits,
Bouncing and hopping, stepping on bubbles,
To the pond piled high with reeds,
Searching for sleeping perch
And stars bathing in the water.

Go, child of the world,
Take the spirit's little hand,
Walk toward the open fields and streams,
Do not let a troubled world扰 your peace.

Come, child of the world,
Be happy in the jungle, together with the spirits.
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 精灵来了
fields.content:
甜蜜的爱情总是那么贪心，想要很多很多，也想要永远永远，还想要两个人一起爱，三个人一起爱，四个人一起爱，一家人一起爱。
于是，经过了十天的不安与等待，甜蜜的纠结终于停在那两条小小的红杠杠上。拿着它，感觉自己的心都快跳出来了，氧气猛然间就不够用了。我的眼睛几乎湿润了，空气似乎凝结了，强烈的心动传递给了每根微微颤抖的神经……这是真的吗？我不敢相信，使劲再看看那两条热烈的颜色，是真的！一个小小的精灵飞进了我的身体，是真的！一个小小的天使飞进了我的世界。
看着他兴奋欣喜的表情，感受着他紧紧的拥抱，幸福在我心中洋溢着。我知道，从此，生活忽然之间就变了，从此，我们多了一份甜蜜的担忧，多了一份神奇的牵挂。从此，我们的心连得更近，我们的手牵得更紧，我们的爱更深，一直深到肚肚下面，那个好小好小的你……
fields.content_en:
Title: The Little Elf Has Come

Sweet love is always so greedy — it wants so much, wants forever and ever, wants two people to love together, three people to love together, four people to love together, a whole family to love together.
So, after ten days of restless waiting, the sweet worry finally came to rest on those two little red lines. Holding it, I felt my heart nearly leap out of my chest. I could barely catch my breath. My eyes grew moist, the air seemed to freeze, and a strong flutter ran through every trembling nerve... Is this real? I couldn't believe it. I looked harder at those two bright red lines — they were real! A tiny little elf had flown into my body. They were real! A tiny little angel had flown into my world.
Watching his excited, joyful expression and feeling his tight hug, happiness overflowed inside me. I knew that from now on, everything had suddenly changed. From now on, we would carry a sweet little worry, a magical thread of care. From now on, our hearts would be drawn even closer together, our hands would hold on even tighter, and our love would run deeper — all the way down, all the way to your very small, sweet little self in my belly...
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 生命的召唤
fields.content:
洗手池边上的镜子里依然是我曾经熟悉的脸，只不过现在，是一张苍白而憔悴的脸。一次次折磨人的孕吐令我艰难地喘息着，一阵阵强烈的心悸令我虚弱无力。
这些日子以来，身体，仿佛忽然不属于自己了，从未有过的疲惫不堪和日益严重的头痛紧紧伴随着我，莫名的焦虑和烦躁时时纠缠着我，头发掉得好厉害，连呼吸都觉得那么困难，自己仿佛变了一个人……在他紧张而心疼的怀抱中，我第一次强烈感受到，原来，这，就是生命的召唤！
我侧身看着自己镜中的身体，似乎不认识这个再熟悉不过的身体了，神奇隆起的腹部让我的身体呈现出不可思议的美妙曲线。我惊叹着生命的力量，就在这一秒，我轻抚着自己的身体，突然明白了，我早已不是原来的那个我。肌肤深处那小小的宝贝啊，我，是你的妈妈！
fields.content_en:
# The Call of Life

In the mirror above the sink is still my once-familiar face, only now it is a pale and tired face. Time after time, the relentless pregnancy nausea makes me catch my breath with difficulty, and wave after wave of strong palpitations leave me weak and frail.

Over these past days, my body feels as though it no longer belongs to me. Unprecedented exhaustion and steadily growing headaches follow me closely. Nameless anxiety and restlessness tangle with me constantly. I'm losing so much hair, even breathing feels difficult, and I feel as though I've become someone else... In his worried and tender embrace, I feel it strongly for the first time — this, this is the call of life!

I lie on my side, looking at my body in the mirror, as if I don't recognize this once-so-familiar body. The miraculously rounded belly gives my form an incredible, wonderful curve. I marvel at the power of life, and right in this moment, as I gently stroke my body, I suddenly understand — I am no longer the person I used to be. My precious little one deep within my skin, I am your mommy!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 天使要长大
fields.content:
宝贝，这些日子你过得好开心啊！每天都在妈妈肚肚里快乐地扭来扭去，房间太小不够住了吗？亲爱的宝贝，似乎妈妈没法给你换更大的房间了，只能靠你自己把房间变得更大一点了。你是个强壮的宝贝，一定可以做到的哦！
因为，我在经常鼓起的大肚皮上看见你撅着小屁屁拱来拱去，看见你伸了伸小胳膊，打了个哈欠，踢了踢小腿腿，舒展着身体……你想告诉妈妈，你是个多么健壮的小家伙；你想告诉妈妈，你长眉毛啦，长小指头啦，长脚趾甲啦，你的小胳膊小腿上有肌肉啦……
你想告诉妈妈，你游来游去的好开心，但是地方小了点，总会撞到肉肉的墙上；你还想告诉妈妈，你能听见各种奇怪的不明白的声音啦，但是你知道妈妈的声音。你喜欢妈妈每天跟你说的甜蜜的话，你喜欢妈妈抚摸着你，给你讲的一个个美丽故事，欢快童谣……
fields.content_en:
Title: Growing Up in the Tummy

Dear baby, you've been so happy these days! Wriggling and turning about cheerfully in Mama's tummy all day long. Is the room too small for you? Dear baby, it seems Mama can't give you a bigger room, so you'll have to make it grow bigger yourself. You're such a strong little one—you can do it, I know!

Because, on my often-swollen tummy, I see you sticking out your little bottom, squirming around; I see you stretch out your little arms, let out a yawn, kick your little legs, and舒展 your body… You want to tell Mama what a sturdy little fellow you are. You want to tell Mama that you've grown eyebrows now, tiny fingers, toenails, and that your little arms and legs have muscles…

You want to tell Mama how happily you swim around, though the place is a bit cramped and you keep bumping into the soft, meaty walls. And you want to tell Mama that you can hear all sorts of strange, puzzling sounds now—but you know Mama's voice. You love the sweet words Mama says to you every day. You love when Mama strokes you and tells you those beautiful stories and cheerful little nursery rhymes…
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 幸福的大肚子
fields.content: 妈妈知道你好想早点出来跟妈妈亲亲，可是妈妈还要和你一起耐心地等待，等待你再胖一点，再健康一点。虽然，妈妈越来越笨重了，肚子越来越大了，腿越来越肿了，走路越来越累了，青春姣美的面容也有点儿小走样了，连睡觉都变成一件非常辛苦的事了……但是，宝贝，妈妈真的好幸福！妈妈抚摸着在温暖的小房子里快乐地玩耍的你，妈妈的心在陪着你的心一起跳动……
fields.content_en:
Title: The Happy Big Belly

Mommy knows you really want to come out early and give Mommy kisses. But Mommy is still waiting patiently with you, waiting until you're a little plumper, a little healthier. Though Mommy is getting more and more clumsy, her belly keeps growing, her legs keep swelling, walking feels more tiring every day, her once-youthful pretty face has changed a little, and even sleeping has become quite hard... but, baby, Mommy is so happy! When Mommy strokes you as you play happily inside your warm little house, Mommy's heart beats together with yours...
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 天使降临人间
fields.content:
真的是你吗，我的宝贝？那个粉嫩嫩的小人儿，那个奋力大声啼哭的小人儿，那个始终眯缝着小眼睛小嘴寻找妈妈的小人儿！你终于躺在我的身边，我终于可以拥你入怀！非人的疼痛在这一刻，已经被泪水冲淡，原来世间还有如此神奇的爱。这种爱让我看不见自己，这种爱令我的眼里只有你。宝贝，这就是，妈妈的爱！
什么是幸福的感觉？就是，妈妈再也不用隔着一堵墙和你亲密相爱了。现在，我终于可以，一秒钟都不停地看着你垂着长睫毛在美美地享受你专属的佳肴；我终于可以，怀抱着你这个软软的小肉球，闻着你淡淡的奶香；我终于可以，看着你一噘一噘的小嘟嘴，摸着你嫩嫩的迷你小手指……这一刻，世界都与我无关了，你就是我的世界，我的宝贝！
fields.content_en:
Title: Angels Descend to the World

Is it really you, my darling? That tiny pink little soul, that baby who cries so strongly and loudly, that one who always keeps squinting those tiny eyes and little mouth, searching for Mommy! You are finally lying by my side, and I can finally hold you in my arms! The pain I endured is washed away by tears in this moment. There truly is such magical love in this world. This love makes me forget myself; in my eyes, there is only you. Baby, this is… a mother's love!

What does happiness feel like? It means Mommy no longer has to love you through a wall. Now, I can finally watch you, second after endless second, enjoying your special meal with those long lashes drooping sweetly. I can finally hold you, my soft little ball of flesh, and smell your faint milk fragrance. I can finally watch your little pouty lips purse again and again, and touch your tender tiny fingers… In this moment, the whole world fades away from me. You are my world, my darling!
fields.source: 精选睡前胎教故事（川川）

fields.title: 给宝宝种下善良的种子
fields.title_en: Planting Seeds of Kindness in Baby
fields.subtitle: 改编自霍桑《石面人像》
fields.subtitle_en: Adapted from Hawthorne's The Snow-Image
fields.content:
相由心生
从前，一个村庄里有一个小孩，名叫欧尼斯特，
他有一个挺拔的鼻子，一双炯炯有神的大眼睛，
他闭着嘴巴，却有一丝笑意。
欧尼斯特时常仰起头，看着村里的石面人，
村里的人认为，肯定会有一个人拥有石面人这样的长相，
欧尼斯特也认同这一点。
一天，有人说拥有石面人长相的人就要来了，
人们都很激动。
这个人的名字就有富贵的含义，
果然他变得很有钱回到了村庄。
所有人都觉得他的长相酷似石面人。
但是欧尼斯特并不觉得。
后来，又有一些著名人士和思想家来到村庄，
但是欧尼斯特还是觉得没有人像石面人。
他相信，只要一直守在这里，一定能看到酷似石面人的人，
因此他从不离开这里。
时光流转，欧尼斯特慢慢老去，
终于，人们觉得，欧尼斯特的脸非常像石面人。
这是真的，
石面人总是关注着村民，而欧尼斯特的脸处处彰显着智慧，两个人非常像。
美国第十六任总统林肯曾经说：
“人一定要为自己的脸负责。”
意思就是说，当一个人的想法、人生观、价值观发生了变化，
长相和命运也会出现变化。
欧尼斯特对石面人充满敬佩，
并且对此坚定不移，
所以他的脸才会越来越像石面人。
这就是相由心生。
妈妈说，宝宝听
宝宝，你知道“相由心生”的意思吗？简单来说，就是人内心的美与丑会在脸上反映出来。心灵美丽，容貌就会比较端庄；心灵邪恶，容貌就会比较丑陋。宝宝呀，你的善良、豁达，会让你成为最美的人。
会魔法的小流星
在美丽的流星宫殿里，住着许许多多的流星。有一颗小流星耐不住寂寞，她渴望同自己的哥哥姐姐们一样能够开始自己的宇宙之旅，于是便偷偷地跑了出去。
小流星兴奋极了，跑得非常快，因为流星的天性本就如此。她跑的时候天空中划出一条优美而明亮的弧线，在远处静静观赏的群星们都很羡慕她的美丽。小流星觉得飞翔在广阔宇宙的感觉真的很好，自由自在，无忧无虑。
“快看快看，有流星耶！”
“在哪儿？在哪儿？快指给我看！”
“那儿呢，别愣着了！快许愿，快许愿！”
小流星听到有人在喊她的名字，就好奇地找寻着声音的来源，原来地面上有很多人正虔诚地紧闭双眼，双手合十，对着自己小声许愿呢。
小流星仔细地听着，人们的愿望各种各样，有些愿望自己也不太明白，但她还是认真地把它们都记在了心里：
一个可爱的小女孩希望妈妈的病可以快点好起来；
一个满身泥水的建筑工人希望自己能快点儿赚到足够的钱，这样就能给女儿凑齐上大学的费用；
一个双目失明的小男孩希望自己能够重新看见这个世界；
一个怀孕的女士希望自己不久后能生下聪明健康的宝宝……
小流星非常想帮助这些人实现自己的愿望，但却不知道该怎么做。于是她回到流星宫殿，找到流星国王，问道：“我可以帮助他们完成心愿吗？”
“是的，我的孩子，”流星国王用富有磁性的声音答道，“我们流星家族都拥有一种帮助别人实现愿望的魔法，只是，这需要以生命为代价。当你拖着美丽的尾巴划破天空时，人们的愿望就会实现，但你也会消失在宇宙中——这就是我们流星家族的使命。”
小流星听后点点头，说道：“我知道如何使用魔法了。”她又来到茫茫苍穹，看到那些对着自己许愿的人们，于是，她拖着长长的尾巴在空中跳起了欢快的舞蹈，然后如烟花般绚烂地划过夜空，带着满足与幸福的笑容消失在天际……
妈妈说，宝宝听
小流星用瞬间的美丽圆了别人的梦想，换来了自己的永恒，她就是美丽的天使。宝宝，妈妈也曾在流星划过的时候许下美丽的愿望，你想知道是什么愿望吗？当然是希望你健健康康、平平安安地来到我们身边哦。
月亮的生日礼物
小棕熊很喜欢月亮，他想送给月亮一份生日礼物，但是，他不知道月亮的生日是哪一天，也不知道该送什么才好。有一天，小棕熊划着小船渡过清清的小河，又穿过一片茂密的树林，来到他认为已经足够高的山顶上。
小棕熊心想：“这回我和月亮说话，它一定能听到。”于是，小棕熊将双手放在嘴边作喇叭状喊道：“你好！”
山谷中传来声音：“你好！”
小棕熊高兴极了。他想：“哇，真棒！月亮居然和我说话了！”
“你的生日是哪天？”小棕熊问。
“你的生日是哪天？”山谷中又传来了声音。
“明天就是我的生日呀！”小棕熊高兴地回答。
“明天就是我的生日呀！”山谷中又传来声音。小棕熊更高兴了，因为月亮居然与自己是同一天的生日。
“你想要什么生日礼物？”小棕熊问道。
“你想要什么生日礼物？”山谷中传来问话。
“我想要一顶很酷的帽子。”小棕熊兴奋地答道。
“我想要一顶很酷的帽子。”山谷中传来回答。小棕熊别提多高兴了，月亮居然和自己想要同样的礼物。
“我知道了，再见！”小棕熊挥手和月亮告别。
“我知道了，再见！”山谷中传来欢快的声音。
小棕熊回到家，美美地睡了一觉。
第二天一大早，小棕熊就拿出自己的零花钱去商店买了一顶看上去特别酷的帽子。
到了晚上，小棕熊爬上门前的小树，把帽子挂在了树梢上，然后静静地坐在树下等着月亮出现。
不一会儿，月亮出现了，它慢慢地穿过树枝，爬到树梢，然后戴上了帽子。
小棕熊在树下乐得手舞足蹈。“哇，刚刚好哦，好漂亮！”小棕熊高兴地说道，“生日快乐！”
晚上，小棕熊梦见月亮来到自己的床前，甜甜地说：“生日快乐！”
妈妈说，宝宝听
宝贝，在小棕熊的世界里，万物都是有生命的，都是可以对话的，所以，他的世界很美。小棕熊渴望友谊，学习建立友谊，很值得咱们学习哦。乐观积极的小棕熊真诚地交友，让我们每个人都感到温暖无比。
月亮是什么味道
浩瀚的夜空，皎洁的月光，大地一片祥和，树林里的小动物们聚在一起赏月。
小兔子说：“你们谁知道月亮是什么味道？是甜的，还是咸的呢？”
小松鼠说：“这可真不知道，我也想尝一小口呢。”
动物们望着月亮想啊想啊，就是想不出月亮到底是什么味道。于是，他们想先用手摸摸月亮，可是呢，不管怎么伸长脖子，伸长胳膊，踮起脚，就是够不着月亮。
于是，他们决定爬到最高的山顶上去摸一摸月亮。他们气喘吁吁地爬上山顶，可还是够不着月亮。
小兔子想到一个好办法，那就是用叠罗汉的方式搭天梯，让最上面的动物够到月亮，咬下来一点儿，让大家尝一尝。
小兔子说：“小松鼠，你到我背上来，肯定能够到月亮。”小松鼠踩在小兔子的背上，使劲儿伸长了脖子，可还是够不着。
小松鼠叫来了小花猫：“小花猫，你跳到我背上，应该能够到！”小花猫在小松鼠背上努力伸长了脖子，可还是够不着。
小花猫叫来了小鸭子：“小鸭子，你到我背上来，说不定我们就可以够到了！”但小鸭子依然够不着月亮。
小鸭子叫来小公鸡：“小公鸡，你到我背上来，肯定能成功！”可就在这时，最下面的小兔子支撑不住了，于是大家一个个都掉下来摔在了地上。
大家爬起来，揉揉摔疼的地方，沮丧地下山了。
山下池塘里的小青蛙看到这一切后，怎么也闹不明白：“他们为什么要那么费力，到高高的天上去摘月亮？这不是还有一个嘛。看，就在我的池塘里啊，我什么时候想吃就跳下去咬一口，多方便啊！”
妈妈说，宝宝听
小动物们对什么都充满好奇心，竟然想尝尝月亮的味道，虽然最后没有成功，但是他们团结起来去做一件事的精神是很可贵的。宝贝，小青蛙够聪明有趣吧。其实，小动物们就和小朋友一样，总是用一颗童心去看待周围的世界，你将来也会是这样哦！
小兔和雪孩子
冬季里的一天，下了整整一晚上的大雪，外面白茫茫的一片。
兔妈妈要出门办事，为了不让小兔感到孤单，就给小兔堆了一个雪孩子，还用两个桂圆核做眼睛，一节胡萝卜做鼻子，一下子就使雪孩子更加漂亮，更加神采奕奕了。
兔妈妈走后，小兔开始围着雪孩子玩，和他说话。突然，雪孩子开始活动了，小兔高兴极了：“雪孩子，你居然能动，太好了，这回我有好朋友了。”他们俩一起滑雪，一会儿爬上山坡，一会儿又滑到坡底。
后来，小兔玩累了，对雪孩子说：“雪孩子，你先自己玩一会儿吧，我回屋睡一会儿。”雪孩子就在树林里和松鼠玩起来。雪越下越大，但小木屋里却温暖极了，原来兔妈妈临走时在屋里生好了火炉。小兔睡着了，睡梦中翻了个身，被子滑了下来，却被火烧着了。
火势很快蔓延开来，雪孩子看到小木屋的窗户冒出了浓烟，知道小木屋着火了，立刻跑过去，冲进小木屋，将雪球扔向大火，但这无济于事，火越着越大。因为雪人是怕热的，雪水一下流满了雪孩子的全身，但听到小兔叫“妈妈”的哭喊声时，雪孩子又不顾一切地扑进大火，找到小兔后抱起她冲出火海。这时雪孩子的身体变得越来越瘦小了，最后化成了一摊清水。
这时，兔妈妈回来了，小兔一头扑进妈妈的怀里，伤心地说：“妈妈，雪孩子为了救我，自己被大火烤化成水了。”兔妈妈看着地上一汪清水和两个桂圆核，一节胡萝卜，也非常难过，但她安慰小兔说：“雪孩子永远和我们在一起，你抬头看看天空。”小兔抬起头向天空望去，这时太阳出来了，水变成蒸汽开始升腾，逐渐幻化成一个雪孩子模样的云朵，徐徐升向高空，正向小兔微笑呢。
妈妈说，宝宝听
雪孩子救出了火中的小兔，自己却变成了一摊洁净的水，两颗乌黑的桂圆核和一节胡萝卜。雪孩子的身体是冰冷的，善良的心却带给这世间温暖。宝贝，雪孩子逝去的痛楚在我们心中都留下了一滴泪，却也滋润了心中爱的种子，相信你也感受到这种爱了，对吧？
最棒的彩虹天使
天空中美丽的彩虹是怎么形成的呢？原来是精挑细选的彩虹天使们画出来的。
思思今天刚刚成为彩虹天使，她对一切都感到很新奇。大雨就快停了，她跟着六个姐姐赶紧飞去画彩虹，再晚就来不及了。
正当她们在空中飞行时，听到了一个小女孩的声音：“彩虹天使们，我虽然眼睛看不见你们，但我能感觉到你们，能不能让我抱抱你们？”
其他的几个彩虹天使都听到了小女孩的话，可是她们一刻也不敢停留。因为她们怕耽误画彩虹的最佳时间。但是，思思被小女孩的恳求触动了，她对姐姐们说：“我们画美丽的彩虹，不就是帮助别人实现美好的愿望吗？现在，我想先去实现这个小女孩的愿望，然后我马上就赶过去画彩虹。”不等姐姐们答应，思思就向小女孩飞去。
“思思第一天当彩虹天使，就这样不守规矩，万一耽误了时间，她以后可就很难再成为彩虹天使了。”一个叫文文的彩虹天使说道。
思思降落在小女孩面前，并轻轻地抱了抱她。小女孩流下了激动欣喜的泪水，这些泪水不小心滴落在了思思的画笔上。思思并没有介意，她抖了抖画笔上的泪珠，心想：但愿不要影响到画彩虹。
思思赶到的时候，彩虹只剩下自己的颜色没有画上了，她赶紧拿出画笔。
“思思你快一点儿，太阳马上就出来啦！”文文说道。
可是思思的画笔却怎么也画不出颜色。“糟糕！”她心想，“可能是小女孩的泪水浸湿了画笔，才画不出颜色的。”
“这可怎么办，七色彩虹变成了六色彩虹！”大家都很焦急。
“思思，你画的是什么颜色？”彩虹天使琪琪惊呼，“太漂亮啦！彩虹的上面有一道银色的白光。”
此时，彩虹的出现吸引人们都出来欣赏，大家对今天的彩虹大加赞叹：“今天的彩虹格外美丽。”“我从来没有见过带银色白光的彩虹！”……
正当人们称赞彩虹闪着银光时，小女孩的眼睛被一道银光照射，那光线很温暖，她不由地睁开眼睛，她简直不敢相信，因为她的眼睛亮了！她看到了这个世界，更看到了此刻最美丽的彩虹。
现在，大家都说思思是最棒的彩虹天使。
妈妈说，宝宝听
宝贝，思思是个很有同情心的小天使，她面对失明小女孩的请求时，不忍拒绝小女孩的愿望，于是在有可能失去画彩虹的机会的情况下，去安慰小女孩，实现小女孩的心愿，可见她有一颗不计较个人得失的善良之心。妈妈希望你长大后，也拥有一颗同情心，能用自己的心去感受别人的不幸，并设法帮助他人。
五叶草
冬天过去了，春风婆婆唤醒了沉睡的大地。
“春风婆婆，辛苦了！”五叶草微笑着向春风婆婆打招呼。
这时，一只蚂蚱跳到了五叶草的叶子下面。“你为什么慌慌张张的？”五叶草问。
“现在有一只青蛙正在捉我，我不得不藏在绿色的叶子下面。”蚂蚱说道。
“那你摘一片我的叶子试试看，这样或许可以躲避危险！”五叶草慷慨地说。
“谢谢你！五叶草。”蚂蚱摘了一片五叶草的叶子，让自己躲藏起来。
过了几天，下起了第一场春雨，五叶草听见低低的抽泣声。
“小蚂蚁，你为什么哭呢？”五叶草问。
“我自己出来玩儿，现在下雨了，我没有雨伞没法回家。”
“也许我的叶子可以做你的雨伞。”五叶草说道。
小蚂蚁摘了一片叶子遮在头上：“谢谢五叶草！雨伞真合适，我会记得你的。”小蚂蚁高高兴兴地走了。
又过了几天，五叶草听到身后有来回走动的声音。
“蟋蟀，你遇到什么难事了吗？”
“我想去看望我的朋友，可是这条沟积满了水，我过不去。”
“我的叶子也许能给你当船用呢。”五叶草说道。
蟋蟀摘了五叶草的叶子，放在水面上，轻松地到了对岸。
天气越来越热，一只小鸟在上空来回盘旋。
“喂，鸟儿，你在找什么吗？”
“天气这么热，我想给我的孩子弄点儿水喝，但是没有碗给它带回去。”
“我的叶子不是正好可以给你做碗吗？赶紧去喂你的鸟宝宝吧！”
鸟儿摘了一片叶子，感激地说：“谢谢你，五叶草，遇见你真是我的幸运，我不会忘记你的。”
就这样，五叶草总是将自己的叶子送给有需要的小动物们，渐渐地，它的叶子越来越少，失去了以往的活力，但它的内心充满幸福感，因为它觉得自己的存在是有价值的。
妈妈说，宝宝听
宝贝，五叶草是个好孩子，他用自己的叶子帮助其他许多小动物渡过了难关，带给他们幸福。妈妈希望你以后能和五叶草一样，用自己的智慧和力量，去帮助那些需要帮助的小朋友，好不好？
草莓公主
